original_question: Let G=(V,E,ω) be a weighted graph with landmark set L⊂V and witness set W⊂V. For the Dowker complexes built from G, study stability in two directions. First, if G'=(V,E,ω') has the same vertices and edges as G but a different weight function ω', bound the bottleneck distance between the persistence diagrams of the Dowker complexes of G and G' in terms of the supremum distance between ω and ω'. Second, if L and L' are both ε-nets for G, find conditions under which Dow_α(W,L) and Dow_α(W,L') have the same homotopy type.
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E, ω) be a finite connected weighted graph, where ω : E → (0, ∞) assigns positive weights to edges. The weighted graph induces a shortest-path (pseudo)metric d_G on V. Fix two subsets L ⊂ V (landmarks) and W ⊂ V (witnesses). For a scale parameter α ≥ 0, the Dowker complex Dow_α(W, L) is the simplicial complex on the vertex set L whose simplices are the finite subsets σ ⊂ L such that there exists w ∈ W with d_G(w, ℓ) ≤ α for every ℓ ∈ σ. Letting α vary yields the Dowker filtration of (W, L) in G, whose persistent homology produces a persistence diagram Dgm(G; W, L).

A subset L ⊂ V is called an ε-net for G if for every v ∈ V there is some ℓ ∈ L with d_G(v, ℓ) ≤ ε, and any two distinct points of L are at distance more than ε. For two weight functions ω, ω' on the same edge set E, define the supremum distance ‖ω − ω'‖_∞ = max_{e ∈ E} |ω(e) − ω'(e)|.

(i) (Stability under reweighting.) Let G = (V, E, ω) and G' = (V, E, ω') be weighted graphs with the same vertex and edge sets, and fix L, W ⊂ V. Establish an explicit bound of the form
   d_B(Dgm(G; W, L), Dgm(G'; W, L)) ≤ C · ‖ω − ω'‖_∞,
where d_B denotes the bottleneck distance between persistence diagrams, and identify the optimal constant C (possibly depending on combinatorial features of G).

(ii) (Stability under change of landmarks.) Let L, L' ⊂ V both be ε-nets for G, and let W ⊂ V be a fixed witness set. Determine combinatorial or metric conditions on (L, L', W, G, α, ε) that guarantee Dow_α(W, L) and Dow_α(W, L') have the same homotopy type.
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem on stability of Dowker complexes. Recent work (e.g., on functorial Dowker theorems, asymmetrically weighted Dowker persistence, and persistent path diagrams) addresses related stability statements for Dowker filtrations on networks, but none provides the explicit bottleneck bound in terms of the supremum weight-distance for landmark/witness Dowker complexes on weighted graphs, nor the homotopy-type criterion for differing ε-nets. The problem appears to still be open.

paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
context_brief: Exact and efficient solvability by choice of A
original_question: With the same setup as the computational problem for the expressiveness indicators m_i^A(x), classify the families of nonzero binary column sets A for which the probability P((m_i(x)=m_i(y)) for all i), with x and y sampled uniformly at random, can be computed exactly, and classify the families A for which that probability can be computed efficiently.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n,k$ be positive integers, and let $A = \{a_1, \dots, a_k\} \subseteq \{0,1\}^n \setminus \{0\}$ be a family of nonzero binary column vectors of length $n$. For $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ and each $i \in \{1,\dots,k\}$, define the expressiveness indicator $m_i^A(x) := \langle a_i, x \rangle \bmod 2 \in \{0,1\}$ (or, more generally, any fixed Boolean readout of $x$ associated with $a_i$ in the same manner). Let $x,y$ be independent uniformly random elements of $\{0,1\}^n$, and consider the quantity
$$P(A) \;:=\; \Pr\!\left[\, m_i^A(x) = m_i^A(y) \text{ for all } i=1,\dots,k \,\right].$$

(a) Characterize (classify) all families $A$ of nonzero binary columns for which $P(A)$ can be computed exactly in closed form.

(b) Characterize (classify) all families $A$ for which $P(A)$ can be computed efficiently, i.e., by an algorithm running in time polynomial in $n$ and $k$.

paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
original_question: Consider a 4-uniform hypergraph H=(V,E) with source node s and sink node t. In the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem, one must separate s and t while minimizing the number of 1-vs-3 hyperedge splits and forbidding any 2-vs-2 hyperedge splits. Determine the computational complexity of this problem.
self_contained_problem:
Let H = (V, E) be a 4-uniform hypergraph (every hyperedge contains exactly four vertices) with two distinguished vertices s, t ∈ V. Given a bipartition (S, V \ S) with s ∈ S and t ∈ V \ S, each hyperedge e ∈ E is classified by how its four vertices split between S and V \ S as 4-vs-0, 3-vs-1, or 2-vs-2. Call the bipartition admissible if no hyperedge is split 2-vs-2 (i.e., every hyperedge has all four endpoints on the same side, or exactly one endpoint on one side and three on the other). The No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem asks, among all admissible bipartitions separating s from t, for one minimizing the number of hyperedges that are split 1-vs-3. 

Determine the computational complexity of this problem: is it polynomial-time solvable, NP-hard, or otherwise classified?
status_search_result: Subsequent work on cardinality-based minimum s-t cut problems in hypergraphs establishes that the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem is NP-hard, via a reduction from maximum cut. This resolves the complexity question by showing the problem is intractable (assuming P ≠ NP).

paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
original_question: Let G=(V,E) be a directed acyclic graph. Eliminating a vertex j removes j and adds every edge (i,k) with i a predecessor of j and k a successor of j; the cost of eliminating j is |P_j|·|S_j|. A complete vertex elimination sequence is a sequence of such eliminations that transforms G into the corresponding bipartite DAG representation of the Jacobian, and its cost is the sum of the individual elimination costs. Given G and an integer k≥0, determine whether there exists a complete vertex elimination sequence whose total cost is at most k.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a directed acyclic graph with a set of source (input) vertices and a set of sink (output) vertices. For an intermediate (non-source, non-sink) vertex $j\in V$, let $P_j=\{i\in V:(i,j)\in E\}$ denote its set of predecessors and $S_j=\{k\in V:(j,k)\in E\}$ its set of successors. The operation of eliminating vertex $j$ consists of (i) inserting, for every pair $(i,k)\in P_j\times S_j$, the edge $(i,k)$ into the graph (if $(i,k)$ already exists, no duplicate is added), and (ii) removing $j$ together with all edges incident to $j$. The cost of this elimination is defined to be $|P_j|\cdot|S_j|$.

A complete vertex elimination sequence is a sequence of vertex eliminations applied to intermediate vertices of $G$ (and of the intermediate graphs produced along the way) which, when carried out in order, eliminates every intermediate vertex, leaving a bipartite directed acyclic graph whose edges go only from sources to sinks. The cost of the sequence is the sum of the costs of its individual eliminations.

Decision problem: Given a directed acyclic graph $G$ (with specified sources and sinks) and a nonnegative integer $k$, decide whether there exists a complete vertex elimination sequence for $G$ whose total cost is at most $k$. Determine the computational complexity of this decision problem.
status_search_result: A 2025 preprint ("Structural Optimal Jacobian Accumulation and Minimum Edge Count are NP-Complete Under Vertex Elimination", arXiv:2506.17521) establishes NP-completeness of the structural optimal Jacobian accumulation problem under vertex elimination, resolving the long-standing open complexity question. The paper also provides an O*(2^n)-time exact algorithm that is essentially tight under the exponential time hypothesis.

paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
original_question: Let M be an n×n real matrix with spectral radius λ=ρ(M)<1, partitioned into an ℓ×ℓ array of blocks. For a delay matrix δ with zero diagonal, define the asynchronous update operator M^(δ) by allowing block i at the next step to depend on block j from δ_{ji} steps earlier. If every delay is bounded by k, is it always true that ρ(M^(δ))≤λ^(1/(k+1))? If not, does there nevertheless exist a function f:(0,1)×N→(0,1) such that ρ(M^(δ))≤f(λ,k)?

Let $M$ be an $n\times n$ real matrix with spectral radius $\rho(M)=\lambda<1$. Fix an integer $\ell\ge 1$ and partition $M$ into an $\ell\times\ell$ array of blocks $M_{ij}$ (with compatible row/column block sizes summing to $n$). For a delay matrix $\delta\in\{0,1,\dots,k\}^{\ell\times\ell}$ with zero diagonal entries, define the asynchronous update on block-vectors $\tilde x=(\tilde x_1,\dots,\tilde x_\ell)$ by
$$\tilde x_i(t+1)=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell} M_{ij}\,\tilde x_j(t-\delta_{ji}),\qquad i=1,\dots,\ell,$$
where $\tilde x_j(s)=0$ for $s<0$. This recurrence is a linear map on the extended state $(\tilde x(t),\tilde x(t-1),\dots,\tilde x(t-k))$; let $M^{(\delta)}$ denote the corresponding finite-dimensional linear operator and let $\rho(M^{(\delta)})$ be its spectral radius.

(a) Is it true that for every such $M$, every block partition, every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, and every $\delta\in\{0,1,\dots,k\}^{\ell\times\ell}$ with zero diagonal,
$$\rho(M^{(\delta)})\le \lambda^{1/(k+1)}\,?$$

(b) If (a) fails, does there exist a function $f:(0,1)\times\mathbb{N}\to(0,1)$ such that $\rho(M^{(\delta)})\le f(\lambda,k)$ holds for all choices of $M$, partition, $k$, and $\delta$ as above?

paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
original_question: Let G=(V,E) be a graph and let k≥0. A set Z⊂V is an (n−k)-contingent zero-forcing set if it remains a zero-forcing set after deletion of any set of at most k edges. Determine whether there is an efficient algorithm for finding a minimum-size (n−k)-contingent zero-forcing set for graphs with few cycles or, more generally, for sparse graphs with large diameter.
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph on n = |V| vertices. The zero-forcing color-change rule is: starting from a subset Z ⊆ V whose vertices are colored blue (the others white), repeatedly apply the rule that if a blue vertex u has exactly one white neighbor w, then w becomes blue. A set Z ⊆ V is called a zero-forcing set for G if iteratively applying this rule starting from Z eventually colors all of V blue.

Fix an integer k ≥ 0. A set Z ⊆ V is an (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set for G if, for every set of edges E₀ ⊆ E with |E₀| ≤ k, the set Z is a zero-forcing set for the edge-deleted graph G − E₀ = (V, E ∖ E₀). Let Z_{(n−k)}(G) denote the minimum cardinality of an (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set of G.

Question: Does there exist an efficient (polynomial-time) algorithm that, given as input a graph G drawn from one of the following classes, computes Z_{(n−k)}(G) (or a minimum-size (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set)?
(a) Graphs with few cycles (e.g., graphs G with |E| − |V| + c(G) bounded by a constant, where c(G) is the number of connected components).
(b) More generally, sparse graphs with large diameter.
status_search_result: A web search for algorithms computing minimum contingent zero-forcing sets on sparse or low-cycle graphs returns general zero-forcing computational literature (IP approaches, Wavefront algorithm, complexity of connected zero forcing) but no result addressing the (n − k)-contingent variant on these graph classes. There is no evidence that an efficient algorithm has been established for this specific problem, so it appears to remain open.

original_question: Let V_{d1,...,dk} be the Segre-Veronese variety of partially symmetric rank-one tensors in P(S^{d1}V1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ S^{dk}Vk). For each r, the r-th secant variety σ_r(V_{d1,...,dk}) has expected dimension min{r dim(V_{d1,...,dk}) + r - 1, ambient dimension}. Which Segre-Veronese varieties are r-defective (that is, have secant variety of smaller than expected dimension), and what are the actual dimensions of their secant varieties?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k\ge 1$ be an integer, and for each $i=1,\dots,k$ let $V_i$ be a complex vector space of dimension $n_i+1\ge 2$, and let $d_i\ge 1$ be a positive integer. Consider the Segre–Veronese variety
$$V_{d_1,\dots,d_k}\;\subset\;\mathbb{P}\bigl(S^{d_1}V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes S^{d_k}V_k\bigr),$$
defined as the image of $\mathbb{P}(V_1)\times\cdots\times\mathbb{P}(V_k)$ under the embedding given by the line bundle $\mathcal{O}(d_1,\dots,d_k)$; equivalently, it parametrizes partially symmetric rank-one tensors $v_1^{\otimes d_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_k^{\otimes d_k}$ up to scalar. Let $N=\dim\mathbb{P}(S^{d_1}V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes S^{d_k}V_k)$ and let $n=\dim V_{d_1,\dots,d_k}=\sum_i n_i$. For an integer $r\ge 1$, the $r$-th secant variety $\sigma_r(V_{d_1,\dots,d_k})$ is the Zariski closure of the union of linear spans of $r$ points of $V_{d_1,\dots,d_k}$. Its expected dimension is
$$\operatorname{expdim}\sigma_r(V_{d_1,\dots,d_k})=\min\{\,r\,n+r-1,\;N\,\}.$$
The variety $V_{d_1,\dots,d_k}$ is called $r$-defective if $\dim\sigma_r(V_{d_1,\dots,d_k})$ is strictly smaller than this expected dimension.

Problem. Classify all tuples $(n_1,\dots,n_k;\,d_1,\dots,d_k;\,r)$ for which the Segre–Veronese variety $V_{d_1,\dots,d_k}$ is $r$-defective, and in each defective case determine the exact value of $\dim\sigma_r(V_{d_1,\dots,d_k})$.
status_search_result: A complete classification is not known. original_question: Given a variety X, a line bundle L on X, and an integer r, determine whether there exists a 0-dimensional subscheme X ⊆ X that is a disjoint union of degree-2 schemes such that the reduced subscheme X_red imposes independent conditions on L while X itself does not.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an algebraic variety over an algebraically closed field, let $L$ be a line bundle on $X$, and let $r$ be a positive integer. A 0-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$ is said to impose independent conditions on $L$ if the natural restriction map $H^0(X,L)\to H^0(Z,L|_Z)$ is surjective (equivalently, has rank equal to $\deg(Z)$). A degree-2 scheme in $X$ is a 0-dimensional subscheme of length 2 (either two reduced points or a non-reduced length-2 scheme supported at a single point, i.e. a tangent vector). 

Determine whether there exists a 0-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$ of degree $r$ that is a disjoint union of degree-2 schemes, such that the reduced subscheme $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ imposes independent conditions on $L$, while $Z$ itself does not impose independent conditions on $L$. More generally, characterize the triples $(X,L,r)$ for which such a subscheme $Z$ exists.
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open research problem in a 2023 collection of open problems on the geometry of tensors. No subsequent work found resolving it in general; it remains open.

original_question: Determine the maximal possible Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity reg(X) of an irredundant scheme X that is apolar to a form f ∈ S^dV.
self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space and let $S^\bullet V = \bigoplus_{d\ge 0} S^d V$ denote the symmetric algebra on $V$, viewed as the polynomial ring whose degree-$d$ piece is $S^d V$. Let $S^\bullet V^* = \bigoplus_{d\ge 0} S^d V^*$ be the dual symmetric algebra, acting on $S^\bullet V$ by contraction (the apolarity action): for $\partial \in S^k V^*$ and $f \in S^d V$, the element $\partial \cdot f \in S^{d-k} V$ is given by partial differentiation. For a form $f \in S^d V$, the apolar (annihilator) ideal is
$$ f^\perp \;=\; \{\, \partial \in S^\bullet V^*: \partial \cdot f = 0 \,\} \;\subset\; S^\bullet V^*. $$
A closed subscheme $X \subset \mathbb{P}(V^*)$ is said to be apolar to $f$ if its homogeneous (saturated) ideal $I_X \subset S^\bullet V^*$ is contained in $f^\perp$. A zero-dimensional apolar scheme $X$ is called irredundant (with respect to $f$) if no proper closed subscheme $X' \subsetneq X$ is also apolar to $f$.

For a closed subscheme $X \subset \mathbb{P}(V^*)$, let $\mathrm{reg}(X)$ denote the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of its saturated homogeneous ideal $I_X$ (equivalently, of the structure sheaf $\mathcal{O}_X$).

Problem. As $f$ ranges over forms in $S^d V$ and $X$ ranges over all irredundant zero-dimensional schemes apolar to $f$, determine the maximum possible value of $\mathrm{reg}(X)$ (as a function of $d$ and $\dim V$).
status_search_result: A follow-up work studying schemes evinced by generalized additive decompositions establishes partial results: irredundant apolar schemes need not be $d$-regular in general, but irredundant apolar schemes of length at most $2d+1$, and tangential decompositions of minimal length, are shown to be $d$-regular. A sharp general bound for $\mathrm{reg}(X)$ over all irredundant apolar schemes does not appear to be established, so the problem remains only partially solved.

original_question: Develop general lower bounds for the degree of higher secant varieties, analogous in spirit to the lower-bound framework used for second secant varieties.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^N$ be a non-degenerate irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. For each integer $s \geq 1$, the $s$-th secant variety of $X$ is defined as
$$\sigma_s(X) \;=\; \overline{\bigcup_{x_1,\dots,x_s \in X} \langle x_1,\dots,x_s \rangle} \;\subset\; \mathbb{P}^N,$$
i.e. the Zariski closure of the union of all linear spans of $s$ points of $X$. Assume that $\sigma_s(X)$ is a proper subvariety of $\mathbb{P}^N$ (equivalently, $X$ is not $s$-defective in the sense that $\sigma_s(X)$ fills the ambient space).

For $s = 2$, there is a known general lower bound for $\deg \sigma_2(X)$ expressed in terms of invariants of $X$ (such as $\dim X$, $\deg X$, and the codimension of $\sigma_2(X)$), obtained via a refinement of Terracini's lemma.

Problem: Develop, in the same spirit, general lower bounds for $\deg \sigma_s(X)$ for arbitrary $s \geq 2$, expressed in terms of intrinsic invariants of $X$ and of the embedding $X \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^N$, and which reduce (up to the appropriate specialization) to the known bound when $s = 2$.
status_search_result: A search reveals work on degrees of second secant varieties (notably refinements of Terracini's lemma giving sharp lower bounds for $\deg \sigma_2(X)$), and on dimensions/degrees of higher secants in special cases (Segre, Veronese, Segre–Veronese), but no general lower bound framework for $\deg \sigma_s(X)$ for arbitrary $s$ analogous to the $s=2$ case appears in the literature. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Fix n and d, and let D_{n,d} be the generic number of eigenscheme points for degree-d forms in n+1 variables. Let E_{n,d} denote the Zariski-closed locus in the symmetrized product (PV)^(·D_{n,d}) (equivalently in Hilb_{D_{n,d}}(PV)) consisting of eigenconfigurations that occur as eigenschemes X_f of some f ∈ S^dV. Determine defining equations (in the broad Zariski-closed-condition sense) for E_{n,d}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $V = \mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ with coordinates $x_0,\dots,x_n$, and let $S^dV$ denote the space of homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ in these variables. For $f \in S^dV$, the eigenscheme $X_f \subset \mathbb{P}V$ is the closed subscheme defined by the $2\times 2$ minors of the matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix} x_0 & x_1 & \cdots & x_n \\ \partial f/\partial x_0 & \partial f/\partial x_1 & \cdots & \partial f/\partial x_n \end{pmatrix},$$
i.e., the locus of points $v \in \mathbb{P}V$ such that $\nabla f(v)$ is proportional to $v$. For generic $f$, $X_f$ consists of a fixed number $D_{n,d}$ of reduced points (the generic eigenscheme cardinality, equal to $\sum_{i=0}^{n}(d-1)^i$).

Define the eigenconfiguration variety
$$E_{n,d} = \overline{\{(v_1,\dots,v_{D_{n,d}}) \in (\mathbb{P}V)^{(\cdot D_{n,d})} : X_f = \{v_1,\dots,v_{D_{n,d}}\} \text{ for some } f \in S^dV\}}$$
inside the symmetric product $(\mathbb{P}V)^{(\cdot D_{n,d})}$ (equivalently inside $\mathrm{Hilb}_{D_{n,d}}(\mathbb{P}V)$); this is a Zariski-closed subset.

Problem: Determine explicit defining equations (polynomial conditions cutting out the Zariski-closed locus) for $E_{n,d}$.
status_search_result: The problem of determining defining equations for the eigenconfiguration variety $E_{n,d}$ is posed as an open problem in the literature on tensor eigenschemes and symmetric tensor decomposition. No general answer has been found; partial results are known only for special small cases (e.g., $n=1$, related to binary forms, where eigenconfigurations are well understood). No search evidence indicates a general solution.

original_question: For non-symmetric tensors in V⊗d, each choice of contracted d-1 factors defines an eigenscheme, and the eigencompatibility variety EC_{n,d} records d-tuples of schemes that can simultaneously occur from one tensor. Determine the dimension and defining equations of EC_{n,d}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a complex vector space of dimension $n$, and let $d \geq 2$. For a tensor $T \in V^{\otimes d}$ and each index $i \in \{1,\dots,d\}$, contracting $T$ in the $d-1$ factors other than the $i$-th with a vector $v \in V$ defines a multilinear map whose fixed points (up to scalar) give a zero-dimensional subscheme $X_i^T \subset \mathbb{P}V$, called the $i$-th eigenscheme of $T$. For generic $T$, each $X_i^T$ has a fixed length $D_{n,d}$ depending only on $n$ and $d$. Let $\mathrm{Hilb}^{D_{n,d}}(\mathbb{P}V)$ denote the Hilbert scheme of length-$D_{n,d}$ subschemes of $\mathbb{P}V$. Define the eigencompatibility variety
$$\mathrm{EC}_{n,d} = \overline{\{(X_1,\dots,X_d) \in \mathrm{Hilb}^{D_{n,d}}(\mathbb{P}V)^{\times d} : \exists\, T \in V^{\otimes d} \text{ with } X_i = X_i^T \text{ for all } i\}}.$$
Determine the dimension of $\mathrm{EC}_{n,d}$ and a system of defining equations for $\mathrm{EC}_{n,d}$ inside $\mathrm{Hilb}^{D_{n,d}}(\mathbb{P}V)^{\times d}$.
status_search_result: The eigencompatibility variety was introduced by Abo–Seigal–Sturmfels (2017) for the symmetric case, and the non-symmetric version is posed as an open problem in recent tensor-geometry literature. A web search did not surface any paper computing the dimension or defining equations of $\mathrm{EC}_{n,d}$ in the non-symmetric setting, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For probability tensors, determine which counts of real critical points can occur among the aEDdeg(S_{n1,...,nd}) critical points.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n_1,\dots,n_d\ge 2$ be integers and set $N=n_1n_2\cdots n_d$. Consider the Segre variety
$$S_{n_1,\dots,n_d}\subset\mathbb{P}^{N-1}$$
of rank-one tensors, parameterizing the classes of nonzero tensors of the form $v_1\otimes v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_d$ with $v_i\in\mathbb{C}^{n_i}$. The affine cone $\widehat{S}_{n_1,\dots,nd}\subset\mathbb{C}^N$ consists of all rank-one tensors (including zero).

The probability simplex of tensors is
$$\Delta=\Bigl\{\,u=(u_{i_1\dots i_d})\in\mathbb{R}^N\;:\;u_{i_1\dots i_d}\ge 0,\ \sum_{i_1,\dots,i_d}u_{i_1\dots i_d}=1\,\Bigr\}.$$
A tensor in $\Delta$ is called a probability tensor.

For a generic complex tensor $u\in\mathbb{C}^N$, the squared-distance function $T\mapsto \sum (T_{i_1\dots i_d}-u_{i_1\dots i_d})^2$ restricted to the smooth locus of $\widehat{S}_{n_1,\dots,n_d}$ has a finite number of complex critical points. This number is called the affine Euclidean distance degree $\mathrm{aEDdeg}(S_{n_1,\dots,n_d})$ and is independent of the generic choice of $u$.

Problem. For a generic probability tensor $u\in\Delta$, determine the set of possible numbers of real critical points among the $\mathrm{aEDdeg}(S_{n_1,\dots,n_d})$ complex critical points of the squared-distance function from $u$ to $\widehat{S}_{n_1,\dots,n_d}$, as $u$ ranges over $\Delta$.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2023 survey on geometry of tensors. No subsequent work fully classifying the possible counts of real critical points among the affine ED critical points of Segre varieties at probability tensors was located; only partial results on average and total ED degrees of Segre varieties are available.

original_question: For each complexity class C among VWaring, VChow, and VBP, determine whether the class equals its corresponding border analogue.
self_contained_problem:
Background. In algebraic complexity theory, polynomials over a field (taken here to be the complex numbers) are computed by various models, giving rise to complexity classes that consist of (sequences of) polynomials whose computational cost grows polynomially in the input parameters.

(a) The class VBP consists of (sequences of) polynomials computable by polynomial-size algebraic branching programs: directed acyclic graphs with a source s and a sink t whose edges are labeled by affine linear forms in the input variables, the polynomial computed being the sum over all s–t paths of the product of edge labels.

(b) The class VChow consists of polynomials of polynomial Chow rank, i.e. those degree-d homogeneous polynomials f(x_1,...,x_n) expressible as a sum f = ∏_{j=1}^{d} L_{1,j} + ∏_{j=1}^{d} L_{2,j} + ... + ∏_{j=1}^{d} L_{r,j} of r products of d linear forms, with r bounded polynomially in n and d.

(c) The class VWaring consists of polynomials of polynomial Waring rank, i.e. degree-d homogeneous polynomials expressible as a sum f = ∑_{i=1}^{r} L_i^d of r d-th powers of linear forms, with r polynomially bounded.

For each such class C, its border (or approximative) closure C̄ is defined as the class of polynomials f that can be written as a limit (in the Euclidean or Zariski topology, equivalently as the ε→0 limit of polynomials whose coefficients are Laurent polynomials in a formal parameter ε) of polynomials f_ε belonging to C, with the relevant complexity measure of f_ε remaining polynomially bounded uniformly in ε.

Problem. For each C ∈ {VWaring, VChow, VBP}, decide whether C = C̄; i.e., determine whether every polynomial in the border closure of C already lies in C.
status_search_result: Recent surveys and papers (2024–2025) on debordering describe the equality of these algebraic complexity classes with their border closures as an open central question. Progress has been made on quantitative debordering (e.g., improved upper bounds on Waring rank in terms of border Waring rank such as d·r^{O(√r)}, and fixed-parameter debordering of Waring rank), but no proof of equality (or separation) of VWaring, VChow, or VBP with their respective border analogues has been established.

original_question: Determine defining equations for the tensor network variety TNS^Γ_{m,n}; if necessary, restrict to specific graph classes Γ or specific assignments of bond and local dimensions.
self_contained_problem:
Let Γ = (V, E) be a finite simple graph with vertex set V = {1, …, n} and edge set E. Fix a bond dimension m_e ∈ ℕ for each edge e ∈ E and a local (physical) dimension d_v ∈ ℕ for each vertex v ∈ V. For each vertex v, let H_v = ℂ^{d_v} and for each edge e ∈ E incident to v, let B_{v,e} = ℂ^{m_e}. Form the vector space
   A_v = H_v ⊗ ⨂_{e ∋ v} B_{v,e}.
A tensor T_v ∈ A_v at each vertex v can be contracted along the edges of Γ: for each edge e = {u, v} ∈ E, pair the tensor factor B_{u,e} = ℂ^{m_e} with B_{v,e} = ℂ^{m_e} via the standard bilinear pairing. The contraction yields a tensor
   κ_Γ(T_1, …, T_n) ∈ H_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ H_n.
The tensor network variety TNS^Γ_{m,n} is defined as the Zariski closure in H_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ H_n of the image of the contraction map
   κ_Γ : A_1 × ⋯ × A_n → H_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ H_n,  (T_1, …, T_n) ↦ κ_Γ(T_1, …, T_n).

Problem. Determine an explicit system of polynomial equations defining the variety TNS^Γ_{m,n} as a subvariety of H_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ H_n. If necessary, restrict attention to specific classes of graphs Γ (for example, cycles, trees, or regular lattices) and/or to particular assignments of the bond dimensions (m_e)_{e ∈ E} and local dimensions (d_v)_{v ∈ V}.
status_search_result: No general defining equations for tensor network varieties TNS^Γ_{m,n} are known. Existing literature (e.g., Ye–Lim on tensor network ranks and subsequent work on tensor network varieties) treats only partial results—dimensions, set-theoretic descriptions, or equations in very restricted cases such as small cycles or trees with specific bond/local dimensions. The general problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Develop intrinsic methods for upper bounds on tensor subrank Q(T) and border subrank Q_bar(T) that do not proceed by upper-bounding these quantities through other rank notions.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field and let $T \in \mathbb{F}^{n_1} \otimes \mathbb{F}^{n_2} \otimes \mathbb{F}^{n_3}$ be a 3-tensor. The subrank $Q(T)$ is defined as the largest integer $r$ such that the diagonal tensor $\langle r \rangle = \sum_{i=1}^{r} e_i \otimes e_i \otimes e_i$ can be obtained from $T$ by applying linear maps to each of the three factors; equivalently, $Q(T) \geq r$ iff there exist linear maps $A_j : \mathbb{F}^{n_j} \to \mathbb{F}^r$ ($j=1,2,3$) such that $(A_1 \otimes A_2 \otimes A_3)(T) = \langle r \rangle$. The border subrank $\underline{Q}(T)$ is the largest $r$ such that $\langle r \rangle$ lies in the Zariski closure of the orbit $\{(A_1 \otimes A_2 \otimes A_3)(T) : A_j \in \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{F}^{n_j}, \mathbb{F}^r)\}$ (working over an algebraically closed field, or in the corresponding topological sense over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$).

Known upper bounds on $Q(T)$ and $\underline{Q}(T)$ typically proceed indirectly: one bounds the subrank from above by another rank-type invariant of $T$ (for example, by the slice rank, analytic rank, geometric rank, partition rank, G-stable rank, or similar quantities) which is itself easier to control.

Problem: Develop a genuinely intrinsic method for proving upper bounds on the subrank $Q(T)$ and the border subrank $\underline{Q}(T)$ of a tensor $T$ that does not proceed by first upper-bounding $Q(T)$ or $\underline{Q}(T)$ by another rank notion of $T$.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., border subrank via a generalised Hilbert–Mumford criterion, 2024; the Chang dissertation on border subrank, 2024) continues to develop techniques, but the standard upper bounds on subrank and border subrank still proceed via auxiliary rank notions (geometric rank, slice rank, etc.) or via the laser method. No source verifies that a fully intrinsic upper bound method has been established, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Prove a super-linear lower bound for the stabilizer rank of quantum states in the stated d-qubit stabilizer framework.
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Consider the n-qubit Hilbert space (ℂ²)^⊗n. The (pure) stabilizer states are the states obtained from |0⟩^⊗n by applying elements of the Clifford group; equivalently, they are the joint +1-eigenstates of maximal abelian subgroups of the n-qubit Pauli group (up to phases). The (exact) stabilizer rank χ(|ψ⟩) of a state |ψ⟩ ∈ (ℂ²)^⊗n is the smallest integer r such that there exist stabilizer states |s_1⟩, …, |s_r⟩ and complex coefficients c_1, …, c_r with
   |ψ⟩ = Σ_{i=1}^{r} c_i |s_i⟩.

The magic state is |T⟩ = cos(π/8)|0⟩ + e^{iπ/4} sin(π/8)|1⟩, and the n-fold tensor product |T⟩^⊗n is the canonical family used to study stabilizer rank.

Problem. Exhibit an explicit family of n-qubit quantum states |ψ_n⟩ (for example |T⟩^⊗n) and prove that
   χ(|ψ_n⟩) = ω(n),
i.e., establish a super-linear lower bound on the exact stabilizer rank of an explicit sequence of n-qubit states.
status_search_result: A quadratic Ω(n²) lower bound has been established for the approximate stabilizer rank (for a wide range of approximation parameters), giving a super-linear lower bound in the approximate setting. However, for the exact stabilizer rank of explicit families such as |T⟩^⊗n, no lower bound better than linear is known; thus the problem in its exact form appears to remain open, while the approximate version has been resolved super-linearly.

paper_title: Private Information Retrieval and Its Applications: An Introduction, Open Problems, Future Directions
context_brief: Fundamental limits for PRUW and PSU-based FSL
original_question: For private read-update-write (PRUW), where a user downloads a chosen section of a data-storage system, updates it, and uploads the updates back without revealing the downloaded or uploaded content or their positions, and for PSU-based federated submodel learning (FSL), where private set union and symmetric private information retrieval are used so the server learns only the union or aggregate of submodels updated by clients rather than any individual client contribution, what are the fundamental converse limits on performance metrics such as read-write communication cost, and do those limits lead to capacity characterizations for PRUW and PSU-based FSL?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following two information-theoretic privacy settings.

(1) Private Read-Update-Write (PRUW). A data-storage system consists of N non-colluding databases, each storing M submodels (sections) of equal size L over a finite field. A user wishes to (a) download exactly one chosen submodel indexed by θ ∈ {1,...,M}, (b) compute a local update to that submodel, and (c) upload the update back so that the corresponding stored submodel is correctly modified, while every other stored submodel is unchanged. The privacy requirement is that, from the queries, answers, and uploaded symbols observed by any single database, no information is revealed about the index θ or about the values of the downloaded and uploaded symbols. Define the reading cost D as the expected number of bits downloaded per database normalized by L, the writing cost U as the expected number of bits uploaded per database normalized by L, and the total communication cost as C = D + U.

(2) PSU-based Federated Submodel Learning (FSL). A central server stores a model partitioned into M submodels. In each training round, a set of clients each selects a private subset of submodels to update. Using a combination of Private Set Union (PSU) and Symmetric Private Information Retrieval (SPIR), the protocol must ensure that the server learns only the union (or the aggregate of updates over that union) of the submodels collectively updated by the clients, and nothing about any individual client's chosen subset or its specific contribution; clients similarly learn nothing about the other clients' selections. Define analogous per-round communication costs (download + upload, normalized appropriately).

Problem. Establish tight converse (impossibility) bounds on the achievable reading cost, writing cost, and total communication cost for PRUW, and on the analogous communication costs for PSU-based FSL, that match the best known achievable schemes. Equivalently, determine the capacity (the infimum of the total normalized communication cost over all valid schemes) of PRUW and of PSU-based FSL.
status_search_result: Recent works on PRUW and PSU-based FSL focus on achievable schemes (with and without sparsification, storage constraints, and heterogeneous databases) and provide only partial lower bounds. No matching converse establishing the capacity of PRUW or PSU-based FSL appears in the literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Private Information Retrieval and Its Applications: An Introduction, Open Problems, Future Directions
original_question: Can PRUW be generalized from the existing single-client system model to a multi-client system model in which private read-write communication is defined for a group of clients, the same privacy, security, and correctness requirements are maintained, and communication cost is reduced by combining queries, answers, or updates from multiple clients?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a distributed storage system in which a database is replicated (or coded) across $N$ non-colluding servers. Each server stores a model partitioned into $M$ disjoint sections (submodels). A single-client Private Read-Update-Write (PRUW) protocol allows a client to (i) privately download the contents of a chosen section $\theta \in \{1,\dots,M\}$, (ii) compute an update locally, and (iii) upload the update back to the same section, subject to the following requirements:
- Privacy: no server (or any allowed colluding subset) learns the index $\theta$ of the section read or written.
- Security: no server learns the values downloaded or the values of the update uploaded.
- Correctness: after the protocol, the chosen section is correctly updated at all servers, and the client correctly recovers the requested section's contents.

The communication cost is measured as the total number of symbols exchanged between the client(s) and the servers per unit of information read/written.

Problem. Generalize the PRUW model to a multi-client setting in which $K \geq 2$ clients simultaneously interact with the $N$ servers. Concretely, design a protocol satisfying:
1. Each client $k \in \{1,\dots,K\}$ privately reads from a chosen section $\theta_k$ and privately writes an update to that section, with the same privacy, security, and correctness guarantees as in the single-client PRUW model (extended to apply jointly to the group of clients, so that the multi-set $\{\theta_1,\dots,\theta_K\}$ and all update/read values remain hidden from any non-colluding subset of servers).
2. The protocol combines (aggregates or jointly encodes) queries, answers, and/or updates across the $K$ clients so as to achieve a strictly smaller total communication cost (per client, or in aggregate) than $K$ independent executions of the best known single-client PRUW protocol.

Determine whether such a multi-client PRUW protocol exists, and characterize the optimal achievable read and write communication costs as functions of $N$, $M$, and $K$ (and any colluding parameters).
status_search_result: A web search shows that existing PRUW work (including PRUW in federated submodel learning, with sparsification, and with heterogeneous databases) is formulated for a single client interacting with the servers. No publication was located that formalizes a multi-client PRUW system model with combined queries/answers/updates and characterizes its communication cost. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Private Information Retrieval and Its Applications: An Introduction, Open Problems, Future Directions
context_brief: Rate-privacy tradeoff for PRUW with sparsification
original_question: For PRUW in private federated learning or federated submodel learning with sparsification, how does the communication cost change if the privacy requirement is relaxed through a rate-privacy tradeoff, for example by incorporating differential privacy so that a specified amount of information may leak about the desired indices and the values of selected updates or parameters, rather than only about sparse-update indices as in existing rate-privacy-storage tradeoff work?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of Private Read–Update–Write (PRUW) in federated learning / federated submodel learning with top-r sparsification, defined as follows. A model consisting of M submodels is stored, in a coded fashion, across N non-colluding databases. In each round, a client (i) downloads (reads) a fraction r' of the parameters of one desired submodel — the "most significant" parameters according to a sparsification rule — and (ii) uploads (writes) updates to a fraction r of the parameters of that submodel. Communication cost is measured by the read rate R_R = L/D and write rate R_W = L/U, where L is the number of symbols of useful information, and D, U are the total numbers of symbols downloaded and uploaded per round, respectively.

In the standard information-theoretic privacy formulation, the mutual information between (a) the index of the desired submodel, (b) the indices (positions) of the sparse parameters/updates, and (c) the values of those updates, on one side, and all information observed by any individual database, on the other side, is required to be exactly zero. Existing rate–privacy–storage tradeoffs only relax the zero-leakage requirement on the indices of the sparse updates, which has limited impact on the communication rate.

Problem: Formulate and characterize the rate–privacy tradeoff for PRUW with top-r sparsification when privacy is relaxed via a differential-privacy-style constraint that simultaneously permits a prescribed amount of information leakage about (1) the index of the desired submodel, (2) the indices of the selected sparse parameters/updates, and (3) the values of the selected updates/parameters. Specifically, determine the optimal achievable read and write communication rates (R_R, R_W) as functions of the allowed leakage parameters (e.g., (ε, δ)-DP budgets or analogous mutual-information bounds) for each of the three categories of information, and exhibit explicit schemes attaining these rates.
status_search_result: Existing work on PRUW with sparsification addresses information-theoretic privacy and a rate–distortion or rate–privacy–storage tradeoff that allows leakage only on the indices of sparse updates. No published result was found that characterizes the rate–privacy tradeoff under a differential-privacy-style relaxation permitting leakage on the desired submodel index and the values of selected updates/parameters; this is posed as a future research direction and appears unresolved.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: For a closed manifold M of dimension at least 2, can the real-analytic diffeomorphisms Diff^ω(M) be classified up to topological conjugacy by complete invariants, and is the topological-conjugacy equivalence relation on Diff^ω(M) Borel?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) smooth manifold of dimension at least $2$, and let $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$ denote the space of real-analytic diffeomorphisms of $M$, endowed with its natural Polish topology. Two diffeomorphisms $f, g \in \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$ are said to be topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h \colon M \to M$ such that $h \circ f = g \circ h$; this defines an equivalence relation $E_{\mathrm{tc}}$ on $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$.

(a) Does there exist a classification of the elements of $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$ up to topological conjugacy by complete invariants? More precisely, is there a Polish (or standard Borel) space $Y$ and a Borel map $\Phi \colon \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M) \to Y$ such that $\Phi(f) = \Phi(g)$ if and only if $f$ and $g$ are topologically conjugate?

(b) Is the equivalence relation $E_{\mathrm{tc}}$ a Borel subset of $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M) \times \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$?
status_search_result: Anti-classification results in the smooth category (Foreman–Gorodetski and Foreman–Weiss) show that for closed manifolds of dimension ≥ 2 the topological/measure-isomorphism conjugacy relation on smooth diffeomorphisms is not Borel. In the real-analytic category, Banerjee–Kunde extended such anti-classification (for measure-isomorphism) to real-analytic diffeomorphisms of the 2-torus, and Goncharuk obtained anti-classification results for real-analytic flows on the 2-torus. However, the question for topological conjugacy on $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$ for general closed manifolds $M$ with $\dim M \ge 2$ does not appear to be fully settled in the literature.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: For a manifold M with dim M ≥ 2, does there exist an open dense subset or a dense Gδ subset of Diff∞(M) on which the equivalence relation of topological conjugacy is Borel?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold with $\dim M \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{Diff}^\infty(M)$ denote the space of $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms of $M$, equipped with the $C^\infty$ topology (a Polish space). Two diffeomorphisms $f, g \in \mathrm{Diff}^\infty(M)$ are said to be topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h \colon M \to M$ such that $h \circ f = g \circ h$; this defines an equivalence relation $\sim_{tc}$ on $\mathrm{Diff}^\infty(M)$. An equivalence relation $E$ on a Polish space $X$ is called Borel if $E \subseteq X \times X$ is a Borel subset of the product.

Question: Does there exist a subset $U \subseteq \mathrm{Diff}^\infty(M)$ which is either open and dense, or a dense $G_\delta$ set, such that the restriction of $\sim_{tc}$ to $U$ (viewed as a subset of $U \times U$) is Borel?
status_search_result: Related anti-classification results by Foreman and Gorodetski show that the topological conjugacy relation on $\mathrm{Diff}^\infty(M)$ is not Borel (for $\dim M \geq 5$, and that no Borel complete invariants exist for $\dim M \geq 2$). However, the specific question of whether the relation becomes Borel when restricted to some open dense or dense $G_\delta$ subset does not appear to be resolved in the available literature; it continues to be cited as an open question attributed to Gorodetski.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: Let C be the collection of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold M that are topologically conjugate to a structurally stable diffeomorphism, and let E be topological conjugacy restricted to C. Is E Borel reducible to equality?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold and let $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ denote the Polish space of $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms of $M$ (with the $C^\infty$ topology). A diffeomorphism $f \in \mathrm{Diff}(M)$ is called structurally stable if there exists a neighborhood $U$ of $f$ in $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ such that for every $g \in U$ there is a homeomorphism $h : M \to M$ with $h \circ f = g \circ h$. Two diffeomorphisms $f, g \in \mathrm{Diff}(M)$ are topologically conjugate, written $f \sim_{\mathrm{top}} g$, if there exists a homeomorphism $h : M \to M$ such that $h \circ f = g \circ h$.

Let
$$C = \{ f \in \mathrm{Diff}(M) : f \text{ is topologically conjugate to some structurally stable diffeomorphism} \},$$
and let $E$ denote the equivalence relation $\sim_{\mathrm{top}}$ restricted to $C \times C$.

Recall that an equivalence relation $E$ on a standard Borel space $X$ is Borel reducible to equality on a standard Borel space $Y$ (written $E \leq_B {=}_Y$) if there is a Borel function $\varphi : X \to Y$ such that for all $x, x' \in X$, $x\, E\, x'$ if and only if $\varphi(x) = \varphi(x')$.

Question: Is $E$ Borel reducible to equality?
category_tag: Borel equivalence relations in smooth dynamics
status_search_result: The question is attributed to Foreman as an open problem in the area of anti-classification results for smooth dynamical systems. While Foreman and collaborators have proven that topological conjugacy on all of Diff(M) is not a Borel equivalence relation, no published resolution of the restriction to the structurally stable conjugacy class C is evident in current literature; the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
context_brief: Flip conjugacy on Cantor minimal systems
original_question: Is the topological flip-conjugacy relation on the class of all Cantor minimal systems a Borel equivalence relation?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ denote the Cantor space (the unique up to homeomorphism nonempty compact metrizable, perfect, totally disconnected space). A Cantor minimal system is a pair $(K,T)$ where $T:K\to K$ is a homeomorphism such that every $T$-orbit $\{T^n(x):n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ is dense in $K$. Let $\mathrm{Homeo}(K)$ denote the Polish group of homeomorphisms of $K$ (with the uniform topology), and let $\mathrm{Min}(K)\subseteq\mathrm{Homeo}(K)$ denote the Borel set of minimal homeomorphisms of $K$, regarded as a standard Borel space.

Two Cantor minimal systems $(K,S)$ and $(K,T)$ are said to be flip conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h:K\to K$ such that either $h\circ S\circ h^{-1}=T$ or $h\circ S\circ h^{-1}=T^{-1}$. This defines an equivalence relation $E_{\mathrm{flip}}$ on $\mathrm{Min}(K)$.

Question: Is $E_{\mathrm{flip}}$ a Borel subset of $\mathrm{Min}(K)\times\mathrm{Min}(K)$?
category_tag: Borel equivalence relations in topological dynamics
status_search_result: Recent work (2024) shows that the topological conjugacy relation on minimal Cantor systems is not Borel, and in fact not classifiable by countable structures; the same arguments apply to flip conjugacy, so the answer to the question is negative. This is established in work of Li–Peng (arXiv:2401.11310) on pointed minimal systems and in the work referenced as DGKKK/DGRK+24 on minimal Cantor systems.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: Is there an algorithm that decides whether two subshifts of finite type are topologically conjugate by homeomorphisms?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite set of finite words over $A$. The (two-sided) subshift of finite type determined by $\mathcal{F}$ is the set
$$X_{\mathcal F}=\{x\in A^{\mathbb Z}: \text{no word from }\mathcal F\text{ occurs in }x\},$$
equipped with the product topology and the shift map $\sigma:X_{\mathcal F}\to X_{\mathcal F}$ defined by $(\sigma x)_n=x_{n+1}$. Two such subshifts $(X,\sigma_X)$ and $(Y,\sigma_Y)$ are said to be topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h:X\to Y$ with $h\circ\sigma_X=\sigma_Y\circ h$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given as input two finite presentations (i.e., the alphabets $A,B$ and finite forbidden-word lists $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$) of subshifts of finite type $X_{\mathcal F}\subseteq A^{\mathbb Z}$ and $X_{\mathcal G}\subseteq B^{\mathbb Z}$, decides whether $X_{\mathcal F}$ and $X_{\mathcal G}$ are topologically conjugate?
category_tag: Symbolic dynamics / subshifts of finite type
status_search_result: The decidability of topological conjugacy for two-sided one-dimensional subshifts of finite type is a long-standing open problem in symbolic dynamics, prominently listed in Boyle's open-problems survey. Partial results exist: conjugacy is decidable for one-sided SFTs and for tree-shifts of finite type, and "direct conjugacy" via N-block presentations is decidable; the multidimensional case has hardness results. The general two-sided question remains open.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: When measure isomorphism is restricted to K-automorphisms, is it a Borel equivalence relation, and can it be reduced to an S∞-action?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic probability space, and let $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish group of invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mu)$, modulo equality $\mu$-almost everywhere, endowed with the weak topology. A transformation $T \in \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ is called a $K$-automorphism if there exists a sub-$\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{K} \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ such that $T\mathcal{K} \supseteq \mathcal{K}$, $\bigvee_{n\geq 0} T^n\mathcal{K} = \mathcal{B}$ (mod $\mu$), and $\bigcap_{n\geq 0} T^{-n}\mathcal{K}$ is the trivial $\sigma$-algebra. Let $K \subseteq \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ be the set of $K$-automorphisms; it is a Borel subset. Define the measure-isomorphism equivalence relation $\cong$ on $K$ by $S \cong T$ if and only if there exists $\varphi \in \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ with $\varphi S \varphi^{-1} = T$.

(a) Is the equivalence relation $\cong$ on $K$ a Borel subset of $K \times K$?

(b) Is $\cong\!\upharpoonright\! K$ Borel reducible to an action of $S_\infty$ (the Polish group of permutations of $\mathbb{N}$)? That is, does there exist a Borel function $f: K \to Y$, where $Y$ is a standard Borel $S_\infty$-space, such that $S \cong T$ if and only if $f(S)$ and $f(T)$ lie in the same $S_\infty$-orbit?
category_tag: Descriptive set theory of measure-preserving transformations
status_search_result: Anti-classification results of Foreman–Rudolph–Weiss show that measure isomorphism on the full space of ergodic measure-preserving transformations is not Borel, and recent work by Foreman–Gerber and others extends anti-classification phenomena to weakly mixing diffeomorphisms. However, no source located explicitly resolves whether the restriction of measure isomorphism to the class of K-automorphisms is Borel or whether it is reducible to an $S_\infty$-action; the question appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: Where does Kakutani equivalence on ergodic measure-preserving transformations lie among analytic equivalence relations, and is it reducible to an S∞-action?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic probability space, and let $\mathrm{Erg}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish space of ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mu)$, equipped with the weak topology. Two transformations $T,S \in \mathrm{Erg}(X,\mu)$ are said to be Kakutani equivalent if there exist measurable sets $A \subseteq X$ (positive measure, $T$-sweeping out) and $B \subseteq X$ (positive measure, $S$-sweeping out) such that the induced transformations $T_A$ and $S_B$ are measure-theoretically isomorphic (equivalently, $T$ and $S$ have measurably isomorphic suspension flows up to a time change). This defines an analytic equivalence relation $E_K$ on $\mathrm{Erg}(X,\mu)$.

Recall the framework of Borel reducibility: for analytic equivalence relations $E$ on a Polish space $X$ and $F$ on a Polish space $Y$, one writes $E \leq_B F$ if there is a Borel function $f : X \to Y$ such that $x E x' \iff f(x) F f(x')$. An equivalence relation $E$ is said to be classifiable by an $S_\infty$-action (where $S_\infty$ is the Polish group of permutations of $\mathbb{N}$) if $E \leq_B F$ for some orbit equivalence relation induced by a Borel action of $S_\infty$ on a Polish space; equivalently, $E$ is Borel reducible to the isomorphism relation on countable structures in some countable language.

Determine the precise location of the Kakutani equivalence relation $E_K$ in the Borel-reducibility hierarchy of analytic equivalence relations. In particular, decide whether $E_K$ is Borel reducible to an orbit equivalence relation induced by a Borel action of $S_\infty$.
category_tag: Borel reducibility of equivalence relations in ergodic theory
status_search_result: Foreman, Gerber and Kunde proved that the Kakutani equivalence relation on ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformations of a standard non-atomic probability space is not a Borel set, ruling out classification by countable structures with Borel-computable invariants and showing non-reducibility to many classification problems. However, the precise location of $E_K$ among analytic equivalence relations and, in particular, whether it is Borel reducible to an $S_\infty$-orbit equivalence relation, does not appear to have been fully settled in the literature.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
context_brief: Mixing maps with completely positive entropy
original_question: For integers k ≥ 0 and n ≥ 2, is the class CPE^k(T^n) ∩ Mix of mixing C^k self-maps of the n-torus with completely positive entropy a Borel set?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ and $k\ge 0$ be integers, and let $\mathbb{T}^n=\mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ denote the $n$-dimensional torus. Equip the space $C^k(\mathbb{T}^n,\mathbb{T}^n)$ of $C^k$ self-maps of $\mathbb{T}^n$ with the standard $C^k$ topology, making it a Polish space.

For a continuous self-map $f:\mathbb{T}^n\to\mathbb{T}^n$, a topological factor is a continuous surjection $\pi:\mathbb{T}^n\to Y$ onto a compact metric space $Y$ together with a continuous map $g:Y\to Y$ such that $\pi\circ f=g\circ\pi$; the factor is non-trivial if $Y$ has more than one point. Say that $f$ has completely positive entropy if every non-trivial topological factor $(Y,g)$ of $f$ has positive topological entropy. Let
$$\mathrm{CPE}^k(\mathbb{T}^n)=\{f\in C^k(\mathbb{T}^n,\mathbb{T}^n): f\text{ has completely positive entropy}\}.$$
Let $\mathrm{Mix}\subset C^k(\mathbb{T}^n,\mathbb{T}^n)$ denote the set of topologically mixing self-maps, i.e. those $f$ such that for every pair of non-empty open sets $U,V\subset\mathbb{T}^n$ there exists $N$ with $f^{-m}(U)\cap V\neq\emptyset$ for all $m\ge N$.

Question: Is the set $\mathrm{CPE}^k(\mathbb{T}^n)\cap\mathrm{Mix}$ a Borel subset of $C^k(\mathbb{T}^n,\mathbb{T}^n)$?

The problem is posed as an open question in the surveyed problem list, and no subsequent work resolving it was found.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: Are Kakutani equivalence classes Borel sets, and if they are, what is the complexity of the isomorphism relation restricted to a Kakutani equivalence class?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic probability space, and let $\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish group of invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mu)$, endowed with the weak topology. Two transformations $T,S\in\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ are said to be Kakutani equivalent if there exist measurable sets $A,B\subseteq X$ of positive measure such that the induced transformation $T_A$ on $A$ is measure-theoretically isomorphic to the induced transformation $S_B$ on $B$ (where $T_A(x)$ is defined as $T^{n(x)}(x)$ with $n(x)$ the first return time of $x$ to $A$, and analogously for $S_B$). This defines an equivalence relation $\mathcal{K}$ on $\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ whose equivalence classes are called Kakutani equivalence classes.

(a) For which (if any) Kakutani equivalence classes $[T]_{\mathcal{K}}\subseteq\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ is $[T]_{\mathcal{K}}$ a Borel subset of $\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$?

(b) Whenever such a class is Borel, determine the descriptive set-theoretic complexity of the measure-theoretic isomorphism equivalence relation $\cong$ (where $T\cong S$ iff there exists $\varphi\in\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ with $\varphi T=S\varphi$) restricted to $[T]_{\mathcal{K}}$, in the sense of Borel reducibility among Borel/analytic equivalence relations.
category_tag: descriptive set theory of ergodic transformations
status_search_result: Recent work (Foreman–Gerber–Kunde and Foreman–Weiss) has shown that the Kakutani equivalence relation and the isomorphism relation on ergodic/weakly mixing measure-preserving transformations are not Borel (anti-classification results), but the specific question of which individual Kakutani equivalence classes are Borel and the Borel/analytic complexity of isomorphism restricted to such a class does not appear to have a complete answer in the literature, and is generally treated as an open problem.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: Let X2 be the free part of the full shift {0,1}^{Z^2} with shift action σ, let XH be the space of directed bi-infinite Hamiltonian paths in Z^2, and let Φ : (X2, σ) → (XH, σ) be a Borel equivariant map as in Theorem 3.2, inducing a Z-action T_Φ on X2. Can Φ be chosen so that for all invariant ergodic probability measures μ and ν on X2, the systems (X2, μ, σ) and (X2, ν, σ) are conjugate if and only if (X2, μ, T_Φ) and (X2, ν, T_Φ) are conjugate?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X = \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}^2}$ with the natural shift action of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, and let $X_2 \subseteq X$ denote the free part of this action (i.e. the Borel set of points with trivial stabilizer). Write $\sigma$ for the restricted $\mathbb{Z}^2$-action on $X_2$. Let $X_H \subseteq (\mathbb{Z}^2)^{\mathbb{Z}}$ denote the Polish space of directed bi-infinite Hamiltonian paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$, i.e. bijections $p:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}^2$ such that $p(n+1)-p(n)$ is a unit vector for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$; equip $X_H$ with the natural $\mathbb{Z}^2$-action by translation (shifting the image by a vector in $\mathbb{Z}^2$), also denoted $\sigma$.

Assume there exists a Borel $\mathbb{Z}^2$-equivariant map $\Phi : (X_2,\sigma) \to (X_H,\sigma)$. Such a map induces a Borel $\mathbb{Z}$-action $T_\Phi$ on $X_2$ defined by following the Hamiltonian path: for $x\in X_2$, $T_\Phi(x) = \sigma_{v(x)}(x)$, where $v(x) = \Phi(x)(1)-\Phi(x)(0) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$. Every $\sigma$-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $X_2$ is then $T_\Phi$-invariant, and ergodicity is preserved. Let $M_e$ denote the set of ergodic $\sigma$-invariant Borel probability measures on $X_2$.

Question: Can $\Phi$ be chosen so that for all $\mu,\nu \in M_e$, the measure-preserving $\mathbb{Z}^2$-systems $(X_2,\mu,\sigma)$ and $(X_2,\nu,\sigma)$ are measurably conjugate if and only if the measure-preserving $\mathbb{Z}$-systems $(X_2,\mu,T_\Phi)$ and $(X_2,\nu,T_\Phi)$ are measurably conjugate?

Web searches return related works of Chandgotia and Meyerovitch on Borel embeddings into subshifts and Hamiltonian path spaces, but no source claiming a resolution. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: Fix an ergodic measure-preserving transformation T0 on a standard probability space (X, μ), and let [T0] be its full group, consisting of bimeasurable bijections U : X → X that send each point to another point in its T0-orbit. If T1 and T2 are Bernoulli shifts with equal entropy and the same orbits as T0, does there exist T ∈ [T0] such that T1 = T T2 T^{-1}?

Let $(X,\mu)$ be a standard probability space and let $T_0 : X \to X$ be an ergodic measure-preserving automorphism. The full group of $T_0$ is
$$[T_0] = \{U : X \to X \text{ bimeasurable bijection} : U(x) \in \{T_0^n x : n \in \mathbb{Z}\} \text{ for $\mu$-a.e. } x\}.$$
Suppose $T_1$ and $T_2$ are two Bernoulli shifts on $(X,\mu)$ that have the same Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy and such that, for $\mu$-a.e. $x \in X$, the $T_1$-orbit, the $T_2$-orbit and the $T_0$-orbit of $x$ all coincide. Must there exist $T \in [T_0]$ such that
$$T_1 = T\, T_2\, T^{-1}\,?$$

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: Is the conjugation action of Aut(X, μ) on itself unbalanced in the sense of Allison and Panagiotopoulos, and if so does this remain true after restricting to ergodic transformations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mu)$ be a standard atomless probability space, and let $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish group of measure-preserving automorphisms of $(X,\mu)$ (modulo null sets), equipped with the weak topology. The group $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ acts on itself by conjugation: $g\cdot T = gTg^{-1}$.

Recall the following notion (due to Allison and Panagiotopoulos): a continuous action of a Polish group $G$ on a Polish space $Y$ is called \emph{unbalanced} if there is no Borel-definable way to assign, in a $G$-invariant manner, points of a Polish space carrying a Polish group action with a compatible bi-invariant metric; more precisely, the orbit equivalence relation $E^Y_G$ is not Borel reducible to any orbit equivalence relation induced by a continuous action of a Polish group admitting a compatible two-sided invariant metric. (Equivalently, the action exhibits a generic "unbalanced" dynamical obstruction in the sense of the games-orbits-play framework.)

Questions:
(a) Is the conjugation action of $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ on itself unbalanced?
(b) If yes, does this remain true when the action is restricted to the set of ergodic measure-preserving transformations (which is a $G_\delta$ invariant subset of $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$)?
category_tag: descriptive set theory and ergodic actions
status_search_result: A 2025 arXiv preprint titled "Unbalancedness of the conjugacy relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations" (arXiv:2510.04989) proves that the isomorphism relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations is unbalanced, i.e., it is not Borel reducible to any orbit equivalence relation arising from a Polish group action with a compatible bi-invariant metric. This answers both parts of the question affirmatively, including the restriction to ergodic transformations.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
context_brief: Topological full groups of Polish-group actions
original_question: For the topological full groups arising from continuous actions of Polish groups on compact Polish spaces, especially actions of the real line, what general structure results hold? In particular, when are these groups coarsely bounded, when do they admit a dense finitely generated subgroup, how many such groups are there, and can one classify their actions by homeomorphisms?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a Polish group (a topological group whose underlying space is separable and completely metrizable) acting continuously on a compact Polish space $X$. Define the topological full group of this action to be the group of all homeomorphisms $h \colon X \to X$ for which there exists an open cover $X = U_1 \cup \cdots \cup U_n$ and elements $g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ such that $h(x) = g_i \cdot x$ for every $x \in U_i$ and every $i$; equip this group with its natural Polish group topology.

Recall that a subset $A$ of a topological group $H$ is coarsely bounded (in the sense of Rosendal) if $A$ has finite diameter with respect to every continuous left-invariant pseudometric on $H$, equivalently, if every continuous isometric action of $H$ on a metric space has bounded $A$-orbits. The group $H$ itself is called coarsely bounded if $H$ is a coarsely bounded subset of itself.

Investigate the structure of the topological full groups arising in this way, with special emphasis on the case $G = \mathbb{R}$:

1. Characterize when such a topological full group is coarsely bounded.
2. Characterize when such a topological full group admits a dense finitely generated subgroup.
3. Determine, up to isomorphism, how many topological full groups arise in this manner.
4. Provide a classification of the continuous actions by homeomorphisms of such topological full groups on compact Polish spaces.
category_tag: Topological full groups of Polish-group actions
status_search_result: No published resolution of this cluster of questions about topological full groups associated to continuous Polish-group actions on compact Polish spaces was found. The framework of coarse boundedness (Rosendal) and topological full groups is actively studied, but no source addressing precisely these structural questions for actions of the real line was located. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: With the same notation as in Question 5.1, is there a Borel map G from Auth^{<∞}(I, λ) into the disjoint union over n of Diff(T^n, λ^n) such that each system (I, λ, T) is Kakutani equivalent to (T^n, λ^n, G(T))?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(I,\lambda)$ denote the unit interval with Lebesgue measure, and for each positive integer $n$ let $(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$ denote the $n$-dimensional torus with normalized Lebesgue measure. Let $\mathrm{Auth}^{<\infty}(I,\lambda)$ be the Polish space of invertible Lebesgue measure-preserving automorphisms of $(I,\lambda)$ with finite Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy, endowed with the weak topology, and for each $n$ let $\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$ denote the Polish space of $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{T}^n$ preserving $\lambda^n$. Two measure-preserving systems $(X,\mu,S)$ and $(Y,\nu,R)$ are said to be Kakutani equivalent if they have measurably isomorphic induced systems on positive-measure subsets, equivalently if each is isomorphic to a measurable time-change (suspension/induced map) of the other.

$$G:\mathrm{Auth}^{<\infty}(I,\lambda)\longrightarrow \bigsqcup_{n\geq 1}\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$$
such that for every $T\in\mathrm{Auth}^{<\infty}(I,\lambda)$, the system $(I,\lambda,T)$ is Kakutani equivalent to $(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n,G(T))$, where $n=n(T)$ is the dimension of the torus into which $T$ is mapped?

original_question: Does every measure-preserving action of a free group admit a uniquely ergodic topological model?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a finitely generated free group and let $F \curvearrowright (X,\mu)$ be a measure-preserving action on a standard probability space, i.e., a Borel action of $F$ on a standard Borel space $X$ preserving a Borel probability measure $\mu$. A topological model of this action is a continuous action $F \curvearrowright Y$ on a compact metrizable space $Y$ together with an $F$-invariant Borel probability measure $
u$ on $Y$ such that the systems $(X,\mu,F)$ and $(Y,
u,F)$ are measurably isomorphic. The topological model $(Y,F)$ is called uniquely ergodic if $
u$ is the unique $F$-invariant Borel probability measure on $Y$.

Question: Does every measure-preserving action of a free group on a standard probability space admit a uniquely ergodic topological model?

paper_title: Around the Gauss circle problem: Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles
context_brief: Hardy's conjecture for the Gauss circle problem
original_question: Let N(R) denote the number of integer lattice points inside the radius-R disc B(R) in the plane. Is it true that the Gauss circle problem has error term N(R) = Area(B(R)) + O(R^(1/2+o(1))) as R → ∞? Equivalently, can one prove Hardy's conjecture that the discrepancy between the lattice-point count and the disc area is bounded up to subpower factors by the square-root scale R^(1/2)?
self_contained_problem:
For a real number $R \geq 1$, let $B(R) = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : \|x\| \leq R\}$ denote the closed disc of radius $R$ centered at the origin in the Euclidean plane, and define
$$N(R) = \#\{\lambda \in \mathbb{Z}^2 : \lambda \in B(R)\},$$
the number of integer lattice points contained in $B(R)$. The area of $B(R)$ equals $\pi R^2$. Define the error term
$$E(R) = N(R) - \pi R^2.$$
Prove or disprove: for every $\varepsilon > 0$,
$$E(R) = O_\varepsilon\!\left(R^{1/2 + \varepsilon}\right) \quad \text{as } R \to \infty.$$
Equivalently, show that the discrepancy between the lattice-point count and the area of the disc is bounded, up to arbitrarily small power factors, by the square-root scale $R^{1/2}$.
status_search_result: Hardy's conjecture for the Gauss circle problem remains a famous open problem. The best known upper bound on the error term, due to Huxley (2003), is $O(R^{131/208+\varepsilon})$ with $131/208 \approx 0.6298$, far from the conjectured $1/2$. The conjectured lower bound exponent of $1/2$ matches known $\Omega$-results (Hardy, Soundararajan) up to log factors, but the upper bound remains unproved.

paper_title: Around the Gauss circle problem: Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles
original_question: As R → ∞ and then k → ∞, do the pairs (A_R(λ_j), A_R(λ_{j+k})) converge in distribution to the random vector (Y_1, Y_2) = (A_∞(r, θ), A_∞(r', θ)), where (r, θ, r') is uniformly distributed on [-1/√2, 1/√2] × [0, 2π) × [-1/√2, 1/√2]? In other words, after first taking the large-radius limit and then sending the index separation k to infinity, does the joint law of the two boundary-square intersection areas approach the random-model limit proposed in Conjecture 2.3?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{Z}^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ denote the standard integer lattice, and let $\{\lambda_j\}_{j\geq 1}$ be the increasing sequence of distinct values of $|v|^2$ for $v \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ (i.e., the squared radii on which lattice points lie). For $R>0$ and $\lambda>0$, consider the annulus $\mathcal{A}_R(\lambda) := \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : R^2 \leq |x|^2 \leq R^2 + \sqrt{\lambda}\}$, and for each lattice point $v \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ define the rescaled intersection area
$$A_R(\lambda; v) := \mathrm{Area}\bigl((v + [-1/2,1/2]^2) \cap \mathcal{A}_R(\lambda)\bigr) \cdot (\text{normalization})$$
so that $A_R(\lambda_j)$ records, in a fixed normalization, the area of intersection between a unit square centred at a lattice point of squared norm $\lambda_j$ and a thin annular strip of radius $\sim R$.

Define the random-model object $A_\infty(r,\theta)$ as the area of intersection between the unit square $[-1/2,1/2]^2$ and the half-plane region cut out by the line at signed perpendicular distance $r$ from its centre at angle $\theta$ (i.e., $\{x \in [-1/2,1/2]^2 : x\cdot(\cos\theta,\sin\theta) \leq r\}$).

Let $(r,\theta,r')$ be uniformly distributed on $[-1/\sqrt 2, 1/\sqrt 2] \times [0,2\pi) \times [-1/\sqrt 2, 1/\sqrt 2]$, and set
$$(Y_1, Y_2) := \bigl(A_\infty(r,\theta),\, A_\infty(r',\theta)\bigr).$$

Prove or disprove: for every fixed $k \geq 1$ and every $j$ in a generic range, the random vectors $(A_R(\lambda_j), A_R(\lambda_{j+k}))$ converge in distribution, in the iterated limit $R \to \infty$ followed by $k \to \infty$, to $(Y_1,Y_2)$.

context_brief: Improve the sector-length range in Proposition 6.1
original_question: In Proposition 6.1, the authors prove an asymptotic formula for the number of lattice points in the annulus Γ_R whose shifted polar data satisfy θ_λ ∈ [c,d] mod 2π and r_λ ∈ I, uniformly when the sector length |d-c| is at least R^(-1/2). Can this asymptotic be proved for a wider range of shorter sector lengths than the one established in the paper?
self_contained_problem:
Let $R \geq 2$ be a large real parameter and consider the thin annulus
$$\Gamma_R = \{ x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : R - 1 \leq |x| \leq R + 1 \}.$$
For each lattice point $\lambda \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \cap \Gamma_R$, write its polar coordinates as $\lambda = (|\lambda|\cos\theta_\lambda, |\lambda|\sin\theta_\lambda)$, and set $r_\lambda = |\lambda| - R$ (the signed radial distance to the circle of radius $R$). 

For an interval $I \subset [-1,1]$ and an arc $[c,d] \subset \mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ of length $|d - c|$, define
$$N(R; I, [c,d]) = \#\{ \lambda \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \cap \Gamma_R : \theta_\lambda \bmod 2\pi \in [c,d],\ r_\lambda \in I \}.$$
It is known that an asymptotic formula
$$N(R; I, [c,d]) \sim \frac{|d-c|\,|I|}{2\pi} \cdot R \qquad (R \to \infty)$$
holds uniformly in such intervals provided the sector length satisfies $|d-c| \geq R^{-1/2+o(1)}$ (equivalently, the arclength on the circle is at least $R^{1/2+o(1)}$).

Problem: Establish the same asymptotic for a wider range of shorter sector lengths $|d - c|$, i.e., extend the asymptotic to $|d-c| \geq R^{-1/2 - \delta}$ for some $\delta > 0$ (or as far below the threshold $R^{-1/2}$ as possible).
status_search_result: No published results were located that extend the sector-length range below the $R^{-1/2+o(1)}$ threshold for this counting asymptotic in the thin annulus. The authors themselves note the range was not optimized. Status appears unknown without further evidence.

original_question: Let G be a graph of order n with clique number omega. Is it always true that sqrt(s+(G)) <= (1 - 1/omega)n, where s+(G) is the sum of the squares of the positive adjacency eigenvalues of G?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A(G)$, and let $\lambda_1 \ge \lambda_2 \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_n$ denote the eigenvalues of $A(G)$. Define
$$s^{+}(G) = \sum_{\lambda_i > 0} \lambda_i^2,$$
the sum of the squares of the positive adjacency eigenvalues of $G$. Let $\omega = \omega(G)$ denote the clique number of $G$. Prove or disprove that for every such graph $G$,
$$\sqrt{s^{+}(G)} \le \left(1 - \frac{1}{\omega}\right) n.$$
status_search_result: The inequality is the Elphick–Wocjan conjecture (2018), a spectral strengthening of Turán's theorem. It has been verified for several classes (triangle-free graphs, weakly perfect graphs, Kneser graphs, conference graphs, certain strongly regular and Ramanujan graphs, and almost all graphs), and no counterexamples have been found computationally up to 40 vertices, but the conjecture remains open in general as of recent works (2024–2025).

original_question: Let G be a graph with m edges, let n+(G) be the number of positive adjacency eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, and let ell = min{n+(G), omega(G)}. Must the inequality sum_{i=1}^{ell} lambda_i(G)^2 <= 2(1 - 1/omega(G))m always hold?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with $m$ edges. Let $A(G)$ be its adjacency matrix and let $\lambda_1(G) \ge \lambda_2(G) \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_n(G)$ be the eigenvalues of $A(G)$. Define:
- $n^+(G)$ = the number of positive eigenvalues of $A(G)$ (counted with multiplicity);
- $\omega(G)$ = the clique number of $G$ (the size of a largest complete subgraph);
- $\ell = \min\{n^+(G),\, \omega(G)\}$.

Determine whether the inequality
$$\sum_{i=1}^{\ell} \lambda_i(G)^2 \;\le\; 2\!\left(1 - \frac{1}{\omega(G)}\right) m$$
holds for every such graph $G$.
status_search_result: The conjecture has been verified for several graph classes (weakly perfect graphs, Kneser graphs, Johnson graphs, certain strongly regular graphs). A related conjecture of Wocjan-Elphick-Anekstein involving the vector chromatic number was recently proved via conic programming, but the formulation with clique number $\omega(G)$ stated here is not established in general and is reported as still open in recent literature.

original_question: For all sufficiently large n, is the n-vertex planar 3-uniform hypergraph with maximum spectral radius uniquely the one whose shadow graph is K_2 joined with P_{n-2}?
self_contained_problem:
Let H be a 3-uniform hypergraph on n vertices, i.e., V(H) is a finite set of size n and E(H) is a collection of 3-element subsets of V(H). The shadow (2-section) of H is the simple graph G on the same vertex set V(H) in which two distinct vertices u,v are adjacent if and only if {u,v} is contained in some edge of H. Call H planar if its shadow graph is planar.

The spectral radius ρ(H) of H is defined as the spectral radius of its adjacency tensor A(H), namely the largest value λ for which there exists a nonnegative, nonzero vector x ∈ R^n with (A(H) x^2)_i = λ x_i^2 for every i ∈ V(H), where (A(H) x^2)_i = Σ_{{i,j,k} ∈ E(H)} 2 x_j x_k.

For graphs F and G on disjoint vertex sets, the join F ∨ G is the graph obtained from the disjoint union of F and G by adding every edge between V(F) and V(G). Let K_2 denote the complete graph on 2 vertices and P_{n-2} the path on n-2 vertices. Let H* denote the unique 3-uniform hypergraph on n vertices whose shadow equals K_2 ∨ P_{n-2} and whose edge set consists of all triples {u,v,w} ⊆ V that span a triangle in K_2 ∨ P_{n-2}.

Prove or disprove: there exists n_0 such that for every integer n ≥ n_0, among all planar 3-uniform hypergraphs on n vertices, H* is the unique hypergraph attaining the maximum value of ρ(·).
status_search_result: A survey on spectral theory of hypergraphs (2025) describes Ellingham–Lu–Wang's result for the outer-planar case and lists the planar 3-uniform analogue as an open conjecture. No paper found that resolves the planar case.
