paper_title: Imaging with LINC-NIRVANA, the Fizeau interferometer of the Large Binocular Telescope: state of the art and open problems
original_question: How can image reconstruction for LINC-NIRVANA, the Fizeau interferometer of the Large Binocular Telescope, be extended from a space-invariant point-spread-function model to a space-variant point-spread-function model? In this setting, multiple deconvolution combines several interferometric images of the same astronomical target; the point-spread function can change with baseline orientation, adaptive-optics correction, and position in the field of view. A self-contained solution should estimate point-spread-function variation across the field from available star images, partition the image into domains where each point-spread function can be treated as approximately space-invariant, correct boundary effects inside those domain reconstructions, and recombine the results into a mosaic.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a Fizeau-type optical interferometric imaging system consisting of two circular apertures of diameter D separated by a baseline of length B, mounted on a common alt-azimuth platform so that the baseline orientation with respect to the sky can take prescribed angles θ_1,…,θ_p. For each baseline orientation θ_k the instrument records, on a two-dimensional detector of N×N pixels, a noisy image

   g_k(x) = (H_k * f)(x) + n_k(x),    x ∈ Ω ⊂ ℝ^2,  k = 1,…,p,

of the same astronomical target with intensity distribution f(x) ≥ 0. The blurring is assumed to be linear, but the point-spread function (PSF) H_k(x, y) depends not only on the baseline orientation θ_k and on the residual adaptive-optics correction in the field, but also on the position x in the field of view, so that

   (H_k * f)(x) = ∫ H_k(x, y) f(y) dy,

i.e. H_k is space-variant. The system can produce simultaneous images of a finite set of natural reference stars located at positions {x_j} inside the field of view, from which samples H_k(x_j, ·) of the PSF are available.

Devise a multiple-image deconvolution procedure for estimating f from the data {g_k}_{k=1}^p which:

(i) from the star images {H_k(x_j, ·)}, builds a model of the spatial variation of each H_k(x, ·) across the field;

(ii) partitions the field of view Ω into a collection of overlapping subdomains Ω_1,…,Ω_M on each of which H_k can be approximated, with prescribed accuracy, by a space-invariant PSF H_k^{(m)};

(iii) on each subdomain Ω_m performs a multiple-image deconvolution of the restricted data, using a method (for instance a maximum-likelihood iteration for Poisson noise such as the Ooe–Richardson–Lucy or Scaled Gradient Projection scheme) that correctly handles the boundary effects produced by the truncation of the convolution to Ω_m;

(iv) recombines the local reconstructions {f̂_m}_{m=1}^M into a single mosaic estimate f̂ of f over Ω in a way that ensures continuity and consistency in the overlap regions.

Provide a fully specified algorithm together with the convergence and accuracy guarantees required for it to constitute a practical solution of the space-variant multiple-image reconstruction problem for such a Fizeau interferometer.
status_search_result: The space-invariant multiple-image deconvolution problem for LINC-NIRVANA has been treated by several works (Bertero–Boccacci and collaborators), including methods for combining images with different baseline orientations, accelerated multi-image Richardson–Lucy/Scaled Gradient Projection iterations, blind deconvolution variants, and explicit reduction of boundary effects. Extension to space-variant PSFs via field partitioning and mosaicking has been proposed and prototyped in simulations, but a fully validated, general-purpose algorithm with rigorous accuracy/convergence guarantees does not yet appear to be established in the literature, so the overall problem is best classified as partially solved.

paper_title: Imaging with LINC-NIRVANA, the Fizeau interferometer of the Large Binocular Telescope: state of the art and open problems
original_question: How can LINC-NIRVANA image reconstruction recover high-dynamic-range astronomical scenes in which bright point sources are superimposed on diffuse faint structure, such as a bright star lying on top of a diffuse cloud in young stellar object observations? Existing adaptive regularization handles separated bright and faint components only when there is a large brightness difference and angular separation, so the unresolved case is reconstruction when the bright source and diffuse emission overlap.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a Fizeau interferometric imaging system that produces multiple long-exposure images $g_j$, $j=1,\dots,p$, of the same astronomical scene at different parallactic angles, each modeled as

$$g_j = K_j f + b_j + n_j,$$

where $f \ge 0$ is the unknown sky brightness distribution defined on a discrete pixel grid, $K_j$ is a known linear shift-invariant imaging operator (convolution with the corresponding point spread function of the interferometric baseline at orientation $j$), $b_j$ is a known background, and $n_j$ is Poisson photon noise. Assume the target $f$ has the form

$$f = c\,\delta_{x_0} + h,$$

i.e.\ the superposition of one (or several) bright point sources of unknown intensity $c>0$ located at known positions $x_0$ and a non-negative diffuse component $h \ge 0$ representing extended faint structure, such that the integrated flux ratio between the point source and the diffuse component is very large (high dynamic range) and the angular support of $h$ contains $x_0$ (the bright source overlaps spatially with the diffuse emission rather than being well separated from it).

Design a reconstruction algorithm — for instance a regularized maximum-likelihood method of the form

$$\min_{c \ge 0,\, h \ge 0}\; \sum_{j=1}^p D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\big(g_j \,\|\, K_j(c\,\delta_{x_0}+h)+b_j\big) + \mu\, R(h),$$

with $D_{\mathrm{KL}}$ the Kullback–Leibler (Csiszár) divergence appropriate for Poisson data and $R$ a smoothness-promoting regularizer acting on the diffuse component — that, in the overlapping high-dynamic-range regime, simultaneously recovers (i) the intensity $c$ of the bright point source and (ii) the diffuse structure $h$ underneath it, without the point source's reconstruction artifacts contaminating the recovered diffuse emission. Establish convergence and stability properties of the resulting iterative scheme, and prove (or characterize) the conditions on the dynamic range, on the point spread functions $\{K_j\}$, and on the regularization functional $R$ under which the diffuse component beneath the bright source can be faithfully recovered.
category_tag: Inverse problems in astronomical image reconstruction
status_search_result: Follow-up work has developed split-component reconstruction methods that model the target as a bright point source plus a diffuse component, with a smoothness-enforcing regularizer on the diffuse part and Poisson likelihood. Simulations on stellar jets have shown success in some regimes, but the fully overlapping case in which the bright source sits inside (rather than next to) the diffuse emission remains only partially addressed — methods exist as heuristics validated on simulations, without general theoretical guarantees on dynamic-range limits and recovery fidelity.

paper_title: Imaging with LINC-NIRVANA, the Fizeau interferometer of the Large Binocular Telescope: state of the art and open problems
original_question: How can blind or myopic deconvolution for LINC-NIRVANA be made mathematically sound and computationally efficient when the point-spread functions are unknown or only partly known? The formulation should jointly estimate the astronomical object and the point-spread functions under physical constraints such as nonnegativity, band-limiting, and known Strehl-ratio information, and should exploit the relationship between this deconvolution problem and nonnegative matrix factorization to obtain convergence analysis and practical reconstruction algorithms.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-frame imaging model in which p observed images g_j : Z^2 -> R_{>=0} (j = 1, ..., p) of a common astronomical object f : Z^2 -> R_{>=0} are produced by convolution with unknown point-spread functions (PSFs) K_j : Z^2 -> R_{>=0}, possibly corrupted by Poisson noise:

   g_j ≈ Poisson(K_j * f),   j = 1, ..., p.

The object f and each PSF K_j are required to satisfy the following physical constraints:
  (i) Nonnegativity: f >= 0, K_j >= 0.
  (ii) Normalization / flux conservation: sum_x K_j(x) = 1.
  (iii) Band-limiting: the Fourier transforms of the K_j are supported in a prescribed bounded region Ω ⊂ R^2 (the optical transfer function support of a Fizeau interferometric aperture).
  (iv) Strehl-ratio information: a known lower bound s_j ∈ (0,1] on the Strehl ratio of K_j, defined as the ratio of the peak of the in-focus PSF to that of the corresponding diffraction-limited PSF.

The joint blind (or myopic, when partial knowledge of K_j is available) deconvolution problem is to recover (f, K_1, ..., K_p) from the data {g_j} by minimizing a data-fidelity functional (e.g. the Kullback–Leibler divergence)

   J(f, K_1, ..., K_p) = sum_{j=1}^p D_{KL}(g_j || K_j * f)

subject to constraints (i)–(iv).

Tasks:

(a) Reformulate this constrained joint estimation problem as a nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) problem, identifying the matrices whose nonnegative factorization corresponds to (f, K_1, ..., K_p) and showing how the constraints (i)–(iv) translate into constraints on the factors.

(b) Using this reformulation, design a computationally efficient iterative algorithm (for example, of multiplicative-update or alternating-projection type) that enforces all constraints (i)–(iv) at every iteration.

(c) Provide a rigorous convergence analysis: prove that the iterates produce a monotonically nonincreasing sequence of objective values and that limit points are stationary points of J on the constraint set.

(d) Establish identifiability/uniqueness conditions (up to natural ambiguities) under which the joint reconstruction of f and the K_j is well-posed given the constraints (i)–(iv).

The problem remains generally regarded as open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Densities
original_question: Let A⊆N and let upper_d_α(A) be the upper α-density of A for α≥−1. Because α↦upper_d_α(A) is increasing, define upper_d_∞(A)=lim_{α→∞} upper_d_α(A). Characterize this limit in terms of intrinsic properties of A. In particular, determine its relationship to the upper uniform, or Banach, density u(A), and to inf{u(B): B⊆N and d(AΔB)=0}, where Δ is symmetric difference and d is asymptotic density.
self_contained_problem:
For a subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ and a real parameter $\alpha\ge -1$, define the upper $\alpha$-density of $A$ by
$$\overline{d}_\alpha(A)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{\sum_{k\in A,\,k\le n}k^\alpha}{\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^\alpha}.$$
It is known that the map $\alpha\mapsto \overline{d}_\alpha(A)$ is non-decreasing on $[-1,\infty)$, so the limit
$$\overline{d}_\infty(A)=\lim_{\alpha\to\infty}\overline{d}_\alpha(A)$$
exists. Recall also the upper uniform (Banach) density
$$u(A)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\max_{k\ge 0}\frac{|A\cap[k+1,k+n]|}{n},$$
and the asymptotic (natural) density $d$ on subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ where it is defined. Let
$$\mathcal{S}(A)=\{B\subseteq\mathbb{N}:d(A\triangle B)=0\},$$
where $\triangle$ denotes symmetric difference.

It is straightforward that $\overline{d}_\infty(A)\le u(A)$ and that every $B\in\mathcal{S}(A)$ shares all $\alpha$-densities with $A$, hence
$$\overline{d}_\infty(A)\le \inf\{u(B):B\in\mathcal{S}(A)\}.$$

Problem: Characterize $\overline{d}_\infty(A)$ in terms of intrinsic combinatorial or structural properties of the set $A$. In particular, determine the precise relationship between $\overline{d}_\infty(A)$, the upper Banach density $u(A)$, and the quantity $\inf\{u(B):B\in\mathcal{S}(A)\}$; decide whether either of the inequalities above can be equalities in general, and if not, give examples and a complete description of the gap.
status_search_result: Searches on upper α-densities and their limit as α→∞ in relation to Banach density (work of Grekos and collaborators) did not surface any publication characterizing $\overline{d}_\infty(A)$ or deciding the inequalities with $u(A)$ and $\inf\{u(B):B\in\mathcal{S}(A)\}$. Related papers discuss equivalent definitions of Banach density and general frameworks for upper/lower densities, but the specific characterization problem appears not to have been resolved in the accessible literature.

paper_title: Open Problems on Densities
original_question: Let A⊆N. For B⊆A, define lower and upper uniform, or Banach, densities by taking the limiting lower and upper proportions of B in long intervals, namely through the limits as s→∞ of the liminf and limsup over k of B(k+1,k+s)/s. Characterize the uniform-density set R_u(A)={(upper_u(B), lower_u(B)): B⊆A} for a fixed set A.
self_contained_problem:
For a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and integers $1 \le m \le n$, write $X(m,n) = |X \cap [m,n]|$. For real $s \ge 1$ define
$$\underline{\alpha}_s(X) = \liminf_{k\to\infty} X(k+1, k+s), \qquad \overline{\alpha}_s(X) = \limsup_{k\to\infty} X(k+1, k+s).$$
The lower uniform (Banach) density and upper uniform (Banach) density of $X$ are
$$\underline{u}(X) = \lim_{s\to\infty} \frac{\underline{\alpha}_s(X)}{s}, \qquad \overline{u}(X) = \lim_{s\to\infty} \frac{\overline{\alpha}_s(X)}{s}$$
(these limits exist by subadditivity/superadditivity).

Fix a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$. Describe the set
$$R_u(A) = \{(\overline{u}(B), \underline{u}(B)) : B \subseteq A\} \subseteq [0,1]^2.$$
That is, give a characterization of which pairs $(x,y) \in [0,1]^2$ arise as $(\overline{u}(B), \underline{u}(B))$ for some subset $B$ of $A$.

The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Densities
original_question: Let A={a_1<a_2<...}⊆N have positive asymptotic density d, so that n/a_n→d. Does there always exist a subset B={b_1<b_2<...}⊆A with positive asymptotic density d_0, where 0<d_0≤d, such that n/b_n converges to d_0 more rapidly than n/a_n converges to d? Equivalently, can one find such a B and a function f(n)→0 with b_n=n/d_0(1+o(f(n)))? In particular, can this be done with f(n)=1/log n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be a set of positive integers with positive asymptotic density $d$, meaning $\lim_{n\to\infty} n/a_n = d \in (0,1]$.

(a) Does there always exist a subset $B=\{b_1<b_2<\cdots\}\subseteq A$ having positive asymptotic density $d_0$ with $0<d_0\le d$, such that the convergence $n/b_n\to d_0$ is faster than the convergence $n/a_n\to d$? Equivalently, do there exist such a $B$ and a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to(0,\infty)$ with $f(n)\to 0$ for which
$$b_n=\frac{n}{d_0}\bigl(1+o(f(n))\bigr)\qquad(n\to\infty)?$$

(b) In particular, can this be achieved with the explicit rate $f(n)=1/\log n$, i.e. can one always find $B\subseteq A$ of positive asymptotic density $d_0\in(0,d]$ with
$$b_n=\frac{n}{d_0}\Bigl(1+o\!\left(\tfrac{1}{\log n}\right)\Bigr)?$$

Either prove that such a subset $B$ always exists, or exhibit a set $A$ of positive asymptotic density for which no such $B$ exists.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a published resolution of this problem on faster convergence of $n/b_n$ to the density for subsets of a set of positive asymptotic density. Related work on uniform/Banach density and on densities of subsets by Grekos and collaborators exists, but no specific source confirming the problem as solved (in either direction, including the case $f(n)=1/\log n$) was identified.

paper_title: Open Problems on Densities
original_question: Given a set M of positive integers, call S⊆N an M-set if a,b∈S implies a−b∉M. Determine μ(M)=sup_S upper_d(S), where S ranges over all M-sets and upper_d(S) is the upper asymptotic density of S. The problem is especially open beyond known particular cases when |M|=3.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$. For a nonempty set $M$ of positive integers, call a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ an $M$-set if for all $a, b \in S$ one has $a - b \notin M$. The upper asymptotic density of a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is defined by
$$\overline{d}(S) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{|S \cap \{1, 2, \dots, n\}|}{n}.$$
Define
$$\mu(M) := \sup\{\overline{d}(S) : S \subseteq \mathbb{N} \text{ is an } M\text{-set}\}.$$
Determine $\mu(M)$ as an explicit function of $M$. In particular, give a closed-form (or otherwise effective) evaluation of $\mu(M)$ for every three-element set $M = \{m_1, m_2, m_3\}$ of positive integers.
status_search_result: Motzkin's problem of determining μ(M) is known to be solved for |M| ≤ 2 (Cantor–Gordon), with only partial results for |M| = 3 (e.g., families like {1, j, k} treated by Haralambis, Gupta–Tripathi, and others). Recent works (2020–2024) continue to give partial progress, and the general case |M| = 3 remains open.

original_question: For a strict triangular norm T on [0, 1], let F_T be the smallest class of functions from [0, 1] to [0, 1] that contains the identity function and is closed under T, under the standard negation n(x) = 1 - x, and under limits of comonotone sequences. Let T_P be the product t-norm, for which F_TP is the class of all Borel measurable functions from [0, 1] to [0, 1]. Let T_H be the Hamacher product T_H(x, y) = xy / (x + y - xy) for (x, y) not equal to (0, 0), and call a strict t-norm nearly Hamacher when it is isomorphic to T_H by an isomorphism that also generates the standard negation. Does there exist a strict t-norm T such that F_T is different from both F_TP and F_TH? If F_T equals F_TH for a strict t-norm T, must T be nearly Hamacher?
self_contained_problem:
A triangular norm (t-norm) is a function $T:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ that is associative, commutative, non-decreasing in each argument, and satisfies $T(1,x)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$. A t-norm $T$ is called strict if it is continuous and strictly increasing on $(0,1]^2$. Two important examples are:
- the product t-norm $T_P(x,y)=xy$;
- the Hamacher product $T_H(x,y)=\dfrac{xy}{x+y-xy}$ for $(x,y)\neq(0,0)$, with $T_H(0,0)=0$.

Let $n:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ denote the standard negation $n(x)=1-x$. A sequence of functions $(f_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$, with $f_k:[0,1]\to[0,1]$, is called comonotone if for every pair of indices $i,j$ and every $x,y\in[0,1]$, $(f_i(x)-f_i(y))(f_j(x)-f_j(y))\geq 0$.

For a strict t-norm $T$, define $\mathcal{F}_T$ to be the smallest class of functions from $[0,1]$ to $[0,1]$ that
(i) contains the identity function $\mathrm{id}(x)=x$;
(ii) is closed under $T$, i.e.\ if $f,g\in\mathcal{F}_T$ then the pointwise function $T(f,g)$ belongs to $\mathcal{F}_T$;
(iii) is closed under composition with the standard negation $n$;
(iv) is closed under pointwise limits of comonotone sequences whose pointwise limit exists.

It is known that $\mathcal{F}_{T_P}$ equals the class of all Borel measurable functions $[0,1]\to[0,1]$.

A strict t-norm $T$ is called nearly Hamacher if there exists an order-preserving bijection $\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ such that $T(x,y)=\varphi^{-1}(T_H(\varphi(x),\varphi(y)))$ and additionally $\varphi$ generates the standard negation, i.e.\ $\varphi^{-1}(1-\varphi(x))=1-x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$.

Answer the following:
(a) Does there exist a strict t-norm $T$ such that $\mathcal{F}_T\neq\mathcal{F}_{T_P}$ and $\mathcal{F}_T\neq\mathcal{F}_{T_H}$?
(b) If $\mathcal{F}_T=\mathcal{F}_{T_H}$ for some strict t-norm $T$, must $T$ necessarily be nearly Hamacher?

The current status could not be verified from publicly available sources.

original_question: Is the following characterization true: an Archimedean triangular norm T is 1-Lipschitz with respect to the L_p norm if and only if every additive generator of T is the p-th power of a convex function?
self_contained_problem:
A triangular norm (t-norm) is a binary operation $T:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ that is commutative, associative, non-decreasing in each argument, and satisfies $T(x,1)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$. A t-norm $T$ is called Archimedean if it is continuous and $T(x,x)<x$ for all $x\in(0,1)$. Every continuous Archimedean t-norm admits a representation $T(x,y)=t^{(-1)}(t(x)+t(y))$ via a continuous additive generator, i.e. a continuous strictly decreasing function $t:[0,1]\to[0,\infty]$ with $t(1)=0$, where $t^{(-1)}$ is the pseudo-inverse of $t$.

For $p\in[1,\infty)$, the t-norm $T$ is said to be $1$-Lipschitz with respect to the $L_p$-norm if
$$\bigl|T(x_1,y_1)-T(x_2,y_2)\bigr|\;\le\;\bigl(|x_1-x_2|^p+|y_1-y_2|^p\bigr)^{1/p}$$
for all $x_1,x_2,y_1,y_2\in[0,1]$.

A function $f:[0,1]\to[0,\infty]$ is said to be the $p$-th power of a convex function if there exists a convex function $g:[0,1]\to[0,\infty]$ such that $f(x)=g(x)^p$ for all $x\in[0,1]$.

Decide whether the following characterization holds: an Archimedean t-norm $T$ is $1$-Lipschitz with respect to the $L_p$-norm if and only if every additive generator of $T$ is the $p$-th power of a convex function.
status_search_result: The characterization appears to have been established in subsequent work on $k$-$l_p$-Lipschitz t-norms, where Archimedean $1$-$l_p$-Lipschitz t-norms are shown to be exactly those whose additive generators are $p$-convex (equivalently, $p$-th powers of convex functions), with necessary and sufficient conditions provided.

original_question: Archimedean copulas are copulas generated by additive generators. For dimension 2, every associative 2-copula C: [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] with C(x, x) < x for all x in (0, 1) is Archimedean. Is there an algebraic characterization of Archimedean 3-copulas, and more generally of Archimedean n-copulas for n > 2?
self_contained_problem:
An n-copula is a function C: [0,1]^n → [0,1] that is the joint cumulative distribution function of a random vector (U_1, ..., U_n) each of whose marginals is uniform on [0,1]; equivalently, C is grounded, has uniform univariate marginals, and is n-increasing. An n-copula C is called Archimedean if there exists a continuous, strictly decreasing function φ: [0,1] → [0,∞] with φ(1) = 0 (called an additive generator) such that
   C(u_1, ..., u_n) = φ^{[-1]}(φ(u_1) + ··· + φ(u_n))   for all (u_1,...,u_n) ∈ [0,1]^n,
where φ^{[-1]} denotes the pseudo-inverse of φ. A 2-copula C is associative if C(C(x,y),z) = C(x, C(y,z)) for all x,y,z ∈ [0,1]; it is known that every associative 2-copula C satisfying C(x,x) < x for all x ∈ (0,1) is Archimedean.

Problem. Provide an algebraic characterization of Archimedean 3-copulas, and more generally of Archimedean n-copulas for n > 2; that is, find a set of purely algebraic (functional-equation type) conditions on an n-copula C that are equivalent to C being Archimedean.
status_search_result: Several algebraic-style characterizations of n-dimensional Archimedean copulas have been proposed (e.g., the Jouini–Clemen characterization, and characterizations via n-ary associativity in the sense of Post, alongside differential and diagonal characterizations). Associative n-copulas in the Post sense have been shown to be n-ary extensions of associative 2-copulas with special constraints, and associative copulas decompose as ordinal sums of Archimedean copulas and the minimum copula. A definitive, universally accepted purely algebraic characterization analogous to the 2-dimensional case still does not appear to be settled, so the problem can be considered partially solved.

original_question: Every n-copula C can be represented by measure-preserving transformations phi_i: [0, 1] -> [0, 1] for i = 1, ..., n through C(x1, ..., xn) = lambda(phi_1^{-1}([0, x1]) intersect ... intersect phi_n^{-1}([0, xn])), where lambda is Lebesgue measure on the Borel subsets of [0, 1]. Which particular properties of an n-copula C correspond to representations in which the n transformations are all ergodic, or all weakly mixing?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\lambda$ denote Lebesgue measure on the Borel subsets of $[0,1]$. A measurable map $\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ is measure-preserving if $\lambda(\varphi^{-1}(B))=\lambda(B)$ for every Borel set $B\subseteq[0,1]$. Such a $\varphi$ is ergodic if every Borel set $B$ with $\varphi^{-1}(B)=B$ satisfies $\lambda(B)\in\{0,1\}$, and weakly mixing if for all Borel $A,B\subseteq[0,1]$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\bigl|\lambda(\varphi^{-k}A\cap B)-\lambda(A)\lambda(B)\bigr|=0.$$

An $n$-copula is a function $C:[0,1]^n\to[0,1]$ that is the joint distribution function of an $n$-tuple of random variables each uniformly distributed on $[0,1]$. It is known that every $n$-copula $C$ admits a representation

paper_title: Open problems posed at the eighth international conference on fuzzy set theory and applications
original_question: A fuzzy implication is a function I: [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] that is non-increasing in its first component, non-decreasing in its second component, satisfies I(1, 0) = 0, and satisfies I(0, x) = I(x, 1) = 1 for every x in [0, 1]. A t-norm T is an associative, commutative, non-decreasing operation on [0, 1] with neutral element 1. For a given continuous t-norm T, characterize all fuzzy implications I satisfying the law of importation I(x, I(y, z)) = I(T(x, y), z) for all x, y, z in [0, 1]. Since commutativity of T makes this law imply the exchange principle I(x, I(y, z)) = I(y, I(x, z)), does the exchange principle conversely imply the existence of a t-norm T for which the law of importation holds? If so, is T unique; if not, give an example and characterize the fuzzy implications for which the converse is true.
self_contained_problem:
A fuzzy implication is a function I:[0,1]^2 → [0,1] that is non-increasing in its first argument, non-decreasing in its second argument, and satisfies I(1,0)=0 together with I(0,x)=I(x,1)=1 for every x∈[0,1]. A t-norm is a binary operation T:[0,1]^2 → [0,1] that is associative, commutative, non-decreasing in each argument, and has 1 as neutral element. Given a t-norm T, a fuzzy implication I is said to satisfy the law of importation with respect to T (denoted LI(T)) if
   I(x, I(y, z)) = I(T(x,y), z) for all x,y,z ∈ [0,1].
A fuzzy implication I satisfies the exchange principle (EP) if
   I(x, I(y, z)) = I(y, I(x, z)) for all x,y,z ∈ [0,1].

Address the following:

(a) For an arbitrary (in particular, continuous) t-norm T, give a complete characterization of all fuzzy implications I that satisfy LI(T).

(b) Since the commutativity of T implies that LI(T) entails EP, investigate the converse: does every fuzzy implication I satisfying the exchange principle satisfy LI(T) for some t-norm T? If so, is such a T uniquely determined by I? If not, exhibit a counterexample and characterize precisely the class of fuzzy implications for which the converse implication does hold (and for which uniqueness of T holds).
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on both parts. For (a), characterizations of fuzzy implications satisfying LI(T) have been obtained for the minimum t-norm, continuous Archimedean t-norms, ordinal sums thereof, and in particular for fuzzy implications with continuous natural negation under any continuous t-norm T (Massanet–Torrens, IEEE TFS 2016, and follow-up work through 2021). For (b), it has been shown that LI is strictly stronger than EP and that EP does not in general imply the existence of a t-norm T with LI(T); partial classes for which the converse holds have been identified. A fully general characterization remains incomplete, so the overall problem is partially solved.

original_question: Let p > 0 and 0 < q < infinity. Let w: (0, infinity) -> R be positive and Lebesgue integrable, and define W(x) = integral from 0 to x of w(s) ds. For positive measurable weights u and v, and for a real continuous strictly monotone function g with inverse g^{-1}, define the generalized weighted mean operator of a positive Lebesgue integrable function f by M^g_w f(x) = g^{-1}((1 / W(x)) * integral from 0 to x of w(t) g(f(t)) dt). Find necessary and sufficient conditions on u and v and establish a class of functions g such that the inequality (integral_0^infinity u(x) (M^g_w f(x))^q dx)^(1/q) <= C (integral_0^infinity v(x) f(x)^p dx)^(1/p) holds for every f >= 0 with a positive finite constant C. Also estimate the best possible constant C in this inequality.
self_contained_problem:
Let $p>0$ and $0<q<\infty$. Let $w:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a positive Lebesgue integrable function, and define
$$W(x)=\int_0^x w(s)\,ds,\qquad x>0.$$
For a real-valued continuous strictly monotone function $g$ on the range of positive measurable functions (with inverse $g^{-1}$), and for a positive Lebesgue integrable function $f:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, define the generalized weighted mean operator
$$M_w^g f(x)=g^{-1}\!\left(\frac{1}{W(x)}\int_0^x w(t)\,g(f(t))\,dt\right),\qquad x>0.$$
Let $u,v:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be positive measurable weights.

(a) Find necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(u,v)$, together with a class of admissible functions $g$, such that there exists a finite positive constant $C$ for which
$$\left(\int_0^\infty u(x)\bigl(M_w^g f(x)\bigr)^q\,dx\right)^{1/q}\le C\left(\int_0^\infty v(x)\,f(x)^p\,dx\right)^{1/p}$$
holds for every measurable $f\ge 0$.

(b) Estimate the best possible (smallest) constant $C$ in the above inequality.
status_search_result: A web search located related work on inequalities involving generalized weighted means (e.g., Sbert–Poch, J. Inequal. Appl. 2016) and the well-studied two-weight Hardy-type inequalities, but no source was found that fully resolves the problem in this generality (arbitrary continuous strictly monotone $g$, general $0<p$ and $0<q<\infty$, with sharp constant). The status appears to be unresolved in this full form, but this could not be definitively verified.

paper_title: Complex symmetric operators
original_question: Let a bounded operator T on a complex Hilbert space be complex symmetric if T = C T* C for some conjugation C. In finite dimensions, every complex symmetric operator is known to be unitarily equivalent to a direct sum of irreducible complex symmetric matrices and matrices formed as the direct sum of A and A^t, where A is irreducible and is not itself complex symmetric, and irreducible means not unitarily equivalent to a nontrivial direct sum. What is the corresponding infinite-dimensional analogue of this finite-dimensional decomposition theorem for complex symmetric operators?
self_contained_problem:
Let H be a separable complex Hilbert space and let B(H) denote the algebra of bounded linear operators on H. A conjugation on H is an antilinear map C : H → H that is involutive (C² = I) and isometric (⟨Cx, Cy⟩ = ⟨y, x⟩ for all x, y ∈ H). A bounded operator T ∈ B(H) is called complex symmetric if there exists a conjugation C on H such that T = C T* C. An operator A ∈ B(H) is called irreducible if it is not unitarily equivalent to a nontrivial orthogonal direct sum B ⊕ D of two bounded operators on nonzero Hilbert spaces.

In the finite-dimensional case (dim H < ∞), every complex symmetric operator T is unitarily equivalent to an orthogonal direct sum of blocks of two types:
 (i) irreducible complex symmetric matrices, and
 (ii) blocks of the form A ⊕ A^t, where A is an irreducible matrix that is not itself complex symmetric and A^t denotes its transpose with respect to some orthonormal basis.

Problem: Formulate and prove the analogous structural decomposition theorem for complex symmetric operators on an infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space. That is, determine whether every complex symmetric operator T ∈ B(H) admits a canonical decomposition (in some appropriate sense, e.g., as a direct sum or direct integral) into "irreducible" complex symmetric pieces together with pieces of the form A ⊕ CA*C where A is irreducible and not complex symmetric, and identify the precise formulation under which such a decomposition holds.
status_search_result: The infinite-dimensional analogue of the finite-dimensional decomposition theorem for complex symmetric operators is regarded as an open structural problem. Subsequent work (e.g., Liu's 2019 paper on reducible and irreducible approximation of complex symmetric operators in J. London Math. Soc.) addresses related approximation questions but does not produce a full canonical decomposition theorem analogous to the finite-dimensional one. No source verifying a complete solution was found.

paper_title: Complex symmetric operators
original_question: Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let T be a bounded complex symmetric operator on H, meaning T = C T* C for some conjugation C. Must T have an invariant subspace that is both proper and nontrivial, that is, a subspace other than {0} and H that is mapped into itself by T?
self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. A conjugation on $H$ is a map $C:H\to H$ that is antilinear, isometric (i.e., $\langle Cx,Cy\rangle=\langle y,x\rangle$ for all $x,y\in H$), and involutive ($C^2=I$). A bounded linear operator $T$ on $H$ is called complex symmetric if there exists a conjugation $C$ on $H$ such that $T=CT^*C$.

Question: Must every bounded complex symmetric operator $T$ on $H$ possess a nontrivial proper invariant closed subspace, i.e., a closed subspace $M\subset H$ with $M\neq\{0\}$ and $M\neq H$ such that $T(M)\subseteq M$?
status_search_result: The general invariant subspace problem for bounded operators on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space remains open (a 2023 preprint of Enflo claiming a positive solution has not been broadly verified). The restriction of the problem to the class of complex symmetric operators is not known to be settled either; it is highlighted as an open question in surveys on complex symmetric operators.

paper_title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
original_question: Let G_{bi,mult}(2n,r) be the class of bipartite r-regular multigraphs on 2n vertices and let lambda(k,n,r) be the minimum, over that class, of the number of k-matchings. Is the lower matching conjecture true, namely that for every k = 1,...,n, lambda(k,n,r) is at least binom(n,k)^2 times ((nr-k)/nr)^(rn-k) times (kr/n)^k?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{bi,mult}}(2n,r)$ denote the class of bipartite $r$-regular multigraphs on $2n$ vertices (with two color classes of size $n$ each, parallel edges allowed). For a graph $G$ and integer $k\ge 0$, let $m_k(G)$ be the number of matchings of $G$ of size $k$ (i.e., sets of $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint edges). Define
$$\lambda(k,n,r) := \min_{G\in\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{bi,mult}}(2n,r)} m_k(G).$$
Prove or disprove: for every integers $n\ge 1$, $r\ge 1$, and every $k\in\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$,
$$\lambda(k,n,r) \;\ge\; \binom{n}{k}^{\!2}\left(\frac{nr-k}{nr}\right)^{\!rn-k}\!\left(\frac{kr}{n}\right)^{\!k}.$$
status_search_result: The Lower Matching Conjecture of Friedland (for bipartite r-regular (multi)graphs) was proved by Péter Csikvári in "Lower matching conjecture, and a new proof of Schrijver's and Gurvits's theorems" (arXiv:1406.0766, 2014; published in J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2017). Csikvári proves a slightly stronger statement using local weak (Benjamini–Schramm) convergence, statistical physics, and graph covers.

paper_title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
original_question: For an infinite r-regular graph G, let h_G(p) be its p-matching entropy, where p is the limiting density of vertices covered by matchings. Is h_G(p) always at most the p-matching entropy of a countable disjoint union of copies of K_{r,r}, for every p in [0,1]?
self_contained_problem:
Let $r\ge 1$ be an integer. For a finite graph $H$, a matching of $H$ is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges, and $m_k(H)$ denotes the number of matchings of $H$ with exactly $k$ edges. 

Let $G$ be an infinite, locally finite, $r$-regular graph. Choose any sequence $(G_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of finite induced subgraphs of $G$ whose vertex sets exhaust $V(G)$ and such that the proportion of vertices of $G_n$ that are $r$-regular in $G_n$ tends to $1$. For $p\in[0,1]$, define the $p$-matching entropy of $G$ by
$$h_G(p) \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{|V(G_n)|}\,\log m_{\lfloor p\,|V(G_n)|/2\rfloor}(G_n),$$
assuming the limit exists and is independent of the chosen exhaustion (which is the case under mild homogeneity hypotheses such as $G$ being a Cayley graph or a graph admitting an invariant random regular structure).

Let $K_{r,r}^\infty$ denote the countable disjoint union of copies of the complete bipartite graph $K_{r,r}$, and let $h_{K_{r,r}^\infty}(p)$ be its $p$-matching entropy, defined analogously (which exists and equals $\tfrac{1}{2r}\log m_{\lfloor pr\rfloor}(K_{r,r})$ extended continuously to $p\in[0,1]$).

Prove or disprove: for every infinite $r$-regular graph $G$ (for which $h_G$ is defined) and every $p\in[0,1]$,
$$h_G(p) \;\le\; h_{K_{r,r}^\infty}(p).$$
status_search_result: The finite Upper Matching Conjecture of Friedland–Krop–Markström, from which the asymptotic version follows, was proved for all sufficiently large $d$-regular bipartite graphs by Davies, Jenssen, Perkins and Roberts (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 2021), and Ilinca–Kahn (2013) established asymptotic forms. Earlier, Friedland and collaborators verified the asymptotic matching conjectures in various special cases. The full conjecture for all (not necessarily bipartite, possibly infinite) $r$-regular graphs and all $p\in[0,1]$ does not appear to be completely resolved, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

paper_title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
original_question: In the non-bipartite regular multigraph setting of the source, let omega(k,n,r) denote the minimum number of k-matchings in the relevant r-regular multigraph class. For fixed r >= 2 and fixed density p in (0,2/3), does omega(k,n,r) grow exponentially in n for every integer k in the interval [pn, 2n/3], and what are sharp or useful lower bounds for that exponential growth rate?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer $r \geq 2$, let $\mathcal{G}(n,r)$ denote the class of $r$-regular multigraphs on $n$ vertices (with $rn$ even, allowing parallel edges but no loops). A $k$-matching in a multigraph is a set of $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint edges. For integers $k$ with $0 \leq k \leq n/2$, define
$$\omega(k,n,r) = \min_{G \in \mathcal{G}(n,r)} m_k(G),$$
where $m_k(G)$ is the number of $k$-matchings in $G$.

Fix $r \geq 2$ and a real number $p \in (0, 2/3)$. Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $c = c(p,r) > 1$ such that for every integer $k$ with $pn \leq k \leq 2n/3$,
$$\omega(k,n,r) \geq c^{n}$$
for all sufficiently large $n$. Moreover, determine sharp (or useful) lower bounds on the exponential growth rate $\liminf_{n\to\infty} \omega(k,n,r)^{1/n}$ as a function of $r$ and the density $k/n$.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not find a definitive resolution of this conjecture about exponential growth of the minimum number of k-matchings in r-regular multigraphs for densities k/n in (0,2/3). Related results exist on perfect matchings and matchings at density 1/2 in regular graphs, but the specific conjecture for the interval [pn, 2n/3] does not appear to be resolved in the literature retrievable through search.

paper_title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
original_question: With mu_{k,n} = min_{B in Psi_{2n}} haf_k(B), is the uniform complete-graph matrix (1/(2n-1))A(K_{2n}) always a minimizer, so that mu_{k,n} = haf_k((1/(2n-1))A(K_{2n})) for every k = 2,...,n? The source explicitly resolves this proposed exact formula negatively for k = n and sufficiently large n.
self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and consider symmetric matrices of order 2n. Denote by Ψ_{2n} the set of all symmetric 2n × 2n matrices B = (b_{ij}) with nonnegative entries, zero diagonal, and all row sums equal to 1 (the set of symmetric doubly stochastic matrices with zero diagonal). For an integer 2 ≤ k ≤ n, define the k-th hafnian of B by

   haf_k(B) = (1/k!) ∑ b_{i_1 j_1} b_{i_2 j_2} ⋯ b_{i_k j_k},

where the sum runs over all ordered k-tuples of pairwise disjoint unordered pairs {i_1,j_1}, …, {i_k,j_k} ⊂ {1, …, 2n} (so haf_k(B) counts, with weights given by products of entries, the partial matchings of size k in the weighted complete graph on 2n vertices defined by B). Let

   μ_{k,n} = min_{B ∈ Ψ_{2n}} haf_k(B).

Let A(K_{2n}) denote the adjacency matrix of the complete graph K_{2n} (all off-diagonal entries 1, diagonal 0). Then (1/(2n−1)) A(K_{2n}) lies in Ψ_{2n}. Determine whether, for every integer n ≥ 2 and every k with 2 ≤ k ≤ n,

   μ_{k,n} = haf_k( (1/(2n−1)) A(K_{2n}) );

that is, whether the uniform matrix (1/(2n−1)) A(K_{2n}) is always a minimizer of haf_k over Ψ_{2n}.

This disproof is recorded in surveys on matchings in regular graphs discussing the asymptotic matching conjecture.

paper_title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
original_question: For arbitrary infinite r-regular graphs that need not be bipartite, what is the correct analog of the asymptotic lower matching conjecture for p-matching entropy at densities p in [0,2/3]? In particular, what explicit lower-bound function should h_G(p) satisfy in that non-bipartite setting?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be an infinite $r$-regular graph (not necessarily bipartite). For a finite $r$-regular graph $H$ on $n$ vertices, let $m_k(H)$ denote the number of matchings of $H$ of size $k$, and for $p \in [0,1]$ define the normalized matching entropy
$$ h_H(p) = \frac{1}{n}\ln m_{\lfloor pn/2\rfloor}(H). $$
For an infinite $r$-regular graph $G$, define $h_G(p)$ as the limit of $h_{H_n}(p)$ along any Benjamini–Schramm convergent sequence of finite $r$-regular graphs $H_n \to G$ (assume such a limit exists and is independent of the sequence).

For the bipartite case, the asymptotic lower matching conjecture asserts that, for every $p\in[0,1]$,
$$ h_G(p) \;\ge\; \frac{1}{2}\Big( p\ln r - p\ln p - 2(1-p)\ln(1-p) + (r-p)\ln(1-p/r)\Big), $$
with equality for the infinite $r$-regular tree.

Problem: Determine the correct analog of this asymptotic lower matching inequality for arbitrary infinite $r$-regular graphs $G$ that need not be bipartite, valid at least for matching densities $p \in [0,2/3]$. Specifically, find an explicit function $L_r(p)$ (depending only on $r$ and $p$) such that
$$ h_G(p) \;\ge\; L_r(p) \qquad \text{for all } p\in[0,2/3] $$
holds for every infinite $r$-regular graph $G$, and which is sharp on a natural extremal $r$-regular (non-bipartite) graph.
status_search_result: Searches indicate that the asymptotic lower matching conjecture and its sharp form are established (and partially proved) for bipartite r-regular graphs via results connected to Schrijver's and Gurvits's theorems, but a precise non-bipartite analog of the lower bound for the p-matching entropy h_G(p) on the range p ∈ [0,2/3] has not been formulated explicitly nor proved in the literature available. The non-bipartite case remains open.

paper_title: Problemas abiertos en series de Fourier de Jacobi-Sobolev
original_question: In the general theory of orthogonal polynomials defined by Sobolev inner products that may include derivative-evaluation terms, determine which analytic properties of standard orthogonal polynomials are preserved, what algebraic properties the new polynomials have, whether a parallel Hilbert-space operator theory exists, and which Pade approximants are associated with these polynomials and how those approximants behave.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mu_0, \mu_1, \dots, \mu_m$ be (possibly signed or discrete) Borel measures on the real line, and let $\{c_{j,k}\}$ be a finite collection of real coefficients with associated points $\{x_{j,k}\} \subset \mathbb{R}$. Define a Sobolev-type inner product on the space of real polynomials by
$$\langle p, q\rangle_S \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{m} \int_{\mathbb{R}} p^{(k)}(x)\, q^{(k)}(x)\, d\mu_k(x) \;+\; \sum_{j,k} c_{j,k}\, p^{(k)}(x_{j,k})\, q^{(k)}(x_{j,k}),$$
and let $\{S_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ denote the corresponding sequence of monic orthogonal polynomials (assumed to exist and be unique). Investigate the following four questions for general families of such inner products:

(a) Analytic properties. Which analytic properties of standard orthogonal polynomials (asymptotic behavior on and off the support, $n$th-root and strong asymptotics, location and limiting distribution of zeros, Mehler–Heine type formulas, convergence and summability of associated Fourier expansions) carry over to the polynomials $\{S_n\}$, and under what conditions on the measures and derivative-evaluation terms?

(b) Algebraic properties. What algebraic relations (recurrence relations replacing the three-term recurrence, Christoffel–Darboux type kernels, differential or difference equations, ladder operators, connection formulas) are satisfied by $\{S_n\}$?

(c) Operator theory. Does there exist a parallel Hilbert-space operator theory: a natural self-adjoint or symmetric operator on a suitable Hilbert space completion of the polynomials whose spectral analysis encodes $\{S_n\}$, analogous to the role of the Jacobi matrix and multiplication operator in the classical theory?

(d) Padé approximation. Which Padé (or multipoint Padé / Hermite–Padé) approximants are naturally associated with $\{S_n\}$ and the Cauchy/Stieltjes transforms of the measures $\mu_k$, and what are their convergence, error, and pole-distribution properties?
status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers on Sobolev orthogonal polynomials emphasize that general analytic, algebraic, operator-theoretic and Padé-approximation aspects remain active areas with major unresolved problems. In particular, the lack of a three-term recurrence and Christoffel–Darboux formula in the Sobolev setting, the non-symmetry of the multiplication operator, and the convergence of Sobolev–Fourier expansions are explicitly identified as open problems in current literature.

original_question: Let w be the classical Jacobi weight on [-1,1], dmu(x) = (1-x)^alpha (1+x)^beta dx with alpha,beta > -1, and define a discrete Sobolev-type inner product by <f,g> = integral f(x)g(x)dmu(x) plus the finite sum over k=1..K and i=0..N_k of M_{k,i} f^(i)(a_k) g^(i)(a_k), with mass points a_k in (-1,1) and nonnegative coefficients M_{k,i}. Establish upper estimates for the associated orthogonal polynomials, adapting the known exterior-mass-point Jacobi-Sobolev Fourier-series methods to the interior-mass setting where the Christoffel-Darboux formulas develop singularities at the mass points.
self_contained_problem:
Let $d\mu(x) = (1-x)^\alpha (1+x)^\beta\, dx$ be the classical Jacobi measure on $[-1,1]$, with parameters $\alpha,\beta > -1$. Fix points $a_1,\dots,a_K \in (-1,1)$ (interior mass points), nonnegative integers $N_1,\dots,N_K$, and nonnegative real coefficients $M_{k,i}$ for $1 \le k \le K$ and $0 \le i \le N_k$. Define the discrete Sobolev-type inner product on the space of polynomials by
$$\langle f,g\rangle \;=\; \int_{-1}^{1} f(x)g(x)\,d\mu(x) \;+\; \sum_{k=1}^{K}\sum_{i=0}^{N_k} M_{k,i}\, f^{(i)}(a_k)\, g^{(i)}(a_k).$$
Let $\{Q_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ denote the sequence of monic orthogonal polynomials with respect to $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$. Establish uniform upper estimates on $[-1,1]$ for $|Q_n(x)|$ (suitably normalized, e.g., relative to the standard Jacobi polynomials $P_n^{(\alpha,\beta)}$ and to Jacobi-type weight factors), of the type known when the mass points lie outside $[-1,1]$, but valid in the present interior-mass-point regime. The principal difficulty to be overcome is that the Christoffel–Darboux kernel associated with $d\mu$ develops singularities at the points $a_k \in (-1,1)$, which obstructs the direct adaptation of the exterior-mass-point Fourier-series methods. Provide estimates strong enough to support a convergence/divergence analysis of the associated Fourier–Sobolev series expansions.
status_search_result: Recent literature on Jacobi–Sobolev orthogonal polynomials addresses Fourier series, Cohen-type inequalities, and relative asymptotics when mass points lie in the support of the measure, but no source located establishes the desired uniform upper estimates for the interior-mass-point case in the generality posed. The problem appears to remain open, with progress mainly in related directions (exterior mass points, asymptotics, Cohen-type inequalities).

paper_title: Problemas abiertos en series de Fourier de Jacobi-Sobolev
context_brief: Generalized Jacobi weights in Sobolev products
original_question: Let w(x)=h(x)(1-x)^alpha(1+x)^beta product_{j=1}^N |x-t_j|^gamma_j on [-1,1], where alpha,beta,gamma_j > -1, the points t_j are distinct points in (-1,1), h is continuous and positive on [-1,1], and the modulus of continuity condition w(h,delta) delta^(-1) is integrable on (0,2). For the discrete Sobolev-type inner product formed from w(x)dx and finitely many derivative-evaluation mass terms, extend the known upper estimates for orthogonal polynomials with generalized Jacobi weights to this Sobolev-type setting.
self_contained_problem:
Let $w$ be a generalized Jacobi weight on $[-1,1]$ of the form
$$w(x) = h(x)(1-x)^{\alpha}(1+x)^{\beta}\prod_{j=1}^{N}|x-t_j|^{\gamma_j},$$
where $\alpha,\beta,\gamma_j>-1$, $t_1,\dots,t_N$ are distinct points in $(-1,1)$, and $h$ is continuous and strictly positive on $[-1,1]$ with modulus of continuity $\omega(h,\delta)$ satisfying $\int_0^2 \omega(h,\delta)\,\delta^{-1}\,d\delta < \infty$.

Fix points $c_1,\dots,c_M\in\mathbb{R}$, nonnegative integers $k_1,\dots,k_M$, and positive masses $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_M>0$. Define the discrete Sobolev-type inner product
$$\langle f,g\rangle_S = \int_{-1}^{1} f(x)g(x)\,w(x)\,dx + \sum_{i=1}^{M}\lambda_i f^{(k_i)}(c_i)g^{(k_i)}(c_i),$$
and let $\{q_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ denote the sequence of polynomials orthonormal with respect to $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_S$.

For ordinary orthonormal polynomials $\{p_n\}$ associated with generalized Jacobi weights of this type, pointwise upper estimates of the form
$$|p_n(x)|\,\sqrt{w(x)}\,\big(\sqrt{1-x^2}+1/n\big)^{1/2} \leq C$$
(with appropriate modifications near the endpoints and the singular points $t_j$) are known.

Problem: Extend these pointwise upper estimates to the Sobolev-type orthonormal polynomials $q_n$ associated with $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_S$; that is, establish analogous uniform pointwise bounds for $q_n(x)$ on $[-1,1]$ in terms of $n$, the weight $w$, and the discrete Sobolev data $(c_i,k_i,\lambda_i)$.
status_search_result: Pointwise upper estimates for orthonormal polynomials with generalized Jacobi weights are classical (Badkov, Nevai), and asymptotic/upper-bound results exist for several Jacobi-Sobolev settings. However, no source located clearly establishes the analogous uniform pointwise upper estimates for discrete Sobolev-type inner products with a fully general generalized Jacobi weight including interior singularities $|x-t_j|^{\gamma_j}$. The problem appears to remain open in this generality.

paper_title: Problemas abiertos en series de Fourier de Jacobi-Sobolev
context_brief: Laguerre-Sobolev estimates with mass location cases
original_question: For Laguerre-Sobolev-type orthogonal polynomials on an unbounded support, use the classical estimates for Laguerre polynomials to derive estimates for the Sobolev-type polynomials, distinguishing the case where the mass is located at the boundary of the support from the case where the mass is located in the positive real half-line. Also derive estimates for the corresponding kernels using the Sobolev extension of the Christoffel-Darboux formula.
self_contained_problem:
For a parameter $\alpha>-1$, let $\{L_n^{(\alpha)}\}_{n\ge 0}$ denote the classical Laguerre orthogonal polynomials, orthogonal on $[0,\infty)$ with respect to the weight $d\mu_\alpha(x)=x^{\alpha}e^{-x}\,dx$. Fix $c\ge 0$, $\lambda\ge 0$, and $N\ge 0$, and consider the discrete Sobolev-type inner product
$$\langle f,g\rangle_S \;=\; \int_0^{\infty} f(x)\,g(x)\,x^{\alpha}e^{-x}\,dx \;+\; N\,f'(c)\,g'(c),$$
acting on real polynomials. Let $\{S_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ be the sequence of monic polynomials orthogonal with respect to $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_S$, and let
$$K_n^S(x,y)=\sum_{k=0}^n \frac{S_k(x)S_k(y)}{\langle S_k,S_k\rangle_S}$$
denote the corresponding reproducing (Christoffel–Darboux) kernels.

(a) Using the known asymptotic and pointwise estimates for the classical Laguerre polynomials $L_n^{(\alpha)}$ on $[0,\infty)$, derive sharp uniform and pointwise estimates for $S_n(x)$ on compact subsets of $[0,\infty)$ and on the oscillatory and Plancherel–Rotach regions, treating separately:
 (i) the boundary mass case $c=0$;
 (ii) the interior mass case $c>0$.

(b) Using a Sobolev-type extension of the Christoffel–Darboux formula adapted to $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_S$, derive the corresponding estimates for the kernels $K_n^S(x,y)$ in both cases (i) and (ii).
status_search_result: No specific resolution of these Laguerre–Sobolev estimates with mass at the boundary versus in the interior was located. Several partial results exist in the literature on Laguerre–Sobolev-type polynomials (asymptotics, Mehler–Heine formulas), but a complete answer covering both mass-location regimes together with Christoffel–Darboux-type kernel bounds does not appear to be settled, so the status is taken as unknown.

paper_title: Problemas abiertos en series de Fourier de Jacobi-Sobolev
context_brief: Partial sums and projection boundedness in Jacobi-Sobolev norm
original_question: For Fourier expansions in Jacobi-Sobolev polynomials associated with the non-discrete Sobolev inner product with two continuous measures, obtain estimates for the nth Fourier partial sums and analyze whether the Fourier projection operator is bounded with respect to the Jacobi-Sobolev norm.
self_contained_problem:
Fix parameters $\alpha,\beta>-1$ and consider the Jacobi measure $d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}(x)=(1-x)^{\alpha}(1+x)^{\beta}\,dx$ on $(-1,1)$. Let $d\nu_{\gamma,\delta}(x)=(1-x)^{\gamma}(1+x)^{\delta}\,dx$ be a second Jacobi-type measure on $(-1,1)$ (with $\gamma,\delta>-1$), and define the non-discrete Jacobi–Sobolev inner product
$$\langle f,g\rangle_S \;=\; \int_{-1}^{1} f(x)\,g(x)\,d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}(x)\;+\;\lambda\int_{-1}^{1} f'(x)\,g'(x)\,d\nu_{\gamma,\delta}(x),\qquad \lambda>0,$$
together with its associated Sobolev norm $\|f\|_S^2=\langle f,f\rangle_S$. Let $\{q_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ denote the sequence of orthonormal polynomials with respect to $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_S$, and for a function $f$ in the corresponding Sobolev space let
$$S_n f \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{n}\langle f,q_k\rangle_S\, q_k$$
be the $n$-th Fourier–Sobolev partial sum operator (the orthogonal projection onto the subspace of polynomials of degree at most $n$).

(a) Obtain sharp asymptotic estimates for $\|S_n f\|_S$ in terms of $f$ and $n$.

(b) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the parameters $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)$ (and on the function space in which $f$ lies) under which the family of projection operators $\{S_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ is uniformly bounded with respect to the Jacobi–Sobolev norm $\|\cdot\|_S$, and consequently characterize the convergence $S_n f\to f$ in this norm.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has addressed related Jacobi–Sobolev settings: complete characterizations of uniform boundedness of Fourier partial sum operators have been obtained in the discrete Jacobi–Sobolev case and in discrete–continuous Jacobi–Sobolev spaces, and convergence/boundedness results are known for coherent pairs of Jacobi measures. However, a fully general treatment for the non-discrete Sobolev inner product with two arbitrary continuous Jacobi measures does not appear to be completely settled, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
original_question: Let Φ^t: Ω → Ω be an open dynamical system, with t discrete for maps and continuous for flows, and let H ⊂ Ω be a hole through which trajectories are absorbed. For an initial measure μ0, let Ω_t be the survivor set of points whose trajectories do not enter H during (0,t], let P(t)=μ0(Ω_t) be the survival probability, and let γ be the exponential escape rate when it exists. If μ∞ is a conditionally invariant limiting survivor measure and ν is the natural invariant measure on the repeller, how generally does the escape-rate formula γ = sum of the positive Lyapunov exponents minus the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy h_KS, with the quantities computed with respect to ν, remain valid, especially beyond uniformly hyperbolic maps and for flows?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi^t:\Omega\to\Omega$ be a dynamical system on a state space $\Omega$, where $t$ ranges over the non-negative integers (in the discrete-time case) or the non-negative reals (in the continuous-time case). Fix a measurable subset $H\subset\Omega$ (the "hole") and an initial probability measure $\mu_0$ on $\Omega$. For $t\ge 0$ define the survivor set
$$\Omega_t=\{x\in\Omega:\Phi^s(x)\notin H\ \text{for all}\ 0<s\le t\}$$
and the survival probability $P(t)=\mu_0(\Omega_t)$. When the limit
$$\gamma=-\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{1}{t}\log P(t)$$
exists and is positive, it is called the (exponential) escape rate. Assume there exists a conditionally invariant limiting survivor measure $\mu_\infty$ (i.e. a probability measure satisfying $\Phi^t_*\mu_\infty=e^{-\gamma t}\mu_\infty$ on $\Omega\setminus H$) and an associated natural invariant measure $\nu$ supported on the noninvasive repeller (the set of points whose forward and backward orbits avoid $H$). Let $\{\lambda_i\}$ denote the Lyapunov exponents of $\nu$ and let $h_{KS}(\nu)$ denote its Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy.

Determine the most general class of open dynamical systems for which the escape rate formula
$$\gamma=\sum_{i:\lambda_i>0}\lambda_i-h_{KS}(\nu)$$
holds. In particular, establish (or refute) its validity beyond the setting of uniformly hyperbolic maps, including non-uniformly hyperbolic maps with singularities and continuous-time flows.
category_tag: open dynamical systems and escape rates
status_search_result: The escape-rate formula is established as an equality for uniformly hyperbolic systems and for systems admitting Markov tower extensions with spectral gaps (e.g., work generalizing Eckmann–Ruelle/Pesin to open systems, including results of Demers–Wright–Young and others). General upper bounds on the escape rate hold for diffeomorphisms with singularities and arbitrary holes, but matching lower bounds—and hence equality—are not known in full generality, and the case of flows and broad non-uniformly hyperbolic settings remains only partially settled.

paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
original_question: In open dynamical systems, including billiards with distortion, nonuniform hyperbolicity, or no hyperbolicity, how should the position of a hole be chosen in order to maximize or minimize escape, where the measure of escape may be the escape rate γ, the full survival probability function P(t), or another suitably defined escape statistic?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, T, \mu)$ be a measure-preserving dynamical system, where $T : M \to M$ is a (possibly non-uniformly hyperbolic, or distorted, or non-hyperbolic) map and $\mu$ is an invariant probability measure. Given a measurable subset $H \subset M$ called the "hole", define the survival set up to time $t$ by
$$S_t(H) = \{ x \in M : T^k(x) \notin H \text{ for all } 0 \le k \le t \},$$
and let the survival probability function be $P_H(t) = \mu(S_t(H))$. When the limit exists, define the escape rate through the hole $H$ by
$$\gamma(H) = -\lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log P_H(t).$$
The setting includes the case where $T$ is the billiard map associated with a planar billiard table (possibly with distortion, non-uniform hyperbolicity, or no hyperbolicity), and $H$ is a small region of the phase space (e.g., an arc on the boundary).

Problem. Consider a class $\mathcal{H}$ of admissible holes (for instance, all holes of a fixed $\mu$-measure $\varepsilon > 0$). Determine, in terms of the dynamics of $T$ and the geometry of $M$:
(a) which holes $H^* \in \mathcal{H}$ maximize the escape rate $\gamma(H)$, and which minimize it;
(b) more generally, which holes maximize or minimize the survival probability function $P_H(t)$ (for all $t$, or pointwise in $t$), or another suitably defined statistic of escape.
Provide a characterization of optimal hole positions covering systems with distortion, non-uniform hyperbolicity, and the absence of hyperbolicity.
status_search_result: For strongly chaotic (uniformly hyperbolic) systems with small holes, partial results characterize hole-position effects: e.g., faster escape through holes containing a periodic point of minimal period (Bunimovich–Yurchenko and follow-ups), and there are escape-rate formulas via periodic orbits. However, for general open systems with distortion, non-uniform hyperbolicity, or no hyperbolicity, a complete characterization of optimal hole placement remains open; recent works (e.g., on intermittent maps with shrinking holes, physical billiards) continue to address special cases.

paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
original_question: Does every triangular billiard contain at least one periodic orbit, and more generally does every polygonal billiard contain at least one periodic orbit when arbitrary directions of motion are allowed?
self_contained_problem:
A polygonal billiard is the dynamical system describing the motion of a point particle inside a planar polygon $P$: the particle travels in straight lines at unit speed and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at the boundary, with trajectories that hit a vertex being undefined. A trajectory is called periodic if, after finitely many reflections, the particle returns to its initial position with its initial direction of motion.

Prove or disprove the following statements:

(a) Every triangle $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ admits at least one periodic billiard trajectory.

(b) More generally, every simple polygon $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ admits at least one periodic billiard trajectory.

Here arbitrary initial directions of motion are allowed (the question is not about a fixed directional flow; for rational polygons one can construct directions whose flow has no periodic orbits, but this does not preclude the existence of periodic orbits in some other direction).
status_search_result: The existence of a periodic billiard orbit is classically known for rational polygons and for acute and right triangles (Fagnano's orbit and its analogues). For obtuse triangles, R. E. Schwartz proved that every obtuse triangle whose largest angle is at most 100° has a periodic orbit, and computer-assisted work has pushed this bound further (towards roughly 112.5°), but the general case for arbitrary obtuse triangles, and a fortiori the case of arbitrary simple polygons, remains open as of 2026.

paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
original_question: In open polygonal billiards, is the asymptotic survival probability P(t) as t tends to infinity entirely determined by neighborhoods of non-escaping periodic orbits?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a polygon in $\mathbb{R}^2$, possibly with one or several edges (or open subsets of edges) designated as "holes." A billiard trajectory in $P$ is the path of a point particle moving with unit speed in straight lines inside $P$ and reflecting elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) on the non-hole portion of $\partial P$. A trajectory escapes if it meets a hole; otherwise it survives forever. Equip the phase space (unit tangent bundle over $P$) with the standard Liouville measure $\mu$, normalized to be a probability measure on the set of initial conditions. Define the survival probability
$$P(t) = \mu\big(\{(x,v) : \text{the trajectory starting at }(x,v)\text{ has not escaped by time }t\}\big).$$
A periodic orbit of the closed billiard in $P$ is called non-escaping if it (and a neighborhood of it in phase space) avoids the holes for all times.

Question: Is the asymptotic behavior of $P(t)$ as $t \to \infty$ entirely determined by the dynamics in arbitrarily small phase-space neighborhoods of the set of non-escaping periodic orbits? Equivalently, do the neighborhoods of non-escaping periodic orbits give the leading-order contribution to $P(t)$ as $t \to \infty$ for every open polygonal billiard?
status_search_result: The question is stated as an explicit open problem in surveys on open billiards. Numerical evidence in irrational polygons indicates a $C/t$ decay attributable to periodic orbits, and in rational polygons without periodic orbits the survival ends in finite time, but no proof in general is known. No recent literature appears to establish or refute the conjecture.

paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
context_brief: reinjection near marginally unstable periodic orbits
original_question: For stadium-like billiards containing marginally unstable periodic orbits, can one comprehensively characterize their dynamical properties, including escape properties, in terms of reinjection dynamics, meaning the way trajectories that leave the neighborhood of such periodic orbits are returned to that neighborhood?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a stadium-like planar billiard table, i.e. a bounded domain whose boundary consists of two parallel straight segments joined by two focusing (e.g. circular) arcs, and consider the associated billiard flow (a point particle moving in straight lines inside $Q$ and reflecting elastically off $\partial Q$) together with its Poincaré (collision) map on the boundary phase space. Such a table possesses a one-parameter family of "bouncing-ball" periodic orbits, which are marginally unstable periodic orbits (MUPOs): orbits whose linearized Poincaré map is parabolic (eigenvalues equal to $1$), so that nearby trajectories drift away polynomially rather than exponentially. A trajectory that leaves a small neighborhood $U$ of such a MUPO eventually returns to $U$; the induced first-return map from $U^c$ back to $U$ is called the reinjection map, and the statistics of return positions, return times, and angles constitute the reinjection dynamics.

Now place a "hole" (an open subset of $\partial Q$ or of the phase space) and consider the open billiard: study the survival probability $P(t)=\mu\{x:\text{the trajectory of }x\text{ has not entered the hole by time }t\}$ and related escape quantities (escape rate, asymptotic decay law, conditionally invariant measures).

Problem. Provide a comprehensive characterization of the dynamical properties of MUPOs in stadium-like billiards — in particular the asymptotic behavior of $P(t)$ and other escape statistics for the corresponding open systems — purely in terms of the reinjection dynamics, i.e. derive the escape law, its prefactors, and the structure of conditionally invariant measures from quantitative properties (distribution of return times, return locations, and angles) of the reinjection map associated with the MUPO family.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about giving a complete characterization of escape and other dynamical properties of MUPOs in stadium-like billiards in terms of reinjection dynamics. Searches return work establishing the prevalence of MUPOs and partial results on escape (e.g., polynomial decay of survival probability, rotating leaks in the stadium), but no comprehensive characterization in terms of reinjection dynamics appears in the literature. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
original_question: In mushroom billiards and similar mixed-phase-space billiards, how can one characterize escape at the boundary between regular and chaotic regions, including the possible slowing of survival decay by sticky marginally unstable periodic orbits and by the regular-chaotic boundary itself when the hole lies in the chaotic region?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a mushroom billiard: a planar domain consisting of a semicircular "cap" attached to a rectangular "stem", in which a point particle moves in straight lines and reflects elastically off the boundary. The phase space of this dynamical system is mixed: it contains an invariant regular region (corresponding to trajectories that remain in the cap forever, integrable in nature) and an invariant chaotic region; these two regions are separated by a sharp boundary in phase space. The chaotic region typically contains families of marginally unstable periodic orbits (MUPOs), namely periodic orbits with neutral linear stability that occupy zero volume in phase space but cause intermittent "sticky" dynamics, and a single MUPO family is known to contribute a term proportional to 1/t to the survival probability.

Now make the billiard "open" by removing a small arc (a "hole") from the boundary, located in the chaotic component. Let P(t) denote the survival probability, i.e. the measure (with respect to a natural invariant measure on the chaotic component, e.g. the Liouville measure conditioned on the chaotic region) of initial conditions whose forward trajectory has not yet hit the hole by time t.

Problem. Characterize the escape dynamics associated with the boundary between the regular and chaotic regions in mushroom billiards (and analogous mixed-phase-space billiards). In particular:

(a) Quantify how the asymptotic decay of P(t) as t → ∞ is influenced by the family of marginally unstable periodic orbits embedded in the chaotic component.
(b) Quantify the additional contribution to slowing of the decay coming from the regular–chaotic boundary itself, independently of the MUPO contribution.
(c) Provide asymptotic formulas (with explicit constants depending on the geometry of the mushroom, the position and size of the hole, and the invariant measure) for P(t) that simultaneously account for both effects.
status_search_result: Partial results exist: it is known that a single MUPO family contributes a C/t term to the survival probability in mushroom billiards, and stickiness near the regular-chaotic boundary has been studied numerically and heuristically (e.g., "How sticky is the chaos/order boundary?" and related works on intermittent billiards). However, a complete characterization of escape at the regular–chaotic boundary, including a rigorous asymptotic for P(t) that combines MUPO stickiness with boundary stickiness, does not appear to have been obtained, so the problem remains open in its general form.

paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
original_question: For billiard-like models used in statistical mechanics, including Lorentz gases with infinitely many convex scatterers and Ehrenfest gases with infinitely many polygons, what minimum microscopic dynamical properties are required to obtain a chaotic macroscopic limit, such as recurrence, ergodicity, a normal diffusion coefficient, or convergence to a limiting Wiener diffusion process?
self_contained_problem:
Consider billiard-like models used in statistical mechanics, namely:

(a) Lorentz gases: a point particle moving with unit speed in the plane (or in $\mathbb{R}^d$) in the complement of a locally finite, infinite configuration of pairwise disjoint strictly convex scatterers (e.g., congruent disks placed periodically or randomly), reflecting elastically off the boundaries of the scatterers.

(b) Ehrenfest gases: a point particle moving with unit speed in the plane in the complement of a locally finite, infinite configuration of pairwise disjoint polygonal scatterers, again with elastic reflection.

Both models define a measure-preserving microscopic dynamical system (the billiard flow, or its discrete collision map preserving the natural invariant measure on the collision space). Under appropriate space–time rescaling $X_n(t) = \varepsilon_n q(t/\varepsilon_n^2)$ (where $q(s)$ is the position of the particle at microscopic time $s$ and $\varepsilon_n \to 0$), one asks whether the rescaled trajectory $X_n$ converges in law to a Brownian motion (Wiener process) with a finite, nondegenerate diffusion matrix.

Identify the minimal qualitative dynamical hypotheses on the microscopic billiard dynamics that are sufficient to guarantee each of the following "chaotic" macroscopic-limit conclusions:

1. Recurrence of the particle's position process.
2. Ergodicity of the microscopic dynamics with respect to its natural invariant measure.
3. Existence and finiteness of a normal (i.e., nonzero and finite) diffusion coefficient $D = \lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t}\, \mathbb{E}\|q(t)-q(0)\|^2$.
4. Convergence under diffusive rescaling to a limiting Wiener process.

That is, find the weakest natural conditions on the configuration of scatterers and on the resulting billiard map/flow (e.g., positive Lyapunov exponents, hyperbolicity, finite horizon, decay-of-correlations rates, mixing properties) under which each of (1)–(4) holds.
status_search_result: The question is posed as a broad open problem about identifying minimal dynamical hypotheses ensuring recurrence, ergodicity, normal diffusion, and Wiener-process limits in infinite Lorentz and Ehrenfest gases. While many partial results exist (e.g., Bunimovich–Sinai–Chernov central limit theorems for periodic finite-horizon Lorentz gases, Szász–Varjú for infinite-horizon, recurrence results by Schmidt and Conze, and partial results on polygonal channels by Dettmann, Bálint and others), no comprehensive characterization of the minimal sufficient conditions appears in the literature, and the polygonal/Ehrenfest case in particular remains largely open. The problem is generally treated as still open.

paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
original_question: For an open quantum billiard, modeled by the Helmholtz equation (∇^2 + k^2)ψ = 0 with Dirichlet boundary conditions and resonance solutions whose wavenumber k has negative imaginary part, is the number of resonant states with Re(k_n) < k and Im(k_n) > -C for a positive constant C of order k^(d_H+1) as k tends to infinity, where d_H is the partial Hausdorff dimension of the classical non-escaping set?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an open quantum billiard in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d\ge 2$) consisting of a region containing a finite collection of compact obstacles such that classical trajectories may escape to infinity. The stationary wavefunctions $\psi$ satisfy the Helmholtz equation
$$(\nabla^2 + k^2)\psi = 0$$
with Dirichlet boundary conditions on the obstacles and outgoing radiation conditions at infinity. Resonances are non-trivial solutions of this boundary-value problem corresponding to complex wavenumbers $k_n$ with $\operatorname{Im}(k_n) < 0$.

Let $K$ denote the classical non-escaping (trapped) set, i.e., the set of phase-space points whose forward and backward trajectories under the billiard flow remain in a bounded region forever, and let $d_H$ be the partial Hausdorff dimension of $K$ (the Hausdorff dimension of its intersection with a Poincaré section, or equivalently $\dim_H K = 2 d_H + 1$).

For a fixed constant $C > 0$, let
$$N(k, C) \;=\; \#\{ n : \operatorname{Re}(k_n) < k,\ \operatorname{Im}(k_n) > -C \}.$$

Prove or disprove: as $k \to \infty$,
$$N(k, C) \;=\; \Theta\!\left(k^{\,d_H + 1}\right).$$
That is, establish the fractal Weyl law for the number of scattering resonances of the open billiard with real part bounded by $k$ and imaginary part bounded below by $-C$, with the exponent given by $d_H + 1$, where $d_H$ is the partial Hausdorff dimension of the classical non-escaping set.
category_tag: fractal Weyl law for open quantum billiards
status_search_result: The fractal Weyl conjecture remains open in general. Sharp upper bounds of the conjectured order have been established (Sjöstrand, Zworski, Nonnenmacher–Sjöstrand–Zworski, Dyatlov, Naud) and there is strong numerical evidence (e.g., three-disk scatterers), but a matching lower bound—the full asymptotic—has not been proved. A 2025 preprint even reports counter-examples to the fractal Weyl law for certain semiclassical resonances, indicating that the conjecture as stated does not hold universally and is still actively investigated.

paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
original_question: For a given open or generalized billiard system, can the survival probability P(t) be expressed exactly, or at least expanded for large time t beyond the leading asymptotic term, particularly in well-understood cases such as integrable and dispersing billiards?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Q \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded domain (the billiard table) with piecewise smooth boundary $\partial Q$, and let $H \subset \partial Q$ be a designated open subset called the hole. Consider the billiard flow $\Phi_t$ on the unit tangent bundle $M$ of $Q$, in which a point particle moves with unit speed along straight lines in the interior of $Q$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) whenever it meets $\partial Q \setminus H$; once a trajectory hits the hole $H$, it escapes and is no longer tracked. Let $\mu$ denote the natural (Liouville) invariant probability measure on $M$. Define the survival probability at time $t \geq 0$ by
$$P(t) = \mu\bigl(\{x \in M : \Phi_s(x) \text{ is defined and has not escaped for all } 0 \leq s \leq t\}\bigr).$$

For a given open or generalized billiard system of this type — in particular for the well-understood classes of integrable billiards (such as circular, elliptic, rectangular, or spherical tables) and of dispersing (Sinai-type) billiards whose boundary components are strictly convex inwards — determine whether $P(t)$ admits an exact closed-form expression, or, failing that, an asymptotic expansion as $t \to \infty$
$$P(t) \;\sim\; \sum_{k} c_k\, f_k(t),$$
that goes beyond the known leading-order term (exponential decay in the dispersing case, power-law decay of order $t^{-1}$ in typical integrable cases), giving explicit formulas for the coefficients $c_k$ and the gauge functions $f_k(t)$ together with sharp control of the remainder.
status_search_result: Partial results exist: exact long-time asymptotic expansions of the survival probability have been derived in specific integrable cases (stadium billiard, spherical billiards) with explicit constant terms and subleading corrections, some linked to number-theoretic objects. However, a general framework producing exact or beyond-leading-order expansions for arbitrary open integrable or dispersing billiards remains unresolved.
