status_search_result: Related results exist for second-order linear PDEs and higher-order directional differential equations with bounded L-index hypotheses (e.g., works on slice holomorphic solutions and entire solutions of linear PDEs), but no source found directly resolves the stated first-order two-direction problem with general data $f_1,f_2,h$. Status appears unresolved in full generality based on available search results.

For the equation P1(z1,z2) partial F/partial z1 + P2(z1,z2) partial F/partial z2 = h(z1,z2), what direction b and what additional assumptions imply that an entire solution F has bounded L-index in direction b?

Let $L:\mathbb{C}^2\to(0,\infty)$ be a positive continuous function. For a nonzero direction $c\in\mathbb{C}^2$, write $D_c H(z):=\sum_{j=1}^{2}c_j\,\partial H/\partial z_j(z)$ and inductively $D_c^k H = D_c(D_c^{k-1}H)$. An entire function $H:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to be of bounded $L$-index in the direction $c$ if there exists a nonnegative integer $m_0$ such that for every $m\in\mathbb{N}_0$ and every $z\in\mathbb{C}^2$,
$$\frac{|D_c^m H(z)|}{m!\,L(z)^m}\ \le\ \max_{0\le k\le m_0}\frac{|D_c^k H(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k}.$$
The least such $m_0$ is the $L$-index of $H$ in direction $c$.

Let $P_1(z_1,z_2)$ and $P_2(z_1,z_2)$ be entire functions such that $P_1$ is of bounded $L$-index in direction $(1,0)$ and $P_2$ is of bounded $L$-index in direction $(0,1)$, and let $h:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ be entire. Consider the first-order linear PDE
$$P_1(z_1,z_2)\,\frac{\partial F}{\partial z_1}(z_1,z_2)\ +\ P_2(z_1,z_2)\,\frac{\partial F}{\partial z_2}(z_1,z_2)\ =\ h(z_1,z_2).$$

Determine a direction $b\in\mathbb{C}^2\setminus\{0\}$ and additional sufficient conditions on $P_1$, $P_2$, $h$, and $L$ such that every entire solution $F$ of this equation has bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$.

paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
original_question: Let l be a positive continuous function of one complex variable, and say that an entire function has bounded l-index if finitely many normalized derivatives |f^(k)(z)|/(k! l(z)^k) dominate all normalized derivative orders at every z. If f(z) has bounded l-index and w is an entire solution of the infinite-order linear differential equation sum_{k=0}^infty a_k w^(k)(z) = f(z), what assumptions on the coefficients a_k and on f(z) guarantee that w also has bounded l-index?
self_contained_problem:
Let $l:\mathbb{C}\to(0,\infty)$ be a positive continuous function. An entire function $g:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to have bounded $l$-index if there exists a non-negative integer $N$ such that for every $z\in\mathbb{C}$,
$$\frac{|g^{(N)}(z)|}{N!\,l(z)^{N}}\;\ge\;\max_{0\le k\le N}\frac{|g^{(k)}(z)|}{k!\,l(z)^{k}}\;\ge\;\frac{|g^{(k)}(z)|}{k!\,l(z)^{k}}\quad\text{for all }k\ge 0,$$
and the least such $N$ is the $l$-index of $g$.

Let $\{a_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of complex numbers (or, more generally, entire functions), and let $f$ be an entire function of bounded $l$-index. Consider an entire solution $w$ of the infinite-order linear differential equation
$$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k\, w^{(k)}(z) \;=\; f(z),\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}.$$

Determine sufficient conditions on the coefficients $\{a_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ (for instance, conditions on their growth or decay, on the radius of convergence of $\sum a_k\zeta^k$, or on majorization by $l$) and on $f$ which guarantee that every such entire solution $w$ also has bounded $l$-index.
status_search_result: The problem of identifying conditions on coefficients of infinite-order linear differential equations that guarantee bounded l-index of solutions appears to remain open. Known results address finite-order equations, polynomial/rational coefficient cases (Lepson, and subsequent work on vector-valued bounded-index solutions), and special bounded-L-index settings, but no general criterion for the infinite-order case with bounded l-index data is reported in the available literature.

paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
context_brief: Logarithmic derivative and zero counting criterion
original_question: Let F be entire on C^n and L be in Q_b^n. For each b-line t -> F(z0+tb), let G_r^b(F) be the union of scaled r-neighborhoods, measured with L, around the zeros of these one-variable slices. Is F of bounded L-index in direction b if and only if there is a single r > 0 and constants P > 0 and n_tilde such that (1) outside G_r^b(F), the logarithmic directional derivative satisfies |D_b F(z)/F(z)| <= P L(z), and (2) on every nonzero slice t -> F(z0+tb), each scaled disc of radius r/(|b| L(z0+t0 b)) contains at most n_tilde zeros?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ and let $\mathbf{b}\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$. Let $Q_{\mathbf b}^n$ denote the class of positive continuous functions $L:\mathbb{C}^n\to(0,\infty)$ such that for every $R>0$ there is a constant $\lambda(R)\ge 1$ with
\[ \lambda(R)^{-1}\le \frac{L(z+t\mathbf b)}{L(z)}\le \lambda(R) \qquad \text{whenever } z\in\mathbb{C}^n,\ t\in\mathbb{C},\ |t|\le R/(|\mathbf b|\,L(z)). \]
For an entire function $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ and $L\in Q_{\mathbf b}^n$, define the directional derivatives
\[ D_{\mathbf b}^0 F(z)=F(z),\qquad D_{\mathbf b}^{k+1}F(z)=\sum_{j=1}^n b_j\,\partial_{z_j}(D_{\mathbf b}^k F)(z). \]
$F$ is said to be of bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf b$ if there exists $N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ such that for every $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and every $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$,
\[ \frac{|D_{\mathbf b}^k F(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k}\le \max_{0\le j\le N}\frac{|D_{\mathbf b}^j F(z)|}{j!\,L(z)^j}. \]
For $r>0$ and $z_0\in\mathbb{C}^n$, set
\[ G_r^{\mathbf b}(F)=\bigcup_{z_0\in\mathbb{C}^n}\bigcup_{t_0\in Z_{z_0}}\Bigl\{ z_0+t\mathbf b:\ |t-t_0|\le \tfrac{r}{|\mathbf b|\,L(z_0+t_0\mathbf b)}\Bigr\}, \]
where $Z_{z_0}=\{t\in\mathbb{C}: F(z_0+t\mathbf b)=0\}$ when $F(z_0+\cdot\,\mathbf b)\not\equiv 0$ (and is empty otherwise).

Question: Is it true that $F$ is of bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf b$ if and only if there exist a single $r>0$, a constant $P>0$, and a nonnegative integer $\tilde n$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] for every $z\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus G_r^{\mathbf b}(F)$ with $F(z)\ne 0$,
\[ \Bigl|\frac{D_{\mathbf b}F(z)}{F(z)}\Bigr|\le P\,L(z); \]
\item[(2)] for every $z_0\in\mathbb{C}^n$ with $F(z_0+\cdot\,\mathbf b)\not\equiv 0$ and every $t_0\in\mathbb{C}$, the disc $\{t\in\mathbb{C}:|t-t_0|\le r/(|\mathbf b|\,L(z_0+t_0\mathbf b))\}$ contains at most $\tilde n$ zeros of $t\mapsto F(z_0+t\mathbf b)$ (counted with multiplicity)?
\end{enumerate}
status_search_result: Closely related logarithmic-derivative and zero-distribution criteria for entire functions of bounded L-index in a direction have been established by Bandura and Skaskiv (e.g., Ukrainian Math. J. 2017 and subsequent works), and analogous criteria have been proved for slice holomorphic functions and for functions in the unit ball. The exact equivalence as stated, using a single value of r, does not appear to be explicitly settled in the published literature found, so the precise formulation remains, at most, partially resolved.

original_question: Can one choose complex numbers a1, a2, c1, and c2, together with an entire function F(z1,z2), so that F(z1,z2) has bounded L-index in a fixed direction b = (b1,b2), but the affine coordinate change G(z1,z2) = F(a1 z1 + c1, a2 z2 + c2) has unbounded L-index in that same direction b = (b1,b2)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $b=(b_1,b_2)\in\mathbb{C}^2\setminus\{0\}$ be a fixed direction and let $L:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{R}_+$ be a fixed positive continuous function. For an entire function $F:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$, define the directional derivatives along $b$ by
$$\partial_b^0 F(z)=F(z),\qquad \partial_b^k F(z)=\frac{\partial^k}{\partial t^k}F(z+tb)\Big|_{t=0}\quad(k\ge 1),\ z\in\mathbb{C}^2.$$
The function $F$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$ if there exists a nonnegative integer $N$ such that for every $z\in\mathbb{C}^2$ and every nonnegative integer $k$,
$$\frac{|\partial_b^k F(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k}\le \max_{0\le j\le N}\frac{|\partial_b^j F(z)|}{j!\,L(z)^j}.$$
The least such $N$ is the $L$-index of $F$ in direction $b$; if no such $N$ exists, $F$ is said to have unbounded $L$-index in direction $b$.

Question: Do there exist complex numbers $a_1,a_2,c_1,c_2\in\mathbb{C}$ (with $a_1,a_2\neq 0$) and an entire function $F(z_1,z_2)$ such that $F$ has bounded $L$-index in the direction $b=(b_1,b_2)$, while the entire function
$$G(z_1,z_2)=F(a_1 z_1+c_1,\ a_2 z_2+c_2)$$
has unbounded $L$-index in the same direction $b$?

paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
original_question: Consider an entire product in C^n with planar zeros, pi(z) = product_{k>=1} g(<z,a_k>|a_k|^{-2},p), where g(u,p) = (1-u) exp(u + u^2/2 + ... + u^p/p) for p != 0 and g(u,0) = 1-u, and where the sequence a_k has genus p through sum |a_k|^{-p-1} < infinity and sum |a_k|^{-p} = infinity. Existing sufficient conditions for bounded L-index in a direction assume the zero-defining vectors lie on a fixed ray, a_kj = m_j |a_k|. Are there sufficient conditions for bounded L-index in a direction for such products without imposing that fixed-ray condition?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer $p\geq 0$, define the Weierstrass primary factor
$$g(u,p)=\begin{cases}1-u,& p=0,\\ (1-u)\exp\!\left(u+\tfrac{u^2}{2}+\cdots+\tfrac{u^p}{p}\right),& p\geq 1.\end{cases}$$
Let $n\geq 2$ and let $(a_k)_{k\geq 1}\subset \mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$ be a sequence with genus $p$, i.e.
$$\sum_{k\geq 1}|a_k|^{-(p+1)}<\infty,\qquad \sum_{k\geq 1}|a_k|^{-p}=\infty,$$
where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb{C}^n$. Consider the canonical product with "planar" zero set
$$\pi(z)=\prod_{k\geq 1} g\!\left(\tfrac{\langle z,a_k\rangle}{|a_k|^{2}},\,p\right),\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}^n,$$
where $\langle z,a\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^n z_j\overline{a_j}$. Fix a direction $\mathbf{b}\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$ and a positive continuous function $L:\mathbb{C}^n\to(0,\infty)$. An entire function $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for all $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and all $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$,
$$\frac{|\partial^{\,m}_{\mathbf{b}}F(z)|}{m!\,L(z)^m}\;\leq\;\max_{0\leq k\leq N}\frac{|\partial^{\,k}_{\mathbf{b}}F(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k},$$
where $\partial_{\mathbf{b}}F(z)=\sum_{j=1}^n b_j\,\partial F/\partial z_j$. The least such $N$ is the $L$-index of $F$ in the direction $\mathbf{b}$.

Known sufficient conditions guaranteeing that $\pi$ has bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ have been established under the additional hypothesis that all vectors $a_k$ lie on a single fixed ray, i.e. $a_{k,j}=m_j|a_k|$ for some fixed unit vector $(m_1,\dots,m_n)\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and every $k$.

Problem: Without imposing this fixed-ray restriction on the sequence $(a_k)$, find sufficient conditions on $(a_k)$, $\mathbf{b}$, and $L$ under which the canonical product $\pi$ has bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$.

status_search_result: Subsequent work by Bandura, Skaskiv and collaborators has produced sufficient conditions for boundedness of L-index in a direction for entire functions with "plane" zeros, but the available sources do not clearly confirm whether the fixed-ray hypothesis on the zero-defining vectors $a_k$ has been removed in the canonical-product setting described. The status of this specific problem could not be definitively verified from the search results.

paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
context_brief: Combining bounded indices across variable blocks
original_question: Let F:C^{n+m}->C be entire, let L1:C^n->R+ and L2:C^m->R+ be positive functions, and split variables into a first block of n coordinates and a second block of m coordinates. Suppose that, for every fixed second block, F has uniformly bounded L1-index in the direction (b1,...,bn,0,...,0), and for every fixed first block, F has uniformly bounded L2-index in the direction (0,...,0,b_{n+1},...,b_{n+m}). What positive function L:C^{n+m}->R+ makes F have bounded L-index in the combined direction b = (b1,...,b_{n+m})?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n,m\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $F:\mathbb{C}^{n+m}\to\mathbb{C}$ be an entire function. Write the variable as $(z',z'')$ with $z'\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and $z''\in\mathbb{C}^m$. Fix a direction $\mathbf{b}=(b_1,\dots,b_{n+m})\in\mathbb{C}^{n+m}\setminus\{0\}$, and set $\mathbf{b}'=(b_1,\dots,b_n,0,\dots,0)$ and $\mathbf{b}''=(0,\dots,0,b_{n+1},\dots,b_{n+m})$ in $\mathbb{C}^{n+m}$.

Recall that for a positive continuous function $L:\mathbb{C}^{n+m}\to\mathbb{R}_+$ and a direction $\mathbf{b}\in\mathbb{C}^{n+m}\setminus\{0\}$, an entire function $G:\mathbb{C}^{n+m}\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists $N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ such that for every $z\in\mathbb{C}^{n+m}$,
$$\frac{1}{N!}\frac{|\partial_{\mathbf{b}}^N G(z)|}{L(z)^N}\ \ge\ \frac{1}{k!}\frac{|\partial_{\mathbf{b}}^k G(z)|}{L(z)^k}\qquad\text{for all }k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},$$
where $\partial_{\mathbf{b}}G(z)=\sum_{j=1}^{n+m}b_j\,\partial G/\partial z_j(z)$ and $\partial_{\mathbf{b}}^k$ denotes its $k$-th iterate. The least such $N$ is the $L$-index of $G$ in the direction $\mathbf{b}$.

Now let $L_1:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+$ and $L_2:\mathbb{C}^m\to\mathbb{R}_+$ be positive continuous functions. Suppose:
(i) there exists $N_1\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ such that for every fixed $z''\in\mathbb{C}^m$, the entire function $z'\mapsto F(z',z'')$ on $\mathbb{C}^n$ has $L_1$-index in the direction $(b_1,\dots,b_n)$ at most $N_1$;
(ii) there exists $N_2\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ such that for every fixed $z'\in\mathbb{C}^n$, the entire function $z''\mapsto F(z',z'')$ on $\mathbb{C}^m$ has $L_2$-index in the direction $(b_{n+1},\dots,b_{n+m})$ at most $N_2$.

Determine an explicit positive continuous function $L:\mathbb{C}^{n+m}\to\mathbb{R}_+$, built from $L_1$ and $L_2$, such that $F$ has bounded $L$-index in the combined direction $\mathbf{b}$.

paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
context_brief: Bounded slice indices with unbounded directional index
original_question: What conditions on the zero set and growth of an entire function F(z1,z2) provide both of the following properties: for every base point (z1^0,z2^0) in C^2, the one-variable slice t -> F(z1^0 + b1 t, z2^0 + b2 t) has bounded index, but the two-variable function F(z1,z2) has unbounded L-index in the direction b = (b1,b2)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ be an entire function and let $\mathbf{b}=(b_1,b_2)\in\mathbb{C}^2\setminus\{0\}$ be a fixed direction. Let $L:\mathbb{C}^2\to(0,\infty)$ be a positive continuous function.

For each base point $(z_1^0,z_2^0)\in\mathbb{C}^2$, define the slice function
$$g_{(z_1^0,z_2^0)}(t)\;=\;F(z_1^0+b_1 t,\;z_2^0+b_2 t),\qquad t\in\mathbb{C}.$$
A one-variable entire function $g$ is said to have bounded index if there exists a non-negative integer $N$ such that for every $t\in\mathbb{C}$,
$$\max_{0\le k\le N}\frac{|g^{(k)}(t)|}{k!}\;\ge\;\frac{|g^{(n)}(t)|}{n!}\quad\text{for all }n\in\mathbb{N}_0.$$

The entire function $F$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists a non-negative integer $N$ such that for every $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb{C}^2$,
$$\max_{0\le k\le N}\frac{1}{k!\,L(z)^k}\Big|\partial^k_{\mathbf{b}}F(z)\Big|\;\ge\;\frac{1}{n!\,L(z)^n}\Big|\partial^n_{\mathbf{b}}F(z)\Big|\quad\text{for all }n\in\mathbb{N}_0,$$
where $\partial_{\mathbf{b}}F(z)=b_1\frac{\partial F}{\partial z_1}(z)+b_2\frac{\partial F}{\partial z_2}(z)$ and $\partial^k_{\mathbf{b}}F$ denotes the $k$-th iterate.

Find conditions on the zero set $F^{-1}(0)$ and on the growth of $F$ which together ensure both of the following simultaneously:

(i) for every base point $(z_1^0,z_2^0)\in\mathbb{C}^2$, the slice function $g_{(z_1^0,z_2^0)}(t)$ has bounded index (as a one-variable entire function);

(ii) the entire function $F$ does not have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ for the given $L$.

status_search_result: The problem belongs to a list of open problems on entire functions of bounded index in direction. Subsequent literature (work by Bandura, Skaskiv and collaborators in Matematychni Studii, MDPI Axioms, Ukrainian Mathematical Journal and Journal of Mathematical Sciences) develops criteria for boundedness of the L-index in direction (zero distribution, logarithmic derivative estimates, composition results), but no source located resolves this specific dichotomy of bounded slice indices coexisting with unbounded directional L-index. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Magic matrices with their powers, numerical ranges and some open problems
original_question: Let a magic matrix of order n mean an n by n square matrix whose entries are the natural numbers 1, 2, ..., n^2 with no repeated entry, and whose row sums, column sums, main diagonal sum, and antidiagonal sum are all equal. For general n, how can one describe exactly, or estimate, the number of magic matrices of order n?
status_search_result: Exact enumeration is known only for small n: M(3)=1, M(4)=880 (Frénicle), M(5)=275305224 (Schroeppel, 1973), all up to symmetries. For n=6 the exact count is unknown; Monte Carlo estimates (Pinn–Wieczerkowski) give roughly (1.7745 ± 0.0016)·10^19, with subsequent refinements via modular lifting techniques. No general formula or sharp asymptotic for M(n) is known; the problem of describing or estimating M(n) for general n remains open.

paper_title: Magic matrices with their powers, numerical ranges and some open problems
original_question: Let a magic matrix of order n mean an n by n square matrix whose entries are the natural numbers 1, 2, ..., n^2 with no repeated entry, and whose row sums, column sums, main diagonal sum, and antidiagonal sum are all equal. For any such matrix, let s denote the common row, column, main diagonal, and antidiagonal sum, which is an eigenvalue. Among magic matrices of the same order, how much can the eigenvalues other than s differ? May those non-s eigenvalues have arbitrary phase, and are they always symmetric with respect to zero?
self_contained_problem:
Define a magic matrix of order $n$ to be an $n \times n$ matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ with entries from the set $\{1,2,\dots,n^2\}$ such that all entries are distinct (each integer in $\{1,2,\dots,n^2\}$ appears exactly once), and such that the sum of the entries in every row, every column, the main diagonal, and the antidiagonal are all equal to a common value $s$. Since the all-ones vector $(1,1,\dots,1)^T$ is an eigenvector with eigenvalue $s$, the number $s = n(n^2+1)/2$ is always an eigenvalue of $A$.

For magic matrices of a fixed order $n$, investigate the variation of the remaining eigenvalues (those different from $s$). Specifically:

(a) Quantitatively bound or describe how much the non-$s$ eigenvalues can differ between two magic matrices of the same order $n$.

(b) Determine whether the non-$s$ eigenvalues of magic matrices of order $n$ can attain arbitrary complex phase (argument), or whether their arguments are constrained to a proper subset of $[0,2\pi)$.

(c) Determine whether, for every magic matrix of order $n$, the multiset of non-$s$ eigenvalues is symmetric about $0$ in the complex plane (i.e., $\lambda$ is a non-$s$ eigenvalue with multiplicity $m$ if and only if $-\lambda$ is, with the same multiplicity), or exhibit magic matrices for which this fails.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any published results that resolve the question of how much the non-$s$ eigenvalues of magic matrices of fixed order can vary, whether they can take arbitrary phase, or whether they are always symmetric about zero. No follow-up work addressing these specific questions was located, so the current status appears unverified.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: uniqueness of the radial Ginzburg-Landau solution
original_question: Let Omega be the unit disc in R^2, let epsilon > 0, and consider maps u: Omega -> R^2 solving the Ginzburg-Landau system Delta u = epsilon^{-2} u(1 - |u|^2) in Omega with boundary value u(x)=x on the boundary. The source defines the radial solution U_epsilon(x) = (x/|x|) f_epsilon(|x|), where f_epsilon solves the associated radial ODE with f_epsilon(0)=0 and f_epsilon(1)=1. Is this radial solution U_epsilon the only solution of the Ginzburg-Landau boundary value problem?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit disc in $\mathbb{R}^2$, and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Consider maps $u : \overline{\Omega} \to \mathbb{R}^2$ satisfying the Ginzburg–Landau boundary value problem
$$\Delta u = \frac{1}{\varepsilon^2}\, u\bigl(|u|^2 - 1\bigr) \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u(x) = x \quad \text{for } |x| = 1.$$
Define the radial solution $U_\varepsilon : \overline{\Omega} \to \mathbb{R}^2$ by
$$U_\varepsilon(x) = \frac{x}{|x|}\, f_\varepsilon(|x|),$$
where $f_\varepsilon : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ is the unique solution of the ordinary differential equation
$$f_\varepsilon''(r) + \frac{1}{r} f_\varepsilon'(r) - \frac{1}{r^2} f_\varepsilon(r) = \frac{1}{\varepsilon^2} f_\varepsilon(r)\bigl(f_\varepsilon(r)^2 - 1\bigr), \quad r \in (0,1),$$
with $f_\varepsilon(0) = 0$ and $f_\varepsilon(1) = 1$.

Is $U_\varepsilon$ the only solution of the above boundary value problem?
status_search_result: Uniqueness of the radial solution to this Dirichlet problem on the disc is a long-standing question of Brezis. Partial results are known: Mironescu proved that for small $\varepsilon$ the radial solution is the unique minimizer (and radially symmetric), and Ignat–Nguyen–Slastikov–Zarnescu established uniqueness of minimizers when either the energy or the Ginzburg–Landau parameter is small. Uniqueness among all critical points (the full open problem) does not appear to be resolved in the literature.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: asymptotic radial symmetry for p-Ginzburg-Landau minimizers and critical points
original_question: For p > 2, let Omega be the unit disc in R^2 with boundary value g(x)=x, and define the p-Ginzburg-Landau energy E_{epsilon,p}(u) = (1/p) integral_Omega |grad u|^p + (1/(4 epsilon^2)) integral_Omega (|u|^2 - 1)^2 on W^{1,p}_g(Omega; R^2). If u_epsilon is any minimizer, or more generally any critical point, of E_{epsilon,p}, must u_epsilon(x) converge to x/|x| on Omega without the origin as epsilon -> 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be the open unit disc, and fix $p > 2$. For $\varepsilon > 0$, consider the $p$-Ginzburg–Landau energy
$$E_{\varepsilon,p}(u) = \frac{1}{p}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^p\,dx + \frac{1}{4\varepsilon^2}\int_\Omega (|u|^2 - 1)^2\,dx$$
defined on the affine Sobolev space $W^{1,p}_g(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) = \{ u \in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) : u|_{\partial\Omega} = g \}$, where $g(x) = x$ for $x \in \partial\Omega$.

Let $u_\varepsilon \in W^{1,p}_g(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$ be any minimizer of $E_{\varepsilon,p}$, or more generally any critical point of $E_{\varepsilon,p}$. Determine whether
$$u_\varepsilon(x) \longrightarrow \frac{x}{|x|} \qquad \text{as } \varepsilon \to 0$$
on $\Omega \setminus \{0\}$ (e.g., locally uniformly, or in an appropriate Sobolev sense on compact subsets of $\Omega \setminus \{0\}$).
status_search_result: The asymptotic radial-symmetry question for minimizers and critical points of the $p$-Ginzburg–Landau functional ($p>2$) on the disc with boundary datum $x$ has been investigated in several works on $p$-energy and Ginzburg–Landau-type asymptotics, but no definitive resolution for all critical points (or even all minimizers) was located. Available results address partial cases (convergence in $W^{1,p}$, $C^{1,\alpha}$ convergence away from singular sets, weighted versions, higher dimensions), without confirming or refuting the full conjectured convergence $u_\varepsilon(x)\to x/|x|$ on $\Omega\setminus\{0\}$ for arbitrary critical points.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: automatic finite potential energy for entire Ginzburg-Landau solutions
original_question: For a smooth map u: R^2 -> R^2 satisfying the entire Ginzburg-Landau equation Delta u = u(1 - |u|^2) and the condition |u(x)| -> 1 as |x| -> infinity, must the finite-potential-energy condition integral_{R^2} (|u|^2 - 1)^2 < infinity automatically hold?
self_contained_problem:
Let $u\colon \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth map satisfying the Ginzburg–Landau equation
\[
\Delta u = u\bigl(|u|^2 - 1\bigr) \quad \text{on } \mathbb{R}^2,
\]
together with the boundary condition at infinity
\[
|u(x)| \to 1 \quad \text{as } |x| \to \infty.
\]
Must $u$ then automatically satisfy the finite potential energy condition
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \bigl(|u|^2 - 1\bigr)^2 \, dx < \infty\, ?
\]
Equivalently, does pointwise convergence of $|u|$ to $1$ at infinity for an entire solution of the planar Ginzburg–Landau equation force quadratic integrability of $|u|^2 - 1$?
status_search_result: No source located in the search establishes a resolution of this specific implication ("|u|→1 at infinity implies ∫(|u|²−1)² < ∞" for entire planar Ginzburg–Landau solutions). It is listed as an open problem in Brezis-type problem collections and is referenced through standard problem lists (Bethuel–Brezis–Hélein Problem 2; Brezis "Open Problem 2"). A recent 2025 preprint by Wei et al. announces a complete solution to "Brezis' First Open Problem," which concerns the classification/uniqueness of degree ±1 entire solutions rather than this automatic-finite-energy question. Hence this problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: continuous harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2
original_question: Let Omega be the unit ball B^3 in R^3. Given a smooth boundary map g: boundary Omega, identified with S^2, to S^2 with degree zero, consider weak harmonic maps u in H^1(Omega; R^3) satisfying Delta u_i = u_i |grad u|^2, |u|=1 in Omega, and u=g on the boundary. Does there always exist a continuous harmonic map satisfying this boundary value problem?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the open unit ball, and identify its boundary $\partial\Omega$ with the unit sphere $S^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$. Let $g\colon S^2 \to S^2$ be a smooth map of topological degree $\deg g = 0$. Consider weak harmonic maps $u \in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3)$ from $\Omega$ to $S^2$, that is, maps satisfying
\[ \Delta u_i = u_i\,|\nabla u|^2 \quad \text{in } \Omega \quad (i=1,2,3), \qquad |u(x)| = 1 \text{ for a.e. } x \in \Omega, \]
with the Dirichlet boundary condition $u = g$ on $\partial\Omega$ in the trace sense.

Question: Does there always exist a continuous map $u \in C^0(\overline{\Omega};S^2)$ that is a weak harmonic map and satisfies the boundary condition $u|_{\partial\Omega} = g$?
status_search_result: The question of whether every smooth degree-zero boundary map $g\colon S^2\to S^2$ admits a continuous harmonic extension $u\colon \overline{B^3}\to S^2$ is a longstanding open problem in the theory of harmonic maps, going back to work of Hardt–Lin and others. Energy-minimizing extensions can have singularities even when $\deg g=0$, and various partial constructions exist, but no general existence theorem for continuous harmonic extensions in the degree-zero case is known. Web searches did not reveal a resolution.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: continuity of minimizers of relaxed harmonic-map energy
original_question: For the relaxed energy R on H^1_g(Omega; S^2), defined by weak H^1 limits of continuous competitors in the B^3-to-S^2 harmonic-map problem, minimizers of R exist. Are all minimizers of R continuous on the closed ball, or at least does there exist one minimizer of R that is continuous on the closed ball?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the open unit ball, and let $g : \partial\Omega \to S^2$ be a smooth boundary datum. Denote
$$H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^3) : |u| = 1 \text{ a.e.}, \ u|_{\partial\Omega} = g \}.$$
Let $C^0_g(\overline\Omega; S^2)$ denote the subclass of maps in $H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ that are continuous on $\overline\Omega$. The Dirichlet energy is
$$E(u) = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx.$$
Because $C^0_g(\overline\Omega; S^2)$ is in general not sequentially weakly $H^1$-dense in $H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$, define the relaxed energy on $H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ by
$$R(u) = \inf\left\{ \liminf_{k\to\infty} E(u_k) : u_k \in C^0_g(\overline\Omega; S^2),\ u_k \rightharpoonup u \text{ weakly in } H^1\right\}.$$
It is known that the infimum of $R$ over $H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ is attained.

Question: Is every minimizer $u^*$ of $R$ continuous on $\overline\Omega$? If not, does there exist at least one minimizer of $R$ that is continuous on $\overline\Omega$?
status_search_result: Bethuel–Brezis–Coron and subsequent work (e.g., Hardt–Lin–Poon, Giaquinta–Modica–Souček) established that minimizers of the relaxed energy are smooth away from a finite (or small) singular set, but the question of full continuity up to the closed ball — or even existence of a single continuous minimizer — does not appear to have been resolved in the literature. Recent works on relaxed harmonic map energies continue to treat the regularity/continuity of relaxed minimizers as an open issue.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: sharp p-to-1 behavior in fractional degree estimates
original_question: For maps f in W^{1/p,p}(S^1; S^1), with 1 < p <= 2, does there exist a universal constant c such that the degree satisfies |deg f| <= c (p-1) integral_{S^1} integral_{S^1} |f(x)-f(y)|^p / |x-y|^2 dx dy for every such f?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle in $\mathbb{R}^2$, equipped with arclength measure. For $1<p\le 2$, consider the fractional Sobolev space $W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ consisting of measurable maps $f:S^1\to S^1\subset\mathbb{C}$ such that the Gagliardo seminorm
$$[f]_{1/p,p}^p:=\int_{S^1}\int_{S^1}\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy$$
is finite. It is known that every such map $f$ has a well-defined integer topological degree $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$, and that there exists a constant $C_p$ (depending on $p$) such that
$$|\deg f|\le C_p\,[f]_{1/p,p}^p\qquad\text{for all }f\in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1).$$
Question: Does there exist a universal constant $c>0$, independent of $p$, such that the sharper estimate
$$|\deg f|\le c\,(p-1)\int_{S^1}\int_{S^1}\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy$$
holds for every $1<p\le 2$ and every $f\in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the area of fractional Sobolev degree estimates on the circle. Web searches for "Bourgain–Brezis–Nguyen" type degree estimates with the sharp $(p-1)$ factor did not produce any published resolution; related work continues on BBM-type formulas and sharp constants, but the specific universal-constant inequality with the linear $(p-1)$ prefactor for the degree on $S^1$ appears to remain unresolved.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: small-threshold improvement of a topological degree estimate
original_question: For a continuous map f: S^1 -> S^1 and delta > 0, define I_delta(f) as the double integral over pairs (x,y) in S^1 x S^1 with |f(x)-f(y)| >= delta of dx dy / |x-y|^2. Does there exist a universal constant c such that |deg f| <= c delta I_delta(f) for every continuous f: S^1 -> S^1 and every delta <= sqrt(3)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle, equipped with arc-length measure. For a continuous map $f:S^1\to S^1$, let $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$ denote its topological degree. For each $\delta>0$, define
$$ I_\delta(f) \;=\; \iint_{\{(x,y)\in S^1\times S^1\,:\,|f(x)-f(y)|\ge \delta\}} \frac{dx\,dy}{|x-y|^2}, $$
where $|x-y|$ denotes the Euclidean (chordal) distance in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Does there exist a universal constant $c>0$ such that
$$ |\deg f| \;\le\; c\,\delta\, I_\delta(f) $$
for every continuous map $f:S^1\to S^1$ and every $\delta\in(0,\sqrt{3}]$?
status_search_result: The estimate is known for sufficiently small $\delta$ (with constants depending on a small threshold), and the question whether it can be extended up to the threshold $\sqrt{3}$ was posed as an open problem by Brezis (and earlier by Bourgain–Brezis–Nguyen). Web searches did not reveal a resolution of this small-threshold improvement; recent work on Bourgain–Brezis–Mironescu type formulas does not address this specific endpoint, so the status appears to remain open but could not be definitively confirmed.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: whether Fourier magnitudes determine degree below the known regularity threshold
original_question: Let f,g: S^1 -> S^1 have Fourier coefficients a_n(f) and a_n(g) with |a_n(f)| = |a_n(g)| for every n in Z. Theorem 5.5 says deg f = deg g for f,g in W^{1/3,3}(S^1;S^1), hence also for Holder maps of exponent alpha > 1/3. Does the same conclusion hold when f,g are in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1) for p > 3, or when f,g are in C^{0,alpha}(S^1;S^1) for alpha <= 1/3?
self_contained_problem:
For a measurable map $h:S^1\to\mathbb{C}$, denote by $a_n(h)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S^1} h(e^{i\theta})e^{-in\theta}\,d\theta$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, its Fourier coefficients. For $s\in(0,1)$ and $p\in[1,\infty)$, the fractional Sobolev space $W^{s,p}(S^1;S^1)$ consists of measurable maps $f:S^1\to S^1$ with
$$\iint_{S^1\times S^1}\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{1+sp}}\,dx\,dy<\infty.$$
For such $f$ the topological degree $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$ is well defined whenever $sp\ge 1$, in particular in $W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ for every $p\ge 1$. The space $C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ ($0<\alpha\le 1$) consists of Hölder continuous maps $f:S^1\to S^1$ of exponent $\alpha$; for $\alpha>0$ the degree is also defined.

It is known that if $f,g\in W^{1/3,3}(S^1;S^1)$ satisfy $|a_n(f)|=|a_n(g)|$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, then $\deg f=\deg g$; consequently the same conclusion holds for $f,g\in C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ with $\alpha>1/3$.

Question: Does the conclusion $\deg f=\deg g$ continue to hold under the hypothesis $|a_n(f)|=|a_n(g)|$ for all $n\in\mathbb{Z}$ when:
(a) $f,g\in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ for some $p>3$; or
(b) $f,g\in C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ for some $\alpha\le 1/3$?

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: map-dependent summation process for degree recovery
original_question: Given a particular map f in C(S^1;S^1), or more generally in VMO(S^1;S^1), does there exist a summation process depending on that f such that lim_{epsilon->0} sum_{n in Z} n |a_n(f)|^2 sigma_{n,epsilon} = deg f?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle in $\mathbb{C}$. For a measurable map $f: S^1 \to S^1$, write its Fourier series $f(e^{i\theta}) \sim \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} a_n(f) e^{in\theta}$, where $a_n(f) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} f(e^{i\theta}) e^{-in\theta}\, d\theta$. Recall that $\mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$ denotes the class of maps of vanishing mean oscillation from $S^1$ into $S^1$, and that the topological degree $\deg f \in \mathbb{Z}$ is well defined for every $f \in C(S^1;S^1)$ and, more generally, for every $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$. For such $f$, one has the Parseval-type identity
$$\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} |a_n(f)|^2 = 1,$$
and formally
$$\deg f \;=\; \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2,$$
where the right-hand side need not converge absolutely.

By a summation process we mean a family of coefficients $\{\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z},\, 0<\varepsilon<1}$ such that, for each $\varepsilon>0$, $\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\to 0$ sufficiently fast as $|n|\to\infty$ (so the relevant series converges), and $\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\to 1$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$ for each fixed $n$.

Question: Given any $f \in C(S^1;S^1)$ (respectively any $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$), does there exist a summation process $\{\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\}$, possibly depending on $f$, such that
$$\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0^+} \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} n\, |a_n(f)|^2\, \sigma_{n,\varepsilon} \;=\; \deg f\;?$$
category_tag: Fourier series and topological degree of VMO maps
status_search_result: The question of recovering the degree of a continuous or VMO map $S^1 \to S^1$ via a summation process applied to the formal identity $\deg f = \sum n |a_n(f)|^2$ is documented as an open problem in Brezis's collection of favorite open problems and in related literature on winding numbers and Fourier series. No published resolution has been located.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: distances between homotopy classes of H^1 maps S^2 to S^2
original_question: For H^1 maps from S^2 to S^2, let E_d be the homotopy class of maps of degree d, and define Dist_{H^1}(E_{d1},E_{d2}) = sup_{f in E_{d1}} inf_{g in E_{d2}} ||grad(f-g)||_{L^2}. Is Dist_{H^1}(E_{d1},E_{d2})^2 = 8 pi |d1-d2| for all integers d1,d2? Even more basically, is Dist_{H^1}(E_{d1},E_{d2}) symmetric in d1 and d2 for all integers d1,d2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^2$ denote the standard 2-sphere. Consider the Sobolev space $H^1(S^2;S^2)$ of maps $f:S^2\to S^2$ with $\int_{S^2}|\nabla f|^2\,d\mathrm{vol}<\infty$. For each integer $d\in\mathbb{Z}$, let $E_d\subset H^1(S^2;S^2)$ denote the homotopy class consisting of maps of (Brouwer) degree $d$ (the degree being well-defined on $H^1(S^2;S^2)$). Define the asymmetric distance
$$\mathrm{Dist}_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2}) \;=\; \sup_{f\in E_{d_1}}\,\inf_{g\in E_{d_2}}\,\|\nabla(f-g)\|_{L^2(S^2)}.$$
Answer the following:
(a) Is it true that
$$\mathrm{Dist}_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})^2 \;=\; 8\pi\,|d_1-d_2|$$
for all integers $d_1,d_2\in\mathbb{Z}$?
(b) More basically, is $\mathrm{Dist}_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})$ symmetric in $d_1$ and $d_2$ for all $d_1,d_2\in\mathbb{Z}$?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on distances between homotopy classes of sphere-valued Sobolev maps (Brezis–Mironescu–Shafrir and related works). Searches turn up papers studying this asymmetric distance for $W^{s,p}(S^N;S^N)$, but no result establishing the equality $\mathrm{Dist}_{H^1}^2 = 8\pi|d_1-d_2|$ or even the symmetry of the distance for $H^1(S^2;S^2)$ appears to be available; the problem is treated as open.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: unbounded extremal solutions in high dimension
original_question: Let Omega be a bounded smooth convex set in R^N with N >= 10. For the extremal solution u^* of the nonlinear Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda e^u in Omega, u>0 in Omega, u=0 on the boundary, is u^* unbounded? If not for some convex domains, can one choose another smooth increasing convex nonlinearity f with f(0)>0 and f(t)/t -> infinity, possibly depending on Omega, so that the corresponding extremal solution is not in L^infinity(Omega)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded smooth convex domain with $N\geq 10$. For $\lambda>0$ consider the semilinear Dirichlet problem
$$-\Delta u = \lambda e^{u}\ \text{in } \Omega,\qquad u>0\ \text{in } \Omega,\qquad u=0\ \text{on }\partial\Omega.$$
It is classical that there is a critical parameter $\lambda^{*}\in(0,\infty)$ such that for $\lambda\in(0,\lambda^{*})$ the problem has a minimal classical solution $u_{\lambda}$, and for $\lambda>\lambda^{*}$ no solution exists. The extremal solution is defined as $u^{*}(x):=\lim_{\lambda\uparrow\lambda^{*}}u_{\lambda}(x)$; it is the unique weak solution at $\lambda=\lambda^{*}$.

(a) Is $u^{*}\notin L^{\infty}(\Omega)$ for every such $\Omega$?

(b) If (a) fails — i.e., if there exist bounded smooth convex domains $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ with $N\geq 10$ for which the extremal solution of the above problem is bounded — does there exist, possibly depending on $\Omega$, a smooth increasing convex nonlinearity $f:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ with $f(0)>0$ and $\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)/t=\infty$ such that the extremal solution of
$$-\Delta u = \lambda f(u)\ \text{in } \Omega,\quad u>0\ \text{in }\Omega,\quad u=0\ \text{on }\partial\Omega$$
fails to be in $L^{\infty}(\Omega)$?
category_tag: extremal solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
status_search_result: For general (not necessarily convex) bounded smooth domains, Cabré–Figalli–Ros-Oton–Serra (2020) proved that stable solutions to semilinear elliptic equations are bounded if and only if $N\leq 9$, settling the regularity threshold in the general setting. On convex domains, however, boundedness of the extremal solution for the exponential nonlinearity in dimensions $N\geq 10$ remains an open question, as does the existence of a convex nonlinearity producing an unbounded extremal solution on every convex domain in high dimension. No published resolution of either part for convex domains was located.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: strengthened phase estimate in Bourgain-Brezis theory
original_question: On the N-dimensional torus T^N with N >= 2, does the strengthened Bourgain-Brezis type estimate (7.6) hold: for all test functions phi, is the quotient norm of phi minus its mean in H^{1/2}+W^{1,1} bounded by a constant times the quotient norm of grad phi in H^{1/2}+L^1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N\geq 2$ and let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ denote the $N$-dimensional flat torus. For a (smooth) test function $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^N)$, write $\overline{\varphi}=\int_{\mathbb{T}^N}\varphi$ for its mean value. Recall the Sobolev–Slobodeckij space $H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)$ defined via the norm $\|f\|_{H^{1/2}}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}^N}(1+|k|)\,|\widehat f(k)|^2$, and the Lebesgue/Sobolev spaces $L^1(\mathbb{T}^N)$ and $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{T}^N)$.

For a sum space $X+Y$ of two Banach spaces continuously embedded in a common topological vector space, equip it with the quotient norm
$$\|u\|_{X+Y}=\inf\{\|x\|_X+\|y\|_Y : u=x+y,\ x\in X,\ y\in Y\}.$$
For a vector field $F=(F_1,\ldots,F_N)$ on $\mathbb{T}^N$ define $\|F\|_{H^{1/2}+L^1}=\sum_{j=1}^N\|F_j\|_{H^{1/2}+L^1}$.

Question: Does there exist a constant $C=C(N)>0$ such that for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^N)$,
$$\|\varphi-\overline{\varphi}\|_{H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}}\;\leq\; C\,\|\nabla\varphi\|_{H^{1/2}+L^1}\,?$$
status_search_result: Standard surveys on Bourgain–Brezis limiting estimates list this strengthened sum-space inequality on the torus as undecided. A recent search did not surface a published proof or disproof of the specific $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ vs. $H^{1/2}+L^1$ inequality on $\mathbb{T}^N$; related Bourgain–Brezis estimates and variants continue to be actively studied, but the status of this specific question could not be confirmed from the available sources.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: constant-function characterization using liminf nonlocal tails
original_question: Let Omega be a smooth bounded connected domain in R^N, and for lambda > 0, p >= 1, and measurable u: Omega -> R, let Phi_{lambda,p}(u) be the measure of pairs (x,y) in Omega x Omega for which |u(x)-u(y)|^p / |x-y|^{p+N} >= lambda. If liminf_{lambda->infinity} lambda Phi_{lambda,p}(u)=0 for some p >= 1, must u be almost everywhere constant?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a smooth bounded connected domain. For a measurable function $u:\Omega \to \mathbb{R}$, a real number $p \ge 1$, and $\lambda > 0$, define
$$\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u) \;=\; \mathcal{L}^{2N}\!\left(\Big\{ (x,y)\in \Omega\times\Omega : \frac{|u(x)-u(y)|^{p}}{|x-y|^{p+N}} \ge \lambda \Big\}\right),$$
where $\mathcal{L}^{2N}$ denotes Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^{2N}$.

Suppose that for some $p \ge 1$,
$$\liminf_{\lambda \to \infty} \lambda\, \Phi_{\lambda,p}(u) \;=\; 0.$$
Must $u$ be almost everywhere constant on $\Omega$?
category_tag: Sobolev space characterizations via nonlocal functionals
status_search_result: The question, posed in the context of nonlocal characterizations of Sobolev/BV norms studied by Brezis, Van Schaftingen, Yung, Seeger, and Nguyen, is listed as an open problem. Recent surveys and 2024–2025 papers on these functionals state related open questions but do not report a resolution; partial negative results exist in different parameter regimes (e.g., for related quantities with $\gamma<0$) but do not settle the constancy question for $\liminf_{\lambda\to\infty}\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u)=0$.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: For the nonlocal functionals lambda Phi_{lambda,p} associated with the pairwise threshold |u(x)-u(y)|^p / |x-y|^{p+N}, do these functionals Gamma-converge as lambda -> infinity to a local Sobolev/BV functional: c_p ||grad u||_{L^p}^p for u in W^{1,p}(Omega), infinity otherwise when p>1, and c_1 ||grad u||_M for u in BV(Omega), infinity otherwise when p=1, for some positive constants c_p and c_1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded smooth domain and fix $p \geq 1$. For a measurable function $u:\Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\lambda > 0$, define the nonlocal threshold-type functional
$$\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u) \;=\; \iint_{\{(x,y)\in\Omega\times\Omega \,:\, |u(x)-u(y)|>\lambda\}} \frac{\lambda^{p}}{|x-y|^{p+N}}\,dx\,dy,$$
or, equivalently up to the convention used here, the family of functionals built from the pairwise "threshold" density
$$\frac{|u(x)-u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{p+N}}\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|u(x)-u(y)|>\lambda\}},$$
and consider the rescaled family $\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,p}$ on $L^1(\Omega)$ (or $L^p(\Omega)$).

Define the candidate limit functional $\Psi_p:L^1(\Omega)\to [0,\infty]$ by:
- if $p>1$:
$$\Psi_p(u) \;=\; \begin{cases} c_p \displaystyle\int_\Omega |\nabla u(x)|^p\,dx & \text{if } u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega),\\ +\infty & \text{otherwise};\end{cases}$$
- if $p=1$:
$$\Psi_1(u) \;=\; \begin{cases} c_1\, |Du|(\Omega) & \text{if } u\in BV(\Omega),\\ +\infty & \text{otherwise};\end{cases}$$
where $c_p, c_1 > 0$ are appropriate positive constants depending only on $p$ and $N$.

Question: Does the family $\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,p}$ $\Gamma$-converge, as $\lambda \to \infty$, to the functional $\Psi_p$, with respect to the $L^1(\Omega)$ topology? More precisely, prove or disprove that there exist positive constants $c_p$ (for $p>1$) and $c_1$ (for $p=1$) such that:
1. (liminf inequality) For every sequence $u_\lambda \to u$ in $L^1(\Omega)$, $\liminf_{\lambda\to\infty} \lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u_\lambda) \geq \Psi_p(u)$.
2. (recovery sequence) For every $u\in L^1(\Omega)$, there exists $u_\lambda \to u$ in $L^1(\Omega)$ with $\limsup_{\lambda\to\infty}\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u_\lambda) \leq \Psi_p(u)$.
status_search_result: Recent surveys and papers on Brezis–Nguyen-type nonlocal characterizations of Sobolev and BV norms (e.g., Nguyen's 2025 survey on arXiv) continue to discuss pointwise/integral convergence and inequalities for these threshold functionals but do not announce a resolution of the Γ-convergence statement to c_p‖∇u‖_p^p (or c_1|Du| in the BV case). No source found establishing or refuting the Γ-convergence as λ → ∞; the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
original_question: For finite patterns, where a pattern is a word over variables such as alpha, beta, and gamma, and avoidability means that there exists an infinite word avoiding that pattern, what is the computational complexity of deciding whether a given pattern p is avoidable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $V = \{\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots\}$ be a countably infinite set of variables (letters of the pattern alphabet). A pattern is a finite nonempty word $p \in V^+$. Given a finite alphabet $\Sigma$, a word $w \in \Sigma^*$ is said to encounter $p$ if there exist a nonerasing morphism $h \colon V^+ \to \Sigma^+$ and factors of $w$ such that $h(p)$ occurs as a factor of $w$; otherwise $w$ avoids $p$. The pattern $p$ is called avoidable if there exist a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ and an infinite word $w \in \Sigma^{\mathbb{N}}$ such that every factor of $w$ avoids $p$.

Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem:

INPUT: a finite pattern $p \in V^+$.
QUESTION: is $p$ avoidable?

In particular, is this problem decidable, and if so, what is its precise complexity class?
status_search_result: The decidability and complexity of recognizing avoidable patterns over a free variable alphabet remains an open problem in combinatorics on words. Related variants have been studied: deciding avoidability of finite sets of partial words is NP-hard and lies in PSPACE, and deciding unavoidability of a single word (a special case) has been shown NP-complete. However, the general question of the exact computational complexity (and even a sharp upper bound for decidability beyond the known algorithmic characterizations of Bean–Ehrenfeucht–McNulty and Zimin) of pattern avoidability is still listed as open in recent surveys.

paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
original_question: In partial-word pattern avoidance, determine the avoidability index of the binary pattern alpha beta beta alpha. A partial word may contain holes, and the avoidability index of a pattern is the smallest alphabet size k for which an infinite partial word over k letters avoids the pattern, with infinity used when no such alphabet size exists.
self_contained_problem:
A partial word over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ is a sequence whose entries are either letters of $\Sigma$ or a special "hole" symbol $\diamond$ that is considered to match every letter (and itself). A pattern is a nonempty word $p$ over an alphabet of variables. An infinite partial word $w$ over $\Sigma$ is said to meet the pattern $p$ if there exists a non-erasing morphism $h$ from the variable alphabet to nonempty partial words over $\Sigma$ such that $h(p)$ occurs as a factor of $w$ in the sense that every defined position matches the corresponding position of $w$ (with $\diamond$ matching anything). Otherwise $w$ avoids $p$. The partial word avoidability index of $p$ is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that there exists an infinite partial word over a $k$-letter alphabet (with infinitely many holes) that avoids $p$, or $\infty$ if no such $k$ exists.

Determine the partial word avoidability index of the binary pattern $\alpha\beta\beta\alpha$ (where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are distinct variables).
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Blanchet-Sadri and collaborators on computing partial word avoidability indices of binary patterns establishes that the partial word avoidability index of $\alpha\beta\beta\alpha$ is 3, completing the classification of binary patterns in partial words.

paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
original_question: For every binary pattern p and alphabet size k, classify p with respect to minimum hole sparsity and non-trivial minimum hole sparsity in partial words. Here a partial word is lambda-sparse when every factor of length lambda contains at least one hole; minimum hole sparsity is the smallest positive lambda for which there exists an infinite lambda-sparse partial word over k letters that avoids all occurrences of p, while the non-trivial version only requires avoiding non-trivial occurrences. Determine this lambda for each p and k, or determine that it is infinite when no such partial word exists.
self_contained_problem:
Let an alphabet be a finite set of letters and let ⋄ denote a special symbol called a hole. A partial word over an alphabet Σ is a (finite or infinite) sequence with entries in Σ ∪ {⋄}; positions containing ⋄ are called holes and are considered compatible with every letter of Σ. A factor of a partial word is any contiguous block of its entries. For a positive integer λ, a partial word is said to be λ-sparse if every factor of length λ contains at least one hole.

A pattern is a nonempty word p over a pattern alphabet of variables. An occurrence of p in a partial word w is a morphism h sending each variable to a nonempty partial word such that the image h(p) is compatible with some factor of w (i.e., matches it in every non-hole position); the occurrence is called trivial if h sends some variable to a partial word consisting of a single hole, and non-trivial otherwise. The partial word w avoids p if no occurrence of p appears in w; it avoids p non-trivially if no non-trivial occurrence appears.

For a binary pattern p (a pattern over an alphabet of two variables) and an integer k ≥ 1, define
- ms(p,k) = the smallest positive integer λ such that there exists an infinite λ-sparse partial word over a k-letter alphabet that avoids p, and ms(p,k) = ∞ if no such infinite λ-sparse partial word exists for any λ;
- ms*(p,k) = the analogous quantity where avoidance is required only non-trivially.

Problem: For every binary pattern p and every alphabet size k ≥ 1, determine the values of ms(p,k) and ms*(p,k) (including determining when they are infinite).
status_search_result: The minimum hole sparsity classification has been completed for unary patterns in partial words, but the corresponding classification for binary patterns and arbitrary alphabet size k appears to remain an open problem in the literature on avoidable patterns in partial words. No source was found announcing a complete solution for the binary case.

paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
original_question: How densely can infinitely many holes be inserted into an abelian n-free word so that the resulting partial word remains abelian n-free? Constantly bounded spacing between consecutive holes is ruled out by the cited result, so the question asks whether the gaps can be made smaller than exponential spacing, for example with distances between consecutive holes bounded by a polynomial.
self_contained_problem:
A partial word over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ is a sequence $w \in (\Sigma \cup \{\diamond\})^*$ or $w \in (\Sigma \cup \{\diamond\})^\omega$, where the symbol $\diamond$ denotes a "hole" (a do-not-care position). Two full words $u, v \in \Sigma^*$ of the same length are abelian equivalent if every letter of $\Sigma$ occurs the same number of times in $u$ as in $v$. A partial word $w$ is said to contain an abelian $n$-th power if there exist factors $w[i_0..i_1-1], w[i_1..i_2-1], \dots, w[i_{n-1}..i_n-1]$ of $w$, all of the same length, such that for some choice of full words $u_1, \dots, u_n \in \Sigma^*$ that are pairwise abelian equivalent, each factor is compatible with the corresponding $u_j$ (i.e., agrees with $u_j$ at every non-hole position). Otherwise $w$ is called abelian $n$-free.

It is known that there exist infinite abelian $n$-free partial words containing infinitely many holes, but that no such partial word can have the gaps between consecutive holes bounded by a constant.

Question: For each integer $n \ge 2$, determine the smallest possible asymptotic growth rate of the gaps between consecutive holes in an infinite abelian $n$-free partial word over some finite alphabet that contains infinitely many holes. In particular, can such a partial word be constructed in which the distance between consecutive holes is bounded above by a polynomial in their index (rather than only by an exponential function)?
status_search_result: The question of how densely holes can be inserted into an abelian $n$-free partial word, specifically whether polynomial spacing between consecutive holes is achievable, is listed as an open problem in the literature on avoidable patterns in partial words. Recent works on abelian pattern avoidance in partial words discuss constructions with infinitely many holes and exponential spacing, but no polynomial-spacing construction or matching lower bound appears to have been established.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: Let G be a triangle-free graph on n vertices. Can G always be made bipartite by deleting at most n^2/25 edges?
self_contained_problem: A graph is called triangle-free if it contains no three pairwise adjacent vertices, and bipartite if its vertex set can be partitioned into two parts so that every edge has its endpoints in different parts. paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: Let k be an integer at least 2 and let G be a graph with m edges. Define h(m) = sqrt(2m + 1/4) - 1/2. Does V(G) always have a k-partition (V1, V2, ..., Vk) satisfying both of the following bounds: the cross-edge count e(V1, V2, ..., Vk) is at least ((k - 1)/k)m + ((k - 1)/(2k))h(m) - (k - 2)/(8k), and every induced part has at most m/k^2 + ((k - 1)/(2k^2))h(m) edges?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a finite simple graph with $m$ edges and vertex set $V(G)$. Define
$$h(m)=\sqrt{2m+\tfrac14}-\tfrac12.$$
For a partition $(V_1,V_2,\dots,V_k)$ of $V(G)$ into $k$ (possibly empty) parts, let $e(V_i)$ denote the number of edges of $G$ with both endpoints in $V_i$, and let
$$e(V_1,V_2,\dots,V_k)=m-\sum_{i=1}^{k} e(V_i)$$
denote the number of edges of $G$ with endpoints in distinct parts. Does there always exist a partition $(V_1,V_2,\dots,V_k)$ of $V(G)$ such that both of the following hold simultaneously:
$$e(V_1,V_2,\dots,V_k)\ \ge\ \frac{k-1}{k}\,m+\frac{k-1}{2k}\,h(m)-\frac{k-2}{8k},$$
$$\max_{1\le i\le k} e(V_i)\ \le\ \frac{m}{k^2}+\frac{k-1}{2k^2}\,h(m)\,?$$
status_search_result: Each of the two bounds is known individually (proved by Bollobás and Scott). The question of whether a single partition can achieve both bounds simultaneously was raised by Bollobás and Scott as an open problem (Problem 1 in their judicious-partitions problem list). Recent surveys and work on judicious k-partitions (e.g., Ma and collaborators) discuss progress on related judicious partition problems but the simultaneous version for all k≥2 does not appear to have been fully resolved.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: What is the computational complexity of the minimum bisection problem on weighted planar graphs, where a bisection is a bipartition whose two vertex classes have sizes as equal as possible?
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E, w) be an edge-weighted planar graph with nonnegative edge weights w : E → ℝ≥0. A bisection of G is a partition of V into two disjoint sets V1, V2 with V = V1 ∪ V2 satisfying ||V1| − |V2|| ≤ 1. The weight (or cost) of a bisection is the sum of w(e) over all edges e ∈ E with one endpoint in V1 and the other in V2. The minimum bisection problem on weighted planar graphs asks, given such a G, to compute a bisection of minimum cost.

Determine the computational complexity of this problem: is it solvable in polynomial time, or is it NP-hard?
status_search_result: The complexity of minimum bisection on (weighted) planar graphs appears to remain open: it is not known whether the problem is in P or NP-hard. Recent work has focused on approximation, including a polynomial-time bicriteria approximation scheme for planar bisection, while exact polynomial-time algorithms exist only for restricted subclasses such as bounded-treewidth graphs and grid graphs without holes.

original_question: For each integer k at least 1, what is the smallest constant c(k) such that every graph G with minimum degree delta(G) at least k has a bisection (S, T) for which both induced subgraphs G[S] and G[T] contain at most c(k)e(G) edges?

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with $e(G)=|E|$ edges and minimum degree $\delta(G)$. A bisection of $G$ is an ordered partition $(S,T)$ of $V$ into two disjoint sets with $||S|-|T||\le 1$. For a vertex set $X\subseteq V$, write $e(X)$ for the number of edges of $G$ with both endpoints in $X$.

For each integer $k\ge 1$, determine the smallest constant $c(k)$ with the following property: every graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\ge k$ admits a bisection $(S,T)$ such that
$$\max\{e(S),\,e(T)\}\le c(k)\,e(G).$$

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
context_brief: Removing o(m) from judicious bisection bound
original_question: Let k be a positive integer. Can the o(m) term be removed from Lee et al.’s bisection theorem, so that every graph with m edges and minimum degree 2k or 2k + 1 has a bisection (S, T) satisfying max{e(S), e(T)} <= ((k + 1)/(2(2k + 1)))m?

For a vertex set $U\subseteq V$, let $e(U)$ denote the number of edges of $G$ with both endpoints in $U$. It is known that every graph $G$ with $m$ edges and minimum degree at least $2k$ or $2k+1$ admits a bisection $(S,T)$ satisfying
$$\max\{e(S),e(T)\}\le\left(\frac{k+1}{2(2k+1)}+o(1)\right)m,$$

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: Does every graph G admit a bisection (S, T) such that for every vertex u in S, the number of neighbors of u in T is at least d_S(u) - 1, and for every vertex v in T, the number of neighbors of v in S is at least d_T(v) - 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. A bisection of $G$ is an ordered partition $(S,T)$ of $V$ into two disjoint sets with $\big||S|-|T|\big|\le 1$. For a vertex $u\in V$ and a set $X\subseteq V$, let $d_X(u)$ denote the number of neighbors of $u$ in $X$, and let $N_X(u)$ denote the set of neighbors of $u$ in $X$.

Decide whether the following statement holds: every finite simple graph $G$ admits a bisection $(S,T)$ such that
$$|N_T(u)| \ge d_S(u)-1 \quad \text{for every } u\in S,$$
and
$$|N_S(v)| \ge d_T(v)-1 \quad \text{for every } v\in T.$$
status_search_result: Recent work indicates that the original conjecture (with additive constant −1) fails for an infinite family of graphs, so the statement as posed is false in general; however, the natural weaker version replacing the constant −1 by an O(1) additive term remains widely open, and special cases (e.g., for various classes of regular graphs) have been established.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: For positive integers s and t, let f(s,t) be the least connectivity threshold such that every f(s,t)-connected graph can be partitioned into two sets S and T for which the induced subgraphs G[S] and G[T] have connectivity at least s and t, respectively. Is f(s,t) always equal to s + t + 1?
self_contained_problem: For positive integers $s$ and $t$, define $f(s,t)$ to be the least positive integer $k$ (if it exists) such that for every $k$-vertex-connected finite simple graph $G$, the vertex set $V(G)$ admits a partition into two nonempty parts $S$ and $T$ for which the induced subgraph $G[S]$ is $s$-vertex-connected and the induced subgraph $G[T]$ is $t$-vertex-connected. It is known that $f(s,t)$ exists for all positive integers $s,t$, and that $f(s,t) \ge s+t+1$ (as witnessed by the complete graph $K_{s+t+1}$). Determine whether $f(s,t) = s+t+1$ holds for all positive integers $s$ and $t$.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
context_brief: Degree partition for triangle-free K2,3-free graphs
original_question: Let G be a triangle-free graph with no K_{2,3} subgraph, and let a and b be integer-valued functions on V(G) such that a(x) >= 2, b(x) >= 2, and d(x) >= a(x) + b(x) - 1 for every vertex x. Must V(G) have a partition (A, B) such that every x in A has at least a(x) neighbors inside A and every y in B has at least b(y) neighbors inside B?

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph that is triangle-free (contains no $K_3$ subgraph) and $K_{2,3}$-free (contains no subgraph isomorphic to the complete bipartite graph $K_{2,3}$). For each vertex $x \in V$, let $d(x)$ denote its degree in $G$. Suppose $a, b : V \to \mathbb{Z}$ are functions such that for every $x \in V$:
\[ a(x) \ge 2, \quad b(x) \ge 2, \quad d(x) \ge a(x) + b(x) - 1. \]
For a subset $S \subseteq V$ and $x \in S$, let $d_S(x)$ denote the number of neighbors of $x$ that lie in $S$.

Determine whether $V$ necessarily admits a partition $V = A \sqcup B$ such that
\[ d_A(x) \ge a(x) \text{ for every } x \in A, \quad \text{and} \quad d_B(y) \ge b(y) \text{ for every } y \in B. \]

The strengthening to triangle-free and $K_{2,3}$-free graphs with the sharper degree condition $d(x) \ge a(x)+b(x)-1$ and variable functions $a,b$ does not appear to have a confirmed resolution in the accessible literature.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
context_brief: Lovasz induced path with connected complement
original_question: For every natural number l at least 3, does there exist an integer f(l) such that for any two vertices x and y in any f(l)-connected graph G, there is an induced path P from x to y for which the vertex-deleted graph G - V(P) is l-connected?
self_contained_problem:
A graph G is k-connected if it has more than k vertices and remains connected after the deletion of any fewer than k vertices. An induced path in G is a path P such that the subgraph of G induced by V(P) is exactly P (i.e., no chords). For a subgraph H of G, let G - V(H) denote the graph obtained from G by deleting the vertices of H together with all incident edges.

Prove or disprove: for every integer l ≥ 3, there exists an integer f(l) such that for every f(l)-connected graph G and every pair of distinct vertices x, y of G, there exists an induced x–y path P in G for which G - V(P) is l-connected.

(It is known that such an f exists with f(1) = 3 and f(2) = 5; the question concerns all l ≥ 3.)
status_search_result: The induced-path removal conjecture of Lovász/Kriesell is verified for l = 1 (Tutte's wheel theorem) and l = 2 (Kriesell; Chen et al.). For l ≥ 3 the existence of f(l) remains open. A non-induced weakening was established by Kawarabayashi–Reed–Wollan, and an induced-cycle variant has been proved, but the induced-path statement is still listed as open (e.g., on the Open Problem Garden).

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: Let s be a positive integer. Does every graph with minimum degree at least 2s + 1 admit a bisection (S, T) such that both induced subgraphs G[S] and G[T] have minimum degree at least s?

Let $s$ be a positive integer. A bisection of a graph $G=(V,E)$ on $n$ vertices is an ordered partition $(S,T)$ of $V$ with $\lvert\,|S|-|T|\,\rvert\le 1$. For a subset $U\subseteq V$, let $G[U]$ denote the subgraph of $G$ induced by $U$, and let $\delta(H)$ denote the minimum degree of a graph $H$. 

Determine whether the following statement is true: every finite simple graph $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G)\ge 2s+1$ admits a bisection $(S,T)$ such that 
$$\min\{\delta(G[S]),\ \delta(G[T])\}\ \ge\ s.$$
(If true, the bound $2s+1$ on the minimum degree is best possible, as shown by the complete graph $K_{2s+1}$.)

No source found resolves this specific question, which continues to be cited as an open problem in the area of judicious bipartitions.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: For a graph G = (V, E), the Coloring problem asks whether G has a coloring with at most k colors, where a coloring assigns colors to vertices so that adjacent vertices receive different colors. A graph is even-cycle-free if it has no induced cycle of even length, and it is even-anticycle-free if it has no induced subgraph that is the complement of an even cycle. What is the computational complexity of Coloring when the input is restricted to even-cycle-free graphs, and what is the computational complexity of Coloring when the input is restricted to even-anticycle-free graphs?
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple undirected graph. A (proper) coloring of G is an assignment of colors to the vertices of G such that no two adjacent vertices receive the same color. For an integer k ≥ 1, the Coloring problem takes as input a graph G and an integer k, and asks whether G admits a proper coloring using at most k colors.

An induced cycle in G is a cycle whose vertex set induces, in G, exactly the edges of that cycle (a chordless cycle). Call a graph even-cycle-free if it contains no induced cycle of even length, and even-anticycle-free if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to the complement of an even-length cycle.

Determine the computational complexity (e.g., polynomial-time solvable, NP-complete, or otherwise) of the Coloring problem in each of the following two cases:
(a) the input graph G is restricted to be even-cycle-free;
(b) the input graph G is restricted to be even-anticycle-free.
status_search_result: The complexity of Coloring restricted to even-cycle-free graphs and even-anticycle-free graphs is described as a long-standing open problem. While the analogous problems for odd-cycle-free (bipartite) and odd-anticycle-free (cobipartite) graphs are polynomial-time solvable, switching the parity from odd to even yields two open complexity questions that remain unresolved.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: A graph is chordal bipartite if it is bipartite and every induced cycle in it has exactly four vertices. What is the computational complexity of List 3-Coloring on chordal bipartite graphs, where each vertex has a list of allowed colors drawn from {1, 2, 3} and the task is to find a proper coloring respecting the lists? What is the computational complexity of 3-Precoloring Extension on chordal bipartite graphs, where a partial 3-coloring is given and the task is to decide whether it extends to a proper 3-coloring of the whole graph?
self_contained_problem:
A graph G=(V,E) is called chordal bipartite if it is bipartite and every induced cycle in G has exactly four vertices (equivalently, G is bipartite and contains no induced cycle of length at least 6).

Consider the following two decision problems on chordal bipartite graphs:

(a) LIST 3-COLORING. Given a chordal bipartite graph G=(V,E) together with a list assignment L: V → 2^{{1,2,3}}, decide whether there exists a proper coloring c: V → {1,2,3} such that c(v) ∈ L(v) for every v ∈ V and c(u) ≠ c(v) whenever uv ∈ E.

(b) 3-PRECOLORING EXTENSION. Given a chordal bipartite graph G=(V,E), a subset W ⊆ V, and a proper coloring c_W : W → {1,2,3}, decide whether c_W can be extended to a proper 3-coloring c: V → {1,2,3} of G.

Determine the computational complexity of each of these two problems on the class of chordal bipartite graphs: is each of them solvable in polynomial time, or is it NP-complete?
status_search_result: The complexity of List 3-Coloring and 3-Precoloring Extension restricted to chordal bipartite graphs is reported as open in the literature. Related results show that 4-List Coloring is NP-complete on P8-free chordal bipartite graphs, 4-Precoloring Extension is NP-complete on P10-free chordal bipartite graphs, and 3-Precoloring Extension is NP-complete on bipartite (and planar bipartite) graphs in general, but no resolution of the 3-coloring variants on chordal bipartite graphs has been found.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: The 5-Coloring problem asks whether the vertices of a graph can be colored with colors from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} so that adjacent vertices receive different colors. What is the computational complexity of 5-Coloring for graphs whose maximum vertex degree is at most 6?
self_contained_problem: The 5-Coloring problem takes as input a finite simple graph $G=(V,E)$ and asks whether there exists a function $c:V\to\{1,2,3,4,5\}$ such that $c(u)\neq c(v)$ whenever $uv\in E$. Determine the computational complexity of 5-Coloring when restricted to the class of graphs whose maximum vertex degree is at most 6. In particular, decide whether this restricted problem is solvable in polynomial time or is NP-complete.
status_search_result: The problem is widely cited as open. It is known that k-Coloring is NP-complete for graphs of maximum degree at most k + ⌈√k⌉ − 1, and combined with Brooks' theorem the smallest unresolved case is exactly 5-Coloring on graphs of maximum degree 6. Recent surveys on graph coloring complexity continue to list this as an open problem.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: A graph is AT-free if it has no asteroidal triple: there do not exist three mutually non-adjacent vertices such that each pair is joined by a path avoiding the neighborhood of the third vertex. What is the computational complexity of the Coloring problem on AT-free graphs, where Coloring asks whether a given graph has a proper coloring with at most k colors for an input integer k?
self_contained_problem:
An asteroidal triple in a simple undirected graph G is a set of three pairwise non-adjacent vertices {u,v,w} such that for every pair among them there is a path in G connecting the two vertices that avoids the closed neighborhood of the third. A graph is called AT-free if it contains no asteroidal triple. The Coloring problem takes as input a graph G and a positive integer k, and asks whether G admits a proper k-coloring, i.e., a map c:V(G)→{1,…,k} with c(x)≠c(y) for every edge xy of G.

Determine the computational complexity of the Coloring problem when the input graph is restricted to be AT-free (with k part of the input). In particular, decide whether this problem is solvable in polynomial time or is NP-complete.
status_search_result: The complexity of Coloring on AT-free graphs is listed as an open problem in surveys on graph coloring for special graph classes. Partial results are known: Stacho showed 3-Coloring is polynomial-time solvable on AT-free graphs, and the problem is polynomial for fixed small k on certain subclasses, but the general complexity (with k part of the input, or even for fixed k≥4) appears to remain unresolved as of recent literature.

original_question: A problem is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to a parameter p if instances (I, p) can be solved in time f(p)|I|^O(1) for some computable function f depending only on p. An AT-free graph is a graph with no asteroidal triple. Is the Coloring problem fixed-parameter tractable on AT-free graphs when the parameter is the number k of colors?
self_contained_problem:
A parameterized decision problem is fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) with respect to a parameter p if every instance (I,p) can be decided in time f(p)·|I|^{O(1)} for some computable function f depending only on p.

In a graph G=(V,E), an asteroidal triple is a set of three pairwise non-adjacent vertices such that between any two of them there is a path avoiding the closed neighborhood of the third. A graph is AT-free if it contains no asteroidal triple.

The Coloring problem takes as input a graph G and a positive integer k, and asks whether there is a proper k-coloring of G, i.e., a map c:V→{1,…,k} with c(u)≠c(v) whenever uv∈E.

Question: Is the Coloring problem, restricted to AT-free input graphs and parameterized by the number k of colors, fixed-parameter tractable?
status_search_result: The parameterized complexity of Coloring on AT-free graphs (with k as parameter) is listed as an open problem in a survey on graph coloring open problems for special graph classes. Web search did not surface a subsequent resolution; related work (Kratsch–Müller on Coloring AT-free graphs) addresses other complexity aspects but not the FPT question. Status appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: A complete + pv graph is a graph that can be transformed into a complete graph by deleting at most p vertices. In List Coloring, each vertex has a list of admissible colors and the task is to find a proper coloring that respects all lists. In Precoloring Extension, a partial k-coloring is given and the task is to decide whether it extends to a proper k-coloring of the whole graph. What is the parameterized complexity, with parameter p, of List Coloring and of Precoloring Extension on complete + pv graphs?
self_contained_problem:
For a nonnegative integer $p$, call a graph $G$ a "complete $+pv$" graph if there exists a set $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|\le p$ such that $G-S$ is a complete graph. Consider the following two problems on complete $+pv$ graphs:

(1) List Coloring: each vertex $v$ is given a list $L(v)$ of admissible colors; decide whether there is a proper coloring $c$ of $G$ with $c(v)\in L(v)$ for every vertex $v$.

(2) Precoloring Extension: given an integer $k$ and a partial proper $k$-coloring of a subset of vertices of $G$, decide whether it extends to a proper $k$-coloring of all of $G$.

Determine the parameterized complexity of List Coloring and of Precoloring Extension on complete $+pv$ graphs when parameterized by $p$. In particular, decide for each problem whether it is fixed-parameter tractable, admits a polynomial kernel, or is $\mathrm{W}[1]$-hard with respect to $p$.
status_search_result: The problem was resolved by Hermelin, Kratsch, and others (STACS 2020): with respect to the size $k$ of a clique modulator (equivalently the parameter $p$ for complete $+pv$ graphs), List Coloring admits an $O^*(2^k)$ randomized FPT algorithm, and Precoloring Extension admits a kernel with at most $3k$ vertices. This directly answers the open question.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: In online graph coloring, vertices are revealed one by one and must be colored irrevocably using only the revealed part of the graph. For each graph G, chi_OL(G) is the minimum, over online coloring algorithms, of the worst-case number of colors used over all vertex orders; a graph class is online chi_OL-bounded if some online coloring algorithm uses at most h(chi_OL(G)) colors for every graph G in the class, for some function h. For every integer k >= 1, is the class of bipartite graphs with no induced path P_k online chi_OL-bounded?
self_contained_problem:
In the online graph coloring model, the vertices of a graph G are revealed one at a time together with all edges connecting the newly revealed vertex to previously revealed vertices; upon revelation, each vertex must be assigned a color (a positive integer), different from the colors of its already-revealed neighbors, and this assignment is irrevocable. An online coloring algorithm is a (deterministic) rule that produces such a coloring for any input order. For a graph G, let chi_OL(G) denote the minimum, over all online coloring algorithms A, of the maximum number of colors used by A over all possible vertex orderings of G. A class C of graphs is said to be online chi_OL-bounded if there exists a function h: N -> N and an online coloring algorithm A such that for every G in C and every ordering of V(G), the algorithm A uses at most h(chi_OL(G)) colors on G. For a positive integer k, let P_k denote the path on k vertices, and call a graph "P_k-free" if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to P_k.

Question: For every integer k >= 1, is the class of P_k-free bipartite graphs online chi_OL-bounded?
status_search_result: The question is known to hold for small values of k: P_k-free bipartite graphs are online chi_OL-bounded for k up to 9 (results by Micek and others, e.g., the P_8- and P_9-free bipartite cases were established with explicit competitive algorithms). However, the general question "for every k" remains open; no positive result is known for all k, and the broader problem of whether bipartite graphs themselves admit an online competitive algorithm is also still open.
