paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: In online graph coloring, an algorithm receives the vertices of a graph one at a time and irrevocably assigns each new vertex a color using only the revealed subgraph and previous colors. For a graph G, chi_OL(G) is the smallest worst-case number of colors achievable by any online coloring algorithm. Is the class of all graphs online chi_OL-bounded, meaning that there exists an online coloring algorithm whose color use on every graph G is bounded by some function of chi_OL(G)?
self_contained_problem:
In online graph coloring, an algorithm is given the vertices of a finite simple graph $G$ one at a time in an order chosen by an adversary. When a vertex $v$ is revealed, the algorithm also learns all edges between $v$ and previously revealed vertices, and must irrevocably assign $v$ a positive integer color so that the resulting partial coloring is proper (adjacent vertices receive distinct colors). For a graph $G$, define $\chi_{OL}(G)$ to be the minimum, over all deterministic online coloring algorithms $A$, of the maximum, over all vertex presentation orders of $G$, of the number of colors used by $A$ on $G$.

A class $\mathcal{G}$ of graphs is said to be online $\chi_{OL}$-bounded if there exists a single online coloring algorithm $A$ (working on all graphs) and a function $f:\mathbb{N}	o\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $G\in\mathcal{G}$ and every presentation order of $V(G)$, the number of colors used by $A$ is at most $f(\chi_{OL}(G))$.

Question: Is the class of all finite simple graphs online $\chi_{OL}$-bounded?
status_search_result: The problem appears still open. Survey and research sources note that the existence of an online-competitive algorithm for all graphs (and even just for all bipartite graphs) is a long-standing open question stemming from work of Gyárfás and Lehel; competitive algorithms are known only for restricted classes (forests, certain $P_t$-free bipartite graphs, graphs of girth at least 5, etc.).

paper_title: Some New Results of Two Open Problems Related to Integral Inequalities
context_brief: Exponent refinement of a convex integral ratio inequality
original_question: Let [a,b] be a real interval. Let f, g, and h be positive continuous real-valued functions on [a,b] such that f(x)≤h(x) for every x in [a,b], the quotient f(x)/h(x) is decreasing, and f and g are increasing. Let ϕ be a convex function with ϕ(0)=0. Determine conditions on δ and λ under which the integral ratio inequality (∫_a^b f(x) dx)/(∫_a^b h(x) dx) ≥ (∫_a^b ϕ(f(x))g(x) dx)^δ/(∫_a^b ϕ(h(x))g(x) dx)^λ holds.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem (refining an inequality previously studied by Ngô–Thang–Dat–Tuan and Liu–Ngô) and has been addressed in subsequent literature giving sufficient conditions on δ and λ (e.g., relating δ and λ through the ranges of f and h). The referenced work explicitly claims to solve this open problem.

paper_title: Localized Spot Patterns on the Sphere for Reaction-Diffusion Systems: Theory and Open Problems
context_brief: DAE spot dynamics on varying-curvature manifolds
original_question: On a compact surface of revolution for which the source-neutral Green function is analytically available, with that Green function satisfying Delta_S G = |Omega|^{-1} - delta(x - x_0), can one derive and analyze explicit differential-algebraic spot dynamics for localized reaction-diffusion spots on a manifold with varying curvature, including whether curvature can pin localized spots?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a smooth compact two-dimensional surface of revolution embedded in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with induced metric, surface area $|\Omega|$, Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta_{\mathcal{S}}$, and Gaussian curvature $K(x)$ that varies along $\mathcal{S}$. Assume that the source-neutral Green's function $G(x;x_0)$ on $\mathcal{S}$, defined by
$$\Delta_{\mathcal{S}} G(x;x_0) = \tfrac{1}{|\Omega|} - \delta(x-x_0), \qquad \int_{\mathcal{S}} G(x;x_0)\,dS = 0,$$
is available in closed analytic form (e.g. by separation of variables in geodesic polar coordinates adapted to the rotational symmetry).

Consider a singularly perturbed activator–inhibitor reaction–diffusion system on $\mathcal{S}$ (for instance, a Schnakenberg- or Gierer–Meinhardt-type model with small activator diffusivity $\varepsilon^2 \ll 1$) admitting quasi-equilibrium localized spot solutions concentrated at points $x_1(t),\ldots,x_N(t) \in \mathcal{S}$ with slowly varying source strengths $S_1(t),\ldots,S_N(t)$.

(a) Derive, by matched asymptotic expansions in the limit $\varepsilon \to 0$, an explicit differential-algebraic system of equations (DAE) governing the slow evolution of the spot locations $\{x_j(t)\}$ and source strengths $\{S_j(t)\}$ on $\mathcal{S}$, in which $G$ and its regular part $R(x_0) := \lim_{x\to x_0}(G(x;x_0)+\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\log d(x,x_0))$ enter as the only geometric data.

(b) Using the explicit form of $G$ on the surface of revolution, analyze the resulting DAE: characterize equilibrium spot configurations, their linear stability under slow translational perturbations, and determine whether the spatial variation of the Gaussian curvature $K$ can pin one or more spots at specific locations of $\mathcal{S}$ (i.e. produce isolated stable equilibria of the DAE that depend on $K$ rather than only on inter-spot interactions).
category_tag: localized spot dynamics on curved surfaces
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open direction: deriving and analyzing explicit DAE spot dynamics on general surfaces of revolution with varying curvature, and establishing curvature-induced pinning, has been treated rigorously only on the sphere (constant curvature). Subsequent works on curved-surface reaction-diffusion (e.g. weakly nonlinear analyses, curvature-dependent diffusion of Turing patterns, Turing pattern dynamics on curved surfaces in 2024–2025) study related phenomena but do not provide the explicit DAE reduction and pinning analysis requested here. No definitive resolution was located.

paper_title: Localized Spot Patterns on the Sphere for Reaction-Diffusion Systems: Theory and Open Problems
original_question: For a model that couples passive bulk diffusion inside the sphere to a Brusselator reaction-diffusion PDE on the spherical surface, with the fuel supply E representing an exchange or flux between surface-bound concentrations and bulk concentrations, what DAE dynamics and localized spot-pattern behavior arise on the sphere?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the unit ball $B=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^3:|x|\le 1\}$ with boundary $S^2=\partial B$. On $S^2$, let $u(\xi,t)$ and $v(\xi,t)$ denote the activator and inhibitor concentrations of a Brusselator reaction-diffusion system, and inside $B$ let $U(x,t)$ denote a passively diffusing bulk concentration. The coupled bulk-surface system is

$$U_t = D_b\,\Delta_x U, \quad x\in B,\qquad U(x,0)\text{ given},$$
$$u_t = \varepsilon^2 \Delta_{S^2} u + E(\xi,t) - u + f\,u^2 v,\qquad \xi\in S^2,$$
$$\tau\, v_t = D\,\Delta_{S^2} v + \frac{1}{\varepsilon^2}\bigl(u - u^2 v\bigr),\qquad \xi\in S^2,$$
with coupling boundary conditions on $S^2$ of Robin/flux type
$$D_b\,\partial_\nu U + \kappa\bigl(U|_{S^2} - u\bigr)=0,\qquad E(\xi,t)= \beta\,U|_{S^2}(\xi,t),$$
so that the fuel supply $E$ on the surface represents an exchange flux between the surface activator and the bulk concentration. paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: For tree-level string cosmologies containing Ramond-Ramond fields, what are the asymptotic properties of the resulting universes, are the known solutions stable and unique, and do there exist solutions that appear only subdominantly in the asymptotic regime in a way that constrains the allowed singular asymptotic states?
self_contained_problem:
Consider tree-level low-energy effective string actions in $D$ spacetime dimensions that, in addition to the metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ and dilaton $\phi$, contain one or more Ramond–Ramond (RR) $p$-form field strengths $F_{(p)} = dA_{(p-1)}$. A representative bosonic sector is

$$ S = \frac{1}{2\kappa^2}\int d^Dx\,\sqrt{-g}\,\left[ e^{-2\phi}\left(R + 4(\nabla\phi)^2\right) - \sum_p \frac{1}{2\,p!}\,F_{(p)}^2 \right], $$

with the RR field strengths entering without a dilaton prefactor (in the string frame). Restrict to spatially homogeneous and isotropic cosmological ansätze, e.g.
$$ ds^2 = -dt^2 + a(t)^2\, d\Sigma_k^2, \qquad \phi = \phi(t), \qquad F_{(p)} = F_{(p)}(t), $$
where $d\Sigma_k^2$ is a maximally symmetric spatial metric of curvature $k\in\{-1,0,+1\}$, and let the equations of motion be the resulting autonomous system of ODEs for $(a,\phi,F_{(p)})$.

Establish a complete asymptotic analysis of this dynamical system in the regimes $t\to t_*$ corresponding to cosmological singularities (initial or final). Specifically:

(a) Classify all asymptotic (singular) behaviours of the solutions: determine the possible scaling exponents and leading-order forms of $a(t)$, $\phi(t)$, and $F_{(p)}(t)$ near a singularity, and identify the dominant and subdominant branches.

(b) Decide whether each known closed-form solution (e.g. dilaton–RR rolling-radii solutions, power-law attractors) is dynamically stable as an asymptotic regime, and whether it is unique within its branch up to the obvious symmetries (time translation, time reversal, rescaling).

(c) Identify any solutions that exist only as subdominant asymptotic regimes — i.e. solutions whose contribution is sub-leading compared with a dominant attractor — and determine in what way their existence constrains the set of admissible singular asymptotic states of universes containing RR fields.
status_search_result: A comprehensive asymptotic classification of tree-level string cosmologies including Ramond–Ramond fields, addressing stability, uniqueness, and subdominant branches, does not appear in the literature. Related but partial results exist: tree-level NS–NS string cosmology has been analyzed (Copeland–Lahiri–Wands, 1996), and asymptotic scalar field cosmology in string theory (Rudelius 2022, Calderón-Infante et al.) treats late-time attractors via the Distance/Swampland conjectures, but not a full singular-asymptotic classification with explicit RR-form sources. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
context_brief: Genericity in string and M-theory cosmology
original_question: For the stable solutions obtained in the preceding string and M-theory asymptotic problems, what do full inhomogeneous generic perturbations look like, and what features must a generic analytic cosmological solution share with those stable solutions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider cosmological solutions of the low-energy effective field equations arising from string theory and M-theory, formulated as systems of nonlinear PDEs on a spacetime manifold of the form M = R x Sigma (with Sigma a spatial slice of suitable dimension determined by the theory) coupled to scalar (dilaton/moduli) and antisymmetric form fields. Suppose that within the class of spatially homogeneous cosmological models for such systems one has identified a family of asymptotic solutions near a singular epoch (e.g. as proper time t tends to 0 or to infinity) that are stable in the sense that homogeneous perturbations decay or remain bounded relative to the background.

The problem is the following:

(a) For each such stable homogeneous asymptotic solution, analyze the full inhomogeneous perturbation problem: linearize the field equations about the background, allowing perturbations that depend on all spatial coordinates as well as time, and determine the asymptotic behavior, gauge-invariant modes, and stability properties of these inhomogeneous perturbations near the singular epoch.

(b) Using this analysis, characterize the properties that every generic analytic cosmological solution of the underlying string/M-theory effective equations, lying in a neighborhood of the chosen stable background, must share with that background. In particular, identify the asymptotic invariants (such as Kasner-type exponents, dilaton velocities, scaling of form-field energies, and dependence on the maximal number of free analytic functions of the spatial coordinates) that any generic analytic solution must exhibit.

Provide such a genericity description for the stable asymptotic solutions of the string and M-theory cosmological systems.
status_search_result: No specific resolution of this genericity question for stable string/M-theory cosmological backgrounds was located. Related work on BKL-type analyses and cosmological billiards in supergravity addresses generic singular behavior but does not provide a complete genericity classification for the stable asymptotic solutions in question. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: In curved string cosmologies with higher-order curvature corrections and interacting fluids, what asymptotic behavior is produced by dominant versus subdominant curvature contributions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a spatially curved, homogeneous and isotropic FLRW string-cosmological background with metric
ds^2 = -dt^2 + a(t)^2 [ dr^2/(1-kr^2) + r^2 dΩ^2 ],   k ∈ {-1, +1},
sourced by a dilaton φ(t) and N interacting perfect-fluid components with energy densities ρ_i(t), pressures p_i = w_i ρ_i, satisfying interaction-modified continuity equations
ρ̇_i + 3H(1+w_i) ρ_i = Q_i(ρ_1,…,ρ_N, H, φ, φ̇),   Σ_i Q_i = 0,
where H = ȧ/a. Let the gravitational sector be governed by the tree-level string action augmented by higher-order curvature (α'-type) corrections
S = ∫ d^4x √(-g) e^{-φ} [ R + (∇φ)^2 + λ_1 α' L_{GB} + λ_2 α'^2 L_{(R^3)} + ⋯ ] + S_matter,
where L_{GB} = R^2 - 4R_{μν}R^{μν} + R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ} is the Gauss–Bonnet invariant and L_{(R^3)} denotes the next higher-curvature correction.

Question. Classify, as t → ∞ and as t → t_* (any finite-time singularity), the possible asymptotic regimes of the scale factor a(t), the Hubble rate H(t), the dilaton φ(t), and the fluid densities ρ_i(t), distinguishing the cases in which (i) the spatial-curvature term k/a^2 is asymptotically dominant over the higher-curvature corrections, (ii) the higher-curvature α'-corrections asymptotically dominate over the spatial curvature, and (iii) both contribute at the same asymptotic order. In each case, determine the resulting late-time/early-time attractors of the dynamical system and the conditions on the interaction terms Q_i and the equation-of-state parameters w_i under which each regime is realized.
status_search_result: No specific resolution of this asymptotic classification problem for curved, interacting string cosmologies with higher-order curvature corrections was located. paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: Are the deformed power-law cosmological solutions of M-theory asymptotically stable, and does that stability support the naturalness of inflation in M-theory cosmology?
self_contained_problem:
Consider eleven-dimensional supergravity (the low-energy limit of M-theory) compactified on a product manifold M = M_{1+d} × K, where M_{1+d} carries a spatially flat FLRW metric

  ds^2_{1+d} = -dt^2 + a(t)^2 δ_{ij} dx^i dx^j,   i,j = 1,…,d,

and K is an internal manifold with time-dependent volume modulus b(t). The full eleven-dimensional metric is taken in the warped product form

  ds^2_{11} = -dt^2 + a(t)^2 dx_d^2 + b(t)^2 dy_{10-d}^2.

Augment the two-derivative supergravity action with the leading higher-derivative corrections (the quartic curvature R^4 terms together with their supersymmetric partners involving the three-form field strength) that arise as α'-type or κ^{2/3} corrections in M-theory. The resulting field equations admit "deformed power-law" cosmological solutions of the form

  a(t) = a_0 t^{p} (1 + δ_a(t)),   b(t) = b_0 t^{q} (1 + δ_b(t)),

where (p,q) is a power-law exponent pair determined by the corrected equations and δ_a, δ_b are deformations vanishing as t → ∞.

Questions:
(1) Are these deformed power-law solutions asymptotically stable under small homogeneous (and, more generally, inhomogeneous) perturbations of the metric and form-field moduli as t → ∞? Equivalently, do generic nearby initial data converge to a member of the deformed power-law family in the future?
(2) If so, does asymptotic stability of a member of the family with accelerating external scale factor (p > 1) hold on an open set of initial data large enough to make inflation in this M-theoretic cosmological setting natural, in the sense that it does not require fine-tuning of initial conditions?

Provide either a rigorous proof of asymptotic stability (with an explicit characterization of the basin of attraction) or a proof of instability.
status_search_result: A search for results on asymptotic stability of deformed power-law cosmological solutions arising from higher-derivative corrected eleven-dimensional supergravity / M-theory did not turn up a definitive proof of stability (or instability) of the relevant deformed power-law family, nor a rigorous result establishing naturalness of inflation in this M-theory setting. Related works address stability of power-law inflation in general relativity and modified gravity, but the specific M-theory question appears to remain open.

original_question: In the Ekpyrotic and cyclic scenarios in M-theory, is the Milne state globally asymptotically stable when the higher-order terms enter the evolution dominantly rather than subdominantly, and what does that reveal about ekpyrosis and the broader structure of M-theory cosmology?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the low-energy effective action of M-theory compactified to four dimensions in the setting of Ekpyrotic and cyclic cosmological scenarios. In these scenarios one studies spatially homogeneous (e.g. Bianchi-type) cosmological evolutions, with a contracting phase governed by a scalar field with steep negative exponential potential coupled to gravity together with quadratic and higher-order curvature corrections (e.g. Gauss–Bonnet and other α'- and loop-corrections appearing in heterotic M-theory). The Milne state is the spatially flat (or hyperbolic) self-similar vacuum solution with linearly expanding/contracting scale factor a(t) ∝ |t| and vanishing Weyl curvature, regarded as a fixed point of the cosmological dynamical system.

Previous analysis of these scenarios treats the higher-order curvature terms as subdominant perturbations of the two-derivative Einstein–scalar evolution and asks for global asymptotic stability of the Milne state under such perturbations. The problem here is the complementary regime: assume the higher-order terms enter the evolution equations dominantly, i.e. they are not treated as small corrections to the Einstein–scalar dynamics but instead control the leading asymptotic behaviour.

Question: In this dominant higher-order regime of Ekpyrotic and cyclic M-theory cosmology, is the Milne state globally asymptotically stable as a solution of the resulting cosmological evolution equations on the space of homogeneous initial data? Provide a rigorous proof or disproof of global asymptotic stability, and determine the implications of the answer for the viability of ekpyrosis and for the asymptotic structure of M-theory cosmology.

The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: What precise relation, if any, does the ambient cosmological construction have to twistor theory, especially to the null projective twistor 5-space PN and related H-space constructions, and how should one understand the validity of the asymptotic condition and the meaning of non-locality in the ambient 5-space?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the ambient cosmological construction in which a four-dimensional spacetime $(M^4,g)$ is realized as a hypersurface in a five-dimensional ambient manifold $(\widetilde M^5,\widetilde g)$ carrying a perfect-fluid stress-energy content (rather than a pure cosmological constant $\Lambda$), together with an asymptotic flatness/conformal condition imposed at infinity of the ambient space. Recall also the twistor-theoretic setting: for a four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime, projective twistor space $\mathbb{PT}\cong\mathbb{CP}^3$ contains the null projective twistor 5-space $\mathbb{PN}\subset\mathbb{PT}$ (the real hypersurface of projective twistors satisfying the null condition $Z^\alpha\bar Z_\alpha=0$), and the associated nonlinear graviton / $\mathcal{H}$-space constructions produce complex four-manifolds with self-dual conformal structures from deformations of (regions of) twistor space.

Formulate and answer the following:

(a) Construct an explicit correspondence (or prove the non-existence of such a correspondence) between the ambient 5-manifold $\widetilde M^5$ of the perfect-fluid ambient cosmological construction and the null projective twistor 5-space $\mathbb{PN}$ of the embedded spacetime $M^4$, identifying how the fluid data on $\widetilde M^5$ translate into structures on $\mathbb{PN}$ and into associated $\mathcal{H}$-space constructions.

(b) Determine under what precise geometric and analytic conditions on the ambient fluid the asymptotic condition imposed in the ambient construction is well-defined and consistent (analogous to, but distinct from, the asymptotic conditions natural in the $\Lambda$-vacuum case).

context_brief: Characterizing implicative pseudo-BCK algebras by pseudo-filters
original_question: Let A be a pseudo-BCK algebra with binary operations ⇀ and ⇝ and top element 1. Call A an implicative pseudo-BCK algebra when, for every x and y in A, the identities (x ⇝ y) ⇀ x = x and (x ⇀ y) ⇝ x = x hold. A nonempty subset F of A is a pseudo-filter when it is upward closed and satisfies the closure rule that x in F together with either x ⇀ y in F or x ⇝ y in F implies y in F. A pseudo-filter F is Boolean when (x ⇀ y) ⇝ x in F implies x in F and (x ⇝ y) ⇀ x in F implies x in F for all x,y; it is implicative when (x ⇀ y) ⇀ x in F implies x in F and (x ⇝ y) ⇝ x in F implies x in F for all x,y. Let $(A,\rightharpoonup,\rightsquigarrow,1)$ be a pseudo-BCK algebra, where $\rightharpoonup$ and $\rightsquigarrow$ are binary operations and $1$ is the top element with respect to the induced order $x\le y\iff x\rightharpoonup y=1\iff x\rightsquigarrow y=1$. Call $A$ an implicative pseudo-BCK algebra if, for all $x,y\in A$,
$$(x\rightsquigarrow y)\rightharpoonup x=x\quad\text{and}\quad(x\rightharpoonup y)\rightsquigarrow x=x.$$
A nonempty subset $F\subseteq A$ is a pseudo-filter if it is upward closed (with respect to $\le$) and, for all $x,y\in A$, $x\in F$ together with $x\rightharpoonup y\in F$ or $x\rightsquigarrow y\in F$ implies $y\in F$. A pseudo-filter $F$ is called:
- a Boolean filter if for all $x,y\in A$, $(x\rightharpoonup y)\rightsquigarrow x\in F\Rightarrow x\in F$ and $(x\rightsquigarrow y)\rightharpoonup x\in F\Rightarrow x\in F$;
- an implicative pseudo-filter if for all $x,y\in A$, $(x\rightharpoonup y)\rightharpoonup x\in F\Rightarrow x\in F$ and $(x\rightsquigarrow y)\rightsquigarrow x\in F\Rightarrow x\in F$.

Prove or disprove: $A$ is an implicative pseudo-BCK algebra if and only if every pseudo-filter of $A$ is a Boolean filter, and equivalently if and only if every pseudo-filter of $A$ is an implicative pseudo-filter.

original_question: What additional obstructions prevent a Riemannian manifold M from admitting a CR-immersion into a Kahler manifold, beyond the necessary conditions that M admit a CR structure, that the orthogonal complement of Re(H plus conjugate H) in TM be integrable, and that Re(H plus conjugate H) be a minimal distribution? self_contained_problem:
Let $(\tilde M, J, \tilde g)$ be a Kähler manifold, with complex structure $J$ and compatible Riemannian metric $\tilde g$. A Riemannian submanifold $M \subset \tilde M$ is called a CR-submanifold if there exist two orthogonal smooth distributions $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal D^\perp$ on $M$ with $TM = \mathcal D \oplus \mathcal D^\perp$ such that $\mathcal D$ is holomorphic (i.e. $J\mathcal D_p = \mathcal D_p$ for every $p \in M$) and $\mathcal D^\perp$ is totally real (i.e. $J\mathcal D^\perp_p \subset T_p^\perp M$ for every $p \in M$). An isometric immersion of a Riemannian manifold $M$ into a Kähler manifold realizing $M$ as a CR-submanifold is called a CR-immersion.

Recall that an (abstract) CR structure on a smooth manifold $M$ is a complex subbundle $H \subset T_{\mathbb C}M = TM \otimes \mathbb C$ such that $H \cap \overline H = 0$ and $H$ is involutive (i.e. $[H,H] \subset H$). (i) $M$ carries a CR structure $H$;
(ii) the orthogonal complementary distribution $(\mathrm{Re}(H \oplus \overline H))^\perp$ in $TM$ is integrable;
(iii) the distribution $\mathrm{Re}(H \oplus \overline H)$ is a minimal distribution (its leaves, where defined, are minimal).

Problem: Determine whether there exist additional obstructions, beyond conditions (i)–(iii), that prevent a Riemannian manifold $M$ from admitting a CR-immersion into a Kähler manifold; and if so, exhibit and characterize such obstructions.

Let $x : M^n \to \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold into Euclidean $(n+1)$-space, and let $\Delta$ denote the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $M^n$ acting componentwise on the position vector $x$. The immersion $x$ is said to be of finite type if its position vector admits a finite spectral decomposition
$$x = x_0 + x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k,$$
where $x_0 \in \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is constant and each non-constant $x_i$ ($i=1,\ldots,k$) satisfies $\Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i$ for some real number $\lambda_i$, with the $\lambda_i$ pairwise distinct. The smallest such integer $k$ is called the type of $x$, and $M^n$ is then called a $k$-type submanifold. A finite-type submanifold is said to be of null $k$-type if one of the eigenvalues $\lambda_i$ in the above decomposition equals $0$. A minimal hypersurface is one whose mean curvature vector vanishes identically (equivalently $\Delta x = 0$). A standard hypersphere is a round sphere $S^n(r) \subset \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$.

Problem. Prove or disprove: every complete noncompact finite-type hypersurface in Euclidean space $\mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is either a minimal hypersurface or a hypersurface of null $2$-type. (Equivalently, the only complete hypersurfaces of finite type in $\mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ are the standard hyperspheres, the minimal hypersurfaces, and the hypersurfaces of null $2$-type.)
status_search_result: This is a well-known conjecture of B.-Y. Chen on finite-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean space. Recent surveys and research papers (e.g., on δ(2)- and δ(3)-ideal null 2-type hypersurfaces, and on related biharmonic problems) treat it as still-open, with progress only in special subcases such as small codimension restrictions, low number of distinct principal curvatures, or specific δ-ideal classes. No general resolution appears in the literature.

paper_title: Open Problems on Ultrafilters and Some Connections to the Continuum
original_question: Let λ be an infinite cardinal, let I be a set with |I| = λ, and let D be a regular ultrafilter on I. For the ultrapower (ω,<)^I/D of the usual linear order on the natural numbers, define C(D) to be the set of pairs (κ1,κ2) such that κ1 and κ2 are infinite regular cardinals, κ1 + κ2 ≤ |I|, and (ω,<)^I/D has a (κ1,κ2)-cut: a strictly increasing sequence of cofinality κ1 and a strictly decreasing sequence of cofinality κ2 with all left-side elements below all right-side elements and with no element of the ultrapower lying strictly between the two sequences. Which sets can occur as C(D) for regular ultrafilters D?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\lambda$ be an infinite cardinal and let $I$ be a set with $|I|=\lambda$. An ultrafilter $D$ on $I$ is called regular if there exists a family $\{X_i : i\in I\}\subseteq D$ such that every $i_0\in I$ belongs to only finitely many of the $X_i$. Form the ultrapower $(\omega,<)^I/D$ of the standard linear order on the natural numbers.

For infinite regular cardinals $\kappa_1,\kappa_2$ with $\kappa_1+\kappa_2\le |I|$, say that $(\omega,<)^I/D$ has a $(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)$-cut if there exist sequences $\langle a_\alpha : \alpha<\kappa_1\rangle$ and $\langle b_\beta : \beta<\kappa_2\rangle$ in the ultrapower such that:
- $\alpha<\alpha'<\kappa_1 \Rightarrow a_\alpha < a_{\alpha'}$ in $(\omega,<)^I/D$,
- $\beta<\beta'<\kappa_2 \Rightarrow b_\beta > b_{\beta'}$ in $(\omega,<)^I/D$,
- $a_\alpha < b_\beta$ for all $\alpha<\kappa_1$, $\beta<\kappa_2$,
- there is no element $c$ of $(\omega,<)^I/D$ with $a_\alpha<c<b_\beta$ for all $\alpha<\kappa_1$, $\beta<\kappa_2$.

Define the cut spectrum
$$C(D)=\{(\kappa_1,\kappa_2): \kappa_1,\kappa_2 \text{ infinite regular cardinals with } \kappa_1+\kappa_2\le|I|, \text{ and } (\omega,<)^I/D \text{ has a }(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)\text{-cut}\}.$$

Determine, as $\lambda$ varies over infinite cardinals and $D$ varies over regular ultrafilters on sets of size $\lambda$, exactly which subsets of $\{(\kappa_1,\kappa_2):\kappa_1,\kappa_2\text{ infinite regular},\ \kappa_1+\kappa_2\le\lambda\}$ arise as $C(D)$.
status_search_result: The problem of fully characterizing the possible cut spectra $C(D)$ of regular ultrafilters is a longstanding open question studied extensively by Malliaris and Shelah. Major partial results are known: regular ultrafilters cannot omit $(\kappa,\kappa)$-cuts under suitable treetops hypotheses, and the celebrated $p=t$ theorem of Malliaris–Shelah arose from related symmetric-cut analysis. However, the full classification of which sets can occur as $C(D)$ remains open, with the question continuing to drive current work on ultrafilter construction and Keisler's order.

original_question: Let D be a regular ultrafilter on I, and let C(D) be the set of all pairs of infinite regular cardinals (κ1,κ2) whose corresponding unfilled cuts occur in (ω,<)^I/D. If (κ1,κ2) belongs to C(D), must the symmetric cut (κ1 + κ2, κ1 + κ2) also belong to C(D)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $I$ be an infinite set and let $D$ be a regular ultrafilter on $I$ (i.e., there is a family $\{X_i : i \in I\} \subseteq D$ such that every infinite subfamily has empty intersection). Consider the ultrapower $(\omega, <)^I/D$ of the natural linear order. For regular infinite cardinals $\kappa_1, \kappa_2$, a $(\kappa_1, \kappa_2)$-pre-cut in $(\omega, <)^I/D$ is a pair of sequences $\langle a_\alpha : \alpha < \kappa_1\rangle$, $\langle b_\beta : \beta < \kappa_2\rangle$ with $a_\alpha < a_{\alpha'} < b_{\beta'} < b_\beta$ for $\alpha < \alpha' < \kappa_1$, $\beta' < \beta < \kappa_2$; such a pre-cut is unfilled (a cut) if there is no element $c$ of the ultrapower with $a_\alpha < c < b_\beta$ for all $\alpha < \kappa_1, \beta < \kappa_2$. Define
$$C(D) = \{(\kappa_1, \kappa_2) : \kappa_1, \kappa_2 \text{ regular infinite, and } (\omega,<)^I/D \text{ has an unfilled } (\kappa_1,\kappa_2)\text{-cut}\}.$$
Question: If $(\kappa_1, \kappa_2) \in C(D)$, must $(\kappa_1 + \kappa_2,\, \kappa_1 + \kappa_2) \in C(D)$?
category_tag: Regular ultrafilters and cuts in ultrapowers
status_search_result: The question of whether the existence of a $(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)$-cut in a regular ultrapower forces the symmetric cut $(\kappa_1+\kappa_2,\kappa_1+\kappa_2)$ to occur appears as an open problem in the literature on cofinality spectrum problems and regular ultrafilters by Malliaris and Shelah. Partial results exist (e.g., ruling out symmetric $(\kappa,\kappa)$-cuts under treetops hypotheses, and constructions producing many alternations of cuts using large cardinals), but no full resolution of this implication appears in recent searches.

paper_title: Open Problems on Ultrafilters and Some Connections to the Continuum
context_brief: Uniqueness of cuts in cut spectra
original_question: For a regular ultrafilter D on I with λ = |I|, say that D has uniqueness for a regular cardinal κ when any two cuts in C(D) with left cofinality κ have the same right cofinality: if (κ,θ) and (κ,θ') both belong to C(D), then θ = θ'. What are necessary and sufficient conditions on D ensuring that D has uniqueness for every regular κ ≤ λ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $I$ be an infinite set of cardinality $\lambda$, and let $D$ be a regular ultrafilter on $I$ (i.e., $D$ contains a family $\{X_i : i \in I\}$ such that every $\alpha \in I$ belongs to only finitely many $X_i$). Consider the linear order $(\mathbb{N}, <)^I / D$. A pair $(\kappa, \theta)$ of regular cardinals is said to belong to the cut spectrum $\mathcal{C}(D)$ if there exist sequences $(a_\alpha)_{\alpha < \kappa}$ and $(b_\beta)_{\beta < \theta}$ in $(\mathbb{N}, <)^I / D$ such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item $a_\alpha < a_{\alpha'}$ for $\alpha < \alpha' < \kappa$,
\item $b_\beta > b_{\beta'}$ for $\beta < \beta' < \theta$,
\item $a_\alpha < b_\beta$ for all $\alpha < \kappa$ and $\beta < \theta$,
\item there is no $c$ with $a_\alpha < c < b_\beta$ for all $\alpha, \beta$ (i.e., the pre-cut is unfilled).
\end{itemize}
Say that $D$ has uniqueness for the regular cardinal $\kappa$ if whenever $(\kappa, \theta)$ and $(\kappa, \theta')$ both belong to $\mathcal{C}(D)$, then $\theta = \theta'$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on a regular ultrafilter $D$ on $I$ for $D$ to have uniqueness for every regular cardinal $\kappa \le \lambda$.
status_search_result: The problem appears in the Malliaris–Shelah line of work on cofinality spectra and cut spectra of regular ultrafilters. While there are partial results characterizing which pairs $(\kappa,\theta)$ can appear in $\mathcal{C}(D)$ (e.g., symmetric cuts, peculiar cuts, lower cofinality conditions), a complete necessary-and-sufficient characterization of uniqueness for all regular $\kappa \le \lambda$ does not appear to have been established in the available literature, and the problem is posed as open in surveys on ultrafilter problems.

paper_title: Open Problems on Ultrafilters and Some Connections to the Continuum
context_brief: Cardinal invariants from weaker saturation notions
original_question: Let p denote the first cardinal κ for which Martin's axiom MA_κ for σ-centered partial orders fails. For weaker saturation notions than the one captured by p, especially those corresponding to combinatorially natural first-order theories such as T_feq, the theory of an existentially closed model of a parametrized family of independent equivalence relations, and T_{3,2}, the theory of the generic tetrahedron-free three-hypergraph, do these weaker notions give rise to natural and interesting cardinal invariants?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{p}$ denote the pseudo-intersection number, that is, the least cardinal $\kappa$ for which Martin's axiom $\mathrm{MA}_\kappa$ restricted to $\sigma$-centered partial orders fails. (Equivalently, the least cardinality of a family $\mathcal{F}$ of infinite subsets of $\omega$ that is closed under finite intersections, has the strong finite intersection property, and admits no single infinite subset of $\omega$ almost contained in every member of $\mathcal{F}$.)

The invariant $\mathfrak{p}$ may be viewed model-theoretically as a saturation cardinal associated with a particular complete first-order theory. Consider the following two combinatorially natural complete first-order theories:

(a) $T_{\mathrm{feq}}$: the model companion of the theory of a parametrized family of independent equivalence relations. The language has a binary predicate $E(x,y;z)$ such that for each parameter $z$, $E(\cdot,\cdot;z)$ is an equivalence relation, and the family of these equivalence relations is generic/independent; $T_{\mathrm{feq}}$ is the theory of its existentially closed models.

(b) $T_{3,2}$: the theory of the Fraïssé limit (generic structure) of the class of finite $3$-uniform hypergraphs that omit the complete $3$-hypergraph on $4$ vertices (the "tetrahedron-free generic $3$-hypergraph").

For each such theory $T$, one may associate a cardinal invariant $\mathfrak{p}(T)$ measuring the least $\kappa$ for which a natural saturation/realization property at level $\kappa$ fails (analogous to how $\mathfrak{p}$ arises from the saturation of a specific theory), with $\mathfrak{p}(T) \ge \mathfrak{p}$ since these theories are properly weaker (in Keisler's order, or in associated combinatorial complexity) than the theory giving rise to $\mathfrak{p}$.

Problem: Do the weaker saturation notions corresponding to $T_{\mathrm{feq}}$ and $T_{3,2}$ give rise to natural and interesting cardinal invariants of the continuum? In particular, identify such invariants $\mathfrak{p}(T_{\mathrm{feq}})$ and $\mathfrak{p}(T_{3,2})$, determine their ZFC-provable relationships with the standard invariants $\mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{t}, \mathfrak{b}, \mathfrak{d}, \dots$, and decide whether any of them can be proved strictly greater than $\mathfrak{p}$ in ZFC.
status_search_result: The problem asks whether weaker saturation notions, corresponding to theories such as T_feq and T_{3,2}, give rise to natural cardinal invariants. While Malliaris and Shelah's program connects Keisler's order with cardinal invariants of the continuum (most famously proving p = t), the literature available does not record a definitive identification of such invariants for T_feq or T_{3,2}, and the question is posed as an open direction. No source was found announcing a resolution.

paper_title: Open Problems on Ultrafilters and Some Connections to the Continuum
context_brief: Good for equality versus good ultrafilters
original_question: Let D be a regular ultrafilter. If D is good for equality, must C(D) be empty? Equivalently, must D be good, where good means |I|^+-good: every monotonic function from finite subsets of |I| into D has a multiplicative refinement? Equivalently, if D admits internal maps between small sets in the sense captured by good-for-equality, must D also admit internal order-preserving maps between small increasing sequences?
self_contained_problem:
Let I be an infinite index set and let D be a regular ultrafilter on I (regular: there exists a family {X_i : i ∈ I} ⊆ D such that every index of I lies in only finitely many X_i). 

For a cardinal λ, D is called λ-good if every monotonic function f: [λ]^{<ω} → D (i.e., u ⊆ v implies f(u) ⊇ f(v)) has a multiplicative refinement, that is, a function g: [λ]^{<ω} → D with g(u) ⊆ f(u) for all u and g(u ∪ v) = g(u) ∩ g(v) for all finite u, v. Say D is good if D is |I|^+-good.

Say D is good for equality if for every set X with |X| ≤ |I| and every function h: I → X, there exists a "distribution" producing internal representatives realizing equality types: more precisely, for every such h there is a refinement assigning to each pair (i, j) the truth value of h(i) = h(j) in a way that is multiplicative on D, capturing the existence of internal maps between small sets up to D-equality.

Let C(D) denote the set of cuts (a, b) in the linear order (ω, <)^I/D of cofinalities (κ_1, κ_2) with κ_1, κ_2 regular uncountable cardinals ≤ |I| that are not realized in this ultrapower (equivalently, the "symmetric cut spectrum" of D as customarily defined for regular ultrafilters).

Question: If D is good for equality, must C(D) = ∅? Equivalently, must every regular ultrafilter that is good for equality be good (i.e., |I|^+-good)?
status_search_result: The question is stated as a general open problem in the literature on ultrafilter saturation and Keisler's order. Recent works by Malliaris and Shelah (including ultrafilter-construction papers through 2025) continue to discuss good-for-equality as a distinct property whose relation to goodness and to realization of symmetric cuts remains an active line of research, with no resolution found in the searched sources.

A weakly peculiar (δ,θ)-D-cut in ω^ω consists of functions f_α for α < δ and g_β for β < θ such that the f_α sequence is increasing modulo D, the g_β sequence is decreasing modulo D, every f_α is below every g_β modulo D, and no function f can fill the cut after strengthening D by any D-positive set. Let spec_uq be the set of regular cardinals κ satisfying uniqueness for such cuts: if there are weakly peculiar cuts of left cofinality κ and right cofinalities θ0 and θ1, then θ0 = θ1. Let spec_uqm be the analogous spectrum in which the uniqueness is witnessed by an internal order-preserving partial map between the corresponding sequences. Are these two spectra equal? paper_title: Open Problems on Ultrafilters and Some Connections to the Continuum
original_question: Let D be a regular ultrafilter on λ, let μ be sufficiently large, and form the ultrapower N = (H(μ),∈)^λ/D, where H(μ) denotes the sets hereditarily of cardinality less than μ. Suppose N is λ^+-saturated for functions, meaning that every partial function from N to N whose domain has cardinality at most λ is extended by some internal function. Must D be good?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\lambda$ be an infinite cardinal and let $D$ be a regular ultrafilter on $\lambda$ (that is, $D$ contains a family $\{X_\alpha : \alpha < \lambda\} \subseteq D$ such that every $i \in \lambda$ lies in only finitely many $X_\alpha$). For a sufficiently large cardinal $\mu$, let $H(\mu)$ denote the set of all sets hereditarily of cardinality less than $\mu$, and form the ultrapower
$$N = (H(\mu), \in)^\lambda / D.$$
An element $g \in N$ is called an internal function (of $N$) if $N \models$ "$g$ is a function"; equivalently, $g = [\langle g_i : i < \lambda\rangle]_D$ where each $g_i$ is a function in $H(\mu)$.

Say that $N$ is $\lambda^+$-saturated for functions if, whenever $f$ is a partial function from $N$ to $N$ with $|\mathrm{dom}(f)| \le \lambda$, there exists an internal function $g \in N$ such that $g(x) = f(x)$ for every $x \in \mathrm{dom}(f)$.

Recall that $D$ is called good (i.e., $\lambda^+$-good) if every monotonic function $h : [\lambda]^{<\aleph_0} \to D$ admits a multiplicative refinement, i.e., a function $h' : [\lambda]^{<\aleph_0} \to D$ with $h'(u) \subseteq h(u)$ for all $u$ and $h'(u \cup v) = h'(u) \cap h'(v)$ for all $u, v \in [\lambda]^{<\aleph_0}$.

Question: Must every regular ultrafilter $D$ on $\lambda$ for which $N = (H(\mu), \in)^\lambda/D$ is $\lambda^+$-saturated for functions (for sufficiently large $\mu$) be good?

The status of this specific question could not be verified from the available sources.

paper_title: Some open problems in concurrences
original_question: Using the same definition of P* for orthogonal projections from a point P to the sides of a triangle ABC, find proofs of the Gergonne-point and Nagel-point existence criteria that avoid reliance on Maple or computational algebra and are more geometric or elegant.
self_contained_problem:
Let ABC be a triangle in the Euclidean plane, and for any point P in the plane let P* denote the triangle whose vertices are the orthogonal projections of P onto the three (extended) sides BC, CA, AB of ABC (the pedal triangle of P with respect to ABC).

Consider the following two known concurrence criteria, each of which gives a characterization of a special point of the triangle in terms of pedal-triangle constructions of the type P → P*:

(i) (Gergonne-point criterion) A characterization of the Gergonne point of ABC — the point at which the three cevians joining each vertex of ABC to the point where the incircle touches the opposite side concur — expressed via the operation P ↦ P*.

(ii) (Nagel-point criterion) A characterization of the Nagel point of ABC — the point at which the three cevians joining each vertex of ABC to the point where the opposite side is touched by the corresponding excircle concur — expressed via the same operation P ↦ P*.

Provide proofs of these two concurrence criteria that are purely synthetic / geometric in nature, avoiding any reliance on computer algebra systems or extensive symbolic computation. The goal is to obtain proofs whose steps consist of classical Euclidean-geometric arguments (for example using Ceva's theorem, isogonal/isotomic conjugacy, projective duality, properties of pedal triangles, Desargues' or Brianchon's theorem, trigonometric identities, etc.) rather than coordinate or algebraic verification.
status_search_result: A web search reveals substantial literature on the Gergonne and Nagel points, including synthetic treatments via Ceva's theorem, isotomic conjugacy, Brianchon's theorem, and generalizations to simplices. However, no specific source was located that gives elegant non-computational proofs of the particular pedal-triangle ("P*") concurrence criteria asked here. The status of this specific request is therefore unclear from available sources.

paper_title: Some open problems in concurrences
original_question: Let ABC be a triangle and P an interior point. Let P(A), P(B), and P(C) be the intersections of the cevians AP, BP, and CP with the side lines BC, CA, and AB, respectively. Erect perpendiculars to BC, CA, and AB at P(A), P(B), and P(C), and define P(*) when those three perpendiculars are concurrent. For standard triangle centers such as the centroid, circumcenter, incenter, orthocenter, Gergonne point, and Nagel point, determine the analogues for P(*) of the existence and identification questions asked for P*.
self_contained_problem:
Let ABC be a triangle in the Euclidean plane and let P be an interior point. Define the cevian traces
- P_A = AP ∩ BC,
- P_B = BP ∩ CA,
- P_C = CP ∩ AB.

At each trace erect the line perpendicular to the corresponding side of the triangle: let ℓ_A be the line through P_A perpendicular to BC, ℓ_B the line through P_B perpendicular to CA, and ℓ_C the line through P_C perpendicular to AB. When the three perpendiculars ℓ_A, ℓ_B, ℓ_C are concurrent, denote their common point by P^*; in this case call P "dual-perpendicular admissible" and call P^* the dual-perpendicular companion of P.

Investigate the following for each of the classical triangle centers P ∈ {centroid G, circumcenter O, incenter I, orthocenter H, Gergonne point Ge, Nagel point Na}:

(a) Determine whether P is dual-perpendicular admissible for every triangle ABC (i.e., whether ℓ_A, ℓ_B, ℓ_C are always concurrent for that choice of P). If admissibility holds only on a proper subfamily of triangles, characterize that subfamily.

(b) When P^* exists, identify the point P^* as a named triangle center (or give explicit barycentric/trilinear coordinates for P^* in terms of the side lengths a, b, c of ABC).

(c) Describe the locus of points P in the interior of ABC for which the three perpendiculars ℓ_A, ℓ_B, ℓ_C are concurrent, and describe the map P ↦ P^* on this locus.
status_search_result: A web search for the dual-perpendicular concurrence construction associated with the listed classical triangle centers did not turn up published resolutions identifying the resulting points P^* or characterizing the admissible locus for centroid, circumcenter, incenter, orthocenter, Gergonne, and Nagel points in this specific dual form. Standard references discuss the orthocenter case (P = orthocenter trivially yields concurrence via the altitudes) but a complete treatment for all six centers in the dual-perpendicular setting was not located, so the overall status is taken as unknown.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
original_question: For higher-genus correlation functions of rational conformal field theories, can one prove convergence of the series built from intertwining operators, so that their sums define functions on Teichmuller spaces and yield higher-genus chiral and full correlation functions?
self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a rational vertex operator algebra (satisfying the standard finiteness and reductivity conditions that make its module category a modular tensor category), and for each genus $g \geq 1$ consider the formal series built from compositions of intertwining operators among $V$-modules that are used to construct higher-genus chiral correlation functions on Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundary components. These series are indexed by insertions of intermediate modules along a pants decomposition of a genus-$g$ surface and depend on local coordinates and on moduli of the surface.

Prove that for every such configuration the series converges absolutely on the appropriate domain in the (infinite-dimensional) Teichmüller space of Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundary, so that its sum extends to a well-defined function on Teichmüller space. Show moreover that suitable combinations of these sums yield higher-genus chiral correlation functions (multivalued analytic functions on the moduli space of Riemann surfaces with marked points and local coordinates) and that pairing chiral and antichiral blocks via a modular-invariant assignment produces single-valued higher-genus full correlation functions of the corresponding rational conformal field theory.
status_search_result: The convergence of the higher-genus series built from intertwining operators is described as a major open problem, requiring conjectures on functions over infinite-dimensional Teichmüller spaces and moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundaries. Recent progress (Radnell–Schippers–Staubach on the moduli spaces, and modular invariance results for logarithmic intertwining operators) addresses related sub-problems, but the full higher-genus convergence statement does not appear to have been established.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
original_question: For a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, is every grading-restricted generalized module of finite length completely reducible exactly when, for every positive integer n, the nth cohomology of the algebra with coefficients in any bimodule is zero? In particular, does the same equivalence hold for a grading-restricted vertex algebra viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, allowing the left and right bimodule actions to differ?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A meromorphic open-string vertex algebra (MOSVA) is a Z-graded vector space V = ⊕_{n∈Z} V_(n) with grading-restriction conditions (dim V_(n) < ∞ and V_(n) = 0 for n sufficiently negative), equipped with a vertex map Y_V: V ⊗ V → V[[x, x^{-1}]] and a vacuum 1 ∈ V_(0), satisfying the rationality, associativity, identity, creation, d/dx, and grading axioms appropriate to the non-commutative (open-string) setting (in which Y_V(u, x_1)Y_V(v, x_2) and Y_V(v, x_2)Y_V(u, x_1) are not required to be analytic continuations of each other, but products and iterates of vertex operators converge to rational functions on suitable domains). A V-bimodule W is a graded vector space carrying compatible left and right vertex operator actions in the MOSVA sense. For a V-bimodule W and a positive integer n, one has the n-th cohomology group H^n(V, W) defined via the chain complex of "shuffle-compatible" maps from configuration spaces of n points to W (the cohomology theory developed for MOSVAs that generalizes Huang's cohomology of vertex algebras). A grading-restricted generalized V-module is a graded module M = ⊕_{α∈C, n∈Z} M_{[α]+n} with dim M_{[α]+n} < ∞ and finite-dimensional generalized L(0)-eigenspaces, vanishing in sufficiently negative real parts. Such a module is completely reducible if every grading-restricted generalized V-submodule has a graded complement that is also a submodule.

Problem. Prove or disprove the following equivalence:

(a) Every grading-restricted generalized V-module of finite length is completely reducible.

(b) For every positive integer n and every V-bimodule W, H^n(V, W) = 0.

In particular, establish the analogous equivalence for a grading-restricted vertex algebra V (in the usual commutative sense), regarded as a MOSVA, where the bimodule W is allowed to have left and right V-actions that need not coincide.
status_search_result: The conjecture remains open in full generality. Partial progress has been made: Huang and Qi proved (under a convergence assumption) that vanishing of the first cohomology with coefficients in any bimodule implies complete reducibility of finite-length modules satisfying a composability condition, giving one direction in degree n = 1. The full equivalence over all positive degrees n and all bimodules has not, to current evidence, been established.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
original_question: Can one find a criterion stated in terms of a grading-restricted vertex algebra itself that determines complete reducibility of its modules?
self_contained_problem:
Let $V = \bigoplus_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} V_{(n)}$ be a grading-restricted vertex algebra; that is, $V$ is a $\mathbb{Z}$-graded vector space equipped with a vacuum vector $\mathbf{1}$, an endomorphism $D$, and a vertex operator map $Y: V \otimes V \to V((x))$ satisfying the standard axioms (vacuum, $D$-derivative, and Jacobi/weak commutativity-associativity), and such that $\dim V_{(n)} < \infty$ for all $n$ and $V_{(n)} = 0$ for $n$ sufficiently negative. A grading-restricted generalized $V$-module is a $\mathbb{C}$-graded vector space $W = \bigoplus_{h \in \mathbb{C}} W_{[h]}$ with a vertex operator $Y_W: V \otimes W \to W((x))$ satisfying the module axioms, such that $\dim W_{[h]} < \infty$ and $W_{[h-n]} = 0$ for $n$ sufficiently large (depending on $h$). Say that $V$ has the complete reducibility property if every grading-restricted generalized $V$-module is a direct sum of irreducible grading-restricted $V$-modules.

Problem: Formulate a criterion, stated purely in terms of intrinsic structural data of the grading-restricted vertex algebra $V$ itself (and not in terms of properties verified on the category of its modules), that is equivalent to $V$ having the complete reducibility property.
status_search_result: Partial progress exists: Huang and Qi have developed a cohomological approach (using the first cohomology of grading-restricted vertex algebras with coefficients in bimodules) that yields complete-reducibility criteria under composability/finiteness hypotheses, and related work establishes complete reducibility under conditions such as $C_1$-cofiniteness. However, a fully intrinsic if-and-only-if criterion stated solely on $V$ itself appears not to have been established in full generality.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
original_question: In the nonsemisimple setting relevant to logarithmic conformal field theories, can one define the correct notion of modular tensor category and prove that the braided tensor category of grading-restricted generalized modules for a simple C2-cofinite vertex operator algebra satisfying V(0)=C1, V(n)=0 for n<0, and V' equivalent to V has this structure? From such a nonsemisimple modular tensor category, can one still construct a three-dimensional topological quantum field theory and invariants of knots and 3-manifolds?
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on all three parts. Definitions of nonsemisimple (finite factorizable ribbon) modular tensor categories have been formulated (Lyubashenko; Kerler–Lyubashenko; Shimizu). Huang and collaborators (notably Creutzig–Jiang–Hung–Yang and McRae) have established that the category of grading-restricted generalized modules for a $C_2$-cofinite VOA satisfying the stated conditions is a finite (often rigid factorizable) braided ribbon tensor category, with modular invariance of pseudo-trace conformal blocks proved (Fiordalisi; recent work of McRae–Yang and others 2023–2024). De Renzi–Gainutdinov–Patureau-Mirand–Runkel–Tarrach (Selecta Math. 2021) constructed 3d TQFTs from nonsemisimple modular categories, producing knot and 3-manifold invariants. Full rigidity of $\mathcal{C}_V$ in complete generality and a uniform TQFT construction directly from VOA data remain not fully settled, so the overall problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
original_question: Let V be a simple C2-cofinite vertex operator algebra with V(0)=C1, V(n)=0 for n<0, V' equivalent to V, and let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V, without assuming complete reducibility. Do the twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among all g-twisted V-modules satisfy associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance?
self_contained_problem:
Let $V=\bigoplus_{n\ge 0}V_{(n)}$ be a simple vertex operator algebra over $\mathbb{C}$ such that:
(i) $V_{(0)}=\mathbb{C}\mathbf{1}$ and $V_{(n)}=0$ for $n<0$;
(ii) $V$ is $C_2$-cofinite, i.e. $\dim V/C_2(V)<\infty$ where $C_2(V)=\mathrm{span}\{u_{-2}v : u,v\in V\}$;
(iii) $V$ is isomorphic to its contragredient module $V'$.
Let $G$ be a finite group of automorphisms of $V$. Do not assume that the category of (generalized) $V$-modules is semisimple, so logarithmic modules and logarithmic intertwining operators must be considered.

For each $g\in G$, consider the category of grading-restricted generalized $g$-twisted $V$-modules, and the spaces of (logarithmic) twisted intertwining operators of types $\binom{W_3}{W_1\,W_2}$ where $W_i$ is a $g_i$-twisted $V$-module ($i=1,2,3$) with $g_3=g_1g_2$.

Prove or disprove: the twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among all $g$-twisted $V$-modules ($g\in G$) satisfy the associativity property (the product of two such operators can be expanded as an iterate, and vice versa, in the sense of analytic continuation and convergence of the relevant multivalued series), the commutativity property (products of two such operators in different orders are analytic continuations of each other), and the modular invariance property (the space spanned by appropriate shifted pseudo-$q$-traces of products of geometrically modified twisted logarithmic intertwining operators is invariant under the action of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$).
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: associativity and commutativity for (logarithmic) twisted intertwining operators among g-twisted modules over C2-cofinite VOAs have been established in work on twisted intertwining operators for not-necessarily-commuting automorphisms, and modular invariance of (logarithmic) intertwining operators in the untwisted C2-cofinite setting was proven in the 2024 Communications in Mathematical Physics paper (arXiv:2305.15152). However, a complete proof of all three properties (associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance) simultaneously for the twisted logarithmic case under the stated hypotheses does not yet appear to be fully established in the literature.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
original_question: Can one construct a functor from the category of Calabi-Yau manifolds to the category of N=2 vertex operator superalgebras such that the Fermat quintic threefold maps to the N=2 vertex operator superalgebra for the Gepner model and deformations of Calabi-Yau manifolds correspond to deformations of N=2 superconformal field theories?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{CY}$ denote the category whose objects are Calabi-Yau manifolds (compact Kähler manifolds with vanishing first Chern class, equipped with a Ricci-flat Kähler metric) and whose morphisms are an appropriate notion of Calabi-Yau morphisms. Let $\mathcal{V}_{N=2}$ denote the category whose objects are vertex operator superalgebras endowed with an $N=2$ superconformal structure (i.e. a representation of the $N=2$ super-Virasoro algebra by fields whose modes act on the underlying super vector space, compatible with the vertex algebra structure), and whose morphisms are vertex superalgebra homomorphisms preserving the $N=2$ structure.

Construct a functor 
$$F : \mathcal{CY} \longrightarrow \mathcal{V}_{N=2}$$
satisfying both of the following properties:

(1) The Fermat quintic threefold $\{[z_0:\dots:z_4]\in\mathbb{P}^4 : z_0^5+z_1^5+z_2^5+z_3^5+z_4^5=0\}$ is sent by $F$ to the $N=2$ vertex operator superalgebra underlying the Gepner model $(k=3)^{\otimes 5}$ (the GSO-projected tensor product of five copies of the $N=2$ minimal model at level $k=3$).

(2) Deformations of a Calabi-Yau manifold $X$ (in the sense of complex-structure and Kähler-class deformations) correspond, via $F$, to deformations of the associated $N=2$ superconformal field theory (i.e. to deformations of the $N=2$ vertex operator superalgebra $F(X)$ within $\mathcal{V}_{N=2}$).
category_tag: Vertex operator superalgebras and Calabi-Yau geometry
status_search_result: Partial constructions exist (e.g. the chiral de Rham complex of Malikov–Schechtman–Vaintrob attaches a sheaf of vertex superalgebras to a complex manifold, and Ben-Zvi–Heluani–Szczesny and Heluani showed that a Ricci-flat Kähler metric induces an N=2 superconformal structure on its global sections of the twisted chiral de Rham complex). However, no construction is known that simultaneously assigns to the Fermat quintic the Gepner model VOSA and realizes Calabi-Yau deformations as N=2 SCFT deformations in a functorial way. The problem is generally regarded as open.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
original_question: Assuming N=2 vertex operator superalgebras for Calabi-Yau manifolds, their basic representation theory, and full N=2 superconformal field theories can be constructed, can physicists' conjectures about Calabi-Yau manifolds, such as quantum cohomology and mirror symmetry, be formulated and proved mathematically using those structures?
self_contained_problem:
Assume that the following can be carried out rigorously within the framework of vertex operator superalgebras and conformal field theory:

(a) For every Calabi-Yau manifold X (a compact Kähler manifold with vanishing first Chern class), one can construct an N=2 vertex operator superalgebra V_X, i.e. a vertex operator superalgebra equipped with an action of the N=2 superconformal algebra (generated by a Virasoro field L, a u(1)-current J, and two odd supercurrents G^+, G^-) with central charge c = 3·dim_C(X), that suitably encodes the geometry of X.

(b) The basic representation theory of V_X has been established: classification of irreducible modules, modular invariance of characters, fusion rules, and the structure of intertwining operator algebras.

(c) From V_X one can construct a full N=2 superconformal field theory associated to X (a consistent system of correlation functions on Riemann surfaces of arbitrary genus respecting modular invariance, locality, and the sewing axioms).

Under these assumptions, formulate and prove, purely within this mathematical framework, the physicists' conjectures concerning Calabi-Yau manifolds. In particular:

(i) Realize the quantum cohomology ring of X as a structure naturally extracted from V_X and its associated N=2 superconformal field theory (for instance, from a chiral ring of suitable BPS states or from genus-zero correlators), and prove that this structure coincides with the quantum cohomology defined by Gromov-Witten invariants of X.

A topological space $X$ is countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D_1, D_2 \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h : X \to X$ with $h(D_1) = D_2$. For a cardinal $\kappa$, declare two countable dense subsets of $X$ equivalent if some self-homeomorphism of $X$ maps one onto the other; call $X$ $\tfrac{1}{\kappa}$-CDH if there are exactly $\kappa$ equivalence classes of countable dense subsets of $X$ under this relation. A Polish space is a separable, completely metrizable topological space.

Question: Does every Polish $\tfrac{1}{\omega}$-CDH space $X$ contain a nonempty dense open subspace $U \subseteq X$ such that $U$ (with the subspace topology) is countable dense homogeneous?
status_search_result: No published resolution was found. Recent works on countable dense homogeneity (e.g., on zero-dimensional metrizable CDH spaces and CDH topological groups, 2024–2025) continue to investigate structural questions about Polish CDH spaces but do not report a solution to this specific question about Polish 1/ω-CDH spaces containing a dense open CDH subspace.

paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
original_question: Does there exist a homogeneous subset of the real line R that is 1/2-CDH, meaning that it has exactly two equivalence classes of countable dense subsets under self-homeomorphisms?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a separable topological space. Call two countable dense subsets D, E ⊆ X equivalent if there exists a homeomorphism h : X → X with h(D) = E; this is an equivalence relation on the family D(X) of all countable dense subsets of X. Let the CDH-number of X be the cardinality of D(X) modulo this relation. The space X is called n-CDH (for a cardinal n) if its CDH-number equals n; in particular, X is 1-CDH (i.e. countable dense homogeneous) if any two countable dense subsets are related by a self-homeomorphism, and X is (1/2)-CDH if it has exactly two equivalence classes of countable dense subsets. Recall that X is homogeneous if for every x, y ∈ X there is a homeomorphism of X carrying x to y.

Question: Does there exist a subset X ⊆ ℝ (with the subspace topology) such that X is homogeneous and X is (1/2)-CDH, i.e., the action of the self-homeomorphism group of X on its countable dense subsets has exactly two orbits?
status_search_result: Web searches surface the original problem list and surrounding literature on countable dense homogeneity (works of Hrušák, van Mill, Medini and others), but no source located explicitly resolves the existence of a homogeneous (1/2)-CDH subset of ℝ. The status appears to still be open, but no definitive recent reference confirming resolution was found, so the status is recorded as unknown.

paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
original_question: Is it consistent that there is a filter that is 1/kappa-CDH for some cardinal kappa strictly between 1 and the continuum c?
self_contained_problem:
A filter on the countable set $\omega$ is identified, via characteristic functions, with a subset of the Cantor set $2^\omega$, thereby inheriting a separable metrizable topology. A topological space $X$ is countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D,E\subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h:X\to X$ with $h(D)=E$. 

For a cardinal $\kappa\geq 1$, say that a filter $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^\omega$ is $\tfrac{1}{\kappa}$-CDH if there are exactly $\kappa$ orbits of countable dense subsets of $\mathcal{F}$ under the action of the homeomorphism group $\mathrm{Homeo}(\mathcal{F})$; equivalently, there is a family $\{D_\alpha:\alpha<\kappa\}$ of countable dense subsets of $\mathcal{F}$ such that every countable dense subset of $\mathcal{F}$ is mapped onto some $D_\alpha$ by a self-homeomorphism of $\mathcal{F}$, and $\kappa$ is the least such cardinal. (Thus $\tfrac{1}{1}$-CDH coincides with CDH.) Let $\mathfrak{c}=2^{\aleph_0}$ denote the cardinality of the continuum.

Is it consistent with ZFC that there exists a filter $\mathcal{F}$ on $\omega$ and a cardinal $\kappa$ with $1<\kappa<\mathfrak{c}$ such that $\mathcal{F}$ is $\tfrac{1}{\kappa}$-CDH?
status_search_result: The question is attributed to Kunen, Medini, and Zdomskyy and is recorded as an open problem in the recent literature on countable dense homogeneity of filters. Searches on related work (Hrušák–Hernández, Medini–Zdomskyy, and follow-up papers from 2024–2025 on CDH filters and topological groups) do not indicate a resolution: the existence of an intermediate $1/\kappa$-CDH filter for $1<\kappa<\mathfrak{c}$ remains unsettled.

original_question: Is the Hilbert cube, equipped with its standard metric, Lipschitz countable dense homogeneous, meaning that for every epsilon > 0 and every two countable dense subsets A and B there is an epsilon-almost isometry h with h[A] = B?
self_contained_problem:
Equip the Hilbert cube $Q = \prod_{n=1}^{\infty} [0,1]$ with its standard metric $d(x,y) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} 2^{-n} |x_n - y_n|$. Given $\varepsilon > 0$, a bijection $h\colon (X,d) \to (X,d)$ between metric spaces is called an $\varepsilon$-almost isometry if $(1-\varepsilon)\, d(x,y) \le d(h(x), h(y)) \le (1+\varepsilon)\, d(x,y)$ for all $x,y \in X$. A metric space $(X,d)$ is said to be Lipschitz countable dense homogeneous (Lipschitz-CDH) if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every pair $A, B$ of countable dense subsets of $X$, there exists an $\varepsilon$-almost isometry $h\colon X \to X$ with $h[A] = B$.

Determine whether the Hilbert cube $(Q,d)$, with its standard metric as above, is Lipschitz-CDH.

The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: compact CDH spaces without Cantor sets
original_question: Does there exist a compact countable dense homogeneous space that contains no copy of the Cantor set?
self_contained_problem:
A topological space $X$ is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if $X$ is separable and, for every pair of countable dense subsets $D_1, D_2 \subseteq X$, there exists a homeomorphism $h \colon X \to X$ with $h(D_1) = D_2$. A space is said to contain a copy of the Cantor set if it has a subspace homeomorphic to the standard Cantor set $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$.

Question: Does there exist a compact Hausdorff space that is countable dense homogeneous and contains no topological copy of the Cantor set?
status_search_result: Under the Continuum Hypothesis, a compact Hausdorff CDH crowded space containing no copy of the Cantor set has been constructed (Hrušák, "Countable dense homogeneity and the Cantor set", arXiv:1705.01203). A ZFC construction does not appear to be known, so the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
context_brief: minimal weight of separable non-CDH manifolds
original_question: Is the cardinal invariant b the minimal possible weight of a separable non-countable-dense-homogeneous manifold; if not, is there a natural combinatorial characterization of that minimal weight?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A topological space $X$ is countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D, E \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h \colon X \to X$ with $h(D) = E$. The weight $w(X)$ of a topological space $X$ is the minimum cardinality of a base for its topology. A manifold here is a (Hausdorff) topological space in which every point has an open neighborhood homeomorphic to some Euclidean (or Hilbert-cube) chart; in particular separable manifolds of arbitrarily large weight are admitted (so the manifold need not be second countable).

Let $\mathfrak{b}$ denote the bounding number, i.e. the least cardinality of an unbounded family in $(\omega^{\omega}, \le^{*})$, where $f \le^{*} g$ means $f(n) \le g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$.

Define
$$\mu = \min\{\, w(M) : M \text{ is a separable manifold that is not CDH}\,\}.$$

Questions.
(a) Is $\mu = \mathfrak{b}$?
(b) If not, is there a natural combinatorial characterization (in the sense of cardinal invariants of the continuum) of the cardinal $\mu$?
status_search_result: No published resolution of this problem was located. It is stated as an open problem in the survey on countable dense homogeneity, and subsequent web searches did not turn up any paper announcing that the minimal weight of a separable non-CDH manifold equals $\mathfrak{b}$ or providing a combinatorial characterization. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
original_question: For beta-expansions, let d_beta(1-) denote the left-limit expansion of 1, and call beta a Parry number when d_beta(1-) is eventually periodic. Does there exist a Salem number beta that is not a Parry number, meaning that d_beta(1-) is not eventually periodic? In particular, does the Salem-periodicity problem have a counterexample associated with x^6 - 3x^5 - x^4 - 7x^3 - x^2 - 3x + 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let β > 1 be a real number. The Rényi β-expansion of 1 is defined by iterating the map T_β(x) = βx − ⌊βx⌋ on [0,1): set a_i(1) = ⌊β · T_β^{i−1}(1)⌋ for i ≥ 1, giving d_β(1) = a_1 a_2 a_3 …. The left-sided expansion d_β(1^−) is defined as the limit lim_{x → 1^−} d_β(x), which coincides with d_β(1) when d_β(1) is infinite (not ending in 0^ω), and otherwise is the standard left-limit modification. A real number β > 1 is called a Parry number if d_β(1^−) is eventually periodic. A Salem number is a real algebraic integer β > 1 all of whose Galois conjugates have modulus ≤ 1, with at least one conjugate of modulus exactly 1.

(a) Does there exist a Salem number β that is not a Parry number, i.e. such that d_β(1^−) is not eventually periodic?

(b) In particular, let β be the real root greater than 1 of the polynomial x^6 − 3x^5 − x^4 − 7x^3 − x^2 − 3x + 1 (a Salem number of degree 6). Is d_β(1^−) eventually periodic, or does this β provide a counterexample to the Parry property among Salem numbers?
status_search_result: The question whether every Salem number is a Parry number remains open. It is known for Salem numbers of degree 4 (Boyd), and conjectured to hold for degree 6 but expected to fail for some degree 8 Salem numbers based on heuristics. Recent works (e.g., Akiyama–Hichri 2022 on periodic expansion of 1 by Salem numbers, and work on degree-6 co-factors) provide only partial density results, not a full resolution. The specific candidate x^6 − 3x^5 − x^4 − 7x^3 − x^2 − 3x + 1 raised by Boyd has not been resolved.

paper_title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
original_question: For a Salem number beta, let d_beta(x) be the greedy beta-expansion digit sequence of x in [0,1). Is d_beta(x) eventually periodic for every x in Q(beta) ∩ [0,1)?
self_contained_problem:
Let β > 1 be a real number. The greedy β-expansion of x ∈ [0,1) is the sequence d_β(x) = (a_1, a_2, a_3, …) of nonnegative integers a_i ∈ {0, 1, …, ⌈β⌉−1} defined by the iteration of the β-transformation T_β(y) = βy − ⌊βy⌋: set a_i = ⌊β T_β^{i−1}(x)⌋ for i ≥ 1, so that x = ∑_{i≥1} a_i β^{−i}. The sequence d_β(x) is said to be eventually periodic if there exist integers N ≥ 0 and p ≥ 1 such that a_{n+p} = a_n for every n > N.

A Salem number is a real algebraic integer β > 1 all of whose other Galois conjugates have modulus ≤ 1, with at least one conjugate of modulus exactly 1. Let Q(β) denote the field generated by β over the rationals.

Question: For every Salem number β, is the greedy β-expansion d_β(x) eventually periodic for every x ∈ Q(β) ∩ [0,1)?
status_search_result: The analogous statement for Pisot β is a theorem of Schmidt (1980), but the Salem case is widely regarded as open. It is known only in restricted situations (e.g., for Salem β of degree 4, by Boyd), and even the eventual periodicity of d_β(1) is conjectural for general Salem β, verified only in low degree with conflicting heuristics in higher degree.

original_question: Let r = (r_0, r_1, ..., r_{d-1}) be a shift radix system parameter vector, meaning that every integer sequence governed by 0 <= r_0 a_n + r_1 a_{n+1} + ... + r_{d-1} a_{n+d-1} + a_{n+d} < 1 eventually reaches the trivial all-zero cycle. The associated polynomial is x^d + r_{d-1}x^{d-1} + ... + r_0. Must every polynomial associated with a shift radix system be contractive, meaning that all of its roots have modulus less than one?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $d\ge 1$ and a vector $\mathbf{r}=(r_0,r_1,\ldots,r_{d-1})\in\mathbb{R}^d$. Define the map $\tau_{\mathbf{r}}:\mathbb{Z}^d\to\mathbb{Z}^d$ by
$$\tau_{\mathbf{r}}(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1})=(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{d-1},-\lfloor r_0 a_0+r_1 a_1+\cdots+r_{d-1}a_{d-1}\rfloor),$$
so that the integer sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge 0}$ generated by $\mathbf{r}$ satisfies
$$0\le r_0 a_n+r_1 a_{n+1}+\cdots+r_{d-1} a_{n+d-1}+a_{n+d}<1\qquad (n\ge 0).$$
The vector $\mathbf{r}$ is called a shift radix system (SRS) if, for every starting tuple $(a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1})\in\mathbb{Z}^d$, the orbit under $\tau_{\mathbf{r}}$ eventually reaches the all-zero fixed point $(0,\ldots,0)$. Associate to $\mathbf{r}$ the polynomial
$$p_{\mathbf{r}}(x)=x^d+r_{d-1}x^{d-1}+\cdots+r_1 x+r_0\in\mathbb{R}[x].$$
The polynomial $p_{\mathbf{r}}$ is called contractive if every complex root of $p_{\mathbf{r}}$ has modulus strictly less than $1$.

Question: Is it true that for every $d\ge 1$ and every shift radix system $\mathbf{r}\in\mathbb{R}^d$, the associated polynomial $p_{\mathbf{r}}$ is contractive?
status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in surveys of shift radix systems. It is known that contractivity of $p_{\mathbf r}$ implies that every orbit of $\tau_{\mathbf r}$ is ultimately periodic (so the SRS set lies in the closure of the Schur–Cohn region), but the converse — that every SRS polynomial must have all roots inside the unit disk — appears to remain unresolved in the literature.

original_question: In the two-dimensional shift radix system parameter plane with coordinates (x,y), prove or disprove that every point in the region {(x,y) | 0 < 2x < y < x + 1} defines a shift radix system; equivalently, determine whether that whole open region is an SRS region.
self_contained_problem:
For a parameter vector $r=(r_0,r_1,\dots,r_{d-1})\in\mathbb{R}^d$, define the mapping $\tau_r:\mathbb{Z}^d\to\mathbb{Z}^d$ by
$$\tau_r(a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{d-1}) = (a_1,a_2,\dots,a_{d-1},-\lfloor r_0 a_0 + r_1 a_1 + \cdots + r_{d-1}a_{d-1}\rfloor).$$
The parameter $r$ is called a shift radix system (SRS) if for every $a\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $\tau_r^n(a)=0$. Let
$$\mathcal{D}_d := \{r\in\mathbb{R}^d : r \text{ is an SRS}\}.$$
Consider the two-dimensional case $d=2$ with parameters $(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2$, where
$$\tau_{(x,y)}(a_0,a_1) = (a_1, -\lfloor x a_0 + y a_1 \rfloor).$$
Prove or disprove that
$$\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2 : 0 < 2x < y < x+1\} \subseteq \mathcal{D}_2,$$
i.e., that every point of this open region defines a shift radix system.
