paper_title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
original_question: Let tau be an irreducible Pisot substitution on the alphabet {0,1,...,d-1}, and consider a fixed point of tau. Does there exist a nonempty word w such that occurrences of infinite patterns of the form w x_1 w x_2 w x_3 ... are relatively dense in that fixed point, where the x_i are arbitrary words and the length condition |w x_1 w x_2 ... w x_m| = |tau^{m-1}(w y)| is satisfied for some fixed word y?
self_contained_problem:
Let $d\geq 2$ and let $\tau$ be a substitution on the alphabet $\mathcal{A}=\{0,1,\dots,d-1\}$, that is, a map $\tau:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}^*$ extended to $\mathcal{A}^*$ and $\mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{N}}$ by concatenation. Assume $\tau$ is primitive (some power of its incidence matrix $M_\tau\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{d\times d}$ has all entries positive), and that the Perron–Frobenius eigenvalue $\beta$ of $M_\tau$ is a Pisot number whose minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$ has degree $d$ (i.e. $\tau$ is an irreducible Pisot substitution). Let $u=u_0u_1u_2\cdots\in\mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{N}}$ be a fixed point of $\tau$, so $\tau(u)=u$.

A set $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ is called relatively dense if there exists $R>0$ such that every interval of length $R$ in $\mathbb{N}$ meets $S$.

Determine whether there must exist a nonempty word $w\in\mathcal{A}^+$ and a fixed word $y\in\mathcal{A}^*$ such that the set of indices $n\in\mathbb{N}$ for which there is an infinite sequence of words $x_1,x_2,x_3,\ldots\in\mathcal{A}^*$ with
$$u_n u_{n+1} u_{n+2} \cdots = w\,x_1\,w\,x_2\,w\,x_3\,\cdots$$
and satisfying, for every $m\geq 1$,
$$|w x_1 w x_2 \cdots w x_m| = |\tau^{m-1}(wy)|,$$
is relatively dense in $\mathbb{N}$.
status_search_result: The Pisot substitution conjecture and related strong coincidence conjecture for irreducible Pisot substitutions remain open in general. While the Pisot conjecture has been resolved for beta-substitutions and various special cases, the general question regarding combinatorial coincidence structure in fixed points of irreducible Pisot substitutions is still considered open in the literature.

original_question: Let alpha be an algebraic integer all of whose conjugates have modulus greater than one, let N(alpha) be the absolute norm of alpha over Q, and set B = {0, ±1, ±2, ..., ±(N(alpha)-1)}. Is there a simple proof that Z[alpha] equals B[alpha]?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\alpha$ be an algebraic integer such that every Galois conjugate of $\alpha$ (over $\mathbb{Q}$), including $\alpha$ itself, has absolute value strictly greater than $1$. Let
$$N(\alpha) = \left|\mathrm{N}_{\mathbb{Q}(\alpha)/\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha)\right|$$
denote the absolute value of the field norm of $\alpha$, and set
$$B = \{0, \pm 1, \pm 2, \ldots, \pm(N(\alpha)-1)\} \subset \mathbb{Z}.$$
Define $B[\alpha]$ to be the set of all finite sums $\sum_{i=0}^{n} b_i \alpha^i$ with $n \ge 0$ and $b_i \in B$.

Provide a simple/elementary proof (or show that no such proof exists) of the equality
$$\mathbb{Z}[\alpha] = B[\alpha].$$
That is, show that every element of the ring $\mathbb{Z}[\alpha]$ can be written as a polynomial in $\alpha$ with integer coefficients drawn from $B$.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Asymptotic Geometric Analysis
context_brief: hyperplane conjecture for centered convex bodies
original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant c > 0, independent of the dimension n, such that every centered convex body K in R^n with volume |K| = 1 has at least one hyperplane section through the origin whose (n-1)-dimensional volume is greater than c?
self_contained_problem:
A convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact convex set with nonempty interior. It is called centered if its centroid (barycenter) is the origin. For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, let $|K|$ denote its $n$-dimensional Lebesgue volume, and for a hyperplane $H\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ through the origin let $|K\cap H|$ denote the $(n-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue volume of the section $K\cap H$.

Does there exist an absolute constant $c>0$, independent of the dimension $n$, with the following property: for every $n\ge 1$ and every centered convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with $|K|=1$, there exists a hyperplane $H$ through the origin such that
$$|K\cap H| > c\,?$$
status_search_result: Bourgain's hyperplane (slicing) conjecture was resolved affirmatively in December 2024 by Boaz Klartag and Joseph Lehec, using a recent bound of Qingyang Guan together with stochastic localization, Milman's M-ellipsoid theory, and stability estimates for the Shannon–Stam inequality. The result has appeared in Geometric and Functional Analysis.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Asymptotic Geometric Analysis
original_question: For a fixed p > 0 and an n-dimensional convex body K, choose n+1 points x_1, ..., x_{n+1} independently and uniformly in K and let m_p(K) be the normalized p-th moment of the volume of the random simplex conv{x_1, ..., x_{n+1}}. Determine, up to nondegenerate affine transformations, which convex bodies minimize m_p(K) and which convex bodies maximize m_p(K); in particular, settle the open maximization direction in dimensions n >= 3.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ be an integer and let $p>0$ be fixed. For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior) of volume $|K|>0$, let $X_1,\dots,X_{n+1}$ be independent random points distributed uniformly in $K$, and define the normalized $p$-th moment of the random-simplex volume by
$$m_p(K)\;=\;\frac{\mathbb{E}\bigl[\,\mathrm{vol}_n(\mathrm{conv}\{X_1,\dots,X_{n+1}\})^{p}\,\bigr]}{|K|^{p}}.$$
The quantity $m_p(K)$ is invariant under nondegenerate affine transformations of $K$.

(a) Determine all convex bodies $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, up to nondegenerate affine transformations, that minimize $m_p(K)$ among all $n$-dimensional convex bodies.

(b) Determine all convex bodies $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, up to nondegenerate affine transformations, that maximize $m_p(K)$ among all $n$-dimensional convex bodies. In particular, settle this maximization problem for every dimension $n\ge 3$ (it is conjectured that the maximizers are exactly the simplices).
status_search_result: The minimizer direction is classically known to be ellipsoids (Groemer), while the maximization direction—conjecturally simplices—remains open for dimensions n ≥ 3. Recent literature confirms only partial results: the planar case is settled (triangles maximize, due to Blaschke), structural results show that polytopal local maximizers with a simplicial vertex must be simplices, and various symmetric/related variants have been studied, but the general maximizer problem in n ≥ 3 is still unresolved.

paper_title: Constructing groups of 'small' order: Recent results and open problems
context_brief: Counting groups of a given order
original_question: Let L_n denote a set containing one representative of each isomorphism type of finite group of order n, so |L_n| is the number of isomorphism types of groups of order n. Is there a closed formula for |L_n|, or a general method that determines |L_n| for arbitrary n without explicitly listing all groups?
self_contained_problem: For a positive integer $n$, let $L_n$ denote a complete set of representatives, one from each isomorphism class, of the finite groups of order $n$, and let $g(n) = |L_n|$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of finite groups of order $n$. Determine whether there exists a closed-form expression for $g(n)$ as a function of $n$, or more generally a procedure that computes $g(n)$ for arbitrary $n$ without enumerating, up to isomorphism, all groups of order $n$.
status_search_result: No closed formula or general method is known for computing the number of isomorphism types of groups of order $n$. Partial results exist: a clean formula for abelian groups via prime-power factorizations, and Higman–Sims asymptotics for prime-power orders. Computationally, $g(n)$ is known for $n \le 2047$, with $n = 2048 = 2^{11}$ the smallest open case. The general enumeration problem remains open.

paper_title: Constructing groups of 'small' order: Recent results and open problems
original_question: Let E2 be the set of integers n with 1 <= n <= 20000 for which 2^9 * p is a proper divisor of n for some p in {3, 5, 7}. For the 18 orders in E2, can the finite groups of order n be enumerated up to isomorphism despite the large number of groups already occurring at each base order 2^9 * p?
self_contained_problem:
Let
$$E_2 = \{\, n \in \mathbb{Z} : 1 \le n \le 20000 \text{ and there exists } p \in \{3,5,7\} \text{ such that } 2^{9}\cdot p \text{ is a proper divisor of } n \,\},$$
where "proper divisor" means a divisor strictly smaller than $n$. The set $E_2$ consists of exactly $18$ integers. For each base order $b \in \{2^{9}\cdot 3,\; 2^{9}\cdot 5,\; 2^{9}\cdot 7\} = \{1536, 2560, 3584\}$, the number of pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups of order $b$ is already extremely large (in particular, this number is so large at $b = 1536$ that a complete list of the isomorphism types of groups of order $1536$ is not currently available).

Problem: For each of the $18$ orders $n \in E_2$, determine, up to isomorphism, all finite groups of order $n$. More precisely, develop a constructive classification (or a complete enumeration up to isomorphism) of the finite groups of every order $n$ in $E_2$, or else establish a definite obstruction to producing such a classification.
status_search_result: Surveys on the classification of finite groups of small order (including a 2024 article in Foundations of Computational Mathematics) and the GAP SmallGroups library documentation indicate that orders divisible by 2^9·3 = 1536 remain outside the range of complete enumeration: groups of order 1536 have not been fully classified, and proper multiples up to 20000 (the set E2) are likewise not enumerated. No source found announces a completion of these cases, so the problem remains open.

paper_title: Constructing groups of 'small' order: Recent results and open problems
original_question: For the six exceptional orders n = 8748 = 2^2 * 3^7, 10368 = 2^7 * 3^4, 13122 = 2 * 3^8, 16000 = 2^7 * 5^3, 17496 = 2^3 * 3^7, and 18816 = 2^7 * 3 * 7^2, can the finite groups of each order be constructed up to isomorphism, including determining the missing solvable groups while keeping the known nilpotent counts and known non-solvable counts fixed?
self_contained_problem:
For each of the six positive integers
n ∈ { 8748 = 2^2·3^7,  10368 = 2^7·3^4,  13122 = 2·3^8,  16000 = 2^7·5^3,  17496 = 2^3·3^7,  18816 = 2^7·3·7^2 },
construct, explicitly and up to isomorphism, a complete and irredundant list of all finite groups of order n.

For each such n, the counts of nilpotent groups of order n (equivalently, of groups whose Sylow subgroups are direct factors, given by the product over primes p ∣ n of the number of groups of order p^{v_p(n)}) and the counts of non-solvable groups of order n are known. The problem is therefore equivalent to determining all solvable (in fact, all non-nilpotent solvable) groups of order n up to isomorphism, in such a way that the total list is consistent with these known nilpotent and non-solvable counts.

In particular, give an algorithmic construction that, for each of these six orders, produces representatives of every isomorphism class of finite group of order n and an isomorphism-distinguishing invariant separating them.

paper_title: Constructing groups of 'small' order: Recent results and open problems
context_brief: Independent verification of computed group data
original_question: Can the remaining small-order group enumerations that lack an independent verification be cross-checked by a second method? The unresolved reliability target consists of six non-solvable cases that were not cross-checked and, on the solvable side, 183 orders below 20000 for which the solvable groups were enumerated by only one method, while another 39 orders still remained open for enumeration.
self_contained_problem:
For each positive integer $n$, let $g(n)$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of finite groups of order $n$. Various computational methods exist for enumerating and constructing representatives of these isomorphism classes (for example, the Frattini extension method for solvable groups, cyclic-extension methods, coclass-based methods, and methods for non-solvable groups built on top of classifications of simple and almost-simple groups). A computed enumeration $g(n)$ together with an explicit list of representatives is said to be "independently verified" if it has been obtained by at least two essentially different construction methods that agree.

Consider the following situation for orders $n \le 20000$:

(a) On the non-solvable side, there are exactly six orders $n \le 20000$ for which the groups of order $n$ have been constructed and counted by only one method, and no independent cross-check exists.

(b) On the solvable side, there are exactly $183$ orders $n \le 20000$ for which the solvable groups of order $n$ have been enumerated by only one method, with no second independent verification.

(c) In addition, there remain $39$ orders $n \le 20000$ for which a complete enumeration of all groups of order $n$ has not yet been carried out at all.

Problem: Provide a second, independent construction method that successfully cross-checks the existing enumerations in cases (a) and (b), thereby producing matching counts and isomorphism-class lists by two essentially different methods; and complete the enumeration of all groups of order $n$ for each of the $39$ orders $n \le 20000$ in case (c).
status_search_result: Search results indicate that the enumeration of groups of small order remains an active area, with the Small Groups Library covering most orders up to 20000 but with a small number of exceptional orders (notably orders divisible by 2^8·p^2 for small primes p) still resistant to complete construction. Subsequent work (e.g., the perfect groups of order up to two million, and counting supersolvable/solvable group orders, 2024) has reduced but not eliminated the list of unverified and unconstructed orders below 20000. No source found confirms full resolution of all six non-solvable cases, the 183 unverified solvable orders, and the 39 open orders.

paper_title: Open Problems About Sumsets in Finite Abelian Groups: Minimum Sizes and Critical Numbers
original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and for an m-element subset A={a1,...,am} define hA as the set of all sums λ1a1+...+λm am with nonnegative integer coefficients summing to h. Define ρ(G,m,h) as the minimum possible value of |hA| over all m-element subsets A of G. In the boundary case p = hm - h + 1, classify all m-element subsets A of G for which |hA|=ρ(G,m,h). In particular, determine all extremal subsets beyond the known possibilities of arithmetic progressions of length m and m-subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of order p.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, written additively, and let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For a finite subset $A = \{a_1, \dots, a_m\} \subseteq G$ of size $m$ and a positive integer $h$, define the $h$-fold sumset of $A$ by
$$hA = \Big\{ \sum_{i=1}^m \lambda_i a_i \;\Big|\; \lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_m \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},\ \sum_{i=1}^m \lambda_i = h \Big\}.$$
Define
$$\rho(G, m, h) = \min\{\,|hA| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\,\}.$$
Assume the boundary equality $p = hm - h + 1$. Classify all $m$-element subsets $A \subseteq G$ that attain $|hA| = \rho(G, m, h)$. In particular, characterize all such extremal subsets beyond the two known families:
(i) arithmetic progressions of length $m$ in $G$, and
(ii) $m$-element subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of $G$ of order $p$.
status_search_result: No published classification of the extremal sets in the boundary case $p = hm-h+1$ was located. The question is posed as an open classification problem; searches for inverse results on $\rho(G,m,h)$ in this regime returned only general background on sumsets in abelian groups and no resolution of the boundary case.

paper_title: Open Problems About Sumsets in Finite Abelian Groups: Minimum Sizes and Critical Numbers
context_brief: Inverse problem for restricted sumsets above the prime threshold
original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, and for an m-element subset A={a1,...,am} define h^A as the set of sums of h distinct elements of A. Let p be the smallest prime divisor of n. Suppose 2 ≤ h ≤ m - 2 and p > hm - h^2 + 1. Classify the m-element subsets A of G for which |h^A| has the minimum value hm - h^2 + 1. Is it true that equality occurs if and only if either h=2, m=4, and A={a, a+g1, a+g2, a+g1+g2} for some a,g1,g2 in G, or A is an arithmetic progression in G?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, and let p denote the smallest prime divisor of n. For an m-element subset A = {a_1, …, a_m} of G and an integer h with 1 ≤ h ≤ m, define the h-fold restricted sumset

   h^∧A = { λ_1 a_1 + λ_2 a_2 + … + λ_m a_m : λ_i ∈ {0,1}, λ_1 + … + λ_m = h }.

Assume that 2 ≤ h ≤ m − 2 and that p > hm − h^2 + 1. It is known that under these hypotheses |h^∧A| ≥ hm − h^2 + 1.

Classify all m-element subsets A ⊆ G that attain equality |h^∧A| = hm − h^2 + 1. In particular, decide whether equality holds if and only if either:
 (i) h = 2, m = 4, and A = {a, a + g_1, a + g_2, a + g_1 + g_2} for some a, g_1, g_2 ∈ G; or
 (ii) A is an arithmetic progression in G, i.e. A = {a, a + d, a + 2d, …, a + (m−1)d} for some a, d ∈ G.
status_search_result: The analogous classification for sets of integers (Freiman/Lev-style inverse theorem for restricted h-fold sumsets at the threshold hm − h^2 + 1) is known by Nathanson and has been extended for slightly larger sumset sizes by recent authors (e.g. Mohan–Pandey, Daza et al., 2024–2025). However, the corresponding statement for general finite abelian groups under the prime-threshold hypothesis p > hm − h^2 + 1 does not appear to have been fully established and remains posed as a conjecture in the additive-combinatorics literature.

paper_title: Open Problems About Sumsets in Finite Abelian Groups: Minimum Sizes and Critical Numbers
context_brief: Frequency of disagreement for two-fold signed sumsets
original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, and let A={a1,...,am} be an m-element subset of G. For h=2, define the ordinary sumset 2A using nonnegative integer coefficients with total 2, and define the signed sumset 2±A using integer coefficients λ1,...,λm with |λ1|+...+|λm|=2. Let ρ(G,m,2) and ρ±(G,m,2) be the minimum possible sizes of these two sumsets over all m-element subsets A of G. Is it true that ρ±(G,m,2) and ρ(G,m,2) differ for fewer than n/4 values of m?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, written additively, and let $m$ be a positive integer with $1 \le m \le n$. For an $m$-element subset $A = \{a_1, \dots, a_m\} \subseteq G$, define the (2-fold) ordinary sumset
$$2A = \Bigl\{ \sum_{i=1}^m \lambda_i a_i \;\Big|\; \lambda_i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},\; \sum_{i=1}^m \lambda_i = 2 \Bigr\},$$
and the (2-fold) signed sumset
$$2_\pm A = \Bigl\{ \sum_{i=1}^m \lambda_i a_i \;\Big|\; \lambda_i \in \mathbb{Z},\; \sum_{i=1}^m |\lambda_i| = 2 \Bigr\}.$$
Set
$$\rho(G,m,2) = \min\{|2A| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\}, \qquad \rho_\pm(G,m,2) = \min\{|2_\pm A| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\}.$$
Prove or disprove: for every finite abelian group $G$ of order $n$, the number of values $m \in \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ for which $\rho_\pm(G, m, 2) \ne \rho(G, m, 2)$ is strictly less than $n/4$.
status_search_result: The conjecture is stated as an open problem in surveys of minimum sumset sizes. Bajnok and Matzke initiated detailed study of ρ±(G,m,h) and obtained equality results in particular cases (e.g., cyclic groups for certain h), but no published resolution of the n/4 disagreement conjecture for h=2 in arbitrary finite abelian groups was found.

paper_title: Open problems from NCS 2018
context_brief: Finite regular bands in semigroup rings
original_question: Given a finite left regular band or finite right regular band B, is the skew lattice generated by B inside the semigroup ring Z(B) necessarily finite?
self_contained_problem:
Let $B$ be a finite band (i.e., a semigroup in which every element is idempotent) that is either left regular (satisfying $xyx = xy$ for all $x,y \in B$) or right regular (satisfying $xyx = yx$ for all $x,y \in B$). Consider the integral semigroup ring $\mathbb{Z}(B)$, whose elements are finite $\mathbb{Z}$-linear combinations of elements of $B$ with multiplication induced from $B$. Inside $\mathbb{Z}(B)$, the multiplication $\cdot$ of the ring and the operation $x \nabla y := x + y - xy$ (when restricted to suitable idempotent elements) generate a skew lattice: namely the smallest subset of $\mathbb{Z}(B)$ containing $B$ that is closed under both the ring multiplication and $\nabla$, and forms a skew lattice (a set with two associative, idempotent, mutually absorbing band operations $\wedge$ and $\vee$ satisfying the absorption identities $x \wedge (x \vee y) = x = x \vee (x \wedge y)$ and their duals). 

Question: Must the skew lattice generated by $B$ inside $\mathbb{Z}(B)$ be finite?
status_search_result: The question is recorded as an open problem from the NCS 2018 workshop. Searches did not surface any subsequent publication resolving whether the skew lattice generated by a finite left or right regular band inside its integral semigroup ring is necessarily finite. Related literature on skew lattices arising from regular bands in rings exists, but no source explicitly settles this specific finiteness question.

paper_title: Open problems from NCS 2018
original_question: Find necessary and sufficient conditions under which a skew lattice S can be embedded into a ring as an isomorphic copy of idempotent elements, with the skew-lattice operations represented by ring multiplication and either the quadratic or cubic join. The source lists distributivity, hence categoricity, and cancellativity, hence symmetry, as preconditions, and notes that skew Boolean algebras and their duals, strongly distributive skew lattices, and dual strongly distributive lattices can be embedded. Are there additional sufficient conditions, and what are the complete necessary and sufficient conditions?
self_contained_problem:
A skew lattice is an algebra (S, ∧, ∨) where ∧ and ∨ are associative, idempotent binary operations satisfying the absorption identities x ∧ (x ∨ y) = x = x ∨ (x ∧ y) and (x ∧ y) ∨ y = y = (x ∨ y) ∧ y. Given a ring R, its set E(R) of idempotents carries skew-lattice operations defined by e ∧ f = efe·... using ring multiplication for the meet, and either the quadratic join e ∨ f = e + f − ef − fe + efe + fef (cubic join) or e ∨ f = e + f − ef (quadratic join, defined when ef = fe ought not be assumed) — more precisely, when these formulas produce idempotents one obtains skew lattices inside R.

A skew lattice S is said to be embeddable into a ring if there exist a ring R and an injective homomorphism of S onto a sub-skew-lattice of (E(R), ·, ∨) where ∨ is either the quadratic or the cubic join.

Recall: S is distributive if x ∧ (y ∨ z) ∧ x = (x ∧ y ∧ x) ∨ (x ∧ z ∧ x) and the dual identity hold; S is cancellative if x ∨ y = x ∨ z and x ∧ y = x ∧ z imply y = z (and dually); S is symmetric if x ∧ y = y ∧ x ⟺ x ∨ y = y ∨ x; S is categorical if nonempty composites of coset bijections between comparable D-classes are coset bijections. It is known that distributivity (which implies categoricity) and cancellativity (which implies symmetry) are necessary preconditions, and that every skew Boolean algebra, its dual, every strongly distributive skew lattice, and every dual strongly distributive skew lattice can be embedded into a ring in this sense.

Problem: Determine complete necessary and sufficient conditions on a skew lattice S for it to be embeddable into a ring (with meet given by ring multiplication and join given by either the quadratic or cubic join) as a sub-skew-lattice of the idempotents of that ring.
status_search_result: The problem of finding complete necessary and sufficient conditions for embedding a general skew lattice into a ring as a sub-skew-lattice of idempotents appears to remain open. Known partial results cover skew Boolean algebras, their duals, strongly distributive skew lattices, and (in matrix rings) symmetric normal skew lattices with finite distributive maximal lattice image, but no full characterization has been found.

denote the congruence class of the constant $0^A$. Call $A$ dually congruence $0$-distributive if for all congruences $\Theta, \Psi, \Phi \in \operatorname{Con}(A)$,

paper_title: Open problems from NCS 2018
original_question: Let A be an algebra and let S = End(A) be its endomorphism monoid. It is known that if S has commuting idempotents, then A has property RI, meaning the intersection of two retracts of A is also a retract; property UR, meaning each retract of A corresponds to a unique idempotent with that range; and the dual properties RI*, meaning the join of two coretracts of A is a coretract, and UR*, meaning each retraction has a unique section. Does the converse hold: do RI, UR, RI*, and UR* imply that the idempotents of End(A) commute?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a universal algebra and let $S = \mathrm{End}(A)$ denote its monoid of endomorphisms. A subalgebra $B \subseteq A$ is called a retract of $A$ if there exists an idempotent endomorphism $e \in S$ (i.e. $e^2 = e$) whose image is $B$; such an $e$ is called a retraction onto $B$, and an endomorphism $s \colon B \to A$ with $e \circ s = \mathrm{id}_B$ (viewed appropriately) is called a section of $e$. Dually, by a coretract one means the kernel congruence of a retraction, and the join of coretracts is the join in the congruence lattice. Consider the following four properties of $A$:
\begin{itemize}
  \item[(RI)] The intersection of any two retracts of $A$ is again a retract of $A$.
  \item[(UR)] To each retract of $A$ there corresponds a unique idempotent of $S$ whose image equals that retract.
  \item[(RI*)] The join of any two coretracts of $A$ is again a coretract of $A$.
  \item[(UR*)] Each retraction in $S$ has a unique section.
\end{itemize}
It is known that if the idempotents of $S$ commute (i.e. $ef = fe$ for all idempotent $e, f \in S$), then $A$ satisfies (RI), (UR), (RI*), and (UR*).

Question: Does the converse hold? That is, if an algebra $A$ satisfies all four properties (RI), (UR), (RI*), and (UR*), must the idempotents of $\mathrm{End}(A)$ commute?

context_brief: Order-theoretic characterization of left regular bands
original_question: Generalize the order-theoretic characterization described for left normal bands to left regular bands. The source considers a set X with a preorder and a refining partial order, defines lower bounds and infima of ordered pairs using those relations, and says that left normal bands in this order-theoretic sense are precisely left normal bands in the algebraic sense. For left regular bands, what property should replace the condition that if x and y are equivalent for the preorder and both are below z in the partial order, then x = y?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let X be a set equipped with a preorder ⪯ and a partial order ≤ which refines ⪯ (that is, x ≤ y implies x ⪯ y). For a, b ∈ X, call c ∈ X a lower bound of the ordered pair (a, b) if c ≤ a and c ⪯ b. A greatest lower bound of (a, b) (with respect to ≤ among lower bounds of (a,b)) is called an infimum of (a, b) and denoted a ∧ b when it exists.

Background characterization (left normal bands). One can show that the structures (X, ⪯, ≤) in which every ordered pair has an infimum, together with the condition

(∗) for all x, y, z ∈ X, if x ⪯ y, y ⪯ x and x ≤ z, y ≤ z, then x = y,

are exactly the left normal bands (idempotent semigroups satisfying xyz = xzy) under the assignment a · b := a ∧ b, with ⪯ recovered as the natural preorder of the band (a ⪯ b iff ab = a, equivalently the semilattice congruence ordering) and ≤ recovered as the partial order a ≤ b iff ab = ba = a.

Find an order-theoretic axiom (∗′) on the basic structure (X, ⪯, ≤) — to replace (∗) — such that the resulting class of structures (X, ⪯, ≤) in which (a, b) ↦ a ∧ b is well-defined corresponds bijectively, via the same assignment a · b := a ∧ b, to the class of left regular bands (idempotent semigroups satisfying xyx = xy). Equivalently, characterize left regular bands order-theoretically in the framework (X, ⪯, ≤, ∧) above by determining the precise condition that must be imposed in place of (∗).

paper_title: Open problems from NCS 2018
context_brief: Coverings of lattices and skew lattices
original_question: Define a precise concept of a covering of a lattice or skew lattice, and develop a theory for such coverings using the analogy with covering graphs and voltage assignments.
self_contained_problem:
A skew lattice is an algebraic structure $(S;\wedge,\vee)$ where $\wedge$ and $\vee$ are associative, idempotent binary operations satisfying the absorption identities $x\wedge(x\vee y)=x=(y\vee x)\wedge x$ and $x\vee(x\wedge y)=x=(y\wedge x)\vee x$. A lattice is the commutative special case. In topological graph theory, a covering of a graph $G$ is a graph homomorphism $p:\tilde G\to G$ that is a local bijection on neighborhoods, and such coverings are classified combinatorially via voltage assignments: a labeling of the edges of $G$ by elements of a group $\Gamma$ giving rise to a derived covering graph $G^\Gamma$.

Problem. Formulate a precise definition of a covering of a lattice (and, more generally, of a skew lattice) that is analogous to the notion of a covering of a graph, and develop the corresponding theory. In particular:
(a) Specify what is meant by a covering morphism $p:\tilde L\to L$ between (skew) lattices, including the appropriate local conditions analogous to being a local bijection.
(b) Introduce an analogue of voltage assignments on a (skew) lattice $L$ taking values in a suitable group (or other algebraic object) $\Gamma$, and define the derived covering (skew) lattice $L^\Gamma$.
(c) Prove a classification theorem showing that, up to isomorphism, coverings of $L$ correspond to voltage assignments on $L$ modulo an appropriate equivalence (e.g.\ a Galois-type correspondence between coverings and subgroups of a fundamental group of $L$).
(d) Investigate how this covering theory interacts with the structural features of skew lattices, such as the Green's relation $\mathcal D$, the maximal lattice image, and decompositions into rectangular bands.
status_search_result: A web search does not turn up any developed theory of "coverings of skew lattices" modeled on covering graphs and voltage assignments. The problem is posed as a programmatic open problem from the Noncommutative Structures conference (NCS 2018), and no subsequent works appear to have carried out this program. Status appears to remain open.

original_question: Given a finite lattice K, find a test that decides whether K is isomorphic to the congruence lattice Con(N) of some antilattice N.
self_contained_problem:
An antilattice is an algebra $(N;\vee,\wedge)$ of type $(2,2)$ satisfying the same axioms as a lattice except that the commutativity laws for $\vee$ and $\wedge$ are replaced by their anticommutative analogues: for all $x,y\in N$, if $x\vee y=y\vee x$ then $x=y$, and if $x\wedge y=y\wedge x$ then $x=y$ (equivalently, both operations are anticommutative idempotent operations satisfying associativity and the absorption laws). paper_title: Open problems from NCS 2018
context_brief: Coset-law identities for skew lattice varieties
original_question: Determine whether coset law-like identities can always be described so as to determine a variety of skew lattices, or whether some varieties of skew lattices do not permit characterization by such coset law-like identities.
self_contained_problem:
A skew lattice is an algebra (S; ∨, ∧) with two associative idempotent binary operations satisfying the absorption identities x ∧ (x ∨ y) = x = x ∨ (x ∧ y) and (x ∧ y) ∨ y = y = (y ∨ x) ∧ y. Green's relation D on a skew lattice is a congruence whose quotient S/D is the maximal lattice image, and each D-class is a maximal rectangular band. Given comparable D-classes A > B in S, the D-class B partitions A into cosets, giving rise to coset bijections between rectangular bands. A "coset law-like identity" is an equation (or quasi-identity) built from terms of the form C ∨ x ∨ C, C ∧ x ∧ C (with C ranging over D-class representatives) that captures relationships among coset decompositions arising from distinct pairs of comparable or incomparable D-classes (such as the chain law: for D-classes A > B > C, C ∨ a ∨ C = C ∨ a' ∨ C iff B ∨ a ∨ B = B ∨ a' ∨ B and C ∨ b ∨ C = C ∨ b' ∨ C whenever a > b, a' > b'; and the analogous diamond law). 

Question: Is it the case that every variety of skew lattices can be axiomatized (within the variety of all skew lattices) by some collection of coset law-like identities of this form? Equivalently, does there exist a variety of skew lattices that admits no characterization by any set of coset law-like identities?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the collection of open problems from NCS 2018. Available sources on coset structures in skew lattices (Pita Costa, Cvetko-Vah, and related work) describe specific coset laws (chain law, diamond law) and varieties such as categorical and distributive skew lattices, but no source found resolves whether every variety of skew lattices can be characterized by coset law-like identities.

paper_title: Open problems from NCS 2018
context_brief: Representing algebraic lattices by weak congruence lattices
original_question: Given an algebraic lattice L and a chosen element a of L, determine the conditions under which there exists an algebra whose weak congruence lattice is isomorphic to L and whose diagonal equality relation corresponds to a under the isomorphism. The source notes that all weak congruences form an algebraic lattice under inclusion, that the diagonal relation has a particular role, and that not every element can occur because the chosen element should be codistributive and satisfy additional conditions.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{A} = (A, F)$ be an algebra. A binary relation $\rho \subseteq A \times A$ is called a weak congruence on $\mathbb{A}$ if it is symmetric, transitive, and compatible with all operations in $F$ (note: reflexivity is not required, so $\rho$ is a congruence on some subalgebra of $\mathbb{A}$). The set $\mathrm{Cw}(\mathbb{A})$ of all weak congruences on $\mathbb{A}$, ordered by inclusion, forms an algebraic lattice; the diagonal $\Delta_A = \{(x,x) : x \in A\}$ is a distinguished element of this lattice.

An element $u$ of an algebraic lattice $L$ is called codistributive if $u \vee (x \wedge y) = (u \vee x) \wedge (u \vee y)$ for all $x, y \in L$.

Problem. Let $L$ be an algebraic lattice and let $a \in L$ be a fixed element. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(L, a)$ under which there exists an algebra $\mathbb{A}$ together with a lattice isomorphism $\varphi : L \to \mathrm{Cw}(\mathbb{A})$ such that $\varphi(a) = \Delta_A$.

(It is known that any such element $a$ must be codistributive in $L$, and must satisfy further restrictions, so the problem asks for a complete characterization of the "diagonal-suitable" pairs $(L, a)$.)

paper_title: Open problems from NCS 2018
original_question: Find the correct universal-algebra generalization of order congruence lattices and, more broadly, find examples of comodernistic lattices. In the source, an element m of a lattice L is left-modular when for every x ≤ y in L, (x ∨ m) ∧ y = x ∧ (m ∧ y), and a lattice is comodernistic when every nontrivial interval [a, b] has a coatom that is left-modular in that interval. Order congruence lattices O(P) of finite posets are given as examples, and the question asks whether a wider class of congruence lattices from universal algebra or similar settings yields comodernistic lattices.
self_contained_problem:
Let $L$ be a finite lattice with order relation $\le$, join $\vee$, and meet $\wedge$. An element $m\in L$ is called left-modular if for every pair $x\le y$ in $L$ one has
\[(x\vee m)\wedge y \;=\; x\vee(m\wedge y).\]
A nontrivial interval of $L$ is an interval $[a,b]=\{z\in L:a\le z\le b\}$ with $a<b$; a coatom of $[a,b]$ is an element $c\in[a,b]$ with $c<b$ and no element strictly between $c$ and $b$. The lattice $L$ is called comodernistic if every nontrivial interval $[a,b]$ of $L$ contains a coatom that is left-modular within the sublattice $[a,b]$.

For a finite poset $P$, the order congruence lattice $O(P)$ is the lattice of partitions of $P$ into nonempty convex pieces such that the natural quotient relation on $P$ is again a partial order, ordered by refinement; each such $O(P)$ is comodernistic.

(a) Identify a natural universal-algebra construction that generalizes the assignment $P\mapsto O(P)$ from finite posets to a wider class of algebras, in such a way that the order congruence lattices of finite posets arise as a special case and the resulting congruence-type lattices are comodernistic.

(b) More broadly, exhibit further families of comodernistic lattices arising from universal algebra or related settings.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution identifying a universal-algebra generalization of order congruence lattices that yields comodernistic lattices, nor a definitive list of new comodernistic-lattice families answering the broader question. Standard references on congruence lattices and modular/left-modular elements appear, but none explicitly settle this question, so the current status is unclear from the available evidence.

context_brief: Optimality of Algorithm 7.2 for regular sequences
original_question: For the single-machine problem with processing times p_j(t) = 1 + b_j t and objective sum_j C_j, let beta_j = 1 + b_j be the deterioration-rate factor sequence. Suppose this sequence is regular, such as an arithmetic sequence, geometric sequence, or Fibonacci sequence. Algorithm 7.2 constructs a V-shaped schedule in O(n) time by using the periodic sign behavior of the signature S^-(beta), rather than recomputing that signature during the greedy construction. Does Algorithm 7.2 always generate an optimal schedule for every regular sequence of deterioration-rate factors?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the single-machine scheduling problem with n jobs whose processing times depend on their starting times in the linear deteriorating form
  p_j(t) = 1 + b_j · t,   j = 1, …, n,
where b_j > 0 and t ≥ 0 denotes the starting time of job j. All jobs are available at time 0 and the machine processes at most one job at a time without preemption. For a permutation π = (π(1), …, π(n)) the completion times are defined recursively by C_{π(0)} = 0 and C_{π(k)} = (1 + b_{π(k)}) · (1 + C_{π(k−1)}). The objective is to minimize the total completion time Σ_{j=1}^n C_j.

Define the deterioration-rate factors β_j = 1 + b_j and let β = (β_1, …, β_n) be a fixed sequence. For a permutation, the signature S^−(β) records the sign pattern of certain pairwise comparisons used to determine when swapping adjacent jobs decreases the objective; this signature is known to exhibit periodic behavior when the sequence β is "regular," for instance when (β_j) is an arithmetic progression, a geometric progression, or a Fibonacci-type sequence.

Algorithm 7.2 is a greedy procedure that, exploiting this periodic sign behavior of S^−(β) instead of recomputing it during construction, builds a V-shaped schedule (i.e. a schedule whose β-values are non-increasing up to a minimum and non-decreasing thereafter) in O(n) time.

Question: Does Algorithm 7.2 produce a schedule that minimizes Σ_j C_j for every regular sequence β of deterioration-rate factors (in particular, for every arithmetic, geometric, or Fibonacci sequence)?
status_search_result: The question is posed as a conjecture in the survey on time-dependent scheduling. Subsequent literature on V-shaped optimal sequencing for single-machine deteriorating-job problems (e.g., refined optimality conditions and notes on exact algorithms/heuristics for V- and Λ-shaped sequences) addresses related properties but does not appear to confirm or refute the optimality of the specific O(n) greedy procedure for all regular β-sequences. No resolution of the conjecture was located.

Call a topological group $G$ S-separable if for every topological group $H$ in which every closed subgroup is separable, every closed subgroup of the product $G \times H$ is separable.

1. Is every separable locally compact topological group S-separable?
2. Is the additive group $(\mathbb{R}, +)$ of real numbers with its usual Euclidean topology S-separable?
3. Does there exist a separable metrizable topological group that fails to be S-separable?
4. Is the free topological group $F([0,1])$ on the closed unit interval $[0,1]$ S-separable?

(Recall that a topological space is separable if it contains a countable dense subset, and that the free topological group $F(X)$ on a Tychonoff space $X$ is the unique topological group containing $X$ as a topological subspace, algebraically free on $X$, with the universal property that every continuous map from $X$ into a topological group extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism from $F(X)$.)

original_question: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a quotient Banach space that is both separable and infinite-dimensional?
self_contained_problem:
A Banach space is a complete normed vector space over the real or complex numbers. Given a Banach space $X$ and a closed linear subspace $Y \subseteq X$, the quotient $X/Y$ equipped with the norm $\|x+Y\| = \inf_{y\in Y}\|x-y\|$ is again a Banach space, called a quotient Banach space of $X$. A Banach space is separable if it contains a countable dense subset.

Determine whether the following statement is true: every infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$ admits a closed subspace $Y$ such that the quotient Banach space $X/Y$ is both infinite-dimensional and separable.

paper_title: On two long standing open problems on Lp-spaces
original_question: Let P be a bounded projection on L1 whose range is a complemented subspace of L1 and suppose P is non-Dunford-Pettis, equivalently its range is not Schur in the formulation given by the source. Must P be an Enflo operator, meaning that P fixes a copy of L1; equivalently, is every non-Schur complemented subspace of L1 isomorphic to L1?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the real (or complex) Banach space $L_1 = L_1[0,1]$. Recall the following definitions.

• A bounded linear operator $T$ between Banach spaces is called Dunford–Pettis (or completely continuous) if it maps weakly null sequences to norm null sequences.
• A Banach space $X$ has the Schur property if every weakly null sequence in $X$ is norm null; equivalently, the identity operator on $X$ is Dunford–Pettis.
• A closed subspace $Y \subseteq L_1$ is called complemented if there exists a bounded linear projection $P: L_1 \to L_1$ with range $Y$.
• A bounded operator $T \in \mathcal{L}(L_1, Y)$ is said to fix a copy of $L_1$ if there is a closed subspace $Z \subseteq L_1$ isomorphic to $L_1$ such that $T$ restricted to $Z$ is an isomorphism onto its image. Such an operator is called an Enflo operator.

Note that a projection $P \in \mathcal{L}(L_1)$ is non-Dunford–Pettis if and only if its range $P(L_1)$ fails the Schur property.

Question: Must every non-Dunford–Pettis bounded projection $P \in \mathcal{L}(L_1)$ be an Enflo operator? Equivalently, is every complemented subspace of $L_1$ that fails the Schur property isomorphic to $L_1$?
status_search_result: This is a long-standing open problem in the isomorphic theory of L_1: whether every non-Schur (equivalently, non-Dunford–Pettis-projection) complemented subspace of L_1 is isomorphic to L_1. Searches yield related literature on Dunford–Pettis and Schur properties, but no resolution of this specific question; it continues to be cited as open in surveys on the structure of L_p-spaces.

paper_title: Aspects of Semiclassical Black Holes: Development and Open Problems
original_question: In semiclassical black-hole evaporation, a massive star collapses to a black hole with an event horizon; quantum fields near the horizon produce Hawking radiation, and an outside observer can access only the emitted radiation after tracing over interior degrees of freedom. self_contained_problem:
Consider a semiclassical model of gravitational collapse and black-hole evaporation in which a massive body collapses to form a black hole bounded by an event horizon, and quantum fields propagating on the resulting curved spacetime produce Hawking radiation at infinity. An asymptotic exterior observer has access only to the radiation degrees of freedom; the interior degrees of freedom (those causally disconnected behind the horizon) are traced out, yielding a reduced density matrix on the exterior that, in the standard Hawking calculation, is thermal (mixed) and depends only on a few macroscopic parameters (mass, charge, angular momentum) of the initial collapsing matter. Quantum mechanics, on the other hand, demands that the global evolution of an initially pure state remain unitary, so that the final state after complete evaporation should also be pure and should encode all information about the initial matter configuration and any subsequent perturbations.

Problem: Provide a mathematically consistent description of the entire formation-and-evaporation process — including a precise specification of the global Hilbert space, the in/out state spaces, and the evolution map between them — such that:
(i) the total evolution from the initial collapsing-matter state to the final post-evaporation state is unitary;
(ii) any pure initial state evolves to a pure final state supported on the exterior radiation Hilbert space after the black hole has fully evaporated; and
(iii) the information characterizing the initial matter (and any infalling perturbations) is recoverable, in principle, from the final exterior quantum state via some explicit decoding map.

Equivalently, determine whether such a unitary, information-preserving description exists, and if so exhibit it; otherwise prove that no such description is compatible with the standard semiclassical assumptions (locality of effective quantum field theory outside the horizon, validity of general relativity in low-curvature regions, and the equivalence principle near a smooth horizon).

Significant progress since 2019–2020 via the "island formula" and replica wormhole computations has reproduced a unitary Page curve for the radiation entropy in certain semiclassical gravitational path-integral calculations, providing strong evidence consistent with unitarity. However, a complete, mechanism-level resolution—an explicit unitary map and information-recovery protocol within a fully consistent semiclassical (or quantum-gravitational) framework—is not established, and the problem is widely regarded as still open.

paper_title: Aspects of Semiclassical Black Holes: Development and Open Problems
original_question: Consider low-curvature corrections to classical general relativity motivated by the firewall paradox: stress-tensor fluctuations near the horizon source metric perturbations h_mu_nu; accumulated backreaction over a Schwarzschild-radius scale or over the black-hole lifetime could alter the Hawking spectrum, modify the near-horizon geometry, and induce nonlocal effects that carry information out. Are these soft quantum corrections valid and strong enough to restore unitarity of black-hole evaporation while preserving the equivalence principle, and can they yield testable predictions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a four-dimensional Schwarzschild black hole of mass M and horizon radius r_s = 2GM/c^2, treated semiclassically: the metric g_{\\mu\\nu} satisfies the classical Einstein equations while a quantum matter field on this background possesses a renormalized stress-energy expectation value <T_{\\mu\\nu}> together with fluctuations \\delta T_{\\mu\\nu} = T_{\\mu\\nu} - <T_{\\mu\\nu}>. Allow the background to be perturbed by a metric correction h_{\\mu\\nu} sourced through the linearized Einstein equations by these stress-tensor fluctuations near the horizon, and let h_{\\mu\\nu} accumulate either over a light-crossing time of order r_s/c or over the full evaporation lifetime of order G^2 M^3/(\\hbar c^4). Such corrections are called \"soft\" if they remain small in local curvature invariants (so that an infalling observer crossing the horizon experiences no large tidal forces, in accordance with the equivalence principle) yet are coherent enough to imprint nontrivial correlations on the outgoing Hawking radiation.

Determine whether soft horizon corrections of this type can:
(a) modify the Hawking spectrum and induce nonlocal correlations between early and late Hawking quanta sufficient to render the full evaporation process described by a unitary S-matrix from infalling matter to outgoing radiation, while
(b) preserving the equivalence principle in the sense that no observer-detectable high-energy structure (firewall) appears at or near the horizon for a freely falling observer, and
(c) yielding quantitative, in-principle testable predictions distinguishing this scenario from strict semiclassical evolution.

Provide either a derivation establishing such corrections with quantitative estimates of their magnitude and information-carrying capacity, or an obstruction showing that no soft corrections satisfying (a) and (b) simultaneously can exist.
status_search_result: The black hole information paradox and the question of whether soft near-horizon backreaction corrections can restore unitarity while preserving the equivalence principle remains an active and unresolved area of research. While progress on entanglement-island and replica-wormhole computations (since 2019–2020) has reproduced a unitary Page curve in certain semiclassical setups, these results do not by themselves give a complete mechanism for soft corrections that are testable and free of firewalls in physical four-dimensional evaporating black holes. The problem is widely characterized as still open.

paper_title: Solutions to two open problems in topological residuated lattices
context_brief: Cardinality of filter topologies versus linear topological residuated lattices
original_question: Let L be a residuated lattice and let F(L) be the set of all filters of L. For each filter F, define T_F = {U subseteq L : for every x in U, x/F is contained in U}; this construction makes (L, T_F) a linear Alexandrov topological residuated lattice, and distinct filters produce distinct topologies, so there is an injective map from F(L) to LTRL(L), where LTRL(L) denotes the set of all linear topological residuated lattices whose underlying set is L. Are the sets F(L) and LTRL(L) equipotent?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(L,\wedge,\vee,\odot,\to,0,1)$ be a residuated lattice; that is, $(L,\wedge,\vee,0,1)$ is a bounded lattice, $(L,\odot,1)$ is a commutative monoid, and $\odot,\to$ form an adjoint pair: $x\odot y \le z$ iff $x\le y\to z$. A filter of $L$ is a nonempty subset $F\subseteq L$ that is upward closed under $\le$ and closed under $\odot$. Let $\mathcal F(L)$ denote the set of all filters of $L$. For each filter $F$, define the equivalence class $x/F=\{y\in L:(x\to y)\odot(y\to x)\in F\}$, and set 
$$\mathcal T_F=\{U\subseteq L:\text{for every }x\in U,\ x/F\subseteq U\}.$$
Then $(L,\mathcal T_F)$ is an Alexandrov topological residuated lattice (i.e., the lattice operations, $\odot$ and $\to$ are continuous, and arbitrary intersections of opens are open) which is moreover linear, meaning the topology is closed under arbitrary unions and intersections in the relevant sense for the algebraic operations. Distinct filters yield distinct topologies, so $F\mapsto\mathcal T_F$ is an injection from $\mathcal F(L)$ into $\mathrm{LTRL}(L)$, the set of all linear topological residuated lattice structures on the underlying set $L$.

Question: For every residuated lattice $L$, is $|\mathcal F(L)|=|\mathrm{LTRL}(L)|$?
status_search_result: The question was posed as one of two open problems in earlier work on topological residuated lattices and was addressed by He, Yang, and Wang in "Solutions to two open problems in topological residuated lattices" (Fuzzy Sets and Systems, 2021), which provides resolutions to both problems concerning the relationship between filters and linear topological residuated lattices.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: To what extent is the analogy between apparent horizons and minimal surfaces valid, including whether a meaningful second-variation or stability theory for apparent horizons exists even though no functional is known whose Euler-Lagrange equations are the apparent-horizon equations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth spacelike Cauchy initial data set in a four-dimensional spacetime, where $g$ is a Riemannian metric on the 3-manifold $M$ and $K$ is the second fundamental form. For a smooth, closed, two-sided hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ with outward unit normal $\nu$, let $H$ denote the mean curvature of $\Sigma$ in $(M,g)$ and let $\mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$ denote the trace of $K$ along $\Sigma$. The outgoing null expansion is $\theta^+ := H + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$, and $\Sigma$ is called an apparent horizon (a marginally outer trapped surface) if $\theta^+ \equiv 0$.

Unlike minimal surfaces (where $H=0$ are critical points of the area functional), no functional is known whose Euler–Lagrange equations are the apparent-horizon equations $\theta^+ = 0$. Nevertheless, by analogy with the minimal surface theory one can attempt to define and use a notion of "stability" and a "second variation" for apparent horizons.

Determine the extent to which the analogy between apparent horizons and minimal surfaces is mathematically valid. In particular:

(a) Decide whether there exists a meaningful variational principle whose Euler–Lagrange equations coincide with $\theta^+ = 0$.

(b) Develop a stability/second-variation theory for apparent horizons that plays the role of the second variation of area for minimal surfaces, identifying to what extent its spectral and geometric consequences (existence of stable apparent horizons, area estimates, foliations by apparent horizons, rigidity, etc.) parallel those of minimal surface theory.
status_search_result: A substantial stability theory for marginally outer trapped surfaces (apparent horizons) was developed by Andersson, Mars, and Simon (PRL 2005; Adv. Theor. Math. Phys. 2008), who introduced a (non-self-adjoint) stability operator $L_v$ whose principal eigenvalue plays a role analogous to the second variation of area for minimal surfaces, and used it to prove existence of marginally outer trapped tubes and area/rigidity results. Subsequent work (e.g., Galloway–Schoen on topology of horizons, Eichmair on Plateau-type existence, free-boundary MOTS) has extended the analogy considerably. However, no variational/functional formulation whose Euler–Lagrange equation is $\theta^+ = 0$ is known, so the question is only partially resolved.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Does there exist an asymptotically flat metric on R3 with zero scalar curvature that admits a minimal 2-sphere, and can such a minimal 2-sphere be stable; alternatively, can one prove that no such metric exists?
self_contained_problem:
A complete Riemannian metric $g$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ is called asymptotically flat if there exists a compact set $K \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ and a diffeomorphism from $\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus K$ to the complement of a ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ such that, in the induced coordinates $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$, the metric components satisfy
$$g_{ij}(x) = \delta_{ij} + O(|x|^{-1}), \qquad \partial_k g_{ij}(x) = O(|x|^{-2}), \qquad \partial_k\partial_l g_{ij}(x) = O(|x|^{-3})$$
as $|x| \to \infty$, and the scalar curvature is integrable. The metric is said to be scalar-flat if its scalar curvature satisfies $R_g \equiv 0$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$. A closed embedded 2-sphere $\Sigma \subset (\mathbb{R}^3, g)$ is minimal if its mean curvature vanishes identically, and is stable if the second variation of area is non-negative for all smooth normal variations.

Decide which of the following holds:
(a) There exists an asymptotically flat, scalar-flat metric $g$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ that admits a minimal embedded 2-sphere; moreover, such a minimal 2-sphere can be chosen to be stable.
(b) No asymptotically flat, scalar-flat metric on $\mathbb{R}^3$ admits a minimal embedded 2-sphere.

Either construct such a metric (with a stable minimal 2-sphere if possible) or prove that no such metric exists.
status_search_result: The existence question has been answered affirmatively. Constructions by P. Miao and by Chruściel–Delay produce asymptotically flat, scalar-flat metrics on $\mathbb{R}^3$ admitting (multiple) stable minimal 2-spheres; in particular, time-symmetric vacuum initial data containing apparent horizons (stable minimal spheres) provide such examples.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: For a conformally flat asymptotically flat metric g = phi^4 delta with non-negative scalar curvature, what conditions on the conformal factor phi guarantee that g has no horizon?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\phi:\mathbb{R}^3\to(0,\infty)$ be a smooth positive function, and consider the conformally flat Riemannian metric
$$g = \phi^4\,\delta$$
on $\mathbb{R}^3$, where $\delta$ denotes the standard Euclidean metric. Assume that:

(i) $g$ is asymptotically flat, meaning $\phi(x)\to 1$ as $|x|\to\infty$ (with appropriate decay of derivatives), so that $\phi$ admits an expansion $\phi(x) = 1 + \tfrac{A}{|x|} + O(|x|^{-2})$ at infinity for some constant $A\ge 0$ (the ADM mass is $2A$);

(ii) the scalar curvature $R_g$ of $g$ is non-negative; equivalently, in dimension three, $-\Delta\phi \ge 0$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$, i.e., $\phi$ is superharmonic.

A horizon (more precisely, an apparent horizon / outermost minimal surface) for $g$ is a closed embedded surface $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ that is minimal with respect to $g$ and encloses a bounded region.

Problem: Determine explicit sufficient conditions on the conformal factor $\phi$ that guarantee that the metric $g = \phi^4\,\delta$ contains no horizon, i.e., admits no closed minimal surface in $(\mathbb{R}^3,g)$.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a definitive resolution of this question. Related work on conformally flat asymptotically flat 3-metrics with non-negative scalar curvature (e.g., the Riemannian Penrose inequality and results on minimal surfaces in such metrics) is well developed, but a clean general characterization of conformal factors $\phi$ ensuring absence of horizons does not appear to have been established. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: For a compact 3-manifold M and conformal data (gamma_ab, A_cd, tau) used in the Lichnerowicz-Choquet-Bruhat-York system, where gamma_ab is a Riemannian metric, A_cd is traceless, divergence-free, and symmetric, and tau is the mean curvature, what conditions guarantee solvability when tau is not constant?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact 3-manifold without boundary. Consider the following conformal data on $M$:
- a Riemannian metric $\gamma_{ab}$,
- a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor $A_{cd}$ that is traceless ($\gamma^{cd}A_{cd}=0$) and transverse (divergence-free, $\nabla^c A_{cd}=0$) with respect to $\gamma_{ab}$,
- a smooth scalar function $\tau$ on $M$ (the prescribed mean curvature).

The Lichnerowicz–Choquet-Bruhat–York (LCBY) system for an unknown positive conformal factor $\varphi>0$ and an unknown vector field $W^a$ on $M$ is:
$$\Delta_\gamma \varphi \;=\; \tfrac{1}{8} R(\gamma)\,\varphi \;-\; \tfrac{1}{8}\,\bigl|A + \mathbb{L}W\bigr|_\gamma^{2}\,\varphi^{-7} \;+\; \tfrac{1}{12}\,\tau^{2}\,\varphi^{5},$$
$$\nabla^{b}\!\bigl(\mathbb{L}W\bigr)_{ab} \;=\; \tfrac{2}{3}\,\varphi^{6}\,\nabla_{a}\tau,$$
where $(\mathbb{L}W)_{ab} = \nabla_a W_b + \nabla_b W_a - \tfrac{2}{3}\gamma_{ab}\nabla_c W^c$ is the conformal Killing operator and $R(\gamma)$ is the scalar curvature of $\gamma_{ab}$.

Solving the LCBY system produces an initial data set $(\bar\gamma_{ab},\bar K_{ab})=(\varphi^{4}\gamma_{ab},\, \varphi^{-2}(A+\mathbb{L}W)_{ab} + \tfrac{1}{3}\tau\varphi^{4}\gamma_{ab})$ for the vacuum Einstein constraint equations on $M$.

Problem. Determine general conditions on the conformal data $(\gamma_{ab}, A_{cd}, \tau)$, with $\tau$ not constant on $M$, which guarantee that the LCBY system admits a solution $(\varphi, W)$ with $\varphi>0$. In particular, identify a sharp class of non-CMC data extending the known constant-$\tau$ existence theory (e.g., generalizing it so as to apply whenever $|\nabla \log \tau|$ is sufficiently small, and beyond).
status_search_result: The problem of solvability of the LCBY (conformal) constraint equations for non-constant mean curvature $\tau$ on closed 3-manifolds remains only partially solved. The constant-mean-curvature case was fully classified by Isenberg (1995). For non-CMC data, existence results have been obtained in the near-CMC regime by Isenberg–Moncrief and others, and in the far-from-CMC regime by Holst–Nagy–Tsogtgerel (2009) and Maxwell (2009) under smallness assumptions on the freely specified data; Maxwell also produced non-existence and non-uniqueness counterexamples for far-from-CMC data. A fully general criterion characterizing solvability for arbitrary non-constant $\tau$ is still not known.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Which hyperboloidal initial data arise from spacetimes with smooth conformal null infinity, and what class of Lichnerowicz-Choquet-Bruhat-York conformal data (gamma_ab, A_cd, tau) constructs such hyperboloidal initial data?
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Consider the vacuum Einstein equations on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold (M, g). A hyperboloidal initial data set is a triple (S, h, K) where S is a 3-manifold with boundary ∂S, h is a Riemannian metric on the interior, and K is a symmetric 2-tensor playing the role of the second fundamental form, such that S embeds into (M, g) as a spacelike hypersurface whose boundary ∂S lies on (a cross-section of) future null infinity ℐ⁺ and which is asymptotically null near ∂S. A spacetime (M, g) is said to admit a smooth conformal null infinity if there exists a conformal compactification (M̃, g̃ = Ω² g) with smooth boundary ℐ on which Ω = 0, dΩ ≠ 0, and g̃ extends smoothly to ℐ.

The Lichnerowicz–Choquet-Bruhat–York (LCBY) conformal method parametrizes solutions of the Einstein constraint equations on S by the following free conformal data:
• a Riemannian metric γ_ab on S (conformal class representative),
• a symmetric, transverse, traceless tensor A_cd with respect to γ (the TT-part of the rescaled extrinsic curvature), and
• a scalar function τ on S (the mean curvature).
Given (γ_ab, A_cd, τ), one solves the Lichnerowicz equation for a conformal factor φ and the vector momentum constraint for a vector field W, and then recovers physical data (h, K) on S by appropriate conformal rescaling.

Problem. 
(a) Characterise intrinsically those hyperboloidal initial data sets (S, h, K) that arise as the induced data on a spacelike hyperboloidal hypersurface of a vacuum spacetime (M, g) admitting a smooth conformal null infinity ℐ⁺.
(b) Identify and describe explicitly a class of LCBY conformal data (γ_ab, A_cd, τ) on S — including their regularity and asymptotic behaviour at ∂S — such that the LCBY procedure yields exactly hyperboloidal initial data of the type characterised in (a).
status_search_result: The problem has been actively studied with substantial partial results but no complete intrinsic characterisation. Andersson–Chruściel proved that generic hyperboloidal data lead to polyhomogeneous (not smooth) expansions at ℐ, with smoothness occurring only for a non-generic subclass; necessary conditions such as vanishing shear at the conformal boundary are known. Recent work (e.g., 2025 results on hyperboloidal initial data without logarithmic singularities) continues to refine the LCBY-conformal-method construction of smooth hyperboloidal data, but a full characterisation remains incomplete.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Can the space of globally hyperbolic vacuum Einstein metrics on V = R x M3 have more than one connected component, and what compactness or Palais-Smale-type condition for the mass function would be needed to analyze this question in the asymptotically flat setting?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M^3$ be a smooth, closed (or asymptotically flat) oriented 3-manifold and set $V = \mathbb{R} \times M^3$. Consider the space $\mathcal{E}(V)$ of smooth Lorentzian metrics $g$ on $V$ that (i) satisfy the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$, and (ii) are globally hyperbolic, i.e. $V$ admits a Cauchy hypersurface for $g$. Endow $\mathcal{E}(V)$ with a natural smooth topology (e.g. $C^\infty$-topology on metrics, modulo diffeomorphisms of $V$).

(a) Can $\mathcal{E}(V)$ have more than one connected component?

(b) Restrict attention to the asymptotically flat (AF) setting: let $\mathfrak{M}$ denote the space of maximal AF vacuum initial data sets $(M^3, g, K)$ satisfying the hypotheses of the positive mass theorem, and let $m : \mathfrak{M} \to [0, \infty)$ be the ADM mass functional. It is known that $m$ has a unique smooth critical point, namely flat Euclidean $\mathbb{R}^3$ with $K=0$. Formulate and establish a compactness or Palais–Smale–type condition for $m$ on $\mathfrak{M}$ sufficient to conclude that the space of asymptotically flat vacuum spacetimes admitting a maximal Cauchy surface is connected.
status_search_result: No source found establishing connectedness (or multiple components) for the space of globally hyperbolic vacuum Einstein metrics on $\mathbb{R}\times M^3$, nor a Palais–Smale condition for the ADM mass on the space of maximal AF initial data. The problem appears to remain open; related recent work (e.g., gluing of small black holes into initial data sets, large-data results for vacuum Einstein equations) addresses the structure of the initial data manifold but does not resolve the component count or the Palais–Smale question.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Can one give a good local characterization of the Kerr solution among stationary metrics, preferably one that does not depend on the slicing used?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold that is a solution of the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ and that is stationary, i.e. admits a Killing vector field $\xi$ which is timelike on an open region of $M$. The Kerr family is the two-parameter family of stationary, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat vacuum solutions parametrized by mass $m\ge 0$ and angular momentum per unit mass $a$ with $|a|\le m$.

Problem: Find a "good" local characterization of the Kerr solution among stationary vacuum metrics. Whether any of these qualifies as the "good" slicing-independent local characterization sought remains a matter of viewpoint; the problem is partially solved but not definitively settled.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: What singularities can occur in solutions of the static and stationary vacuum Einstein equations, beginning with the possible singularities of the spacelike slices?
self_contained_problem:
Consider solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold $(M,g)$ that are either static (admitting a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector field) or, more generally, stationary (admitting a timelike Killing vector field). In the static case the metric can be written, on the region where the Killing field is timelike, as $g = -V^2\, dt^2 + h$, where $h$ is a Riemannian metric on a 3-dimensional quotient manifold $\Sigma$ (a "spacelike slice") and $V>0$ satisfies $V\,\mathrm{Ric}(h)=\nabla^2 V$, $\Delta V=0$; in the stationary case one obtains an analogous quotient $(\Sigma,h)$ with additional twist data. A singularity is understood as a point or set where the metric $g$ (or, on the quotient, the data $(h,V)$ and the twist) fails to be smoothly extendible.

Provide a general classification and description of the possible types of singularities that can occur for solutions of the static and stationary vacuum Einstein equations. In particular, begin by describing the possible singularities of the spacelike slice $(\Sigma,h)$ (such as conical singularities, asymptotic ends, points where $V\to 0$ or $V\to\infty$, curvature blow-up, degenerations of the metric, struts, etc.) and then determine which of these correspond to genuine spacetime singularities of $(M,g)$ versus removable or coordinate singularities.
status_search_result: The problem of giving a general classification of singularities for static and stationary vacuum Einstein solutions, beginning with singularities of the spacelike slices, remains a broad open program. While individual examples (e.g., Schwarzschild-type, Curzon, conical struts, periodic Kasner-asymptotic ends, multi-black-hole configurations) and partial results (e.g., 5-dimensional space-periodic static solutions, uniqueness theorems for stationary black holes) are known, no comprehensive classification has been established in the literature.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Can one prove that there is no static spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills solution with non-zero electric field?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Yang–Mills system on a four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold with gauge group SU(2): the unknowns are a Lorentzian metric g and a connection (gauge potential) A on a principal SU(2)-bundle with curvature F, satisfying the coupled field equations
   Ric(g) − (1/2) R(g) g = 8π T(F),   d⋆F + [A,⋆F] = 0,
where T(F) is the Yang–Mills stress-energy tensor of F. A solution is called static if the metric admits a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector field ξ and the gauge potential is invariant under the flow of ξ, and spherically symmetric if it is invariant under an isometric SO(3)-action whose orbits are spacelike 2-spheres, with the gauge action lifting to the bundle. In a standard gauge such a solution is described by a metric of the form
   −T(r)² dt² + R(r)² dr² + r² (dθ² + sin²θ dφ²)
together with electric and magnetic gauge potential functions; the "electric" components are those associated with the timelike Killing direction (the dt-part of A), and the solution is said to have non-zero electric field if these electric components give a non-trivial Yang–Mills electric field F(ξ, ·).

Prove that there exists no globally regular (or asymptotically flat) static, spherically symmetric solution of the SU(2) Einstein–Yang–Mills equations with non-zero electric field.
status_search_result: Web search did not turn up a definitive published proof that no static, spherically symmetric Einstein–Yang–Mills solution with non-zero electric field exists. Existing rigorous works (e.g., Smoller–Wasserman and follow-ups) restrict to the purely magnetic ansatz, while the vanishing of the electric component is typically imposed as a gauge/ansatz choice rather than derived as a theorem. The status of a fully general proof appears to remain unsettled.

original_question: Are there axially symmetric static or stationary Einstein-Yang-Mills solutions that generalize the Kerr-Newman solution?

Consider the Einstein–Yang–Mills equations on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ coupled to a non-abelian gauge connection $A$ with compact (e.g. $SU(2)$) structure group, namely
$$\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2} R\, g = 8\pi T(F),\qquad d\!\star\! F + [A,\star F]=0,$$
where $F=dA+A\wedge A$ is the Yang–Mills curvature and $T(F)$ is its energy-momentum tensor. paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Can one prove that every static black-hole solution of the Einstein-Yang-Mills equations is Reissner-Nordstrom?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Yang–Mills (EYM) system on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime (M,g), consisting of a metric g and a connection A on a principal bundle with compact, semi-simple gauge group G (e.g. SU(2)), with curvature 2-form F. The field equations are
  Ric(g) − (1/2) R(g) g = 8π T(F),  d⋆F + [A,⋆F] = 0,
where T(F) is the Yang–Mills stress–energy tensor.

A black-hole solution is an asymptotically flat, regular solution of these equations possessing a non-empty event horizon. The solution is called static if (M,g) admits a Killing vector field that is timelike near spatial infinity and orthogonal to a family of spacelike hypersurfaces, and if A is invariant under the corresponding flow.

The Reissner–Nordström family consists of the spherically symmetric solutions with an Abelian (Coulombic) Yang–Mills field, i.e. F valued in a fixed Cartan subalgebra and given by an electric/magnetic monopole on each Lie-algebra direction, with metric
  g = −(1 − 2M/r + Q²/r²) dt² + (1 − 2M/r + Q²/r²)⁻¹ dr² + r² dΩ²,
for constants M and Q.

Problem. Prove or disprove: every static, asymptotically flat black-hole solution of the Einstein–Yang–Mills equations is gauge-equivalent to a Reissner–Nordström solution.
status_search_result: The conjectured statement is now known to be false in the non-Abelian setting: Bartnik–McKinnon solitons (1988) and the subsequent "colored black holes" of Bizoń, Künzle–Masood-ul-Alam, and Volkov–Gal'tsov provide explicit static, asymptotically flat, spherically symmetric black-hole solutions of the SU(2) Einstein–Yang–Mills equations that are not Reissner–Nordström, thereby violating the no-hair conjecture for EYM. These hairy black holes are typically unstable, but exist as genuine static solutions, so the proposed uniqueness statement does not hold as stated.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Can one show that any solution of the Einstein equations linearized about Minkowski space is close to a non-flat exact solution of the full Einstein equations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\mathbb{R}^{1+3}, \eta)$ be Minkowski space, where $\eta = \mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Consider the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$ for a Lorentzian metric $g$ on a $4$-manifold. Writing $g = \eta + h$ and discarding terms of order $\geq 2$ in $h$, one obtains the linearized vacuum Einstein equations about Minkowski space for the symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field $h$ on $\mathbb{R}^{1+3}$.

Prove or disprove the following: For every (sufficiently regular, e.g. smooth and suitably decaying) solution $h$ of the linearized vacuum Einstein equations about Minkowski space, there exists a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ on $\mathbb{R}^{1+3}$ which is an exact solution of the full vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$, is not isometric to Minkowski space (i.e. is non-flat), and is close to $\eta + h$ in an appropriate function-space topology (for instance, a weighted Sobolev or $C^k$ norm capturing the regularity and decay of $h$).

Equivalently: show that every non-trivial linearized perturbation of Minkowski space can be approximated by (or arises as the linearization of) a non-flat exact vacuum solution of the Einstein equations.
status_search_result: General linearization-stability results about Minkowski are known (e.g., Choquet-Bruhat–Deser, and the Christodoulou–Klainerman nonlinear stability of Minkowski space, 1993), and certain linearized solutions can be promoted to exact solutions via specific gauges. However, no source in the search clearly settles the general statement that every linearized vacuum solution about Minkowski is close to a non-flat exact vacuum solution, so the precise status of this problem as posed could not be verified.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Can one prove the existence of a limiting regime in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein field equations of general relativity for a Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ coupled to a matter model (for instance a perfect fluid). Introduce a dimensionless parameter $\lambda = 1/c$, where $c$ denotes the speed of light, and consider one-parameter families of solutions $(M, g_\lambda, T_\lambda)$ of the Einstein equations indexed by $\lambda \in (0, \lambda_0]$.

A Newtonian spacetime is a four-dimensional manifold equipped with the Newton–Cartan structure: a closed one-form $dt$ (absolute time), a symmetric positive semidefinite contravariant tensor $h^{ab}$ of rank three with $h^{ab}(dt)_b = 0$ (spatial metric), and a torsion-free connection $\nabla$ compatible with $dt$ and $h^{ab}$, whose Ricci tensor satisfies the Newton–Cartan field equation $R_{ab} = 4\pi G \rho\, (dt)_a (dt)_b$, where $\rho$ is the mass density of the matter source.

Problem. Prove that there exist non-trivial one-parameter families of solutions $(g_\lambda, T_\lambda)$ of the Einstein equations, defined on a common spacetime region, such that as $\lambda \to 0$ the geometric data $(g_\lambda, T_\lambda)$ converge (in a suitable function-space sense, on appropriate space-time domains and for general physically reasonable matter models and initial data) to a solution of the Newton–Cartan equations describing a Newtonian spacetime. In particular, establish a rigorous limiting regime — including, where possible, global-in-time control and treatment of cosmologically relevant settings — in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes.
status_search_result: Rigorous results on the Newtonian limit of the Einstein equations have been obtained (e.g., Ehlers' frame theory and subsequent work by Rendall, Oliynyk and others using PDE methods with multiple time scales), proving that one-parameter families of solutions to Einstein's equations converge on finite time intervals to Newtonian solutions for various matter models. However, a fully general result covering all physically relevant settings (including global-in-time and cosmological regimes with general matter) is not established, so the problem is regarded as partially solved.

original_question: Can one show that test particles, modeled as very small but finite bodies, move along spacetime geodesics?
