paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
original_question: How far is D_mu(M), the Frechet Lie group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms with the right-invariant L2 hydrodynamic metric, from being an infinite-dimensional locally symmetric Riemannian space?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth Riemannian manifold equipped with a smooth volume form $\mu$. Let $\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$ denote the Fréchet Lie group of smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$, endowed with the right-invariant weak Riemannian metric induced at the identity by the $L^2$ inner product on divergence-free vector fields:
$$\langle u, v\rangle = \int_M \langle u(x), v(x)\rangle_{g}\,d\mu(x),$$
for $u,v \in T_e\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$. With respect to this metric, geodesics on $\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$ correspond (via Arnold's principle) to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$. Let $R$ denote the sectional curvature tensor of this weak Riemannian structure on $\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$.

Recall that a Riemannian manifold (in the finite-dimensional sense) is locally symmetric if and only if $\nabla R \equiv 0$, where $\nabla$ is the Levi-Civita connection. Extending this notion to the infinite-dimensional Fréchet setting, quantify in a precise sense the extent to which $\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$, equipped with the right-invariant $L^2$ hydrodynamic metric, fails to be a locally symmetric Riemannian space. In particular, characterize (or estimate) the covariant derivative $\nabla R$ of the curvature tensor, identify obstructions to local symmetry, and determine for which manifolds $M$ (if any) the space $\mathcal{D}_\mu(M)$ is locally symmetric.

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
original_question: For Yudovich solutions of the Euler equations, where the velocity field is divergence-free and has bounded vorticity curl u, are particle trajectories analytic in time? If only Gevrey regularity is known, is that Gevrey regularity sharp?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Euler equations on a domain in R^2 (or on a smooth bounded planar domain),
  ∂_t u + (u·∇)u = −∇p,   div u = 0,
with initial velocity u_0 having bounded vorticity ω_0 = curl u_0 ∈ L^∞. By Yudovich's theorem there exists a unique global weak solution u with curl u ∈ L^∞_t L^∞_x, and the associated flow map X(t,x) defined by
  d/dt X(t,x) = u(t, X(t,x)),   X(0,x) = x,
is well defined.

Question: For every such Yudovich solution, is the trajectory t ↦ X(t,x) real-analytic in time? Equivalently, is the flow map t ↦ X(t,·) real-analytic as a map into the group of measure-preserving homeomorphisms?

If only Gevrey-class regularity of the trajectories t ↦ X(t,x) can be established (i.e., the trajectories belong to some Gevrey class G^s with s > 1 but are not known to be analytic), determine whether the Gevrey index s obtained is sharp: that is, exhibit either an improvement to a smaller Gevrey index (ultimately analyticity, s = 1), or construct an example of a Yudovich initial datum whose trajectories fail to belong to G^{s'} for any s' < s.
status_search_result: Partial results are known: for bounded planar domains with smooth boundary, Yudovich-class trajectories are C^∞ in time, and for Gevrey-M boundaries they are Gevrey of order M+2 (Sueur and collaborators). On the whole plane, time-analyticity of Lagrangian trajectories has been established under slightly better-than-continuous vorticity (Chemin, Constantin–Vicol–Kukavica, Frisch–Zheligovsky type results). Full analyticity for general bounded vorticity, and sharpness of the Gevrey index when only Gevrey regularity is available, remain open.

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
original_question: For every compact analytic two-dimensional Riemannian manifold M with analytic boundary, is the set GM(M) of generalized minimal flows a nonempty proper subset of the Yudovich space YU(M), where YU(M) consists of divergence-free vector fields with bounded vorticity?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact two-dimensional real-analytic Riemannian manifold with real-analytic boundary. Define the Yudovich space
$$\mathrm{YU}(M) = \{ u \in L^2(M; TM) : \operatorname{div} u = 0,\ u \cdot \nu|_{\partial M} = 0,\ \operatorname{curl} u \in L^\infty(M)\},$$
i.e., divergence-free, tangent-to-boundary vector fields on $M$ whose vorticity $\omega = \operatorname{curl} u$ is essentially bounded. Within $\mathrm{YU}(M)$, call $u$ a generalized minimal flow if it is a stationary solution of the incompressible Euler equation on $M$ that arises as a weak limit (or, equivalently, as a minimizer in the appropriate variational/relaxed sense) of the energy among isovortical rearrangements—so that $u$ minimizes the kinetic energy $\tfrac12\int_M |u|^2$ within its generalized vorticity class. Let $\mathrm{GM}(M) \subset \mathrm{YU}(M)$ denote the set of all such generalized minimal flows on $M$.

Prove that for every such $M$, the set $\mathrm{GM}(M)$ is a nonempty proper subset of $\mathrm{YU}(M)$:
$$\varnothing \neq \mathrm{GM}(M) \subsetneq \mathrm{YU}(M).$$
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the surveys on geometric hydrodynamics; the search returned no proof establishing nonemptiness and properness of GM(M) inside the Yudovich space YU(M) for all compact analytic surfaces with analytic boundary. It is listed among current open problems on generalized minimal flows.

original_question: For every generalized minimal flow whose vorticity domain decomposes numerically into blobs B_1,...,B_N and a background region B_0, is curl u constant on the background B_0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a two-dimensional flow domain (for instance the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^2$) and let $u$ be a smooth divergence-free vector field on $M$ with scalar vorticity $\omega = \operatorname{curl} u$. Call $u$ a generalized minimal flow (GM-flow) if it is a critical point of the $L^2$-norm of vorticity restricted to the coadjoint orbit of $\omega$ under the action of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms; equivalently, every field $\tilde u$ whose vorticity is obtained from $\omega$ by an area-preserving rearrangement satisfies $\|\operatorname{curl}\tilde u\|_{L^2} \ge \|\operatorname{curl} u\|_{L^2}$ at the infinitesimal level. Suppose the vorticity configuration of such a GM-flow decomposes into finitely many "vorticity blobs" $B_1,\dots,B_N \subset M$ (compactly supported regions on which $\omega$ takes non-trivial, localized profiles) together with a complementary "background" region $B_0 = M \setminus \bigcup_{i=1}^N B_i$.

Question: Must $\operatorname{curl} u$ be constant on the background region $B_0$ for every such GM-flow?

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
original_question: Can one define anisotropic function spaces for ideal hydrodynamics that encode higher smoothness along flow lines, and prove existence and uniqueness of ideal fluid motion in those spaces in arbitrary dimension?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an ideal incompressible fluid on a Riemannian manifold $M$ of arbitrary dimension $n$, whose motion is governed by the incompressible Euler equations
$$\partial_t u + \nabla_u u = -\nabla p, \qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
with initial data $u_0$ tangent to $\partial M$ (if non-empty). Classical local well-posedness is known in isotropic Sobolev spaces $H^s$ with $s > n/2 + 1$ (Ebin–Marsden), where smoothness is required equally in all spatial directions.

Define a scale of anisotropic function spaces $\mathcal{A}^{s,k}(M)$ for divergence-free vector fields with the property that elements of $\mathcal{A}^{s,k}$ possess a baseline transverse regularity of order $s$ but additional regularity of order $k$ along the flow lines of the velocity field $u$ itself (so that directional derivatives $(u\cdot\nabla)^j u$ for $0 \le j \le k$ are controlled in the transverse space). Then prove existence and uniqueness of solutions to the incompressible Euler equations in these anisotropic spaces $\mathcal{A}^{s,k}(M)$, in arbitrary dimension $n \ge 2$, with regularity thresholds lower than those required by the isotropic theory.
category_tag: Anisotropic function spaces for Euler equations
status_search_result: No construction of anisotropic function spaces tailored to ideal hydrodynamics with the proposed flow-line regularity, together with a corresponding existence–uniqueness theorem in arbitrary dimension, appears in the literature. While anisotropic regularity conditions for Navier–Stokes and Lagrangian/flow-decoupling techniques exist, the problem of building such spaces and proving well-posedness of the Euler equations in them remains an open program.

context_brief: Fredholm failure of the L2 exponential map
original_question: For a compact Riemannian three-manifold M, can one quantify how the L2 exponential map on D_mu^s(M) fails to be a Fredholm map, for example by measuring the noncompact part of the operator that appears in its derivative?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian three-manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the Hilbert manifold of Sobolev-class $H^s$ volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$, for $s > 5/2$. Equip $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ with the right-invariant $L^2$ metric, whose geodesics correspond (by Arnold's theorem) to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$. Let $\exp_e : T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M) \to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ be the associated Riemannian exponential map at the identity $e$.

It is known that, in contrast to the two-dimensional case where $d\exp_e$ at each point decomposes as the sum of an invertible operator and a compact operator (so that $\exp_e$ is a nonlinear Fredholm map of index zero), in dimension three the corresponding "compact part" $K$ appearing in the derivative $d\exp_e$ generally fails to be compact, so $\exp_e$ fails to be Fredholm.

Problem. Quantify the failure of the $L^2$ exponential map $\exp_e$ on $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ to be a nonlinear Fredholm map. For instance, provide a natural measure of the noncompact part of the operator $K$ appearing in $d\exp_e$ (such as its essential spectrum, essential norm, distance in operator norm to the compact operators, or membership in suitable Schatten–von Neumann or other operator ideals as a function of the initial velocity field), and describe how this quantity depends on the geometry of $M$ and on the initial data.
status_search_result: The qualitative result that the $L^2$ exponential map on volume-preserving diffeomorphisms is Fredholm in 2D but generically fails to be Fredholm in 3D (with the relevant operator not even Hilbert–Schmidt) is established in works by Ebin–Misiołek–Preston and follow-ups. However, no published quantitative measure of how badly Fredholmness fails in 3D (e.g. essential norm, Schatten-class membership, or essential spectrum of the compact-part operator) appears in the literature; recent work (e.g. on singular sets of Riemannian exponential maps in hydrodynamics, 2025) still treats this as an open direction.

context_brief: Exponential upper bound on flow complexity
original_question: For a geodesic gamma(t) in D_mu^s(M) on a compact two-dimensional manifold, with absolute complexity C defined via products of small exponential-map neighborhoods of the identity, can one prove that C(gamma(t)) is bounded above exponentially in time by a constant of the form exp(t||dot gamma(0)||_{H^s})?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold (possibly with boundary), and for $s > 2$ let $\mathcal{D}_\mu^s(M)$ denote the group of volume-preserving Sobolev $H^s$-diffeomorphisms of $M$, equipped with the right-invariant $L^2$ metric whose geodesics correspond (via Arnold's formalism) to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$. Near the identity $e \in \mathcal{D}_\mu^s(M)$, fix a sufficiently small open neighborhood $U$ which lies in the image of the Riemannian exponential map at $e$. For any $\varphi \in \mathcal{D}_\mu^s(M)$, define the absolute complexity
$$C(\varphi) := \min\{ k \in \mathbb{N} : \varphi = \varphi_1 \varphi_2 \cdots \varphi_k \text{ with each } \varphi_i \in U \},$$
i.e., the minimal number of factors from $U$ needed to express $\varphi$ as a product.

$$C(\gamma(t)) \le K \exp\!\big(t \, \|\dot{\gamma}(0)\|_{H^s}\big).$$

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
original_question: Can the aging of an ideal fluid be quantified from its velocity field, for example by constructing a continuous Lyapunov function on the velocity space whose value is nondecreasing along Euler solutions and is constant only on a slim subset?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold (with or without boundary) and let $\mathcal{V}$ denote the space of smooth divergence-free vector fields on $M$ (tangent to the boundary, if any), equipped with a suitable topology (e.g., a Sobolev $H^s$ topology with $s$ large enough so that the incompressible Euler equation
$$\partial_t u + \nabla_u u = -\nabla p, \qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
defines a continuous local flow $u(t)$ on $\mathcal{V}$).

Numerical evidence suggests that generic solutions of the Euler equation exhibit "aging": derivatives of the velocity field tend to grow and the field becomes increasingly "wrinkled" with time, in a way that should make the temporal ordering of two snapshots of the same solution detectable from the velocity fields alone.

Question: Does there exist a continuous function $L : \mathcal{V} \to \mathbb{R}$ (a Lyapunov function for aging) such that
1. for every solution $u(t)$ of the Euler equation, the map $t \mapsto L(u(t))$ is nondecreasing, and
2. the set of velocity fields on which $L$ fails to be strictly increasing along the Euler flow (equivalently, the set where $L$ is constant along solutions) is "slim" — for instance, nowhere dense, of first Baire category, or of codimension at least one in $\mathcal{V}$?

More generally, can the aging of an ideal incompressible fluid be quantified from its velocity field, i.e., can one decide from two velocity snapshots of a single Euler solution which one occurred earlier?
status_search_result: The problem of quantifying the "aging" of an ideal fluid via a continuous Lyapunov function on the velocity space is listed as an open problem in Khesin's collection of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics (published in ARMA, 2023, and posted as arXiv:2205.01143). Recent surveys, including a 2025 article on the dynamics of ideal fluid flows, still treat it as an open question; no construction of such a Lyapunov function has been reported.

context_brief: Entropy functions for sets and measures
original_question: For entropy notions of compact sets and probability measures in metric or Hilbert spaces, including H_epsilon, H_{epsilon,delta}, tilde H_epsilon, and tilde H_{epsilon,delta}, what are their properties and how are they related?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\rho)$ be a complete metric space (in particular a separable Hilbert space). For a compact subset $K\subset X$ and $\varepsilon>0$, define the $\varepsilon$-entropy
$$H_\varepsilon(K) := \log_2 N_\varepsilon(K),$$
where $N_\varepsilon(K)$ is the minimal number of closed balls of radius $\varepsilon$ in $X$ needed to cover $K$. For a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $X$ and $\varepsilon,\delta>0$, define the $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-entropy
$$H_{\varepsilon,\delta}(\mu) := \inf\{\log_2 N : \exists \text{ Borel sets } A_1,\dots,A_N \text{ of diameter } \le 2\varepsilon \text{ with } \mu(A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_N)\ge 1-\delta\}.$$
Analogously define the "dual" or covering-by-measures versions $\tilde H_\varepsilon(K)$ as $\log_2$ of the minimal cardinality of an $\varepsilon$-net of $K$ (i.e. a finite subset $F\subset K$ such that every point of $K$ is within $\varepsilon$ of $F$), and $\tilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}(\mu)$ as $\log_2$ of the minimal number of points $x_1,\dots,x_N\in X$ such that $\mu(\bigcup_i B(x_i,\varepsilon))\ge 1-\delta$.

Problem. Investigate the properties of the four functionals $H_\varepsilon$, $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$, $\tilde H_\varepsilon$, $\tilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ (monotonicity, continuity, sub/superadditivity, behaviour under push-forward, asymptotics as $\varepsilon,\delta\to 0$, finiteness/infiniteness, dependence on the ambient geometry), and establish the precise quantitative relations between them — in particular inequalities comparing $H_\varepsilon$ with $\tilde H_\varepsilon$ for compact sets, comparisons between $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ and $\tilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ for probability measures, and the connection between the set-entropies and the measure-entropies via supports and weak limits.
category_tag: metric entropy of sets and measures
status_search_result: While classical $\varepsilon$-entropy of compact sets (Kolmogorov–Tikhomirov) and $\varepsilon$-entropy of probability distributions (Posner–Rodemich and others) are well-developed, a unified systematic comparison of the four variants $H_\varepsilon, H_{\varepsilon,\delta}, \tilde H_\varepsilon, \tilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ as posed appears to remain an investigative problem; no source found resolves it as a single program.

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
original_question: Can one prove non-integrability of the two-dimensional Euler equation, in the sense that the equation fails at least one appropriate notion of integrability for infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems despite having Casimirs and a Lax-type form?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation on a closed surface (for instance the two-torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ or the two-sphere $S^2$) with area form $\mu$. In vorticity form it reads
$$\partial_t \omega + \{\psi, \omega\} = 0, \qquad \Delta \psi = \omega, \qquad \int \omega\,\mu = 0,$$
where $\omega$ is the vorticity, $\psi$ the stream function and $\{\cdot,\cdot\}$ the Poisson bracket induced by $\mu$. This equation is the Hamiltonian flow on the dual of the Lie algebra $\mathrm{svect}(M)$ of divergence-free vector fields, with Hamiltonian $H(\omega) = \tfrac12 \int \psi\,\omega\,\mu$. It admits the infinite family of Casimir functionals $C_f(\omega) = \int f(\omega)\,\mu$ for any smooth $f$, and may be written in Lax form $\dot L = [L, A]$ for suitable operators $L, A$ on the surface.

Prove that, despite possessing this Lax-type representation and the infinite family of Casimirs, the two-dimensional Euler equation is non-integrable as an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian system, in the sense that it fails at least one appropriate notion of complete integrability (for example, the absence of a complete commuting family of analytic first integrals independent of the Casimirs that would foliate generic coadjoint orbits by invariant tori, or the non-existence of action-angle coordinates on generic symplectic leaves).
status_search_result: The non-integrability of the 2D Euler equation as an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian system is widely conjectured but, to current knowledge, not rigorously established. Available literature confirms its non-canonical Hamiltonian structure, the existence of Casimirs (vorticity moments), and Lax-type formulations, while only conjecturing the absence of additional conserved quantities beyond energy and momenta. No source verifies a proof of non-integrability in a rigorous infinite-dimensional sense.

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
original_question: For small numbers of point vortices, can one systematically study their motion and bifurcations on manifolds such as half-planes, quarter-planes, hemispheres, quarter-spheres, disks, tori, cylinders, and half-cylinders?
status_search_result: There is an active body of work on point-vortex dynamics for small N on several of the listed domains: relative equilibria and their bifurcations on the sphere (including hemisphere via reflection) have been studied (Pekarsky–Marsden, Laurent-Polz, Montaldi and collaborators), the 2-vortex problem on a torus is known to be integrable, and stability of latitudinal rings on tori has been analyzed (Sakajo and others). Partial results also exist for the disk and half-plane via image methods. However, a unified systematic treatment of bifurcations across all of the listed geometries (half-plane, quarter-plane, hemisphere, quarter-sphere, disk, torus, cylinder, half-cylinder) does not appear to have been completed.

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
original_question: Does the three-dimensional Euler equation have wandering solutions, analogous to Nadirashvili's two-dimensional annulus example in which a neighborhood of an initial condition never returns sufficiently close after some time?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Euler equations on a bounded three-dimensional domain $M\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ (for instance, a solid torus or a spherical shell) with smooth boundary, written for the velocity field $u:M\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^3$ as
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u = -\nabla p,\qquad \mathrm{div}\,u=0,\qquad u\cdot n|_{\partial M}=0.$$
Regard the Euler flow as a dynamical system on a suitable space $\mathcal{V}$ of divergence-free vector fields tangent to $\partial M$, equipped with a fixed topology (e.g., $C^k$ for some $k\geq 1$, or $L^2$). Call a solution $u(t)$ \emph{wandering} if there exists an open neighborhood $U\subset\mathcal{V}$ of the initial datum $u(0)$ and a time $T>0$ such that the time-$t$ Euler flow $\Phi_t(U)$ satisfies $\Phi_t(U)\cap U=\emptyset$ for all $t\geq T$.

In dimension two on an annulus, Nadirashvili constructed such wandering solutions: there exist smooth, divergence-free initial velocity fields together with a $C^1$-open neighborhood that, after some positive time, never returns to itself under the 2D Euler flow.

Question: Do wandering solutions, in the above sense, exist for the three-dimensional Euler equations on some bounded smooth domain $M\subset\mathbb{R}^3$?
status_search_result: Nadirashvili's 1991 result establishes wandering solutions for the 2D Euler equation on an annulus. According to current literature on geometric hydrodynamics, the existence of a 3D analogue remains unknown; related progress uses KAM-type methods and stability/instability of steady states, but no full 3D wandering construction has been verified.

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
context_brief: Chaos on singular parts of integrable systems
original_question: For an integrable system on a compact 2n-dimensional manifold with n independent commuting first integrals almost everywhere, how wild can the dynamics be on singular submanifolds where the integrals become dependent? What constraints does integrability impose, and can chaotic behavior occur on a tiny singular submanifold?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{2n}, \omega)$ be a compact symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$ equipped with $n$ smooth functions $f_1, \dots, f_n : M \to \mathbb{R}$ that pairwise Poisson-commute, $\{f_i, f_j\} = 0$ for all $i, j$, and whose differentials $df_1, \dots, df_n$ are linearly independent on an open dense subset $U \subset M$. Let $X_{f_1}$ be the Hamiltonian vector field of $f_1$, and let $S := M \setminus U$ denote the singular set where the integrals fail to be independent.

(a) Describe the possible dynamical behaviors of $X_{f_1}$ restricted to invariant subsets of the singular submanifold $S$. In particular, determine what constraints (if any) are imposed by the existence of the commuting integrals on $M$.

(b) Decide whether the flow of $X_{f_1}$ on $S$ (or on an invariant subset of $S$) can exhibit chaotic behavior — for instance, positive topological entropy, a horseshoe, or sensitive dependence on initial conditions — even when $S$ is arbitrarily small (e.g., of arbitrarily small Hausdorff dimension or measure) inside $M$.

(c) Construct an example, or prove the impossibility of such, of a smooth integrable system in the above sense whose restriction to the singular set $S$ supports topologically chaotic dynamics while the integrability on $M \setminus S$ is preserved.
status_search_result: The question concerns the dynamics of integrable Hamiltonian systems on their singular sets, an active research area at the interface of integrable systems and singularity theory. Recent surveys and problem lists on finite-dimensional integrable systems list questions about singular fibers and chaos on them as open, and no general classification or example resolving the question appears in the literature.

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
original_question: Can one find a hierarchy of higher helicity invariants for divergence-free vector fields such that, when all previous invariants vanish, the first nonzero invariant gives a lower bound for the field's energy?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian 3-manifold (or a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with appropriate boundary conditions) and let $\mathcal{V}(M)$ denote the space of smooth divergence-free vector fields on $M$ (tangent to the boundary, if any). For such a field $v \in \mathcal{V}(M)$, the classical helicity is
$$\mathcal{H}(v) = \int_M \langle v, \operatorname{curl}^{-1} v\rangle \, d\mathrm{vol},$$
and Arnold's inequality gives the energy lower bound $\|v\|_{L^2}^2 \geq C\,|\mathcal{H}(v)|$ for some constant $C = C(M) > 0$.

Construct a hierarchy of higher-order invariants $\mathcal{H}_1, \mathcal{H}_2, \mathcal{H}_3, \ldots$ defined on $\mathcal{V}(M)$ (with $\mathcal{H}_1 = \mathcal{H}$ the ordinary helicity), invariant under the action of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms isotopic to the identity, with the following property: for every $k \geq 1$, if $\mathcal{H}_1(v) = \mathcal{H}_2(v) = \cdots = \mathcal{H}_{k-1}(v) = 0$ but $\mathcal{H}_k(v) \neq 0$, then there exists a constant $C_k = C_k(M) > 0$ and an exponent $\alpha_k > 0$ such that
$$\|v\|_{L^2}^2 \geq C_k\,|\mathcal{H}_k(v)|^{\alpha_k}.$$
Does such a hierarchy of higher helicity invariants exist?
status_search_result: The problem of constructing higher helicity invariants giving energy lower bounds when lower-order invariants vanish is a well-known question going back to Arnold. Partial progress exists: cubic helicities and higher asymptotic linking analogs have been constructed (e.g., Bogoyavlenskij, Akhmetiev), and a result by Enciso–Peralta-Salas–Torres de Lizaur shows helicity is essentially the only regular integral invariant under some assumptions, suggesting obstructions. No complete solution providing the full hierarchy with energy lower bounds appears established; the problem remains open.

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
context_brief: Singular reductions of NLS and compressible Euler
original_question: Can one derive a direct reduction from the three-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation to the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation through singular solutions, without passing through the localized induction approximation? Similarly, can compressible Euler equations be reduced from three dimensions to singular solutions supported on one-dimensional submanifolds?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation in three spatial dimensions,
\[
 i\,\partial_t \psi + \Delta \psi + |\psi|^2\psi = 0,\qquad \psi:\mathbb{R}_t\times\mathbb{R}^3_x\to\mathbb{C},
\]
and, separately, the compressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$,
\[
 \partial_t \rho + \nabla\!\cdot(\rho u)=0,\qquad \partial_t(\rho u) + \nabla\!\cdot(\rho u\otimes u) + \nabla p(\rho)=0,
\]
for density $\rho:\mathbb{R}_t\times\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$, velocity $u:\mathbb{R}_t\times\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$, and a prescribed equation of state $p=p(\rho)$.

It is classically known that the localized induction (binormal-flow) approximation for a vortex filament $\gamma(t,s)\subset\mathbb{R}^3$, $\gamma_t=\gamma_s\times\gamma_{ss}$, can be mapped via the Hasimoto transform to the one-dimensional cubic NLS
\[
 i\,\partial_t q + \partial_s^2 q + \tfrac{1}{2}|q|^2 q = 0.
\]
The questions are the following.

(a) Construct a direct reduction of the three-dimensional cubic NLS to the one-dimensional cubic NLS by considering a class of solutions $\psi$ that are singular and concentrated on a moving one-dimensional submanifold (curve) $\gamma(t,\cdot)\subset\mathbb{R}^3$, such that the resulting effective dynamics for an associated complex amplitude along the curve is governed by the 1D cubic NLS — without invoking the localized induction approximation as an intermediate step.

(b) Analogously, construct a reduction of the three-dimensional compressible Euler system to a self-consistent dynamics for singular solutions whose support lies on a one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^3$, deriving the equations of motion for such curve-supported singular Euler solutions.

Determine whether such direct reductions exist, and if so describe the admissible ansätze and the resulting one-dimensional evolution equations.
category_tag: Singular reductions of NLS and Euler
status_search_result: No published direct reduction of 3D NLS to 1D NLS through curve-supported singular solutions (bypassing the localized induction approximation) was found; existing links pass through the binormal/Hasimoto route or rely on symmetry reductions. Likewise, no curve-supported singular reduction of 3D compressible Euler was located. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
original_question: Can the Madelung-transform results identifying symplectomorphism and Kahler map structures be extended to wave functions with zeros on M, and can the quantization-condition controversy be explained through the momentum map for the semidirect product of diffeomorphisms and smooth functions?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian manifold, and consider the space $\mathcal{W}(M)$ of complex-valued wave functions $\psi:M\to\mathbb{C}$ of fixed $L^2$-norm. Let $\mathrm{Dens}(M)$ denote the space of smooth probability densities on $M$, equipped with the Fisher–Rao information metric, and let $T^*\mathrm{Dens}(M)$ be its cotangent bundle. The Madelung transform sends a nowhere-vanishing wave function $\psi = \sqrt{\rho}\,e^{i\theta/\hbar}$ to the pair $(\rho,\theta)\in T^*\mathrm{Dens}(M)$ (modulo a global phase). It is known that, restricted to nowhere-vanishing wave functions, the Madelung transform is a symplectomorphism and indeed a Kähler isometry (with respect to the Fubini–Study metric on $\mathcal{W}(M)$ and the Sasaki-type metric induced from Fisher–Rao on $T^*\mathrm{Dens}(M)$); moreover, it arises as the momentum map of the natural action of the semidirect product group $\mathrm{Diff}(M)\ltimes C^\infty(M,\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathcal{W}(M)$.

(a) Extend these results — the symplectomorphism property, the Kähler isometry property, and the momentum-map interpretation — to the full space $\mathcal{W}(M)$ including wave functions with zeros, identifying the appropriate target space (a suitable completion or stratified extension of $T^*\mathrm{Dens}(M)$) on which the extended Madelung map is well defined.

(b) Using the momentum-map structure for the semidirect product $\mathrm{Diff}(M)\ltimes C^\infty(M,\mathbb{R})$, give a geometric explanation of the quantization condition on the circulation $\oint d\theta \in 2\pi\hbar\,\mathbb{Z}$ that arises around zeros of $\psi$, and clarify the apparent controversy concerning whether such a condition must be imposed.
status_search_result: The Kähler/symplectomorphism property and momentum-map interpretation of the Madelung transform are established for nowhere-vanishing wave functions in works by Khesin–Misiołek–Modin (2019) and Fusca (2017). The full extension to wave functions with zeros and a geometric resolution of the quantization-condition issue via the semidirect product momentum map do not appear to have been completed in the literature; the problem remains open as far as could be verified.

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
original_question: In a countable-ball mechanical model for direct cascade, can one choose family sizes n_i, masses m_i, and radii r_i so that energy cascades toward increasing family index and dissipates from the system, and can one identify corresponding structures in an actual three-dimensional fluid?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a countable mechanical system organized into families indexed by i = 1, 2, 3, .... Family i consists of n_i identical hard balls, each of mass m_i and radius r_i, moving in three-dimensional Euclidean space and interacting via elastic collisions (with collisions also permitted between balls belonging to different families). Equip the system with a notion of kinetic energy E_i associated with family i (the sum of kinetic energies of the n_i balls in family i), and assume that energy may leak out of the system through a prescribed dissipation channel at the largest indices (so that the system is open).

Question: Can one choose the family sizes {n_i}, masses {m_i}, and radii {r_i} (and, if needed, initial conditions or a forcing acting on family 1) so that, in a statistically stationary or long-time-averaged sense, energy is transferred predominantly from family i to family i+1 (i.e., toward increasing family index) and is ultimately dissipated from the system, thereby realizing a direct energy cascade? Furthermore, can the families of balls (with their chosen n_i, m_i, r_i) be put in correspondence with identifiable coherent structures in an actual incompressible three-dimensional viscous fluid undergoing a Kolmogorov-type direct energy cascade?
status_search_result: No literature was found resolving this specific countable hard-ball mechanical model of the direct energy cascade with prescribed family sizes, masses, and radii, nor establishing a correspondence with coherent structures in a real 3D fluid. Standard turbulence references discuss cascade models (shell models, Burgers cutoff models) but not this particular ball-family construction, and the question appears to remain open.

paper_title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
original_question: For the proposed infinite-chamber mechanical model of inverse cascade, is there an analogous mechanism in real hydrodynamics, and can the parameters n_i, m_i, and r_i be chosen so that the apparatus transfers energy to the first few chambers as intended?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following idealized mechanical model intended to mimic an inverse energy cascade. The apparatus consists of a countable sequence of chambers indexed by i = 1, 2, 3, …. The i-th chamber contains n_i identical rigid balls, each of mass m_i and radius r_i, which undergo elastic collisions among themselves and with the walls of the chamber. Neighbouring chambers are coupled so that collisions can transfer kinetic energy between balls in chamber i and balls in chamber i+1 (for instance via a shared wall or piston, with elastic interactions). Energy is injected into the system at small scales (large i) and one seeks to observe a net flow of energy toward large scales (small i), i.e. into the first few chambers.

(a) Is there an analogous mechanism in real (continuum) hydrodynamics — for example in two-dimensional incompressible fluid flow, where an inverse energy cascade is known to occur — which corresponds to this mechanical model?

(b) Can the parameters n_i, m_i, r_i (i ≥ 1) be chosen so that, starting from energy supplied to chambers with large index, the apparatus transfers a positive fraction of the total energy to the first few chambers (those with small i) in the long-time limit?
status_search_result: The question appears as an open problem in a 2022/2023 collection of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics. No subsequent literature found that resolves the question of whether the parameters of such an infinite-chamber mechanical apparatus can be tuned to achieve an inverse energy cascade, nor identifying a precise hydrodynamic analogue. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Erdős-Macintyre type theorem’s for multiple Dirichlet series: exceptional sets and open problems
original_question: Let f(z)=∑_{n=0}∞ a_n z^n be a nonconstant entire function, let M_f(r)=max{|f(z)|: |z|=r}, and let μ_f(r)=max_{n≥0}|a_n|r^n. For a fixed ε>0, Wiman's inequality is M_f(r)≤μ_f(r)(ln μ_f(r))^(1/2+ε) for all r outside an exceptional set E. If E=∪_{n=1}∞[a_n,b_n] satisfies ∫_E (ln r)^(1/2) d ln r<∞, does every such set E occur as an exceptional set for Wiman's inequality for some entire function f and that ε?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n z^n$ be a nonconstant entire function. Define the maximum modulus $M_f(r)=\max\{|f(z)|:|z|=r\}$ and the maximal term $\mu_f(r)=\max_{n\ge 0}|a_n|r^n$. Fix $\varepsilon>0$. A classical inequality of Wiman asserts that
$$M_f(r)\le \mu_f(r)\bigl(\ln \mu_f(r)\bigr)^{1/2+\varepsilon}$$
holds for all $r$ outside some exceptional set $E\subset[1,\infty)$.

paper_title: Erdős-Macintyre type theorem’s for multiple Dirichlet series: exceptional sets and open problems
original_question: Let p≥1 and let F∈D_p(λ^p) be an entire function on C^p represented by an absolutely convergent multiple Dirichlet series F(z)=∑_{n∈Z_+^p} a_n exp(<z,λ_n>). For x∈R^p define M(x,F)=sup{|F(x+iy)|: y∈R^p}, m(x,F)=inf{|F(x+iy)|: y∈R^p}, and μ(x,F)=max{|a_n|exp(<x,λ_n>) : n∈Z_+^p}. Given a positive differentiable function h:R_+→R_+ with h'(t) increasing to +∞, what conditions on F and its exponent system λ^p guarantee that M(x,F)=(1+o(1))μ(x,F) and M(x,F)=(1+o(1))m(x,F) hold as |x|→∞ outside some set E with finite h–τ_p measure ∫_E h'(|x|) dx_1...dx_p/|x|^(p−1)<∞?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $p\ge 1$. Let $\lambda^p=(\lambda_n)_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+^p}\subset\mathbb{R}_+^p$ be a system of exponents, and let $F\colon\mathbb{C}^p\to\mathbb{C}$ be an entire function representable by an absolutely convergent multiple Dirichlet series
$$F(z)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+^p} a_n\exp(\langle z,\lambda_n\rangle),\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}^p,$$
where $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ denotes the standard inner product on $\mathbb{R}^p$. Denote by $\mathcal{D}_p(\lambda^p)$ the class of all such entire functions. For $x\in\mathbb{R}^p$ define
$$M(x,F)=\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^p}|F(x+iy)|,\quad m(x,F)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}^p}|F(x+iy)|,\quad \mu(x,F)=\max_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+^p}|a_n|\exp(\langle x,\lambda_n\rangle).$$
Let $h\colon\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+$ be a positive differentiable function whose derivative $h'(t)$ is increasing and tends to $+\infty$ as $t\to\infty$. For a measurable set $E\subset\mathbb{R}^p$, define its $h$–$\tau_p$ measure by
$$\tau_p^h(E)=\int_E \frac{h'(|x|)}{|x|^{p-1}}\,dx_1\cdots dx_p.$$

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $F\in\mathcal{D}_p(\lambda^p)$ and on the exponent system $\lambda^p$ under which both asymptotic relations
$$M(x,F)=(1+o(1))\,\mu(x,F)\quad\text{and}\quad M(x,F)=(1+o(1))\,m(x,F)$$
hold as $|x|\to\infty$ with $x$ ranging outside some exceptional set $E\subset\mathbb{R}^p$ of finite $h$–$\tau_p$ measure, i.e. $\tau_p^h(E)<\infty$.

paper_title: Addition Machines, Automatic Functions and Open Problems of Floyd and Knuth

original_question: In Floyd and Knuth's integer addition-machine model, registers hold integers and the unit-cost primitive instructions include adding or subtracting register contents, comparing register contents with conditional branching, unconditional jumps, reading input, and writing output. paper_title: Addition Machines, Automatic Functions and Open Problems of Floyd and Knuth
context_brief: sub-bound sorting of positive integers on addition machines
original_question: For an integer addition machine, given an arbitrary sequence of positive integers q_1, q_2, ..., q_m, can the machine sort the sequence in o((m + log(q_1 q_2 ... q_m)) log m) steps? A complete resolution should answer the asymptotic-improvement question for all common definitions of multivariate little-o, since the maximum-based convention gives a negative answer but alternative conventions remain only partially resolved.
self_contained_problem:
An integer addition machine is a register machine whose registers store integers and whose primitive operations are: (i) loading the constants 0 and 1 into a register, (ii) copying a register, (iii) computing the sum or difference of two registers and storing the result in a register, and (iv) conditional branching based on comparisons (=, <) between two registers. The "number of steps" of a computation is the total number of such primitive operations executed.

Given an input sequence of positive integers q_1, q_2, …, q_m (presented in m designated registers), the machine is said to sort the sequence if it produces in m output registers a permutation of q_1, …, q_m in non-decreasing order. Let log denote the base-2 logarithm. Define
   T(m; q_1, …, q_m) := (m + log(q_1 · q_2 · … · q_m)) · log m.

For two positive functions f, g of the multivariate input (m; q_1, …, q_m), say that f(m; q_1, …, q_m) = o(g(m; q_1, …, q_m)) under a chosen convention of multivariate little-o (for example: (a) f/g → 0 as max(m, q_1, …, q_m) → ∞; (b) f/g → 0 as min(m, q_1, …, q_m) → ∞; or any other standard convention).

Question: Does there exist an integer addition machine which, on every input sequence q_1, q_2, …, q_m of positive integers, sorts the sequence in a number of steps that is
   o((m + log(q_1 · q_2 · … · q_m)) · log m)?
Resolve this for each of the common conventions of multivariate little-o (it is known that under convention (a) the answer is negative; the other conventions are to be settled).
status_search_result: The question is one of the open problems of Floyd and Knuth concerning integer addition machines. Recent work establishes a negative answer under the "max-based" version of multivariate little-o (the Wikipedia convention), but the question remains unresolved under other standard conventions of multivariate little-o, so it is only partially solved.

paper_title: Solutions to Some Open Problems About Four Sombor-Index-Like Graph Invariants
context_brief: Extremal SO5 and SO6 for trees and chemical trees
original_question: For a finite graph G, let E(G) be the edge set of G and let d_u be the degree of a vertex u of G. Define the Sombor-index-like graph invariants SO5 and SO6 by SO5(G) = 2π times the sum over all edges uv in E(G) of |d_u^2 - d_v^2| divided by √(2 + 2√(d_u^2 + d_v^2)), and SO6(G) = π times the sum over all edges uv in E(G) of ((d_u^2 - d_v^2) divided by √(2 + 2√(d_u^2 + d_v^2)))^2. For a fixed order n, let T_n be the class of all trees with n vertices, and let CT_n be the class of all chemical trees with n vertices, where a chemical tree is a tree of maximum degree at most 4. What are the minimum and maximum possible values of SO5 and SO6 on T_n and on CT_n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with edge set $E(G)$, and for each vertex $u$ of $G$ let $d_u$ denote the degree of $u$. Define the graph invariants
$$\mathrm{SO}_5(G)=2\pi\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\frac{|d_u^2-d_v^2|}{\sqrt{2+2\sqrt{d_u^2+d_v^2}}},\qquad \mathrm{SO}_6(G)=\pi\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\left(\frac{d_u^2-d_v^2}{\sqrt{2+2\sqrt{d_u^2+d_v^2}}}\right)^{\!2}.$$
For a fixed integer $n\ge 2$, let $\mathcal{T}_n$ be the set of all trees on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathcal{CT}_n\subseteq\mathcal{T}_n$ be the set of all chemical trees on $n$ vertices, i.e., trees with maximum degree at most $4$. Determine the minimum and maximum values of $\mathrm{SO}_5$ and $\mathrm{SO}_6$ over $\mathcal{T}_n$ and over $\mathcal{CT}_n$, and characterize all extremal trees attaining these values.
status_search_result: The extremal problem for the Sombor-index-like invariants SO5 and SO6 over trees and chemical trees has been partially addressed: maximum values of SO5 and SO6 over molecular (chemical) trees of given order have been determined, and lower bounds on these invariants over chemical (n,m,k)-graphs have been obtained, but a complete determination of both minimum and maximum extremal values together with extremal-tree characterization over all of T_n and CT_n does not appear fully resolved in the literature.

paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
original_question: Let X1 and X2 be smooth projective varieties over a field, belonging to the same deformation class, and let Ku(X1) and Ku(X2) denote their Kuznetsov components, i.e. the geometrically meaningful residual admissible subcategories appearing after exceptional objects are removed from Db(X1) and Db(X2). Is X1 isomorphic to X2 if and only if Ku(X1) and Ku(X2) are equivalent as categories?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field. For a smooth projective variety $X$ over $k$, let $D^b(X)$ denote the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on $X$. For certain deformation classes of smooth projective varieties (for example, Enriques surfaces, prime Fano threefolds, cubic fourfolds, etc.), $D^b(X)$ admits a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(X),\, E_1, \dots, E_n \rangle,$$
where $E_1, \dots, E_n$ is an exceptional collection and $\mathcal{K}u(X)$, called the Kuznetsov component of $X$, is the residual admissible subcategory which carries the geometrically meaningful homological information.

Categorical Torelli problem: Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be smooth projective varieties over $k$ that belong to the same deformation class admitting a Kuznetsov component as above. Is it true that
$$X_1 \cong X_2 \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \mathcal{K}u(X_1) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(X_2)$$
as $k$-linear triangulated categories?
status_search_result: The categorical Torelli problem is a guiding conjecture that has been verified in several deformation classes (e.g. cubic threefolds without further assumptions, Enriques surfaces and cubic fourfolds under additional hypotheses on the equivalence, several prime Fano threefolds), but is known to fail in its naive form for Fano threefolds of index 1: there exist non-isomorphic birational Gushel–Mukai threefolds with equivalent Kuznetsov components. Hence the general statement is false as stated, while many refined or class-specific versions are open or solved case by case.

paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
original_question: Let D1 and D2 be admissible subcategories of Db(X1) and Db(X2), respectively, where X1 and X2 are smooth projective varieties over a field K. Is every exact fully faithful functor F: D1 -> D2 of Fourier-Mukai type?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field and let $X_1, X_2$ be smooth projective varieties over $K$. Denote by $D^b(X_i) = D^b(\operatorname{Coh}(X_i))$ the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on $X_i$. Recall that a full triangulated subcategory $\mathcal{D} \subset D^b(X)$ is called admissible if its inclusion functor admits both a left and a right adjoint. An exact functor $F: \mathcal{D}_1 \to \mathcal{D}_2$ between admissible subcategories $\mathcal{D}_i \subset D^b(X_i)$ is said to be of Fourier–Mukai type if there exists an object $E \in D^b(X_1 \times_K X_2)$ such that $F$ is isomorphic to the restriction to $\mathcal{D}_1$ of the functor $\Phi_E: D^b(X_1) \to D^b(X_2)$, $\Phi_E(-) = R(p_2)_*\bigl(E \otimes^{\mathbb{L}} L p_1^*(-)\bigr)$, composed with the projection onto $\mathcal{D}_2$.

Question: Is every exact, fully faithful $K$-linear functor $F: \mathcal{D}_1 \to \mathcal{D}_2$ between admissible subcategories of $D^b(X_1)$ and $D^b(X_2)$ of Fourier–Mukai type?
status_search_result: Orlov's theorem establishes Fourier–Mukai representability for fully faithful exact functors between the full bounded derived categories $D^b(X_1) \to D^b(X_2)$ of smooth projective varieties. The extension to fully faithful functors between admissible subcategories is not known in general and is highlighted as an open question in surveys on Fourier–Mukai functors (Canonaco–Stellari). Counterexamples of Rizzardo–Van den Bergh show that the fully faithful hypothesis cannot be dropped, but they do not address the admissible-subcategory case.

paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
original_question: For an Enriques surface X with a semiorthogonal decomposition whose residual admissible category is the Kuznetsov component Ku(X,L) determined by an exceptional collection L of line bundles, can the Serre functor of Ku(X,L) be described explicitly and computably, is Ku(X,L) indecomposable, and do the Fourier-Mukai representability questions for exact fully faithful functors or equivalences between admissible subcategories have positive answers for such Kuznetsov components?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $\mathcal{L}=(L_1,\dots,L_n)$ be an exceptional collection of line bundles on $X$ in the bounded derived category $D^b(X)$. Consider the semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X)=\langle \mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L}),\, L_1,\dots,L_nangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L})$ is defined as the right orthogonal to $\langle L_1,\dots,L_nangle$ and is an admissible triangulated subcategory. Address the following:

(a) Give an explicit, computable description of the Serre functor $S_{\mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L})}$ of $\mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L})$ (in particular, identify its action on objects up to a shift, and determine whether $\mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L})$ is a fractional Calabi–Yau or Enriques-type category).

(b) Determine whether $\mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L})$ is indecomposable as a triangulated category, i.e., admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition.

(c) Decide whether every exact fully faithful functor (respectively, every exact equivalence) between admissible subcategories of the form $\mathrm{Ku}(X,\mathcal{L})$ and $\mathrm{Ku}(X',\mathcal{L}')$ for Enriques surfaces $X,X'$ is of Fourier–Mukai type, i.e., is isomorphic to the restriction of an integral functor with kernel in $D^b(X	imes X')$.
status_search_result: Partial progress exists. Refined derived Torelli theorems for Enriques surfaces (Li–Nuer–Stellari and follow-ups) show that for general and then non-generic Enriques surfaces, equivalence of Kuznetsov components implies isomorphism, with Fourier–Mukai type equivalences playing a key role. Structural questions about the Serre functor and indecomposability of Ku(X,L) for general exceptional collections of line bundles, and full Fourier–Mukai representability of fully faithful functors between them, remain not fully resolved in general.

paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
original_question: For a cubic fourfold X, is X rational if and only if its Kuznetsov component Ku(X) is equivalent to the bounded derived category of a K3 surface?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^5_{\mathbb{C}}$ be a smooth cubic fourfold, i.e. a smooth hypersurface of degree $3$ in complex projective $5$-space. Consider its bounded derived category of coherent sheaves $D^b(X)$. By results of Kuznetsov, there is a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathrm{Ku}(X),\, \mathcal{O}_X,\, \mathcal{O}_X(1),\, \mathcal{O}_X(2)\rangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathrm{Ku}(X)$ is defined as the right orthogonal
$$\mathrm{Ku}(X) := \{ E \in D^b(X) \;:\; \mathrm{Hom}^\bullet(\mathcal{O}_X(i), E) = 0 \text{ for } i = 0,1,2 \}.$$
The subcategory $\mathrm{Ku}(X)$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-linear triangulated category whose Serre functor is the shift by $2$, so it is a "noncommutative K3 surface". Recall that $X$ is said to be rational if there exists a birational map $X \dashrightarrow \mathbb{P}^4$ over $\mathbb{C}$.

Prove or disprove: a smooth cubic fourfold $X$ is rational if and only if there exists a smooth projective K3 surface $S$ over $\mathbb{C}$ such that $\mathrm{Ku}(X)$ is $\mathbb{C}$-linearly triangulated-equivalent to $D^b(S)$.
status_search_result: The Kuznetsov rationality conjecture for cubic fourfolds remains a major open problem. While necessary and sufficient lattice-theoretic conditions for $\mathrm{Ku}(X) \simeq D^b(S)$ have been established (Addington–Thomas, and refined by Bayer–Lahoz–Macrì–Nuer–Perry–Stellari), and all known rational cubic fourfolds satisfy the conjecture, no proof of equivalence with rationality exists, and no smooth cubic fourfold has been proven irrational.

paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
original_question: For every smooth complex projective polarized variety (X,H), does there exist a modified Chern character determined by a class gamma and an upper semicontinuous real function f such that every gamma-tilt-semistable object E satisfies the Bayer-Macri quadratic inequality Qbar_{s,q}(E) >= 0 for all tilt parameters (s,q) above the graph q > f(s)? In dimension 3, such a statement would imply the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on Db(X).
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,H)$ be a smooth complex projective polarized variety of dimension $n$. For a class $\gamma\in\bigoplus_{i\ge 2}H^{2i}(X,\mathbb{Q})$, define the twisted Chern character
$$\mathrm{ch}^{\gamma}:=(1-\gamma)\cdot\mathrm{ch},$$
and, for real parameters $s,q$, the twisted slope and tilt functions giving rise to the heart $\mathrm{Coh}^{s}(X)$ (the tilt of $\mathrm{Coh}(X)$ at slope $s$ with respect to $H$) and the notion of $\gamma$-tilt-(semi)stability of two-term complexes $E\in\mathrm{Coh}^{s}(X)$. Recall the Bayer–Macrì quadratic form
$$\overline{Q}_{s,q}(E)=(H^{n-1}\mathrm{ch}^{\gamma}_{1}(E)-sH^{n}\mathrm{ch}^{\gamma}_{0}(E))^{2}-2H^{n}\mathrm{ch}^{\gamma}_{0}(E)\cdot(H^{n-2}\mathrm{ch}^{\gamma}_{2}(E)-qH^{n}\mathrm{ch}^{\gamma}_{0}(E))\cdot\text{(suitable normalization)},$$
viewed as a quadratic form in the truncated Chern character of $E$ depending on the parameters $(s,q)$ and on $\gamma$.

Question: Does there exist, for every such $(X,H)$, a class $\gamma$ and an upper semicontinuous function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ with the following property? Every $\gamma$-tilt-semistable object $E\in\mathrm{Coh}^{s}(X)$ satisfies
$$\overline{Q}_{s,q}(E)\ \ge\ 0$$
for all pairs $(s,q)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}$ with $q>f(s)$.

In particular, when $\dim X=3$, prove that such $\gamma$ and $f$ exist; deduce that the bounded derived category $D^{b}(X)$ admits Bridgeland stability conditions.
status_search_result: The original Bayer–Macrì–Toda generalized Bogomolov–Gieseker inequality (the case $\gamma=0$, $f\equiv 0$) is known to fail in general: Schmidt (2016) exhibited a counterexample on the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^3$ at a point. The modified form with a corrective class $\gamma$ and graph $f$ has been verified in several cases (abelian threefolds, Kummer threefolds, Calabi–Yau threefolds of abelian type, and all Fano threefolds via a strengthened Bogomolov-type inequality), yielding Bridgeland stability conditions on $D^{b}(X)$ in those settings. The general statement for arbitrary smooth projective threefolds (and higher dimensions) remains open.

paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
original_question: For which prime Fano threefolds of index 1 or index 2 does the Kuznetsov component admit Serre-invariant stability conditions?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth prime Fano threefold over $\mathbb{C}$, i.e., a smooth projective threefold of Picard rank $1$ with ample anticanonical class $-K_X = i_X H$, where $H$ is the ample generator of $\mathrm{Pic}(X)$ and $i_X \in \{1,2\}$ is the Fano index. Associated to $X$ is the Kuznetsov component $\mathcal{K}u(X) \subset D^b(X)$, defined as the right orthogonal complement of an exceptional collection: for $i_X = 2$, $\mathcal{K}u(X) = \langle \mathcal{O}_X, \mathcal{O}_X(H)\rangle^{\perp}$; for $i_X = 1$, $\mathcal{K}u(X) = \langle \mathcal{O}_X, \mathcal{U}_X^{\vee}\rangle^{\perp}$ when an appropriate tautological bundle $\mathcal{U}_X$ exists, and $\mathcal{K}u(X) = \langle \mathcal{O}_X\rangle^{\perp}$ in the remaining small-genus cases. Let $S_{\mathcal{K}u(X)}$ denote the Serre functor of $\mathcal{K}u(X)$. A Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma = (\mathcal{A}, Z)$ on $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is called Serre-invariant if $S_{\mathcal{K}u(X)} \cdot \sigma = \sigma \cdot \widetilde{g}$ for some $\widetilde{g} \in \widetilde{\mathrm{GL}}^+_2(\mathbb{R})$, i.e., $\sigma$ is preserved by the Serre functor up to the action of the universal cover of $\mathrm{GL}^+_2(\mathbb{R})$ on the stability manifold $\mathrm{Stab}(\mathcal{K}u(X))$.

Determine, for every deformation family of smooth prime Fano threefolds of index $1$ or index $2$ (parameterised by the index together with the degree/genus), whether $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ admits a Serre-invariant Bridgeland stability condition.
category_tag: Serre-invariant stability conditions on Kuznetsov components
status_search_result: Existence of Serre-invariant stability conditions on $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ has been established for all prime Fano threefolds of index $2$ (del Pezzo threefolds) and for index $1$ prime Fano threefolds of genus $\ge 6$ as well as for the small-genus cases studied by Bayer–Lahoz–Macrì–Stellari, Pertusi–Yang, and Feyzbakhsh–Pertusi. Recent work (e.g. arXiv:2310.16950 and follow-ups) describes the connected component of Serre-invariant stability conditions and uniqueness results. While the existence problem is essentially settled in many index $1$ and index $2$ cases, a complete uniform answer covering every prime Fano threefold deformation type is not yet fully formalised in the literature, so the question is best classified as partially solved.

paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
original_question: For an admissible subcategory D of Db(X) that admits Serre-invariant stability conditions, is the stability manifold of D connected?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over $\mathbb{C}$ with bounded derived category of coherent sheaves $D^b(X)$. Recall that a full triangulated subcategory $\mathcal{D} \subset D^b(X)$ is called admissible if its inclusion functor admits both left and right adjoints; in this case $\mathcal{D}$ has a Serre functor $S_{\mathcal{D}}$. A Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma = (\mathcal{A}, Z)$ on $\mathcal{D}$ (consisting of the heart of a bounded t-structure $\mathcal{A}$ and a central charge $Z$ satisfying the usual Bridgeland axioms, including the support property) is called Serre-invariant if $S_{\mathcal{D}} \cdot \sigma = \sigma \cdot \widetilde{g}$ for some $\widetilde{g}$ in the universal cover of $\mathrm{GL}^+_2(\mathbb{R})$ acting on the space $\mathrm{Stab}(\mathcal{D})$ of stability conditions.

Assume that $\mathcal{D}$ admits at least one Serre-invariant Bridgeland stability condition. Is the stability manifold $\mathrm{Stab}(\mathcal{D})$ connected?
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., on Kuznetsov components of prime Fano threefolds, cubic threefolds, Gushel–Mukai threefolds, cubic fivefolds) has identified connected components of stability manifolds containing Serre-invariant stability conditions and proved uniqueness results up to the action of the universal cover of GL⁺₂(ℝ). However, no general proof that the full stability manifold of an admissible subcategory admitting Serre-invariant stability conditions is connected appears in the literature; the question remains open in general.

paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
original_question: Let Y1 be the Veronese double cone, the degree-6 hypersurface in P(1,1,1,2,3). Does a categorical Torelli theorem hold for Y1, meaning that the relevant categorical data of its Kuznetsov component reconstructs Y1 in the expected Torelli sense?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Y_1 \subset \mathbb{P}(1,1,1,2,3)$ be a smooth Veronese double cone, i.e. a smooth hypersurface of degree $6$ in the weighted projective space $\mathbb{P}(1,1,1,2,3)$. The bounded derived category $D^b(\mathrm{Coh}\, Y_1)$ admits a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$ D^b(\mathrm{Coh}\, Y_1) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(Y_1),\, \mathcal{O}_{Y_1},\, \mathcal{O}_{Y_1}(1) \rangle, $$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathcal{K}u(Y_1)$ is defined as the right orthogonal to the exceptional pair $(\mathcal{O}_{Y_1}, \mathcal{O}_{Y_1}(1))$.

Prove or disprove the following categorical Torelli statement: if $Y_1$ and $Y_1'$ are two smooth Veronese double cones and there exists a Fourier–Mukai equivalence $\mathcal{K}u(Y_1) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(Y_1')$, then $Y_1 \cong Y_1'$ as projective varieties.
status_search_result: A 2024 preprint by Bayer, Beckmann, Rota and collaborators (arXiv:2408.08266, "IVHS via Kuznetsov components and categorical Torelli theorems for weighted hypersurfaces") establishes a categorical Torelli theorem for the Veronese double cone by reconstructing the Jacobian ring from its even-degree graded subalgebra via the Hochschild–Serre algebra of the Kuznetsov component. Earlier work (Petkovic–Rota, arXiv:2007.05555) studied the Kuznetsov component of Y_1 but did not prove the full Torelli statement.

paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
original_question: If X is a quartic threefold, are the stability conditions sigma(s,q,mu) constructed on its Kuznetsov component Serre-invariant for at least one choice of the parameters (s,q)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^4$ be a smooth quartic hypersurface (a quartic threefold). Its bounded derived category of coherent sheaves admits a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(X),\, \mathcal{O}_X,\, \mathcal{O}_X(1),\, \mathcal{O}_X(2),\, \mathcal{O}_X(3) \rangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is defined as the right orthogonal $\langle \mathcal{O}_X, \mathcal{O}_X(1), \mathcal{O}_X(2), \mathcal{O}_X(3) \rangle^{\perp}$. The Serre functor $S_{\mathcal{K}u(X)}$ of $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is an autoequivalence of this triangulated category.

Following the standard tilting construction, for real parameters $s \in \mathbb{R}$ and $q \in \mathbb{R}$ in an appropriate region, one considers a weak Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma(s,q)$ on $D^b(X)$ built from a double-tilt of the heart of coherent sheaves with respect to slope stability, together with a central charge depending on $(s,q)$. Choosing a further real parameter $\mu$, one then induces by tilting and restriction a Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma(s,q,\mu)$ on $\mathcal{K}u(X)$.

A Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma$ on $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is said to be Serre-invariant if there exists $\tilde{g} \in \widetilde{\mathrm{GL}}_2^{+}(\mathbb{R})$ such that $S_{\mathcal{K}u(X)} \cdot \sigma = \sigma \cdot \tilde{g}$.

Question: Does there exist at least one choice of admissible parameters $(s,q)$ (and a corresponding $\mu$) such that the induced stability condition $\sigma(s,q,\mu)$ on the Kuznetsov component $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ of a smooth quartic threefold $X$ is Serre-invariant?
status_search_result: Recent literature establishes Serre-invariance of the constructed stability conditions on Kuznetsov components for cubic threefolds, quartic double solids, and Gushel–Mukai threefolds, and characterizes Serre-invariance via bounded homological dimension. However, the case of the (index-one) quartic threefold in $\mathbb{P}^4$ — whose Kuznetsov component is a Calabi–Yau category of higher dimension — does not appear to be settled in the search results found, and no source explicitly resolves Serre-invariance of $\sigma(s,q,\mu)$ for some $(s,q)$ in this case.

paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
original_question: For quartic threefolds, does the birational categorical Torelli theorem hold, i.e. does equivalence of the relevant Kuznetsov components imply birationality of the threefolds?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^4$ be a smooth quartic threefold over $\mathbb{C}$. Its bounded derived category of coherent sheaves $D^b(X)$ admits a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(X), \mathcal{O}_X, \mathcal{O}_X(1), \mathcal{O}_X(2), \mathcal{O}_X(3) \rangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is the right orthogonal to $\langle \mathcal{O}_X, \mathcal{O}_X(1), \mathcal{O}_X(2), \mathcal{O}_X(3) \rangle$. The component $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is a 2-Calabi–Yau category and serves as a categorical analogue of the period of $X$.

Prove or disprove: for any two smooth quartic threefolds $X$ and $X'$, if there exists a $\mathbb{C}$-linear exact equivalence $\mathcal{K}u(X) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(X')$, then $X$ and $X'$ are birational.

status_search_result: Search results indicate the birational categorical Torelli problem for smooth quartic threefolds remains open. Related results have been established for nearby cases (quartic double solids, Gushel–Mukai threefolds, del Pezzo threefolds of degree 4), and Kuznetsov's Fano threefold conjecture has been resolved, but no source found confirms the birational categorical Torelli statement for smooth quartic threefolds in $\mathbb{P}^4$.

paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
context_brief: Hodge-theoretic classification of cubic fourfold Kuznetsov components
original_question: Over the complex numbers, for Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds, is equivalence of two such components characterized by the existence of an orientation-preserving Hodge isometry between their Mukai lattices, analogously to the derived Torelli theorem for K3 surfaces?
self_contained_problem:
Work over the field of complex numbers. For a smooth cubic fourfold $X \subset \mathbb{P}^5$, the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves admits Kuznetsov's semi-orthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(X), \mathcal{O}_X, \mathcal{O}_X(1), \mathcal{O}_X(2) \rangle,$$
where the admissible subcategory $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is called the Kuznetsov component of $X$. The component $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is a 2-Calabi–Yau category whose topological K-theory carries a weight-zero Hodge structure and an even integral lattice (the Mukai lattice) $\widetilde{H}(\mathcal{K}u(X), \mathbb{Z})$, abstractly isometric to $U^{\oplus 4} \oplus E_8(-1)^{\oplus 2}$, equipped with a distinguished positive 4-space (giving an orientation of the positive directions).

Any $\mathbb{C}$-linear exact equivalence $\Phi : \mathcal{K}u(X) \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{K}u(Y)$ between Kuznetsov components of two smooth cubic fourfolds $X$ and $Y$ induces a Hodge isometry
$$\Phi^{\widetilde{H}} : \widetilde{H}(\mathcal{K}u(X), \mathbb{Z}) \xrightarrow{\sim} \widetilde{H}(\mathcal{K}u(Y), \mathbb{Z})$$
which preserves the orientation of the positive 4-spaces.

Question: Is the converse true? That is, given two smooth complex cubic fourfolds $X$ and $Y$, does the existence of an orientation-preserving Hodge isometry
$$\widetilde{H}(\mathcal{K}u(X), \mathbb{Z}) \xrightarrow{\sim} \widetilde{H}(\mathcal{K}u(Y), \mathbb{Z})$$
imply the existence of an exact $\mathbb{C}$-linear equivalence $\mathcal{K}u(X) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(Y)$, in direct analogy with the derived Torelli theorem of Mukai–Orlov (and its twisted/oriented refinement) for K3 surfaces?
status_search_result: A derived-Torelli statement for Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds — characterizing equivalence of Kuznetsov components by the existence of an orientation-preserving Hodge isometry of Mukai lattices, in analogy with Mukai–Orlov for K3 surfaces — is treated as an open conjecture in the literature. Partial results exist (e.g., for special cubic fourfolds whose Kuznetsov component is equivalent to D^b of a (twisted) K3 surface, where Mukai–Orlov-type theorems apply, and various categorical Torelli theorems), but the general statement has not been established.

paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
original_question: Let X1 and X2 be Gushel-Mukai fourfolds and suppose there is an equivalence Phi: Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2) between their Kuznetsov components that commutes with the degree-shift functors. Under which additional assumptions on Phi does it follow that X1 and X2 are isomorphic?
self_contained_problem:
A Gushel–Mukai (GM) fourfold is a smooth complex projective fourfold X obtained as the intersection of the Grassmannian Gr(2,5) (in its Plücker embedding) with a linear subspace and a quadric hypersurface, or as a double cover of a linear section of Gr(2,5) branched along a quadric, with X of dimension 4. The bounded derived category D^b(X) admits a semiorthogonal decomposition

  D^b(X) = ⟨ Ku(X), O_X, U_X^∨, O_X(1), U_X^∨(1) ⟩,

where U_X is the restriction of the tautological rank-2 subbundle on Gr(2,5). The full triangulated subcategory Ku(X), called the Kuznetsov component of X, is a 2-Calabi–Yau category and carries a distinguished autoequivalence, the degree-shift (or rotation) functor σ: Ku(X) → Ku(X) defined by σ(E) := L_{O_X} L_{U_X^∨}(E ⊗ O_X(1)), where L denotes the left mutation functor through the indicated object.

Problem. Let X_1 and X_2 be two Gushel–Mukai fourfolds and let Φ: Ku(X_1) → Ku(X_2) be a C-linear exact equivalence of triangulated categories such that Φ ∘ σ_{X_1} ≅ σ_{X_2} ∘ Φ. Determine natural additional conditions on Φ (for example, compatibility with the Serre functor, preservation of distinguished classes in the numerical Grothendieck group such as those of Kuznetsov–Perry's projection objects, exactness up to shift on a specific heart of a Bridgeland stability condition, or being of Fourier–Mukai type) under which the existence of such an equivalence Φ forces X_1 and X_2 to be isomorphic as complex projective varieties.
status_search_result: The question of formulating sufficient conditions on a degree-shift–commuting Kuznetsov-component equivalence Φ that imply isomorphism of Gushel–Mukai fourfolds is posed as an open problem in recent surveys, and remains open as of recent work (2024). Related categorical Torelli theorems have been established for GM threefolds and cubic fourfolds, but the analogous refined statement for GM fourfolds has not been resolved; moreover, period-partners and duality phenomena make the situation subtler than for cubic fourfolds.

original_question: Let X1 and X2 be Gushel-Mukai varieties of the same dimension. If there is an equivalence Ku(X1) ~= Ku(X2) between their Kuznetsov components, must X1 and X2 be birational?

The bounded derived category D^b(X) admits a semiorthogonal decomposition whose nontrivial "Kuznetsov component" Ku(X) is defined as the right orthogonal to an exceptional collection coming from O_X and (when n is even) U_X^∨, where U_X is the restriction of the tautological rank-2 subbundle on Gr(2,5); more precisely, Ku(X) is the full triangulated subcategory of D^b(X) of objects right-orthogonal to this exceptional collection, and it is a 2-Calabi–Yau category for n even and a fractional Calabi–Yau category for n odd.

status_search_result: The conjecture has been established in significant cases but not in full generality. The general statement across all dimensions and all GM varieties does not appear fully established in the literature.

paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
context_brief: Main infimum problem on odd spheres
original_question: For each integer m > 1 and each r > 0, determine the number V(m,r) defined as the infimum of Vol(V) over all smooth vector fields V of constant length r on the odd-dimensional sphere S^{2m+1}, where Vol(V) is the volume of the submanifold V(S^{2m+1}) in the tangent bundle with the Sasaki metric. If the infimum is attained, characterize all smooth length-r vector fields that attain it.
self_contained_problem:
Let m > 1 be an integer and let r > 0 be a real number. Consider the unit sphere
S^{2m+1} = { x ∈ R^{2m+2} : |x| = 1 }
equipped with its round Riemannian metric induced from R^{2m+2}. Vol(V) = ∫_{S^{2m+1}} √det(I + (∇V)^T ∇V) dvol,

paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
context_brief: Threshold comparing Hopf and parallel-transport bounds
original_question: For each m > 1, define r1(m) as a threshold such that for r > r1(m) the Hopf vector fields of length r on S^{2m+1} have less volume than the parallel-transport vector fields used to produce the alternative upper bound c*(m,r) vol(S^{2m+1}). Determine explicit values or a formula for r1(m), and clarify its relation to the instability threshold r0(m) = sqrt(2m - 3).
self_contained_problem:
Let $m>1$ be an integer and consider the odd-dimensional unit sphere $S^{2m+1}\subset \mathbb{R}^{2m+2}$ endowed with its round metric. A smooth vector field $V$ of constant length $r>0$ on $S^{2m+1}$ may be viewed as a section of the tangent bundle, and its volume is defined as the $(2m+1)$-dimensional volume of its image in $TS^{2m+1}$ equipped with the Sasaki metric:
$$\operatorname{vol}(V)=\int_{S^{2m+1}}\sqrt{\det\bigl(I+(\nabla V)^{T}(\nabla V)\bigr)}\,d\mathrm{vol}.$$
For $r>0$ let $H_r$ denote a Hopf vector field of constant length $r$ on $S^{2m+1}$ (the unit Hopf field rescaled by $r$), and let $\operatorname{vol}(H_r)$ be its volume. There is an alternative upper bound for the infimum of $\operatorname{vol}(V)$ among constant-length-$r$ vector fields on $S^{2m+1}$ of the form
$$c^{*}(m,r)\,\operatorname{vol}(S^{2m+1}),$$
constructed via the family of parallel-transport vector fields (the vector field obtained, off a singular set, by parallel-transporting a fixed unit tangent vector along great circles, and then rescaling by $r$).

Define
$$r_1(m)=\inf\bigl\{\,r_0>0 : \operatorname{vol}(H_r)<c^{*}(m,r)\,\operatorname{vol}(S^{2m+1}) \text{ for all } r>r_0\bigr\}.$$
That is, $r_1(m)$ is the threshold above which the Hopf vector fields of length $r$ have strictly smaller volume than the parallel-transport upper bound. It is known that the Hopf vector field $H_r$ becomes unstable (as a critical point of the volume functional on constant-length sections) when $r>r_0(m):=\sqrt{2m-3}$.

Determine an explicit value or closed-form formula for $r_1(m)$ as a function of $m$, and determine its precise relation to $r_0(m)=\sqrt{2m-3}$ (in particular whether $r_1(m)\le r_0(m)$, $r_1(m)=r_0(m)$, or $r_1(m)>r_0(m)$).
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicitly open question in the survey on volumes of vector fields on Riemannian manifolds, where it is stated that the explicit values of r_1(m) are not known and its relationship with the instability threshold r_0(m)=sqrt(2m-3) remains to be clarified. No subsequent resolution was found.

context_brief: Hopf minimizers on positive-curvature space forms
original_question: Let M be a complete (2m+1)-dimensional Riemannian manifold of constant positive curvature that is not the sphere, and consider smooth vector fields on M of fixed constant length r > 0. Is the infimum of the volume functional over such vector fields attained exactly by Hopf vector fields?

Let $m \geq 1$ be an integer and let $M$ be a complete $(2m+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold of constant positive sectional curvature that is not isometric to the round sphere (so $M$ is a non-trivial quotient $S^{2m+1}(\rho)/\Gamma$ with $\Gamma \neq \{\mathrm{Id}\}$). For a smooth vector field $V$ on $M$, regard $V$ as a section of the tangent bundle and equip $TM$ with the Sasaki metric; the volume of $V$ is then defined as
$$\mathrm{Vol}(V) \;=\; \int_M \sqrt{\det\!\bigl(I + (\nabla V)^t (\nabla V)\bigr)} \, dv_M,$$
or equivalently as the volume of the submanifold $V(M) \subset TM$. Fix a constant $r>0$ and consider the class $\mathcal{V}_r(M)$ of smooth vector fields $V$ on $M$ with $\|V\|\equiv r$ everywhere. A Hopf vector field on $M$ is a unit-length (or, after rescaling, length-$r$) vector field tangent to the fibers of the Hopf fibration on $S^{2m+1}$, descended to the quotient $M$.

Question: Is it true that the infimum
$$\inf_{V \in \mathcal{V}_r(M)} \mathrm{Vol}(V)$$
is attained, and that the minimizers are exactly the Hopf vector fields of constant length $r$ on $M$?

original_question: Let a finite subgroup G of U(m+1) act freely by isometries on the Berger sphere (S^{2m+1}, g_mu), and let H_mu^G be the induced unit Hopf vector field on the quotient S^{2m+1}/G. The vector field H_μ := (1/μ) V is then a unit vector field on (S^{2m+1}, g_μ).

defined on the space of smooth unit vector fields X on (M_μ^G, g_μ); the unit Hopf vector field H_μ^G is a critical point of F.

paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
context_brief: Removing topology assumptions for S2 area minimizers
original_question: On the two-sphere S^2, consider vector fields V of constant length r != 1 that are defined without boundary, and let Sigma_V be the associated surface in the sphere tangent bundle. The known area-minimization theorem assumes that Sigma_V is homeomorphic to a projective plane. Can this projective-plane topology assumption be removed while still concluding that the parallel-transport vector fields are the only area minimizers?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^2$ denote the round unit 2-sphere and, for $r>0$ with $r\neq 1$, let $T^1 S^2(r)$ denote the bundle of tangent vectors to $S^2$ of constant length $r$, equipped with the Sasaki metric. Since $S^2$ admits no nowhere-vanishing continuous tangent vector field, by a "vector field of constant length $r$ without boundary" we mean a smooth map $V:U\to T S^2$ defined on a dense open set $U\subset S^2$ with $|V(p)|=r$ for all $p\in U$, such that the closure $\Sigma_V\subset T^1 S^2(r)$ of the image of $V$ is a surface without boundary. The area of $V$ is defined as the area of $\Sigma_V$ in $T^1 S^2(r)$.

A Pontryagin (parallel-transport) vector field is obtained by fixing a point $p_0\in S^2$ and a vector $v_0$ of length $r$ at $p_0$, and parallel-translating $v_0$ along every great circle through $p_0$; this yields a vector field defined on $S^2\setminus\{-p_0\}$ whose associated closed surface in $T^1 S^2(r)$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^2$.

It is known that if $V$ is a vector field of constant length $r\neq 1$ without boundary and $\Sigma_V$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^2$, then $V$ minimizes area among all such vector fields if and only if $V$ is a Pontryagin field.

Question: Does the same conclusion hold without the topological assumption that $\Sigma_V$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^2$? Equivalently, prove or disprove: every area-minimizing vector field of constant length $r\neq 1$ on $S^2$ (in the above sense) is a Pontryagin parallel-transport vector field.
status_search_result: The known characterization of area minimizers among constant-length vector fields on the round 2-sphere (Borrelli–Gil-Medrano and related works) is stated under the additional hypothesis that the associated surface in the unit tangent bundle is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^2$. Recent works (e.g., on Klein-bottle minimal surfaces in $T^1 S^2$ arising from area-minimizing unit fields on punctured spheres, and on vector field cycles in the tangent bundle) continue to assume or discuss this topological restriction, and no result removing the projective-plane assumption appears to have been established. The problem appears to remain open.
