original_question: Let Q(X, ξ) be an invariant preserving G × G kernel associated with a pair (X, ξ), and recall that Theorem 4.4 characterizes mass-stationarity by requiring equation (4.2) to hold for all bounded invariant preserving kernels Q(X, ξ). Does the same characterization remain valid if one restricts attention to kernels Q(X, ξ) that are Markovian, meaning that each Q(X, ξ)(s, ·) has total mass one?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a locally compact second countable topological group with Haar measure $\lambda$, and let $(X,\xi)$ be a pair consisting of a random element $X$ and a random measure $\xi$ on $G$ defined on a probability space. A kernel $Q(X,\xi)(s,\cdot)$ from $G$ to $G$ (depending measurably on $(X,\xi)$) is called an invariant preserving $G\times G$ kernel for $(X,\xi)$ if it is bounded and satisfies the appropriate $G$-invariance and $\xi$-preserving properties (so that integrating $Q$ against $\xi$ produces an invariant balance with respect to the group action).

Recall the following characterization of mass-stationarity: the pair $(X,\xi)$ is mass-stationary if and only if the identity
$$\mathbb{E}\!\int\!\!\int f(\theta_s X,\theta_s \xi,-s)\,Q(X,\xi)(0,ds)\,\xi(d\cdot) \;=\; \mathbb{E}\!\int\!\!\int f(X,\xi,s)\,Q(X,\xi)(\cdot,ds)\,\xi(d\cdot) \qquad (\ast)$$
holds for every bounded measurable function $f$ and every bounded invariant preserving $G\times G$ kernel $Q(X,\xi)$.

A kernel $Q(X,\xi)$ is called Markovian if $Q(X,\xi)(s,G)=1$ for every $s\in G$ (almost surely).

Question: Does the above characterization of mass-stationarity remain valid if the class of test kernels in $(\ast)$ is restricted to those invariant preserving $G\times G$ kernels $Q(X,\xi)$ that are Markovian?

The characterization via general bounded invariant preserving kernels appears in works of Last and Thorisson on Palm pairs and mass-stationarity, but I found no later paper announcing a positive or negative answer to the Markovian-restriction version. Status appears unresolved.

paper_title: Open Problems in Stringology
original_question: Let Σ be a finite alphabet, let $ be a separator symbol not in Σ, and let string matching mean: given a pattern x and a text y, find all positions where x occurs in y. Does there exist a one-way deterministic finite automaton with finitely many read heads that can perform string matching, equivalently recognize the language {x$uxv | u, x, v ∈ Σ*}, where the substring x that appears before $ occurs again later in the suffix uxv?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\$$ be a separator symbol with $\$\notin\Sigma$. A one-way $k$-head deterministic finite automaton (one-way $k$-head DFA) is a deterministic finite automaton equipped with finitely many ($k$) read-only input heads, each of which can independently move only from left to right over a single input tape (no head may move backward); the automaton accepts or rejects after all heads have reached the right endmarker. Define the string-matching language
$$L = \{\, x\,\$\,u\,x\,v \;:\; x,u,v \in \Sigma^* \,\},$$
i.e., the set of words over $\Sigma\cup\{\$\}$ containing exactly one occurrence of $\$$ such that the prefix $x$ before $\$$ occurs as a (contiguous) factor of the suffix after $\$$.

Question: Does there exist a positive integer $k$ and a one-way $k$-head deterministic finite automaton that recognizes $L$ (equivalently, that performs string matching, identifying all occurrences of a pattern $x$ in a text $uxv$)?
status_search_result: The conjecture of Galil and Seiferas that no one-way k-head DFA can perform string matching was settled in the negative (i.e., string matching cannot be done by any one-way k-head DFA) by T. Jiang and M. Li, "k One-Way Heads Cannot Do String-Matching," J. Comput. System Sci. 1996, building on earlier partial results (Li–Yesha 1986 for k=2; a later paper proving the k=3 case).

paper_title: Open Problems in Stringology
original_question: In parallel exact string matching, let p denote the number of processors, t the running time, and n the input length, so that an algorithm is called optimal when pt = O(n). A WRAM is a shared-memory collection of RAMs that allows simultaneous reads and writes with a conflict-resolution mechanism, while a PRAM allows simultaneous reads but not simultaneous writes. Is it possible to design optimal parallel string-matching algorithms for larger processor counts than were then known, for example up to p ≤ n on the WRAM or p ≤ n / log n on the PRAM?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the exact string-matching problem: given a text of length n and a pattern over some alphabet, find all occurrences of the pattern in the text.

A WRAM (concurrent-read concurrent-write parallel random-access machine) is a collection of RAM processors sharing a common memory in which simultaneous reads and simultaneous writes to the same location are permitted, together with a conflict-resolution rule for concurrent writes. A PRAM (concurrent-read exclusive-write parallel random-access machine) is the same model but only simultaneous reads are allowed; concurrent writes are forbidden.

For a parallel algorithm using p processors and running in time t on inputs of length n, call the algorithm optimal if p·t = O(n).

Question: Does there exist an optimal parallel exact string-matching algorithm
(a) on the WRAM that uses up to p ≤ n processors, and
(b) on the PRAM that uses up to p ≤ n / log n processors?

Equivalently, can one design optimal parallel string-matching algorithms running in time t = O(1) on the WRAM and t = O(log n) on the PRAM?
status_search_result: Subsequent work resolved the question. Breslauer and Galil gave an optimal O(log log n)-time CRCW-PRAM (WRAM) algorithm using n/log log n processors, and later constant-time optimal parallel string-matching algorithms on the CRCW-PRAM were obtained (Galil, 1995), achieving pt = O(n) with p = n on the WRAM. The matching Ω(log log n) lower bound was also established. On the EREW PRAM, optimal algorithms running in O(log n) time with n/log n processors are known. Thus the targets stated in the question have been achieved.

paper_title: Open Problems in the Dynamics of the Expression of Gene Interaction Networks
original_question: Assume the gene-interaction rule A is an m × m adjacency matrix of a gene-gene interaction graph for m genes, with entries A_ij in {0,1}, where A_ij indicates whether gene j influences gene i, and the dynamics evolve by x_{n+1} = A x_n toward an attractor x_f = lim_{n→∞} A^n(x_0). Given experimental information consisting of properties of x_f, and possibly additional observations of intermediate states x_n under the cases described in the chapter, which local, global, group-theoretic, statistical, or other mathematically meaningful properties of the unknown adjacency matrix A can be determined, even though the individual entries, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors of A cannot in general be fully recovered?
self_contained_problem:
Let $m$ be a positive integer and let $A \in \{0,1\}^{m \times m}$ be an unknown adjacency matrix of a directed graph on $m$ vertices, where $A_{ij}=1$ indicates that vertex $j$ influences vertex $i$. For an initial state $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}^m$, define the discrete-time linear dynamics $x_{n+1} = A x_n$ for $n \ge 0$, and assume the attractor $x_f := \lim_{n \to \infty} A^n x_0$ exists in $\mathbb{R}^m$.

It is known that in general one cannot recover the individual entries $A_{ij}$, nor all eigenvalues or eigenvectors of $A$, from $x_f$ alone (or from $x_f$ together with partial observations of intermediate states $x_n$).

Problem: Identify and characterize as large as possible a family of mathematically meaningful invariants of $A$—local invariants (e.g. degrees, neighborhood structure of specific vertices), global invariants (e.g. connectivity, number of strongly connected components, spectral radius, rank), group-theoretic invariants (e.g. automorphism group or symmetry properties of the underlying graph), statistical invariants (e.g. degree distributions, density), or other structural invariants—that are uniquely determined by the knowledge of $x_f$ (and, where specified, of intermediate states $x_n$ for certain finite sets of indices $n$ and certain admissible initial conditions $x_0$). For each such invariant, give an explicit reconstruction procedure, and prove the corresponding identifiability results.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicitly open problem in a discussion of gene interaction network dynamics. No publication identified that resolves the general identifiability question for adjacency matrices from linear attractor data in the form stated. Status appears to remain open, and the problem is somewhat informal in nature.

original_question: Assume the gene-interaction rule A is context-dependent, so that the effect of one molecule or gene on another is influenced by the presence of additional molecules, and therefore A is a nonlinear function of the expression levels of two or more genes x_j, with j = 1, 2, ..., q and q ≥ 2. paper_title: Open problems in the theory of fuzzy metric spaces
context_brief: Separability of the fuzzy Gromov-Prokhorov space of compact fuzzy mm-spaces.
original_question: A compact fuzzy metric-measure space is a quadruple (X, M, *, μ) in which (X, M, *) is a compact fuzzy metric space and μ is a probability measure on X. If one equips the class of all compact fuzzy metric-measure spaces with the fuzzy Gromov-Prokhorov distance M_GP defined via isometric embeddings into a common fuzzy metric space, is the resulting fuzzy metric space separable?
self_contained_problem:
Recall that a continuous t-norm is a binary operation $*\colon [0,1]	imes[0,1]	o[0,1]$ that is commutative, associative, continuous, has $1$ as identity, and is non-decreasing in each argument. A fuzzy metric space (in the sense of George and Veeramani) is a triple $(X,M,*)$ where $X$ is a non-empty set, $*$ is a continuous t-norm, and $M\colon X	imes X	imes(0,\infty)	o[0,1]$ satisfies, for all $x,y,z\in X$ and $t,s>0$:
(i) $M(x,y,t)>0$;
(ii) $M(x,y,t)=1$ if and only if $x=y$;
(iii) $M(x,y,t)=M(y,x,t)$;
(iv) $M(x,y,t)*M(y,z,s)\le M(x,z,t+s)$;
(v) the function $t\mapsto M(x,y,t)$ is continuous on $(0,\infty)$.
The family of open balls $B(x,r,t)=\{y\in X : M(x,y,t)>1-r\}$ generates a topology on $X$, and $(X,M,*)$ is called compact if this topology is compact.

A compact fuzzy metric-measure space is a quadruple $(X,M,*,\mu)$ where $(X,M,*)$ is a compact fuzzy metric space and $\mu$ is a Borel probability measure on $X$. Two such quadruples $(X_1,M_1,*,\mu_1)$ and $(X_2,M_2,*,\mu_2)$ (using the same t-norm $*$) are considered equivalent if there is a measure-preserving isometric bijection between the supports of $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$.

For a fuzzy metric space $(Z,N,*)$ and Borel probability measures $
u_1,
u_2$ on $Z$, the fuzzy Prokhorov value at level $t>0$ is
$$P_N(
u_1,
u_2,t)=\sup\{1-\varepsilon : 
u_1(A)\le 
u_2(B(A,\varepsilon,t))+\varepsilon 	ext{ and } 
u_2(A)\le 
u_1(B(A,\varepsilon,t))+\varepsilon\  orall 	ext{ Borel } A\subseteq Z\},$$
where $B(A,\varepsilon,t)=\{z\in Z: \exists a\in A,\ M(z,a,t)>1-\varepsilon\}$.

For two compact fuzzy metric-measure spaces $(X_i,M_i,*,\mu_i)$, $i=1,2$, define the fuzzy Gromov-Prokhorov value
$$M_{GP}((X_1,M_1,*,\mu_1),(X_2,M_2,*,\mu_2),t)=\sup\{P_N(f_{1*}\mu_1,f_{2*}\mu_2,t)\},$$
where the supremum is taken over all fuzzy metric spaces $(Z,N,*)$ and all isometric embeddings $f_i\colon X_i\hookrightarrow Z$ ($i=1,2$).

Let $\mathcal{K}^{	ext{mm}}_*$ denote the class of equivalence classes of compact fuzzy metric-measure spaces with fixed t-norm $*$, equipped with the fuzzy metric $M_{GP}$.

Question: Is the fuzzy metric space $(\mathcal{K}^{	ext{mm}}_*, M_{GP}, *)$ separable?

paper_title: Open problems in the theory of fuzzy metric spaces
context_brief: Fuzzy analogues of Kantorovich and Gromov λ metrics.
original_question: In the setting of compact fuzzy metric-measure spaces and probability measures on fuzzy metric spaces, can one define fuzzy counterparts of the Kantorovich metric and of Gromov's λ-metric, analogous to the metrics used in the theory of metric-measure spaces?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(a) A fuzzy metric space, in the sense of George and Veeramani, is a triple (X, M, *) where X is a non-empty set, * is a continuous t-norm on [0,1], and M: X × X × (0, ∞) → [0,1] is a function satisfying, for all x, y, z ∈ X and t, s > 0:
  (i) M(x, y, t) > 0;
  (ii) M(x, y, t) = 1 if and only if x = y;
  (iii) M(x, y, t) = M(y, x, t);
  (iv) M(x, y, t) * M(y, z, s) ≤ M(x, z, t + s);
  (v) t ↦ M(x, y, t) is continuous from (0, ∞) to [0,1].
The space (X, M, *) is compact if the topology induced by M on X is compact.

(b) A fuzzy metric-measure space is a quadruple (X, M, *, μ) where (X, M, *) is a compact fuzzy metric space and μ is a Borel probability measure on X.

(c) Recall the classical analogues that should be mimicked:
  • Kantorovich (Wasserstein) metric. For a compact metric space (X, d) and probability measures μ, ν on X, dK(μ, ν) = inf_{π} ∫_{X×X} d(x, y) dπ(x, y), where the infimum is taken over all couplings π of μ and ν.
  • Gromov's λ-metric (or □λ-metric). Given a probability space (X, B, μ) and bounded measurable functions r, s: X × X → R, one defines □λ(r, s) as the infimum over measurable subsets A ⊂ X with μ(A) ≥ 1 − λ of sup_{x,y ∈ A} |r(x, y) − s(x, y)|; this extends to a metric on isomorphism classes of metric-measure spaces by taking the infimum over couplings of the two measures.

Problem. Construct fuzzy counterparts of the Kantorovich metric and of Gromov's λ-metric in the setting of compact fuzzy metric-measure spaces, namely:

1. Define, for a fixed compact fuzzy metric space (X, M, *), a fuzzy metric M_K on the set P(X) of Borel probability measures on X that plays the role of the Kantorovich metric, in the sense that for each t > 0 the value M_K(μ, ν, t) ∈ [0,1] reflects the optimal-transport cost between μ and ν computed against the fuzzy distance M, and verify that (P(X), M_K, *) is itself a fuzzy metric space.

2. Define a fuzzy analogue M_λ of Gromov's λ-metric on the collection of isomorphism classes of compact fuzzy metric-measure spaces (X, M, *, μ), establish that it satisfies the fuzzy metric axioms (up to isomorphism), and relate the induced topology to natural notions of convergence of fuzzy metric-measure spaces.

In both cases, the constructions should reduce, in the special case where the fuzzy metric M arises from an ordinary metric d (e.g. via M(x, y, t) = t/(t + d(x, y))), to the classical Kantorovich metric and to Gromov's λ-metric on metric-measure spaces, respectively.
status_search_result: A search reveals related developments — Gromov–Hausdorff fuzzy metrics on compact (non-Archimedean) fuzzy metric spaces and fuzzy analogues of Kantorovich-type distances in possibility-theoretic settings — but no construction is found that gives both a fuzzy Kantorovich metric on probability measures and a fuzzy Gromov λ-metric on fuzzy metric-measure spaces with the required compatibility. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
context_brief: Unbounded norms on subspaces and quotients
original_question: Let X be an F-space. Does X always contain an infinite-dimensional subspace that admits an equivalent unbounded F-norm, where an F-norm ||x||' is called unbounded when sup_{x in X} ||x||' = +∞? Also, does there exist a subspace M of X such that the quotient space X/M admits an unbounded F-norm?
self_contained_problem:
An F-norm on a real or complex vector space X is a function ||·||: X → [0, ∞) such that: (i) ||x|| = 0 iff x = 0; (ii) ||αx|| ≤ ||x|| whenever |α| ≤ 1; (iii) lim_{α→0} ||αx|| = 0 for every x ∈ X; (iv) ||x + y|| ≤ ||x|| + ||y||. An F-space is a vector space equipped with an F-norm whose induced translation-invariant metric d(x,y) = ||x − y|| is complete. Two F-norms on X are called equivalent if they induce the same topology. An F-norm ||·||' is said to be unbounded if sup_{x ∈ X} ||x||' = +∞.

(a) Does every F-space X contain an infinite-dimensional (closed) linear subspace Y that admits an F-norm, equivalent to the restriction of the F-norm of X, which is unbounded?

(b) Does every F-space X admit a closed linear subspace M such that the quotient F-space X/M admits an equivalent unbounded F-norm?

paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
original_question: If X and Y are locally bounded F-spaces and U: X -> Y is a rotation, meaning an isometry with U(0) = 0, must U be linear even without assuming that the F-norms are concave?
self_contained_problem:
An F-norm on a real vector space $X$ is a function $\|\cdot\|:X\to[0,\infty)$ such that (i) $\|x\|=0$ iff $x=0$; (ii) $\|\alpha x\|=\|x\|$ for every scalar $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|=1$; (iii) $\|\alpha_n x_n - \alpha x\|\to 0$ whenever $\alpha_n\to\alpha$ in $\mathbb{R}$ and $\|x_n-x\|\to 0$; and (iv) $\|x+y\|\le\|x\|+\|y\|$. An F-space is a complete metric linear space whose topology is given by such an F-norm via $d(x,y)=\|x-y\|$. An F-space $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ is called locally bounded if the origin has a bounded neighborhood; equivalently, $X$ admits a $p$-homogeneous quasi-norm for some $0<p\le 1$. The F-norm $\|\cdot\|$ is called concave if $t\mapsto\|tx\|$ is concave on $[0,\infty)$ for every $x\in X$. A rotation from $X$ to $Y$ is a map $U:X\to Y$ that is an isometry (i.e. $\|U(x)-U(y)\|_Y=\|x-y\|_X$ for all $x,y\in X$) and satisfies $U(0)=0$.

Question: Let $X$ and $Y$ be locally bounded F-spaces and let $U:X\to Y$ be a surjective rotation. Must $U$ be linear, without assuming that the F-norms on $X$ and $Y$ are concave?
status_search_result: Classical results of Charzyński and Rolewicz establish linearity of surjective isometries fixing the origin in finite-dimensional F-spaces and in locally bounded spaces with concave F-norms. Subsequent work (e.g. Ding–Huang on locally midpoint constricted F-spaces, and generalizations to p-normed spaces) extends linearity under additional structural assumptions, but a definitive resolution of the general locally bounded case without concavity does not appear in the located sources. The problem's current status could not be conclusively verified.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
context_brief: Maximality of sup norm on C[0,1]
original_question: Consider the Banach space C[0,1] of continuous real-valued functions on the interval [0,1] with the supremum norm. Is this supremum norm maximal, meaning that whenever an equivalent F-norm has a larger group of rotations, the two groups of rotations must in fact coincide?
self_contained_problem:
Let $C[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of all continuous real-valued functions on the interval $[0,1]$ equipped with the supremum norm $\|f\|_\infty=\sup_{t\in[0,1]}|f(t)|$. original_question: Let X be an F-space, let Ω be a measurable space with sigma-field Σ, and let μ: Σ -> X be a nonatomic countably additive X-valued measure. For every bounded measurable scalar-valued function x(t), must the integral ∫_Ω x(t) dμ(t) exist?
self_contained_problem:

Let (Ω, Σ) be a measurable space, and let μ : Σ → X be a countably additive vector measure that is nonatomic, meaning that for every E ∈ Σ with μ(E) ≠ 0 there exists F ∈ Σ with F ⊂ E such that μ(F) ≠ 0 and μ(E \ F) ≠ 0.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
original_question: Let X be a nuclear F-space in the sense defined via diametral approximative dimension. Is every unconditionally convergent series in X necessarily absolutely convergent?
self_contained_problem:
Definitions. An F-space is a complete metrizable topological vector space whose topology is given by a translation-invariant metric (not necessarily locally convex). For a bounded subset B of an F-space X and ε>0, let N(ε,B) denote the smallest cardinality of an ε-net for B (in the invariant metric), and define the diametral approximative dimension of X as the collection of all sequences (t_n) of positive reals such that for every neighborhood U of 0 there is a neighborhood V of 0 with t_n · δ_n(V,U) → 0, where δ_n(V,U) is the n-th Kolmogorov diameter of V with respect to U. Call an F-space X nuclear (in the sense of diametral approximative dimension) if its diametral approximative dimension contains every sequence (t_n) of positive reals tending to infinity, equivalently if it satisfies the Kolmogorov diameter characterization of nuclearity adapted to F-spaces.

A series ∑ x_n in X is said to converge unconditionally if ∑ x_{π(n)} converges in X for every permutation π of ℕ. It is said to converge absolutely if for every continuous F-seminorm (equivalently, for the invariant metric d) one has ∑ d(x_n, 0) < ∞.

Question. Let X be a nuclear F-space in the above sense. Is it true that every unconditionally convergent series in X is absolutely convergent?
status_search_result: The classical Dvoretzky–Rogers theorem (and its locally convex extension by Grothendieck/Pietsch) shows that unconditional convergence implies absolute convergence in nuclear Fréchet (locally convex) spaces. For non-locally-convex nuclear F-spaces defined via diametral approximative dimension, no resolution was located in the search; the question appears to remain unresolved in the literature accessible online.

paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
original_question: Is every nuclear F-space a Montel space, meaning that every bounded subset is compact?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\tau)$ be an F-space, that is, a topological vector space over $\mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{C}$) whose topology is induced by a complete translation-invariant metric (local convexity is not assumed). A subset $B\subset X$ is bounded if for every neighborhood $U$ of $0$ there exists $t>0$ with $B\subset tU$. Call $X$ a Montel space if every bounded closed subset of $X$ is compact.

A nuclear F-space is defined as follows. For an F-seminorm (or, equivalently, a sequence of F-seminorms generating the topology) $\|\cdot\|$ on $X$, a continuous linear operator $T:X\to Y$ between F-spaces is nuclear if it admits a representation
$$T(x)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\lambda_n\, f_n(x)\, y_n,$$
where $(f_n)$ is an equicontinuous sequence in the dual of $X$, $(y_n)$ is a bounded sequence in $Y$, and $(\lambda_n)\in\ell^1$. The F-space $X$ is called nuclear if for every continuous F-seminorm $p$ on $X$ there exists a continuous F-seminorm $q\ge p$ such that the canonical map $X_q\to X_p$ between the associated quotient/completion spaces is nuclear.

Question: Is every nuclear F-space a Montel space?
status_search_result: In the locally convex setting it is classical that every nuclear Fréchet space is Montel. For nuclear F-spaces without the local convexity assumption, the literature located in the search does not provide a definitive answer, and the problem appears in collections of open problems on metric linear spaces without a verified resolution.

original_question: Does every infinite-dimensional F-space contain an infinite-dimensional F-subspace that has nontrivial continuous linear functionals? Does this remain true under the additional assumptions that the ambient space is locally bounded, or nuclear, or has no unbounded norms?
self_contained_problem:
An F-space is a topological vector space $X$ over $\mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{C}$) whose topology is induced by a complete translation-invariant metric. A continuous linear functional on $X$ is a continuous linear map $f\colon X\to\mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{C}$); call $f$ nontrivial if $f\not\equiv 0$. Recall:
- $X$ is locally bounded if it has a bounded neighborhood of $0$ (equivalently, its topology is given by a $p$-norm for some $0<p\le 1$).

be the set of volume-preserving $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms with nonzero Lyapunov exponents on a set of positive $\mu$-measure. A subset of a topological space is called residual in an open set $U$ if it contains a countable intersection of open dense subsets of $U$.

paper_title: Open problems in the theory of non-uniform hyperbolicity
context_brief: Constructing non-uniformly hyperbolic SRB measures on a topological attractor
original_question: Let Λ = ⋂_{n≥0} f^n(U) be a topological attractor with trapping region U for a diffeomorphism f. Under what conditions can one construct a Milnor attractor A contained in Λ by producing a non-uniformly hyperbolic SRB measure supported on Λ via the SRB construction discussed in the paper?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold and let $f: M \to M$ be a $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphism. A non-empty open set $U \subset M$ with $\overline{f(U)} \subset U$ is called a trapping region, and the corresponding topological attractor is
$$\Lambda \;=\; \bigcap_{n\ge 0} f^n(U).$$
A Milnor attractor is a compact invariant set $A \subset M$ such that its basin
$$B(A) \;=\; \{x \in M : \omega_f(x) \subset A\}$$
has positive Lebesgue measure, and no proper compact invariant subset of $A$ has the same property up to a null set.

An $f$-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ supported on $\Lambda$ is said to be a non-uniformly hyperbolic SRB measure if (i) all Lyapunov exponents of $\mu$ are nonzero (some positive and some negative on a set of full $\mu$-measure when $\dim M \ge 2$, allowing mixed signs), and (ii) the conditional measures of $\mu$ on local unstable manifolds are absolutely continuous with respect to the induced Lebesgue measure on those manifolds.

Problem. Identify general geometric and dynamical conditions on the pair $(f,U)$ — and hence on the topological attractor $\Lambda$ — under which there exists a non-uniformly hyperbolic SRB measure $\mu$ supported on $\Lambda$, and such that the support (or some appropriate minimal "observed" invariant subset) of $\mu$ is a Milnor attractor $A \subset \Lambda$. In particular, give verifiable sufficient conditions on $f|_U$ that allow one to construct such an SRB measure on $\Lambda$ by pushing forward and averaging Lebesgue measure on $U$ along the orbits of $f$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a survey of open problems on non-uniform hyperbolicity. While significant progress on constructing SRB measures for non-uniformly hyperbolic systems has been made (e.g., by Pesin, Climenhaga, Dolgopyat, Sarig, and others under specific structural assumptions such as the presence of hyperbolic periodic points with horseshoes, dominated splittings, or Young towers), no general criterion characterizing when an arbitrary topological attractor carries a non-uniformly hyperbolic SRB measure has been established. The problem remains open in full generality.

original_question: Describe the combinatorics of the three tensegrity configuration spaces B_2(K_6), B_3(K_4), and B_3(K_5), where B_d(G) denotes the configuration space of all realizations of the graph G on labeled vertices in R^d and the stratification is by maximal connected components with equivalent self-stress fibers.

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with vertex set $V=\{1,\dots,n\}$. For an integer $d\ge 1$, the configuration space of tensegrity frameworks on $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is
$$B_d(G):=(\mathbb{R}^d)^n,$$
whose points $p=(p_1,\dots,p_n)$ are placements of the labeled vertices of $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$. A self-stress on a framework $p\in B_d(G)$ is an assignment of real weights $w:E\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for every vertex $i\in V$,
$$\sum_{j:\{i,j\}\in E} w_{ij}\,(p_j-p_i)=0.$$
The set of all self-stresses of $p$ forms a real vector subspace $W(p)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^E$, called the stress fiber over $p$. Two configurations $p,p'\in B_d(G)$ are called equivalent if there is an isomorphism between $W(p)$ and $W(p')$ that preserves the signs (positive, negative, zero) of all coordinates indexed by $E$. A stratum of $B_d(G)$ is a maximal connected subset of $B_d(G)$ all of whose points are pairwise equivalent in this sense. The resulting decomposition gives the stratification of $B_d(G)$ by stress-equivalence, and its combinatorics consist of the list of strata together with their dimensions and adjacency relations.

$$B_2(K_6),\qquad B_3(K_4),\qquad B_3(K_5),$$

context_brief: Cayley description of all planar codimension-one strata
original_question: Given a graph G, determine whether there exists one Cayley algebra system, or several such systems, that describes exactly the union of the codimension-1 tensegrity strata in the plane; equivalently, the union of the codimension-1 strata of B_2(K_n). Here a Cayley algebra system means a description built from planar points and lines using join and meet operations.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Work in the real projective plane (or the affine plane with its line at infinity). The planar Cayley algebra consists of two kinds of objects, points and lines, together with two operations:
 • join: given two points, their join is the unique line through them;
 • meet: given two lines, their meet is their intersection point.
A Cayley algebra system is a finite formal expression built from a list of "free" input points and/or lines by iteratively applying join and meet; such a system, evaluated on an admissible configuration of input points, produces a finite collection of derived points and lines, and thus cuts out an algebraic condition on the input configuration (namely, that certain derived objects coincide, are collinear, are concurrent, etc.).

Tensegrity strata. Fix an integer n ≥ 2 and let K_n denote the complete graph on n labeled vertices. A planar tensegrity on K_n is a placement p = (p_1, …, p_n) of the n vertices in the plane together with a nonzero real "stress" ω_{ij} on each edge ij such that, at every vertex i, the equilibrium condition Σ_{j ≠ i} ω_{ij}(p_j − p_i) = 0 holds. For a configuration p ∈ (R^2)^n in sufficiently general position, the dimension of the space W(p) of such stresses is a function of p, and the configuration space (R^2)^n is stratified by the level sets of dim W(p) and of the sign pattern of admissible stresses. The closure of those strata where the local codimension equals 1 (i.e., the configurations p at which exactly one nontrivial linear relation among the edge stresses appears, beyond the generic value) forms the codimension-1 tensegrity stratum B_2(K_n) ⊂ (R^2)^n; denote by S_1(K_n) the union of its codimension-1 components.

Problem. Given a graph G on n vertices (and in particular for G = K_n), decide whether there exists a single Cayley algebra system, or a finite collection of Cayley algebra systems, whose simultaneous vanishing locus on (R^2)^n equals precisely S_1(K_n), the union of the codimension-1 tensegrity strata of the planar configuration space of G. Equivalently, give a Cayley-algebra (join/meet) characterization of S_1(K_n) using only the planar points p_1, …, p_n and the lines obtained from them by iterated join and meet, with no additional auxiliary points or lines allowed.
status_search_result: The problem of giving a pure Cayley-algebra description of the union of codimension-1 tensegrity strata in the plane is recorded as a long-standing open problem on Cayley strata descriptions. A weaker version has been addressed using an extended Cayley algebra (with additional auxiliary elements), but it is not known whether such auxiliary elements can be eliminated, and there are candidate graphs that are suspected to provide counterexamples in the strict (non-extended) setting.

paper_title: Open problems on cyclic codes
context_brief: Exact distances of BCH and QR codes
original_question: For cyclic codes in the classical families discussed in the chapter, what are the exact minimum distances of Bose–Chaudhuri–Hocquenghem (BCH) codes and quadratic residue (QR) codes in the cases where those distances are still unknown?

Let q be a prime power and n a positive integer with gcd(n,q)=1. A cyclic code C of length n over the finite field F_q is an ideal in F_q[x]/(x^n-1), generated by a divisor g(x) of x^n-1; equivalently, C is specified by its set of zeros (the "defining set") among the n-th roots of unity in an extension of F_q. The minimum distance d(C) of C is the smallest Hamming weight of a nonzero codeword in C.

Two classical families:
(1) BCH codes. Fix a primitive n-th root of unity α in an extension of F_q, a "designed distance" δ with 2 ≤ δ ≤ n, and an integer b ≥ 0. The BCH code BCH_q(n,δ,b) is the cyclic code over F_q whose defining set contains {α^{b}, α^{b+1}, …, α^{b+δ-2}}; that is, its generator polynomial is the least-degree monic divisor of x^n−1 over F_q having these elements as zeros. The BCH bound gives d(BCH_q(n,δ,b)) ≥ δ, but the exact value of d is in general not known.
(2) Quadratic residue (QR) codes. Let p be an odd prime such that q is a quadratic residue mod p, and let Q ⊂ (Z/pZ)^* be the set of nonzero quadratic residues mod p. Let β be a primitive p-th root of unity in an extension of F_q. The (binary or q-ary) quadratic residue codes of length p are the cyclic codes over F_q with generator polynomials ∏_{i∈Q}(x−β^i) and ∏_{i∈Q∪{0}}(x−β^i), together with their counterparts using the set of nonresidues. The exact minimum distances of these codes are known in only finitely many cases.

Problem. Determine, in closed form or by an effective rule, the exact minimum distance d(C) of every BCH code BCH_q(n,δ,b) and of every quadratic residue code of prime length p over F_q, in the infinite families of parameters for which this exact value is currently unknown.

original_question: Develop a satisfactory way to determine or sharply estimate the minimum distances of the duals of primitive BCH codes, since the chapter reports that this approximation problem remained open.
self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a prime power, $m\ge 2$ an integer, and set $n=q^m-1$. Let $\alpha$ be a primitive element of $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$. paper_title: Open problems on cyclic codes
original_question: Beyond the known Reed–Muller cases, for which cyclic codes is the entire code generated by its minimum-weight codewords?
self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a prime power and let $n$ be a positive integer with $\gcd(n,q)=1$. A linear code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ is called cyclic if it is invariant under the cyclic shift $(c_0,c_1,\dots,c_{n-1}) \mapsto (c_{n-1},c_0,\dots,c_{n-2})$. Equivalently, via the identification $\mathbb{F}_q^n \cong \mathbb{F}_q[x]/(x^n-1)$, $C$ is an ideal in this quotient ring. The (Hamming) weight $\operatorname{wt}(c)$ of a codeword $c \in C$ is the number of nonzero coordinates, and the minimum distance is $d(C) = \min\{\operatorname{wt}(c) : c \in C,\ c \neq 0\}$. Let $M(C) \subseteq C$ denote the set of minimum-weight codewords of $C$, i.e., those with $\operatorname{wt}(c) = d(C)$.

It is known that binary Reed–Muller codes (which form a class of cyclic-extended codes) have the property that they are generated as $\mathbb{F}_q$-vector spaces by their minimum-weight codewords.

Problem: Characterize, beyond the Reed–Muller family, all cyclic codes $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with the property that $C = \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{F}_q} M(C)$, i.e., $C$ is generated by its minimum-weight codewords.
status_search_result: The general characterization remains open. Recent work (e.g., a 2024 arXiv preprint on low-weight codewords in cyclic codes and 2025 work on BCH codes) continues to study minimum-weight codewords and bases of cyclic/BCH codes, indicating that the question of which cyclic codes are generated by their minimum-weight codewords is still actively studied without a complete answer.

original_question: Classify binary cyclic codes with exactly two zeros by minimum distance and determine their weight enumerators, since the chapter says this classification had not been achieved and the weight-enumerator problem remained very difficult.
self_contained_problem:
Let m ≥ 2 be an integer and let n = 2^m - 1. For integers r, s with 0 ≤ r < s ≤ n-1, define the binary cyclic code C_{r,s} of length n to be the binary cyclic code whose dual has as zeros exactly the conjugates of α^r and α^s, where α is a primitive n-th root of unity in F_{2^m}; equivalently, C_{r,s} is the binary cyclic code of length n whose defining set is the union of the 2-cyclotomic cosets of r and s modulo n. original_question: Welsh conjecture: for binary cyclic codes C_{1,ℓ} of length 2^m−1 with ℓ = 2^t + 3 and m = 2t + 1, prove or disprove that these codes have minimum distance five and the same weight enumerator as the 2-error-correcting BCH code.

Take $\ell = 2^{t} + 3$. 

Prove or disprove the following statement: the code $C_{1,\ell}$ has minimum distance $5$, and its weight enumerator is identical to that of the binary $2$-error-correcting BCH code of length $n = 2^{m}-1$ (i.e., the code $C_{1,3}$).

original_question: Determine the automorphism groups of Goppa codes, since the chapter states that these groups were not known in general.
self_contained_problem:
Let q be a prime power, and let L = (α_1, …, α_n) be a tuple of pairwise distinct elements of an extension field F_{q^m}, and let g(x) ∈ F_{q^m}[x] be a polynomial (the Goppa polynomial) such that g(α_i) ≠ 0 for all i. The classical Goppa code Γ(L, g) is the F_q-linear code

  Γ(L, g) = { (c_1, …, c_n) ∈ F_q^n : ∑_{i=1}^{n} c_i / (x − α_i) ≡ 0 (mod g(x)) }.

The (permutation) automorphism group Aut(Γ(L, g)) is the group of permutations σ ∈ S_n such that (c_{σ(1)}, …, c_{σ(n)}) ∈ Γ(L, g) for every codeword (c_1, …, c_n) ∈ Γ(L, g); more generally, one may consider the monomial or semilinear automorphism group.

paper_title: Open problems on cyclic codes
original_question: Determine the complete weight enumerator of the Melas code, since the chapter explicitly says that this remained open and ties it to Kloosterman sums.
self_contained_problem:
Let $q = 2^m$ with $m \geq 3$, and let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements. The binary Melas code $M(2,m)$ of length $n = q - 1$ is the cyclic code over $\mathbb{F}_2$ whose dual is generated (as a cyclic code) by the parity-check matrix whose columns are the pairs $(\alpha^i, \alpha^{-i})$, where $\alpha$ is a primitive element of $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $i = 0,1,\dots,n-1$; equivalently, $M(2,m)$ is the binary cyclic code of length $2^m - 1$ whose defining set consists of the cyclotomic cosets of $1$ and $-1$ modulo $2^m - 1$, i.e. its zeros are $\alpha$ and $\alpha^{-1}$. The weight enumerator of $M(2,m)$ is the polynomial
$$W_{M(2,m)}(X,Y) = \sum_{c \in M(2,m)} X^{n - \mathrm{wt}(c)} Y^{\mathrm{wt}(c)} = \sum_{w=0}^{n} A_w\, X^{n-w} Y^w,$$
where $A_w$ is the number of codewords of Hamming weight $w$. For a nontrivial additive character $\psi$ of $\mathbb{F}_q$, the Kloosterman sum is
$$K(a) = \sum_{x \in \mathbb{F}_q^{*}} \psi\!\left(x + a x^{-1}\right), \qquad a \in \mathbb{F}_q^{*}.$$
It is known that the weights in the dual of $M(2,m)$ are expressible in terms of values of $K(a)$, but the precise distribution of these values, and hence the full weight distribution of $M(2,m)$, is not known in closed form.

Problem: Determine explicitly the complete weight enumerator $W_{M(2,m)}(X,Y)$, i.e. give a closed-form expression for the coefficients $A_w$ for every $m \geq 3$ and every $0 \leq w \leq 2^m - 1$.
status_search_result: Available literature indicates that the weight distribution of the Melas code (equivalently, the distribution of binary Kloosterman sum values) remains an active object of study, with only partial results — such as divisibility characterizations (e.g., Kloosterman sums divisible by 3), moment computations, and asymptotic Sato–Tate type distribution results — but no closed-form complete weight enumerator. No source found indicates a full resolution.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, and let 0 < λ₁ < λ₂ ≤ λ₃ ≤ ··· be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian, defined by −Δu = λu in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω. Must the ratio (λ₂ + ··· + λₙ₊₁)/λ₁ always be at most the corresponding value for the Euclidean n-ball, namely n j_{p+1,1}² / j_{p,1}² where p = (n−2)/2 and j_{ν,k} denotes the k-th positive zero of the Bessel function J_ν? In particular, for n = 2, is (λ₂ + λ₃)/λ₁ ≤ ((λ₂ + λ₃)/λ₁)_disk ≈ 5.077?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \ge 2$) be a bounded domain, and let
\[
0 < \lambda_1(\Omega) < \lambda_2(\Omega) \le \lambda_3(\Omega) \le \cdots
\]
denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e. the values $\lambda$ for which there exists a nonzero $u \in H^1_0(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u = \lambda u$ in $\Omega$ and $u = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$.

For a real parameter $\nu \ge 0$, let $J_\nu$ denote the Bessel function of the first kind of order $\nu$, and let $j_{\nu,k}$ denote its $k$-th positive zero. Set $p = (n-2)/2$. It is known that, when $\Omega = B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is the Euclidean unit ball, the first eigenvalue equals $j_{p,1}^2$, while $\lambda_2(B) = \cdots = \lambda_{n+1}(B) = j_{p+1,1}^2$, so that
\[
\frac{\lambda_2(B) + \lambda_3(B) + \cdots + \lambda_{n+1}(B)}{\lambda_1(B)} = \frac{n\, j_{p+1,1}^2}{j_{p,1}^2}.
\]

Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$,
\[
\frac{\lambda_2(\Omega) + \lambda_3(\Omega) + \cdots + \lambda_{n+1}(\Omega)}{\lambda_1(\Omega)} \;\le\; \frac{n\, j_{p+1,1}^2}{j_{p,1}^2}.
\]
In particular, for $n = 2$, decide whether
\[
\frac{\lambda_2(\Omega) + \lambda_3(\Omega)}{\lambda_1(\Omega)} \;\le\; \frac{2\, j_{1,1}^2}{j_{0,1}^2} \;\approx\; 5.077
\]
holds for every bounded planar domain $\Omega$, with equality (in the limit) only for the disk.
status_search_result: The inequality is the Ashbaugh–Benguria PPW-type conjecture for the sum of the second through $(n+1)$-st Dirichlet eigenvalues divided by the first. Partial results exist (e.g., work on the Ashbaugh–Benguria conjecture about lower-order Dirichlet eigenvalues, and PPW-type results in symmetric spaces), but the conjecture in its general form for arbitrary bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (including the planar case with bound $\approx 5.077$) appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂, .... For every integer m ≥ 1, must the even-index ratio λ₂ₘ/λₘ always satisfy λ₂ₘ/λₘ ≤ (λ₂/λ₁)_{n-ball}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain, and let $0 < \lambda_1(\Omega) \le \lambda_2(\Omega) \le \lambda_3(\Omega) \le \cdots$ denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e., the values $\lambda$ for which there exists a nonzero $u \in H^1_0(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u = \lambda u$ in $\Omega$. Let $B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ denote any ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (the ratio below is scale-invariant), and write
$$R_n := \frac{\lambda_2(B)}{\lambda_1(B)} = \frac{j_{n/2,1}^2}{j_{n/2-1,1}^2},$$
where $j_{\nu,1}$ is the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$. Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and every integer $m \ge 1$,
$$\frac{\lambda_{2m}(\Omega)}{\lambda_m(\Omega)} \le R_n.$$
status_search_result: The classical PPW conjecture (case m=1) was solved by Ashbaugh and Benguria in the 1990s, but its generalization to ratios λ_{2m}/λ_m for all m ≥ 1 remains an open conjecture. Recent works (e.g., on Ashbaugh–Benguria's conjecture about lower-order Dirichlet eigenvalues) make partial progress but do not establish the general bound.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Among bounded domains Ω in ℝⁿ, what is the optimal upper bound for the Dirichlet eigenvalue ratio λ₃/λ₁, and which domain realizes that supremum, possibly only in a limiting sense? In particular, in dimension 2 the source asks for the exact value of sup_Ω λ₃/λ₁ and the optimizer, noting that the disk is not optimal.
self_contained_problem:
For a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, let $0<\lambda_1(\Omega)<\lambda_2(\Omega)\le\lambda_3(\Omega)\le\cdots$ denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Dirichlet Laplacian, i.e. the values $\lambda$ for which there exists a nonzero $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ satisfying $-\Delta u=\lambda u$ in $\Omega$ and $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$. Define
$$R_n \;=\; \sup_{\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n}\frac{\lambda_3(\Omega)}{\lambda_1(\Omega)},$$
where the supremum is taken over all bounded domains $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$.

(a) Determine $R_n$ explicitly for each $n\ge 2$, and identify a domain (or limiting sequence of domains) realizing this supremum.

(b) In particular, in dimension $n=2$, it is known that
$$\tfrac{35}{11}\;\approx\;3.1818\;\le\;R_2\;\le\;3.83103,$$
and that the disk does not realize $R_2$. Determine the exact value of $R_2$ and the extremal planar domain (possibly in a limiting sense).
status_search_result: The optimal upper bound for $\lambda_3/\lambda_1$ over bounded planar domains, and the identification of the extremal shape, appears to remain open. Known results provide only the bracketing $35/11 \le \sup_\Omega \lambda_3/\lambda_1 \le 3.83103$ in dimension 2, with the disk known not to be optimal; current literature on Dirichlet-Laplacian eigenvalue-ratio bounds continues to refine related estimates but does not give a sharp value.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain with Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ ···. Must the next multiplicity-cluster sums also be bounded by their ball values, namely λ₄ + λ₅ over λ₁ in dimension 2 and, in general dimension n, (λₙ₊₂ + ··· + λ_{n(n+3)/2})/λ₁ ≤ ((n−1)(n+2)/2) · j_{p+2,1}² / j_{p,1}²?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 2$) be a bounded domain, and let
$$0<\lambda_1(\Omega)\le \lambda_2(\Omega)\le \lambda_3(\Omega)\le\cdots$$
denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicities) of the Dirichlet Laplacian $-\Delta$ on $\Omega$, i.e. of the problem
$$-\Delta u=\lambda u\text{ in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega.$$
For an integer $m\ge 0$ and positive integer $k$, let $j_{m,k}$ denote the $k$-th positive zero of the Bessel function $J_m$. For a ball $B\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, the Dirichlet eigenvalues are known explicitly in terms of zeros of Bessel functions $J_{p+\ell}$ with $p=(n-2)/2$, and one has in particular that $\lambda_1(B)$ corresponds to $j_{p,1}^2/R^2$ (where $R$ is the radius), while the next eigenvalue cluster involves $j_{p+1,1}^2/R^2$, and the subsequent cluster involves $j_{p+2,1}^2/R^2$.

On a ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$, the first eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ is simple, the next cluster $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_{n+1}$ consists of $n$ equal eigenvalues, and the following cluster $\lambda_{n+2},\dots,\lambda_{n(n+3)/2}$ consists of $\tfrac{(n-1)(n+2)}{2}$ equal eigenvalues. In particular, for a disk in $\mathbb{R}^2$ ($n=2$, $p=0$),
$$\frac{\lambda_4(B)+\lambda_5(B)}{\lambda_1(B)}=\frac{2\,j_{2,1}^2}{j_{0,1}^2}\approx 9.121.$$

Prove or disprove the following conjectured isoperimetric inequalities for arbitrary bounded domains $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$:

(a) In dimension $n=2$,
$$\frac{\lambda_4(\Omega)+\lambda_5(\Omega)}{\lambda_1(\Omega)}\le \frac{2\,j_{2,1}^2}{j_{0,1}^2}.$$

(b) In general dimension $n\ge 2$, writing $p=(n-2)/2$,
$$\frac{\lambda_{n+2}(\Omega)+\lambda_{n+3}(\Omega)+\cdots+\lambda_{n(n+3)/2}(\Omega)}{\lambda_1(\Omega)}\le \frac{(n-1)(n+2)}{2}\cdot\frac{j_{p+2,1}^2}{j_{p,1}^2},$$
with equality if and only if $\Omega$ is a ball.
status_search_result: The conjectured cluster-sum bounds for higher Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian (extending Ashbaugh–Benguria-type ratios beyond $\lambda_2/\lambda_1$ and $(\lambda_2+\cdots+\lambda_{n+1})/\lambda_1$) appear to remain open. Recent literature on Ashbaugh–Benguria-style conjectures addresses lower-order eigenvalues (e.g., $(\lambda_2+\cdots+\lambda_{n+1})/\lambda_1$), but no proof of the $\lambda_4+\lambda_5$ cluster bound in 2D or its $n$-dimensional generalization was located.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, with area A when n = 2 and volume |Ω| in general, and let λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ ··· be the Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues. Is the scale-invariant quantity |Ω|^{2/n} λₙ₊₁ always at least the n-ball value C_n^{2/n} j_{p+1,1}², so that in particular A λ₃ ≥ (A λ₃)_disk = π j_{1,1}² in dimension 2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain, and let $0<\lambda_1(\Omega)\le\lambda_2(\Omega)\le\cdots$ denote the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e. the values $\lambda$ for which there is a nontrivial $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u=\lambda u$ in $\Omega$ and $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$. Write $|\Omega|$ for the Lebesgue measure of $\Omega$ (denoted $A$ in dimension $n=2$). Let $j_{\nu,1}$ denote the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$, set $p=(n-2)/2$, and let $C_n=\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2+1)$ be the volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$. The scale-invariant quantity $|\Omega|^{2/n}\lambda_{n+1}(\Omega)$ on the $n$-ball equals $C_n^{2/n} j_{p+1,1}^2$.

Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$|\Omega|^{2/n}\,\lambda_{n+1}(\Omega)\ \ge\ C_n^{2/n}\, j_{p+1,1}^2,$$
with equality when $\Omega$ is an $n$-ball. In particular, in dimension $n=2$, is it true that $A\,\lambda_3(\Omega)\ge \pi j_{1,1}^2$, the value attained by a disk?
status_search_result: The conjecture that the disk minimizes $\lambda_3$ among planar domains of fixed area (and that the $n$-ball minimizes $\lambda_{n+1}$ among $n$-dimensional domains of fixed volume) appears to remain open. For $\lambda_1$ the Faber-Krahn inequality is classical, and for $\lambda_2$ the Krahn-Szegő theorem gives two equal balls as the minimizer. For $\lambda_3$ only existence of an optimal domain (and connectedness in dimensions 2 and 3) is known; the conjecture that the optimizer is a single ball is unresolved.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: For Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues on bounded domains Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, do the next-level analogues of the Faber-Krahn-type inequalities hold—namely Aλ₅ ≥ (Aλ₅)_disk, A(λ₄+λ₅) ≥ [A(λ₄+λ₅)]_disk, |Ω|^{2/n} λ_{n(n+3)/2} ≥ (|Ω|^{2/n} λ_{n(n+3)/2})_{n-ball}, and |Ω|^{2/n}(λₙ₊₂ + ··· + λ_{n(n+3)/2}) ≥ the corresponding n-ball value? More generally, for each k ≥ 3, what is the optimal lower bound for |Ω|^{2/n} λ_k, and which domain or limiting family of domains attains it?
self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ be a bounded open domain, and let 0 < λ₁(Ω) ≤ λ₂(Ω) ≤ λ₃(Ω) ≤ ⋯ denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Dirichlet Laplacian on Ω, i.e. the values λ for which there exists a nonzero u ∈ H₀¹(Ω) with −Δu = λu in Ω and u = 0 on ∂Ω. Let |Ω| denote the Lebesgue measure of Ω, and in the planar case (n = 2) write A = |Ω|. For each k ≥ 1, let (·)_{n-ball} denote the value of the corresponding scale-invariant functional evaluated on a Euclidean ball in ℝⁿ (in the planar case, a disk).

Address the following questions.

(a) In the planar case n = 2, does the inequality
    A · λ₅(Ω) ≥ (A · λ₅)_{disk}
hold for every bounded planar domain Ω, with equality only when Ω is a disk?

(b) In the planar case n = 2, does
    A · (λ₄(Ω) + λ₅(Ω)) ≥ [A · (λ₄ + λ₅)]_{disk}
hold for every bounded planar domain Ω?

(c) For every n ≥ 2 and every bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, does
    |Ω|^{2/n} · λ_{n(n+3)/2}(Ω) ≥ ( |Ω|^{2/n} · λ_{n(n+3)/2} )_{n-ball}
hold?

(d) For every n ≥ 2 and every bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, does
    |Ω|^{2/n} · ( λ_{n+2}(Ω) + λ_{n+3}(Ω) + ⋯ + λ_{n(n+3)/2}(Ω) ) ≥ [ |Ω|^{2/n} · ( λ_{n+2} + ⋯ + λ_{n(n+3)/2} ) ]_{n-ball}
hold?

(e) More generally, for each integer k ≥ 3 and each dimension n ≥ 2, determine the sharp constant
    C_{n,k} := inf_{Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ bounded} |Ω|^{2/n} λ_k(Ω),
and identify the domain (or limiting family of domains, possibly disconnected or degenerate) that attains this infimum.
category_tag: Faber-Krahn inequalities for higher Dirichlet eigenvalues
status_search_result: The sharp lower bound for |Ω|^{2/n} λ_k for k ≥ 3 and the optimizing shapes are known only in special cases. The classical Faber–Krahn theorem handles k = 1, and Krahn–Szegő settled k = 2 (two equal balls). For k ≥ 3 the optimizers in ℝⁿ are not generally known; partial results exist (e.g. via Bucur–Mazzoleni–Pratelli existence theory and numerical work), but the explicit conjectured inequalities for λ₅, λ₄+λ₅, λ_{n(n+3)/2}, and the corresponding sums remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: If Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ is a bounded convex domain and 0 = μ₀ < μ₁ ≤ μ₂ ≤ ··· are the Neumann eigenvalues of the Laplacian on Ω, must the ratio μ₂/μ₁ always satisfy μ₂/μ₁ ≤ 4?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded convex domain, and let
$$0 = \mu_0(\Omega) < \mu_1(\Omega) \le \mu_2(\Omega) \le \mu_3(\Omega) \le \cdots$$
denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Laplace operator $-\Delta$ on $\Omega$ with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, i.e. the values $\mu$ for which there exists a nonzero function $u \in H^1(\Omega)$ satisfying
$$-\Delta u = \mu u \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad \frac{\partial u}{\partial \nu} = 0 \text{ on } \partial \Omega,$$
where $\nu$ is the outward unit normal. Prove or disprove: for every bounded convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\frac{\mu_2(\Omega)}{\mu_1(\Omega)} \le 4.$$
status_search_result: A direct search did not return a proof or disproof of the bound $\mu_2/\mu_1 \le 4$ for bounded convex domains. The problem is listed as an open problem on eigenvalues of the Laplacian, and recent related work (e.g., on optimization and simplicity of the second Neumann eigenvalue on planar convex domains) treats nearby questions without resolving this ratio bound. No solution appears in the located literature.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with n ≥ 2. For the buckling problem Δ²v = −ΛΔv in Ω with v = 0 and ∂v/∂n = 0 on ∂Ω, must the lowest buckling eigenvalue Λ₁ satisfy the Faber-Krahn-type inequality |Ω|^{2/n} Λ₁ ≥ (|Ω|^{2/n} Λ₁)_{n-ball}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, $n \geq 2$, be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and let $\nu$ denote the outward unit normal to $\partial\Omega$. Consider the buckling eigenvalue problem
$$\Delta^2 v = -\Lambda \Delta v \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad v = 0 \text{ and } \frac{\partial v}{\partial \nu} = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
and let $\Lambda_1(\Omega)$ denote its lowest eigenvalue (equivalently, the smallest $\Lambda$ for which a nontrivial $v \in H_0^2(\Omega)$ exists). Let $B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a ball, and let $|\cdot|$ denote $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Prove or disprove that
$$|\Omega|^{2/n}\, \Lambda_1(\Omega) \;\geq\; |B|^{2/n}\, \Lambda_1(B),$$
with equality if and only if $\Omega$ is a ball (up to a set of measure zero).
status_search_result: The Faber-Krahn-type inequality for the first buckling eigenvalue (the Pólya–Szegő buckling conjecture, ca. 1950) remains open in general dimension. Partial results exist (e.g., Ashbaugh–Bucur and others establish that the ball is at least a local minimizer and prove related bounds), but the full conjecture for arbitrary bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 2$, has not been established.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, let λ₁(Ω) be its first Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalue, and let Λ₁(Ω) be its first buckling eigenvalue. Must the scale-invariant product |Ω|^{4/n} λ₁(Ω)Λ₁(Ω) always be at least the n-ball value C_n^{4/n} j_{p,1}² j_{p+1,1}², where p = (n−2)/2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 2$) be a bounded domain with sufficiently smooth boundary, and let $|\Omega|$ denote its $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure.

Define $\lambda_1(\Omega)$ as the first eigenvalue of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e. the smallest $\lambda$ such that there exists a nontrivial $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ with
$$-\Delta u=\lambda u\text{ in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega.$$

Define $\Lambda_1(\Omega)$ as the first buckling eigenvalue of $\Omega$, i.e. the smallest $\Lambda$ such that there exists a nontrivial $u\in H_0^2(\Omega)$ with
$$\Delta^2 u=-\Lambda\Delta u\text{ in }\Omega,\qquad u=\partial_\nu u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega.$$

Let $p=(n-2)/2$, and for $\nu\ge 0$ let $j_{\nu,1}$ denote the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$. Let $C_n=\omega_n^{-2/n}\,j_{p,1}^{\,2}$ be the scale-invariant value of $|\Omega|^{2/n}\lambda_1(\Omega)$ when $\Omega$ is an $n$-ball, where $\omega_n$ is the volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

Question: Does the inequality
$$|\Omega|^{4/n}\,\lambda_1(\Omega)\,\Lambda_1(\Omega)\;\ge\;C_n^{4/n}\,j_{p,1}^{\,2}\,j_{p+1,1}^{\,2}$$
hold for every bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, with equality when $\Omega$ is an $n$-ball?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not find a proof or disproof of the specific scale-invariant product inequality $|\Omega|^{4/n}\lambda_1(\Omega)\Lambda_1(\Omega)\ge C_n^{4/n}j_{p,1}^2 j_{p+1,1}^2$. Related conjectures (Payne's $\Lambda_1\ge\lambda_2$, Pólya–Szegő type bounds) are discussed in the literature, but the product conjecture itself appears to remain unresolved.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: For the clamped plate eigenvalues Γ₁ ≤ Γ₂ ≤ ··· and the buckling eigenvalues Λ₁ ≤ Λ₂ ≤ ··· on a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, is the ball the maximizer of the first nontrivial ratios Γ₂/Γ₁ and Λ₂/Λ₁? More generally, what are the sharp upper bounds for ratios such as Γ_{m+1}/Γ_m, Λ_{m+1}/Λ_m, (Γ₂+Γ₃)/Γ₁, and (Λ₂+Λ₃)/Λ₁?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with sufficiently smooth boundary. Consider two fourth-order eigenvalue problems on $\Omega$:

(a) The clamped plate problem
$$\Delta^2 u = \Gamma\, u \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial \nu} = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
with eigenvalues $0 < \Gamma_1 \le \Gamma_2 \le \Gamma_3 \le \cdots$.

(b) The buckling problem
$$\Delta^2 u = -\Lambda\, \Delta u \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial \nu} = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
with eigenvalues $0 < \Lambda_1 \le \Lambda_2 \le \Lambda_3 \le \cdots$.

Among all bounded domains $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ (with fixed volume, say), determine:

1. Whether the ball maximizes the first nontrivial ratios $\Gamma_2/\Gamma_1$ and $\Lambda_2/\Lambda_1$, i.e. prove or disprove that
$$\frac{\Gamma_2(\Omega)}{\Gamma_1(\Omega)} \le \frac{\Gamma_2(B)}{\Gamma_1(B)}, \qquad \frac{\Lambda_2(\Omega)}{\Lambda_1(\Omega)} \le \frac{\Lambda_2(B)}{\Lambda_1(B)},$$
where $B$ is a ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

2. More generally, find sharp upper bounds (and identify the extremal domains) for the ratios
$$\frac{\Gamma_{m+1}}{\Gamma_m}, \qquad \frac{\Lambda_{m+1}}{\Lambda_m}, \qquad \frac{\Gamma_2 + \Gamma_3}{\Gamma_1}, \qquad \frac{\Lambda_2 + \Lambda_3}{\Lambda_1}.$$
status_search_result: The underlying Rayleigh conjecture for the first clamped-plate eigenvalue is known only in dimensions 2 (Nadirashvili) and 3 (Ashbaugh–Benguria), and the Pólya–Szegő conjecture for the first buckling eigenvalue remains open in general. The corresponding sharp upper bounds for the ratios Γ_{m+1}/Γ_m, Λ_{m+1}/Λ_m, (Γ_2+Γ_3)/Γ_1, (Λ_2+Λ_3)/Λ_1, and even the ball-maximizer conjectures for Γ_2/Γ_1 and Λ_2/Λ_1, do not appear to be established in the recent literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For each integer n >= 10, is the connected graph on n vertices that maximizes the irregularity Irr(G) = lambda_1(G) - d_bar(G) always a pineapple graph PA(n,q), where PA(n,q) is the graph formed by a clique of size q together with n-q additional vertices that are pairwise nonadjacent and each adjacent to one common vertex of the clique, with q = floor(n/2) + 1? $$\mathrm{Irr}(G) := \lambda_1(G) - \bar d(G).$$
For positive integers $n > q \geq 2$, the pineapple graph $PA(n,q)$ is the graph on $n$ vertices obtained from a clique $K_q$ by attaching $n-q$ pendant vertices to a single vertex of the clique; equivalently, $PA(n,q)$ consists of a $q$-clique together with $n-q$ pairwise non-adjacent vertices, each adjacent to one common vertex of the clique.

$$\mathrm{Irr}(G) \leq \mathrm{Irr}\bigl(PA(n, \lfloor n/2\rfloor + 1)\bigr),$$
with equality only when $G \cong PA(n, \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1)$.

original_question: For every simple graph G on n vertices, does the Nordhaus-Gaddum sum of adjacency spectral radii satisfy lambda_1(G) + lambda_1(G_complement) <= 4n/3 - 5/3 - f(n), where f(n) = (3n - 2 - sqrt(9n^2 - 12n + 12))/6 when n mod 3 = 1, f(n) = 0 when n mod 3 = 2, and f(n) = (3n - 1 - sqrt(9n^2 - 6n + 9))/6 when n mod 3 = 0? If equality holds, must either G or its complement be a complete split graph whose independent set has size ceil(n/3), and also floor(n/3) when n mod 3 = 2?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple graph on n vertices and let \bar G denote its complement. Write \lambda_1(H) for the largest eigenvalue (spectral radius) of the adjacency matrix of a graph H. Define f: \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1} \to \mathbb{R} by
- f(n) = (3n - 2 - \sqrt{9n^2 - 12n + 12})/6 if n \equiv 1 \pmod 3,
- f(n) = 0 if n \equiv 2 \pmod 3,
- f(n) = (3n - 1 - \sqrt{9n^2 - 6n + 9})/6 if n \equiv 0 \pmod 3.

A complete split graph on n vertices with independence number k is the graph on vertex set partitioned as A \sqcup B with |A|=k, |B|=n-k, where A is an independent set, B induces a complete graph K_{n-k}, and every vertex of A is adjacent to every vertex of B.

Prove or disprove the following statements.
(1) For every simple graph G on n \ge 2 vertices,
\lambda_1(G) + \lambda_1(\bar G) \le \tfrac{4n}{3} - \tfrac{5}{3} - f(n).
(2) Equality is attained if and only if G or \bar G is a complete split graph whose independent set has size \lceil n/3 \rceil; and, when n \equiv 2 \pmod 3, equality is also attained if and only if G or \bar G is a complete split graph whose independent set has size \lfloor n/3 \rfloor.
status_search_result: A 2025 preprint by Yen-Jen Cheng and Chih-wen Weng ("Nordhaus-Gaddum inequality for the spectral radius of a graph of order n", arXiv:2506.11401) determines the extremal graph maximizing \lambda_1(G)+\lambda_1(\bar G) over all graphs of order n, resolving Stevanović's 2007 conjecture and showing the extremal graph is the complete split graph K_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}\vee \overline{K_{\lceil 2n/3\rceil}}. This identification of extremal graphs yields exactly the bound 4n/3 - 5/3 - f(n) with the stated equality cases, so the Aouchiche-Hansen formulation is resolved.

original_question: For n = 14 and for all n >= 16, is the bicyclic molecular graph on n vertices with maximal energy the graph P_n^{6;6}, obtained from two 6-cycles and a path P_(n-12) by attaching each path endpoint to one of the cycles by a single edge? self_contained_problem:
The energy of a finite simple graph $G$ with adjacency eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ is $E(G)=\sum_{i=1}^n |\lambda_i|$. A molecular graph is a connected graph in which every vertex has degree at most 4. A bicyclic graph is a connected graph with exactly $n$ vertices and $n+1$ edges. For integers $n\ge 14$, let $P_n^{6;6}$ denote the graph obtained from two disjoint copies of the 6-cycle $C_6$ and a path $P_{n-12}$ on $n-12$ vertices by joining each endpoint of the path to a single vertex of one of the two 6-cycles (one endpoint to each 6-cycle) via an additional edge.

paper_title: Open problems on k-orbit polytopes
original_question: For a k-orbit abstract polytope—meaning an abstract polytope whose automorphism group has k orbits on flags—suppose one is given a distinguished generating set for its automorphism group analogous to the standard generators used for regular polytopes. What condition on those generators should replace the string C-group intersection condition so that the generator data still captures the polytope structure?
self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope is a partially ordered set with a rank function whose elements (called faces) of ranks 0,...,n-1 satisfy the standard axioms generalizing the face lattice of a convex polytope: it has a unique minimum face and a unique maximum face, every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly n+2 elements, the poset is strongly flag-connected, and the diamond condition holds (for any face F of rank i-1 and any face G of rank i+1 with F<G, there are exactly two faces H of rank i with F<H<G). The automorphism group Γ(P) acts freely on the set of flags. The polytope P is called a k-orbit polytope if Γ(P) has exactly k orbits on flags.

For a regular abstract n-polytope (the case k=1), fixing a base flag yields the distinguished generators ρ_0,...,ρ_{n-1} of Γ(P), and Γ(P) is a string C-group: it is generated by involutions satisfying the string commutation relations (ρ_iρ_j)^2 = 1 for |i-j|≥2, and it satisfies the intersection condition
   ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I⟩ ∩ ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ J⟩ = ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I ∩ J⟩  for all I, J ⊆ {0,...,n-1}.
This intersection condition, together with the string relations, exactly characterizes which groups arise as automorphism groups of regular abstract polytopes.

Problem. Let P be a k-orbit abstract n-polytope (k ≥ 2), and suppose one is given a distinguished generating set of Γ(P) (depending on a choice of base flags from each flag orbit and reflecting the symmetry type graph of P) that plays the role analogous to the distinguished generators ρ_0,...,ρ_{n-1} in the regular case. Determine the precise combinatorial/group-theoretic condition on these generators — replacing the string C-group intersection condition — that is necessary and sufficient for a group with such a generating set to be the automorphism group of an abstract polytope of the prescribed symmetry type, i.e. such that this generator data faithfully recovers the polytope.
status_search_result: Partial answers exist. For 3-orbit polyhedra, explicit necessary and sufficient generator/intersection conditions have been worked out (Cunningham–Pellicer, J. Algebraic Combin., 2022). A general framework realizing every abstract n-polytope as a coset geometry, giving generators, relations, and intersection-type conditions tied to the symmetry type graph, was developed by Hubard et al. ("All polytopes are coset geometries", 2022/2023). A single clean uniform analogue of the string C-group intersection condition for arbitrary k-orbit polytopes, however, is not fully settled in the literature.

original_question: The quotient criterion says, in regular and chiral settings, that under suitable facet hypotheses a regular cover is again polytopal. Find a combinatorial criterion, usable for arbitrary polytopes or maniplexes rather than only regular or chiral ones, that plays the role of this quotient criterion.
self_contained_problem:
Background. An abstract n-polytope is a ranked partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) have ranks in {-1,0,...,n} with unique minimum and maximum, in which every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly one face of each rank, which is strongly flag-connected, and which satisfies the diamond condition: whenever F < G with rank(G) = rank(F)+2, there are exactly two faces H with F < H < G. The facets are the faces of rank n-1. A maniplex of rank n is an edge-n-colored connected graph in which, for each pair of distinct colors i,j with |i-j| > 1, every connected component of the subgraph spanned by edges of colors i and j is a 4-cycle; abstract polytopes correspond to maniplexes satisfying the (strong) path-intersection property. A polytope (or maniplex) Q is a cover of P if there is a rank- and adjacency-preserving surjection of flags from Q to P. A polytope is called regular if its automorphism group acts transitively on flags, and chiral if it has two orbits of flags under automorphisms with adjacent flags lying in different orbits.

A known "quotient criterion" in the regular and chiral settings states that, under suitable assumptions on the facets, a regular (respectively chiral) cover of a regular (respectively chiral) polytope is itself polytopal, i.e. satisfies the intersection property. 

Problem. Formulate and prove a purely combinatorial criterion, applicable to arbitrary abstract polytopes or maniplexes (not assumed to be regular or chiral), which serves the same role as the quotient criterion: namely, given a cover Q -> P of polytopes (or maniplexes), provide combinatorial conditions under which the polytopality (intersection property) of P, together with hypotheses on the facets, guarantees polytopality of Q.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a paper providing a general combinatorial analogue of the quotient criterion for arbitrary polytopes or maniplexes. Related work on symmetry type graphs and k-orbit polytopes/maniplexes exists, but none of the results found directly resolves the problem as stated.

original_question: Either find an abstract polytope P whose monodromy group Mon(P) is not a string C-group but which nevertheless has a unique minimal regular polytopal cover, or prove that no such polytope exists.
self_contained_problem:
Background. An abstract polytope $P$ of rank $n$ is a poset (with a maximum and minimum element) satisfying the standard axioms: every flag has length $n+2$; $P$ is strongly flag-connected; and the diamond condition holds, i.e., for every $(i-1)$-face $F$ and every $(i+1)$-face $G$ with $F<G$, there are exactly two $i$-faces $H$ with $F<H<G$. For each $i\in\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ and each flag $\Phi$, there is a unique flag $\Phi^i$ that differs from $\Phi$ only in its $i$-face. The monodromy group $\mathrm{Mon}(P)$ is the subgroup of the symmetric group on the set of flags generated by the involutions $r_0,r_1,\dots,r_{n-1}$, where $r_i$ sends each flag $\Phi$ to $\Phi^i$. A string C-group of rank $n$ is a group generated by involutions $\rho_0,\dots,\rho_{n-1}$ satisfying the string property $(\rho_i\rho_j)^2=1$ whenever $|i-j|\ge 2$ together with the intersection condition $\langle \rho_i:i\in I\rangle\cap\langle\rho_i:i\in J\rangle=\langle\rho_i:i\in I\cap J\rangle$ for all $I,J\subseteq\{0,\dots,n-1\}$. An abstract polytope $R$ is regular if its automorphism group acts transitively on its flags; equivalently, regular polytopes correspond to string C-groups. A regular polytopal cover of $P$ is a regular abstract polytope $R$ together with a rank- and adjacency-preserving surjection $R\to P$. A minimal regular polytopal cover of $P$ is such a cover that does not factor nontrivially through another regular cover; $P$ has a unique minimal regular polytopal cover when (up to isomorphism) there is exactly one such minimal cover.

Problem. Either exhibit an abstract polytope $P$ such that $\mathrm{Mon}(P)$ is not a string C-group while $P$ nevertheless has a unique minimal regular polytopal cover, or prove that no such abstract polytope exists.
status_search_result: Searches turn up the general framework (monodromy groups of polyhedra are automatically string C-groups, while in rank ≥ 4 minimal regular covers need not be unique, as illustrated by the Tomotope), but no published resolution of the specific question of whether a polytope with non–string-C-group monodromy can still admit a unique minimal regular cover. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems on k-orbit polytopes
original_question: For k-orbit polytopes with k ≥ 3, define the right analogue of the chirality group: a group-theoretic invariant that measures how far the polytope is from being regular and behaves well despite the fact that different flag stabilizers may have different normalizers.
self_contained_problem:
Background. An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set $\mathcal{P}$ (with a minimum and a maximum element) whose elements (called faces) are ranked from $-1$ to $n$, every maximal chain (called a flag) contains exactly one face of each rank, $\mathcal{P}$ is strongly flag-connected, and the diamond condition holds: for any two faces $F<G$ of ranks differing by $2$ there are exactly two faces $H$ with $F<H<G$. The diamond condition implies that for each flag $\Phi$ and each $i\in\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ there is a unique flag $\Phi^i$ differing from $\Phi$ only in its rank-$i$ face. The automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts freely on flags; $\mathcal{P}$ is called a $k$-orbit polytope when this action has exactly $k$ orbits. The polytope is regular iff $k=1$, in which case $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ is generated by involutions $\rho_0,\dots,\rho_{n-1}$ subject to a string Coxeter-type presentation. For a $2$-orbit chiral polytope, the chirality group is defined as follows: let $W$ be the abstract string $C$-group with the regular presentation, and let $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ be presented as a quotient of the orientation-preserving subgroup $W^+\le W$ by a normal subgroup $M\trianglelefteq W^+$; the chirality group is then $X(\mathcal{P})=M/(M\cap M^*)$, where $M^*$ is the conjugate of $M$ by any reflection in $W\setminus W^+$. It is trivial iff $\mathcal{P}$ is regular.

Problem. For each integer $k\ge 3$, define a group-theoretic invariant $X(\mathcal{P})$ (a generalized chirality, or irregularity, group) of a $k$-orbit abstract polytope $\mathcal{P}$ such that: (i) $X(\mathcal{P})$ is trivial if and only if $\mathcal{P}$ is regular; (ii) when $k=2$ and $\mathcal{P}$ is chiral, $X(\mathcal{P})$ recovers the classical chirality group $M/(M\cap M^*)$; (iii) the construction is intrinsic and does not depend on the choice of base flag, despite the fact that stabilizers in $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ of flags in different orbits need not be conjugate and may have non-conjugate normalizers; (iv) $X(\mathcal{P})$ quantifies how far $\mathcal{P}$ is from being regular and behaves functorially with respect to covers and quotients of $k$-orbit polytopes. Construct such an invariant and establish its basic properties.
status_search_result: The question is listed among open problems on $k$-orbit abstract polytopes. Subsequent literature on $k$-orbit polytopes characterizes their automorphism groups via symmetry type graphs but does not appear to provide a generally accepted "correct" generalization of the chirality group to $k$-orbit polytopes for $k\ge 3$. The problem appears to remain open.

An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P with a strictly monotone rank function having range {-1, 0, ..., n}, with a unique minimum face F_{-1} and unique maximum face F_n, such that every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly n+2 faces, P is strongly flag-connected, and the diamond condition holds: whenever F < G with rank(G) − rank(F) = 2, there are exactly two faces H with F < H < G. A maniplex of rank n is a combinatorial generalization of a polytope: it is an n-edge-colored connected graph whose vertices represent flags and whose i-colored edges represent the i-adjacency, satisfying the same local conditions as the flag graph of a polytope, but without requiring the existence of an underlying poset. Every abstract polytope gives rise to a maniplex via its flag graph, but not every maniplex arises this way.

A rooted polytope (resp. rooted maniplex) is a pair (P, Φ) where P is an abstract polytope (resp. maniplex) and Φ is a distinguished base flag of P. For each i, let r_i denote the involution that sends a flag to its i-adjacent flag. The monodromy group Mon(P) is the group generated by r_0, ..., r_{n−1} acting on the flags of P.

Consider the subgroup of Mon(P_1) × Mon(P_2) generated by the diagonal elements (r_i^{P_1}, r_i^{P_2}) for i = 0, ..., n−1. The flags of the mix are the orbits of the base flag pair (Φ_1, Φ_2) under this group, with i-adjacency given by the diagonal generators. original_question: Develop a theory of realizations of regular polytopes in hyperbolic spaces.
self_contained_problem:
An abstract regular polytope is a partially ordered set $P$ with a strictly monotone rank function, having a least and greatest face, satisfying the diamond condition and strong flag-connectedness, and whose automorphism group acts transitively on the set of maximal flags. For abstract regular polytopes in finite rank, McMullen developed a theory of (Euclidean) realizations: a realization is a mapping $\beta$ from the vertex set of $P$ into a Euclidean space $E$ such that the automorphism group of $P$ induces, via $\beta$, a representation by isometries of $E$ extending to an action on the resulting geometric figure. The full set of realizations of a finite regular polytope forms a convex cone, the realization cone, decomposing as a direct (Minkowski) sum of irreducible "pure" realizations indexed by the irreducible orthogonal representations of the automorphism group; an analogous, more delicate theory exists for infinite (Euclidean apeirotope) realizations.

Develop an analogous, systematic theory of realizations of abstract regular polytopes in hyperbolic spaces $\mathbb{H}^n$ (and possibly in other non-Euclidean spaces of constant curvature). In particular, define an appropriate notion of a hyperbolic realization of an abstract regular polytope $P$ as a map from the vertex set of $P$ into $\mathbb{H}^n$ that is compatible (in a suitable sense) with the action of the automorphism group of $P$ by hyperbolic isometries; identify the analogue of pure/irreducible realizations; describe the structure of the space of all hyperbolic realizations of a given regular polytope (e.g., is there an analogue of the realization cone, of the direct sum decomposition, and of the classification by irreducible representations?); and characterize which abstract regular polytopes admit faithful discrete realizations in hyperbolic spaces, recovering the classical hyperbolic regular tessellations and honeycombs as special cases.
status_search_result: A general theory of realizations of abstract regular polytopes in Euclidean space (McMullen) is well established, and individual hyperbolic regular tessellations/honeycombs are classically understood via hyperbolic Coxeter groups. However, no published systematic analogue of McMullen's realization theory in hyperbolic spaces appears to have been developed; recent surveys on symmetry of polytopes and on regular hypertopes continue to treat the hyperbolic setting only piecewise, suggesting the problem remains open.
