original_question: Is the singular Bohr-Sommerfeld formal power series in hbar a spectral invariant? There are various later refinements and extensions of Conjectur e 7.5 [188, 190, 198], following other inverse spectral questions in semiclassical analysis (see for instan ce [234, 115, 118]) which concern integrable systems (or even collections of commuting operators) m ore general than semitoric, and even in higher dimensions. All of them essentially make the same general cla im: "from the semiclassical joint spectrum of a quantum integrable system one can detect the principal symbols of the system". A more concrete problem is:
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a connected symplectic 4-manifold and let $(F_1,F_2):M\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a semitoric integrable system, meaning that $F_1,F_2$ Poisson-commute, the flow of $F_1$ generates an effective $S^1$-action with proper momentum map, and all singularities of $F=(F_1,F_2)$ are non-degenerate with no hyperbolic blocks. Assume $F$ has a focus-focus singular fiber. Consider a semiclassical quantization of $F$: a pair $(P_1(\hbar),P_2(\hbar))$ of commuting self-adjoint semiclassical (pseudodifferential or Berezin–Toeplitz) operators depending on a small parameter $\hbar\in(0,\hbar_0]$, with respective principal symbols $F_1,F_2$. Near the focus-focus critical value, the joint spectrum $\mathrm{JointSpec}(P_1(\hbar),P_2(\hbar))\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ admits a description by singular Bohr–Sommerfeld quantization rules expressible as a formal power series in $\hbar$ (with $\log\hbar$ terms) whose coefficients are smooth functions on a punctured neighborhood of the critical value; call this series the singular Bohr–Sommerfeld series associated to the focus-focus point.
 
Question: Is the singular Bohr–Sommerfeld formal power series in $\hbar$ a spectral invariant? Equivalently, is it determined—term by term and uniquely—by the joint semiclassical spectrum $\mathrm{JointSpec}(P_1(\hbar),P_2(\hbar))$ as $\hbar\to 0^+$, in the sense that any two such quantizations with the same joint spectrum (modulo $O(\hbar^\infty)$) produce the same singular Bohr–Sommerfeld series?
category_tag: semiclassical analysis of semitoric integrable systems
status_search_result: Subsequent work on the inverse spectral problem for quantum semitoric systems (notably Le Floch–Pelayo, arXiv:2104.06704) recovers all symplectic invariants of a semitoric system from the semiclassical joint spectrum and shows semitoric systems are spectrally determined algorithmically; related works confirm that the Taylor-series invariant at focus-focus points can be read off the spectrum. This effectively answers the underlying inverse-spectral claim affirmatively in the semitoric case, but the precise statement that the singular Bohr–Sommerfeld formal power series itself is a spectral invariant (and its extensions beyond semitoric and to higher dimensions) has not been settled in full generality.

original_question: Can one detect from the joint spectrum of a quantum integrabl e system T1,hbar,..., Tn,hbar that a singularity is degenerate? The theory of semitoric systems provides a strong motivation for u nderstanding the connections be- tween integrable systems and Hamiltonian torus actions. In view of t his, we conclude by discussing a possible quantum approach to counting fixed points of symplectic S1-actions. In view of Tolman's recent work constructing a non-Hamiltonian symp lectic S1-action on a compact manifold with isolated fixed points, the questions how many fixed point s symplectic actions have (both upper and lower bounds) and what the relation between having fixed points and being Hamiltonian 38 is, have attracted much interest [214, 92, 184, 93]. See also Pelayo [180] for a discussion and other references. As far as we know, the "quantised" version of this pr oblem is not well understood, although some steps have been taken in this direction [148]. The object to qua ntise can no longer be the momentum map, since there is no momentum map - however, McDuff po inted out in [164] that any symplectic S1-action admits an S1-valued momentum map mu: M → S1. The explicit construction of this map appears in [182], and it can be quantised [148, Section 7] (her e the operator will be unitary, rather than self-adjoint).
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact connected symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, and let $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be a completely integrable system, i.e. smooth functions whose Poisson brackets satisfy $\{f_i,f_j\}=0$ and whose differentials are almost everywhere linearly independent. A point $p\in M$ is a singularity of $F$ if $\mathrm{rank}\,dF(p)<n$; such a singularity is called non-degenerate if, in suitable symplectic coordinates, the Hessians of $f_1,\dots,f_n$ span a Cartan subalgebra of $\mathfrak{sp}(2n,\mathbb{R})$, and is called degenerate otherwise.

A semiclassical quantization of $F$ is a family of commuting self-adjoint operators $T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar}$ (depending on $\hbar\in(0,\hbar_0]$) acting on Hilbert spaces $\mathcal{H}_\hbar$, whose principal symbols are $f_1,\dots,f_n$ and which satisfy the standard axioms of semiclassical pseudodifferential or Berezin–Toeplitz quantization. The joint spectrum $\mathrm{JointSpec}(T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar})$ is the set of tuples $(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ such that there exists a nonzero common eigenvector $v\in\mathcal{H}_\hbar$ with $T_{j,\hbar}v=\lambda_j v$ for all $j$.

Problem: Given the joint spectrum $\mathrm{JointSpec}(T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar})$ as $\hbar\to 0$, devise a procedure (or prove the existence of one) that determines whether the underlying classical integrable system $F$ has a degenerate singularity. Equivalently, can the property "$F$ has a degenerate critical point" be read off from the asymptotic structure of the joint spectrum?
category_tag: Inverse spectral theory of integrable systems
status_search_result: Recent work (Le Floch–Pelayo and collaborators) on inverse spectral theory for semitoric and Jaynes–Cummings-type quantum integrable systems has produced algorithmic procedures to recover symplectic invariants near non-degenerate (focus-focus) singularities from the joint spectrum, but no general result detecting degeneracy of singularities from the joint spectrum for arbitrary quantum integrable systems has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: What are necessary and/or sufficient conditions on a metric g such that every polynomial integral of its geodesic flow is quantisable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian (or pseudo-Riemannian) manifold, and let $H:T^*M\to\mathbb{R}$ be the geodesic Hamiltonian $H(x,p)=\tfrac12 g^{ij}(x)p_ip_j$ generating the geodesic flow on $T^*M$. A function $F:T^*M\to\mathbb{R}$ that is polynomial in the fiber variables $p$ is called a polynomial integral of the geodesic flow if $\{H,F\}=0$ with respect to the canonical Poisson bracket on $T^*M$; equivalently, the coefficients of $F$ in $p$ form a Killing tensor on $(M,g)$.

A polynomial integral $F=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}F^{\alpha}(x)p_\alpha$ is said to be quantisable if there exists a differential operator $\widehat F$ on $M$ (acting on, say, half-densities or functions, of order equal to the degree of $F$, with principal symbol $F$) that commutes with the Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta_g$ of $(M,g)$, i.e.\ $[\Delta_g,\widehat F]=0$.

Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on the metric $g$ that ensure every polynomial integral of its geodesic flow is quantisable in the above sense.
status_search_result: Recent literature (2024–2025) on polynomial integrals of geodesic flows continues to develop existence/classification of Killing tensors and local high-degree polynomial integrals, but no general necessary-and-sufficient condition on a metric guaranteeing quantisability of every polynomial integral has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact symplectic $2n$-manifold equipped with a completely integrable system $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n)\colon M\to\mathbb{R}^n$, i.e. the components $f_i$ Poisson-commute with respect to $\omega$ and are functionally independent on a dense open set. Assume that the singularities of $F$ are non-degenerate in the sense of Williamson, so that every singular point admits local symplectic coordinates in which $F$ is, up to an analytic equivalence, a sum of components of regular ($\partial/\partial\theta_i$), elliptic ($x_i^2+y_i^2$), hyperbolic ($x_iy_i$), and focus-focus ($x_iy_{i+1}-x_{i+1}y_i,\ x_iy_i+x_{i+1}y_{i+1}$) type.

Suppose $(M,\omega)$ carries a prequantum line bundle $(L,\nabla)$ with curvature $\omega$, and let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the real polarization tangent to the fibers of $F$. The geometric quantization of $(M,\omega,L,\mathcal{P})$ is defined as the sheaf cohomology
$$\mathcal{Q}(M,\mathcal{P}) = \bigoplus_{k\ge 0} H^k(M,\mathcal{J}),$$
where $\mathcal{J}$ is the sheaf of sections of $L$ that are flat along $\mathcal{P}$. For polarizations whose only singularities are of regular and non-degenerate elliptic type, a sheaf-theoretic scheme (a Čech-type computation localized at Bohr–Sommerfeld leaves) yields a finite-dimensional quantization space concentrated in a single degree.

Problem. Modify this sheaf-theoretic quantization scheme so as to produce a finite-dimensional representation space $\mathcal{Q}(M,\mathcal{P})$ in the presence of focus-focus and hyperbolic singularities, in such a way that the resulting invariants still encode the symplectic semi-local invariants of those singularities (e.g.\ the Vũ Ngọc Taylor series for focus-focus, and the affine-length / Dufour–Molino–Toulet invariants for hyperbolic singularities) and, more generally, the symplectic invariants of the underlying integrable system.
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Miranda, Presas and Solha (arXiv:1705.06572) and the cotangent-model approach of Miranda and collaborators (e.g. arXiv:2102.02699) provided modifications yielding finite-dimensional quantization spaces in the presence of focus-focus and certain hyperbolic singularities for semitoric and almost-toric systems, cancelling the infinite-dimensional contributions seen in earlier schemes. A complete scheme capturing all symplectic invariants of these singularities in full generality does not yet appear in the literature, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

paper_title: Open problems
original_question: Let f: S → B be a non-isotrivial fibred surface, let ω_f be its relative canonical bundle, let χ_f = deg f_*ω_f, let K_f^2 = c_1^2(ω_f), and let q_f be the relative irregularity coming from the Fujita decomposition of f_*ω_f. The slope is the ratio K_f^2/χ_f. Prove sharper lower bounds for the slope, building on the techniques cited in the source, and determine whether one can strengthen the known bounds as the relative irregularity increases.
self_contained_problem:
Let $f\colon S\to B$ be a non-isotrivial fibration from a smooth complex projective surface $S$ onto a smooth complex projective curve $B$, with connected fibers of genus $g\ge 2$, and assume $f$ is relatively minimal. Let $\omega_f=\omega_S\otimes f^*\omega_B^{-1}$ be the relative canonical bundle, and define
$$\chi_f=\deg f_*\omega_f,\qquad K_f^2=c_1(\omega_f)^2.$$
By the Fujita decomposition, $f_*\omega_f=\mathcal{U}\oplus\mathcal{A}$, where $\mathcal{U}$ is a unitary flat bundle and $\mathcal{A}$ is an ample vector bundle; let $q_f$ denote the relative irregularity of $f$ (equivalently, $q(S)-g(B)$, with $\mathcal{U}$ contributing the unitary rank). The slope of $f$ is
$$\lambda(f)=\frac{K_f^2}{\chi_f}.$$
The classical Cornalba–Harris–Xiao bound asserts $\lambda(f)\ge 4(g-1)/g$.

Problem: Establish sharper lower bounds for $\lambda(f)$ that improve the classical bound as the relative irregularity $q_f$ grows. In particular, decide whether one can prove
$$\lambda(f)\ge \frac{4(g-1)}{g-q_f}$$
for relatively minimal non-isotrivial fibrations under appropriate hypotheses, and identify the largest range of $q_f$ (relative to $g$) for which such a bound holds.
status_search_result: The Barja–Stoppino slope conjecture $\lambda(f)\ge 4(g-1)/(g-q_f)$ has been partially resolved: Lu and Zuo (Ann. Sc. Norm. Super. Pisa, 2019) proved it when $q_f$ is small compared to $g$, and constructed counterexamples when $g$ is odd and $q_f=(g+1)/2$, showing the bound cannot hold in full generality. Sharper slope inequalities involving the unitary rank and Clifford index were obtained by Riva (Proc. LMS, 2022) and further refined in subsequent work (Sci. China Math., 2024). So the broad program of sharpening slope bounds in terms of $q_f$ is actively progressing but not fully closed.

paper_title: Open problems
original_question: Construct a polarised surface (X, L) whose Seshadri constant at a very general point is irrational, or prove that the Seshadri constant on a surface is always rational.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective surface and let $L$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. For a point $x \in X$, the Seshadri constant of $L$ at $x$ is defined by
$$\varepsilon(X,L;x) \;=\; \inf_{C \ni x} \frac{L \cdot C}{\mathrm{mult}_x C},$$
where the infimum runs over all irreducible curves $C \subset X$ passing through $x$. The Seshadri constant of $L$ at a very general point is the value $\varepsilon(X,L) := \varepsilon(X,L;x)$ for $x$ in the complement of a countable union of proper Zariski-closed subsets of $X$ (this common value exists).

Either:
(a) exhibit an explicit polarised smooth complex projective surface $(X,L)$ with $L$ ample such that $\varepsilon(X,L)$ at a very general point is an irrational real number; or
(b) prove that for every polarised smooth complex projective surface $(X,L)$, the Seshadri constant $\varepsilon(X,L)$ at a very general point is a rational number.
status_search_result: The rationality of Seshadri constants on surfaces at a very general point is a well-known long-standing open problem. All explicitly computed Seshadri constants to date are rational, but no unconditional example of irrationality is known. Recent works (e.g., on blow-ups of ruled surfaces and of P^2) establish rationality in special cases or produce irrational examples only conditionally on conjectures such as a strengthened SHGH conjecture. No unconditional resolution has been published as of 2026.

paper_title: Open problems
original_question: Let C be a smooth projective curve of gonality k and genus g. Say that C satisfies the linear growth condition when dim W^1_{k+n}(C) ≤ n for every integer n with 0 ≤ n ≤ g - 2k + 2. Under this definition, study Conjecture (9.1): a smooth projective curve C of gonality k and genus g satisfies the linear growth condition as soon as dim W^1_k(C) = 0.
self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over the complex numbers of genus $g$ and gonality $k$, i.e., $k$ is the minimal degree of a non-constant morphism $C \to \mathbb{P}^1$. For an integer $d \geq 0$, let
$$W^1_d(C) = \{\, L \in \mathrm{Pic}^d(C) : h^0(C,L) \geq 2 \,\}$$
denote the Brill–Noether locus parametrizing line bundles of degree $d$ on $C$ admitting at least a pencil of sections.

Say that $C$ satisfies the linear growth condition if
$$\dim W^1_{k+n}(C) \leq n \quad \text{for every integer } n \text{ with } 0 \leq n \leq g - 2k + 2.$$

Prove or disprove: every smooth projective curve $C$ of gonality $k$ and genus $g$ such that $\dim W^1_k(C) = 0$ satisfies the linear growth condition.
status_search_result: The linear growth condition was introduced by Aprodu in connection with Green's conjecture, and the implication "dim W^1_k(C) = 0 ⇒ linear growth" is a conjectural strengthening used to deduce Green's conjecture in several settings (e.g., curves on K3 surfaces, general k-gonal curves). original_question: Study the ELMS conjecture on exceptional curves, in the setting described in the source.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{X}$ be an exceptional curve in the sense of Lenzing–Kussin, i.e. a noncommutative smooth projective curve of genus zero over a field $k$: a small connected hereditary $k$-linear abelian category $\mathcal{H} = \mathrm{coh}(\mathbb{X})$ that contains a tilting object, that has Serre duality, and whose objects decompose into a "line bundle" part and a torsion part formed of tubes. The "ELMS conjecture" on exceptional curves asserts a precise structural prediction about $\mathbb{X}$ (for instance, on the classification, function field invariants, or representation-theoretic invariants of exceptional curves of a given type). Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^4_{\mathbb{C}}$ be a very general smooth hypersurface of degree $d\ge 6$ (so that $X$ is a smooth projective threefold of general type whose canonical bundle is ample). Let $f\colon X\dashrightarrow Y$ be a dominant rational map onto a smooth projective threefold $Y$.

\begin{itemize}
\item $Y$ is rational, or
\item $f$ is birational (so $Y$ is birational to $X$)?

original_question: Classify the configurations of d^2 points in P^3, for d ≥ 3, such that for every general linear projection from a point x ∈ P^3, the projected configuration of d^2 points in P^2 is the complete intersection of two degree-d plane curves.

Let $d \geq 3$ be an integer. A finite set $Z \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ (over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero) is called $(d,d)$-geproci if for a general point $x \in \mathbb{P}^3$ the image of $Z$ under linear projection $\pi_x : \mathbb{P}^3 \dashrightarrow \mathbb{P}^2$ from $x$ is the complete intersection of two plane curves of degree $d$. Classify all configurations $Z \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ of $|Z| = d^2$ points such that for every general linear projection from a point $x \in \mathbb{P}^3$, the resulting configuration of $d^2$ points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ is the complete intersection of two plane curves of degree $d$. Equivalently, describe all $(d,d)$-geproci sets of $d^2$ points in $\mathbb{P}^3$ for $d \geq 3$.

context_brief: Largest dimension of a linear q-ary code
original_question: For fixed code length n, minimum distance d, and finite field F_q, determine k[n, d], the largest integer k ≤ n for which there exists a linear code C contained in F_q^n with dimension k and minimum Hamming weight d.
self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a prime power and let $\mathbb{F}_q$ denote the finite field with $q$ elements. For a vector $x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)\in\mathbb{F}_q^n$, its Hamming weight is $\mathrm{wt}(x)=|\{i:x_i\neq 0\}|$. A linear $[n,k,d]_q$-code is a $k$-dimensional linear subspace $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ whose minimum Hamming weight $\min\{\mathrm{wt}(c):c\in C,\ c\neq 0\}$ equals $d$.

For fixed positive integers $n$ and $d$ with $1\le d\le n$ and a fixed prime power $q$, define
$$k[n,d] := \max\{k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} : \text{there exists a linear code } C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n \text{ with } \dim_{\mathbb{F}_q} C=k \text{ and minimum weight } d\}.$$

paper_title: Open Problems in Coding Theory
context_brief: Complexity of core coding optimization problems
original_question: What is the computational complexity of determining A(n, d), A(n, d, w), k[n, d], and the analogous optimization problems for permutation codes described in the paper?
self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer n and integer d with 1 ≤ d ≤ n, let A(n, d) denote the maximum size of a binary code of length n with minimum Hamming distance at least d, i.e., the largest cardinality of a subset C ⊆ {0,1}^n such that any two distinct codewords differ in at least d coordinates. For an integer w with 0 ≤ w ≤ n, let A(n, d, w) denote the maximum size of a binary constant-weight code of length n, minimum Hamming distance at least d, with every codeword having Hamming weight exactly w. For positive integers n and d, let k[n, d] denote the maximum dimension k of a binary linear code of length n with minimum distance at least d (so that 2^{k[n,d]} is the largest size of a linear code attaining these parameters). For the permutation analogue, equip the symmetric group S_n with the Hamming metric d_H(σ, τ) = |{i : σ(i) ≠ τ(i)}|, and let M(n, d) denote the maximum size of a subset Γ ⊆ S_n such that d_H(σ, τ) ≥ d for all distinct σ, τ ∈ Γ.

The input to each problem is the parameters (n, d), (n, d, w), or (n, d), encoded in binary (so the input size is logarithmic in n). Determine the computational complexity of each of the following decision/optimization problems:
(i) Given (n, d, N), decide whether A(n, d) ≥ N (equivalently, compute A(n, d)).
(ii) Given (n, d, w, N), decide whether A(n, d, w) ≥ N (equivalently, compute A(n, d, w)).
(iii) Given (n, d, k), decide whether k[n, d] ≥ k (equivalently, compute k[n, d]).
(iv) Given (n, d, N), decide whether M(n, d) ≥ N, and the analogous constant-weight and linear-style problems for permutation codes.

In particular, determine whether each of these problems is in P, NP-complete, coNP-hard, or otherwise classify them within the standard complexity hierarchy.
status_search_result: No source was found establishing the computational complexity of computing A(n,d), A(n,d,w), k[n,d], or their permutation-code analogues. While related problems such as minimum-distance decoding and computing the minimum distance of a linear/stabilizer code are known to be NP-hard, the complexity of these maximum-size code-parameter problems (with parameters given in binary) appears to remain unresolved in the literature.

paper_title: Open Problems in Coding Theory
context_brief: Broadest algebraic setting for duality and MacWilliams relations
original_question: Determine the largest class of algebraic structures A for which one can define a duality theory for codes together with MacWilliams relations.
self_contained_problem:
Let A denote a finite algebraic structure (for example, a finite group, ring, module, or more general finite algebraic object) and, for each positive integer n, equip A^n with a notion of "code" (a distinguished family of substructures C ⊆ A^n) and a notion of "dual code" C^⊥ ⊆ A^n. Assume each code C carries a Hamming weight enumerator W_C(x,y) = Σ_{c∈C} x^{n−wt(c)} y^{wt(c)}, where wt(c) is the number of nonzero coordinates of c. One says that a "duality theory with MacWilliams relations" exists for A if there is an involutive duality operation C ↦ C^⊥ on codes in A^n (for every n) together with an identity of the form
   W_{C^⊥}(x,y) = (1/|C|) · W_C(x + (q−1)y, x − y)
or, more generally, W_{C^⊥}(x,y) = (1/|C|) · W_C(T(x,y)) for some fixed linear transformation T depending only on A, that holds for every code C ⊆ A^n and every n ≥ 1.

It is classically known that such a duality theory with MacWilliams relations exists when A is a finite field, a finite abelian group (with additive codes), or a finite Frobenius ring (with left/right linear codes).

Problem. Determine the largest class of finite algebraic structures A for which a duality theory together with MacWilliams relations (in the sense above) can be defined.
status_search_result: The question of finding the largest class of algebraic structures admitting a MacWilliams duality remains open. Frobenius rings are currently the broadest well-established class for which such a duality theory works for linear codes, and finite abelian groups work for additive codes. Negative results (e.g., no MacWilliams duality holds in general for nonabelian groups) have ruled out certain extensions, but no complete characterization of the maximal class is known.

paper_title: Open Problems in Coding Theory
context_brief: Classification of MDS and MDR codes
original_question: Classify all maximum-distance-separable codes, meaning codes that meet the Singleton bound d ≤ n − k + 1, and all maximum-distance-with-respect-to-rank linear codes over principal ideal rings, meaning codes that meet the analogous bound d(C) ≤ n − k + 1 where k is the rank of the code, across the classes of alphabets considered in the paper.
self_contained_problem:
Let A be an alphabet, which is either a finite set of size |A| ≥ 2 or a finite (commutative) principal ideal ring R. A code of length n over A is a subset C ⊆ A^n; when A = R is a ring, a linear code C is an R-submodule of R^n, and its rank is the smallest cardinality of a generating set of C as an R-module. The Hamming distance between x, y ∈ A^n is d(x, y) = |{i : x_i ≠ y_i}|, and the minimum distance of C is d(C) = min{d(x, y) : x, y ∈ C, x ≠ y}.

Set k = log_{|A|}|C| when A is a finite alphabet, and let k be the rank of C when C is a linear code over a finite principal ideal ring. Then in both settings one has the Singleton-type bound d(C) ≤ n − k + 1. Codes attaining this bound are called Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) in the alphabet case, and Maximum Distance with respect to Rank (MDR) in the linear-over-PIR case.

Problem. Classify (give existence parameters and, up to suitable equivalence, an enumeration of) all MDS codes over finite alphabets and all MDR linear codes over finite principal ideal rings. Concretely, determine the complete set of admissible parameters (n, k, d = n − k + 1) and, for each admissible parameter triple, describe all such codes up to monomial/module-equivalence, across the classes of alphabets and principal ideal rings under consideration (in particular finite fields, Galois rings, finite chain rings, and general finite principal ideal rings).
category_tag: MDS and MDR codes over rings
status_search_result: A full classification remains open. Even over finite fields, the MDS conjecture (the main classification question for MDS codes) is unresolved in general, despite Ball's proof for prime fields. Over finite chain rings, Galois rings, and principal ideal rings, partial existence results, constructions of infinite families (including self-dual MDS/MDR codes), and necessary/sufficient existence conditions are known, but no complete classification across all these alphabet classes is available.

paper_title: Open Problems in Coding Theory
context_brief: Existence of the putative [72,36,16] Type II code
original_question: Does there exist a binary Type II self-dual code with parameters [72, 36, 16], where Type II means that the code is self-dual and every codeword weight is divisible by 4?
self_contained_problem:
A binary linear code of length n is a linear subspace C ⊆ F_2^n. The Hamming weight of a codeword is the number of its nonzero coordinates, and the minimum distance d(C) is the minimum Hamming weight among nonzero codewords. The dual code is C^⊥ = { x ∈ F_2^n : x·c = 0 for all c ∈ C }, where x·c is the standard inner product modulo 2. A code C is self-dual if C = C^⊥, which forces dim C = n/2. A binary self-dual code is called Type II (doubly even) if the Hamming weight of every codeword is divisible by 4; this requires n ≡ 0 (mod 8). For a Type II code of length n, the minimum distance satisfies d ≤ 4⌊n/24⌋ + 4, and a code attaining this bound is called extremal.

Question: Does there exist a binary Type II self-dual code with parameters [72, 36, 16] (i.e., length 72, dimension 36, and minimum distance 16, with all codeword weights divisible by 4)?
status_search_result: The existence of an extremal Type II [72,36,16] binary self-dual code, posed by Sloane in 1973, is a long-standing open problem in coding theory. Substantial partial results restrict the possible automorphism group of such a code (e.g., it cannot contain S_3, A_4, D_8, or an elementary abelian group of order 8; its order must be 5 or a divisor of 24), but as of recent surveys the existence question itself remains unresolved.

paper_title: Open Problems in Coding Theory
context_brief: Existence pattern for extremal doubly-even self-dual binary codes
original_question: For which positive integers k does there exist a doubly-even self-dual binary code with parameters [24k, 12k, 4k + 4]?
self_contained_problem:
A binary linear code of length $n$ is a linear subspace $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$. Its dual is $C^\perp = \{x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n : x\cdot c = 0 \text{ for all } c \in C\}$ with respect to the standard inner product. The code $C$ is self-dual if $C = C^\perp$, and doubly even if the Hamming weight of every codeword is divisible by 4. The minimum distance $d(C)$ is the minimum Hamming weight of a nonzero codeword. For a doubly even self-dual binary code of length $n = 24k$, the Mallows–Sloane bound gives $d(C) \le 4\lfloor n/24 \rfloor + 4 = 4k+4$; a code attaining this bound is called extremal.

Determine the set of positive integers $k$ for which there exists a doubly even self-dual binary code with parameters $[24k,\,12k,\,4k+4]$.
status_search_result: The problem is widely regarded as open. Existence is classically known for $k=1$ (the extended Golay code, $[24,12,8]$) and $k=2$ (the extended quadratic residue code of length 48, $[48,24,12]$). For $k=3$ the existence of a $[72,36,16]$ extremal doubly even self-dual code is a famous long-standing open problem. Non-existence is known for all sufficiently large $k$ (Zhang and subsequent refinements). For most intermediate values of $k$ no extremal code is known nor ruled out.

paper_title: Open Problems in Coding Theory
context_brief: Unimodality of the secrecy ratio of a unimodular lattice
original_question: If L is a unimodular lattice, prove that its secrecy ratio r_L(y) = θ_(Z^n)(y) / θ_L(y) is unimodal for y ≥ 0 and attains its maximum at y = 1.
self_contained_problem:
For a full-rank lattice $L\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, define its theta series by
\[ \theta_L(y) \;=\; \sum_{x\in L} q^{\,x\cdot x}, \qquad q = e^{-\pi y}, \quad y>0, \]
where $x\cdot x$ denotes the standard Euclidean inner product. For the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^n$, set $\theta_{\mathbb{Z}^n}(y)=\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^n} q^{x\cdot x}$. A lattice $L\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is called unimodular if it equals its dual $L^*=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n : v\cdot x\in\mathbb{Z}\ \forall x\in L\}$. For a unimodular lattice $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, define the secrecy ratio
\[ r_L(y) \;=\; \frac{\theta_{\mathbb{Z}^n}(y)}{\theta_L(y)}, \qquad y\geq 0. \]
Prove that for every unimodular lattice $L$, the function $y\mapsto r_L(y)$ is unimodal on $[0,\infty)$ and attains its maximum at $y=1$.
category_tag: Theta series of unimodular lattices (Belfiore–Solé conjecture)
status_search_result: This is the Belfiore–Solé secrecy-function conjecture. It has been verified for many specific families (e.g., all known extremal even unimodular lattices in dimensions less than 80, and unimodular lattices from Type II codes of length up to 40), but it remains open in general for unimodular lattices. Generalizations to $\ell$-modular and isodual/formally unimodular lattices have been disproved by explicit counterexamples, while the original unimodular case has neither been proved nor refuted.

context_brief: Existence of a Type I [56,28,12] code
original_question: Does there exist a Type I self-dual code with parameters [56, 28, 12]?
self_contained_problem:
A binary linear code of length $n$ is a linear subspace $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$. The dual code $C^\perp$ is the set of vectors orthogonal to all codewords of $C$ under the standard inner product. The code $C$ is called self-dual if $C = C^\perp$; this forces $\dim C = n/2$. A binary self-dual code is said to be Type II (doubly even) if the Hamming weight of every codeword is divisible by 4, and Type I (singly even) otherwise. The minimum distance of $C$ is the smallest Hamming weight of a nonzero codeword. A self-dual binary code with parameters $[n,k,d]$ has length $n$, dimension $k=n/2$, and minimum distance $d$.

Question: Does there exist a Type I (singly-even) binary self-dual code with parameters $[56, 28, 12]$?

paper_title: Open Problems in Coding Theory
original_question: Find an efficient decoding algorithm for an infinite family of self-dual codes, or ideally for all self-dual codes.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field and let $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a linear code of length $n$ and dimension $k$. The dual code is $C^\perp = \{ x \in \mathbb{F}_q^n : \langle x, c \rangle = 0 \text{ for all } c \in C \}$, where $\langle x, c \rangle = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i c_i$. The code $C$ is called self-dual if $C = C^\perp$ (which forces $n = 2k$). Given a received word $y = c + e \in \mathbb{F}_q^n$, where $c \in C$ and $e$ is an error vector of Hamming weight at most $\lfloor (d-1)/2 \rfloor$ (with $d$ the minimum distance of $C$), the decoding problem asks to recover $c$ from $y$.

Exhibit an infinite family $\{C_n\}$ of self-dual codes (with $n \to \infty$) together with a decoding algorithm running in time polynomial in $n$ that corrects up to $\lfloor (d_n-1)/2 \rfloor$ errors for every $C_n$ in the family. More ambitiously, produce such a polynomial-time decoding algorithm that works for all self-dual codes (given a generator matrix as input).
status_search_result: No general efficient decoding algorithm for self-dual codes is known. Efficient decoders exist only for sporadic specific codes (e.g., the binary Golay [24,12,8], several Type II [32,16,8] codes, the [48,24,12] code, and certain extremal [40,20,8] codes) or for restricted classes such as self-dual codes admitting an automorphism of odd order. The general problem, posed by Huffman–Pless and reiterated as Open Question 10.1 in the cited problem list, remains open.

paper_title: Open Problems in Coding Theory
original_question: Close the gap between the Varshamov-Gilbert existence bound and the linear-programming upper bound for codes.
self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $n$ and $d$ with $1 \le d \le n$, let $A_2(n,d)$ denote the maximum number of codewords in a binary code $C \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ such that any two distinct codewords differ in at least $d$ coordinates. Define the asymptotic rate function
$$R(\delta) \;=\; \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{\log_2 A_2(n, \lfloor \delta n \rfloor)}{n}, \qquad \delta \in (0, 1/2).$$
Two classical bounds on $R(\delta)$ are:

1. The Gilbert–Varshamov (existence) lower bound:
$$R(\delta) \;\ge\; 1 - H_2(\delta), \qquad H_2(x) = -x \log_2 x - (1-x)\log_2(1-x).$$

2. The linear programming (LP) upper bound: any function $\beta : \{0,1,\dots,n\} \to \mathbb{R}$ that arises as the Hamming-weight enumerator of a code of minimum distance $d$ must satisfy the MacWilliams inequalities, and optimizing over all such functions yields an upper bound $R_{\mathrm{LP}}(\delta)$ on $R(\delta)$. Explicit asymptotic forms (e.g. the McEliece–Rodemich–Rumsey–Welch bound) give
$$R(\delta) \;\le\; H_2\!\left( \tfrac{1}{2} - \sqrt{\delta(1-\delta)} \right).$$

For every $\delta \in (0, 1/2)$, there is a strict gap between the GV lower bound and the LP upper bound. Determine $R(\delta)$ for $\delta \in (0,1/2)$, or more generally close the gap between the Gilbert–Varshamov lower bound and the linear-programming upper bound on $R(\delta)$.
status_search_result: Determining the true asymptotic rate function $R(\delta)$ for binary codes — equivalently closing the gap between the Gilbert–Varshamov lower bound and the linear-programming (MRRW) upper bound — is widely recognized as a longstanding central open problem in coding theory. Known improvements (e.g. Tsfasman–Vlăduț–Zink for $q \ge 49$ and Jiang–Vardy's asymptotic improvement of GV for linear codes) refine the bounds but do not close the gap, and it remains open whether GV is asymptotically tight in the binary case.

paper_title: Open Problems in Coding Theory
original_question: Is there a BCH-type bound for cyclic codes over Z4?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{Z}_4 = \mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$ denote the ring of integers modulo $4$. A cyclic code of length $n$ over $\mathbb{Z}_4$ is a $\mathbb{Z}_4$-submodule $C \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_4^n$ closed under the cyclic shift $(c_0, c_1, \dots, c_{n-1}) \mapsto (c_{n-1}, c_0, \dots, c_{n-2})$. Equivalently, $C$ corresponds to an ideal of $\mathbb{Z}_4[x]/(x^n-1)$. The Lee weight on $\mathbb{Z}_4$ is defined by $w_L(0)=0,\, w_L(1)=w_L(3)=1,\, w_L(2)=2$, extended additively to $\mathbb{Z}_4^n$, and the Lee (or Hamming) distance of $C$ is the minimum Lee (or Hamming) weight of a nonzero codeword. 

Recall the classical BCH bound for cyclic codes over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ (with $\gcd(n,q)=1$): if the defining set of $C$ contains $\delta-1$ consecutive powers of a primitive $n$-th root of unity, then the minimum Hamming distance of $C$ is at least $\delta$.

Problem: Establish a BCH-type lower bound on the minimum (Hamming or Lee) distance of an arbitrary cyclic code over $\mathbb{Z}_4$, expressed in terms of structural data (such as a defining set with respect to Galois extensions of $\mathbb{Z}_4$, or zeros of the generator polynomial) analogous to the classical BCH bound over finite fields.
status_search_result: Searches for a BCH-type bound specifically for cyclic codes over $\mathbb{Z}_4$ did not return a definitive, widely accepted general analogue. Various partial results and bounds for $\mathbb{Z}_4$-cyclic codes exist in the literature (e.g., generator structure $(fh, 2fg)$, Hensel lifting, related Hartmann–Tzeng-type bounds), but no canonical solution to the general question was identified. Status appears unresolved/unknown from accessible sources.

paper_title: Open Problems in Coding Theory
context_brief: Classification of perfect nonlinear one-error-correcting codes
original_question: Classify all perfect nonlinear single-error-correcting codes.
self_contained_problem:
A binary code of length $n$ is a subset $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$. The Hamming distance $d(x,y)$ between two vectors is the number of coordinates in which they differ. A code $C$ is called a perfect single-error-correcting code (a perfect 1-error-correcting code) if the closed Hamming balls of radius $1$ centered at the codewords partition $\mathbb{F}_2^n$; equivalently, $|C| = 2^n/(n+1)$ (so $n = 2^m - 1$ for some integer $m \ge 2$) and every vector of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ lies within Hamming distance $1$ of exactly one codeword. The code $C$ is called linear if it is an $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and nonlinear otherwise. Two codes are considered equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a permutation of coordinates together with a translation by a fixed vector.

Problem: Provide a complete classification, up to equivalence, of all perfect nonlinear single-error-correcting binary codes (of every admissible length $n = 2^m - 1$).
status_search_result: The complete classification of perfect nonlinear single-error-correcting (binary Hamming-length) codes remains open. While linear perfect codes are completely classified (repetition, Hamming, binary/ternary Golay codes), the number of inequivalent nonlinear perfect 1-error-correcting codes grows extremely rapidly with length, and current research treats only partial invariants such as rank, kernel dimension, and connections to Steiner triple systems and tilings. Surveys of perfect codes describe full classification as an open problem.

original_question: Does there exist an asymptotically good family of cyclic binary linear codes, meaning a sequence of codes [n_i, k_i, d_i] for which both lim inf_i→∞ k_i/n_i > 0 and lim inf_i→∞ d_i/n_i > 0 hold?
self_contained_problem:
A binary linear code of length $n$, dimension $k$, and minimum Hamming distance $d$ is denoted $[n,k,d]$. Such a code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is called cyclic if $(c_0, c_1, \dots, c_{n-1}) \in C$ implies $(c_{n-1}, c_0, \dots, c_{n-2}) \in C$. A sequence of binary linear codes $C_i$ with parameters $[n_i, k_i, d_i]$ (with $n_i \to \infty$) is called asymptotically good if
$$\liminf_{i \to \infty} \frac{k_i}{n_i} > 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \liminf_{i \to \infty} \frac{d_i}{n_i} > 0.$$
Question: Does there exist an asymptotically good sequence of binary cyclic linear codes?
status_search_result: The question of whether binary cyclic codes are asymptotically good is a well-known long-standing open problem (over 50 years old). Partial and related results exist: quasi-cyclic codes (index >1) are known to be asymptotically good, certain additive cyclic codes and $\mathbb{Z}_2\mathbb{Z}_4$-additive cyclic codes have been shown asymptotically good, and long BCH codes are known asymptotically bad. The original problem for (ordinary) binary cyclic codes remains unresolved.

context_brief: When a virtually self-dual weight enumerator comes from an actual self-dual code
original_question: Given a virtually self-dual weight enumerator F, determine necessary and sufficient conditions, short of brute-force enumeration, for F to occur as the weight enumerator of some self-dual code C.
self_contained_problem:
Let q be a prime power and let F(x,y) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree n in two variables with non-negative integer coefficients, written
  F(x,y) = sum_{i=0}^{n} A_i x^{n-i} y^i,
with A_0 = 1. Call F a virtual weight enumerator over GF(q) if its coefficients are non-negative integers and A_0 = 1. Call F a virtually self-dual weight enumerator over GF(q) if, in addition, F is invariant under the MacWilliams transform at q, i.e.
  F(x,y) = q^{-n/2} F(x + (q-1) y,\ x - y).
A linear code C ⊆ GF(q)^n is self-dual if C = C^⊥ with respect to the standard inner product, and its Hamming weight enumerator is W_C(x,y) = sum_{c∈C} x^{n - wt(c)} y^{wt(c)}.

The literature provides constructions of self-dual codes with prescribed weight enumerators and various non-existence results (e.g., restrictions on enumerators of singly-even self-dual codes), but no general necessary-and-sufficient criterion, short of enumeration, is known. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: In the setting where G is a connected semisimple Lie group, Γ is an irreducible lattice in G, A is a closed subgroup of a split Cartan subgroup D of G with dim A > 1, and A is not contained in a wall of a Weyl chamber of D, is every C^1-small perturbation of the action of A on G/Γ C^∞-conjugate to an action of A defined by a continuous homomorphism from A to D?
self_contained_problem: Let $G$ be a connected semisimple Lie group, let $\Gamma \subset G$ be an irreducible lattice, and let $D \subset G$ be a split Cartan subgroup. Let $A \subset D$ be a closed subgroup with $\dim A \ge 2$ which is not contained in any wall of a Weyl chamber of $D$. Consider the action $\alpha_0$ of $A$ on the homogeneous space $G/\Gamma$ by left translations. Prove or disprove the following: every $C^1$-small perturbation $\alpha$ of $\alpha_0$ (in the space of $C^\infty$ actions of $A$ on $G/\Gamma$) is $C^\infty$-conjugate to an action of $A$ on $G/\Gamma$ of the form $a \mapsto L_{\rho(a)}$, where $\rho \colon A \to D$ is a continuous homomorphism and $L_g$ denotes left translation by $g$.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
context_brief: Global rigidity of irreducible higher-rank Anosov actions
original_question: Is every irreducible Anosov action of Z^k or R^k, with k ≥ 2, C^∞-conjugate to an algebraic action?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k \geq 2$ and let $G$ be either $\mathbb{Z}^k$ or $\mathbb{R}^k$. A smooth action $\alpha : G \times M \to M$ on a closed smooth manifold $M$ is called Anosov if there exists an element $g_0 \in G$ such that the diffeomorphism $\alpha(g_0, \cdot)$ is Anosov (i.e., the tangent bundle $TM$ admits a continuous $D\alpha(g_0,\cdot)$-invariant splitting $TM = E^s \oplus E^u$ on which $D\alpha(g_0,\cdot)$ is uniformly contracting and expanding, respectively). 

An algebraic action is one of the following: $M = K \backslash H / \Gamma$ where $H$ is a connected Lie group, $\Gamma \subset H$ is a cocompact lattice, $K$ is a compact subgroup of $H$ commuting with the action, and $G$ acts via a homomorphism into $H$ acting by left translations; or more generally an action on an infranilmanifold by affine automorphisms.

The action $\alpha$ is called irreducible if it does not have non-trivial rank-one factors (equivalently, no finite cover of the action splits as a product in which one factor is an action of a rank-one subgroup of $G$), and every finite-index subaction is topologically transitive.

Question: Is every irreducible Anosov action of $\mathbb{Z}^k$ or $\mathbb{R}^k$ with $k \geq 2$ on a closed manifold $C^\infty$-conjugate to an algebraic action?

status_search_result: This is the Katok–Spatzier global rigidity conjecture. It remains open in full generality, but substantial partial results are known: Kalinin–Spatzier and Kalinin–Sadovskaya proved versions under conformality/algebraic assumptions on coarse Lyapunov foliations, and Rodriguez Hertz–Wang established strong global rigidity for higher-rank Anosov $\mathbb{Z}^k$-actions on tori/nilmanifolds assuming only one Anosov element with suitable linearization. A general proof for arbitrary closed manifolds is not available.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
original_question: Do measure-rigidity results for higher-rank abelian group actions produce obstructions to smooth or continuous irreducible actions of a higher-rank abelian group on a compact manifold?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a higher-rank abelian group (for instance $\mathbb{Z}^k$ or $\mathbb{R}^k$ with $k \ge 2$), and let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold. Call an action of $A$ on $M$ irreducible if it does not factor (in an appropriate sense) through an action of a rank-one subgroup or split nontrivially as a product of lower-dimensional actions. Recent measure-rigidity theorems classify the invariant probability measures for various classes of higher-rank abelian actions (e.g., positive-entropy invariant measures for $\mathbb{Z}^k$-actions by toral automorphisms, and related results in homogeneous and hyperbolic settings).

Question: Do these measure-rigidity results for higher-rank abelian group actions yield obstructions to the existence of smooth, or merely continuous, irreducible actions of a higher-rank abelian group on a compact manifold? More precisely, can one use such measure-rigidity theorems to rule out the existence of irreducible smooth (respectively continuous) $A$-actions on certain compact manifolds $M$, or to constrain the topology/geometry of $M$ when such an action exists?

status_search_result: The question, posed as an open problem at a workshop on emerging applications of measure rigidity, remains an active research direction. While significant progress has been made on measure rigidity, cocycle rigidity, and Zimmer-program-style obstructions for lattice actions (e.g., Brown–Fisher–Hurtado), no definitive answer providing general obstructions to smooth or continuous irreducible higher-rank abelian actions on compact manifolds via measure rigidity appears in the literature. The status is best described as open with partial progress.

original_question: For an algebraic Anosov action of R^k or Z^k, k ≥ 2, on a biquotient M of a connected Lie group G, and for an ergodic probability Borel measure μ on M, must either μ be a finite sum of measures constructed from Haar measures on closed subgroups of G, or must supp μ fiber equivariantly over a manifold N on which the action reduces to rank one?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected Lie group and let $M$ be a biquotient of $G$, i.e. $M = A\backslash G / B$ where $A,B$ are closed subgroups of $G$ acting freely and properly on $G$ by left and right translations respectively. An action of $\mathbb{R}^k$ or $\mathbb{Z}^k$ on $M$ is called algebraic if it is induced (via the biquotient construction) by translations of $G$ coming from a homomorphism into $G$. Such an action is called Anosov if some element of $\mathbb{R}^k$ (resp. $\mathbb{Z}^k$) acts as an Anosov diffeomorphism/flow on $M$. Assume $k \ge 2$, and let $\mu$ be an ergodic invariant Borel probability measure on $M$ for the action.

(i) $\mu$ is a finite sum (convex combination) of measures each of which is constructed from a Haar measure supported on a closed subgroup of $G$ (i.e., $\mu$ is "algebraic").
(ii) The support of $\mu$ fibers equivariantly over a manifold $N$ in such a way that the induced action on $N$ reduces to a rank-one action (i.e., factors through a homomorphism $\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{Z}^k\to\mathbb{Z}$).

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
original_question: Can the measure-rigidity results for unipotent flows be extended to the adelic setting?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a global field (for instance $\mathbb{Q}$) and let $\mathbb{A}$ denote its ring of adeles. Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected semisimple algebraic group defined over $K$, and consider the adelic homogeneous space $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A})/\mathbf{G}(K)$. For each place $v$ of $K$, let $U_v \subset \mathbf{G}(K_v)$ be a subgroup generated by one-parameter unipotent subgroups, and let $U$ be a subgroup of $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A})$ that is a product (restricted with respect to compact open unipotent subgroups at non-archimedean places) of such groups $U_v$.

Establish an adelic analogue of Ratner's measure-classification theorem in this setting: prove that every $U$-invariant ergodic probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A})/\mathbf{G}(K)$ is the homogeneous (algebraic) measure supported on a closed orbit $H x$, where $H$ is a closed subgroup of $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A})$ containing $U$ such that $Hx$ carries an $H$-invariant probability measure. Equivalently, extend the orbit-closure and equidistribution conclusions for unipotent flows from the real Lie group setting to the adelic homogeneous space $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A})/\mathbf{G}(K)$.

The linearization technique was likewise adapted to this context by Tomanov and by Gorodnik–Oh. These S-arithmetic/adelic measure-rigidity results are now standard tools in the area, so the problem as posed is regarded as solved.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
context_brief: Horospherical Radon measures in rank one
original_question: For a noncompact semisimple Lie group G of rank one, a discrete subgroup Γ of G, and a horospherical subgroup U of G, what are the U-ergodic Radon measures on G/Γ? In particular, are they all either carried by closed U-orbits or obtained from the harmonic-function construction?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a noncompact semisimple real Lie group of real rank one, let $\Gamma \subset G$ be a discrete subgroup (not assumed to be a lattice), and let $U \subset G$ be a horospherical subgroup (i.e., the unipotent radical of a minimal parabolic subgroup of $G$). Consider the right action of $U$ on the homogeneous space $G/\Gamma$, which preserves the class of locally finite Borel (Radon) measures. A $U$-invariant Radon measure $\mu$ on $G/\Gamma$ is called $U$-ergodic if every $U$-invariant Borel set has either zero or locally full $\mu$-measure. Two natural families of such measures are known:

(a) measures supported on a single closed $U$-orbit in $G/\Gamma$ (giving the Haar measure on that orbit), and

(b) measures produced by the harmonic-function construction: starting from a positive $\Gamma$-invariant eigenfunction (a harmonic function with respect to a suitable Laplacian, equivalently a $\Gamma$-conformal density on the boundary of the symmetric space of $G$), one builds an associated $U$-invariant Radon measure on $G/\Gamma$ via the Burger–Roblin / Babillot–Ledrappier construction.

Classify all $U$-ergodic Radon measures on $G/\Gamma$. In particular, determine whether every such measure is either supported on a closed $U$-orbit or arises from the harmonic-function construction described in (b).
status_search_result: The problem has substantial partial progress. In rank one, Sarig proved the classification for horocycle flows on $\mathbb Z^d$-covers of compact hyperbolic surfaces, and Ledrappier–Sarig extended it to regular covers of finite-volume surfaces. Landesberg–Lindenstrauss-type results and work by Landesberg on geometrically infinite quotients (IMRN 2022) further classify horospherical Radon measures under suitable hypotheses (e.g., when the Bowen–Margulis–Sullivan measure is conservative). paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
context_brief: Invariant measures for large algebraic group actions
original_question: For either a large subgroup Γ of the automorphism group of a finite-volume nilmanifold, or a large subgroup Γ of a Lie group acting by translations on G/Λ where Λ is a lattice in G, are the only ergodic Γ-invariant probability measures those supported on finite Γ-orbits and Haar measure?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma$ be a group acting by measure-preserving transformations in one of the following two settings:

(1) $N$ is a connected, simply connected nilpotent Lie group, $\Lambda \subset N$ is a lattice (so that $N/\Lambda$ is a finite-volume nilmanifold), and $\Gamma$ is a "large" (for instance, Zariski dense in the real algebraic group $\mathrm{Aut}(N)$) subgroup of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(N/\Lambda)$ of the nilmanifold.

(2) $G$ is a Lie group, $\Lambda \subset G$ is a lattice, and $\Gamma$ is a "large" subgroup of $G$ (for instance, generating a Zariski dense subgroup with sufficient unipotent structure) acting on $G/\Lambda$ by left translations.

Prove or disprove: in either setting, every ergodic $\Gamma$-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ on the relevant homogeneous space is either
(a) supported on a finite $\Gamma$-orbit, or
(b) the normalized Haar (Lebesgue) measure on the whole space.
category_tag: Measure rigidity for group actions on homogeneous spaces
status_search_result: The conjecture (attributed to A. Furman) is a measure-rigidity statement that remains open in full generality. Significant partial results exist: for higher-rank abelian actions by toral/nilmanifold automorphisms there are classification theorems under additional hypotheses (positive entropy, TNS conditions, irreducibility) by Katok–Spatzier, Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss, and others; for translation actions, Ratner's theorems handle the case where Γ is generated by unipotents, and recent work of Eskin–Lindenstrauss and Benoist–Quint covers stationary measures under semisimplicity assumptions. Nevertheless, the general Zariski-dense automorphism case (without entropy assumptions) and many translation cases remain unresolved.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
original_question: Let G be a Lie group, Γ a lattice in G, U={u(t)} a one-parameter Ad-unipotent subgroup, and x∈G/Γ with dense Ux. Can one prove equidistribution in G/Γ of {u(t_n)x} when t_n is [n^α] for α>1, [P(n)] for a polynomial P, or the nth prime number?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected Lie group, $\Gamma \subset G$ a lattice, and $U = \{u(t) : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$ a one-parameter Ad-unipotent subgroup of $G$ (i.e., $\mathrm{Ad}(u(t))$ is a unipotent linear operator on the Lie algebra of $G$ for every $t$). By Ratner's theorem, for every $x \in G/\Gamma$ such that the orbit $Ux$ is dense in $G/\Gamma$, the continuous orbit $\{u(t)x : t \in [0,T]\}$ becomes equidistributed in $G/\Gamma$ (with respect to the $G$-invariant probability measure) as $T \to \infty$.

Prove (or disprove) that for every such $G$, $\Gamma$, $U$, and every $x \in G/\Gamma$ with $\overline{Ux} = G/\Gamma$, the discrete sparse orbit $\{u(t_n) x : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is equidistributed in $G/\Gamma$ when $t_n$ is any of the following sequences:
1. $t_n = \lfloor n^\alpha \rfloor$ for a fixed real $\alpha > 1$;
2. $t_n = \lfloor P(n) \rfloor$ for a fixed non-constant polynomial $P(x) \in \mathbb{R}[x]$;
3. $t_n = p_n$, the $n$-th prime number.

Here equidistribution means that for every $f \in C_c(G/\Gamma)$,
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(u(t_n)x) \;\longrightarrow\; \int_{G/\Gamma} f\, d\mu \quad \text{as } N \to \infty,$$
where $\mu$ is the $G$-invariant probability measure on $G/\Gamma$.
status_search_result: The problem (a question of Margulis) is known in several special cases but remains open in full generality. Partial results include: equidistribution along $\lfloor n^{1+\gamma}\rfloor$ for small $\gamma > 0$ and along primes in horocycle flows on $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\Gamma$ (Venkatesh; Sarnak–Ubis; Tanis–Vishe), and recent polynomial effective equidistribution results (Lindenstrauss–Mohammadi–Wang and others) that give some sparse equidistribution applications. Equidistribution for general one-parameter Ad-unipotent flows on arbitrary $G/\Gamma$ along $\lfloor n^\alpha\rfloor$ for all $\alpha > 1$, along arbitrary polynomial sequences, or along the primes is not established in general.

original_question: Let L be a Lie group, G a closed subgroup, Λ a lattice in L, a∈G semisimple with expanding horospherical subgroup U, x0∈L/Λ with dense Gx0, γ:[0,1]→U analytic, and ν the pushforward of Lebesgue measure under t↦γ(t)x0. What condition on γ ensures that a^nν converges to Haar measure λ on L/Λ as n→∞?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L$ be a Lie group, $G \le L$ a closed subgroup, and $\Lambda \le L$ a lattice. Let $a \in G$ be a semisimple element, and let 
$$U = \{u \in G : a^{-n} u a^{n} \to e \text{ as } n \to +\infty\}$$
be its expanding horospherical subgroup in $G$. Fix a point $x_0 \in L/\Lambda$ such that the orbit $G x_0$ is dense in $L/\Lambda$. Let $\gamma : [0,1] \to U$ be a real-analytic curve, and let $\nu$ be the pushforward of Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$ under the map $t \mapsto \gamma(t) x_0$. Let $\lambda$ denote the (normalized) Haar measure on $L/\Lambda$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the curve $\gamma$ under which the translated measures $a^n \nu$ converge in the weak-$*$ topology to $\lambda$ as $n \to \infty$.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: Shah established equidistribution for analytic curves not contained in any proper subgroup of $G^+$ in several settings, and the analyticity assumption has been weakened in subsequent work (e.g., by Shah–Yang and others). Recent works extend results to products of SO(n,1) factors and to non-analytic curves. The general question of giving necessary and sufficient conditions on $\gamma$ in arbitrary $L, G, a$ is not fully resolved.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
original_question: For a semisimple Lie group G acting on a real normed vector space V, a point p∈V with finite stabilizer, R_T={g∈G: ||gp||<T}, a lattice Γ in G, and μ_T the projection to G/Γ of normalized Haar measure on R_T, what is the limiting distribution of μ_T as T→∞?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected semisimple real Lie group equipped with a Haar measure, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space endowed with a norm $\|\cdot\|$. Suppose $G$ acts continuously and linearly on $V$, and let $p \in V$ be a point whose stabilizer $\{g \in G : gp = p\}$ is finite. For each $T > 0$, define the "representation ball"
$$R_T = \{ g \in G : \|gp\| < T \},$$
which has finite Haar measure (assume this), and let $\lambda_T$ be the normalized restriction of Haar measure to $R_T$ (a probability measure on $G$).

Let $\Gamma \subset G$ be a lattice, and let $\pi : G \to G/\Gamma$ be the natural projection. Define $\mu_T = \pi_* \lambda_T$, the pushforward probability measure on $G/\Gamma$.

Determine the weak-$*$ limit of $\mu_T$ on $G/\Gamma$ as $T \to \infty$: does the limit exist, and if so, identify it explicitly (e.g., as the $G$-invariant probability measure on $G/\Gamma$, or as a measure supported on a proper homogeneous subspace, in terms of $G$, $V$, the action, and $p$).
status_search_result: Equidistribution of such representation-ball averages has been established in many cases via work of Eskin–McMullen, Eskin–Mozes–Shah, Gorodnik–Oh, Gorodnik–Weiss and others, particularly when the orbit $Gp$ is affine symmetric or the stabilizer is reductive, yielding convergence to the Haar probability measure on $G/\Gamma$. A complete answer in the full generality stated (arbitrary linear representation with finite stabilizer) does not appear to be fully settled, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

context_brief: Discrete horocycle equidistribution at cusp scale
original_question: For a continuous function f on T^1(X) with the stated cusp growth condition, badly approximable α∈R, and 0<c1<c2, do the averages M^{-1}∑_{m=1}^M f(u_y(αm)) converge uniformly to the Liouville integral as M→∞ for c1M^{-2}≤y≤c2M^{-2}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H} = \{z = x+iy : y>0\}$ denote the upper half-plane with hyperbolic metric, on which $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ acts by Möbius transformations. Let $\Gamma = \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$, let $X = \Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}$ be the modular surface, and let $T^1(X)$ be its unit tangent bundle, identified with $\Gamma\backslash\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Let $\lambda$ denote the Liouville (Haar) probability measure on $T^1(X)$. For $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $y>0$, define the horocycle element
$$u_y(t) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & t \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} y^{1/2} & 0 \\ 0 & y^{-1/2} \end{pmatrix},$$
viewed as a point in $T^1(X)$ via the projection $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R}) \to \Gamma\backslash\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. A real number $\alpha$ is called badly approximable by rationals if there exists $c>0$ such that $|\alpha - p/q| \geq c/q^2$ for every $p/q \in \mathbb{Q}$. Fix constants $0 < c_1 < c_2$. Consider continuous functions $f : T^1(X) \to \mathbb{C}$ that satisfy a prescribed growth condition at the cusp ensuring all averages below are well defined (e.g., $|f(g)| \ll y(g)^{1-\delta}$ for some $\delta>0$, where $y(g)$ is the imaginary part of the base point of $g$).

Prove or disprove: for every such $f$ and every badly approximable $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$,
$$\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^M f\bigl(u_y(\alpha m)\bigr) \;\longrightarrow\; \int_{T^1(X)} f\, d\lambda$$
as $M \to \infty$, uniformly in $y$ with $c_1 M^{-2} \leq y \leq c_2 M^{-2}$.
status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open conjecture attributed to Marklof and Strömbergsson. Related results are known: Marklof–Strömbergsson (GAFA 2003) proved equidistribution of Kronecker sequences along closed horocycles for almost every α and y ≫ N^{-δ}, and subsequent works treat various scaling regimes, but the cusp-scale regime y ≍ M^{-2} for badly approximable α does not appear to be resolved. No reference confirming a complete proof was found.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
original_question: For compact flats F⊂Γ\G with Vol(F)<T and measures ν_T and barν_T formed by volume-weighted and normalized averages over those flats, do ν_T and barν_T converge to normalized Haar measure on Γ\G?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected semisimple real Lie group of real rank at least $2$, let $A\subset G$ be a maximal $\mathbb{R}$-split Cartan subgroup, and let $\Gamma\subset G$ be a torsion-free uniform lattice. A compact flat in $X:=\Gamma\backslash G$ is a closed orbit $F = \Gamma g A \subset X$ that is compact; each such $F$ carries a finite $A$-invariant Haar measure, and we denote by $\mathrm{Vol}(F)$ its volume and by $\mu_F$ the corresponding $A$-invariant probability measure supported on $F$.

For $T>0$, let $\mathcal{F}(T) := \{ F : F \text{ is a compact flat in } X \text{ with } \mathrm{Vol}(F) < T \}$, assumed finite for every $T$. Define the two families of finite Borel measures on $X$:
$$\nu_T := \sum_{F\in\mathcal{F}(T)} \mathrm{Vol}(F)\,\mu_F, \qquad \overline{\nu}_T := \frac{1}{\#\mathcal{F}(T)} \sum_{F\in\mathcal{F}(T)} \mu_F,$$
normalized so as to be probability measures (i.e.\ $\nu_T$ is divided by $\sum_{F\in\mathcal{F}(T)}\mathrm{Vol}(F)$).

Question: As $T\to\infty$, do $\nu_T$ and $\overline{\nu}_T$ converge in the weak-$*$ topology to the normalized $G$-invariant Haar probability measure $m_X$ on $X = \Gamma\backslash G$?
status_search_result: A direct resolution of this equidistribution question for averages over compact flats in higher-rank locally symmetric spaces does not appear in the literature; related work by Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss–Michel–Venkatesh and surveys by H. Oh treat partial cases (e.g., periodic torus orbits in arithmetic settings), but the general statement for both volume-weighted and uniform averages appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
original_question: Can one construct examples of cones D in a maximal R-split torus A with dim D≥3 that have no non-obvious divergent trajectories?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected semisimple real algebraic group defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, let $\Gamma \subset G$ be an arithmetic lattice, and assume $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb{Q}}(G) = \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb{R}}(G)$. Let $A \subset G$ be a maximal $\mathbb{R}$-split torus (which then contains a maximal $\mathbb{Q}$-split torus). A trajectory $\{a_t \cdot x : t \geq 0\}$ in $G/\Gamma$, generated by a one-parameter subsemigroup $\{a_t\}$ of $A$, is called divergent if for every compact $K \subset G/\Gamma$ there exists $T$ with $a_t \cdot x \notin K$ for all $t \geq T$. By a closed cone $D \subset A$ we mean a closed semigroup of the form $D = \{a \in T_0 : \chi_i(a) \geq 0,\ i=1,\dots,k\}$, where $T_0 \subset A$ is a closed connected subgroup and $\chi_1,\dots,\chi_k$ are characters of $T_0$. There is a finite, explicit list of algebraic mechanisms (coming from $\mathbb{Q}$-parabolic subgroups and $\mathbb{Q}$-characters) that produce divergent trajectories for the $D$-action on $G/\Gamma$; these are called obvious divergent trajectories. A divergent trajectory not arising from this list is called a non-obvious divergent trajectory.

Problem: Construct an example of a triple $(G,\Gamma,D)$ as above in which $\dim D \geq 3$ and the action of $D$ on $G/\Gamma$ admits no non-obvious divergent trajectories.
status_search_result: Recent work (Tamam, 2021–2022) classifies non-obvious divergent trajectories in rational rank two and provides existence results showing non-obvious divergent trajectories arise when the diagonalizable subgroup has small dimension relative to the $\mathbb{Q}$-rank. No explicit construction of cones $D$ with $\dim D \geq 3$ free of non-obvious divergent trajectories appears in the literature, and the question is posed as an open construction problem.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
context_brief: Symbolic coding for Weyl chamber flow
original_question: Can analogs of geometric coding and arithmetic coding be constructed for the Weyl chamber flow, equivalently the diagonal group action, on SL(n,R)/SL(n,Z)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ and consider the homogeneous space $X=\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{Z})$. Let $A\subset\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})$ denote the subgroup of positive diagonal matrices (a maximal $\mathbb{R}$-split Cartan subgroup), and consider the Weyl chamber flow, i.e. the action of $A$ on $X$ by left translations.

For $n=2$, the geodesic flow on $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ admits two classical symbolic codings of its closed orbits (equivalently, conjugacy classes of hyperbolic elements of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$):
(i) the "geometric coding," obtained from a Bowen–Series / boundary-expansion construction associated with a fundamental domain for the Fuchsian group, producing a subshift whose sequences record successive sides of the fundamental domain crossed by the geodesic; and
(ii) the "arithmetic coding," obtained from Gauss's reduction theory of indefinite binary quadratic forms and the minus (or plus) continued fraction expansion, producing a sofic/Markov coding intrinsic to $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$.

Problem. Construct genuine analogs of the geometric coding and of the arithmetic coding for the Weyl chamber flow (the action of the full positive diagonal subgroup $A$) on $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{Z})$ for $n\ge 3$. That is, produce symbolic systems (with explicit alphabets and admissibility rules) together with coding maps that conjugate the $A$-action (or a suitable cross-section of it) to these symbolic systems, generalizing the geometric and arithmetic codings known in the rank-one case $n=2$.

status_search_result: The problem, posed by S. Katok, asks for higher-rank analogs of the geometric and arithmetic codings she developed (with Ugarcovici) for the geodesic flow on the modular surface. Searches turn up extensive literature on the rank-one case and on rigidity of Weyl chamber flows (Damjanović–Katok and others), but no construction of geometric/arithmetic symbolic codings for the diagonal action on $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{Z})$ for $n\ge 3$ appears in the available sources. The question seems to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
original_question: Can one find a triangle whose angles are Diophantine modulo 2π and whose billiard flow is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a triangle $T \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with interior angles $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3$ (satisfying $\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3=\pi$). The billiard flow on $T$ is the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of $T$, where a point particle moves in straight lines inside $T$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at the boundary. This flow preserves the Liouville measure (the product of Lebesgue measure on $T$ with the uniform measure on the unit circle of directions).

Call a real number $\theta$ Diophantine modulo $2\pi$ if there exist constants $C>0$ and $\tau \geq 0$ such that for every nonzero integer $q$ and every integer $p$,
$$\left| \frac{\theta}{2\pi} - \frac{p}{q} \right| \geq \frac{C}{|q|^{2+\tau}}.$$

Question: Does there exist a triangle whose three angles $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3$ are all Diophantine modulo $2\pi$ and whose billiard flow is ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure?
status_search_result: Ergodicity of polygonal billiards with Diophantine angles is regarded as one of the central open problems in the dynamics of polygonal billiards. While ergodicity is known to hold for a residual (dense $G_\delta$) set of polygons (Kerckhoff–Masur–Smillie, Zemlyakov–Katok), no explicit triangle—let alone one with Diophantine angles—has been shown to be ergodic, and no general approach is known. The problem appears still open as of recent surveys.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
original_question: Does the set of ergodic billiard tables have positive measure?
self_contained_problem:
Consider planar polygonal billiards: given a simple polygon $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, the billiard flow on $P$ is the geodesic flow of a point particle moving in straight lines inside $P$ and reflecting elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at the boundary. For an integer $n\geq 3$, let $T(n)$ denote the space of simple $n$-gons (parametrized, for example, by the $2n$ coordinates of their vertices, modulo rigid motions and scaling), equipped with a natural finite Lebesgue-type probability measure $\lambda$. Let $E(n)\subset T(n)$ be the subset consisting of those $n$-gons whose billiard flow is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure on the unit tangent bundle.

It is known that $E(n)$ is a residual (dense $G_\delta$) subset of $T(n)$. The question is:

Does $E(n)$ have positive measure, i.e. is $\lambda(E(n))>0$?
status_search_result: Surveys on billiard dynamics list Katok's question—whether the set of ergodic polygonal billiards has positive measure in the parameter space of polygons—as a well-known open problem. While generic (residual) ergodicity has been established for polygonal billiards, no measure-theoretic version has been proved or disproved, and the question remains open as of recent surveys.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
original_question: Let G be the direct product of k≥2 copies of SL(2,R), let U+ and U− be the upper and lower unipotent subgroups, and let Γ+ and Γ− be irreducible lattices in U+ and U−. If the group generated by Γ+ and Γ− is discrete, is it an arithmetic lattice in G?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k \geq 2$ be an integer and let $G = \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})^k$. Let 
$$U^+ = \left\{\begin{pmatrix} 1 & * \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\right\}^k \subset G, \qquad U^- = \left\{\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ * & 1 \end{pmatrix}\right\}^k \subset G$$
be the subgroups of upper-triangular and lower-triangular unipotent elements, both isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^k$. A lattice $\Lambda$ in $U^\pm \cong \mathbb{R}^k$ is called irreducible if it is not contained in any proper sum of coordinate subspaces (equivalently, no finite-index subgroup of $\Lambda$ splits as a product of lattices in coordinate subgroups). Let $\Gamma^+$ be an irreducible lattice in $U^+$ and $\Gamma^-$ an irreducible lattice in $U^-$.

Assume that the subgroup $\langle \Gamma^+, \Gamma^- \rangle$ of $G$ generated by $\Gamma^+ \cup \Gamma^-$ is discrete. Prove or disprove: $\langle \Gamma^+, \Gamma^- \rangle$ is an arithmetic lattice in $G$.
category_tag: Arithmeticity of lattices in Lie groups
status_search_result: A theorem of Benoist and Miquel ("Arithmeticity of discrete subgroups containing horospherical lattices", Duke Math. J. 2020) establishes that in a semisimple real algebraic Lie group of real rank at least 2, any discrete Zariski-dense subgroup containing an irreducible lattice of a horospherical (unipotent) subgroup is an arithmetic lattice. This includes the case $G = \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})^k$ with $k \geq 2$ and resolves the Margulis–Selberg conjecture in the stated form.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
context_brief: Hausdorff dimension of v-approximable points on manifolds
original_question: Using dynamics, can one estimate the Hausdorff dimension of v-approximable vectors lying in a nondegenerate submanifold of R^n?
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers n ≥ 2 and d with 1 ≤ d < n. A smooth submanifold M ⊂ ℝⁿ of dimension d is called nondegenerate at a point x ∈ M if, in some (equivalently any) smooth parameterization f: U → M with f(u₀) = x (U ⊂ ℝᵈ open), the partial derivatives of f of order up to some finite k span ℝⁿ. The manifold M is called nondegenerate if it is nondegenerate at almost every point.

Let v = (v₁, …, vₙ) be an n-tuple of positive real numbers with v₁ + ⋯ + vₙ = 1. A vector y = (y₁, …, yₙ) ∈ ℝⁿ is called v-approximable if there exist infinitely many q ∈ ℕ such that
    max₁≤i≤n ‖qyᵢ‖^{1/vᵢ} < 1/q,
where ‖·‖ denotes the distance to the nearest integer. Denote by W(v) the set of v-approximable vectors in ℝⁿ.

Develop a method, based on the dynamics of one-parameter diagonal flows on the homogeneous space SL_{n+1}(ℝ)/SL_{n+1}(ℤ) and the correspondence between Diophantine approximation and excursions of lattice orbits into the cusp, that yields estimates (upper and/or lower bounds) for the Hausdorff dimension of W(v) ∩ M for an arbitrary nondegenerate submanifold M of ℝⁿ.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made via dynamics and other techniques: Beresnevich (2017) and Beresnevich–Vaughan–Velani–Yang established lower bounds for Hausdorff dimension of (weighted) approximable points on nondegenerate manifolds; complementary upper-bound results exist for curves and analytic manifolds. However, sharp two-sided dimension estimates for v-approximable vectors on general nondegenerate submanifolds, obtained purely via dynamics, remain incomplete, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
original_question: For every pair of real numbers α and β, is liminf_{q→∞} q⟨qα⟩⟨qβ⟩ equal to 0, where ⟨x⟩ denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer?
self_contained_problem:
For a real number $x$, let $\langle x\rangle := \min_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} |x-n|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. Determine whether, for every pair of real numbers $\alpha,\beta \in \mathbb{R}$,
$$\liminf_{q\to\infty}\; q\,\langle q\alpha\rangle\,\langle q\beta\rangle \;=\; 0,$$
where the limit inferior is taken over positive integers $q$.
status_search_result: The statement is the classical Littlewood conjecture (circa 1930), which remains open in general. The strongest known partial result is due to Einsiedler, Katok, and Lindenstrauss (Annals of Math., 2006), which shows that the set of exceptional pairs $(\alpha,\beta)$ for which the equality fails has Hausdorff dimension zero. No proof or disproof of the full conjecture is known.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
context_brief: Finiteness of closed diagonal orbits in compact sets
original_question: For every compact set K in SL(3,R)/SL(3,Z), are there only finitely many closed A-orbits contained in K, where A is the full diagonal group in SL(3,R)?
self_contained_problem: Let $G=\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$, let $\Gamma=\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{Z})$, and consider the homogeneous space $X=G/\Gamma$ equipped with the quotient topology. Let $A\subset G$ denote the full diagonal subgroup, i.e. the subgroup of diagonal matrices with positive entries and determinant $1$ (a connected abelian subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^2$). For a point $x\in X$, the orbit $Ax\subset X$ is called closed if it is a closed subset of $X$. Prove or disprove the following statement: for every compact subset $K\subset X$, there are only finitely many closed $A$-orbits in $X$ that are entirely contained in $K$.
status_search_result: This is a well-known conjecture of Margulis about closed orbits of the full diagonal Cartan subgroup on SL(3,R)/SL(3,Z). It remains open: it is discussed in surveys of open problems in homogeneous dynamics and is closely tied to Littlewood's conjecture and to rigidity of higher-rank diagonal actions. Partial results (e.g., on bounded orbits, exceptional orbits via Schmidt games, and nonhomogeneous orbit closures) exist but do not resolve the finiteness statement.

paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
original_question: For any s,t∈[0,1], is the intersection C_s∩C_t nonempty, where C_s consists of pairs (α,β) with inf_{q≥1} max{q^s⟨qα⟩, q^{1−s}⟨qβ⟩}>0?
self_contained_problem:
For each s ∈ [0,1], let C_s denote the set of pairs (α, β) ∈ ℝ² such that
  inf_{q ≥ 1} max{ q^s ⟨qα⟩,  q^{1−s} ⟨qβ⟩ } > 0,
where ⟨x⟩ denotes the distance from a real number x to the nearest integer, and the infimum is taken over positive integers q. Prove or disprove: for every s, t ∈ [0,1], the intersection C_s ∩ C_t is nonempty.
status_search_result: Schmidt's intersection conjecture for the weighted badly approximable sets Bad(s, 1−s) was resolved affirmatively by Badziahin, Pollington and Velani (Annals of Mathematics, 2011), who proved that any finite intersection of such sets is nonempty and indeed has full Hausdorff dimension. Subsequent work extended this to countable intersections with appropriate restrictions on the weights.
