paper_title: The Hidden Subgroup Problem - Review and Open Problems
original_question: For which finite groups can the information-theoretic ability to distinguish hidden subgroups with only polynomially many oracle queries be converted into a full polynomial-time quantum algorithm that actually outputs subgroup generators, rather than requiring exponential classical postprocessing?
self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $G$ be a finite group and let $f : G \to S$ be a function on $G$ taking values in some finite set $S$. We say that $f$ hides a subgroup $H \le G$ if $f$ is constant on each left coset of $H$ and takes distinct values on distinct cosets. The Hidden Subgroup Problem (HSP) for $G$ is: given oracle access to such an $f$, output a set of generators for the hidden subgroup $H$.

It is known (Ettinger–Høyer–Knill) that for every finite group $G$, only $\mathrm{poly}(\log|G|)$ quantum queries to the oracle suffice to determine $H$ information-theoretically: the resulting quantum state (or measurement statistics) contains enough information to identify $H$ uniquely. However, the only general procedure known for extracting generators of $H$ from this information uses classical postprocessing time exponential in $\log|G|$.

Problem. Characterize the families of finite groups $G$ for which the information-theoretic identifiability of $H$ from polynomially many quantum oracle queries can be upgraded to a fully efficient (i.e. $\mathrm{poly}(\log|G|)$-time) quantum algorithm that outputs generators of the hidden subgroup $H$. In particular, determine for which classes of nonabelian groups such a polynomial-time quantum algorithm exists, and identify obstructions for the remaining classes.
status_search_result: The general nonabelian Hidden Subgroup Problem remains open. Polynomial-time quantum algorithms are known only for special classes such as abelian groups, normal hidden subgroups, nil-2 groups, extraspecial groups, and certain semidirect products. No general efficient procedure for converting the information-theoretic identifiability (Ettinger–Høyer–Knill) into polynomial-time generator extraction is known, and important cases such as the symmetric and dihedral groups (linked to graph isomorphism and lattice problems respectively) remain unresolved as of 2026.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Bell inequalities for finite correlation experiments
original_question: In a Bell-type correlation experiment with N subsystems, M measurement choices per subsystem, and K outcomes per measurement, characterize exactly the measured probability tables that admit a classical local realistic joint probability distribution over all NM observables. Equivalently, describe the convex polyhedron generated by all classical configurations in terms of linear Bell inequalities; for tractable cases, find complete solutions for small triples (N, M, K), efficient methods for generating genuinely new inequalities, infinite or symmetry-restricted families, full-correlation-function versions, correlation inequalities for K = 2, and the margins by which such inequalities can be violated by quantum states, possibly under constraints such as fixed Hilbert-space dimension, symmetry, or positive partial transposes.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a Bell-type correlation experiment with the following setup. There are $N$ spatially separated subsystems. On each subsystem, an experimenter freely chooses one of $M$ possible measurements, and each measurement yields one of $K$ possible outcomes. A run of the experiment produces, for each choice of one measurement setting per subsystem (an element of $\{1,\dots,M\}^N$), an empirical joint probability distribution over the $K^N$ outcome tuples. Call the collection of all such conditional distributions a "behavior" or probability table.

A behavior is said to admit a local realistic (classical) model if there exists a single joint probability distribution over the values of all $NM$ observables (one for each (subsystem, setting) pair, each taking values in $\{1,\dots,K\}$) whose marginals reproduce the measured conditional distributions for every choice of one setting per subsystem.

The set of local realistic behaviors forms a convex polytope $\mathcal{L}(N,M,K)$ in the appropriate Euclidean space of probability tables, whose vertices are the deterministic local assignments. Its facets are linear inequalities (Bell inequalities).

Problems:
1. (Complete characterization.) Determine the full list of facet-defining linear inequalities of $\mathcal{L}(N,M,K)$ for all triples $(N,M,K)$, or for as many small triples as possible beyond those currently known.
2. (Generation of new inequalities.) Develop efficient algorithmic or constructive methods to produce genuinely new (non-liftable, non-symmetry-equivalent) facet inequalities of $\mathcal{L}(N,M,K)$.
3. (Structured families.) Identify infinite families of facet inequalities, families invariant under prescribed symmetry groups (e.g.\ permutations of parties, settings, or outcomes), and the full-correlation-function inequalities involving only joint expectations of products of $\pm 1$-valued observables when $K=2$.
4. (Quantum violations.) For each such inequality, determine the maximal quantum violation, i.e.\ the supremum of its value over behaviors arising from quantum states and measurements, possibly under restrictions such as fixed Hilbert-space dimension, invariance under specified symmetry groups, or positive partial transpose across given bipartitions.
status_search_result: The complete facet enumeration of the local (Bell) polytope is a well-known computationally hard problem (facet enumeration on a polytope whose complexity grows roughly as $O((\exp N)^{\exp N})$). General characterization, efficient generation of new inequalities, and determination of maximal quantum violations under structural constraints remain active open research, with recent work focusing on sampling-based, symmetry-restricted, and permutationally invariant techniques.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For bipartite quantum states, call two density operators equally entangled when they differ only by local choices of basis, meaning there are local unitaries UA and UB with rho = (UA tensor UB) sigma (UA tensor UB)*. A polynomial entanglement invariant is a real-valued local-unitary invariant polynomial in the matrix elements of the density operator. Are polynomial entanglement invariants complete, so that if all polynomial invariants of rho and sigma agree, rho and sigma must be related by such local unitaries?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\mathcal{H}_B$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, and consider density operators on $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$, i.e. positive semidefinite operators of trace one. Two density operators $\rho$ and $\sigma$ on $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ are called locally unitarily equivalent if there exist unitary operators $U_A$ on $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $U_B$ on $\mathcal{H}_B$ such that
$$\rho = (U_A \otimes U_B)\, \sigma\, (U_A \otimes U_B)^*.$$
A polynomial entanglement invariant is a real-valued polynomial $p$ in the (real and imaginary parts of the) matrix entries of a density operator that is invariant under all local unitary transformations $(U_A \otimes U_B)\cdot(\,\cdot\,)\cdot(U_A \otimes U_B)^*$.

Question: Is the family of all polynomial entanglement invariants complete in the sense that, for any two density operators $\rho$ and $\sigma$ on $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$, the equality $p(\rho) = p(\sigma)$ for every polynomial entanglement invariant $p$ implies that $\rho$ and $\sigma$ are locally unitarily equivalent?
status_search_result: The completeness question is answered affirmatively by a classical theorem of Onishchik and Vinberg stating that orbits of a compact linear group on a real vector space are separated by polynomial invariants. Applied to the action of local unitaries on bipartite density operators, this yields completeness of the polynomial entanglement invariants. Concrete complete sets have also been worked out (e.g., Makhlin's 18 invariants for two qubits, and complete sets for arbitrary-dimensional bipartite states in subsequent work).

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For pure bipartite-state transformations under local quantum operations and classical communication, Nielsen’s majorization criterion decides when one state A can be converted to another state B. Because some conversions become possible only after tensoring both states with a suitable entangled catalyst C, give an efficient criterion for deciding when there exists a catalyst C such that A tensor C can be converted to B tensor C.
self_contained_problem:
Let $p = (p_1, \dots, p_n)$ and $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ be probability vectors with entries in non-increasing order. Recall that $p$ is majorized by $q$, written $p \prec q$, if $\sum_{i=1}^k p_i \le \sum_{i=1}^k q_i$ for all $1 \le k \le n-1$ and $\sum_{i=1}^n p_i = \sum_{i=1}^n q_i$. By Nielsen's theorem, a pure bipartite quantum state with Schmidt-coefficient-squared vector $q$ can be deterministically converted to one with Schmidt-coefficient-squared vector $p$ using local operations and classical communication if and only if $p \prec q$.

Say that $p$ is catalytically majorized by $q$, written $p \prec_T q$, if there exists some integer $r \ge 1$ and a probability vector $c = (c_1, \dots, c_r)$ such that
$$ p \otimes c \;\prec\; q \otimes c, $$
where $p \otimes c$ denotes the probability vector with entries $p_i c_j$ arranged in non-increasing order (and similarly for $q \otimes c$).

Problem: Give an efficient (in particular, decidable in finitely many steps as a function of $n$) necessary-and-sufficient criterion, in terms of $p$ and $q$ alone, for whether $p \prec_T q$ holds.
status_search_result: Klimesh and Turgut independently characterized catalytic majorization by an infinite family of Rényi-entropy inequalities (all $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$), and the IQOQI Open Quantum Problems page lists the problem as solved on this basis. However, Gour and others showed that for $d \ge 4$ no finite set of conditions on $p,q$ can be necessary and sufficient, so a strictly finite/efficient criterion in the original sense does not exist; recent work (2025) provides finite sufficient (but not necessary) conditions. Hence the problem is best described as partially solved: characterized by infinite inequalities, with finite necessary-and-sufficient criteria provably impossible in general.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: A nice error basis is an orthogonal basis of d squared unitary operators on a d-dimensional Hilbert space whose products are basis elements up to phases, inducing an index group. A shift-and-multiply basis is obtained, in a suitable Hilbert-space basis, from products of permutation operators and multiplication operators. Is every nice error basis of shift-and-multiply type?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a $d$-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $U(\mathcal{H})$ denote the group of unitary operators on $\mathcal{H}$ equipped with the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product $\langle A,B\rangle = \operatorname{tr}(A^*B)$. A nice error basis on $\mathcal{H}$ is a collection $\mathcal{E} = \{E_g : g \in G\}$ of $d^2$ unitary operators indexed by a finite group $G$ of order $d^2$ such that:
(i) $E_e = I$, where $e$ is the identity of $G$;
(ii) $\operatorname{tr}(E_g) = 0$ for all $g \neq e$ (equivalently, the operators are orthogonal in the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product);
(iii) for all $g,h \in G$ there exists a phase $\omega(g,h) \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|\omega(g,h)| = 1$ such that $E_g E_h = \omega(g,h) E_{gh}$.
The group $G$ is called the index group of $\mathcal{E}$.

A shift-and-multiply basis (also called a monomial nice error basis) is a nice error basis $\mathcal{E}$ such that, in some orthonormal basis $\{|0\rangle, \ldots, |d-1\rangle\}$ of $\mathcal{H}$, every $E_g$ can be written as a product $P_\pi D$ of a permutation operator $P_\pi |k\rangle = |\pi(k)\rangle$ (for some permutation $\pi$ of $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$) and a diagonal unitary operator $D = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_{d-1})$ with $|\lambda_k| = 1$ (i.e., every $E_g$ is a monomial unitary matrix in this basis).

Question: Is every nice error basis of shift-and-multiply type?
category_tag: Nice error bases in quantum information
status_search_result: The question has been resolved in the negative: Klappenecker and Rötteler proved that there exist nice error bases that are not monomial (i.e., not of shift-and-multiply type). Their construction provides explicit non-monomial examples; the smallest known counterexample arises in dimension d = 165.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Two-qubit formula for relative entropy of entanglement
original_question: For a two-qubit quantum state rho, the relative entropy of entanglement ER(rho) is the infimum of the quantum relative entropy S(rho||sigma) over sigma in the convex set of separable states or in the convex set of states with positive partial transpose. Find a closed formula for ER(rho) for two-qubit systems.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\rho$ be a density operator on $\mathbb{C}^2\otimes\mathbb{C}^2$ (a two-qubit state). Let $\mathcal{D}$ denote either the convex set of separable states on $\mathbb{C}^2\otimes\mathbb{C}^2$ (states expressible as $\sum_i p_i \,\rho_i^A\otimes\rho_i^B$ with $p_i\ge 0$, $\sum_i p_i=1$) or, alternatively, the convex set of states with positive partial transpose (states $\sigma$ such that $\sigma^{T_B}\ge 0$). The quantum relative entropy is $S(\rho\|\sigma)=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)-\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\log\sigma)$ when $\mathrm{supp}(\rho)\subseteq\mathrm{supp}(\sigma)$, and $+\infty$ otherwise. The relative entropy of entanglement is defined by
$$E_R(\rho)=\inf_{\sigma\in\mathcal{D}} S(\rho\|\sigma).$$
Problem: Give a closed-form expression for $E_R(\rho)$ as a function of $\rho$, valid for all two-qubit states $\rho$.
status_search_result: Partial results are known: closed-form expressions exist for special families (e.g., states with z-directional Bloch vectors, Bell-diagonal states), and a compact form for the inverse problem (given a separable state, find entangled states for which it is closest) was obtained in 2008. However, no general closed formula for the relative entropy of entanglement of arbitrary two-qubit states has been established, and the problem is still listed on the Open Quantum Problems repository.

original_question: For quantum channels T1 and T2, let chi(T) be the Holevo quantity obtained by maximizing the output entropy of an ensemble average minus the ensemble average of output entropies over input ensembles. Is chi additive under tensor products, meaning chi(T1 tensor T2) = chi(T1) + chi(T2), or is there a counterexample? where the supremum is over all finite probability distributions $(p_1,\dots,p_n)$ and all collections of input states $ho_1,\dots,ho_n\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{in}})$.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: Regard the quantum capacity of a noisy quantum channel as a function on the space of channels. Is this function continuous, for example with respect to the completely bounded norm: whenever two channels are close in channel distance, must their quantum capacities also be close?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\mathcal{H}_B$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, and let $\mathrm{CPTP}(\mathcal{H}_A,\mathcal{H}_B)$ denote the set of completely positive trace-preserving linear maps (quantum channels) from operators on $\mathcal{H}_A$ to operators on $\mathcal{H}_B$. For a channel $\mathcal{N}\in\mathrm{CPTP}(\mathcal{H}_A,\mathcal{H}_B)$, the coherent information for an input state $\rho$ is
$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal{N}) := S(\mathcal{N}(\rho)) - S((\mathcal{N}\otimes\mathrm{id})(|\psi_\rho\rangle\langle\psi_\rho|)),$$
where $S(\sigma)=-\mathrm{Tr}(\sigma\log\sigma)$ is the von Neumann entropy and $|\psi_\rho\rangle$ is any purification of $\rho$. The quantum capacity of $\mathcal{N}$ is defined by the regularized formula
$$Q(\mathcal{N}) := \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\max_{\rho^{(n)}}I_c(\rho^{(n)},\mathcal{N}^{\otimes n}).$$
On the set of channels, equip $\mathrm{CPTP}(\mathcal{H}_A,\mathcal{H}_B)$ with the completely bounded norm distance $\|\mathcal{N}_1-\mathcal{N}_2\|_{cb}$.

Question: Is the map $\mathcal{N}\mapsto Q(\mathcal{N})$ continuous with respect to the cb-norm? Equivalently, for every $\varepsilon>0$ does there exist $\delta>0$ such that whenever $\|\mathcal{N}_1-\mathcal{N}_2\|_{cb}<\delta$ one has $|Q(\mathcal{N}_1)-Q(\mathcal{N}_2)|<\varepsilon$?
status_search_result: The problem is essentially solved. Leung and Smith (2009, "Continuity of Quantum Channel Capacities", Commun. Math. Phys.) proved that the classical, quantum, and private classical capacities are continuous in the diamond/cb-norm on finite-dimensional channels, with explicit continuity bounds depending on the output dimension. Subsequent refined continuity bounds were given by Shirokov, Leditzky and others (tight bounds, energy-constrained versions). The Open Quantum Problems entry lists the problem's status as solved.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Mutually unbiased bases in composite dimensions
original_question: For a D-dimensional Hilbert space, determine the maximum number K of orthonormal bases that are mutually unbiased, meaning that every vector from one basis has squared inner-product magnitude 1/D with every vector from another basis. It is known that K = D + 1 can be achieved when D is a prime power; decide what happens for other composite dimensions, in particular whether seven mutually unbiased bases exist in dimension six.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $D \geq 2$. Two orthonormal bases $\{e^{(k)}_i\}_{i=1}^D$ and $\{e^{(n)}_j\}_{j=1}^D$ of $\mathcal{H}$ are called mutually unbiased if 
$$|\langle e^{(k)}_i, e^{(n)}_j\rangle|^2 = \frac{1}{D} \quad \text{for all } i,j \in \{1,\dots,D\}.$$
A family of $K$ orthonormal bases is called a set of mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) if every two distinct bases in the family are mutually unbiased. Let $N(D)$ denote the maximum cardinality of such a family in dimension $D$. It is known that $N(D) \leq D+1$ for every $D$, and that $N(D) = D+1$ whenever $D$ is a prime power.

(a) Determine $N(D)$ for composite dimensions $D$ that are not prime powers.

(b) In particular, decide whether $N(6) = 7$; that is, determine whether there exist seven mutually unbiased bases in $\mathbb{C}^6$.
status_search_result: The problem remains open. Dimension 6 is still the smallest dimension where the maximum number of MUBs is unknown; only 3 MUBs in C^6 have ever been constructed, and the conjecture that N(6)=3 (in particular that 7 MUBs do not exist) is unresolved. Recent work (2024–2025) reformulates the question as a polynomial optimization problem but has not settled it, and a 2025 comment identified errors in earlier partial proofs concerning Hadamard matrices in dimension 6.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For a mixed state rho on an NM-dimensional Hilbert space, characterize exactly those spectra for which no factorization of the Hilbert space into an N-dimensional tensor an M-dimensional subsystem makes rho nonseparable. Equivalently, determine from the spectrum alone when every such bipartite factorization leaves rho separable.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a complex Hilbert space of dimension $NM$ with $N,M\ge 2$. A density operator (mixed state) on $\mathcal{H}$ is a positive semidefinite operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}$ with $\mathrm{tr}(\rho)=1$. Given a tensor factorization $\mathcal{H}\cong\mathbb{C}^N\otimes\mathbb{C}^M$, the state $\rho$ is called separable with respect to this factorization if it can be written as a convex combination $\rho=\sum_i p_i\,\sigma_i\otimes\tau_i$, where $p_i\ge 0$, $\sum_i p_i=1$, and $\sigma_i,\tau_i$ are density operators on $\mathbb{C}^N$ and $\mathbb{C}^M$ respectively; otherwise $\rho$ is called entangled (nonseparable) with respect to that factorization. Because any two factorizations of $\mathcal{H}$ as $\mathbb{C}^N\otimes\mathbb{C}^M$ are related by a unitary on $\mathcal{H}$, the property that $\rho$ is separable with respect to every such factorization depends only on the spectrum (multiset of eigenvalues) of $\rho$. Such a state is said to be absolutely separable.

Problem: Give a complete characterization, purely in terms of the eigenvalues $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_{NM}\ge 0$ (with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$), of those spectra such that every density operator on $\mathcal{H}$ with that spectrum is separable with respect to every tensor decomposition $\mathcal{H}\cong\mathbb{C}^N\otimes\mathbb{C}^M$.
status_search_result: The problem of "separability from spectrum" / absolute separability is fully solved for the qubit-qudit case (N=2), where absolute separability coincides with absolute PPT and admits an explicit eigenvalue characterization (Johnston, 2013). For general N,M with min(N,M) ≥ 3 the full spectral characterization is still open, and it is not even known whether absolute separability is equivalent to absolute PPT in those cases. The problem is currently listed as an open problem on the Open Quantum Problems list maintained at IQOQI, with active recent work (e.g., 2024–2025 arXiv papers giving sufficient criteria and extreme-point analyses).

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Reverse Shannon theorem for entanglement-assisted coding
original_question: For quantum channels S and T, define CE(T,S) as an entanglement-assisted asymptotic simulation capacity: the supremum of rates r for which many parallel copies of one channel can simulate many copies of the other using arbitrary coding, decoding, and any needed shared entanglement with vanishing error. Is entanglement-assisted coding reversible for all channel pairs, in the sense that CE(T,S) equals the reciprocal of CE(S,T)?
self_contained_problem:
Let S and T be quantum channels (completely positive trace-preserving maps between finite-dimensional matrix algebras). Define the entanglement-assisted asymptotic simulation capacity C_E(T, S) as the supremum of all real numbers r ≥ 0 such that, for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large n, there exist encoding and decoding quantum operations E_n and D_n, together with a (possibly arbitrarily large) shared entangled state between sender and receiver, such that the composite map D_n ∘ S^{⊗n} ∘ E_n (acting with the help of the shared entanglement) simulates T^{⊗⌊rn⌋} to within diamond-norm error at most ε. Prove or disprove: for every pair of quantum channels S and T (with C_E(S,T) > 0),
            C_E(T, S) = 1 / C_E(S, T).
That is, show that entanglement-assisted asymptotic channel simulation is reversible for all pairs of channels.
status_search_result: The Quantum Reverse Shannon Theorem, which implies the reversibility C_E(T,S) = 1/C_E(S,T) via the formula C_E(T,S) = C_E(T)/C_E(S) where C_E is the entanglement-assisted classical capacity, was established by Bennett, Devetak, Harrow, Shor, and Winter (arXiv:0912.5537, published 2014) and independently by Berta, Christandl, and Renner (Comm. Math. Phys., 2011). Thus the problem is solved.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Bell inequalities stronger than CHSH for Werner states
original_question: Find Bell inequalities stronger than the CHSH inequalities for Werner states, in the specific sense that the new inequalities are violated by a wider range of Werner states than CHSH is.
self_contained_problem:
For a parameter $\lambda \in [-1,1]$, the two-qubit Werner state on $\mathbb{C}^2 \otimes \mathbb{C}^2$ is defined by
$$ho_\lambda \;=\; \lambda\, |\psi^-angle\langle\psi^-| \;+\;  rac{1-\lambda}{4}\, I_4,$$
where $|\psi^-angle = (|01angle - |10angle)/\sqrt{2}$ is the singlet state. (Equivalently, $ho_\lambda$ is the unique $U \otimes U$-invariant state with the given singlet fraction.)

The Clauser–Horne–Shimony–Holt (CHSH) inequality states that, for any local hidden-variable model with two dichotomic ($\pm 1$-valued) measurements per party, the quantity
$$\langle A_1 B_1angle + \langle A_1 B_2angle + \langle A_2 B_1angle - \langle A_2 B_2angle$$
is bounded in absolute value by $2$. The Werner state $ho_\lambda$ admits projective dichotomic measurements that violate this CHSH inequality if and only if $\lambda > 1/\sqrt{2}$.

Problem: Exhibit a Bell inequality (i.e. a linear inequality on joint correlations of finitely many local measurement outcomes that is valid for every local hidden-variable model) together with quantum measurements on $ho_\lambda$ such that the inequality is violated by $ho_\lambda$ for some value $\lambda \le 1/\sqrt{2}$. Equivalently, find a Bell inequality whose range of two-qubit Werner states $ho_\lambda$ exhibiting violation strictly contains the CHSH range $\lambda > 1/\sqrt{2}$.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Bell violation activated by tensor products
original_question: Can there exist bipartite density operators rho1 and rho2 such that neither rho1 nor rho2 violates any CHSH Bell inequality individually, but their tensor product rho1 tensor rho2 does violate a CHSH Bell inequality?

$$|\mathrm{Tr}(\rho(A_0\otimes B_0 + A_0\otimes B_1 + A_1\otimes B_0 - A_1\otimes B_1))| > 2.$$
Otherwise, $\rho$ is said to admit no CHSH violation.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Existence of SIC-POVMs in all dimensions
original_question: For every Hilbert-space dimension d, does there exist a symmetric informationally complete POVM: a set of d squared normalized vectors forming equiangular lines, whose associated rank-one projection operators sum to a multiple of the identity and are linearly independent so that every quantum state can be reconstructed from the resulting measurement statistics?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H} = \mathbb{C}^d$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d \ge 2$. A symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measure (SIC-POVM) on $\mathcal{H}$ is a collection of $d^2$ unit vectors $\{|\varphi_i\rangle\}_{i=1}^{d^2} \subset \mathcal{H}$ such that:

(i) (Equiangularity) There exists a constant $c$ with
$$|\langle \varphi_i \mid \varphi_j \rangle|^2 = c \quad \text{for all } i \ne j,$$
and one easily checks that $c$ must equal $\tfrac{1}{d+1}$.

(ii) (Resolution of the identity) The associated rank-one projectors $\Pi_i = |\varphi_i\rangle\langle \varphi_i|$ satisfy
$$\sum_{i=1}^{d^2} \Pi_i = d\, I,$$
so that $\{\tfrac{1}{d}\Pi_i\}_{i=1}^{d^2}$ is a POVM.

(iii) (Informational completeness) The operators $\{\Pi_i\}_{i=1}^{d^2}$ are linearly independent in the real vector space of Hermitian operators on $\mathcal{H}$, hence form a basis, and every density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}$ is uniquely determined by the probabilities $\mathrm{tr}(\rho \Pi_i)/d$.

Question: Does a SIC-POVM exist for every finite dimension $d \ge 2$?
status_search_result: The general existence of SIC-POVMs in all finite dimensions (Zauner's conjecture) remains an open problem as of 2025. Exact and/or numerical solutions are known in many specific dimensions (all $d \le 151$ and additional sporadic cases such as $d = 23$ and various dimensions reachable by Stark-unit constructions), and recent algebraic number theory approaches have produced new exact fiducials, but no proof of existence in arbitrary dimension is known.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Zauner’s conjecture for SIC fiducial vectors
original_question: Let the Clifford group be the normalizer of the Heisenberg group in the d-dimensional unitary group, and let z be the Clifford element acting on Weyl operators by z w(p,q) z* = w(q - p, -p). In every dimension d, can a Heisenberg-group fiducial vector for a covariant SIC-POVM be found among the eigenvectors of z?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer d ≥ 2 and work in the Hilbert space ℂ^d. For p, q ∈ ℤ/dℤ, define the Weyl (displacement) operators w(p,q) on ℂ^d by
  w(p,q) |k⟩ = ω^{q(k+p/2)} |k+p⟩,
where ω = exp(2πi/d) (with the half-integer exponent interpreted via a 2d-th root of unity when d is odd, or via the standard projective convention when d is even). The Heisenberg–Weyl group H(d) is the group generated by the w(p,q) together with phases, and the Clifford group is its normalizer in the unitary group U(d).

There exists a Clifford-group element z whose action on Weyl operators is
  z w(p,q) z* = w(q − p, −p).

A unit vector φ ∈ ℂ^d is called a Heisenberg-covariant fiducial vector for a symmetric informationally complete POVM (SIC-POVM) if the d² rank-one projectors
  {(1/d) w(p,q) |φ⟩⟨φ| w(p,q)* : (p,q) ∈ (ℤ/dℤ)²}
form a SIC-POVM, equivalently
  |⟨φ | w(p,q) | φ⟩|² = 1/(d+1)   for all (p,q) ≠ (0,0).

Question: Is it true that for every dimension d ≥ 2 there exists a Heisenberg-covariant SIC fiducial vector φ that is an eigenvector of z?
status_search_result: Zauner's conjecture remains open in general. SIC fiducial vectors that are eigenvectors of the Zauner unitary have been constructed (numerically or exactly) in many specific dimensions, and a 2025 conditional construction via the Stark conjectures provides candidate fiducials in broad families of dimensions, but no unconditional proof for all d is known.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Secret key distillation from all entangled states
original_question: Can every bipartite entangled state be used to generate secret keys, including bound entangled states for which secret key extraction need not proceed by first distilling pure singlets?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\rho_{AB}$ be a bipartite quantum state on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$. The state $\rho_{AB}$ is called entangled if it cannot be written as a convex combination $\sum_i p_i \sigma^A_i \otimes \tau^B_i$ of product states. The distillable secret key rate $K_D(\rho_{AB})$ is defined as the largest rate $R \geq 0$ such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $n_0$ with the following property: for all $n \geq n_0$ there is an LOCC (local operations and classical communication) protocol acting on $\rho_{AB}^{\otimes n}$ that outputs a classical-classical-quantum state on registers $K_A K_B E$ (with $E$ held by an eavesdropper purifying the protocol) which is $\varepsilon$-close in trace distance to an ideal secret key state $\frac{1}{2^{\lfloor nR \rfloor}} \sum_{k} |kk\rangle\langle kk|_{K_A K_B} \otimes \sigma_E$ for some $\sigma_E$.

Some bound entangled states (entangled states from which no pure maximally entangled pairs can be distilled by LOCC) are known to have $K_D > 0$, so secret key extraction need not proceed via prior distillation of singlets.

Question: Is it true that $K_D(\rho_{AB}) > 0$ for every entangled bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$?
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem (Problem 24, "Secret key from all entangled states") on the Open Quantum Problems database maintained by IQOQI. While partial progress exists — e.g., specific bound entangled states are known to yield positive distillable key, and efficiently computable upper bounds on one-way distillable key have been developed — no general proof or counterexample establishing whether every bipartite entangled state has positive distillable secret key rate is known.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Boundary of the quantum correlation body
original_question: In the (N, M, K) multipartite correlation setting with no-signalling polytope P, quantum correlation body Q, and classical local polytope C, consider the portion of the boundary of Q that is not already contained in the boundary of P. Can every point on that part of the quantum boundary be reached using K-dimensional local Hilbert spaces and complete von Neumann measurements with K orthogonal projectors on pure states of minimal dimension?
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers N, M, K ≥ 2. Consider an N-partite Bell-type scenario in which each party can choose one of M measurement settings, each with K possible outcomes. A correlation is the collection of joint outcome probabilities P(a_1,...,a_N | x_1,...,x_N), where x_i ∈ {1,...,M} is the setting and a_i ∈ {1,...,K} is the outcome of party i.

Define:
- P, the no-signalling polytope: the set of correlations that are non-negative, normalized, and satisfy the no-signalling conditions (the marginal distribution of any subset of parties is independent of the other parties' setting choices).
- Q ⊆ P, the quantum correlation body: the set of correlations of the form P(a_1,...,a_N | x_1,...,x_N) = Tr(ρ · E^{(1)}_{a_1|x_1} ⊗ ··· ⊗ E^{(N)}_{a_N|x_N}), where ρ is a density operator on a tensor product H_1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ H_N of (arbitrary finite-dimensional) Hilbert spaces and {E^{(i)}_{a|x}}_a is a POVM on H_i for each setting x.
- C ⊆ Q, the classical local polytope: correlations admitting a local hidden variable model.

Let ∂Q denote the boundary of Q and ∂P that of P, and consider the relative boundary ∂Q \ ∂P, i.e. quantum-boundary points not lying on the no-signalling boundary.

Question: Is it true that every point of ∂Q \ ∂P can be realized by a quantum model in which each local Hilbert space H_i has dimension exactly K and each local measurement is a complete von Neumann measurement consisting of K rank-one orthogonal projectors onto pure states?
status_search_result: The problem has been solved negatively. Vértesi and Pál (2008) exhibited Bell inequalities whose maximal quantum violation cannot be attained with two-qubit systems and rank-one projective measurements, showing that K-dimensional local Hilbert spaces with complete von Neumann measurements do not suffice to reach all points of the relevant part of ∂Q. This resolution is recorded on the IQOQI "Open Quantum Problems" page for Problem 26.A.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: In the bipartite two-measurement d-outcome Bell setting (N, M, K) = (2, 2, d), show that every face of the local polytope C that is not already contained in a face of the no-signalling polytope P is of CGLMP type, possibly after lifting a lower-dimensional CGLMP inequality by fusing outcomes.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the bipartite Bell scenario with two parties, each performing one of M = 2 measurements, where every measurement has K = d possible outcomes. A behavior is specified by the joint probabilities P(a,b | x,y) for outcomes a,b ∈ {0,1,…,d-1} and measurement choices x,y ∈ {1,2}. Let:

• C be the local (classical) polytope, consisting of all behaviors P(a,b|x,y) that admit a decomposition
   P(a,b|x,y) = ∑_λ q(λ) p_A(a|x,λ) p_B(b|y,λ)
with q a probability distribution and p_A, p_B response functions.

• P be the no-signalling polytope, consisting of all non-negative normalized behaviors satisfying ∑_a P(a,b|x,y) = ∑_a P(a,b|x',y) and ∑_b P(a,b|x,y) = ∑_b P(a,b|x,y') for all parameters.

Then C ⊆ P. A CGLMP inequality is the family of Bell inequalities introduced by Collins, Gisin, Linden, Massar and Popescu for arbitrary outcome number d, in the (2,2,d) scenario; a lifted CGLMP inequality is one obtained from a CGLMP inequality in a (2,2,d') scenario with d' < d by partitioning (fusing) the d outcomes into d' groups.

Prove or disprove: every facet of C that is not also contained in a facet of P is, up to relabelling of parties, measurements, and outcomes, a CGLMP inequality, possibly lifted from a lower-outcome CGLMP inequality by fusing outcomes.
status_search_result: The conjecture has been resolved in the negative. In the bipartite scenario with two settings and four outcomes (2,2,4), a complete classification of inequivalent symmetric facet Bell inequalities revealed eight genuinely 4-outcome facets; only one of these is the CGLMP inequality, while seven others are inequivalent to CGLMP (and not liftings of lower-outcome CGLMP inequalities). Thus the (2,2,d) local polytope is not exhausted by CGLMP-type facets, refuting the conjecture.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Local-unitary versus local-Clifford equivalence of graph states
original_question: For graph states, where vertices represent qubits and edges determine the stabilizer-state phases, decide whether local unitary equivalence always implies local Clifford equivalence. In other words, if two graph states can be mapped into each other by arbitrary tensor products of local unitaries, can they also be mapped into each other by tensor products of local unitaries from the Clifford group?
self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and consider n qubits with Hilbert space (C^2)^{⊗n}. For a simple undirected graph G = (V,E) with V = {1,...,n}, the associated graph state |G⟩ is defined by |G⟩ = (∏_{(i,j)∈E} CZ_{i,j}) |+⟩^{⊗n}, where |+⟩ = (|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2 and CZ_{i,j} is the controlled-Z gate acting on qubits i and j. The single-qubit Pauli group is generated by the matrices X, Y, Z; the single-qubit Clifford group C_1 consists of unitaries U on C^2 such that UPU* is, up to a phase, a Pauli matrix whenever P is.

Two graph states |G⟩ and |G'⟩ on n qubits are said to be local-unitary (LU) equivalent if there exist unitaries U_1,...,U_n on C^2 with |G'⟩ = (U_1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ U_n)|G⟩, and local-Clifford (LC) equivalent if such U_i can additionally be chosen from C_1.

Question: Is it true that every pair of LU-equivalent graph states is also LC-equivalent?
status_search_result: The LU-LC conjecture was disproved in 2007 by Ji, Chen, Wei, and Ying, who exhibited an explicit pair of 27-qubit graph states that are LU-equivalent but not LC-equivalent. A 2026 result further establishes that 27 qubits is minimal: for n ≤ 26 the two notions coincide.

paper_title: A realist view of the electron: recent advances and unsolved problems
context_brief: Numerical intrinsic properties and electron size
original_question: In a realist extended-electron framework in which an electron is determined by intrinsic properties and is assumed to have a finite but unspecified volume V, can the exact numerical values of the electron's intrinsic properties and its actual size or volume be determined rather than left undefined?
self_contained_problem: Consider a realist model of the electron in which the electron is treated as a spatially extended object characterized solely by a collection of intrinsic properties (such as charge, mass, magnetic moment, spin angular momentum, and a characteristic volume V > 0). Assume a non-relativistic inertial frame in which the electron moves with constant velocity u along a fixed direction, and that the electron occupies a finite but a priori unspecified volume V. Within such a framework, determine whether it is possible to derive the exact numerical values of the electron's intrinsic properties together with its actual spatial size (volume V), rather than leaving these quantities undefined parameters of the model. paper_title: A realist view of the electron: recent advances and unsolved problems
original_question: In a photon-interaction model of electrostatic fields where charge is expressed through the properties of emitted and absorbed photons and those photons can produce attraction or repulsion, how can the origin of a specific charge or anticharge in a specific situation be comprehensively described?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a model of electrostatic interactions in which the electromagnetic field between charged particles is mediated entirely by emitted and absorbed photons, and in which the quantity conventionally called "electric charge" of a particle is not a primitive attribute but is instead encoded in the intrinsic properties (e.g. polarization, phase, helicity, or other internal degrees of freedom) of the photons that the particle emits and absorbs. Assume further that, depending on these intrinsic photon properties, the photon exchange between two such particles can give rise either to an attractive or to a repulsive net force. Within this framework, the sign of a particle's charge is therefore not a fixed invariant but a context-dependent quantity determined by the photon-exchange process.

Problem: Provide a comprehensive mathematical description of the origin of a specific charge or anticharge in a specific physical situation within this photon-interaction framework. That is, specify a precise rule or mechanism that, given the intrinsic properties of the emitted and absorbed photons exchanged between two particles in a given configuration, determines the sign and magnitude of the effective charge (or anticharge) attributed to each particle, and explains how attraction versus repulsion arises from these photon properties in a manner consistent with the observed phenomenology of electrostatics.
status_search_result: No mainstream physics literature was found establishing a comprehensive description of charge/anticharge origin within such a photon-property-based model; the question is speculative and lies outside standard QED, where charge is a conserved quantum number rather than an emergent photon property. Status cannot be verified.

paper_title: A realist view of the electron: recent advances and unsolved problems
original_question: How can one construct a mathematical model of scattering processes based on photon interactions for extended electrons, in situations where reducing the problem to a one-body potential problem, as in standard scattering solutions, is not generally applicable?
self_contained_problem: Model an electron as a spatially extended object (rather than a point particle) carrying its charge and spin densities, and consider its interaction with the electromagnetic field via the exchange of photons. Develop a mathematically rigorous framework for scattering processes between such extended electrons (and between an extended electron and other charged matter) in which the interaction is mediated entirely by photon exchange, without assuming that the dynamics can be reduced to a one-body problem in an external potential. Specifically: define the state space and asymptotic in/out states for the extended electron coupled to the quantized electromagnetic field; formulate the scattering operator (S-matrix) for processes governed by photon-mediated interactions; and establish existence, unitarity, and computability of cross sections for elastic and inelastic scattering in this setting, in regimes where the standard reduction to a one-body Schrödinger or Dirac equation with a fixed potential is not available.
status_search_result: The problem of constructing a fully rigorous scattering theory for extended (non-point) electrons interacting via photon exchange, without reduction to a one-body potential problem, has not been resolved. Standard QED scattering is formulated perturbatively for point electrons, and rigorous nonperturbative constructions of interacting QED scattering remain open. No source was found that presents a complete mathematical model of the kind described.

paper_title: Quantum Information Theory: Results and Open Problems
original_question: Suppose an ensemble consists of exactly two quantum states and one wants to maximize the accessible classical information obtained by measuring the received state. Must every measurement that attains this optimum be a von Neumann measurement, or can a more general positive-operator-valued measurement be strictly better even in the two-state case?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\{\rho_1,\rho_2\}$ be an ensemble of two quantum states on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, with prior probabilities $p_1,p_2 \ge 0$ summing to $1$. A general measurement is described by a positive-operator-valued measure (POVM) $\{E_y\}_{y \in Y}$ on $\mathcal{H}$, i.e. a finite collection of positive semidefinite operators with $\sum_y E_y = I$. Given the ensemble and the POVM, the outcome $Y$ has conditional distribution $P(Y=y \mid X=i) = \mathrm{tr}(\rho_i E_y)$ for $i \in \{1,2\}$, and the accessible (mutual) information is
$$ I_{\mathrm{acc}}(\{p_i,\rho_i\}) \;=\; \sup_{\{E_y\}} I(X;Y), $$
where the supremum is over all POVMs. A von Neumann (projective) measurement is a POVM whose elements are mutually orthogonal projectors summing to $I$.

Question: For every two-state ensemble $\{(p_1,\rho_1),(p_2,\rho_2)\}$ on an arbitrary finite-dimensional Hilbert space, is the supremum defining $I_{\mathrm{acc}}$ attained by some von Neumann measurement? Equivalently, can no genuine (non-projective) POVM strictly exceed the best projective measurement when the ensemble contains only two states?
status_search_result: The conjecture is proved for two states on a qubit (two-dimensional Hilbert space) by Keil, but in general dimension it remains open. A 2025 preprint refers to it as a longstanding open conjecture (sometimes called Shor's conjecture on quantum dichotomies) and makes progress on characterizing extremal optimizing measurements, but does not resolve the general case.

paper_title: Quantum Information Theory: Results and Open Problems
original_question: For a mixed bipartite quantum state ρ, are the entanglement of formation and the distillable entanglement always equal? In other words, when two distant parties are restricted to local quantum operations and classical communication, does the asymptotic number of EPR pairs needed to create ρ always equal the asymptotic number of EPR pairs that can be extracted back from copies of ρ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\rho$ be a bipartite mixed quantum state on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ shared by two distant parties $A$ and $B$ who are restricted to local quantum operations and classical communication (LOCC). Define:

(i) The entanglement of formation $E_f(\rho)$ as the asymptotic rate (per copy) of EPR pairs (maximally entangled two-qubit states) required to prepare many copies of $\rho$ by LOCC, i.e. the infimum of $m/n$ such that $n$ copies of $\rho$ can be produced from $m$ EPR pairs by LOCC, in the limit $n \to \infty$.

(ii) The distillable entanglement $E_d(\rho)$ as the asymptotic rate (per copy) of EPR pairs that can be extracted from many copies of $\rho$ by LOCC, i.e. the supremum of $m/n$ such that $m$ EPR pairs can be produced from $n$ copies of $\rho$ by LOCC, in the limit $n \to \infty$.

For pure bipartite states it is known that $E_f(\rho) = E_d(\rho)$. Question: Does the equality $E_f(\rho) = E_d(\rho)$ hold for every bipartite mixed state $\rho$?
status_search_result: The answer is no: for general mixed bipartite states, $E_f$ and $E_d$ are not equal. The Horodecki family proved the existence of bound entangled states — entangled mixed states (e.g. PPT entangled states in dimension $3\times 3$ and higher) for which $E_d = 0$ while $E_f > 0$. This irreversibility of entanglement manipulation under LOCC is well-established in the literature.

context_brief: Necessity of spectral conditions in linear iteration
original_question: Consider the iterative equation Σ_{j=0}^N a_j φ^j(x) = 0 on (0,∞), where φ^j denotes the j-th iterate of φ, and let c > 0 be a positive root of the characteristic polynomial Σ_{j=0}^N a_j λ^j = 0. A theorem in the paper shows that if (i) c is a simple root, (ii) there are no other positive roots, and (iii) every other root λ satisfies |λ| > c, then the only solution on a positive domain is φ(x) = cx. The open problem is whether these three conditions are actually necessary for uniqueness of the continuous or monotone solution φ:(0,∞)→(0,∞) of this iterative equation.
self_contained_problem:
Let $N \ge 2$ be an integer and let $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_N \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a_N 
eq 0$. For a self-map $\varphi:(0,\infty)	o(0,\infty)$ denote by $\varphi^j$ its $j$-th iterate (with $\varphi^0(x)=x$). Consider the linear iterative functional equation
$$\sum_{j=0}^{N} a_j\,\varphi^j(x) = 0, \qquad x \in (0,\infty). \quad (\star)$$
Assume that the characteristic polynomial $P(\lambda)=\sum_{j=0}^{N} a_j\lambda^j$ admits a positive real root $c>0$ satisfying the following three conditions:

(i) $c$ is a simple root of $P$;
(ii) $c$ is the only positive real root of $P$;
(iii) every other (complex) root $\lambda$ of $P$ satisfies $|\lambda|>c$.

Under (i)–(iii) it is known that the only continuous (equivalently monotonic) solution $\varphi:(0,\infty)	o(0,\infty)$ of $(\star)$ is the linear map $\varphi(x)=cx$.

More precisely, decide whether, whenever the equation $(\star)$ has a unique continuous (or monotonic) positive solution $\varphi(x)=cx$ with $c>0$ a root of $P$, the polynomial $P$ must satisfy all three of (i), (ii), (iii); if not, exhibit a counterexample or characterize the precise spectral conditions that are equivalent to uniqueness.

paper_title: Results and Open Problems in Mathematical General Relativity
original_question: Given initial data on a Cauchy hypersurface that satisfy the Einstein constraint equations, does the corresponding maximal globally hyperbolic solution of the Einstein equations exist globally to the future, in the geometric sense that all future-directed causal geodesics are complete?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Sigma, g, K)$ be a smooth initial data set for the vacuum Einstein equations, where $\Sigma$ is a 3-dimensional manifold, $g$ is a Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and $K$ is a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field on $\Sigma$ representing the second fundamental form, satisfying the Einstein vacuum constraint equations
$$R(g) - |K|_g^2 + (\mathrm{tr}_g K)^2 = 0, \qquad \mathrm{div}_g K - d(\mathrm{tr}_g K) = 0,$$
where $R(g)$ denotes the scalar curvature of $g$. By the theorem of Choquet-Bruhat and Geroch, there exists a unique (up to isometry) maximal globally hyperbolic development $(\mathcal{M}, \mathbf{g})$ of $(\Sigma, g, K)$, namely a smooth Lorentzian 4-manifold $(\mathcal{M}, \mathbf{g})$ solving $\mathrm{Ric}(\mathbf{g}) = 0$ such that $\Sigma$ embeds into $\mathcal{M}$ as a Cauchy hypersurface inducing the data $(g, K)$, and which is maximal among all such globally hyperbolic developments.

Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on $(\Sigma, g, K)$ that guarantee future geodesic completeness of the maximal globally hyperbolic development; equivalently, determine for which initial data sets every future-directed causal (timelike or null) geodesic in $(\mathcal{M}, \mathbf{g})$ can be extended to arbitrarily large values of an affine parameter.
status_search_result: The general question is open. Future causal geodesic completeness has been established in several important restricted regimes: stability of Minkowski space (Christodoulou–Klainerman, and later Lindblad–Rodnianski) for small asymptotically flat perturbations of Minkowski data; Friedrich's nonlinear stability of de Sitter space for small perturbations with positive cosmological constant; future asymptotic simplicity and null completeness for small hyperboloidal data; and various symmetry-reduced classes (e.g., polarized $T^2$-symmetric, surface symmetric expanding cosmologies). For general (large, far-from-CMC, or low-symmetry) initial data, future completeness is a major open problem, intimately tied to weak cosmic censorship.

paper_title: Results and Open Problems in Mathematical General Relativity
original_question: For generic initial data for the Einstein Cauchy problem, can one prove or control the formation of a trapped surface, that is, a closed surface whose outgoing null geodesics are converging?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Cauchy problem for the Einstein vacuum equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ on a smooth Lorentzian 4-manifold $(\mathcal{M},g)$. An initial data set consists of a smooth 3-manifold $M$ together with a Riemannian metric $\bar g$ and a symmetric 2-tensor $K$ on $M$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
$$R(\bar g)-|K|_{\bar g}^2+(\mathrm{tr}_{\bar g}K)^2=0,\qquad \mathrm{div}_{\bar g}K-d(\mathrm{tr}_{\bar g}K)=0.$$
Such data evolve, by the Choquet-Bruhat–Geroch theorem, into a unique maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development $(\mathcal{M},g)$ in which $M$ embeds as a Cauchy hypersurface.

A closed (compact without boundary) spacelike 2-surface $S\subset\mathcal{M}$ is called a closed trapped surface if both families of future-directed null geodesics issuing orthogonally from $S$ (the outgoing and ingoing null congruences) have everywhere negative expansion; equivalently, $S$ bounds a relatively compact open set in some Cauchy hypersurface, and the outgoing null geodesics emanating from $S$ are converging.

Problem. Identify a notion of "generic" within an appropriate function space of asymptotically flat vacuum initial data $(M,\bar g, K)$ (with $M$ noncompact) and prove a theorem ensuring that for generic such initial data the maximal vacuum Cauchy development contains a closed trapped surface; more precisely, give criteria on the initial data, satisfied on a residual / open dense / full-measure subset, which can be shown to imply (and thus control) the formation of a closed trapped surface in the future development.
category_tag: Trapped surface formation in general relativity
status_search_result: Christodoulou (2008, published 2009) proved that an explicit open set of regular characteristic initial data—encoded via the "short pulse" ansatz—evolves to a vacuum spacetime containing a closed trapped surface, resolving the long-standing problem of evolutionary formation of trapped surfaces from regular data. Klainerman–Rodnianski (2012) simplified and extended this result, and subsequent works (e.g., An–Luk, fully anisotropic mechanisms, Einstein–Maxwell extensions) have broadened the criteria. However, a sharp characterization of "generic" Cauchy initial data leading to trapped surface formation, in the sense of a control theorem on a generic class within the full Cauchy problem (not only short-pulse-type data), remains open.

original_question: For vacuum Einstein spacetimes whose spatial manifold is S^3, must the spacetime collapse in the future?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g)$ be a globally hyperbolic vacuum spacetime, i.e., a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold satisfying the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$, admitting a Cauchy surface diffeomorphic to the 3-sphere $S^3$. Consider the cosmologically normalized (CMC) Einstein flow on $S^3$, parametrized by mean curvature $\tau$ of CMC Cauchy slices $\Sigma_\tau$, and let $h(\tau)$ denote the induced Riemannian metric on $\Sigma_\tau$.

Prove or disprove: every such maximal future Cauchy development collapses in the future in the sense of Cheeger–Gromov, i.e., as $\tau$ tends to its supremum (corresponding to future infinity in the CMC time gauge), the volume-normalized geometry $(\Sigma_\tau, h(\tau))$ collapses with bounded curvature — equivalently, the injectivity radius (after appropriate rescaling so that sectional curvatures remain bounded) tends to zero uniformly on $\Sigma_\tau$.

(The analogous statement is known to hold under the additional assumption that the spacetime admits a continuous spatial isometry group acting on the $S^3$ Cauchy surfaces.)

paper_title: Results and Open Problems in Mathematical General Relativity
original_question: Given arbitrary initial data for the Einstein equations, what is the future evolution of the corresponding spacetime, when do singularities form, and do the weak and strong cosmic censorship conjectures hold?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein vacuum equations (or the Einstein equations coupled to suitable matter models) on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold (M, g), written as Ric(g) - (1/2) R(g) g = T, where Ric(g) is the Ricci tensor, R(g) the scalar curvature, and T the energy-momentum tensor of the matter. By the theorem of Choquet-Bruhat and Geroch, given an initial data set (Σ, h, K) consisting of a 3-manifold Σ, a Riemannian metric h, and a symmetric 2-tensor K satisfying the Einstein constraint equations, there exists a unique maximal globally hyperbolic development (M, g) of this data.

Address the following questions for arbitrary (suitably regular) initial data:

(a) Describe the global future evolution of the maximal globally hyperbolic development.

(b) Determine when and how singularities (in the sense of geodesic incompleteness or curvature blow-up) form in the future development.

(c) Weak cosmic censorship: Prove or disprove that, for generic asymptotically flat initial data, the maximal globally hyperbolic development possesses a complete future null infinity; equivalently, that singularities formed in gravitational collapse are generically hidden behind event horizons and are not visible from future null infinity.

(d) Strong cosmic censorship: Prove or disprove that, for generic (suitably regular) initial data, the maximal globally hyperbolic development is inextendible as a Lorentzian manifold of appropriate regularity, so that general relativity remains deterministic.
status_search_result: Both the weak and strong cosmic censorship conjectures remain open as of 2025. Recent surveys and research papers continue to investigate them: a January 2025 review discusses modern PDE techniques applied to Strong Cosmic Censorship, while other 2025 works propose potential counterexamples in special settings (e.g., AdS3, with positive cosmological constant). No general proof or definitive counterexample for asymptotically flat 4-dimensional spacetimes has been established.

original_question: Is there any function whose best known or optimal algorithm really needs space s in the ordinary model SPACE(s), but can be computed using almost entirely catalytic memory in the sense of belonging to CSPACE(≪ s, ≈ s), with only a much smaller ordinary work tape and nearly all memory coming from restorable catalytic space?

(i) the best known (or known optimal) algorithm for f in the ordinary model uses work space Θ(s); and

self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

A catalytic Turing machine is a deterministic multitape Turing machine equipped with three tapes: a read-only input tape, a work tape, and an additional catalytic tape. The class CL (catalytic logspace) consists of all languages decided by such machines.

A randomized catalytic logspace machine is defined analogously but is additionally given access to a one-way random tape. The class CBPL consists of all languages L for which there exists a randomized catalytic logspace machine M such that for every input x and every initialization w of the catalytic tape:
 (i) Pr[M(x,w) accepts] ≥ 2/3 if x ∈ L, and Pr[M(x,w) accepts] ≤ 1/3 if x ∉ L,
 (ii) with probability 1 the catalytic tape is restored to its initial content w upon halting.

The class BPL is the standard bounded-error randomized logspace class (no catalytic tape), and the inclusion BPL ⊆ CL is known.

paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
original_question: Can nondeterminism be used together with catalytic computation in a genuinely nontrivial way, rather than merely by definition?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A catalytic Turing machine is a space-bounded Turing machine equipped with three tapes: a read-only input tape, a work tape of size s(n) which is initially blank, and a catalytic (auxiliary) tape of size c(n) which is initialized with an arbitrary string τ. The machine may read and write freely on the catalytic tape during the computation, but is required to restore the catalytic tape to its original content τ by the end of every computation, for every initial τ. The class CSPACE[s(n), c(n)] consists of languages decided by such deterministic machines; the catalytic logspace class CL is defined by s(n) = O(log n) and c(n) = poly(n). A nondeterministic catalytic Turing machine is defined analogously, but the transition relation is nondeterministic; the restoration condition requires that on every computation path (or, in the standard definition, on every accepting path) the catalytic tape is returned to its initial content τ. The corresponding nondeterministic class is denoted NCL.

Problem. Exhibit a "genuinely nontrivial" use of nondeterminism in conjunction with catalytic computation. More precisely, one of the following:

(a) Give a computational task, a complexity-theoretic separation, or a structural result whose proof uses a nondeterministic catalytic algorithm in an essential way — i.e., a way that does not reduce immediately to either a standard deterministic catalytic simulation or to ordinary nondeterministic space, and that goes beyond the use of nondeterminism implicit in the definition of NCL.

(b) Equivalently, design a nondeterministic catalytic logspace algorithm for some language L such that the algorithm crucially exploits both the catalytic tape and the nondeterministic branching (for instance, by solving a problem not known to lie in CL via a guessing-and-verification strategy that maintains the catalyst), and prove its correctness and the catalyst-restoration property.

The task is to produce such an application, or to prove that no such nontrivial combination is possible (e.g., by showing NCL = CL via a simulation that renders nondeterminism inessential in this setting).
status_search_result: The problem of nontrivially combining nondeterminism with catalytic computation is recognized as open in the catalytic-computation literature. Buhrman–Koucký–Loff–Speelman defined nondeterministic catalytic space and asked whether nondeterminism adds power. paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
original_question: Can one prove that the threshold-circuit class TC1 is contained in the arithmetic-circuit class VP?
self_contained_problem:
Define the following complexity classes.

(1) TC^1: the class of Boolean languages decided by a non-uniform family of Boolean circuits {C_n} of polynomial size and O(log n) depth, with gates of unbounded fan-in computing AND, OR, NOT, and MAJORITY (threshold) functions.

(2) VP (Valiant's class P): the class of families of multivariate polynomials (f_n) over a field (say ℚ, or any fixed field) such that f_n has polynomially bounded degree in n and is computed by an arithmetic circuit of polynomial size in n using +, ×, and field constants, with inputs being variables or constants.

A Boolean class C is said to be contained in VP if there is a polynomial-size projection / appropriate reduction sending each language L ∈ C to a polynomial family in VP whose coefficients encode membership in L (formally: for every language L ∈ TC^1 there exists a polynomial family (f_n) ∈ VP and a polynomial-time–computable projection from inputs x of length n to monomials/variable settings such that f_n evaluated at this setting equals 1 if x ∈ L and 0 otherwise).

Problem: Prove or disprove that TC^1 ⊆ VP.
status_search_result: The containment of TC^1 in VP is a known open problem in algebraic and circuit complexity. Existing literature characterizes TC^1 via dual-VP-style arithmetic classes (Agrawal–Allender and follow-ups), but no proof of TC^1 ⊆ VP has been established as of available sources.

paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
original_question: If every node in the network is restricted to sending only linear transformations of its incoming messages, can one prove or disprove the network coding conjecture under that restriction?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G = (V, E)$ be a finite directed acyclic graph with edge capacities, together with a set of $k$ source–sink pairs $(s_1, t_1), \ldots, (s_k, t_k)$. Each source $s_i$ holds an independent message $X_i$ taking values in a finite alphabet (identified with a vector space over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$), and the goal is for sink $t_i$ to recover $X_i$ exactly. A network code assigns to every edge $e = (u,v)$ a function whose output (sent along $e$) is computed from the symbols received by $u$ on its incoming edges (and, if $u = s_i$, from $X_i$); each sink $t_j$ applies a decoding function to its incoming symbols. The routing rate of an instance is the maximum throughput achievable when every internal node may only forward (copy) symbols received on incoming edges, while the network coding rate is the maximum throughput achievable when arbitrary functions are allowed at internal nodes.

The network coding conjecture asserts that for every multiple-unicast instance on a directed acyclic graph, the network coding rate equals the routing rate (equivalently, coding offers no throughput advantage over routing for multiple unicast).

A network code is called linear if for every edge $e = (u,v)$, the symbol transmitted on $e$ is an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear transformation of the vector of symbols available at $u$ (its incoming symbols, together with its source message if $u$ is a source), and every sink's decoder is also $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear.

Problem: Either prove or disprove the network coding conjecture under the restriction that every node is allowed to send only linear transformations of its incoming messages. That is, decide whether, for every multiple-unicast instance, the maximum rate achievable by a linear network code equals the routing rate.
status_search_result: The network coding conjecture (no coding advantage over routing for multiple unicast in DAGs) is a well-known open problem; even its restriction to linear network codes remains unresolved. Partial progress exists (e.g., results by Langberg–Medard and others bounding the gap and connections to I/O complexity and pebbling), but no proof or disproof of the linear case has been published.

paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
original_question: Under a believable cryptographic assumption, can one show that catalytic logspace CL is contained in some plausible subclass of P, perhaps even NC?
self_contained_problem:
Background. Define catalytic logspace, denoted CL, as the class of decision problems decidable by a deterministic Turing machine that has (i) a read-only input tape of length n, (ii) a read/write work tape of length O(log n), and (iii) a read/write auxiliary "catalytic" tape of length 2^{O(log n)} = poly(n) which is initialized to an arbitrary string and is required to be restored to its exact initial contents at the end of every computation, regardless of the input. The machine must accept or reject correctly for every input on every possible initial contents of the catalytic tape.

Let P denote deterministic polynomial time, and let NC denote the class of problems solvable by uniform Boolean circuits of polynomial size and polylogarithmic depth (with fan-in 2 gates). It is known that L ⊆ CL ⊆ ZPP, and CL contains uniform TC^1, but no nontrivial upper bound of CL inside P is known.

Problem. Assuming some believable cryptographic hardness assumption (for example, the existence of one-way functions, hardness of factoring, or hardness of discrete logarithm), prove that CL ⊆ C for some plausible proper subclass C of P. In particular, determine whether one can establish CL ⊆ NC under such a cryptographic assumption.
status_search_result: The question of placing CL in any proper subclass of P (such as NC) remains open. Recent work (2025) showing bipartite matching and linear matroid intersection lie in CL is interpreted as a barrier to placing CL in the NC hierarchy and suggests CL may be more powerful than previously believed. No cryptographic-assumption-based upper bound on CL inside NC appears to have been established.

original_question: Let f: R^n -> R be a convex function with n >= 2, and let x(t) = (t, 0, ..., 0). Assume that the gradient ∇f(x(t)) exists for every t > 0. $$\lim_{t \downarrow 0} \nabla f(x(t))$$
exist in $\mathbb{R}^n$? Equivalently, does there exist a convex function $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ (with $n \geq 2$) such that $\nabla f(x(t))$ exists for every $t > 0$ but the limit above fails to exist?

paper_title: The Strong Convergence of Subgradients of Convex Functions Along Directions: Perspectives and Open Problems
context_brief: Existence of at least one good direction
original_question: In the same setting of a convex function f on a normed space and a fixed point x, is there at least one nonzero direction w for which the directional subdifferential limit lim_{t↓0} ∂f(x + t w) exists?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, \|\cdot\|)$ be a normed (real) vector space and let $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be a continuous convex function. For each $y \in X$ let
$$\partial f(y) = \{ x^* \in X^* : f(z) \ge f(y) + \langle x^*, z - y\rangle \text{ for all } z \in X\}$$
denote the convex subdifferential of $f$ at $y$. Fix a point $x \in X$ and a nonzero direction $w \in X$. Say that the directional subdifferential limit
$$\lim_{t \downarrow 0} \partial f(x + t w)$$
exists (in the strong/norm sense) if there is a singleton $\{x^*\} \subset X^*$ such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $t_0 > 0$ with
$$\sup_{u^* \in \partial f(x + t w)} \|u^* - x^*\| < \varepsilon \quad \text{for all } 0 < t < t_0.$$

Question: Given any continuous convex function $f$ on a normed space $X$ and any point $x \in X$, does there always exist at least one nonzero direction $w \in X$ for which the above limit $\lim_{t \downarrow 0} \partial f(x + tw)$ exists?

In finite-dimensional spaces, Rademacher's theorem yields a full-measure set of good directions, but in general infinite-dimensional normed spaces examples show that the set of "bad" directions can be a dense G_δ, and no general existence result for at least one good direction at every point appears to be known.

original_question: Is it possible to construct a continuous convex function f on a separable Hilbert space such that, at every point x where the Gâteaux derivative D_G f(x) exists, the set of directions along which the directional convergence of subgradients holds is not dense in the space?
self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a separable (infinite-dimensional) Hilbert space, and let $f : H \to \mathbb{R}$ be a continuous convex function. For each $x \in H$, the subdifferential of $f$ at $x$ is
$$\partial f(x) = \{ x^* \in H : f(y) \ge f(x) + \langle x^*, y-x\rangle \text{ for all } y \in H\},$$
which is nonempty, convex, weak*-compact. The Gâteaux derivative $D_G f(x)$ exists at $x$ iff $\partial f(x)$ is a singleton, whose unique element we denote $D_G f(x)$.

For a point $x \in H$ and a unit vector $u \in H$, say that the directional convergence of subgradients holds at $x$ along $u$ if, for every sequence $t_n \downarrow 0$ and every choice $x_n^* \in \partial f(x + t_n u)$, the sequence $(x_n^*)$ converges in norm in $H$ (equivalently, the union $\bigcup_{t \in (0,\varepsilon)} \partial f(x+tu)$ is norm-relatively-compact for some $\varepsilon > 0$, and its limit as $t \downarrow 0$ exists in norm).

Let $G(f) = \{x \in H : D_G f(x) \text{ exists}\}$, and for $x \in G(f)$ let
$$\mathcal{D}(f,x) = \{ u \in H \setminus \{0\} : \text{directional convergence of subgradients holds at } x \text{ along } u/\|u\|\}.$$

Question: Does there exist a continuous convex function $f : H \to \mathbb{R}$ on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$ such that for every $x \in G(f)$, the set $\mathcal{D}(f,x)$ is not dense in $H$?

paper_title: The Strong Convergence of Subgradients of Convex Functions Along Directions: Perspectives and Open Problems
context_brief: Nearby perturbation and nearby direction question
original_question: Fix a direction w_0 and a tolerance ε > 0. For a given convex continuous function f and point x, can one find a nearby direction w with ||w_0 - w|| < ε and another convex continuous function g_ε such that |f(y) - f(x)| <= |g_ε(y) - g_ε(x)| + ε ||y - x|| for all y in X, and such that the directional subdifferential limit lim_{t↓0} ∂g_ε(x + t w) exists?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space with norm $\|\cdot\|$, and let $f: X \to \mathbb{R}$ be a convex continuous function. For $x \in X$, denote by $\partial f(x) \subset X^*$ the (Fenchel–Moreau) subdifferential of $f$ at $x$, i.e. the set of $x^* \in X^*$ such that $f(y) \ge f(x) + \langle x^*, y - x\rangle$ for all $y \in X$.

Fix a point $x \in X$, a direction $w_0 \in X$, and a tolerance $\varepsilon > 0$. Determine whether there always exist a direction $w \in X$ with $\|w_0 - w\| < \varepsilon$ and a convex continuous function $g_\varepsilon : X \to \mathbb{R}$ such that:

(i) for all $y \in X$,
$$|f(y) - f(x)| \le |g_\varepsilon(y) - g_\varepsilon(x)| + \varepsilon\, \|y - x\|;$$

(ii) the directional limit
$$\lim_{t \downarrow 0} \partial g_\varepsilon(x + t w)$$
exists (in an appropriate strong sense, e.g. each net of selections $x^*_t \in \partial g_\varepsilon(x + tw)$ converges in norm of $X^*$ as $t \downarrow 0$).
status_search_result: The question belongs to a family of problems (originating with Giannessi) on directional strong convergence of subgradients of convex functions. The general infinite-dimensional theory is not developed, and this specific perturbation question is posed as an open problem; no subsequent resolution was located in the available literature.

paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Creative Telescoping
context_brief: Reduction-based creative telescoping for mixed terms
original_question: Develop a reduction-based creative telescoping algorithm for a hypergeometric-hyperexponential term f_n(x) in the summation setting. The algorithm should compute, when possible, rational functions c_0(x), c_1(x), ..., c_r(x) in C(x), not all zero, together with a hypergeometric-hyperexponential term g_n(x), such that c_0 f_n(x) + c_1 D_x f_n(x) + ... + c_r D_x^r f_n(x) = g_{n+1}(x) - g_n(x).
self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $x, n$ be independent indeterminates. A bivariate term $f_n(x)$ is called hypergeometric–hyperexponential over $C(x,n)$ if both the shift quotient $f_{n+1}(x)/f_n(x)$ and the logarithmic derivative $(D_x f_n(x))/f_n(x)$ lie in $C(x,n)$, where $D_x$ denotes differentiation with respect to $x$ and the shift $n \mapsto n+1$ acts on $n$.

Design a reduction-based creative telescoping algorithm in the summation setting that, given such a hypergeometric–hyperexponential term $f_n(x)$, decides whether there exist a nonnegative integer $r$, rational functions $c_0(x), c_1(x), \dots, c_r(x) \in C(x)$ not all zero, and a hypergeometric–hyperexponential term $g_n(x)$ such that
$$c_0(x)\, f_n(x) + c_1(x)\, D_x f_n(x) + \cdots + c_r(x)\, D_x^{\,r} f_n(x) \;=\; g_{n+1}(x) - g_n(x),$$
and that computes such $c_0,\dots,c_r$ and $g_n$ when they exist. The algorithm should be "reduction-based" in the sense that the telescoper $L = \sum_i c_i(x) D_x^i$ is obtained from a Hermite/Abramov–Petkovšek-style reduction of the shift class of $f_n(x)$ rather than by computing a certificate directly.
status_search_result: Reduction-based creative telescoping for mixed hypergeometric–hyperexponential terms has been developed in the integration setting (Bostan–Dumont–Salvy, ISSAC 2016) and reduction-based methods have separately been developed for pure hypergeometric summation and, recently, for definite summation of D-finite functions and a unified hypergeometric/q-hypergeometric reduction. We did not find a published paper specifically presenting a reduction-based algorithm for the summation setting on mixed hypergeometric–hyperexponential terms with telescoper in $D_x$ as posed; status is unclear from the available sources.

paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Creative Telescoping
original_question: Derive an order-degree curve for general D-finite functions, meaning a bound that describes how the degree of a telescoper can depend on a chosen operator order for telescopers of those functions.
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $f(x,y)$ be a D-finite function in two variables over $K$; that is, $f$ satisfies a system of linear differential (or, more generally, Ore-algebra) equations with polynomial coefficients whose solution space is finite-dimensional. A telescoper for $f$ with respect to $y$ is a nonzero linear operator $L = \sum_{i=0}^{r} a_i(x)\, \partial_x^{\,i}$, with $a_i(x)\in K[x]$ not all zero, such that there exists a "certificate" $g$ (D-finite in the same sense) with
$$L(x,\partial_x)\, f(x,y) \;=\; \Delta_y\, g(x,y),$$
where $\Delta_y$ is either the derivation $\partial_y$ or the shift $S_y - 1$, depending on the chosen Ore setting. Define the order of $L$ to be $r = \operatorname{ord}(L)$ and its degree to be $d = \deg(L) := \max_i \deg_x a_i$.

It is known empirically that, for fixed $f$, there is a trade-off: telescopers of higher order can have lower degree, and vice versa. For several restricted classes (e.g. bivariate hypergeometric terms, hyperexponential terms, rational functions), explicit "order–degree curves" have been established—functions $\Phi$ such that, for every integer $r$ in an appropriate range, there exists a telescoper $L$ for $f$ with $\operatorname{ord}(L) \le r$ and $\deg(L) \le \Phi(r)$, with $\Phi$ typically describing a hyperbola in the $(r,d)$-plane.

Problem. For a general D-finite bivariate function $f(x,y)$ (specified by an arbitrary system of linear Ore equations satisfied by $f$), derive an explicit order–degree curve: produce an effectively computable bound $\Phi$, depending only on the input data defining $f$ (orders and degrees of the defining operators, etc.), such that for every admissible order $r$ there exists a telescoper $L$ for $f$ of order at most $r$ and degree at most $\Phi(r)$.
status_search_result: Order–degree curves have been established for restricted classes such as bivariate hypergeometric terms, hyperexponential terms, and rational functions (Bostan–Chen–Chyzak–Li–Kauers and others). For general D-finite functions, order bounds for telescopers are known, but no explicit order–degree curve has been worked out as of recent reduction-based creative telescoping work (2024). The problem appears still open.
