paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
original_question: For every probability-measure-preserving system (X, X, μ, T) and bounded measurable functions f, g, h, do the multiple ergodic averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) h(T^{3n} x) and (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N f(T^n x) g(T^{n^2} x) converge for μ-almost every x?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ be a probability-measure-preserving system; that is, $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ is a probability space and $T:X\to X$ is a measurable map with $\mu(T^{-1}A)=\mu(A)$ for every $A\in\mathcal{X}$. For functions $f,g,h\in L^\infty(\mu)$, consider the multiple ergodic averages
$$A_N(x)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(T^n x)\, g(T^{2n} x)\, h(T^{3n} x),\qquad B_N(x)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(T^n x)\, g(T^{n^2} x).$$
Prove or disprove the following:
(a) For every such system and all $f,g,h\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the sequence $A_N(x)$ converges as $N\to\infty$ for $\mu$-almost every $x\in X$.
(b) For every such system and all $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the sequence $B_N(x)$ converges as $N\to\infty$ for $\mu$-almost every $x\in X$.
status_search_result: Part (b), the bilinear average $\frac{1}{N}\sum f(T^n x)g(T^{n^2}x)$, was resolved by Krause, Mirek and Tao (Annals of Mathematics, 2022), who proved pointwise a.e. convergence for bilinear polynomial ergodic averages with a polynomial of degree $\ge 2$. Part (a), pointwise a.e. convergence of the trilinear average $\frac{1}{N}\sum f(T^n x)g(T^{2n}x)h(T^{3n}x)$ for a general measure-preserving system, remains open as of the latest available references; only norm convergence (Host–Kra, Ziegler) and special-case results (e.g., distal systems) are known.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
original_question: Let a(n) be one of the sequences of prime numbers p_n, the Hardy-type sequence [n^c] with c > 0, or the exponential sequence 2^n. For every ergodic system (X, X, μ, T) and bounded measurable f0, ..., fℓ, does the multiple correlation sequence ∫ f0 · T^{a(n)}f1 · ... · T^{ℓ a(n)}fℓ dμ always admit a decomposition ψ(a(n)) + e(n), where ψ is an ℓ-step nilsequence and the Cesàro mean of |e(n)| tends to 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell\ge 1$ be an integer and let $(a(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ denote one of the following integer sequences:
(i) $a(n)=p_n$, the $n$-th prime number;
(ii) $a(n)=\lfloor n^c\rfloor$ for a fixed real number $c>0$;
(iii) $a(n)=2^n$.

Recall that an $\ell$-step nilsequence is a sequence of the form $(F(g^n\cdot x))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, where $G/\Gamma$ is an $\ell$-step nilmanifold ($G$ a connected, simply connected nilpotent Lie group of step $\ell$ and $\Gamma$ a cocompact discrete subgroup), $g\in G$, $x\in G/\Gamma$, and $F:G/\Gamma\to\mathbb{C}$ is continuous; more generally, an $\ell$-step nilsequence is a uniform limit of such sequences.

Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ be an invertible ergodic measure-preserving system on a standard probability space, and let $f_0,f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$. Define the multiple correlation sequence
$$A(n)=\int_X f_0\cdot (T^{a(n)}f_1)\cdot (T^{2a(n)}f_2)\cdots (T^{\ell\, a(n)}f_\ell)\,d\mu.$$

Decide whether, for every such system and choice of functions, there exists a decomposition
$$A(n)=\psi(a(n))+e(n),\quad n\in\mathbb{N},$$
where $(\psi(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is an $\ell$-step nilsequence and the error sequence $(e(n))$ satisfies
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}|e(n)|=0.$$
status_search_result: For the prime case, partial results are known: a decomposition of multicorrelation sequences along primes has been established (in a commuting-transformations setting), but only in the weaker form where for every ε>0 one obtains a nilsequence plus an error term with small Cesàro and uniform averages depending on ε, rather than the single error term with vanishing Cesàro mean of |e(n)| as posed. Subsequent work on nilsequences and multiple correlations along subsequences has refined these results, but the full problem as stated for p_n, ⌊n^c⌋, and 2^n does not appear to be completely resolved.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
context_brief: Characteristic factors for commuting polynomial averages
original_question: Suppose p1, ..., pℓ are pairwise independent integer polynomials and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting measure-preserving transformations. Does there exist d such that the Host-Kra factors Z_{d,T1}, ..., Z_{d,Tℓ} are characteristic for the polynomial averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{p1(n)}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)}fℓ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T_1,\dots,T_\ell$ be commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$. For a single measure-preserving transformation $T$ and an integer $d\ge 0$, let $Z_{d,T}$ denote the $d$-th Host–Kra factor of the system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ (the factor characterized by the property that a bounded function $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}(f\mid Z_{d,T})=0$ if and only if its $(d+1)$-th Host–Kra–Gowers seminorm $\|f\|_{U^{d+1}(T)}$ vanishes).

Call integer polynomials $p_1,\dots,p_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ pairwise independent if for every $i\neq j$ the polynomials $p_i,p_j$ and the constant polynomial $1$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$ (equivalently, $p_i$, $p_j$, $p_i-p_j$ are all non-constant).

A family of factors $(Y_1,\dots,Y_\ell)$ (with $Y_i$ a $T_i$-invariant sub-$\sigma$-algebra) is called characteristic for the averages
$$A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)\;=\;\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} \big(T_1^{p_1(n)}f_1\big)\cdots\big(T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}f_\ell\big)$$
if, for all $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\Big\|A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)-A_N\big(\mathbb{E}(f_1\mid Y_1),\dots,\mathbb{E}(f_\ell\mid Y_\ell)\big)\Big\|_{L^2(\mu)}=0.$$

Problem. Show that there exists $d\in\mathbb{N}$ (depending only on $p_1,\dots,p_\ell$ and $\ell$) such that for every system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T_1,\dots,T_\ell)$ as above, the factors $Z_{d,T_1},\dots,Z_{d,T_\ell}$ are characteristic for the averages $A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)$.
status_search_result: Recent work by Frantzikinakis and Kuca (arXiv:2207.12288, "Joint ergodicity for commuting transformations and applications to polynomial sequences", 2022) proves that the Host–Kra factor is characteristic for multiple ergodic averages of commuting transformations along pairwise independent integer polynomials, without extra assumptions on the system. This appears to resolve the problem affirmatively. Related follow-up work (e.g., arXiv:2209.11033, arXiv:2410.15130) treats the pairwise dependent case.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
context_brief: Optimal lower bounds for polynomial recurrence
original_question: Suppose p1, ..., pℓ are rationally independent integer polynomials with zero constant term and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting measure-preserving transformations. For every measurable set A of positive measure and every ε > 0, must there exist n with μ(A ∩ T1^{p1(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{pℓ(n)}A) at least μ(A)^{ℓ+1} - ε?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T_1,\dots,T_\ell\colon X\to X$ be invertible, commuting, measure-preserving transformations. Let $p_1,\dots,p_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be integer polynomials with zero constant term that are rationally independent (meaning that any non-trivial rational linear combination $\sum_{i=1}^\ell c_i p_i$, with $c_i\in\mathbb{Q}$ not all zero, is a non-constant polynomial). Prove or disprove the following statement: for every measurable set $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive integer $n$ such that
$$\mu\!\left(A\cap T_1^{p_1(n)}A\cap T_2^{p_2(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}A\right)\;\ge\;\mu(A)^{\ell+1}-\varepsilon.$$
category_tag: Multiple ergodic averages and polynomial recurrence
status_search_result: The question, posed as a problem on optimal lower bounds for multiple polynomial recurrence with commuting transformations, appears to remain open in general. Related results are known: for non-commuting transformations along rationally independent polynomials in two variables, a comparable bound has been established by Frantzikinakis, and various joint ergodicity results (e.g. for polynomials of distinct degrees, or under additional ergodicity hypotheses) yield the asserted optimal bound in special cases. No source found establishes the full statement for arbitrary commuting transformations and arbitrary rationally independent polynomials.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
original_question: For every system with two commuting measure-preserving transformations T and S and bounded measurable functions f and g, do the bilinear averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N f(T^n x) g(S^n x) converge for almost every x?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $T,S:X\to X$ be two commuting measure-preserving transformations (i.e., $TS=ST$, and each preserves $\mu$). For any $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, consider the bilinear ergodic averages
$$A_N(f,g)(x) \;=\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(T^n x)\, g(S^n x).$$
Determine whether, for every such system $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T,S)$ and every $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the sequence $A_N(f,g)(x)$ converges as $N\to\infty$ for $\mu$-almost every $x\in X$.
status_search_result: Pointwise a.e. convergence of the bilinear averages (1/N)Σ f(T^n x) g(S^n x) for two general commuting measure-preserving transformations T, S is widely cited as an open problem. Recent advances (e.g., Krause–Mirek–Tao 2022) resolved related nonconventional bilinear polynomial averages for a single transformation, and norm-variation results for commuting transformations have appeared, but the a.e. convergence problem for two commuting transformations in the linear case remains open.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
original_question: Let T1, ..., Tℓ be arbitrary invertible measure-preserving transformations, not assumed to commute, and let p1, ..., pℓ be distinct integer polynomials with zero constant term. For every measurable set A with positive measure, must there exist m, n ∈ N such that μ(A ∩ T1^{m+p1(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{m+pℓ(n)}A) > 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T_1,\dots,T_\ell\colon X\to X$ be invertible measure-preserving transformations (no commutativity is assumed). Let $p_1,\dots,p_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}[n]$ be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Prove or disprove: for every $A\in\mathcal{X}$ with $\mu(A)>0$ there exist $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T_1^{m+p_1(n)}A\cap T_2^{m+p_2(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T_\ell^{m+p_\ell(n)}A\bigr)>0.$$
status_search_result: The problem has been resolved in the special case where the polynomials $p_1,\dots,p_\ell$ are rationally independent (Chu–Frantzikinakis–Host type result, 2013), using reductions to nilfactors and equidistribution on nilmanifolds. The full statement for arbitrary distinct integer polynomials with zero constant term does not appear to have a published resolution.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
original_question: Let F = {a1, ..., aℓ} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth such that every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) stays farther than O(log t) from every real multiple of every integer polynomial. For every ergodic system (X, B, μ, T) and bounded measurable f1, ..., fℓ, must the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{[a1(n)]}f1 · ... · T^{[aℓ(n)]}fℓ converge in L^2 to (∫ f1 dμ) · ... · (∫ fℓ dμ)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote a Hardy field, i.e., a field of germs at $+\infty$ of real-valued functions defined on a half-line $[c,\infty)$ that is closed under differentiation. A function $a \in \mathcal{H}$ is said to have polynomial growth if there exists $k \in \mathbb{N}$ with $a(t)/t^k \to 0$ as $t \to \infty$. 

Let $F = \{a_1, \dots, a_\ell\} \subset \mathcal{H}$ be functions of polynomial growth, and let $\operatorname{span}_*(F)$ denote the set of all nontrivial real-linear combinations $c_1 a_1 + \cdots + c_\ell a_\ell$ with $(c_1,\dots,c_\ell) \in \mathbb{R}^\ell \setminus \{0\}$. Suppose that for every $a \in \operatorname{span}_*(F)$, every $c \in \mathbb{R}$, and every polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[t]$,
$$\frac{|a(t) - c\, p(t)|}{\log t} \longrightarrow \infty \quad \text{as } t \to \infty.$$

Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ be an ergodic invertible measure-preserving system on a standard probability space, and let $f_1, \dots, f_\ell \in L^\infty(\mu)$. Prove or disprove that
$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n=1}^{N} T^{\lfloor a_1(n) \rfloor} f_1 \cdot T^{\lfloor a_2(n) \rfloor} f_2 \cdots T^{\lfloor a_\ell(n) \rfloor} f_\ell \;=\; \prod_{i=1}^{\ell} \int f_i\, d\mu$$
with convergence in $L^2(\mu)$.
category_tag: Multiple ergodic averages along Hardy sequences
status_search_result: The conjecture (joint ergodicity for Hardy-field tuples whose nontrivial linear combinations stay super-logarithmically far from real multiples of integer polynomials) has been established. Tsinas (arXiv:2109.07941, "Joint ergodicity of Hardy field sequences") proves the L^2 convergence to the product of integrals under exactly this log-t separation hypothesis, explicitly confirming Frantzikinakis's conjecture. Subsequent works (e.g., Frantzikinakis–Kuca and later papers on resolving the joint ergodicity problem for Hardy sequences) extend and reaffirm the result.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
original_question: Let F = {a1, ..., aℓ} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth such that every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) stays unboundedly far from every real multiple of every integer polynomial. Must the integer-part family {[a1(n)], ..., [aℓ(n)]} then be good for ℓ-recurrence for a single transformation?
self_contained_problem:
A Hardy field is a field of germs at $+\infty$ of real-valued functions defined on some half-line $[t_0,\infty)$ that is closed under differentiation. A function $a$ in such a field has polynomial growth if there exists $d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $a(t)/t^d\to 0$ as $t\to\infty$. 

Let $F=\{a_1,\dots,a_\ell\}$ be functions from some Hardy field, all of polynomial growth, and let $\operatorname{span}^*(F)$ denote the set of nontrivial real linear combinations $c_1 a_1+\cdots+c_\ell a_\ell$ with $(c_1,\dots,c_\ell)\in\mathbb{R}^\ell\setminus\{0\}$. Assume that for every $a\in\operatorname{span}^*(F)$, every $c\in\mathbb{R}$, and every $p\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$,
$$|a(t)-c\,p(t)|\longrightarrow\infty\quad\text{as }t\to\infty.$$

A family of integer-valued sequences $(b_1(n)),\dots,(b_\ell(n))$ is called good for $\ell$-recurrence (for a single transformation) if for every invertible measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ and every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T^{-b_1(n)}A\cap T^{-b_2(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T^{-b_\ell(n)}A\bigr)>0.$$

Prove that under the hypothesis above, the family $\{(\lfloor a_1(n)\rfloor),\dots,(\lfloor a_\ell(n)\rfloor)\}$ is good for $\ell$-recurrence for a single transformation.

status_search_result: Substantial progress on this type of conjecture has appeared in recent work on multiple ergodic averages along Hardy-field functions (e.g., Frantzikinakis–Moreira–Richter–Robertson, "Multiple ergodic averages along functions from a Hardy field," 2020/2024), which confirms several of Frantzikinakis's conjectures and yields recurrence/combinatorial consequences for such families, including mixtures of polynomial and non-polynomial Hardy functions. However, available sources do not state that the precise problem (in full generality, only under the unbounded-distance-from-real-multiples-of-integer-polynomials hypothesis) is fully resolved.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
original_question: If c > 1 is nonintegral, is the integer sequence [n^c] good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence for arbitrary commuting transformations? More specifically, for every commuting system (X, X, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) and bounded measurable f1, ..., fℓ, does the L^2-limit of (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{[n^c]}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{[n^c]}fℓ exist and equal the L^2-limit of the linear averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^n f1 · ... · Tℓ^n fℓ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $c>1$ be a non-integer real number, and write $[\,\cdot\,]$ for the integer-part (floor) function. Let $\ell\geq 1$, and let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T_1,\dots,T_\ell)$ be a measure-preserving system, meaning $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ is a probability space and $T_1,\dots,T_\ell$ are commuting measure-preserving transformations of $X$. For bounded measurable functions $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, consider the averages
$$A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell) \;=\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N T_1^{[n^c]}f_1 \cdot T_2^{[n^c]}f_2 \cdots T_\ell^{[n^c]}f_\ell$$
and
$$B_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell) \;=\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N T_1^{n}f_1 \cdot T_2^{n}f_2 \cdots T_\ell^{n}f_\ell.$$

Prove the following two statements:

(i) (Multiple recurrence) The sequence $([n^c])_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is good for multiple recurrence for commuting transformations; that is, for every such system and every $A\in\mathcal{X}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T_1^{-[n^c]}A\cap T_2^{-[n^c]}A\cap\cdots\cap T_\ell^{-[n^c]}A\bigr)>0.$$

(ii) (Multiple convergence) The $L^2(\mu)$-limit $\lim_{N\to\infty} A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)$ exists, and is equal to the $L^2(\mu)$-limit $\lim_{N\to\infty} B_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)$.
status_search_result: Norm convergence of linear multiple ergodic averages for commuting transformations is known (Tao, 2008). For fractional iterates $[n^c]$ with $c>1$ non-integer, results exist only for a single transformation or for random/Hardy-field variants; the deterministic case with arbitrary commuting transformations appears to remain open as of recent literature.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
original_question: Consider the random increasing sequence a_n(ω) obtained by selecting each integer n independently with probability σ_n, where nσ_n → ∞. Almost surely, is this random sequence good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence for commuting transformations? Equivalently, for every commuting system (X, X, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) and bounded measurable f1, ..., fℓ, do the random averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{a_n(ω)}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{a_n(ω)}fℓ converge in L^2 to the same limit as the deterministic averages along n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\sigma_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of real numbers with $0\le\sigma_n\le 1$ satisfying $n\sigma_n\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$. Construct a random increasing sequence of positive integers $(a_n(\omega))$ as follows: independently for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, include $n$ in the sequence with probability $\sigma_n$, and let $a_1(\omega)<a_2(\omega)<\cdots$ be the enumeration of the chosen integers (this is well defined almost surely since $\sum\sigma_n=\infty$).

Prove or disprove: almost surely, the sequence $(a_n(\omega))$ is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence with respect to commuting measure-preserving transformations. Precisely, show that almost surely the following holds. For every $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$, every probability space $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ equipped with commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations $T_1,\dots,T_\ell$, and all functions $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} (T_1^{a_n(\omega)}f_1)\cdots(T_\ell^{a_n(\omega)}f_\ell)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$, and the limit equals the $L^2$-limit of the deterministic averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} (T_1^{n}f_1)\cdots(T_\ell^{n}f_\ell).$$
category_tag: multiple ergodic averages along random sequences
status_search_result: Existing literature (Frantzikinakis–Lesigne–Wierdl and related works) establishes random multiple recurrence/convergence results in restricted settings — e.g. powers of a single transformation, or two commuting transformations under specific decay assumptions on σ_n such as σ_n = n^{-a} with a in a small range. No source found resolves the full problem for arbitrary ℓ commuting transformations under only the hypothesis nσ_n → ∞; the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
original_question: Let a_n(ω) and b_n(ω) be two independent random increasing sequences built from selector probabilities n^{-a} and n^{-b} with a, b in (0, 1) and a ≠ b. Almost surely, for every system (X, X, μ, T, S) and bounded measurable f and g, do the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{a_n(ω)} f · S^{b_n(ω)} g converge, in L^2 or pointwise, to E(f | I_T) · E(g | I_S)?
self_contained_problem:
Fix real numbers $a, b \in (0,1)$ with $a \neq b$. Construct two independent random increasing integer sequences as follows: on a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$, let $(\xi_n)_{n\ge1}$ and $(\eta_n)_{n\ge1}$ be independent families of independent Bernoulli random variables with $\mathbb{P}(\xi_n = 1) = n^{-a}$ and $\mathbb{P}(\eta_n = 1) = n^{-b}$. context_brief: relations among weak embeddings of L1
original_question: Suppose L1[0,1] sign-embeds into a Banach space X. Must L1[0,1] then Gδ-embed into X? Suppose instead that L1[0,1] Gδ-embeds into X. Must L1[0,1] semi-embed into X? More generally, does sign-embedding of L1[0,1] into X already imply semi-embedding of L1[0,1] into X?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $L_1 = L_1[0,1]$ denote the space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue integrable real-valued functions on $[0,1]$ with its usual norm. Recall the following notions of weak embedding of $L_1$ into $X$.

(i) A bounded linear operator $T : L_1 \to X$ is called a semi-embedding if $T$ is one-to-one and $T$ maps the closed unit ball $B_{L_1}$ to a closed subset of $X$.

(ii) A bounded linear operator $T : L_1 \to X$ is called a $G_\delta$-embedding if $T$ is one-to-one and $T(B_{L_1})$ is a $G_\delta$ subset of $X$ (i.e. a countable intersection of open sets).

(iii) A bounded linear operator $T : L_1 \to X$ is called a sign-embedding if $T$ is one-to-one and there exists $\delta > 0$ such that $\|T f\| \ge \delta$ for every $f \in L_1$ with $|f| = \mathbf 1_{[0,1]}$ a.e. (equivalently, for every $\{-1,+1\}$-valued $f$).

One says that $L_1$ sign-embeds (respectively $G_\delta$-embeds, semi-embeds) into $X$ if there exists such an operator $T : L_1 \to X$. It is known that
$$\text{semi-embedding} \Longrightarrow G_\delta\text{-embedding} \Longrightarrow \text{sign-embedding}.$$

Determine whether the following implications hold for an arbitrary Banach space $X$:

(A) If $L_1$ sign-embeds into $X$, does $L_1$ necessarily $G_\delta$-embed into $X$?

(B) If $L_1$ $G_\delta$-embeds into $X$, does $L_1$ necessarily semi-embed into $X$?

(C) If $L_1$ sign-embeds into $X$, does $L_1$ necessarily semi-embed into $X$?

context_brief: stability of narrow operators under addition
original_question: For an arbitrary Banach space X, is the sum of two narrow operators from L1[0,1] to X again a narrow operator?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a non-atomic finite measure space (for concreteness, take $[0,1]$ with Lebesgue measure) and let $L_1 = L_1[0,1]$. For a Banach space $X$, a bounded linear operator $T: L_1 \to X$ is called narrow if for every measurable set $A \subseteq [0,1]$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a function $x \in L_1$ of the form $x = \mathbf{1}_B - \mathbf{1}_{A\setminus B}$ (a sign on $A$, i.e. $|x| = \mathbf{1}_A$ and $\int_A x\,d\mu = 0$) such that $\|T x\| < \varepsilon$.

Question: Is it true that for every Banach space $X$ and every pair of narrow operators $T_1, T_2: L_1[0,1] \to X$, the sum $T_1 + T_2$ is again a narrow operator?
status_search_result: The question has been answered in the negative. A theorem of V. Mykhaylyuk and M. Popov (J. Math. Anal. Appl. 404 (2013), 554–561, "On sums of narrow operators on Köthe function spaces") shows that for every Köthe Banach space E on [0,1] — in particular for E = L_1[0,1] — there exist a Banach space X and two narrow operators from E to X whose sum is not narrow. Thus the sum-of-two-narrow-operators property of L_1 does not extend to arbitrary Banach-space-valued operators.

context_brief: Siegel disk size for quadratic polynomials
original_question: For the quadratic polynomial P_λ(z)=λ(z−z^2) with λ=e^{2πiα}, let U be Yoccoz's bounded holomorphic function on the unit disk whose boundary values recover the linearization radius r_λ, and let α range over Brjuno numbers. Is the function α ↦ B(α)+log|U(e^{2πiα})| bounded on R/Z?
self_contained_problem:
For each complex parameter $\lambda$ in the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, consider the quadratic polynomial
$$P_\lambda(z)=\lambda(z-z^2),$$
which fixes $0$ with multiplier $\lambda$. When $\lambda=e^{2\pi i\alpha}$ with $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, the map $P_\lambda$ is said to be linearizable at $0$ if there exists a holomorphic injection $\phi:\mathbb{D}_r\to\mathbb{C}$ with $\phi(0)=0$, $\phi'(0)=1$, defined on a disk of some positive radius $r>0$, such that $P_\lambda\circ\phi(z)=\phi(\lambda z)$; the supremum of such $r$ is called the linearization radius $r_\lambda$ (the conformal radius of the Siegel disk at $0$). For $|\lambda|<1$, $P_\lambda$ has an attracting fixed point at $0$ and one defines $r_\lambda$ as the conformal radius of the immediate basin.

A theorem of Yoccoz asserts that there exists a bounded holomorphic function $U:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ such that $|U(\lambda)|=r_\lambda$ for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{D}$, and that for $\lambda=e^{2\pi i\alpha}$ with $\alpha$ irrational, $P_\lambda$ is linearizable if and only if $\alpha$ is a Brjuno number. Recall that an irrational $\alpha$ is a Brjuno number if
$$B(\alpha):=\sum_{n\geq 0} \beta_{n-1}(\alpha)\,\log\frac{1}{\alpha_n}<\infty,$$
where $\alpha_0=\{\alpha\}$, $\alpha_{n+1}=\{1/\alpha_n\}$, $\beta_{-1}=1$, and $\beta_n=\alpha_0\alpha_1\cdots\alpha_n$; the function $B$ is the Brjuno function.

By Fatou's theorem the radial boundary values $U(e^{2\pi i\alpha}):=\lim_{r\to 1^-}U(re^{2\pi i\alpha})$ exist for almost every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.

Question: Does the function
$$\alpha\;\longmapsto\;B(\alpha)+\log\bigl|U(e^{2\pi i\alpha})\bigr|,$$
defined on the set of Brjuno numbers, belong to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})$?
status_search_result: Yoccoz established that the restriction of $\alpha\mapsto B(\alpha)+\log r(\alpha)$ to Brjuno numbers is bounded above and below by universal constants, answering the boundedness question affirmatively. X. Buff and A. Chéritat (Annals of Mathematics, 2006) strengthened this by showing the function extends continuously to all of $\mathbb{R}$. A finer conjecture of Marmi–Moussa–Yoccoz that the extension is 1/2-Hölder continuous remains open, but the boundedness ($L^\infty$) question itself is resolved.

paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
original_question: For the Blaschke products Q_{a,α}(z)=P_a z^2(z+a)/(1+az), where a>3 and P_a is chosen so that the restriction to the unit circle has rotation number α, suppose α is a Brjuno number. If there is a maximal interval (a0,+∞) on which Q_{a,α} is analytically conjugate to the rigid rotation R_α(z)=e^{2πiα}z, how smooth is the conjugacy at the endpoint a0, and how does that smoothness depend on α?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of degree-4 Blaschke products
$$Q_{a,\alpha}(z) = P_a\, z^2 \cdot \frac{z+a}{1+az},$$
where $a \in (3,+\infty)$ is a real parameter and $P_a \in \mathbb{S}^1$ is the unique unimodular constant chosen so that the rotation number of the restriction $Q_{a,\alpha}\!\restriction_{\mathbb{S}^1}$ to the unit circle is equal to a prescribed irrational number $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. Assume that $\alpha$ is a Brjuno number, i.e. $\sum_{n\ge 0} \frac{\log q_{n+1}}{q_n} < \infty$, where $(p_n/q_n)$ are the convergents of the continued-fraction expansion of $\alpha$.

For each such $\alpha$, suppose that there exists a maximal open interval $(a_0(\alpha), +\infty)$ with $a_0(\alpha) \ge 3$ such that for every $a \in (a_0(\alpha), +\infty)$ the restriction $Q_{a,\alpha}\!\restriction_{\mathbb{S}^1}$ is analytically conjugate to the rigid rotation $R_\alpha(z) = e^{2\pi i \alpha} z$, while $Q_{a_0(\alpha),\alpha}\!\restriction_{\mathbb{S}^1}$ is not analytically conjugate to $R_\alpha$.

Determine the regularity (e.g. $C^k$, $C^\infty$, quasisymmetric, Hölder, etc.) of the conjugacy between $Q_{a_0(\alpha),\alpha}\!\restriction_{\mathbb{S}^1}$ and $R_\alpha$ at the endpoint $a = a_0(\alpha)$, and describe how this regularity depends on the arithmetic properties of $\alpha$.
status_search_result: Recent work on Herman rings of Blaschke-type families (including surgery results showing real-analytic parametrization by the modulus of the Herman ring for Brjuno rotation numbers, and studies of degenerate Herman rings) does not appear to resolve the endpoint regularity question for the conjugacy at $a_0(\alpha)$. Surveys of Herman-ring open problems continue to list endpoint/boundary behavior questions of this kind, suggesting the precise smoothness at the endpoint and its dependence on $\alpha$ remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
original_question: Let G_s denote the Gevrey-s class of one-variable formal germs, and for r>s>0 let g_{r,s} be the set of irrational α such that every F in G_s with multiplier e^{2πiα} is conjugate to the rotation R_α by a conjugacy H in G_r. Determine the arithmetic sets g_{r,s}.
self_contained_problem:
For a real number s>0, let $G_s$ denote the Gevrey-$s$ class of formal power series $F(z)=\sum_{n\ge 1} a_n z^n \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ with $F'(0)\ne 0$, namely those formal germs satisfying a bound of the form $|a_n|\le C\,K^n (n!)^s$ for some constants $C,K>0$. For an irrational number $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, write $R_\alpha(z)=e^{2\pi i\alpha}z$ for the corresponding rotation, and say a germ $F\in G_s$ with multiplier $F'(0)=e^{2\pi i\alpha}$ is conjugate to $R_\alpha$ in $G_r$ if there exists a tangent-to-identity formal germ $H\in G_r$ with $H(0)=0$, $H'(0)=1$, such that $H^{-1}\circ F\circ H = R_\alpha$ as formal series.

For real numbers $r>s>0$, define
$$g_{r,s}\;=\;\bigl\{\,\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}\;:\;\text{every }F\in G_s\text{ with }F'(0)=e^{2\pi i\alpha}\text{ is conjugate to }R_\alpha\text{ via some }H\in G_r\,\bigr\}.$$

Determine the set $g_{r,s}$ explicitly as an arithmetic subset of $\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$; that is, characterize precisely which irrational numbers $\alpha$ belong to $g_{r,s}$ in terms of the Diophantine properties of $\alpha$ (e.g. continued fraction expansion, Brjuno-type sums).
status_search_result: The problem of fully characterizing the sets $g_{r,s}$ for $r>s>0$ appears to remain open. It is classically known that every Brjuno number lies in $g_{s,s}$ (Carletti–Marmi), and recent work (e.g. Bounemoura and collaborators on optimal linearization in non-analytic Gevrey classes for circle diffeomorphisms and vector fields on the torus) has identified weaker-than-Brjuno arithmetic conditions when one allows the conjugacy to be less regular than the germ. However, a complete description of $g_{r,s}$ for arbitrary $r>s>0$ in the germ setting has not been established.

paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
context_brief: Elliptic fixed points and KAM theory
original_question: Let f be a real-analytic symplectic diffeomorphism of R^{2n} fixing the origin, with linear part conjugate to a product of planar rotations and with Diophantine rotation vector α. Does there exist ε0>0 such that the ball ||z||≤ε0 contains a subset of positive Lebesgue measure consisting of invariant Lagrangian tori of f?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^{2n}\to\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ be a real-analytic symplectic diffeomorphism (with respect to the standard symplectic form) fixing the origin. Assume that its linearization $Df(0)\in\mathrm{Sp}(2n,\mathbb{R})$ is conjugate to the direct product of planar rotations by angles $2\pi\alpha_1,\dots,2\pi\alpha_n$, and that the frequency vector $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfies a Diophantine condition: there exist $\gamma>0$ and $\tau>0$ such that for every $k\in\mathbb{Z}^n\setminus\{0\}$ and every $\ell\in\mathbb{Z}$,
$$|\langle k,\alpha\rangle-\ell|\geq \gamma\,|k|^{-\tau}.$$
An invariant Lagrangian torus of $f$ is an embedded $n$-dimensional torus $T\subset\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ that is Lagrangian for the standard symplectic form and satisfies $f(T)=T$.

Prove or disprove: there exists $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that the closed ball $\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}:\|z\|\leq\varepsilon_0\}$ contains a subset of positive Lebesgue measure consisting of invariant Lagrangian tori of $f$.
status_search_result: This is Herman's conjecture (posed at the 1998 ICM) on accumulation of an elliptic fixed point by KAM tori of positive measure. It is established for $n=2$ degrees of freedom and, in higher dimensions, under a Rüssmann transversality condition on the Birkhoff normal form (Eliasson–Fayad–Krikorian); Eliasson–Fayad–Krikorian also showed accumulation by complex-analytic KAM tori in general. The full conjecture without nondegeneracy assumptions remains open.

paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
original_question: Consider a Z^k-action on R^n, with k>n, whose generators are analytically close to translations x↦x+α_i and are C^0-conjugate to those translations. For which rotation vectors α_1,…,α_k must that C^0 conjugacy actually be analytic?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ and $k > n$ be integers, and let $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k \in \mathbb{R}^n$ be vectors that generate $\mathbb{R}^n$ as a real vector space. For each $i$, let $R_{\alpha_i}: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ denote the translation $x \mapsto x + \alpha_i$. These translations commute and define a $\mathbb{Z}^k$-action on $\mathbb{R}^n$ by translations.

Consider real-analytic diffeomorphisms $f_1, \dots, f_k \in \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ that pairwise commute, are sufficiently close to $R_{\alpha_1}, \dots, R_{\alpha_k}$ in the real-analytic topology, and thus define a $\mathbb{Z}^k$-action on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Assume there exists a homeomorphism $h: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ such that
$$ h \circ f_i \circ h^{-1} = R_{\alpha_i} \quad \text{for all } i = 1, \dots, k, $$
i.e., the action is $C^0$-conjugate to the translation action.

Determine, in terms of arithmetic (Diophantine-type) conditions on the rotation vectors $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k$, for which choices of $(\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k)$ the conjugating homeomorphism $h$ must be real-analytic.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem on rigidity of higher-rank abelian translation actions under small-divisor (Diophantine) conditions. Web searches did not reveal a published resolution identifying the precise class of rotation vectors $(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)$ for which $C^0$-conjugacy to a translation action automatically upgrades to analytic conjugacy. Related KAM-type rigidity results exist for higher-rank actions, but a complete characterization for this $\mathbb{Z}^k$-on-$\mathbb{R}^n$ setting with $k>n$ does not appear to be established.

paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
original_question: Let V be a compact smooth manifold and f a smooth diffeomorphism of V. Suppose that for every smooth function φ on V there exist a smooth function ψ and a real constant λ such that ψ∘f−ψ=φ+λ. Must V be a torus and f be C^∞-conjugate to a Diophantine translation?
self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a compact smooth (i.e. $C^\infty$) manifold without boundary, and let $f\colon V\to V$ be a $C^\infty$-diffeomorphism. Assume that $f$ is cohomologically rigid in the following sense: for every smooth function $\varphi\in C^\infty(V)$, there exist a smooth function $\psi\in C^\infty(V)$ and a real constant $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$\psi\circ f-\psi=\varphi+\lambda.$$
A translation $T_\alpha\colon x\mapsto x+\alpha$ on the torus $\mathbb T^d=\mathbb R^d/\mathbb Z^d$ is called Diophantine if there exist constants $C>0$ and $\tau>0$ such that for every $k\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}$ one has $|\langle k,\alpha\rangle-n|\geq C|k|^{-\tau}$ for all $n\in\mathbb Z$.

Prove or disprove: under the above hypothesis, $V$ must be diffeomorphic to a torus $\mathbb T^d$ and $f$ must be $C^\infty$-conjugate to a Diophantine translation of $\mathbb T^d$.
status_search_result: The question is the Herman cohomological rigidity conjecture for diffeomorphisms. It remains open in full generality. The analogous Katok conjecture for vector fields has been established in dimension 3 (Federico Rodriguez Hertz–Kocsard and collaborators), and several partial results are known (e.g., in the almost reducibility regime for quasi-periodic cocycles, and for circle diffeomorphisms via Herman's theory), but no complete proof or counterexample is known for diffeomorphisms of arbitrary compact manifolds.

paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
original_question: Given a smooth twist diffeomorphism with a rotational invariant curve that is not smooth, can that invariant curve be destroyed by an arbitrarily small C^∞ perturbation?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f\colon \mathbb{A} \to \mathbb{A}$ be a $C^\infty$ twist diffeomorphism of the annulus $\mathbb{A} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R}$ (i.e., a diffeomorphism isotopic to the identity which, when lifted to $\mathbb{R}^2$, satisfies the monotone twist condition $\partial \tilde f_1/\partial y > 0$, where $\tilde f(x,y) = (\tilde f_1(x,y), \tilde f_2(x,y))$). A rotational invariant curve for $f$ is an $f$-invariant homotopically nontrivial simple closed curve in $\mathbb{A}$; by Birkhoff's theorem, any such curve is the graph of a Lipschitz function over the base circle.

Suppose that $f$ possesses a rotational invariant curve $\Gamma$ which is not of class $C^\infty$. Determine whether, for every neighborhood $\mathcal{U}$ of $f$ in the $C^\infty$ topology on the space of diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{A}$, there exists $g \in \mathcal{U}$ such that $g$ has no rotational invariant curve in a neighborhood of $\Gamma$ (equivalently, the invariant curve $\Gamma$ can be destroyed by an arbitrarily small $C^\infty$ perturbation).
status_search_result: The question is a problem attributed to J. Mather concerning destruction of non-smooth invariant curves of smooth twist diffeomorphisms. Mather and others have established destruction results for invariant circles of given (Liouville or other) rotation numbers, and there is a substantial body of work on quantitative destruction. However, the precise statement—whether any rotational invariant curve that fails to be $C^\infty$ can be destroyed by an arbitrarily small $C^\infty$ perturbation—does not appear to have a clearly recorded full resolution in the sources found. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
context_brief: Hausdorff dimension of non-curve Aubry-Mather sets
original_question: For a C^r twist area-preserving diffeomorphism with r≥3, is the union of the action-minimizing invariant sets that are neither closed curves nor periodic orbits always of Hausdorff dimension 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A = \mathbb{T} \times \mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{T} \times [0,1]$) be the annulus, and let $f : A \to A$ be a $C^r$ area-preserving diffeomorphism with $r \ge 3$ satisfying the twist condition (in suitable coordinates $(x,y)$, lifting $f$ to $\tilde f(x,y) = (X(x,y), Y(x,y))$ on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}$, one has $\partial X/\partial y > 0$). An $f$-invariant set $K \subset A$ is called action-minimizing (Aubry–Mather) if it is the support of an invariant Borel probability measure that minimizes the average of a generating-function action among all $f$-invariant probability measures with the same rotation number; equivalently, every orbit in $K$ is globally action-minimizing with respect to a generating function for $f$. Define
$$ \mathcal{M}(f) = \bigcup \bigl\{ K : K \text{ is an action-minimizing invariant set of } f,\ K \text{ is not a closed (rotational) invariant curve, and } K \text{ contains no periodic orbit}\bigr\}. $$
Is it true that $\dim_H \mathcal{M}(f) = 0$, where $\dim_H$ denotes Hausdorff dimension?
status_search_result: The question (attributed to M. Herman) about whether the union of non-curve, periodic-orbit-free Aubry–Mather sets of a smooth twist area-preserving diffeomorphism has Hausdorff dimension zero is reported as an open problem in dynamical systems. While related results exist (e.g. work on hyperbolic Aubry–Mather sets being C¹-irregular and on Hausdorff dimension of the Mather quotient by Fathi–Figalli–Rifford), no proof or counterexample resolving Herman's question appears in the literature.

context_brief: Birkhoff problem for the n-body problem
original_question: In the three-body problem (n=2), assuming the total energy is negative and even restricting to planar motion, can the moment of inertia grow to infinity as t→∞ for a dense open set of initial conditions? The source also asks the analogous question for n>2.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Newtonian n+1-body problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$: point masses $m_0, m_1, \dots, m_n > 0$ with positions $q_0(t), \dots, q_n(t) \in \mathbb{R}^d$ evolving according to
$$ m_i \ddot q_i = \sum_{j \neq i} \frac{m_i m_j (q_j - q_i)}{\|q_j - q_i\|^3}, \qquad i = 0, 1, \dots, n. $$
The total energy is $H = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_i m_i \|\dot q_i\|^2 - \sum_{i<j} \frac{m_i m_j}{\|q_i - q_j\|}$, and the moment of inertia about the center of mass is
$$ I(t) = \sum_{i=0}^n m_i \|q_i(t) - q_{\mathrm{cm}}\|^2, \qquad q_{\mathrm{cm}} = \frac{\sum_i m_i q_i}{\sum_i m_i}. $$
Restrict to initial conditions with $H < 0$ (negative total energy), so that the system is bounded in mean (and one may further restrict to planar motion, $d = 2$).

(a) For $n = 2$ (the three-body problem in the plane with negative total energy), is it true that the set of initial conditions for which $I(t) \to \infty$ as $t \to \infty$ contains a dense open subset of the phase space of bounded-energy initial data?

(b) Answer the analogous question for general $n \geq 3$.
status_search_result: Birkhoff's question on whether $I(t) \to \infty$ on a dense open set of negative-energy initial conditions in the three-body problem appears still open. Recent work (e.g., on three-body orbits with large potential) revisits Birkhoff's arguments and constructs orbits with $\limsup I(t) = \infty$ in open sets of initial data, but does not establish density or settle the conjecture. No source in the search shows the conjecture has been proved or disproved.

paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
original_question: Show that any generic analytic one-parameter family of linear quasiperiodic skew-product systems that is sufficiently close to constant coefficients is reducible for almost every parameter value.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\omega \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be a fixed Diophantine frequency vector, and consider one-parameter families $\{A_\lambda\}_{\lambda \in I}$ (with $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ a parameter interval) of analytic maps $A_\lambda : \mathbb{T}^d \to G$, where $G$ is a (semisimple) matrix Lie group such as $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$, $SU(2)$, or more generally a compact or noncompact reductive group. To each $A_\lambda$ one associates the linear quasiperiodic skew-product (cocycle) on $\mathbb{T}^d \times \mathbb{C}^n$ defined by
$$ (\theta, v) \longmapsto (\theta + \omega, \; A_\lambda(\theta) v). $$
Such a cocycle is called reducible if there exists an analytic map $B : \mathbb{T}^d \to G$ (possibly on a double cover) and a constant matrix $C \in G$ such that
$$ B(\theta + \omega)^{-1} A_\lambda(\theta) B(\theta) = C \quad \text{for all } \theta \in \mathbb{T}^d. $$
Assume the family $\lambda \mapsto A_\lambda$ is analytic and sufficiently close to a constant family (i.e., $A_\lambda(\theta)$ is uniformly close to a $\theta$-independent matrix on a complex neighborhood of $\mathbb{T}^d$).

Prove that for a generic such analytic one-parameter family that is sufficiently close to constant coefficients, the cocycle defined by $A_\lambda$ is reducible for Lebesgue-almost every parameter $\lambda \in I$.
status_search_result: The full statement, asking for almost-everywhere reducibility along generic analytic one-parameter families near constant coefficients in arbitrary Lie groups, remains a guiding conjecture in the area. context_brief: Absolutely continuous spectrum from measurable Bloch waves
original_question: Consider the discrete quasiperiodic Schrödinger equation. Suppose there is a measurable function E_∞(α) and, for almost every α, a measurable L^2(T^d) function u_n(α) such that u_n=e^{inα}u_n(θ+nω) gives a solution and such that whenever E_∞(Y) has measure zero, the Haar measure of Y is also zero. Consider the discrete quasiperiodic Schrödinger equation on $\mathbb{Z}$,
$$(H_{\theta,\omega}\psi)_n = \psi_{n+1} + \psi_{n-1} + V(\theta + n\omega)\,\psi_n = E\,\psi_n,$$
where $V \in C^0(\mathbb{T}^d,\mathbb{R})$ is a real-valued function on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d = \mathbb{R}^d/\mathbb{Z}^d$, $\omega \in \mathbb{T}^d$ is a fixed rationally independent frequency vector, and $\theta \in \mathbb{T}^d$ is a phase. (i) a measurable function $E_\infty : \mathbb{T} \to \mathbb{R}$, and
(ii) for almost every $\alpha \in \mathbb{T}$, a measurable map $\theta \mapsto u(\theta;\alpha) \in L^2(\mathbb{T}^d)$ (also measurable in $\alpha$) such that the sequence
$$\psi_n(\theta;\alpha) = e^{i n \alpha} u(\theta + n\omega;\alpha), \qquad n \in \mathbb{Z},$$
solves the equation above with $E = E_\infty(\alpha)$ for almost every $\theta$.

original_question: Find a non-perturbative method for constructing time-periodic solutions of a Hamiltonian PDE, excluding traveling-wave solutions.
self_contained_problem:

   u_t = J ∇H(u),
where u(t,x) belongs to a suitable function space over a spatial domain (e.g. the torus T^d or an interval with appropriate boundary conditions), J is a symplectic structure, and H is a Hamiltonian functional. paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
context_brief: Lower bound for plane spanning ratio
original_question: Determine the best possible universal lower bound on the spanning ratio of plane geometric graphs. More specifically, does there exist a real number t greater than √2.005367532 and a finite planar point set P such that every triangulation of P has spanning ratio at least t?
self_contained_problem:
For a finite point set P in the Euclidean plane, a triangulation of P is a maximal plane straight-line graph whose vertex set is P. For a plane straight-line graph G with vertex set P, the spanning ratio (stretch factor, or dilation) of G is

  sr(G) = max_{u,v ∈ P, u ≠ v} d_G(u,v) / |uv|,

where d_G(u,v) is the length of a shortest path from u to v in G (edges weighted by Euclidean length) and |uv| is the Euclidean distance. For a finite point set P, let

  τ(P) = inf { sr(T) : T is a triangulation of P },

and define the universal lower bound

  t* = sup_P τ(P),

where the supremum is taken over all finite planar point sets P.

It is known that t* ≥ √2.005367532. Determine the exact value of t*. In particular, decide whether there exists a real number t > √2.005367532 and a finite planar point set P such that every triangulation of P has spanning ratio at least t.
status_search_result: The best known universal lower bound for the spanning ratio of plane geometric graphs/triangulations remains close to √2.005367532 ≈ 1.4161. Subsequent work by Dumitrescu and Ghosh (2016) raised the lower bound for general plane spanners to 1.4308 using a 23-point configuration, but for triangulations specifically the question of whether the bound can be strictly improved above √2.005367532 does not appear to have been resolved in the recent literature, and the exact value of the supremum remains unknown.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Determine the best possible lower bound on the worst-case spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation. In particular, can one construct a planar point set whose Delaunay triangulation has spanning ratio strictly greater than 1.5932, and can one do so with the points restricted to convex position so that the spanning ratio is strictly greater than 1.581?
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set P of points in the Euclidean plane in general position, let DT(P) denote the Delaunay triangulation of P, i.e., the planar straight-line graph in which a triangle uvw with vertices in P is a face if and only if the open disk with u, v, w on its boundary contains no point of P in its interior. For two points u, v in P, let d_DT(u, v) denote the length (sum of Euclidean edge lengths) of a shortest path between u and v in DT(P), and let |uv| denote the Euclidean distance between u and v. The spanning ratio of DT(P) is defined as
  sr(P) = max_{u,v ∈ P, u ≠ v} d_DT(u, v) / |uv|,
and the worst-case spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation is
  ρ = sup_{P} sr(P),
where the supremum is taken over all finite point sets P in general position in the plane.

(a) Determine the best possible lower bound on ρ. In particular, exhibit (or prove the nonexistence of) a finite planar point set P such that sr(P) > 1.5932.

(b) Let ρ_conv = sup{ sr(P) : P is a finite point set in convex position in the plane }. Determine the best possible lower bound on ρ_conv. In particular, exhibit (or prove the nonexistence of) a finite point set P in convex position such that sr(P) > 1.581.

For convex position, lower bounds near 1.58 are known but the gap with the upper bound (~2.33 by Cui–Kanj–Xia) persists. paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
context_brief: Complexity of minimum spanning ratio graph
original_question: Given a finite planar point set, determine whether computing a plane geometric graph on that point set whose spanning ratio is minimum among all plane geometric graphs on the same vertex set is NP-hard.
self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane. A plane geometric graph on $P$ is an undirected graph $G=(P,E)$ whose vertex set is $P$, whose edges are straight-line segments between points of $P$ weighted by their Euclidean length, and such that no two edges cross in their relative interiors. For two vertices $u,v \in P$, let $d_G(u,v)$ denote the shortest-path distance in $G$ (with Euclidean edge weights) and let $|uv|$ denote the Euclidean distance. The spanning ratio (or stretch factor / dilation) of a connected plane geometric graph $G$ on $P$ is
$$\mathrm{sr}(G) \;=\; \max_{u\ne v \in P} \frac{d_G(u,v)}{|uv|}.$$
Define $\mathrm{sr}^*(P) = \inf\{\mathrm{sr}(G) : G \text{ is a connected plane geometric graph on } P\}$.

Decide the computational complexity of the following problem: given a finite point set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ (with rational coordinates) and a rational threshold $t \ge 1$, determine whether there exists a connected plane geometric graph $G$ on $P$ with $\mathrm{sr}(G) \le t$. Equivalently, is the problem of computing (or approximating) a plane geometric graph on $P$ whose spanning ratio equals $\mathrm{sr}^*(P)$ NP-hard?
status_search_result: The question of whether computing the plane graph of minimum spanning ratio (minimum dilation/stretch factor) over a given planar point set is NP-hard appears to remain open. Related variants have been resolved: computing a minimum-dilation spanning tree is NP-hard, computing a minimum-dilation graph with at most m edges on n points is NP-hard (with or without crossings), and the minimum-weight Euclidean t-spanner problem is NP-hard. However, no source found settles NP-hardness specifically for the minimum-spanning-ratio plane graph problem without an edge-count or weight constraint.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Suppose a plane geometric graph on a finite planar point set has the α-diamond property for some fixed α and also has the d-good polygon property for some fixed d ≥ 1. Can the known general upper bound 8d(π − α)^2/(α^2 sin^2(α/4)) on its spanning ratio be improved to a strictly smaller bound?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the plane, and let $G=(P,E)$ be a plane straight-line graph on $P$ (i.e., a planar graph whose edges are non-crossing straight-line segments between points of $P$). For a parameter $0<\alpha<\pi/2$, say that $G$ has the $\alpha$-diamond property if, for every edge $e=uv\in E$, at least one of the two isosceles triangles having $e$ as base and base angle $\alpha$ (one on each side of $e$) contains no point of $P\setminus\{u,v\}$ in its interior. For a parameter $d\ge 1$, say that $G$ has the $d$-good polygon property if, for every face $F$ of $G$ and every pair of vertices $u,v$ on the boundary of $F$ such that the open segment $uv$ lies in the interior of $F$, the shorter of the two boundary paths from $u$ to $v$ along $\partial F$ has Euclidean length at most $d\cdot\|u-v\|$.

The spanning ratio of $G$ is $\sup_{u\ne v\in P} \frac{d_G(u,v)}{\|u-v\|}$, where $d_G$ denotes shortest-path distance in $G$ using Euclidean edge lengths.

It is known that any such $G$ satisfying both properties has spanning ratio at most
$$\frac{8d(\pi-\alpha)^2}{\alpha^2\sin^2(\alpha/4)}.$$

Question: Can this upper bound be replaced by a strictly smaller function of $\alpha$ and $d$ that still holds for every finite point set $P$ and every plane straight-line graph $G$ on $P$ with the $\alpha$-diamond property and the $d$-good polygon property?
status_search_result: The known upper bound $8d(\pi-\alpha)^2/(\alpha^2\sin^2(\alpha/4))$ was established as a generalization/slight improvement of Das–Joseph-type bounds for plane graphs with the $\alpha$-diamond and $d$-good polygon properties. Recent searches turn up no published improvement of this constant, and the question is listed as an open problem in the standard survey on plane geometric spanners.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Determine whether the guaranteed α-value in the α-diamond-property analysis of minimum-weight triangulations can be improved beyond π/8.
self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane in general position. A triangulation of $P$ is a maximal planar straight-line graph whose vertex set is $P$. The minimum-weight triangulation $MWT(P)$ is the triangulation of $P$ minimizing the total Euclidean length of its edges.

For an angle $\alpha \in (0, \pi/2)$, a straight-line edge $e = uv$ is said to have the $\alpha$-diamond property (with respect to $P$) if at least one of the two isosceles triangles having $e$ as a base and base angle $\alpha$ contains no point of $P \setminus \{u,v\}$ in its interior. A planar graph $G$ on $P$ has the $\alpha$-diamond property if every edge of $G$ has it. It is known that any planar graph on $P$ whose edges all satisfy the $\alpha$-diamond property is a geometric spanner of the complete Euclidean graph on $P$, with stretch factor bounded by a function of $\alpha$ alone.

It is known that every edge of $MWT(P)$ satisfies the $\alpha$-diamond property for $\alpha = \pi/8$. Determine the largest value of $\alpha$ such that every edge of every minimum-weight triangulation of every finite planar point set $P$ in general position is guaranteed to satisfy the $\alpha$-diamond property. In particular, decide whether this largest value strictly exceeds $\pi/8$.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has improved the diamond-property angle guaranteed by minimum-weight triangulations beyond π/8: Drysdale, McElfresh, and Snoeyink improved the angle to roughly π/4.6, and related works (Das–Joseph; Cheng–Xu, etc.) further refined diamond-property analyses. However, the exact largest angle α for which every edge of every MWT is guaranteed to have the α-diamond property does not appear to be settled, so the problem is partially resolved rather than fully closed.

original_question: For β-skeletons with parameter β in the interval [1, 2], determine whether the known upper bound (n−1)^γ on the spanning ratio, where γ = 1 − log2(√(2/β)), is tight for all β in that range.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of n points in the plane in general position. For a real parameter β ≥ 1, the β-skeleton of P is the undirected graph on vertex set P in which two distinct points p, q ∈ P are joined by an edge if and only if the open "lune" region

  L_β(p,q) = D_1 ∩ D_2,

contains no point of P \ {p,q}, where D_1 and D_2 are the two open disks of radius (β/2)·|pq| whose boundaries pass through p and q and whose centers lie on the line through p and q at distance (β/2 - 1/2)·|pq| on opposite sides of the midpoint of pq (so β = 1 yields the Gabriel graph GG and β = 2 yields the relaxed/relative neighborhood graph RNG, in the "lune-based" definition).

The spanning ratio of a connected geometric graph G on P is

  sr(G) = max_{p,q ∈ P, p ≠ q}  d_G(p,q) / |pq|,

where d_G is shortest-path distance in G with Euclidean edge weights. For β ∈ [1,2], it is known that every β-skeleton on n points satisfies

  sr ≤ (n − 1)^γ,   where γ = 1 − log₂(√(2/β)).

The bound is known to be tight at the endpoints β = 1 (Gabriel graph) and β = 2 (relative neighborhood graph).

Problem. Decide whether the upper bound sr ≤ (n−1)^γ is tight for every β ∈ [1,2]; that is, for each β ∈ [1,2], does there exist, for arbitrarily large n, an n-point set P in the plane whose β-skeleton has spanning ratio Θ((n−1)^γ)?

Discrete Math., 2006, building on a 2002 conference version), is known to be tight only at the endpoints β = 1 (Gabriel graph) and β = 2 (relative neighborhood graph). No source found establishes tightness for intermediate β, and the question of closing the gap appears to remain open.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Determine the smallest possible maximum degree of a plane spanner that is required to be a subgraph of the standard Euclidean Delaunay triangulation of the input point set.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in general position in the Euclidean plane, and let DT(P) denote its (standard) Euclidean Delaunay triangulation: the straight-line plane graph in which two points p, q ∈ P are joined by an edge if and only if there exists a closed disk that has p and q on its boundary and contains no other point of P in its interior.

For a real number t ≥ 1, a geometric graph G on the vertex set P (with straight-line edges weighted by Euclidean distance) is called a t-spanner of P if for every pair of points p, q ∈ P, the length of a shortest path from p to q in G is at most t · |pq|, where |pq| denotes the Euclidean distance. The graph G is called plane if its edges do not cross.

Define
   d* := inf { Δ : there exists a constant t ≥ 1 such that, for every finite point set P in general position in the plane, there is a plane t-spanner of P that is a subgraph of DT(P) and has maximum vertex degree at most Δ }.

Determine the exact value of d*.
status_search_result: The best known upper bound is maximum degree 7, achieved by Bonichon, Gavoille, Hanusse and Ilcinkas (2010), giving a plane constant-spanner that is a subgraph of the Delaunay triangulation with max degree 7. No matching lower bound is known; if one requires the spanner to be a subgraph of DT(P), the optimal maximum degree remains undetermined. Subsequent works that achieve smaller degree (6, 4, …) drop the subgraph-of-Delaunay requirement. The problem appears to still be open as of the most recent literature.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Decide whether the planarity requirement forces a worst-case lower bound on maximum degree that is strictly larger than 3 for geometric spanners. Equivalently, for every real t > 1, must there exist a planar point set P such that every plane degree-3 spanning graph on P has spanning ratio greater than t?
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane. A geometric graph on P is a graph whose vertex set is P and whose edges are straight line segments between pairs of points of P, with the weight of each edge equal to the Euclidean distance between its endpoints. Such a graph is called plane if no two of its edges cross. For t ≥ 1, a geometric graph G on P is a t-spanner of P if for every pair of points p, q ∈ P the length of a shortest path between p and q in G is at most t · |pq|; the spanning ratio of G is the infimum of such t. The maximum degree of G is the largest number of edges of G incident to a single vertex.

Determine whether the planarity constraint forces a worst-case lower bound on the maximum degree that is strictly larger than 3. Equivalently, prove or disprove the following statement:

For every real number t > 1, there exists a finite point set P ⊂ ℝ² (in general position) such that every plane spanning subgraph of the complete geometric graph on P with maximum degree at most 3 has spanning ratio greater than t.

(In other words: is there a constant t > 1 and a construction that produces, for every finite point set P in general position in the plane, a plane t-spanner of P with maximum degree at most 3?)
status_search_result: The question of whether every finite planar point set in general position admits a plane t-spanner of maximum degree 3 with constant t (and dually, whether planarity forces a degree-3 lower bound) appears still open. Constructions of plane degree-3 spanners are known only in restricted settings: for points in convex position a plane (3+4π)/3-spanner of degree 3 is known (Biniaz–Bose et al., 2016/2017), and for general position only via the addition of a linear number of Steiner points. No subsequent work appears to have resolved the unrestricted general-position case.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: For finite planar point sets, improve the dependence on ε in constructions of plane Steiner (1 + ε)-spanners; in particular, can one obtain such spanners using asymptotically fewer Steiner points than the O(n/ε^4) bound described in the paper?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane, and let $\varepsilon > 0$. A plane Steiner $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner for $P$ is a planar straight-line graph $G = (V, E)$ in the plane with $P \subseteq V$ (vertices in $V \setminus P$ are called Steiner points) such that for every pair $p, q \in P$ the shortest-path distance from $p$ to $q$ in $G$ (where each edge has Euclidean length) is at most $(1+\varepsilon)\,\|p-q\|_2$. A classical construction yields such a spanner whose total number of vertices (equivalently, number of Steiner points) is $O(n/\varepsilon^{4})$.

Determine the optimal dependence on $\varepsilon$ in the size of plane Steiner $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanners. In particular, prove or disprove: for every finite planar point set of size $n$ and every $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, there exists a plane Steiner $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner with $o(n/\varepsilon^{4})$ vertices (and provide matching upper and lower bounds on the worst-case size as a function of $n$ and $\varepsilon$).
status_search_result: Recent work has substantially improved the O(n/ε^4) bound. A construction giving Euclidean noncrossing Steiner (1+ε)-spanners with O(n/ε^{3/2}) edges has been established for n points in the plane, together with an almost matching lower bound of Ω(n/ε^{3/2-μ}) for any μ>0. This essentially resolves the size question up to subpolynomial factors in ε, although closing the remaining gap (the μ>0 slack) and analogous questions for related spanner notions remain.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Determine the exact dilation of the five vertices of a regular pentagon in the plane.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite point set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, define the dilation (or stretch factor) of $S$ as
$$\Delta(S) \;=\; \inf_{G} \; \max_{p \neq q \in S} \; \frac{d_G(p,q)}{\|p-q\|_2},$$
where the infimum is taken over all finite plane (i.e. non-crossing) straight-line graphs $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose vertex set contains $S$, $d_G(p,q)$ denotes the length of a shortest path in $G$ between $p$ and $q$ (measured as the sum of Euclidean edge lengths), and $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the Euclidean norm. Edges of $G$ are straight-line segments and additional Steiner points are allowed.

Let $S_5 \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be the set of five vertices of a regular pentagon. Determine the exact value of $\Delta(S_5)$.
status_search_result: The problem of determining the exact dilation of the five vertices of a regular pentagon appears to remain open. The best known upper bound for general regular polygons has been improved (e.g., to about 1.4482 for arbitrary regular n-gons), and a specific upper bound of 1.02046 is known for the pentagon, but no matching lower bound or exact value has been published. No source was found announcing a definitive solution.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: In the constrained visibility-graph setting, where one is given a finite point set P and a noncrossing set L of constrained line segments and studies plane constrained spanners of the visibility graph VIS(P, L), determine the constrained analogues of the open questions from the unconstrained plane-spanner setting, since the constrained model generalizes the unconstrained one.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the plane and let L be a finite set of line segments with endpoints in P such that no two segments of L cross in their interiors (a noncrossing constraint set). The visibility graph VIS(P, L) has vertex set P, and an edge uv whenever the open segment uv is not properly intersected by any segment of L (segments of L are themselves considered visible). A plane constrained spanner of VIS(P, L) is a planar subgraph G of VIS(P, L), containing L, whose Euclidean stretch factor relative to VIS(P, L) is bounded by a constant t; that is, for every edge uv of VIS(P, L), the shortest-path distance in G between u and v (using Euclidean edge weights) is at most t times the length |uv|.

Determine, in this constrained setting, the analogues of the principal open quantitative questions known for unconstrained plane spanners. Concretely:

(a) What is the smallest constant t for which, for every finite point set P and every noncrossing constraint set L, there exists a plane constrained t-spanner of VIS(P, L)?

(b) What is the smallest constant t for which, for every such (P, L), there exists a plane constrained t-spanner of VIS(P, L) of bounded maximum degree, and what is the minimum degree bound achievable simultaneously with a given t?

(c) Establish matching lower bounds (impossibility results) on t in (a) and (b).

The task is to settle these constants and tradeoffs, or to obtain improved upper and lower bounds beyond the currently known ones.
status_search_result: Research on plane constrained spanners of visibility graphs is active. Known results include that the constrained half-Θ₆-graph is a plane 2-spanner of VIS(P,L), the constrained Delaunay triangulation is a 2.42-spanner, and bounded-degree constructions exist with various stretch factors. However, the optimal stretch factor for plane constrained spanners and tight degree-stretch tradeoffs remain unresolved, mirroring the corresponding open problems in the unconstrained setting.

paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
original_question: For the critically loaded finite-capacity queue GI/G/1/K with arrival rate λ equal to service rate μ, renewal inter-arrival process with squared coefficient of variation c_a^2, i.i.d. service times with squared coefficient of variation c_s^2, and K finite buffer capacity, does the BRAVO effect hold in the sense that the long-run departure-process variability parameter γ* satisfies γ* = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) as K grows, at least for light-tailed inter-arrival and service-time distributions? Equivalently, is the large-K critical-load analogue of the known GI/G/1 and M/M/1/K formulas given by the factor 1/3 multiplying c_a^2 + c_s^2?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with finite buffer capacity K (so the system holds at most K customers including the one in service; arriving customers finding the buffer full are lost). Inter-arrival times form a renewal process with rate λ and squared coefficient of variation c_a^2, and service times are i.i.d., independent of arrivals, with rate μ and squared coefficient of variation c_s^2. Assume the critical loading λ = μ and that both inter-arrival and service-time distributions are light-tailed (e.g., have all exponential moments finite in a neighborhood of 0).

Let D(t) denote the number of customers that have departed (completed service) by time t, and define the asymptotic variability parameter of the departure process by
   γ* := lim_{t→∞} Var(D(t)) / E[D(t)],
assuming this limit exists.

Prove or disprove the following: as K → ∞,
   γ* = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K).

That is, establish whether the BRAVO (Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs) phenomenon, known to hold with factor 1/3 in the infinite-buffer GI/G/1 critical case and in the M/M/1/K critical case, extends to the general critically loaded GI/G/1/K queue under light-tailed assumptions, with the indicated O(1/K) correction.
status_search_result: The conjecture appears to remain open. Subsequent work has settled BRAVO for the infinite-buffer GI/G/1 critical queue and for many-server QED systems with finite buffers, and the M/M/1/K case is known explicitly, but no published result establishes the (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) formula for the general critically loaded GI/G/1/K queue with light-tailed inter-arrival and service distributions.

paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
original_question: Why do heavy-tailed Weibull inter-arrival and service distributions appear to follow the same GI/G/1/K BRAVO behavior predicted by Conjecture 1, while Lognormal and Pareto distributions with the same first two moments appear to show a different asymptotic departure-variance behavior? More concretely, what mathematical property separates the distributions that converge to the conjectured factor 1/3 from those that appear to converge to a different limit or to converge much more slowly?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with a finite buffer of size $K$ (a GI/G/1/K queue): customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. inter-arrival times having distribution $A$ (mean $1/\lambda$, squared coefficient of variation $c_a^2$), are served by a single server with i.i.d. service times having distribution $S$ (mean $1/\mu$, squared coefficient of variation $c_s^2$), and any customer arriving to a full buffer is lost. Operate the queue in the critically loaded regime $\lambda=\mu$, and let $D(t)$ denote the number of customer departures in $[0,t]$ in steady state. Define the asymptotic variance rate
$$ V_K := \lim_{t\to\infty} \frac{\operatorname{Var}(D(t))}{t}, $$
and the BRAVO factor
$$ B_K := \frac{V_K}{\lambda\,(c_a^2+c_s^2)}. $$
It is conjectured that for "nice" inter-arrival and service distributions, $B_K \to 1/3$ as $K\to\infty$ (the GI/G/1/K BRAVO conjecture).

Numerical experiments suggest the following dichotomy when $A$ and $S$ are chosen from heavy-tailed families with matched first two moments:
(i) If $A$ and $S$ are heavy-tailed Weibull distributions (shape parameter $<1$), then $B_K$ appears to converge to $1/3$, behaving like light-tailed distributions.
(ii) If $A$ and $S$ are Lognormal or Pareto distributions with the same mean and variance, $B_K$ appears to converge to a different limit, or to converge to $1/3$ extremely slowly.

Problem. Prove or disprove the conjecture $B_K\to 1/3$ for heavy-tailed Weibull inter-arrival and service distributions, and identify a precise distributional property (for example, a tail-decay condition, a moment/Laplace-transform criterion, or a subexponentiality-type characterization) that separates those inter-arrival/service distributions for which $B_K\to 1/3$ holds from those for which it fails or converges at a strictly slower rate. In particular, explain mathematically why heavy-tailed Weibull distributions belong to the former class while Lognormal and Pareto distributions (with the same first two moments) belong to the latter.
status_search_result: The GI/G/1/K BRAVO conjecture (factor 1/3) remains an open problem. Recent works on critically loaded queues and generalized BRAVO (e.g., on busy periods of the critical GI/G/1 queue and BRAVO, and oscillating cumulants/generalized BRAVO) extend related results, but do not provide a distributional criterion explaining the observed heavy-tailed Weibull vs. Lognormal/Pareto dichotomy. No source confirms a proof of the GI/G/1/K conjecture or characterization separating the two regimes.

paper_title: The Flow Associated to Weakly Differentiable Vector Fields: Recent Results and Open Problems
original_question: Let b(t,x)=b_t(x):(0,T)×R^d→R^d be a bounded possibly nonautonomous Borel velocity field, and consider the continuity equation ∂_t w_t + ∇·(b_t w_t)=0. Which assumptions on b ensure existence and uniqueness of nonnegative solutions in L^∞([0,T]; L^1(R^d) ∩ L^∞(R^d))?
self_contained_problem:
Let $T>0$ and let $b:(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$, written $b(t,x)=b_t(x)$, be a bounded Borel measurable (possibly nonautonomous) vector field. Consider the linear continuity equation
$$\partial_t w_t + \nabla\cdot(b_t\, w_t) = 0 \quad \text{in } (0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d,$$
understood in the distributional sense, with initial data $w_0\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$, $w_0\geq 0$. Identify minimal structural conditions on $b$ (e.g., weak differentiability, bounds on the divergence, modulus of continuity, etc.) that guarantee existence and uniqueness of a nonnegative distributional solution
$$w\in L^\infty\bigl([0,T];\, L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)\bigr).$$
Characterize, as broadly as possible, the class of bounded Borel vector fields $b$ for which this well-posedness holds.
category_tag: Continuity equation with weakly differentiable vector fields
status_search_result: Well-posedness is known under various structural hypotheses: the DiPerna–Lions theory (Sobolev $W^{1,1}_{\rm loc}$ vector fields with bounded divergence), Ambrosio's extension to $BV_{\rm loc}$ vector fields with bounded divergence, and further refinements (nearly incompressible $BV$, suitable moduli of continuity, SBD, etc.). However, identifying the sharpest/most general assumptions on a merely bounded Borel vector field guaranteeing existence and uniqueness in $L^\infty([0,T];L^1\cap L^\infty)$ remains open; counterexamples (e.g., by Depauw, Alberti–Bianchini–Crippa, Bruè–Colombo–De Lellis) show non-uniqueness can occur outside these classes, but a complete characterization is not known.

paper_title: The Flow Associated to Weakly Differentiable Vector Fields: Recent Results and Open Problems
original_question: Suppose the vector field has the singular-integral form b_t(x)=∫_{R^d} K(x-y)F_t(y)dy, where K is a standard singular-integral kernel. Can the corresponding well-posedness and flow theory be extended from the case F_t∈L^1(R^d)^d to the case where F_t is merely a measure? Such an extension would cover BV vector fields and even BD vector fields through the same elliptic-PDE representation argument discussed in the source.
self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 2$ and $T>0$. Consider a time-dependent vector field $b:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ of singular-integral form
$$b_t(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} K(x-y)\,dF_t(y),$$
where $K:\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ is a standard Calderón–Zygmund singular-integral kernel (i.e. $K$ is smooth away from the origin, homogeneous of degree $-d$, has zero average on spheres centered at the origin, and the convolution operator $f\mapsto K*f$ is bounded on $L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1<p<\infty$), and $F_t$ is, for almost every $t\in[0,T]$, a finite $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued Radon measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $t\mapsto\|F_t\|_{\mathcal{M}}$ integrable on $[0,T]$. Assume in addition the usual growth bound on $b$ and the bound $\mathrm{div}\,b_t\in L^1((0,T);L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d))$.

Question: Can the well-posedness and stability theory of the regular Lagrangian flow associated with the ODE $\dot{X}_t(x)=b_t(X_t(x))$, $X_0(x)=x$ — known when $F_t\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)^d$ — be extended to the case in which $F_t$ is allowed to be a (signed vector) Radon measure? Such an extension would in particular cover vector fields of bounded variation (BV) and of bounded deformation (BD), via the elliptic-PDE representation of $\nabla b$ (or its symmetric part) as a singular integral of a measure.

Further work by Nguyen and others (including a 2025 paper on Lagrangian flows for very singular integral vector fields) advances the theory in specific singular kernel settings. A complete extension to general measure data $F_t$ covering arbitrary BV/BD vector fields does not appear to be available, so the problem is partially solved.

context_brief: Differentiability in measure of the flow
original_question: Let X(t,x) be the L^d-regular Lagrangian flow associated to a nonsmooth vector field b. In the W^{1,1} case one knows that, for almost every t, there exists a measurable matrix-valued map W_t(x) such that the difference quotients (X(t,x+εy)-X(t,x))/ε converge locally in measure to W_t(x)y as ε↓0. Does this derivative-in-measure property remain valid for BV vector fields?
self_contained_problem:
Let $b:(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ be a (possibly nonsmooth) vector field of bounded variation in the spatial variable, and let $X:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ denote an $\mathcal{L}^d$-regular Lagrangian flow associated to $b$; that is, $X(\cdot,x)$ solves $\dot\gamma(t)=b(t,\gamma(t))$, $\gamma(0)=x$, for a.e. $x$, and the pushforward $X(t,\cdot)_\#\mathcal{L}^d$ is bounded by a constant multiple of $\mathcal{L}^d$ uniformly in $t\in[0,T]$.

In the Sobolev case $b\in L^1((0,T);W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d))$ it is known that for almost every $t\in(0,T)$ there exists a measurable map $W_t:\mathbb{R}^d\to M_{d\times d}(\mathbb{R})$ such that
$$\frac{X(t,x+\varepsilon y)-X(t,x)}{\varepsilon}\ \longrightarrow\ W_t(x)\,y\qquad (\varepsilon\downarrow 0)$$
locally in measure on $\mathbb{R}^d_x\times\mathbb{R}^d_y$, uniformly in $t$.
