paper_title: Time and Norm Optimal Controls: A Survey of Recent Results and Open Problems
original_question: Construct a hypersingular time-optimal control in a space where time-optimal controls are unique, for example in a Hilbert space. Here hypersingularity means that the time-optimal control remains strongly singular on every subinterval [α, β] with 0 ≤ α < β ≤ T, rather than merely failing the maximum principle on the whole control interval. The paper gives hypersingular examples only in the very rough space c_0, where uniqueness of time-optimal controls fails, so the open problem is to obtain such an example in a setting with uniqueness.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $U \subset X$ be the closed unit ball. Consider a linear control system
$$\dot y(t) = A y(t) + u(t), \qquad y(0)=y_0,$$
where $A$ generates a strongly continuous semigroup on $X$ (or, in the finite-dimensional analogue, $A$ is a bounded operator on $X$) and the admissible controls are measurable functions $u:[0,T]\to U$. Given a target $y_1\in X$ reachable from $y_0$, a time-optimal control is an admissible $u^*$ defined on $[0,T^*]$, with $T^*$ the minimal time at which $y_1$ is reachable, that steers $y_0$ to $y_1$.

A time-optimal control $u^*$ is said to satisfy the Pontryagin maximum principle on a subinterval $[\alpha,\beta]\subset[0,T^*]$ if there exists a nonzero functional $\xi\in X^*$ such that for almost every $t\in[\alpha,\beta]$,
$$\langle \xi, e^{(T^*-t)A^*} u^*(t)\rangle = \sup_{v\in U}\langle \xi, e^{(T^*-t)A^*} v\rangle.$$
The control $u^*$ is called strongly singular on $[\alpha,\beta]$ if the maximum principle fails on $[\alpha,\beta]$. The control $u^*$ is called hypersingular if it is strongly singular on every subinterval $[\alpha,\beta]$ with $0\le \alpha<\beta\le T^*$.

It is known that in the space $X=c_0$ hypersingular time-optimal controls exist, but uniqueness of time-optimal controls fails there. It is also known that in a Hilbert space (and more generally in strictly convex reflexive spaces) time-optimal controls, when they exist, are unique.

Problem. Construct a linear control system on a Hilbert space $X$ (or more generally on a Banach space in which time-optimal controls are unique) which admits a hypersingular time-optimal control, or else prove that no such example exists.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any construction of a hypersingular time-optimal control in a Hilbert space or in any setting where time-optimal controls are unique. The known hypersingular examples remain confined to rough spaces such as $c_0$ where uniqueness fails, so the question appears to still be open.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal. Decide whether the situation called case 4 can ever occur, namely whether there exists such an ideal z(N0) for which the range M(I-2S_-|z) is closed and has infinite codimension.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the space of bounded scalar sequences $x=(\xi_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}$. The backward shift $S_-:\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)\to\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is defined by $(S_- x)_k=\xi_{k+1}$ for $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$.

A linear subspace $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)\subseteq\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$, equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\mid\mathfrak{z}\|$ under which it is complete, is called a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal if:
 (i) (monotonicity) whenever $x\in\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and $y\in\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ satisfy $|\eta_k|\le|\xi_k|$ for all $k$, then $y\in\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|y\mid\mathfrak{z}\|\le\|x\mid\mathfrak{z}\|$;
 (ii) (shift invariance) $S_-$ maps $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ into itself continuously, and likewise the forward shift $S_+$ (defined by $(S_+ x)_0=0$, $(S_+ x)_{k+1}=\xi_k$) maps $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ into itself continuously;
 (iii) $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ contains the canonical unit vectors.

Consider the bounded linear operator $I-2S_-$ acting on $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, where $I$ is the identity. Let $M(I-2S_-\mid\mathfrak{z})$ denote the range of $I-2S_-$ in $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

Question. Does there exist a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ such that $M(I-2S_-\mid\mathfrak{z})$ is closed in $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and has infinite codimension? Equivalently, decide whether this situation (called "case 4") is impossible.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem ("Problem 2: Find out whether case 4 is impossible") in Pietsch's 2023 survey on traces on operator ideals over Banach spaces. Web searches surface the survey and related papers in Pietsch's series on shift operators and traces, but no subsequent publication appears to resolve the case-4 question for quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Let A be a quasi-Banach operator ideal of exact trace type 1/r, let d_{r,\infty}(N0) be the shift-monotone sequence ideal of sequences with dyadic decay O(2^{-k/r}), and let A^{APP}_{r,\infty} be the ideal of operators S in A for which the dyadic A-approximation numbers (a_{2^k}(S|A)) lie in d_{r,\infty}(N0). Theorem 1.21 constructs traces on A^{APP}_{r,\infty} from 2^{-1/r}S_+-invariant linear forms φ on d_{r,\infty}(N0) by choosing an (A,d_{r,\infty})-representation S=∑_{k>=0} S_k and setting φ_{r,\infty}(S|A)=φ((2^{-k/r} trace(S_k))_k). Show that every trace on A^{APP}_{r,\infty} is one of these traces.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathfrak{A}$ be a quasi-Banach operator ideal on the class of all Banach spaces that is of exact trace type $1/r$ for some $r>0$ (i.e. equipped with a continuous trace on its finite-rank component compatible with the natural quasi-norm at order $1/r$). For an operator $S\in\mathfrak{A}(X,X)$, denote by $a_n(S\mid\mathfrak{A})$ its $n$-th $\mathfrak{A}$-approximation number.

Let $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ be the shift-monotone sequence ideal consisting of all scalar sequences $\xi=(\xi_k)_{k\ge 0}$ such that $\xi_k = O(2^{-k/r})$, and let $S_+$ denote the forward shift on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

Define
$$\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty} \;:=\; \bigl\{\, S\in\mathfrak{A} \;:\; (a_{2^k}(S\mid\mathfrak{A}))_{k\ge 0}\in d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)\,\bigr\}.$$

Construction of traces. Every operator $S\in\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ admits an $(\mathfrak{A},d_{r,\infty})$-representation
$$S=\sum_{k\ge 0} S_k,$$
where each $S_k$ is a finite-rank operator of rank at most $2^k$, with appropriate quasi-norm control. Given any linear form $\varphi$ on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ that is invariant under $2^{-1/r}S_+$, define
$$\varphi_{r,\infty}(S\mid\mathfrak{A}) := \varphi\bigl( (2^{-k/r}\,\mathrm{trace}(S_k))_{k\ge 0}\bigr).$$
This formula yields a well-defined trace on $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$.

Problem. Prove that conversely every (continuous) trace on the operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ arises in this way from some $2^{-1/r}S_+$-invariant linear form $\varphi$ on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in Pietsch's recent survey on traces on operator ideals over all Banach spaces (zbMATH 7709580). Related classifications are known in the Hilbert-space setting via the equivalence with shift-monotone sequence ideals, but no published resolution for the Banach-space ideal $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ was found.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, and let L^{APP}_z be the corresponding operator ideal of Banach-space operators. For inessential operators, the paper defines a trace to be spectral when its value is determined by the eigenvalue sequence of the operator. Show that every trace on L^{APP}_z is spectral whenever z(N0) is quasi-Banach.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $c_{00}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote sequences of complex numbers indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that are eventually zero. A sequence ideal $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0) \subseteq c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace closed under the pointwise action of $\ell_\infty$. It is called shift-monotone if it is invariant under the right shift $S_r(\xi_0,\xi_1,\dots) = (0,\xi_0,\xi_1,\dots)$ and the left shift $S_l(\xi_0,\xi_1,\dots) = (\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots)$. A quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal is such an ideal endowed with a complete quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathfrak z}$ for which the shifts are bounded.

To such an ideal $\mathfrak z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ associate the operator ideal $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}$ consisting of all operators $T: X \to Y$ between Banach spaces whose approximation-number sequence $(a_n(T))_{n\ge 0}$ belongs to $\mathfrak z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, where $a_n(T) = \inf\{\|T - F\| : \operatorname{rank} F < n\}$ (with the convention $a_0(T)=\|T\|$).

A trace on $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}$ is a linear functional $\tau$ defined on the components $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}(X,X)$ for all Banach spaces $X$ such that $\tau(BA) = \tau(AB)$ whenever the composition makes sense and the trace property is well-defined within the ideal.

An operator $T \in \mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}(X,X)$ is inessential and its eigenvalue sequence $(\lambda_n(T))_{n\ge 0}$ is the sequence of nonzero eigenvalues counted with algebraic multiplicity, arranged in order of nonincreasing modulus, completed by zeros. A trace $\tau$ on $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}$ is called spectral if $\tau(T)$ depends only on $(\lambda_n(T))_{n\ge 0}$ for every $T$ in the ideal.

Problem. Prove that whenever $\mathfrak z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, every trace on the operator ideal $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}$ is spectral.
status_search_result: The question of spectrality of all traces on $\mathfrak L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak z}$ for quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals $\mathfrak z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is posed as an open problem in Pietsch's program on traces on Banach-space operator ideals. paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: For 1 <= r <= 2, let P_{r,2} denote the ideal of (r,2)-summing operators. Theorem 2.4 constructs traces on (P_{r,2})^{APP}_{r,\infty} from 2^{-1/r}S_+-invariant linear forms on d_{r,\infty}(N0). Show that (P_{r,2})^{APP}_{r,\infty} has no traces other than those constructed in Theorem 2.4.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. For $1\le r\le 2$, an operator $T:X\to Y$ between Banach spaces is called $(r,2)$-summing if there exists a constant $c\ge 0$ such that for every finite family $x_1,\dots,x_n\in X$,
$$\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^n \|Tx_k\|^r\Bigr)^{1/r}\le c\,\sup_{\|x^*\|\le 1}\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^n |\langle x_k,x^*\rangle|^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The class of all such operators forms a Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak P_{r,2}$.

Let $\mathfrak P_{r,2}^{\mathrm{APP}}$ denote the approximative kernel of $\mathfrak P_{r,2}$, i.e. the closure of the ideal of finite-rank operators in the $(r,2)$-summing norm. For a Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak A$ and exponents $0<p\le\infty$, the Lorentz-type enlargement $\mathfrak A_{r,\infty}$ consists of operators $T$ whose approximation numbers $a_n(T)$ satisfy $\sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r} a_n(T)<\infty$, suitably combined with $\mathfrak A$. Consider the ideal
$$(\mathfrak P_{r,2})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}.$$

A trace on an operator ideal $\mathfrak I$ is a linear functional $\tau:\mathfrak I(\ell_2)\to\mathbb C$ (or on the components on each Banach space, compatibly) that is unitarily invariant and satisfies $\tau(AB)=\tau(BA)$ whenever both products lie in $\mathfrak I$.

On the sequence space
$$d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb N_0)=\Bigl\{(\xi_k)_{k\ge 0}: \sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r}\xi_n^*<\infty\Bigr\},$$
(with $(\xi_n^*)$ the decreasing rearrangement) let $S_+$ denote the dyadic-block shift, and consider linear forms on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb N_0)$ that are invariant under $2^{-1/r}S_+$. There is a known construction producing traces on $(\mathfrak P_{r,2})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ from such $2^{-1/r}S_+$-invariant linear forms.

Problem. Prove that every trace on the operator ideal $(\mathfrak P_{r,2})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ arises from this construction; equivalently, show that no traces exist on $(\mathfrak P_{r,2})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ other than those produced from $2^{-1/r}S_+$-invariant linear forms on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb N_0)$.

context_brief: Growth of Weyl-generated ideals for r >= 2.
original_question: For 1 <= r <= \infty, let L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty} be the quasi-Banach operator ideal defined by dyadic Weyl-number decay x_{2^k}(S)=O(2^{-k/r}), and let (L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty})^{APP}_{r,\infty} be the ideal obtained by applying the generalized approximation-number construction to L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty}. Determine whether the family (L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty})^{APP}_{r,\infty} strictly increases as r ranges over [2,\infty), or whether it becomes constant there; in particular, decide whether (L^{WEYL}_{2,\infty})^{APP}_{2,\infty}=L^{WEYL}_{1,\infty}.
self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. Let $S:X\to Y$ be a bounded linear operator between Banach spaces. For $n\ge 1$, the $n$-th Weyl number $x_n(S)$ is defined by
$$x_n(S)\;=\;\sup\{\,a_n(S\circ A)\;:\;A:\ell_2\to X,\;\|A\|\le 1\,\},$$
where $a_n(\cdot)$ denotes the $n$-th approximation number, i.e. $a_n(T)=\inf\{\|T-F\|:\operatorname{rank}F<n\}$.

For $1\le r\le \infty$ define the quasi-Banach operator ideal
$$L^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}\;=\;\bigl\{\,S\;:\;\sup_{k\ge 0} 2^{k/r}\,x_{2^k}(S)<\infty\,\bigr\},$$
i.e. the class of operators whose dyadic Weyl numbers satisfy $x_{2^k}(S)=O(2^{-k/r})$.

Given any quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak A$ with quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathfrak A}$, define for an operator $S:X\to Y$ the generalized approximation numbers
$$a_n^{(\mathfrak A)}(S)\;=\;\inf\{\,\|S-F\|_{\mathfrak A}\,:\,F\in\mathfrak A(X,Y),\;\operatorname{rank}F<n\,\},$$
and, for $1\le r\le\infty$, set
$$\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}\;=\;\bigl\{\,S\in\mathfrak A\;:\;\sup_{k\ge 0} 2^{k/r}\,a_{2^k}^{(\mathfrak A)}(S)<\infty\,\bigr\}.$$

Problem. Consider the family of operator ideals
$$\bigl(L^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}\bigr)^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty},\qquad r\in[2,\infty).$$
Determine whether this family is strictly increasing in $r$ on $[2,\infty)$, or whether it is constant on $[2,\infty)$. In particular, decide whether the identity
$$\bigl(L^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{2,\infty}\bigr)^{\mathrm{APP}}_{2,\infty}\;=\;L^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}$$
holds.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: For 1 <= r < \infty, Theorem 2.8 constructs traces on (L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty})^{APP}_{r,\infty} from 2^{-1/r}S_+-invariant linear forms on d_{r,\infty}(N0). Show that there are no other traces on (L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty})^{APP}_{r,\infty} beyond those provided by Theorem 2.8.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ denote the space of bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. For a bounded operator $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$, the $n$-th approximation number is
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\|T-F\|:F\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}(F)<n\},\qquad n\in\mathbb{N},$$
and the $n$-th Weyl number is
$$x_n(T)=\sup\{a_n(TA):A\in\mathcal{L}(\ell_2,X),\ \|A\|\le 1\}.$$
For $1\le r<\infty$ define the Lorentz-type Weyl operator ideal
$$\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}:=\{T:\ \|T\|^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}:=\sup_{n\ge 1}n^{1/r}x_n(T)<\infty\},$$
and consider its approximation-number companion
$$(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}:=\{T:\ T\in\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}\ \text{and}\ \sup_{n\ge1}n^{1/r}a_n(T)<\infty\},$$
viewed as an operator ideal on the class of all Banach spaces.

A trace on an operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is a linear functional $\tau$ defined on the components $\mathfrak{A}(X,X)$ (for all Banach spaces $X$) such that
(i) $\tau(S\circ T)=\tau(T\circ S)$ whenever both compositions belong to $\mathfrak{A}$, and
(ii) $\tau(x'\otimes x)=\langle x,x'\rangle$ for rank-one operators $x'\otimes x$.

On the sequence space
$$d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0):=\{\xi=(\xi_n)_{n\ge0}:\ \sup_{n\ge1}n^{1/r}\xi^*_n<\infty\},$$
where $\xi^*$ is the decreasing rearrangement of $|\xi|$, consider the dyadic shift $S_+$ acting by
$$(S_+\xi)_n=\xi_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\quad\text{(or the analogous block-doubling shift)},$$
and call a linear form $\varphi$ on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ "$2^{-1/r}S_+$-invariant" if $\varphi(2^{-1/r}S_+\xi)=\varphi(\xi)$ for every $\xi\in d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

It is known that every $2^{-1/r}S_+$-invariant linear form on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ induces, via a standard construction, a trace on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$.

Problem. For every $1\le r<\infty$, prove that every trace on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ arises in this way from some $2^{-1/r}S_+$-invariant linear form on $d_{r,\infty}(\mathbb{N}_0)$; equivalently, show that there are no other traces on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ beyond those obtained from this construction.

context_brief: Existence of nonzero traces on L^{WEYL}_{1,∞}.
original_question: Show that the Weyl-number ideal L^{WEYL}_{1,\infty} supports at least one non-vanishing trace. The source explicitly singles this out as the author's personal favourite and suggests that such traces may even be singular and spectral.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a complex Banach space and $T: X \to X$ a bounded linear operator. For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, define the $n$-th Weyl number of $T$ by
$$x_n(T) := \sup\{ a_n(TA) : A: \ell_2 \to X,\ \|A\| \le 1\},$$
where $a_n$ denotes the $n$-th approximation number, $a_n(S) = \inf\{\|S - F\| : F\text{ finite rank},\ \mathrm{rank}(F) < n\}$.

Let $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}$ be the operator ideal consisting of all operators $T$ between arbitrary Banach spaces such that
$$\sup_{n \ge 1} n \cdot x_n(T) < \infty,$$
viewed as a two-sided ideal in the class of all bounded operators between Banach spaces.

A trace on $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}$ is a linear functional $\tau$ defined on the components $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}(X,X)$ for every Banach space $X$, satisfying the commutator property $\tau(AB) = \tau(BA)$ whenever $AB$ and $BA$ both lie in the ideal, and which is unitarily/ideal invariant in the usual sense.

Problem: Prove or disprove that there exists a nonzero trace on $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}$.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Find shift-monotone sequence ideals z(N0) for which the entropy-number generated operator ideal L^{ENT}_z carries non-vanishing singular traces.
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup.

(a) Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the space of real (or complex) sequences $x=(\xi_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ converging to $0$. Let $S_+\colon c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)\to c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the forward shift $(S_+x)_k=\xi_{k-1}$ for $k\ge 1$, $(S_+x)_0=0$, and let $S_-$ denote the backward shift $(S_-x)_k=\xi_{k+1}$. A linear subspace $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)\subseteq c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called a shift-monotone sequence ideal if it is invariant under both $S_+$ and $S_-$ and contains every sequence $y$ for which there exists $x\in\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $|y_k|\le |x_k|$ for all $k$.

(b) For a (bounded linear) operator $T\colon X\to Y$ between Banach spaces, the $n$-th (dyadic) entropy number $\varepsilon_n(T)$ is defined for $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$ as the infimum of those $\varepsilon>0$ such that the image $T(B_X)$ of the closed unit ball can be covered by $2^n$ closed balls of radius $\varepsilon$ in $Y$. Given a shift-monotone sequence ideal $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, the entropy-generated operator ideal is
$$\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_{\mathfrak{z}}:=\bigl\{T\in\mathfrak{L}(X,Y):(\varepsilon_n(T))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\in\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0),\ X,Y\ \text{Banach}\bigr\}.$$

(c) A trace on a two-sided operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is a linear functional $\tau$ defined on the component $\mathfrak{A}(X,X)$ for each Banach space $X$ such that $\tau(ST)=\tau(TS)$ whenever the composition makes sense within $\mathfrak{A}$. A trace $\tau$ is called singular if it vanishes on every finite-rank operator. A trace is non-vanishing if it is not identically zero.

Problem. Characterize, or exhibit a rich family of, shift-monotone sequence ideals $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ for which the entropy-generated operator ideal $\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_{\mathfrak{z}}$ admits a non-vanishing singular trace.
status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in Pietsch's survey on traces on operator ideals defined over all Banach spaces. Related results exist on the existence of singular traces on simply-generated and approximation-number generated operator ideals on Hilbert space, but no published resolution for the entropy-generated case over arbitrary Banach spaces was found.

context_brief: Injectivity of z ↦ L^{APP}_z(X,Y) on large classes.
original_question: Fix infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X and Y. Find large collections Z of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals such that (i) Z contains every Lorentz-type ideal d_{r,w}(N0), and (ii) the map z(N0) ↦ L^{APP}_z(X,Y) is one-to-one on Z.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A quasi-Banach sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of the space of scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$ which is equipped with a complete quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_{z}$ such that whenever $|a_n| \le |b_n|$ for all $n$ and $(b_n) \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, then $(a_n) \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|(a_n)\|_z \le \|(b_n)\|_z$. Such an ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called shift-monotone if for every $(a_n) \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ the shifted sequence $(a_{n+1})_n$ also belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with no greater quasi-norm.

For parameters $0 < r < \infty$ and $0 < w \le \infty$, the Lorentz-type sequence ideal $d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ consists of those sequences $(a_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ whose non-increasing rearrangement $(a_n^*)$ satisfies
\[
\|(a_n)\|_{d_{r,w}} = \Bigl(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (n+1)^{w/r-1}(a_n^*)^w\Bigr)^{1/w} < \infty \quad (w<\infty),
\]
with the usual modification for $w = \infty$.

For a bounded linear operator $T: X \to Y$ between Banach spaces, let $a_n(T)$ denote the $n$-th approximation number, i.e.\ the distance in operator norm from $T$ to the operators of rank at most $n$. Given a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and Banach spaces $X,Y$, define
\[
\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{z}(X,Y) = \{\, T \in \mathcal{L}(X,Y) : (a_n(T))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0} \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\,\}.
\]

Problem. Fix arbitrary infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$. Exhibit large collections $\mathcal{Z}$ of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals such that:
(i) $d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0) \in \mathcal{Z}$ for every admissible pair $(r,w)$;
(ii) the assignment $z(\mathbb{N}_0) \mapsto \mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{z}(X,Y)$ is injective on $\mathcal{Z}$.

original_question: Find Banach spaces that contain an unconditional basic sequence but nevertheless have few approximable operators, meaning that their set app(X) of approximation-number profiles of approximable operators is strictly smaller than the full cone c_0^*(N).
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. For a bounded linear operator $T: X \to X$, the $n$-th approximation number is
$$a_n(T) = \inf\{\|T - F\| : F: X \to X \text{ bounded linear with } \mathrm{rank}(F) < n\}, \qquad n \in \mathbb{N}.$$
An operator $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$ is called approximable if it lies in the operator-norm closure of the finite-rank operators on $X$; equivalently, $a_n(T) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Define
$$\mathrm{app}(X) = \{(a_n(T))_{n \in \mathbb{N}} : T \in \mathcal{L}(X), \ T \text{ approximable}\} \subseteq c_0^*(\mathbb{N}),$$
where $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})$ denotes the cone of non-increasing null sequences of non-negative real numbers. One says that $X$ has few approximable operators if $\mathrm{app}(X) \subsetneq c_0^*(\mathbb{N})$, i.e., there exists a non-increasing null sequence of non-negative reals that is not the approximation-number sequence of any approximable operator on $X$.

Problem: Exhibit a Banach space $X$ that contains an unconditional basic sequence and at the same time has few approximable operators in the sense above.

original_question: Let L^{LEX}_{1,\infty}=H\circ L^{WEYL}_{1,\infty} be the left-hand extension ideal obtained by composing the Hilbert-factorization ideal H with the Weyl-generated ideal L^{WEYL}_{1,\infty}. Show that either (L^{WEYL}_{2,\infty})^{APP}_{2,\infty} is not contained in L^{LEX}_{1,\infty}, or even that the smaller ideal L^{APP}_{1,\infty} is not contained in L^{LEX}_{1,\infty}.
self_contained_problem:
Work in the category of operators acting between arbitrary (complex) Banach spaces. Recall the following constructions of operator ideals.

1. Approximation numbers: for a bounded operator T: X → Y between Banach spaces, the n-th approximation number is
   a_n(T) = inf{ ||T − F|| : F: X → Y, rank(F) < n }.
   The Lorentz-type approximation ideal L^{APP}_{1,∞} consists of all operators T such that
   sup_{n ≥ 1} n · a_n(T) < ∞.
   More generally, L^{APP}_{p,∞} is the class of operators with sup_n n^{1/p} a_n(T) < ∞.

2. Weyl numbers: for T: X → Y, the n-th Weyl number is
   x_n(T) = sup{ a_n(T ∘ A) : A: ℓ_2 → X, ||A|| ≤ 1 }.
   The Weyl-generated ideal L^{WEYL}_{p,∞} consists of all operators with sup_n n^{1/p} x_n(T) < ∞.

3. For an operator ideal A and parameters p,q the "Lorentz-type re-iteration" A^{APP}_{p,∞} denotes the class of operators T whose approximation numbers satisfy a Lorentz-type estimate built from A in the standard way; in particular (L^{WEYL}_{2,∞})^{APP}_{2,∞} is the class of operators T such that sup_n n^{1/2} a_n(T) is controlled in the L^{WEYL}_{2,∞} sense.

4. The Hilbert-factorization ideal H consists of all operators that factor through a Hilbert space:
   T ∈ H(X,Y) ⇔ there exist a Hilbert space K and bounded operators T: X → K, S: K → Y with T = S ∘ R.

5. Define the left-hand extension ideal
   L^{LEX}_{1,∞} := H ∘ L^{WEYL}_{1,∞},
   that is, the ideal of operators that can be written as a composition U ∘ V with V ∈ L^{WEYL}_{1,∞} and U ∈ H.

Problem. Prove that
   (L^{WEYL}_{2,∞})^{APP}_{2,∞} ⊄ L^{LEX}_{1,∞},
or, even stronger, that
   L^{APP}_{1,∞} ⊄ L^{LEX}_{1,∞}.

Equivalently, exhibit a Banach-space operator belonging to L^{APP}_{1,∞} (respectively to (L^{WEYL}_{2,∞})^{APP}_{2,∞}) that does not admit a factorization U ∘ V with V of Weyl-type (1,∞) and U factoring through a Hilbert space.

self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{A}$ be a quasi-Banach operator ideal (in the sense of Pietsch: a class of bounded linear operators between arbitrary Banach spaces, closed under composition with bounded operators on either side, containing the finite-rank operators, and equipped with a complete quasi-norm). For a quasi-Banach (shift-monotone) sequence ideal $\mathfrak{x}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ — that is, a linear subspace of the space of scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is invariant under the forward and backward shift operators, complete in a given quasi-norm, and such that the quasi-norm is monotone with respect to shifts — one defines the approximation-type operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{x}}$ as the class of operators $T : X \to Y$ between Banach spaces for which the sequence of approximation numbers (or, more generally, the sequence of $\mathfrak{A}$-approximation numbers) $\bigl(a_n^{\mathfrak{A}}(T)\bigr)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$, defined by
$$a_n^{\mathfrak{A}}(T) = \inf\{\|T-L\|_{\mathfrak{A}} : L\in\mathfrak{A}(X,Y),\ \operatorname{rank}(L)\le n\},$$
belongs to $\mathfrak{x}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, equipped with the natural induced quasi-norm.

Prove that, for every quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ and every pair of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals $\mathfrak{x}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and $\mathfrak{y}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, there exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ such that the iterated APP-construction collapses to a single step:
$$\bigl(\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{x}}\bigr)^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{y}} \;=\; \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{z}}.$$
Equivalently, identify (and describe explicitly) such a sequence ideal $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ in terms of $\mathfrak{x}$ and $\mathfrak{y}$, with equality of the associated quasi-norms up to equivalence.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in Pietsch's list of open problems on traces of operator ideals over Banach spaces. Searches for a published resolution of the reiteration identity $(\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{x}})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{y}} = \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{\mathfrak{z}}$ for general quasi-Banach operator ideals and shift-monotone sequence ideals did not yield a solution; related work treats approximation spaces and reiteration in restricted (e.g., Hilbert space, or specific sequence-ideal) settings but does not establish the general Banach-space version. Status appears to remain open.

paper_title: Two Open Problems for Absolutely Convergent Dirichlet Series
context_brief: Sharp constant in the S_ψ(Λ) growth bound
original_question: Let Λ=(λ_n)_{n≥0} be a strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative numbers with λ_0=0, let F(z)=∑_{n=0}^{∞} a_n e^{zλ_n}, let M(x,F)=sup_t |F(x+it)|, and let μ(x,F)=max_n |a_n|e^{xλ_n}. For ψ in L, let S_ψ(Λ) be the class of entire Dirichlet series with infinitely many nonzero coefficients satisfying |a_n|≤e^{-λ_nψ(λ_n)} for all sufficiently large n. Assume h∈L_0 and that conditions (4) and (5) of the paper hold, so that for every F∈S_ψ(Λ) there exist c>0 and x_0 such that M(x,F)<μ(x,F) h(cx) for all x≥x_0. What is the exact, i.e. sharp, value of the constant c for which this inequality can always be guaranteed?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Lambda=(\lambda_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative real numbers with $\lambda_0=0$ and $\lambda_n\to\infty$. Consider entire Dirichlet series of the form
$$F(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n e^{z\lambda_n},$$
and define
$$M(x,F)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|F(x+it)|, \qquad \mu(x,F)=\max_{n\geq 0}|a_n|e^{x\lambda_n}.$$
Let $L$ denote the class of continuous, positive, nondecreasing functions on $[x_0,\infty)$ tending to $+\infty$, and let $L_0\subset L$ denote the subclass of those $h\in L$ satisfying the additional regularity condition that $\ln h(x)$ is concave (slowly varying type) with $h(x+O(1))\sim h(x)$.

For $\psi\in L$, let $S_\psi(\Lambda)$ denote the class of entire Dirichlet series $F$ as above such that $\#\{n: a_n\neq 0\}=+\infty$ and
$$|a_n|\leq \exp\{-\lambda_n\psi(\lambda_n)\} \quad \text{for all sufficiently large } n.$$

Assume $h\in L_0$ and that the regularity conditions
\begin{align}
&\text{(i)} \quad \int^{\infty}\frac{dx}{x\,\psi(x)}<\infty, \\
&\text{(ii)} \quad \ln h(x) \text{ is comparable to a suitable inverse function of } \psi
\end{align}
hold, so that for every $F\in S_\psi(\Lambda)$ there exist constants $c>0$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}$ with
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\, h(cx) \quad \text{for all } x\geq x_0.$$

Determine the sharp (smallest possible) value of the constant $c>0$ for which this inequality is guaranteed to hold for every $F\in S_\psi(\Lambda)$.

The question's status therefore could not be conclusively verified.

context_brief: Sharp constant in the S^0_ψ(Λ) half-plane bound
original_question: Let ψ∈L_1, let S^0_ψ(Λ) be the class of Dirichlet series F∈S^0(Λ) such that |a_n|≤e^{λ_n/ψ(λ_n)} for all sufficiently large n, and let M(x,F)=sup_t |F(x+it)| and μ(x,F)=max_n |a_n|e^{xλ_n}. Assume h∈L_0 and that conditions (7) and (5) of the paper hold, so that for every F∈S^0_ψ(Λ) there exist c>0 and x_0<0 with M(x,F)<μ(x,F) h(c/|x|) for all x∈[x_0,0). What is the exact, i.e. sharp, value of the constant c for which this inequality can always be guaranteed?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Lambda=(\lambda_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative real numbers with $\lambda_n\to\infty$, and let $S^0(\Lambda)$ denote the class of (general) Dirichlet series
$$F(s)=\sum_{n\ge 1} a_n e^{s\lambda_n}$$
that converge absolutely in the open left half-plane $\{\operatorname{Re} s<0\}$. For $x<0$ and $F\in S^0(\Lambda)$ set
$$M(x,F)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|F(x+it)|,\qquad \mu(x,F)=\max_{n\ge 1}|a_n|e^{x\lambda_n}\;.$$
Let $L_1$ denote the class of positive, continuous, nondecreasing functions $\psi:[a,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ tending to $\infty$ such that $\psi(t)/t$ is nonincreasing and $\int^\infty dt/(t\psi(t))<\infty$ (so $\psi\in L_1$), and let $L_0$ denote the class of positive, continuous, nondecreasing functions $h:[b,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ tending to $\infty$. For $\psi\in L_1$, let
$$S^0_\psi(\Lambda)=\{F\in S^0(\Lambda): |a_n|\le \exp(\lambda_n/\psi(\lambda_n))\ \text{for all sufficiently large }n\}.$$
Assume that $h\in L_0$ together with $\psi$ satisfy the standard compatibility conditions ensuring that for every $F\in S^0_\psi(\Lambda)$ there exist $c=c(F)>0$ and $x_0=x_0(F)<0$ such that
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h\!\left(\frac{c}{|x|}\right)\qquad \text{for all } x\in[x_0,0).$$
Determine the sharp (smallest) value of the constant $c>0$ for which this inequality is guaranteed to hold for every $F\in S^0_\psi(\Lambda)$.

paper_title: Two open problems in graph theory
original_question: If one is given only the set of vertex-deleted subgraphs of a finite graph, with duplicate isomorphic cards removed and multiplicities forgotten, is the original graph uniquely determined by that set?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on vertex set $V(G)$ with $|V(G)| \ge 4$. For each vertex $v \in V(G)$, let $G - v$ denote the vertex-deleted subgraph obtained by removing $v$ and all edges incident to it. Define the deck-set of $G$ to be
$$\mathcal{S}(G) = \{[G-v] : v \in V(G)\},$$
where $[G-v]$ denotes the isomorphism class of $G-v$, and where $\mathcal{S}(G)$ is considered as a set (so isomorphic vertex-deleted subgraphs are identified and multiplicities are discarded).

A graph $G$ is said to be set-reconstructible if every finite simple graph $H$ with $\mathcal{S}(H) = \mathcal{S}(G)$ is isomorphic to $G$.

Question: Is every finite simple graph on at least four vertices set-reconstructible? Equivalently, do there exist non-isomorphic finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$, each with at least four vertices, such that $\mathcal{S}(G) = \mathcal{S}(H)$?
status_search_result: The set reconstruction conjecture (a strengthening of the Kelly–Ulam reconstruction conjecture, proposed by Harary) is widely reported to remain open. It has been verified computationally for all graphs on at most a small number of vertices (McKay's computations), but no general proof or counterexample is known.

paper_title: Two open problems in graph theory
original_question: A graph is hypohamiltonian if it is not hamiltonian but every vertex-deleted subgraph is hamiltonian. For which integers n does there exist a hypohamiltonian graph on n vertices? In particular, does such a graph exist on 17 vertices?
self_contained_problem: A simple graph G is called hypohamiltonian if G itself does not contain a Hamiltonian cycle, but for every vertex v of G the vertex-deleted subgraph G − v does contain a Hamiltonian cycle. Determine the set of positive integers n for which there exists a hypohamiltonian graph on n vertices. In particular, decide whether a hypohamiltonian graph on exactly 17 vertices exists.
status_search_result: The order spectrum of hypohamiltonian graphs is now completely known. Such graphs exist precisely for n = 10, 13, 15, 16, and for every n ≥ 18; no hypohamiltonian graph exists for n ∈ {3,…,9, 11, 12, 14, 17}. In particular, the existence question for n = 17 has been settled negatively via exhaustive computer enumeration (Aldred–McKay–Wormald and subsequent verifications).

paper_title: Two open problems in graph theory
original_question: Does there exist an infinite hypohamiltonian graph in which every vertex has finite degree; that is, a locally finite infinite hypohamiltonian graph?
self_contained_problem: A simple graph $G = (V,E)$ (possibly infinite) is called hypohamiltonian if $G$ itself contains no Hamiltonian cycle (a cycle, possibly two-way infinite, passing through every vertex exactly once; for an infinite graph this is interpreted as a spanning two-way infinite path/cycle), while for every vertex $v \in V$ the subgraph $G - v$ obtained by deleting $v$ does contain such a Hamiltonian cycle. paper_title: Two open problems in precedence constrained scheduling
context_brief: single-machine total tardiness with chain-like precedence and release dates
original_question: Determine the computational complexity of the following optimization problem. There are n jobs, all of unit processing time, to be processed nonpreemptively on a single machine. Each job j has an integer due date d_j and a release date r_j, so job j is unavailable before time r_j. The precedence constraints are chain-like: in the directed precedence graph on the jobs, each vertex has indegree at most one and outdegree at most one. A feasible schedule must respect both the release dates and the precedence arcs, and if job j completes at time C_j then its tardiness is max(0, C_j - d_j). What is the complexity of finding a feasible schedule minimizing the total tardiness over all jobs?
self_contained_problem: Consider the following single-machine scheduling problem. There are n jobs, each of unit processing time, to be processed nonpreemptively on a single machine that can handle at most one job at a time. Each job j (1 ≤ j ≤ n) has an integer due date d_j and an integer release date r_j; job j may not start before time r_j. A directed precedence graph G is given on the vertex set {1,...,n} in which every vertex has indegree at most one and outdegree at most one (so the precedence constraints form a disjoint union of chains). A feasible schedule assigns a start time S_j ≥ r_j to each job such that the intervals [S_j, S_j+1) are pairwise disjoint and S_j + 1 ≤ S_k whenever (j,k) is an arc of G. Let C_j = S_j + 1 denote the completion time of job j and let its tardiness be T_j = max(0, C_j − d_j). Determine the computational complexity of finding a feasible schedule that minimizes the total tardiness Σ_{j=1}^{n} T_j: in particular, is this problem solvable in polynomial time, or is it NP-hard?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not locate a definitive resolution of the complexity of the unit-time single-machine total tardiness problem with chain precedence and release dates. Surveys and recent overviews of single-machine scheduling complexity (e.g., the 2024 overview on arXiv) still list related variants among unresolved cases, and no polynomial-time algorithm or NP-hardness proof for this exact problem could be confirmed. The status is therefore reported as unknown/likely still open.

paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
original_question: Can one prove finite-time droplet pinch-off in the lubrication approximation for a liquid jet falling from a nozzle, where h is the outer surface radius, x is the axial coordinate, v is the leading-order axial velocity, and the reduced model approximates the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes free-surface equations with gravity, surface tension, density, and viscosity? The target is an analytical proof that the reduced system develops a finite-time singularity corresponding to droplet breakup, rather than only numerical evidence for such a singularity.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the lubrication (slender-jet) approximation for a viscous liquid jet falling from a nozzle under gravity, surface tension, and inertia. Let h(x,t) > 0 denote the outer free-surface radius of the axisymmetric jet and let v(x,t) denote the leading-order axial velocity, where x is the axial coordinate and t is time. After non-dimensionalization with density ρ, dynamic viscosity μ, surface tension coefficient σ, and gravitational acceleration g, the reduced one-dimensional system obtained by asymptotic expansion of the three-dimensional axisymmetric Navier–Stokes free-surface equations takes the form

  ∂_t(h^2) + ∂_x(h^2 v) = 0,
  ρ (∂_t v + v ∂_x v) = -σ ∂_x κ(h) + (3μ / h^2) ∂_x(h^2 ∂_x v) + ρ g,

where κ(h) is the leading-order mean-curvature term in the slender-jet approximation (for example κ(h) = 1/h − ∂_xx h / (1+(∂_x h)^2)^{3/2}, or a standard reduction thereof), posed on a suitable axial interval with boundary conditions modeling a nozzle at one end and a free end below.

Prove analytically that, for an appropriate class of smooth initial data with h > 0, there exists a finite time T* < ∞ at which the solution develops a pinch-off singularity, i.e.

  liminf_{t → T*-} inf_x h(x,t) = 0,

corresponding to droplet breakup. The goal is a rigorous mathematical proof (not merely numerical or asymptotic evidence) that this reduced lubrication system produces a finite-time zero of h.
status_search_result: The literature provides extensive numerical and asymptotic (self-similar) evidence for finite-time pinch-off in the slender-jet lubrication model, and rigorous results exist for related but distinct models (e.g., a Hele-Shaw thin-neck model where pinch-off in finite or infinite time has been proved, and fourth-order thin-film equations where weak solutions are constructed past possible singularities). However, no rigorous analytical proof of finite-time pinch-off for the slender-jet lubrication system describing a liquid jet from a nozzle appears in the literature; surveys continue to list this as an open problem.

paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
original_question: In a Hele-Shaw cell treated as a two-dimensional incompressible Darcy free-boundary problem whose boundary pressure is controlled by surface tension, can the evolution produce a finite-time topological singularity in which one connected region of fluid pinches off and becomes two disconnected regions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a Hele-Shaw cell modeled as the following two-dimensional incompressible Darcy free-boundary problem. Let Ω(t) ⊂ ℝ² be a bounded, possibly multiply-connected open set occupied by a viscous fluid at time t ≥ 0, with smooth boundary Γ(t) = ∂Ω(t). The fluid pressure p(·,t) : Ω(t) → ℝ satisfies

  Δp = 0 in Ω(t),
  p = σ κ on Γ(t),

where σ > 0 is the surface tension coefficient and κ denotes the (signed) curvature of Γ(t). The interface Γ(t) is transported by the Darcy velocity v = −∇p; equivalently, the normal velocity of Γ(t) is V_n = −∂p/∂n, where n is the outward unit normal.

Question: Does there exist a smooth initial domain Ω(0) which is connected such that the resulting evolution Ω(t) develops, in finite time T < ∞, a topological singularity at which Ω(t) pinches off, i.e. lim_{t↑T} Ω(t) breaks into two (or more) disjoint connected components? Prove or disprove the occurrence of such finite-time topology change for this surface-tension-driven Hele-Shaw flow.
status_search_result: Numerical and asymptotic studies (Goldstein–Pesci–Shelley and others) strongly support generic finite-time pinch-off in surface-tension-driven Hele-Shaw flow, and rigorous results exist for related lubrication/thin-film reductions showing pinch-off in finite or infinite time. For the full two-dimensional Darcy free-boundary problem with surface tension, however, a rigorous proof that a smooth connected initial fluid region can pinch into disconnected components in finite time does not appear to be available in the literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
original_question: For fourth-order degenerate thin-film equations for a nonnegative film height h, when the film has compact support and the equation degenerates as h approaches zero at a moving contact line, what boundary conditions should be imposed at the edge of the support so that the contact-line problem is physically and mathematically well posed?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the fourth-order degenerate thin-film equation
  h_t + (m(h) h_{xxx})_x = 0,    x ∈ Ω(t) ⊂ ℝ, t > 0,
for a nonnegative film height h(x,t) ≥ 0, where the mobility m(h) ≥ 0 vanishes at h = 0 (typical examples include m(h) = h^n with n > 0, derived from the lubrication approximation of surface-tension-driven flow of a thin viscous film on a solid substrate). Assume the film has compact support so that Ω(t) = {x : h(x,t) > 0} is a bounded open set, and let the moving contact line be the boundary ∂Ω(t) where h = 0 and the equation degenerates.

Determine which boundary conditions must be imposed at the moving contact line ∂Ω(t) (in addition to h = 0 there) so that the resulting free-boundary problem is both physically meaningful (consistent with the underlying fluid-mechanical model of a contact line on a solid substrate, including treatment of the classical no-slip stress singularity) and mathematically well posed (admitting a unique solution depending continuously on the data, in an appropriate class of nonnegative weak or classical solutions). In particular, specify a complete set of contact-line conditions (e.g. prescribing the contact angle |h_x|, a kinematic law for the speed of ∂Ω(t), or a flux condition) that yields a well-posed evolution for general mobilities m(h) and general wetting regimes (complete and partial wetting).
status_search_result: The general question of the correct contact-line boundary conditions for degenerate fourth-order thin-film equations remains an active research area, but substantial partial progress has been made. Well-posedness has been established in several regimes: with prescribed contact angle h=0, |h_x|=const in partial wetting (Knüpfer, Giacomelli–Knüpfer–Otto, Gnann and collaborators) and for the perfect-wetting (zero contact angle) regime (e.g. Gnann–Petrache 2023/2025) for broad classes of mobilities. A fully general, physically and mathematically definitive prescription valid across all mobility exponents and wetting regimes, including slippage models, is not yet complete.

paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
original_question: For an unforced one-dimensional fourth-order degenerate lubrication equation for a thin film or Hele-Shaw neck, with film height h and mobility depending on a power of h, can one prove finite-time singularity formation without imposing special forcing boundary conditions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional fourth-order degenerate parabolic equation
   h_t + (h^n h_{xxx})_x = 0,   x ∈ I, t > 0,
modeling, in the lubrication approximation, the evolution of the height h(x,t) ≥ 0 of a thin viscous film or of the neck thickness in a Hele-Shaw cell driven by surface tension, where n > 0 is a fixed mobility exponent. Consider the "unforced" setting: either the equation is posed on the real line (or on a periodic interval) with smooth, nonnegative, compactly supported (or periodic) initial data h(·,0) = h_0, or on a bounded interval I with homogeneous (non-driving) boundary conditions that do not inject mass, momentum, or pressure (so, in particular, no prescribed positive pressure jump or fixed positive boundary heights driving a pinch-off).

Prove (or disprove) that for some range of mobility exponents n > 0 and for some class of smooth nonnegative initial data h_0, there exist solutions h(x,t) of the above equation that develop a finite-time singularity, in the sense that
   inf_{x} h(x,t) → 0   as t ↑ T*   for some finite T* < ∞,
without imposing any forcing through the boundary conditions or external terms.
category_tag: Thin-film lubrication equations and singularity formation
status_search_result: Rigorous finite-time singularity (pinch-off) proofs for the 1D fourth-order lubrication / Hele-Shaw neck equation have so far required driving boundary conditions: Constantin–Elgindi–Nguyen–Vicol (Comm. Math. Phys. 2018) prove pinch-off in finite or infinite time for the Hele-Shaw neck equation under boundary conditions h(±1,t)=1 and h_{xx}(±1,t)=P>2, which is a forced setting. For long-wave unstable variants (with a destabilizing lower-order term) finite-time blow-up of weak solutions is known. For the genuinely unforced surface-tension-driven thin-film/Hele-Shaw equation with mobility h^n, a proof of finite-time singularity formation without special forcing boundary conditions does not appear in the literature and remains an open problem actively discussed in recent work on touchdown singularities.

paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
original_question: For two-dimensional versions of the fourth-order degenerate lubrication equations for a surface-tension-driven film height h, what analytical theory can be developed for existence, regularity, rupture, and asymptotic behavior, given that the one-dimensional theory does not yet extend to two spatial dimensions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the fourth-order degenerate parabolic equation modeling a thin viscous film driven by surface tension in two spatial dimensions:
  h_t + ∇·( f(h) ∇Δh ) = 0,    x ∈ Ω ⊂ ℝ², t > 0,
where h(x,t) ≥ 0 denotes the film height, f(h) = |h|^n with mobility exponent n > 0, and Ω is either a bounded domain (with suitable no-flux/zero-contact-angle boundary conditions) or the torus 𝕋². Initial data h(x,0) = h₀(x) ≥ 0 is prescribed with h₀ ∈ H¹(Ω).

Develop an analytical theory for this two-dimensional problem addressing the following items:
(a) Existence of nonnegative weak (and, where possible, strong) solutions for the full range of mobility exponents n > 0.
(b) Regularity properties of weak solutions, including higher Sobolev regularity, positivity sets, and propagation of the support.
(c) Rupture phenomena: determine for which exponents n finite-time singularities (touch-down of h to zero) can occur, and characterize the local structure (e.g. self-similar profiles) of such singularities.
(d) Long-time asymptotic behavior of global solutions, including convergence to equilibria (constants, droplets) and convergence rates.

Specifically, extend the one-dimensional theory of nonnegative weak solutions, entropy/energy dissipation estimates, finite-speed-of-propagation results, and rupture analysis to the genuinely two-dimensional setting.
status_search_result: Partial progress exists: weak existence and some long-time-behavior results for the multi-dimensional thin-film equation have been established (e.g., Bertozzi–Pugh and subsequent work, including results on convergence to mean and entropy methods). However, a complete two-dimensional theory matching the one-dimensional results — covering the full range of mobility exponents, sharp regularity, finite-speed-of-propagation, and rupture/singularity analysis — remains incomplete. Surveys note that "in 2D, very little is known" relative to the 1D case, although several pieces have been filled in over the past two decades.

paper_title: Some open problems in elasticity
original_question: For nonlinear elastostatics, prove that the elastic energy admits minimizers when the stored-energy function W is quasiconvex and satisfies the singular determinant condition W(A) tends to infinity as det A tends to 0 from above, with W(A) infinite when det A is nonpositive so that orientation collapse is excluded.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \ge 2$) be a bounded Lipschitz domain representing the reference configuration of an elastic body. A deformation is a map $u : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^n$, and its gradient $\nabla u(x)$ takes values in the set $M^{n\times n}$ of real $n\times n$ matrices. Let $M^{n\times n}_+ = \{A \in M^{n\times n} : \det A > 0\}$.

A stored-energy function is a Borel measurable function $W : M^{n\times n} \to [0,\infty]$ satisfying:
(i) (Orientation preservation / non-interpenetration on the energy level) $W(A) = +\infty$ whenever $\det A \le 0$;
(ii) (Singular determinant condition) $W(A) \to +\infty$ as $\det A \to 0^+$, uniformly on bounded subsets of $M^{n\times n}_+$;
(iii) (Quasiconvexity) $W$ is quasiconvex on $M^{n\times n}_+$ in the sense of Morrey: for every $A \in M^{n\times n}_+$ and every $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $A + \nabla\varphi(x) \in M^{n\times n}_+$ a.e.,
$$\int_\Omega W(A + \nabla \varphi(x))\,dx \ge W(A)\,|\Omega|;$$
(iv) (Coercivity) there exist $p \ge 1$ and constants $c > 0$, $b \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $W(A) \ge c|A|^p + b$ for all $A \in M^{n\times n}$.

Consider the energy
$$I(u) = \int_\Omega W(\nabla u(x))\,dx$$
on an admissible class $\mathcal{A}$ of deformations consisting of maps $u \in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ satisfying a prescribed Dirichlet boundary condition $u = u_0$ on a portion $\partial\Omega_1 \subset \partial\Omega$ of positive surface measure (with $u_0$ chosen so that $\mathcal{A}$ is nonempty and $\inf_{\mathcal{A}} I < \infty$).

Prove (or disprove) that under hypotheses (i)–(iv) the functional $I$ attains its infimum on $\mathcal{A}$; equivalently, that there exists $u^* \in \mathcal{A}$ with $I(u^*) = \inf_{u \in \mathcal{A}} I(u)$.
status_search_result: The problem is a long-standing open question. It is widely known as Ball's problem of existence of minimizers in nonlinear elastostatics under quasiconvexity together with the singular behavior of $W$ at $\det A = 0^+$. Polyconvex existence theory (Ball, 1977) handles a stronger convexity hypothesis, and partial results exist (e.g., relaxation results, existence with cavitation/fracture, and special cases), but the general quasiconvex case with the singular determinant constraint remains unresolved as of recent surveys.

paper_title: Some open problems in elasticity
original_question: Determine conditions under which a global minimizer y* of the nonlinear elastic energy I(y)=∫Ω W(Dy) dx is smooth in Ω and smooth up to the boundary, apart from expected singularities near points where the displacement and traction boundary parts meet.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2$ or $3$) be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary $\partial \Omega = \overline{\partial_1\Omega} \cup \overline{\partial_2\Omega}$, where $\partial_1\Omega$ and $\partial_2\Omega$ are disjoint relatively open subsets on which displacement (Dirichlet) and traction (Neumann) boundary conditions are imposed respectively. Let $W : \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ be a stored-energy density (smooth on the set of matrices with positive determinant, polyconvex or quasiconvex, satisfying $W(F) \to \infty$ as $\det F \to 0^+$, and coercive in an appropriate Sobolev space sense). Consider the elastic energy
$$I(y) = \int_\Omega W(Dy(x))\, dx - \langle \text{loads}, y\rangle,$$
defined on admissible deformations $y : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^n$ with $y = y_0$ on $\partial_1\Omega$, $\det Dy > 0$ a.e. Assume the existence of a global minimizer $y^* \in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ of $I$.

Determine geometric and analytic conditions on $W$, $\Omega$, the boundary data, and the loads under which $y^*$ is $C^\infty$ in $\Omega$ and $C^\infty$ up to the boundary except possibly near points of $\overline{\partial_1\Omega} \cap \overline{\partial_2\Omega}$ where displacement and traction boundary regions meet.
status_search_result: The smoothness of global minimizers of nonlinear elastic energies is a long-standing open problem repeatedly highlighted by Ball and others. Only partial regularity results for general quasiconvex functionals (Evans, Kristensen–Mingione, etc.) are known, and these do not apply directly under the determinant-blow-up condition typical in elasticity. No general resolution has been reported.

paper_title: Some open problems in elasticity
original_question: Under reasonable growth conditions on the stored-energy function W, determine whether global minimizers or suitably defined local minimizers of I(y)=∫Ω W(Dy) dx satisfy the weak Euler-Lagrange equation ∫Ω DAW(Dy) · Dφ dx = 0 for all smooth test fields φ that vanish on the displacement boundary.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary, representing the reference configuration of an elastic body, and let $\partial\Omega = \partial_1\Omega \cup \partial_2\Omega$ be a disjoint decomposition into a displacement (Dirichlet) part $\partial_1\Omega$ and a traction-free part $\partial_2\Omega$. Let $W:M^{n\times n}_+\to\mathbb{R}$ be a stored-energy function defined on the set $M^{n\times n}_+$ of $n\times n$ matrices with positive determinant, assumed $C^1$, and satisfying "reasonable" growth conditions (for example, polyconvexity together with a coercivity estimate $W(A)\ge c|A|^p - C$ for some $p\ge 1$, and a growth bound on the derivative $D_AW$ that is compatible with the function space in which minimizers live). Consider the elastic energy
$$ I(y) \;=\; \int_\Omega W(Dy(x))\,dx, $$
defined on the admissible class
$$ \mathcal{A} \;=\; \{\, y\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n) : \det Dy>0\ \text{a.e.},\ y|_{\partial_1\Omega} = y_0 \,\}, $$
where $y_0$ is a prescribed boundary datum.

Prove or disprove: every global minimizer $y\in\mathcal{A}$ of $I$ (and, more generally, every suitably defined local minimizer) satisfies the weak form of the Euler-Lagrange equation
$$ \int_\Omega D_A W(Dy(x)) : D\varphi(x)\,dx \;=\; 0 $$
for every smooth test field $\varphi\in C^\infty_c(\Omega\cup\partial_2\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ vanishing on $\partial_1\Omega$.

status_search_result: The question is a longstanding open problem in the calculus of variations and nonlinear elasticity. Known one-dimensional counterexamples (the Lavrentiev phenomenon) show that without restrictions minimizers need not satisfy the Euler-Lagrange equation, and partial positive results are available for special growth conditions (Ball–Murat, Bauman–Owen–Phillips, and recent work on incompressible minimizers), but the general case under "reasonable" growth on W remains unresolved.

paper_title: Some open problems in elasticity
original_question: Justify the Ciarlet-Necas constrained minimization formulation, or an appropriate modification of it, as a model of smooth frictionless self-contact for elastic bodies, including the vanishing of tangential stress components near self-contact and the regularity of the free boundary.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary, representing the reference configuration of a hyperelastic body, and let $W : \Omega \times \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ be a polyconvex stored-energy function satisfying standard coercivity and growth conditions, with $\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+$ denoting the matrices with positive determinant. Consider the constrained minimization problem of Ciarlet–Nečas type: minimize the elastic energy
$$E(u) = \int_\Omega W(x, \nabla u(x))\,\mathrm{d}x$$
over the class of admissible deformations
$$\mathcal{A} = \Bigl\{ u \in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3) : \det\nabla u > 0 \text{ a.e.,}\ \int_\Omega \det\nabla u(x)\,\mathrm{d}x \le \mathrm{vol}(u(\Omega)),\ u|_{\Gamma_0} = u_0 \Bigr\}$$
(with $p > 3$, prescribed boundary data $u_0$ on a portion $\Gamma_0 \subset \partial\Omega$), the integral inequality being the Ciarlet–Nečas global injectivity condition that allows boundary self-contact but prevents interpenetration.

Provide a rigorous justification of this minimization formulation (or a suitable modification thereof) as a model of smooth frictionless self-contact. Specifically, prove that for a minimizer $u^*$:
(a) the tangential components of the Cauchy stress vector vanish on the deformed self-contact set (no friction);
(b) the free boundary separating the regions of self-contact from the non-contact region is regular (e.g., smooth or locally a $C^1$ hypersurface) under appropriate smoothness hypotheses on $W$ and on the data;
(c) construct admissible variations supported in a neighborhood of the self-contact region needed to derive the corresponding Euler–Lagrange/variational inequality conditions.
status_search_result: The Ciarlet–Nečas formulation (1987) guarantees existence of energy minimizers satisfying the global injectivity condition, but the variational/free-boundary characterization of frictionless self-contact (vanishing tangential stress, regularity of the free boundary) has not been fully established. Recent works (e.g., Krömer–Valdman, ARMA 2021) have refined the admissible class and injectivity properties, but a complete justification including stress conditions and free-boundary regularity remains an open program.

paper_title: Some open problems in elasticity
original_question: Clarify how variational fracture models with energy I(y)=∫Ω W(Dy) dx plus a surface term over the jump set Sy relate to classical fracture mechanics and to nonlinear elastostatics, especially for fracture initiation, stability, and local minimizers.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain representing the reference configuration of an elastic body, and let $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}\to[0,\infty]$ be a stored-energy density satisfying the standard assumptions of nonlinear elastostatics: frame indifference $W(RF)=W(F)$ for all $R\in SO(3)$, material symmetry, $W(F)\to\infty$ as $\det F\to 0^+$, $W(F)=\infty$ if $\det F\le 0$, and suitable polyconvexity/coercivity ensuring existence of minimizers in the classical pure elastic setting.

For a deformation $y:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^3$ in a space of special functions of bounded variation (so that the approximate gradient $Dy$ exists a.e. and the jump set $S_y$ is a countably $\mathcal{H}^{2}$-rectifiable subset of $\Omega$), and for a surface energy density $\psi:\mathbb{R}^3\times \mathbb{R}^3\times S^2\to [0,\infty)$ (depending on the one-sided traces $y^\pm$ and the unit normal $\nu_y$ to $S_y$), define the Griffith-type variational fracture energy
$$
I(y)=\int_{\Omega} W(Dy)\,dx+\int_{S_y}\psi(y^+,y^-,\nu_y)\,d\mathcal{H}^{2},
$$
subject to prescribed Dirichlet boundary data on a portion of $\partial\Omega$.

Clarify the precise relationship between the variational fracture model based on minimizing (or finding local minimizers / stable critical points of) the functional $I$ and (i) classical Griffith fracture mechanics, and (ii) the variational theory of nonlinear elastostatics (where only the bulk term is present). In particular, address the following:

(a) Fracture initiation: characterize, in terms of $W$, $\psi$, and the loading, the conditions under which a globally stable elastic equilibrium $y$ with $S_y=\emptyset$ ceases to be a local minimizer of $I$, and identify the mechanism by which a nontrivial jump set first appears.

(b) Stability: give intrinsic criteria distinguishing global minimizers, local minimizers, and merely stationary configurations of $I$, and relate these to stability notions in classical fracture mechanics (e.g., Griffith's energy-release criterion) and to quasi-static evolutions.

(c) Local minimizers vs. global minimizers: determine whether and in what sense the local-minimization formulation of $I$ is the correct selection principle, and how the resulting solutions compare with the classical solutions of nonlinear elastostatics in regimes where no fracture occurs.

Substantial partial results exist (existence of global minimizers in SBV/GSBD by Dal Maso, Francfort, Toader and others; quasi-static evolutions; convergence to Griffith in special regimes), but a complete clarification covering initiation, stability, and local minimizers in genuinely nonlinear elasticity remains open.

paper_title: Some open problems in elasticity
original_question: Develop a qualitative dynamics for dynamic elasticity theories: after obtaining a global solution theory, determine convergence to equilibria, attraction basins, stable and unstable manifolds, global attractors, and whether dynamic orbits realize local minimizing sequences for ballistic free energy.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a dynamic theory of nonlinear elasticity for a body occupying a reference configuration $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ (a bounded, sufficiently regular domain), with deformation $y:\Omega 	imes [0,\infty) 	o \mathbb{R}^3$ governed by a system of evolution equations of the form
\[
\rho\, y_{tt} = \operatorname{Div}\, S(\nabla y) + \text{(dissipative terms)} ,
\]
where $S = \partial W/\partial F$ is the Piola–Kirchhoff stress derived from a stored-energy function $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying standard frame-indifference, polyconvexity or quasiconvexity, and coercivity assumptions, together with suitable boundary conditions (e.g., mixed displacement/traction) and dissipation (e.g., viscous, viscoelastic of rate type, or thermomechanical coupling giving a ballistic free energy $\Psi$).

Assume that a global-in-time solution theory has been established in an appropriate function space $X$, generating a (possibly multivalued) semiflow $\{S(t)\}_{t\ge 0}$ on $X$.

Develop a qualitative theory of the dynamics of this semiflow by establishing the following:

1. Convergence of trajectories: characterize which initial data $y_0 \in X$ produce solutions $S(t)y_0$ whose $\omega$-limit sets consist of equilibria (stationary solutions of the elastostatic problem $\operatorname{Div}\,S(\nabla y) = 0$ with the given boundary data), and describe the modes of convergence.

2. Basins of attraction: for each (stable) equilibrium $\bar y$, determine the structure of its basin of attraction $\mathcal{B}(\bar y) = \{y_0 \in X : S(t)y_0 \to \bar y\}$.

3. Invariant manifolds: construct local stable, unstable, and center manifolds at equilibria, and clarify their regularity and persistence.

4. Global attractors: prove existence and characterize the structure (e.g., finite Hausdorff/fractal dimension, gradient structure) of a global attractor $\mathcal{A} \subset X$ for the semiflow.

5. Energy minimization along orbits: determine whether dynamic orbits realize local minimizing sequences for the ballistic free energy functional $\Psi$ — that is, whether for generic initial data the trajectory $t \mapsto S(t)y_0$ provides a minimizing sequence (in an appropriate local sense) for $\Psi$ over an admissible class, and characterize the limiting microstructures (e.g., Young measures) that may emerge when classical minimizers fail to exist.

Provide answers to (1)–(5) under explicit and physically reasonable hypotheses on $W$, the dissipation mechanism, and the boundary conditions.
status_search_result: This is a long-standing programmatic open problem in nonlinear elastodynamics. Partial results exist for special cases (viscoelasticity of rate type, one-dimensional models, gradient-flow approximations, quasistatic limits), but no comprehensive qualitative dynamics theory covering convergence to equilibria, basins of attraction, invariant manifolds, global attractors, and minimizing-orbit properties for ballistic free energy is available in the general 3D nonlinear elasticity setting. The problem remains open.

paper_title: Some open problems in elasticity
original_question: Establish the relationship between continuum elasticity theory and atomistic models, including whether elasticity can be derived from quantum, density-functional, Thomas-Fermi, or interatomic-potential models; what limiting energy and function space arise from atomistic minimizers; and how atomistic-continuum matching methods such as quasicontinuum schemes can be rigorously understood.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a crystalline solid modeled as a discrete configuration of atoms occupying, in a reference state, the lattice $\varepsilon \mathbb{Z}^d \cap \Omega$ (or a more general Bravais/multilattice) inside a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, where $\varepsilon>0$ is the interatomic spacing. To each deformation $y:\varepsilon\mathbb{Z}^d\cap\Omega \to \mathbb{R}^d$ associate a discrete energy $E_\varepsilon(y)$ derived from one of the following atomistic descriptions:
(i) a quantum many-body Schrödinger Hamiltonian for nuclei and electrons;
(ii) a Kohn–Sham or Hartree–Fock density-functional energy;
(iii) a Thomas–Fermi (or Thomas–Fermi–von Weizsäcker) functional;
(iv) a classical interatomic potential energy $E_\varepsilon(y)=\sum_{i} V_i\bigl(\{y(x_j)-y(x_i)\}_{j}\bigr)$ involving pair, three-body, or many-body interactions (e.g. Lennard–Jones, embedded-atom, Stillinger–Weber).

Address rigorously the following three coupled questions.

1. (Derivation of continuum elasticity.) For each class of atomistic model above, identify a continuum elastic energy functional
$$E(u)=\int_\Omega W(\nabla u(x))\,dx$$
(or its appropriate non-simple/higher-gradient generalization) and a function space $X$ of admissible deformations $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $E_\varepsilon \xrightarrow{\Gamma} E$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$ in a suitable topology, and characterize the stored-energy density $W$ (e.g. via the Cauchy–Born rule $W(F)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N^d}\min E_{\rm cell}(F\cdot\,\cdot\,)$) together with its domain of validity (small strains, frame indifference, material symmetry, possible loss of validity under large or non-rank-one strains).

2. (Limits of true minimizers.) Let $y_\varepsilon$ be a sequence of (almost) minimizers of $E_\varepsilon$ subject to prescribed boundary or loading data. Determine the limiting functional $\mathcal{F}$ and function space $X^*$ (which may differ from $X$ above and may incorporate defects: dislocations, cracks, grain boundaries, or plastic slip) such that, up to subsequence, $y_\varepsilon \to u$ in $X^*$ and $u$ minimizes $\mathcal{F}$, and identify the mechanism by which microstructure, defects, or singular measures arise in $\mathcal{F}$.

3. (Quasicontinuum coupling.) Formulate quasicontinuum-type atomistic-to-continuum coupling schemes (energy-based, force-based, blended, or ghost-force-free variants) in which the atomistic energy is retained in a small subdomain while a Cauchy–Born continuum approximation is used elsewhere, and establish: (a) consistency (truncation/coupling error), (b) stability of the linearized coupled operator uniformly in $\varepsilon$ and in the size of the atomistic region, and (c) optimal a priori and a posteriori error estimates between the coupled solution and the fully atomistic minimizer in the presence of typical defects (point defects, dislocations, cracks).

Provide a unified rigorous theory, valid for at least one of the model classes (i)–(iv), that simultaneously answers (1), (2), and (3).
status_search_result: Significant partial results exist: Γ-convergence derivations of nonlinear elasticity from pair interactions (Alicandro–Cicalese, Friesecke–Theil), rigorous plate theory (Friesecke–James–Müller), Cauchy–Born validity in small-strain regimes (E–Ming, Conti–Dolzmann–Kirchheim–Müller), and convergence/error analyses of quasicontinuum methods (Ortner, Luskin, Süli, and collaborators), including blended force-based schemes for multilattices with defects. However, a unified rigorous derivation starting from quantum, DFT, or Thomas–Fermi models, a complete characterization of limits of true atomistic minimizers in the presence of generic defects, and a fully general convergence theory for atomistic/continuum coupling remain open active research areas.

paper_title: Some open problems in elasticity
original_question: For a thermoelastic single crystal undergoing a diffusionless phase transformation at critical temperature θc, determine the quasiconvexification K(θ)^qc of the set K(θ) of energy-minimizing deformation gradients for temperatures θ≤θc, including the cubic-to-tetragonal case at and below θc.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a thermoelastic single crystal in three dimensions undergoing a diffusionless (displacive) phase transformation at a critical temperature θ_c. Let M^{3×3} denote the set of real 3×3 matrices and M^{3×3}_+ the subset of matrices with strictly positive determinant. Suppose ψ : M^{3×3}_+ × ℝ → [0,∞) is a frame-indifferent stored-energy density (so ψ(RA,θ) = ψ(A,θ) for every R ∈ SO(3)) which is materially symmetric under the cubic point group, and which for each temperature θ attains its minimum value 0. Define the set of energy-minimizing deformation gradients at temperature θ by

   K(θ) := { A ∈ M^{3×3}_+ : ψ(A,θ) = 0 }.

For a compact set K ⊂ M^{3×3}, its quasiconvexification K^{qc} is defined as

   K^{qc} := { A ∈ M^{3×3} : f(A) ≤ sup_{B ∈ K} f(B) for every quasiconvex f : M^{3×3} → ℝ },

where f : M^{3×3} → ℝ is quasiconvex if for every bounded open Ω ⊂ ℝ^3, every A ∈ M^{3×3}, and every φ ∈ W^{1,∞}_0(Ω;ℝ^3),

   ∫_Ω f(A + ∇φ(x)) dx ≥ |Ω| f(A).

For the cubic-to-tetragonal case at and below θ_c, one has explicitly
   K(θ) = SO(3) U_1(θ) ∪ SO(3) U_2(θ) ∪ SO(3) U_3(θ)    for θ < θ_c,
   K(θ_c) = SO(3) ∪ SO(3) U_1(θ_c) ∪ SO(3) U_2(θ_c) ∪ SO(3) U_3(θ_c),
where U_i(θ) = diag(η_2, η_2, η_2) with the entry η_1 in the i-th diagonal position (η_1, η_2 > 0 temperature-dependent stretch parameters with η_1 ≠ η_2 for θ < θ_c, and η_1 = η_2 = 1 at θ = θ_c giving the austenite identity).

Problem. Determine the quasiconvexification K(θ)^{qc} explicitly for all θ ≤ θ_c, in particular for the cubic-to-tetragonal three-well case (and the four-well case at θ = θ_c that also includes SO(3)).
status_search_result: The problem is widely regarded as open. While the two-well quasiconvexification (relevant to e.g. orthorhombic-to-monoclinic transitions) has been computed via minors relations, the three-well cubic-to-tetragonal case—and the four-well case including SO(3) at θ = θ_c—remains unresolved. Partial results, such as characterizing rank-one connections between SO(3) and K(θ)^{qc} (Ball–Carstensen) and other structural properties, are known, but a complete explicit description of K(θ)^{qc} is not available.

paper_title: Some open problems in elasticity
original_question: Give rigorous derivations of one-dimensional rod models and two-dimensional plate or shell models from three-dimensional elasticity, proving that their solutions approximate appropriate three-dimensional elastic solutions as the thickness parameter h tends to zero, with convergence and error estimates that handle loads, boundary conditions, buckling, and boundary layers.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega_h = \omega \times (-h/2, h/2) \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ for a bounded Lipschitz domain $\omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ (or, for rods, let $\Omega_h$ be a thin tube of cross-sectional diameter $h$ around a smooth curve in $\mathbb{R}^3$). Consider three-dimensional hyperelastic bodies governed by a stored-energy functional
$$E_h(y) = \int_{\Omega_h} W(\nabla y(x))\, dx - \int_{\Omega_h} f_h \cdot y\, dx - \int_{\partial_N \Omega_h} g_h \cdot y\, dS,$$
where $W : \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3} \to [0,\infty]$ is a frame-indifferent stored-energy density satisfying $W(R) = 0$ for $R \in SO(3)$, $W(F) \ge c\,\mathrm{dist}^2(F, SO(3))$, and is suitably regular near $SO(3)$; deformations $y : \Omega_h \to \mathbb{R}^3$ are subject to mixed Dirichlet/Neumann boundary conditions on the lateral and end (or top/bottom) faces of $\Omega_h$, and $f_h, g_h$ are applied body and surface loads.

(a) Rigorously derive one-dimensional rod models and two-dimensional plate and shell models as the limits of $E_h$ when the thickness parameter $h \to 0$, for all natural scalings of the elastic energy (e.g., $h^\beta$-scalings yielding stretching, von Kármán, linearized von Kármán, bending, and constrained membrane regimes).

(b) Prove that, for each such regime, the sets of (approximate) minimizers and, more generally, solution sets of the corresponding three-dimensional boundary value problems converge — in a suitable topology after rescaling to a fixed reference domain — to the solution sets of the limit lower-dimensional models, with quantitative error estimates in $h$.

(c) Extend these convergence and error results to handle:
  (i) general dead and live loads and mixed boundary conditions;
  (ii) buckling phenomena, including bifurcation diagrams of the 3D problem versus those of the reduced model;
  (iii) boundary layers near lateral boundaries and points of boundary-condition change.

Give a unified rigorous theory establishing such derivations together with explicit convergence and error estimates that cover (a), (b), and (c).
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on this program. Via Γ-convergence, a complete hierarchy of plate models (membrane, von Kármán, linearized von Kármán, bending/Kirchhoff) has been rigorously derived from 3D nonlinear elasticity (Friesecke–James–Müller and successors), as well as analogous theories for rods (including bending–torsion, curved, and incompressible rods) and shells (nonlinear bending shells, von Kármán shells, homogenized shells). However, a unified theory delivering quantitative error estimates, convergence of full solution sets (not just minimizers) under general loads and mixed boundary conditions, rigorous treatment of buckling/bifurcation, and complete boundary-layer analysis remains incomplete; many of these aspects are still active research problems.
