paper_title: Open Problems in Real-time Scheduling
original_question: For a preemptive multiprocessor real-time system under global scheduling, determine the computational complexity of feasibility analysis for sporadic task systems with arbitrary deadlines. The input is a sporadic task system tau and a positive integer m > 1; global scheduling permits a job to begin execution on any processor and to resume on any processor after preemption. Is tau feasible on a platform of m preemptive processors, meaning that for every legal sequence of job arrivals generated by tau there exists a schedule meeting all deadlines?
self_contained_problem:
A sporadic task system is a finite collection τ = {τ_1, …, τ_n} of tasks, where each task τ_i = (C_i, D_i, T_i) is specified by a worst-case execution requirement C_i ∈ ℚ_{>0}, a (relative) deadline D_i ∈ ℚ_{>0}, and a minimum inter-arrival separation T_i ∈ ℚ_{>0}. No restriction is imposed between D_i and T_i (the "arbitrary-deadline" model). A legal job-arrival sequence generated by τ consists of, for each task τ_i, an arbitrary (possibly infinite) sequence of jobs whose successive release times differ by at least T_i; the job released at time r by τ_i has execution requirement C_i and absolute deadline r + D_i.

Given an integer m > 1, a platform of m identical preemptive processors is governed by the global scheduling paradigm: at every instant, any subset of at most m jobs may be executed in parallel (each on a distinct processor), and a preempted job may later resume execution on any processor (migration is allowed at no cost). A job is assumed to never execute on more than one processor simultaneously.

The task system τ is said to be feasible on m processors under global scheduling if, for every legal job-arrival sequence generated by τ, there exists a schedule on the m processors in which every job receives C_i units of execution between its release time and its absolute deadline.

Problem. Determine the computational complexity of deciding, given as input a sporadic task system τ with arbitrary deadlines and an integer m > 1, whether τ is feasible on m preemptive processors under global scheduling.
status_search_result: Subsequent work after the problem was posed produced exact decision procedures for the arbitrary-deadline global feasibility problem (notably state-space / antichain algorithms by Baker–Cirinei and by Bonifaci–Marchetti-Spaccamela), and PSPACE-hardness has been established for related multiprocessor sporadic feasibility problems. However, a tight complexity classification (matching upper and lower bounds) specifically for arbitrary-deadline global feasibility on m identical preemptive processors does not appear to be settled in the literature, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

paper_title: Open Problems in Real-time Scheduling
original_question: For a preemptive multiprocessor real-time system with implicit-deadline sporadic tasks and a specified total priority order on the tasks, determine whether global fixed-priority schedulability is decidable by an exact test and what its computational complexity is. The input is tau, m > 1 preemptive processors, and the priority assignment; the question is whether fixed-priority scheduling on m processors meets every deadline for every legal job-arrival sequence generated by tau.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. An implicit-deadline sporadic task system is a finite set τ = {T_1, …, T_n} of tasks, where each task T_i = (C_i, P_i) consists of a worst-case execution time C_i > 0 and a period P_i ≥ C_i; its relative deadline equals P_i. A legal job-arrival sequence generated by τ produces, for each task T_i, an infinite stream of jobs such that consecutive jobs of T_i are released at least P_i time units apart; each released job requires up to C_i units of processor time and must complete by P_i time units after its release.

Global fixed-priority (FP) scheduling on m identical processors (m > 1, integer), under a given total priority order ≺ on the tasks, works as follows: at every instant the scheduler executes, on the m processors, the (up to) m active jobs whose tasks have highest priority under ≺; preemption and migration of jobs across processors are permitted at no cost. The system τ is said to be FP-schedulable on m processors under ≺ if, for every legal job-arrival sequence generated by τ, every job meets its deadline.

Problem. Given as input an implicit-deadline sporadic task system τ, an integer m > 1, and a total priority assignment on τ:

(a) Is the question "Is τ FP-schedulable on m processors under the given priority assignment?" decidable by an exact algorithm?

(b) If decidable, determine its computational complexity.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has established decidability of exact global fixed-priority schedulability for implicit-deadline sporadic tasks on identical multiprocessors by exhibiting a bounded "decidability interval" and a pre-order/simulation-based exact test, but the resulting algorithms are of very high complexity and only handle small systems (a handful of tasks/processors). The precise computational complexity (e.g., tight hardness classification) remains unresolved, so the problem is at best partially solved.

paper_title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity for left D-Chebyshev convexity
original_question: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and let C be a nonempty closed subset of U. The Bregman distance induced by f is D(x, y) = f(x) - f(y) - <grad f(y), x - y> for y in U. The set C is called left D-Chebyshev when, for every y in U, the left nearest-points map P_left,C(y) = {x in C | D(x, y) = inf_{z in C} D(z, y)} is a singleton. It is known that if f is supercoercive and C is left D-Chebyshev, then C is convex. Is the supercoercivity assumption actually necessary for that convexity conclusion?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X=\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $f\colon X\to[-\infty,+\infty]$ be a convex function of Legendre type (i.e., proper, lower semicontinuous, essentially smooth, and essentially strictly convex). Set $U=\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom} f$, and define the Bregman distance induced by $f$ by
$$D(x,y)=f(x)-f(y)-\langle \nabla f(y),x-y\rangle\quad\text{for }x\in\operatorname{dom} f,\ y\in U.$$
Recall that $f$ is called supercoercive if $\lim_{\|x\|\to\infty} f(x)/\|x\|=+\infty$.

Let $C\subseteq U$ be a nonempty closed subset. For $y\in U$, define the left Bregman nearest-point map
$$P^{\leftarrow}_C(y)=\bigl\{x\in C\ :\ D(x,y)=\inf_{z\in C} D(z,y)\bigr\}.$$
The set $C$ is said to be left $D$-Chebyshev if $P^{\leftarrow}_C(y)$ is a singleton for every $y\in U$.

It is known that if $f$ is supercoercive and $C$ is left $D$-Chebyshev, then $C$ is convex.

Question: Is the supercoercivity assumption on $f$ essential for this conclusion? Equivalently, does there exist a Legendre convex function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ that is not supercoercive together with a nonempty closed left $D$-Chebyshev subset $C\subseteq U$ which fails to be convex; or can the conclusion that $C$ is convex be obtained without assuming supercoercivity?
status_search_result: Web search did not locate a published resolution of the question whether supercoercivity is essential for convexity of left D-Chebyshev sets. Subsequent work on generalized Bregman distances continues to assume supercoercivity (or related coercivity hypotheses) when deriving convexity-type conclusions, indicating the problem remains open.

paper_title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
context_brief: Existence of nonquadratic full-domain right D-Chebyshev geometry
original_question: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function with full domain X, and define the Bregman distance D(a, b) = f(a) - f(b) - <grad f(b), a - b>. A nonempty closed convex subset C of X is right D-Chebyshev if every x in X has a unique point y in C minimizing D(x, y). Does there exist such an f that is not quadratic, but for which every nonempty closed convex subset of X is right D-Chebyshev? Equivalently, can a nonquadratic full-domain Legendre generator have a nonaffine gradient map that nevertheless preserves convexity strongly enough to make all nonempty closed convex subsets right D-Chebyshev?
self_contained_problem:
Let X = R^n with the standard inner product ⟨·,·⟩. A function f: X → (−∞, +∞] is called a convex function of Legendre type with full domain X if:
(i) dom f = X, f is convex, lower semicontinuous, and essentially smooth in the sense that f is differentiable on X with ∇f continuous; and
(ii) f is essentially strictly convex, equivalently, ∇f is injective on X (so that ∇f: X → ∇f(X) is a bijection onto an open convex set with ∇f^{-1} = ∇f*, where f* denotes the Fenchel conjugate of f).

For such f, define the Bregman distance
   D(a, b) = f(a) − f(b) − ⟨∇f(b), a − b⟩, for a, b ∈ X.

A nonempty closed convex subset C ⊆ X is called right D-Chebyshev if, for every x ∈ X, there exists a unique point y = y(x) ∈ C minimizing the function y ↦ D(x, y) over C (i.e., the second argument is the variable point in C).

Question: Does there exist a convex Legendre function f: X → R with full domain X which is not a quadratic function (equivalently, whose gradient map ∇f is not affine), yet for which every nonempty closed convex subset C of X is right D-Chebyshev?

Note: An affirmative answer would produce a nonaffine yet convexity-preserving smooth bijection ∇f of X onto an open convex subset of X.

paper_title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity in near-Chebyshev single-valuedness
original_question: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and define the Bregman distance D(a, b) = f(a) - f(b) - <grad f(b), a - b> for b in U. For a nonempty closed subset C of U, let P_left,C(y) be the set of points in C minimizing D(., y). Suppose f is twice continuously differentiable and the Hessian grad^2 f(y) is positive definite for every y in U. If f is additionally supercoercive, then P_left,C is known to be single-valued almost everywhere and generically on U. Is the supercoercivity assumption genuinely necessary for this almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness conclusion?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X = \mathbb{R}^n$ and let $f: X \to [-\infty, +\infty]$ be a convex function of Legendre type (i.e., essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex). Set $U = \operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom} f)$, and define the Bregman distance
$$D(a, b) = f(a) - f(b) - \langle \nabla f(b), a - b \rangle \quad \text{for } a \in X,\ b \in U.$$
For a nonempty closed subset $C \subseteq U$, define the left Bregman projection
$$P_{\leftarrow, C}(y) = \operatorname*{argmin}_{c \in C} D(c, y), \quad y \in U.$$
Assume in addition that $f$ is twice continuously differentiable on $U$ and that the Hessian $\nabla^2 f(y)$ is positive definite for every $y \in U$. It is known that if $f$ is moreover supercoercive (i.e., $\lim_{\|x\| \to \infty} f(x)/\|x\| = +\infty$), then $P_{\leftarrow, C}$ is single-valued both Lebesgue-almost everywhere and on a generic (dense $G_\delta$) subset of $U$.

Question: Is the supercoercivity hypothesis on $f$ genuinely necessary for the conclusion that $P_{\leftarrow, C}$ is almost everywhere and generically single-valued on $U$? Equivalently, does there exist a convex Legendre function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, twice continuously differentiable with positive definite Hessian on $U$ but not supercoercive, together with a nonempty closed subset $C \subseteq U$, for which $P_{\leftarrow, C}$ fails to be single-valued almost everywhere or generically on $U$?

paper_title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
context_brief: Bregman analogues of Chebyshev and Klee functions
original_question: Let X = R^n and let g: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a proper lower semicontinuous function. In the Euclidean theory of Chebyshev and Klee functions, the discrepancy is q(x) = (1/2)||x||^2, the halved Euclidean distance squared. What are the corresponding characterizations when that Euclidean discrepancy is replaced by a Bregman distance generated by a Legendre function f? In particular, how should one characterize the admissible generator f and the associated Chebyshev point in the Bregman-distance setting?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X=\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $g:X\to[-\infty,+\infty]$ be a proper lower semicontinuous function. In the Euclidean setting, define the halved squared-distance discrepancy $q(x)=\tfrac{1}{2}\|x\|^2$, and recall that:
- the Chebyshev (proximal) function of $g$ is $\mathrm{env}_g(x)=\inf_{y\in X}\{g(y)+q(x-y)\}$, and $g$ is called a Chebyshev function if the proximal mapping $\mathrm{Prox}_g(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y}\{g(y)+q(x-y)\}$ is single-valued for every $x\in X$;
- the Klee (farthest) function of $g$ is $\sup_{y\in X}\{q(x-y)-g(y)\}$, and $g$ is called a Klee function if the farthest mapping is single-valued for every $x\in X$.

Now replace $q$ by a Bregman distance. Let $f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be a Legendre function (i.e., a proper lower semicontinuous convex function that is essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex on $\mathrm{int}\,\mathrm{dom}\,f$), and define the Bregman distance
$$D_f(x,y)=f(x)-f(y)-\langle \nabla f(y),\,x-y\rangle,\qquad x\in\mathrm{dom}\,f,\ y\in\mathrm{int}\,\mathrm{dom}\,f.$$
Replace $q(x-y)$ by $D_f(x,y)$ (or by $D_f(y,x)$ for the right Bregman variant) in the definitions of the proximal and farthest envelopes of $g$.

Problem: Provide intrinsic characterizations, in the Bregman-distance setting, of:
(i) the class of Legendre generators $f$ for which the Bregman Chebyshev (respectively Klee) function of $g$ is well-defined and has the expected single-valuedness and regularity properties;
(ii) the Bregman Chebyshev point (the unique minimizer in the Bregman proximal problem) of a proper lsc function $g$ in terms of $f$, $g$, and the geometry induced by $D_f$.

That is, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $f$ and on $g$ under which $g$ is a Bregman-Chebyshev (resp. Bregman-Klee) function, and give an explicit description of the associated Chebyshev point.
status_search_result: Related work has established Bregman analogues of Klee sets and Chebyshev centers (e.g., uniqueness of Klee sets and Chebyshev centers with respect to right Bregman distances induced by Legendre functions), and Chebyshev/Klee functions have been studied in the Euclidean case. However, a complete characterization of admissible Legendre generators $f$ and of the Bregman Chebyshev point at the level of functions (rather than sets) does not appear to be definitively settled in the literature surveyed; partial results exist but a full answer to the stated problem remains unverified.

paper_title: Introduction to the Yang-Baxter Equation with Open Problems
original_question: For Yang-Baxter operators obtained from algebra structures, can these operators be obtained from a universal R-matrix, with the universal R-matrix understood in connection with quasi-triangular structures? Here a Yang-Baxter operator is an invertible solution of the Yang-Baxter braid relation, and the algebra-structure family refers to operators arising from k-algebras.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $V$ be a $k$-vector space. A Yang–Baxter operator on $V$ is a $k$-linear isomorphism $R: V\otimes V \to V\otimes V$ satisfying the braid relation
$$ (R\otimes \mathrm{id}_V)(\mathrm{id}_V\otimes R)(R\otimes \mathrm{id}_V) = (\mathrm{id}_V\otimes R)(R\otimes \mathrm{id}_V)(\mathrm{id}_V\otimes R) $$
on $V\otimes V\otimes V$. 

Given a unital associative $k$-algebra $A$ and scalars $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in k$ (not all zero, satisfying the standard non-degeneracy condition that ensures invertibility), the operator
$$ R^A_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}(a\otimes b) = \alpha\, ab\otimes 1 + \beta\, 1\otimes ab - \gamma\, a\otimes b $$
on $A\otimes A$ is a Yang–Baxter operator; the family of such operators (as $A$ and the parameters vary) is referred to as the family of Yang–Baxter operators from algebra structures.

A quasi-triangular bialgebra is a pair $(H,\mathcal{R})$ where $H$ is a $k$-bialgebra and $\mathcal{R}\in H\otimes H$ is an invertible element (called a universal $R$-matrix) satisfying
$$ \Delta^{\mathrm{op}}(h) = \mathcal{R}\,\Delta(h)\,\mathcal{R}^{-1}\quad (h\in H), $$
$$ (\Delta\otimes \mathrm{id})(\mathcal{R}) = \mathcal{R}_{13}\mathcal{R}_{23},\qquad (\mathrm{id}\otimes \Delta)(\mathcal{R}) = \mathcal{R}_{13}\mathcal{R}_{12}. $$
Every representation $\rho: H \to \mathrm{End}(V)$ of a quasi-triangular bialgebra gives rise to a Yang–Baxter operator $R = \tau\circ (\rho\otimes\rho)(\mathcal{R})$ on $V\otimes V$, where $\tau$ is the flip.

Question: Can every Yang–Baxter operator from an algebra structure (i.e., every operator of the form $R^A_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}$ as above) be realized as arising from a universal $R$-matrix of some quasi-triangular bialgebra, via a suitable representation?
status_search_result: The conjecture that Yang–Baxter operators from algebra structures arise from some universal R-matrix (related to quasi-triangular bialgebras) is stated as an open problem in the literature on the Yang–Baxter equation and continues to be referenced as an active conjecture in subsequent surveys and papers by Nichita and collaborators. No resolution was found.

paper_title: Models, feedback control, and open problems of 3D bipedal robotic walking
original_question: Develop models, analysis procedures, control designs, and especially stability notions for bipedal locomotion that do not assume the gait is periodic. In particular, characterize and control aperiodic walking behaviors that arise naturally when a biped walks over uneven ground or maneuvers around obstacles.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a 3D bipedal walking robot modeled as a hybrid dynamical system

  Σ:  ẋ = f(x) + g(x)u   when x ∈ 𝒳 ∖ 𝒮,
        x⁺ = Δ(x⁻)        when x⁻ ∈ 𝒮,

where 𝒳 ⊂ ℝⁿ is the state manifold of joint positions and velocities, 𝒮 ⊂ 𝒳 is a switching surface representing foot impacts with the ground, Δ: 𝒮 → 𝒳 is a (possibly discontinuous) reset map encoding the impact dynamics and leg swap, and u ∈ ℝᵐ is the control input applied through joint actuators.

Most of the existing analysis and feedback-control framework for such systems (including hybrid zero dynamics and Poincaré-map-based stability analysis) assumes the closed-loop walking gait is a periodic orbit of Σ. The task is the following:

1. Define a precise and useful notion of stability for non-periodic (aperiodic) walking trajectories of Σ, applicable in particular to:
   (a) walking over terrain whose ground-height profile is not periodic and is not known in advance, and
   (b) maneuvering tasks where the biped must change heading and step placement to avoid obstacles, so that successive steps cannot be assumed identical.

2. Develop modeling, analysis procedures, and constructive feedback control designs that certify this stability notion for the hybrid system Σ in three spatial dimensions, without reducing the problem to tracking or stabilizing a predetermined periodic orbit.

Provide:
  - a formal definition of aperiodic-gait stability for Σ (e.g., in terms of forward invariance of a step-to-step set-valued map, input-to-state stability with respect to terrain/obstacle disturbances, or contraction of a non-autonomous Poincaré-like map);
  - analysis tools sufficient to certify this stability property;
  - a control synthesis methodology producing feedback laws u = k(x, ξ), with ξ encoding terrain/obstacle information, that achieve the stability property on a non-trivial class of 3D bipedal models.
category_tag: Bipedal robotic walking / aperiodic gait stability
status_search_result: This is a long-standing open research direction in legged locomotion control. While there has been substantial progress since 2014 on aperiodic and rough-terrain walking (e.g., step-to-step dynamics, control Lyapunov function and MPC-based approaches, capture-point/ALIP methods, and contraction-based analyses), no universally accepted stability notion or general control-design framework for aperiodic 3D bipedal gaits has emerged. The problem is generally regarded as still open.

paper_title: Models, feedback control, and open problems of 3D bipedal robotic walking
original_question: Develop methods for maneuvering a 3D bipedal robot, such as turning or steering, that come with rigorous stability guarantees and also respect unilateral ground-contact constraints during the maneuver. The goal is not only to generate maneuvers heuristically, but to explain how a robot can change direction safely while maintaining dynamically stable walking.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a 3D bipedal robot modeled as a hybrid dynamical system: during each single-support phase the robot evolves according to Lagrangian dynamics with the stance foot acting as a pivot subject to unilateral ground-contact constraints (non-negative normal reaction force, friction-cone constraints, and no roll/slip of the stance foot), and at foot touchdown the state undergoes an impact reset map. A periodic walking gait is a hybrid limit cycle of this system that respects the unilateral contact constraints throughout, and is called dynamically stable if the associated Poincaré return map has a locally exponentially stable fixed point.

Develop a feedback control design methodology for executing maneuvers — in particular, turning or steering to change the robot's heading direction — that satisfies all of the following:

(i) Throughout the maneuver, the closed-loop trajectory satisfies the unilateral ground-contact constraints (positive normal force, friction-cone, and no foot rotation/slip) at every instant.

(ii) The maneuver is realized by transitioning between, or continuously deforming, families of parametrized periodic gaits (e.g., gaits parametrized by turning radius or heading rate), and the transitions admit a rigorous proof of stability — for instance, via a common Lyapunov function, a multiple Lyapunov function with dwell-time conditions, or contraction-based arguments applied to the hybrid Poincaré map.

(iii) The method yields verifiable certificates (analytical or computational) that the robot can change direction by a prescribed amount while maintaining dynamic stability and contact feasibility.

Provide either such a construction together with a proof, or establish obstructions showing why such guarantees cannot be obtained under stated assumptions on the model.

The question is generally regarded as an open research direction in the dynamic-walking community.

paper_title: Models, feedback control, and open problems of 3D bipedal robotic walking
original_question: Design control methods that let a biped with passive feet or passive ankles stand stably and recover a quiescent standing posture after external pushes. The problem is specifically about balance recovery and stationary stabilization when the ankle is not actively actuated.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a 3D bipedal robot modeled as a rigid multibody system whose feet (or ankles) are passive, i.e., the ankle joints supply no active torque and the foot–ground interaction is only a unilateral contact (the foot rolls or pivots freely about its support region subject to non-penetration and friction constraints). Let the joint configuration be q ∈ Q with actuated coordinates q_a (legs, hips, torso, arms) and unactuated coordinates q_u (the rigid-body pose modulo the contact and the passive ankle degrees of freedom), governed by the constrained Euler–Lagrange dynamics

    M(q) q̈ + C(q,q̇) q̇ + G(q) = B u + J(q)^T λ,

with contact wrench λ constrained to a friction cone and supported on the foot contact region, and B selecting only the actuated joints.

Design a feedback control law u = k(q, q̇) (possibly with internal state and hybrid switching among contact modes such as flat-foot, toe-roll, heel-roll, or stepping) such that:

(i) (Quiet stance) The closed-loop system admits an asymptotically stable equilibrium corresponding to a desired upright standing posture q* with q̇* = 0, while keeping the contact wrench inside the friction cone and the center of pressure within the support polygon.

(ii) (Push recovery) There exists a non-empty, characterizable set D of admissible external impulsive disturbances applied to the robot's body such that, for every disturbance in D, the closed-loop trajectory returns asymptotically to the quiescent standing posture q*, possibly after a finite number of automatic stepping or contact transitions, while maintaining all unilateral contact and friction constraints throughout.

Either exhibit such a controller together with a proof and an explicit characterization of the disturbance set D, or show that no such controller exists under the passive-ankle constraint.
status_search_result: The problem of stable quiet standing and push recovery for bipeds with passive feet/ankles remains an active research topic. Recent work proposes partial solutions (e.g., whole-body locomotion control for passive-ankle robots, footstep-adjustment push recovery, series-elastic ankle reflex control), but no general controller with provable recovery guarantees for arbitrary admissible pushes on fully passive-ankle 3D bipeds has been established. The problem is therefore considered open in general, with partial results in restricted settings.

original_question: Compute or characterize the domain of attraction of a periodic walking gait for a bipedal robot, especially in the hybrid-systems setting and in the presence of modeling errors that arise when transferring a controller from simulation to the physical robot. The problem asks for practical ways to estimate which perturbations and initial conditions still converge to the desired periodic gait.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a planar or three-dimensional bipedal walking robot modeled as a hybrid dynamical system: continuous-time rigid-body Lagrangian dynamics during the single- (and possibly double-) support phase, together with a discrete reset map modeling the instantaneous impact of the swing leg with the ground. Let the closed-loop system, under a chosen feedback controller, admit an exponentially stable periodic orbit O (a hybrid limit cycle) corresponding to a desired walking gait, with associated Poincaré return map P having a fixed point x* whose linearization is Schur stable.

(1) Develop a constructive method to compute or rigorously inner-approximate the domain of attraction D(O) := { x in the hybrid state space : the trajectory starting at x is defined for all forward time and converges to O } of such a hybrid periodic orbit, going beyond local linearization at x*.

(2) Extend the method to the robust setting: given a family of admissible perturbations to the continuous and discrete dynamics (e.g., bounded parametric model errors in inertia, mass, link lengths, contact location, and impact map), characterize or inner-approximate the robust domain of attraction—the set of initial conditions guaranteed to converge to a neighborhood of the nominal gait for every admissible perturbation—so that the estimate yields practical guarantees when transferring a controller designed in simulation to the physical robot.

Provide either an algorithmic procedure (with convergence/soundness guarantees) or analytic characterizations producing certified inner approximations of D(O), together with quantitative bounds in terms of the size of the modeling errors.

status_search_result: Computation of regions of attraction for hybrid limit cycles in bipedal walking remains an active research area. Recent works (e.g., SOS/Lyapunov-based RoA computation for hybrid limit cycles, cell-mapping methods, and contraction-based estimates) provide partial inner approximations and locally certified results, but a general, scalable, and robust characterization that accounts for modeling errors when transferring controllers from simulation to hardware is still considered open. paper_title: Models, feedback control, and open problems of 3D bipedal robotic walking
original_question: Construct a metric for comparing walking gaits, including a distance between solutions of hybrid systems even when the underlying hybrid models are different, so that one can decide which controller and which hybrid model produce the most human-like walking. Such a metric should also support comparison between robotic walking data and human walking data.
self_contained_problem:
Background. A hybrid dynamical system is a tuple H = (Γ, D, U, S, Δ, F) consisting of a directed graph Γ with vertices V and edges E, a domain D_v ⊂ R^{n_v} and admissible control set U_v for each v ∈ V, a guard (switching surface) S_e ⊂ D_{source(e)} and a reset map Δ_e : S_e → D_{target(e)} for each e ∈ E, and a family of controlled vector fields F_v on D_v. An execution (solution) of H is a piecewise-smooth trajectory that flows under F_v inside each domain and jumps across edges via Δ_e whenever it reaches a guard. A periodic walking gait of a bipedal robot or a human is a periodic execution of such a hybrid system.

Two different bipedal walkers (e.g., a robot model with given mechanical parameters and feedback controller, or a human modeled from motion-capture data) are typically described by hybrid systems H_1 and H_2 whose graphs, domain dimensions, guards, and reset maps need not coincide.

Problem. Construct a metric d that assigns to any pair (x_1, x_2) of executions of (possibly distinct) hybrid systems H_1 and H_2 a nonnegative real number d(x_1, x_2) such that:

(i) d is a metric (nonnegativity, identity of indiscernibles up to a natural equivalence, symmetry, and triangle inequality) on a space containing executions of arbitrary hybrid systems of the above form, including the case H_1 ≠ H_2 with differing graphs, domain dimensions, guards, and reset maps;

(ii) d restricts to a meaningful distance on periodic gaits, so that, given a fixed hybrid robot model H with various feedback controllers producing periodic solutions x^*_1, …, x^*_k, the value d(x^*_i, x^*_human) ranks the controllers by closeness to a reference human gait x^*_human (which is itself an execution of a different hybrid system H_human);

(iii) d is computable from finite measured trajectory data and is well-defined when applied to recorded robotic walking data and recorded human walking data.

Provide an explicit construction of such a metric, prove that it satisfies the metric axioms, and demonstrate that it can distinguish "more human-like" from "less human-like" gaits in a principled way.
status_search_result: No general metric on solutions of hybrid systems with differing underlying models has been established in the literature. Existing approaches (e.g., RMSE on spatiotemporal/kinematic features, the Combined Gait Asymmetry Metric CGAM, and various task-specific gait similarity scores) compare gaits via fixed scalar parameter sets rather than as solutions of hybrid dynamical systems with possibly different graphs, dimensions, guards, and resets. The general problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Extend 3D bipedal locomotion modeling and control to robots or prosthetic systems with spherical or otherwise nontrivial foot shapes, and determine how to achieve gait stability when passive or active prostheses are present. paper_title: Some open problems on Banach spaces
original_question: Does there exist a Banach space X such that its bidual X** has the Daugavet property, meaning that every finite-rank operator T from X** to X** satisfies ||Id + T|| = 1 + ||T||?
self_contained_problem:
A Banach space $X$ is said to have the Daugavet property if every bounded finite-rank linear operator $T : X \to X$ satisfies the norm equality
$$\|\mathrm{Id} + T\| = 1 + \|T\|,$$
where $\mathrm{Id}$ denotes the identity operator on $X$.

For a Banach space $X$, let $X^{**}$ denote its bidual, i.e., the topological dual of $X^*$, regarded as a Banach space with its canonical norm.

Question: Does there exist a Banach space $X$ such that the bidual $X^{**}$ has the Daugavet property?

The status appears to remain unsettled based on the available evidence.

paper_title: Some open problems on Banach spaces
original_question: What duality theory exists for injective Banach lattices, where injective means 1-injective: every positive operator from a closed sublattice of a Banach lattice into the lattice extends to a positive operator on the whole Banach lattice with no increase in norm?
self_contained_problem:
A Banach lattice $X$ is called 1-injective (or simply injective) if for every Banach lattice $Y$, every closed vector sublattice $Y_0 \subseteq Y$, and every positive linear operator $T_0 : Y_0 \to X$, there exists a positive linear extension $T : Y \to X$ with $\|T\| = \|T_0\|$. It is known that every injective Banach lattice $X$ carries a mixed "LM-structure," which suggests that the dual $X^*$ should carry, in a dual sense, an "ML-structure."

Develop a duality theory for injective Banach lattices: identify and describe in intrinsic Banach-lattice (or geometric/order) terms the class of dual spaces $X^*$ of injective Banach lattices $X$, and conversely characterize those Banach lattices whose duals are injective. The desired theory should describe the structural correspondence between an injective Banach lattice and its dual analogous to the AL–AM duality in the classical case.
status_search_result: Some progress has been made on geometric and Boolean-valued characterizations of injective Banach lattices and their preduals (e.g., works by Kusraev and collaborators using a Boolean-valued transfer principle representing injective Banach lattices as AL-spaces, and recent geometric characterizations of preduals of injective Banach lattices). However, no complete duality theory analogous to AL–AM duality appears to be established, so the problem is best described as partially solved/still open in its full generality.

paper_title: Some open problems on Banach spaces
original_question: Describe the metric approximation property for the Banach operator ideal P of absolutely summing operators. More explicitly, characterize when a Banach space X has the property that for every Banach space Y and every absolutely summing operator T:X -> Y, there is a net of finite-rank operators S_alpha on X converging to the identity uniformly on compact subsets of X and satisfying limsup_alpha ||T S_alpha||_P <= ||T||_P.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the Banach operator ideal of absolutely summing operators between Banach spaces, equipped with its usual ideal norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{P}}$ (an operator $T:X\to Y$ is absolutely summing if there is a constant $C$ such that for every finite family $(x_i)\subset X$, $\sum_i \|Tx_i\| \le C \sup_{\|x^*\|\le 1}\sum_i |x^*(x_i)|$, and $\|T\|_{\mathcal{P}}$ is the least such $C$). For a Banach space $X$, let $\mathcal{F}(X,X)$ denote the space of finite-rank operators on $X$.

Say that a Banach space $X$ has the metric approximation property (MAP) with respect to $\mathcal{P}$ if for every Banach space $Y$ and every absolutely summing operator $T \in \mathcal{P}(X,Y)$ there exists a net $(S_\alpha)\subset \mathcal{F}(X,X)$ such that:
(i) $S_\alpha \to \mathrm{id}_X$ uniformly on compact subsets of $X$, and
(ii) $\limsup_\alpha \|T S_\alpha\|_{\mathcal{P}} \le \|T\|_{\mathcal{P}}$.

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterization of those Banach spaces $X$ which possess the MAP with respect to $\mathcal{P}$.
status_search_result: No characterization of the metric approximation property with respect to the ideal of absolutely summing operators appears in the literature. Related work (e.g., approximation properties determined by operator ideals, right/left approximation properties, and the p-approximation property) treats general operator ideals but does not provide an intrinsic description for the absolutely summing case, which remains an explicitly posed open problem.

paper_title: Some open problems on Banach spaces
original_question: Does the separable complementation property imply the m-complementation property for every cardinal m? For a Banach space X, the separable complementation property means that every separable subspace E of X is contained in a separable complemented subspace F of X. The m-complementation property means that every subspace E of X with density character m is contained in a complemented subspace F of X with density character m.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space. For a closed subspace $E \subseteq X$, the density character $\operatorname{dens} E$ is the least cardinality of a dense subset of $E$. Say that $X$ has the separable complementation property (SCP) if every separable closed subspace $E$ of $X$ is contained in a separable closed subspace $F$ of $X$ that is complemented in $X$ (i.e., $F$ is the range of a bounded linear projection $X \to X$). For an infinite cardinal $\mathfrak{m}$, say that $X$ has the $\mathfrak{m}$-complementation property ($\mathfrak{m}$-CP) if every closed subspace $E$ of $X$ with $\operatorname{dens} E = \mathfrak{m}$ is contained in a complemented closed subspace $F$ of $X$ with $\operatorname{dens} F = \mathfrak{m}$.

Question: Does the SCP imply the $\mathfrak{m}$-CP for every infinite cardinal $\mathfrak{m}$? That is, if a Banach space $X$ has the separable complementation property, must $X$ have the $\mathfrak{m}$-complementation property for every infinite cardinal $\mathfrak{m}$?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a definitive resolution of the implication SCP ⇒ 𝔪-CP for all infinite cardinals 𝔪. Status appears unresolved in the accessible search evidence.

original_question: Let E be a Kothe Banach space on [0,1], meaning a Banach space E contained in L^1[0,1] with 1_[0,1] in E and the lattice ideal property that |x| <= |y| with y in E implies x in E and ||x|| <= ||y||, and let X be a Banach space. Must every l2-strictly singular bounded linear operator T:E -> X be narrow, where l2-strictly singular means that the restriction of T to any subspace of E isomorphic to l2 is not an into-isomorphism?
self_contained_problem:
Definitions. A Köthe Banach space on [0,1] is a Banach space E with E ⊆ L^1[0,1] such that the constant function 1_{[0,1]} belongs to E and such that, for every measurable x and every y ∈ E with |x| ≤ |y| almost everywhere, one has x ∈ E and ‖x‖_E ≤ ‖y‖_E.

Let E be a Köthe Banach space on [0,1] and let X be a Banach space. A bounded linear operator T : E → X is called narrow if for every measurable set A ⊆ [0,1] and every ε > 0 there exists a function x ∈ E with x = -x on A (i.e. x takes only two opposite values on A and vanishes off A; equivalently, a "sign" of mean zero supported on A: x = 1_{A_1} − 1_{A_2} with A_1, A_2 disjoint and A_1 ∪ A_2 = A) such that ‖T(x)‖ < ε.

A bounded linear operator T : E → X is called ℓ_2-strictly singular if there is no closed infinite-dimensional subspace Y ⊆ E which is isomorphic to ℓ_2 and on which T acts as an into-isomorphism (i.e. there is no Y ⊆ E with Y ≃ ℓ_2 such that T|_Y is bounded below).

Question. Is it true that for every Köthe Banach space E on [0,1], every Banach space X, and every bounded linear operator T : E → X, if T is ℓ_2-strictly singular then T is narrow?
category_tag: narrow operators on Köthe Banach spaces
status_search_result: The general question (going back to Plichko–Popov, 1990) appears to still be open in full generality for arbitrary Köthe Banach spaces on [0,1]. Significant partial progress is known: Mykhaylyuk, Popov, Randrianantoanina, and Schechtman (Israel J. Math., 2014) proved that every ℓ_2-strictly singular operator from L_p (1 < p < ∞) to any Banach space with an unconditional basis is narrow. No source found that resolves the question for all Köthe Banach spaces.

paper_title: Some open problems on Banach spaces
original_question: Let E be a Kothe Banach space on [0,1], meaning a Banach space E contained in L^1[0,1] with 1_[0,1] in E and the lattice ideal property that |x| <= |y| with y in E implies x in E and ||x|| <= ||y||. Must T be narrow whenever T is E-strictly singular, meaning Z-strictly singular in the special case Z = E, where Z-strictly singular means that the restriction of T to any subspace of E isomorphic to Z is not an into-isomorphism?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A Köthe Banach space on $[0,1]$ is a Banach space $E\subseteq L^1[0,1]$ such that the constant function $\mathbf 1_{[0,1]}\in E$ and, for every measurable $x$ and every $y\in E$, the inequality $|x|\le|y|$ a.e. implies $x\in E$ and $\|x\|_E\le\|y\|_E$. Such a space $E$ is said to have absolutely continuous norm on the unit if $\|\mathbf 1_A\|_E\to 0$ whenever $A\subseteq[0,1]$ is measurable with Lebesgue measure tending to $0$.

Let $X$ be a Banach space and $T\colon E\to X$ a bounded linear operator. 

(i) Given an infinite-dimensional Banach space $Z$, $T$ is called $Z$-strictly singular if the restriction $T|_Y$ is not an into-isomorphism for any subspace $Y\subseteq E$ that is isomorphic to $Z$. In particular, $T$ is called $E$-strictly singular when $Z=E$.

(ii) $T$ is called narrow if for every measurable $A\subseteq[0,1]$ with $\|\mathbf 1_A\|_E>0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a measurable decomposition $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ with $\int_{A_1}\mathbf 1\,d\mu=\int_{A_2}\mathbf 1\,d\mu$ (i.e. $\mathbf 1_{A_1}-\mathbf 1_{A_2}$ is a sign on $A$) such that $\|T(\mathbf 1_{A_1}-\mathbf 1_{A_2})\|_X<\varepsilon$.

Question. Assume $E$ is a Köthe Banach space on $[0,1]$ with absolutely continuous norm on the unit, $X$ is a Banach space, and $T\in\mathcal L(E,X)$. Must $T$ be narrow whenever $T$ is $E$-strictly singular?

original_question: Let E be a non-normable separable Frechet space, and let L(E) denote its continuous linear operators. An operator $T \in L(E)$ is said to be hypercyclic if there exists a vector $x \in E$ whose orbit $\{T^n x : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is dense in $E$. 

Question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional linear subspace $\mathcal{A} \subseteq L(E)$ such that every nonzero operator $T \in \mathcal{A}$ is hypercyclic?

No source located confirms a resolution of this specific question for non-normable separable Fréchet spaces, so the current status is treated as unknown (likely still open).

paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
original_question: Fix a real number a in [0, 2), and let E_a be the class of all two-dimensional Banach spaces E whose characteristic of convexity epsilon_0(E) equals a. For a Banach space X, the modulus of convexity is delta_X(epsilon) = inf {1 - ||(x + y)/2|| : ||x|| <= 1, ||y|| <= 1, ||x - y|| >= epsilon}, and epsilon_0(X) = sup {epsilon : delta_X(epsilon) = 0}. Given epsilon in [a, 2), what is the supremum of delta_E(epsilon) over all E in E_a?
self_contained_problem:
For a real Banach space $X$, define the modulus of convexity
$$\delta_X(\varepsilon) = \inf\bigl\{\, 1 - \tfrac{1}{2}\|x+y\| \;:\; \|x\|\le 1,\ \|y\|\le 1,\ \|x-y\|\ge \varepsilon \,\bigr\}, \qquad \varepsilon\in[0,2],$$
and the characteristic of convexity
$$\varepsilon_0(X) = \sup\{\varepsilon\in[0,2] : \delta_X(\varepsilon) = 0\}.$$
Fix $a \in [0,2)$ and let $\mathcal{E}_a$ denote the class of all two-dimensional real Banach spaces $E$ with $\varepsilon_0(E) = a$. For each $\varepsilon \in [a,2)$, determine
$$\Delta_a(\varepsilon) \;=\; \sup_{E \in \mathcal{E}_a} \delta_E(\varepsilon),$$
and (if attained) identify the two-dimensional Banach spaces $E \in \mathcal{E}_a$ achieving this supremum.
category_tag: Modulus of convexity in Banach spaces
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a specific reference resolving the extremal value of $\delta_E(\varepsilon)$ over two-dimensional Banach spaces with prescribed characteristic of convexity $\varepsilon_0(E)=a$. While there is extensive literature on bounds, exact values, and comparisons between moduli of convexity in Banach spaces, no source was found that explicitly computes this supremum across the class $\mathcal{E}_a$ for general $a\in[0,2)$. The status is therefore reported as unknown.

original_question: If, for a fixed a in [0, 2), there exists a two-dimensional Banach space E_star with epsilon_0(E_star) = a whose modulus of convexity dominates the modulus of every other two-dimensional Banach space E with epsilon_0(E) = a, is such an extremal space unique in some appropriate sense?

Let $E$ be a real two-dimensional Banach space with unit ball $B_E$ and unit sphere $S_E$. The modulus of convexity of $E$ is the function $\delta_E:[0,2]\to[0,1]$ defined by
$$\delta_E(\varepsilon)=\inf\Bigl\{1-\tfrac{\|x+y\|}{2}:\ x,y\in S_E,\ \|x-y\|\ge \varepsilon\Bigr\},$$
and one sets

$$\delta_E(\varepsilon)\le \delta_{E_*}(\varepsilon)\quad\text{for all }\varepsilon\in[0,2].$$

original_question: Let X be a complex Banach space, T in L(X) a bounded operator, and Y = E_X(T) the linear subspace formed from the generalized kernels of lambda - T, equivalently the union of p(T)^{-1}(0) over all nonzero polynomials p. Let T'_Y : X/Y -> X/Y be the quotient operator induced by T. Is the point spectrum pi(T'_Y), meaning the set of lambda for which lambda - T'_Y is not injective, empty?

Let $X$ be a complex Banach space and let $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$ be a bounded linear operator on $X$. Define
$$E_X(T) \;=\; \bigcup_{\lambda \in \mathbb{C}} \ker\!\big((\lambda I - T)^{\infty}\big) \;=\; \bigcup_{0 \neq p \in \mathbb{C}[z]} \ker p(T),$$
where $\ker((\lambda I - T)^\infty) = \bigcup_{n\geq 1} \ker((\lambda I - T)^n)$ is the generalized kernel of $\lambda I - T$. Set $Y = E_X(T)$, viewed as a (not necessarily closed) linear subspace of $X$ that is invariant under $T$. Let $\widetilde{Y}$ denote the closure of $Y$ in $X$, and let $T'_Y : X/\widetilde{Y} \to X/\widetilde{Y}$ denote the bounded quotient operator induced by $T$. The point spectrum of an operator $S$ is
$$\pi(S) \;=\; \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : \lambda I - S \text{ is not injective}\}.$$
Question: Is it true that $\pi(T'_Y) = \emptyset$ for every choice of complex Banach space $X$ and every $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$?

paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
original_question: Let A and B be semisimple Banach algebras, and let T : A -> B be a unital surjective linear map. If T preserves spectra in the sense that sigma(Ta) = sigma(a) for every a in A, where sigma denotes the spectrum, must T be a Jordan homomorphism, meaning T(a^2) = T(a)^2 for every a in A?
self_contained_problem: Let $A$ and $B$ be unital complex semisimple Banach algebras. For an element $x$ of a unital Banach algebra, denote by $\sigma(x)$ its spectrum, i.e., the set of complex numbers $\lambda$ such that $x-\lambda\mathbf{1}$ is not invertible. Suppose $T : A \to B$ is a surjective linear map that is unital (i.e., $T(\mathbf{1}_A) = \mathbf{1}_B$) and preserves spectra in the sense that $\sigma(T(a)) = \sigma(a)$ for every $a \in A$. Must $T$ be a Jordan homomorphism, that is, must $T(a^2) = T(a)^2$ hold for every $a \in A$?
category_tag: Spectrum-preserving linear maps on Banach algebras
status_search_result: The question, known as Kaplansky's problem (equivalent in the unital surjective linear setting to the invertibility-preserver formulation by Aupetit), remains open in general, even for C*-algebras. paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
context_brief: Spectrally bounded maps on II_1 factors
original_question: For a von Neumann factor of type II_1, does the finite-matrix characterization of unital surjective spectrally bounded linear maps remain valid? The finite-matrix statement is: a linear map T : M_n(C) -> M_n(C) is unital, surjective, and spectrally bounded, meaning r(Tx) <= M r(x) for some M >= 0 and all x, if and only if there are a Jordan automorphism S of M_n(C) and a nonzero complex number gamma such that T x = gamma Sx + (1 - gamma) tau(x), where tau is the normalized center-valued trace.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a von Neumann factor of type $\mathrm{II}_1$, with unique normalized faithful normal tracial state $\tau$ (the center-valued trace, which on a factor takes scalar values). For $x\in M$ let $r(x)$ denote its spectral radius. A linear map $T: M\to M$ is called spectrally bounded if there exists $M_0\ge 0$ such that $r(Tx)\le M_0\, r(x)$ for all $x\in M$, and unital if $T(1)=1$.

The finite-dimensional model is the following theorem on $M_n(\mathbb{C})$: a linear map $T:M_n(\mathbb{C})\to M_n(\mathbb{C})$ is unital, surjective and spectrally bounded if and only if there exist a Jordan automorphism $S$ of $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ and a nonzero complex number $\gamma$ such that
$$T(x) = \gamma\, S(x) + (1-\gamma)\,\tau(x)\,1 \qquad \text{for all } x\in M_n(\mathbb{C}),$$
where $\tau$ is the normalized trace.

Question: Does this characterization extend to every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $M$? That is, is every unital surjective spectrally bounded linear map $T:M\to M$ of the form $T(x)=\gamma S(x)+(1-\gamma)\tau(x)\,1$ for some Jordan automorphism $S$ of $M$ and some nonzero $\gamma\in\mathbb{C}$?
category_tag: Spectrally bounded maps on von Neumann algebras
status_search_result: Existing results (Mathieu and collaborators) treat spectrally bounded unital surjections from properly infinite von Neumann algebras, showing they are Jordan homomorphisms; the type II_1 factor case is explicitly highlighted as an open problem, and recent literature on spectrally bounded/additive maps does not resolve it. No source confirming a solution was found.

paper_title: Bayesian predictive densities for linear regression models under α-divergence loss: some results and open problems
context_brief: Shrinkage versus invariant prediction under α-divergence
original_question: Consider estimation of the predictive density of a future observation in a normal linear regression model with observed data y distributed as N_n(Xβ, σ² I_n), future data ỹ distributed as N_m(X̃β, σ² I_m), y and ỹ conditionally independent given β and σ², and σ² unknown. Let k be the number of regression coefficients. Assume the repeated-design condition AS1: m ≥ k ≥ 3, n = mN for a positive integer N, and X = 1_N ⊗ X̃. Under α-divergence loss D_α for −1 < α < 1, does the generalized Bayes predictive density based on the shrinkage prior π_S,1(β, σ²) = {β′X̃′X̃β}^{1−k/2}{σ²}^{−2} improve on the best invariant predictive density, namely the generalized Bayes predictive density based on the right invariant prior π_I,1(β, σ²) = {σ²}^{−1}?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following Gaussian linear regression prediction setup. Let $y \in \mathbb{R}^n$ be observed data and $\tilde y \in \mathbb{R}^m$ be a future observation, with
$$y \mid \beta,\sigma^2 \sim N_n(X\beta,\sigma^2 I_n), \qquad \tilde y \mid \beta,\sigma^2 \sim N_m(\tilde X\beta,\sigma^2 I_m),$$
where $y$ and $\tilde y$ are conditionally independent given $(\beta,\sigma^2)$, $\beta \in \mathbb{R}^k$, $\sigma^2>0$ is unknown, and $X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}$, $\tilde X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times k}$ are known design matrices of full column rank.

Assume the repeated‑design condition (AS1): $m\ge k\ge 3$, $n=mN$ for some positive integer $N$, and $X=\mathbf{1}_N\otimes \tilde X$ (so that the $n\times k$ design matrix is the vertical stacking of $N$ copies of $\tilde X$).

For $\alpha\in(-1,1)$, the $\alpha$-divergence between two densities $p$ and $q$ on $\mathbb{R}^m$ is
$$D_\alpha(p,q)=\frac{4}{1-\alpha^2}\int\Bigl(\tfrac{1-\alpha}{2}p(\tilde y)+\tfrac{1+\alpha}{2}q(\tilde y)-p(\tilde y)^{(1-\alpha)/2}q(\tilde y)^{(1+\alpha)/2}\Bigr)d\tilde y,$$
and the corresponding risk of a predictive density $\hat p(\tilde y\mid y)$ is $R_\alpha(\beta,\sigma^2;\hat p)=E_{\beta,\sigma^2}[D_\alpha(p(\cdot\mid\beta,\sigma^2),\hat p(\cdot\mid y))]$.

Consider two improper priors on $(\beta,\sigma^2)$:
- the right‑invariant prior $\pi_{I,1}(\beta,\sigma^2)=(\sigma^2)^{-1}$;
- the shrinkage prior $\pi_{S,1}(\beta,\sigma^2)=(\beta^\top \tilde X^\top \tilde X\beta)^{1-k/2}(\sigma^2)^{-2}$.

Let $\hat p_{I,1}$ and $\hat p_{S,1}$ denote the generalized Bayes predictive densities (formed as $\hat p_\pi(\tilde y\mid y)=\int p(\tilde y\mid\beta,\sigma^2)\pi(\beta,\sigma^2\mid y)\,d\beta\,d\sigma^2$) corresponding to $\pi_{I,1}$ and $\pi_{S,1}$, respectively. It is known that $\hat p_{I,1}$ is the best invariant predictive density.

Question: Under assumption (AS1) and $\alpha$-divergence loss with $-1<\alpha<1$, does $\hat p_{S,1}$ dominate $\hat p_{I,1}$ in the sense that
$$R_\alpha(\beta,\sigma^2;\hat p_{S,1})\le R_\alpha(\beta,\sigma^2;\hat p_{I,1})$$
for all $(\beta,\sigma^2)$, with strict inequality somewhere?

paper_title: Bayesian predictive densities for linear regression models under α-divergence loss: some results and open problems
original_question: Consider the normal linear regression predictive-density problem with unknown variance under α-divergence loss D_α for −1 ≤ α < 1. In dimensions k = 1 or k = 2, does the best invariant predictive density remain inadmissible? If it does, which Bayesian predictive density, or which class of Bayesian predictive densities, improves on the best invariant predictive density?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the normal linear regression prediction problem with unknown variance. Let $Y = X\beta + \sigma\varepsilon$ be the observed response, where $X$ is an $n\times p$ known design matrix of full rank $p$, $\beta\in\mathbb{R}^p$ is an unknown regression coefficient, $\sigma^2>0$ is an unknown scale parameter, and $\varepsilon\sim N(0,I_n)$. Let $\widetilde Y = \widetilde X\beta + \sigma\widetilde\varepsilon$ be a future $k$-dimensional response with $\widetilde X$ a known $k\times p$ matrix of full row rank and $\widetilde\varepsilon\sim N(0,I_k)$ independent of $\varepsilon$. The goal is to construct a predictive density $\hat p(\widetilde y\mid y)$ for $\widetilde Y$ given $Y$.

For $-1\le\alpha<1$, the $\alpha$-divergence loss between the true conditional density $p(\widetilde y\mid\beta,\sigma)$ and the predictive density $\hat p(\widetilde y\mid y)$ is
$$D_\alpha(p,\hat p) = \frac{4}{1-\alpha^2}\left\{1-\int p(\widetilde y)^{(1-\alpha)/2}\,\hat p(\widetilde y)^{(1+\alpha)/2}\,d\widetilde y\right\},$$
with the corresponding risk obtained by integrating over $Y$. The best invariant (minimum risk equivariant) predictive density under the group of location–scale transformations preserving the regression structure is the Bayes density with respect to the right-invariant prior $\pi(\beta,\sigma)\propto 1/\sigma$, and equals a multivariate Student-$t$ density centered at $\widetilde X\hat\beta$ where $\hat\beta$ is the least-squares estimator.

Question: For $k=1$ and $k=2$, is the best invariant predictive density inadmissible under the $\alpha$-divergence loss $D_\alpha$ for every $-1\le\alpha<1$? If so, exhibit a Bayesian predictive density (or a class of such densities, e.g.\ those associated with suitable shrinkage priors on $\beta$ and $\sigma$) that strictly dominates the best invariant predictive density under $D_\alpha$ for these dimensions.
status_search_result: Subsequent work on predictive density estimation under α-divergence loss (e.g., Boisbunon–Maruyama and Kubokawa–Marchand–Strawderman 2019) extends domination results in dimensions k ≥ 3 and for various loss parameters but does not appear to settle the low-dimensional cases k = 1, 2 under general α-divergence with unknown variance. No source found that resolves the inadmissibility question or constructs an improving Bayes predictive density for k = 1, 2 across the full range −1 ≤ α < 1.

paper_title: Multiplier sequences, classes of generalized Bessel functions and open problems
original_question: Let {gamma_k}_{k>=0} be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers such that f(x)=sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k/k! is an entire function. For every parameter p with -p not in N, define F_p(x)=sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k/(k! Gamma(k+p+1)). Characterize exactly which such sequences {gamma_k} have the property that F_p belongs to the Laguerre-Polya class L-P of real entire functions, meaning the class of real entire functions admitting the standard Laguerre-Polya product representation with only real zeros, for every admissible p.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}$ denote the Laguerre–Pólya class of real entire functions, i.e., the class of real entire functions $\varphi$ admitting a representation of the form
$$\varphi(x) = c\, x^{m} e^{-a x^{2} + b x} \prod_{k}\left(1 + \frac{x}{x_{k}}\right) e^{-x/x_{k}},$$
where $c, b, x_{k} \in \mathbb{R}$, $a \geq 0$, $m \in \mathbb{N}_{0}$, and $\sum_{k} 1/x_{k}^{2} < \infty$.

Let $\{\gamma_{k}\}_{k \geq 0}$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers such that
$$f(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{\gamma_{k}}{k!}\, x^{k}$$
defines an entire function. For each real parameter $p$ with $-p \notin \mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, 3, \ldots\}$, define the associated generalized Bessel-type function
$$F_{p}(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{\gamma_{k}}{k!\,\Gamma(k + p + 1)}\, x^{k}.$$

Give an exact characterization of all such nonnegative sequences $\{\gamma_{k}\}_{k \geq 0}$ for which $F_{p} \in \mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}$ for every admissible $p$ (i.e., every real $p$ with $-p \notin \mathbb{N}$).
status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in the literature on multiplier sequences and generalized Bessel functions. Recent work characterizes multiplier sequences for generalized Laguerre bases and Fox–Wright extensions, but no complete characterization of nonnegative sequences making $F_p$ belong to the Laguerre–Pólya class for all admissible $p$ appears to have been established.

paper_title: Multiplier sequences, classes of generalized Bessel functions and open problems
original_question: Is the sequence {(1+k+k^2)/k!}_{k>=0} a complex zero decreasing sequence? Equivalently, for the diagonal operator T on real polynomials defined by T[x^k]=((1+k+k^2)/k!) x^k, is it true that T never increases the number of nonreal zeros of any real polynomial, counted with multiplicity?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{R}[x]$ denote the ring of polynomials with real coefficients. For a real polynomial $p(x)$, let $Z_C(p)$ denote the number of nonreal zeros of $p$, counted with multiplicity. A sequence of real numbers $\{\gamma_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is called a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if the linear operator $T: \mathbb{R}[x] \to \mathbb{R}[x]$ defined by $T[x^k] = \gamma_k x^k$ satisfies
$$Z_C(T[p(x)]) \le Z_C(p(x)) \quad \text{for every } p \in \mathbb{R}[x].$$
Determine whether the sequence
$$\gamma_k = \frac{1+k+k^2}{k!}, \qquad k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots,$$
is a CZDS.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in the literature on CZDS / multiplier sequences (associated with work of Craven and Csordas). paper_title: Multiplier sequences, classes of generalized Bessel functions and open problems
original_question: For every real number s>0, does there exist an integer m>=1 such that the entire function sum_{k>=0} k^s x^k/(k!)^m belongs to L-P+? Here L-P+ denotes the subclass of the Laguerre-Polya class consisting of real entire functions whose Taylor coefficients are all nonnegative.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^{+}$ denote the subclass of the Laguerre–Pólya class consisting of real entire functions $\varphi(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\gamma_k x^k$ all of whose Taylor coefficients satisfy $\gamma_k\ge 0$ and which can be expressed as a (possibly finite) locally uniform limit of polynomials having only real zeros. Equivalently, $\varphi\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^{+}$ if and only if $\varphi$ has the Hadamard factorization
$$\varphi(x)=c\,x^{n}e^{\alpha x}\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\left(1+\tfrac{x}{x_k}\right),$$
where $c\ge 0$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, $\alpha\ge 0$, $x_k>0$, and $\sum 1/x_k<\infty$.

For each real number $s>0$, consider the entire function
$$F_{s,m}(x)\;=\;\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{k^{s}}{(k!)^{m}}\,x^{k}, \qquad m\in\mathbb{N}.$$

Prove or disprove: for every real $s>0$ there exists an integer $m\ge 1$ such that $F_{s,m}\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^{+}$.

paper_title: Multiplier sequences, classes of generalized Bessel functions and open problems
original_question: Characterize all classical multiplier sequences {gamma_k}_{k>=0} that admit a C_k-representation. This means that there exist not-necessarily-distinct functions phi and Phi in L-P+ and real parameters s,t such that gamma_k=C_k^{phi,Phi}(t,s) for every k>=0, where B_k^phi(t)=sum_{j=0}^k binom(k,j)(1-t)^j gamma_{k-j} t^{k-j} when phi(x)=sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k/k!, and C_k^{phi,Phi}(t,s)=sum_{j=0}^k binom(k,j) B_j^phi(t) B_{k-j}^Phi(s). Here L-P+ is the nonnegative-coefficient part of the Laguerre-Polya class, and a classical multiplier sequence is a real sequence whose diagonal operator preserves real-rootedness of real polynomials.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^+$ denote the subclass of the Laguerre–Pólya class consisting of entire functions that are locally uniform limits of polynomials with only real, non-positive zeros; equivalently, entire functions of the form $\phi(x)=Cx^n e^{\alpha x}\prod_{k}(1+\alpha_k x)$ with $C\ge 0$, $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$, $\alpha\ge 0$, $\alpha_k\ge 0$, and $\sum \alpha_k<\infty$. Such functions have a power series $\phi(x)=\sum_{k\ge 0}\gamma_k x^k/k!$ with all $\gamma_k\ge 0$.

A real sequence $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is called a classical multiplier sequence if, for every real polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k$ whose roots are all real, the polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^n \gamma_k a_k x^k$ also has only real roots.

For $\phi\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^+$ with $\phi(x)=\sum_{k\ge 0}\gamma_k x^k/k!$ and $t\in\mathbb{R}$, define
$$B_k^{\phi}(t)=\sum_{j=0}^k \binom{k}{j}(1-t)^j\,\gamma_{k-j}\,t^{k-j},\qquad k\ge 0.$$
For $\phi,\Phi\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^+$ and $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$, define
$$C_k^{\phi,\Phi}(t,s)=\sum_{j=0}^k \binom{k}{j}B_j^{\phi}(t)\,B_{k-j}^{\Phi}(s),\qquad k\ge 0.$$

Say that a real sequence $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ admits a $C_k$-representation if there exist functions $\phi,\Phi\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^+$ (not necessarily distinct) and real numbers $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $\gamma_k=C_k^{\phi,\Phi}(t,s)$ for every $k\ge 0$.

Problem: Characterize all classical multiplier sequences that admit a $C_k$-representation.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open characterization problem in the survey context. No subsequent paper providing a full characterization of classical multiplier sequences admitting a $C_k$-representation could be located, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: On three open problems related to quasi relative interior
original_question: Let X be a separated locally convex topological vector space. For a subset S of X, let cone(S) denote the conic hull of S and let cl(cone(S)) denote its closure in X. For a convex set E in X, define the quasi-relative interior qri(E) as the set of points x in E such that cl(cone(E - x)) is a linear subspace of X. For convex sets C and D in X, define the Minkowski sum C + D as {c + d : c in C and d in D}. Since qri(C) + qri(D) is always contained in qri(C + D), can this inclusion be proper? Equivalently, do there exist convex sets C and D in a separated locally convex space X such that qri(C) + qri(D) is a proper subset of qri(C + D)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a separated locally convex topological vector space. For a subset $S\subseteq X$, denote by $\operatorname{cone}(S)=\{\lambda s : \lambda\ge 0,\ s\in S\}$ the conic hull of $S$, and by $\overline{\operatorname{cone}}(S)$ its closure in $X$. For a convex set $E\subseteq X$, define the quasi-relative interior of $E$ by
$$\operatorname{qri}(E)=\{x\in E : \overline{\operatorname{cone}}(E-x)\text{ is a linear subspace of }X\}.$$
For convex sets $C,D\subseteq X$, let $C+D=\{c+d : c\in C,\ d\in D\}$ denote the Minkowski sum. It is known that $\operatorname{qri}(C)+\operatorname{qri}(D)\subseteq \operatorname{qri}(C+D)$ always holds. 

Determine whether this inclusion can be strict: do there exist a separated locally convex space $X$ and convex sets $C,D\subseteq X$ such that
$$\operatorname{qri}(C)+\operatorname{qri}(D)\subsetneq \operatorname{qri}(C+D)?$$
status_search_result: The question is addressed in C. Zălinescu's note "On three open problems related to quasi relative interior" (Journal of Convex Analysis 22 (2015), 641–645), which answers two questions of Borwein–Goebel (2003) and a conjecture of Grad–Pop (2014) concerning calculus rules for the quasi (relative) interior, including the Minkowski-sum inclusion in question.

paper_title: Quasiwypukłość i otwarte problemy analizy funkcjonalnej
original_question: Let f be a real-valued function on the space of m by n real matrices. Say that f is quasiconvex when, for every bounded domain Omega in R^n, every matrix A, and every smooth compactly supported vector field phi from Omega to R^m, the average of f(A + D phi(x)) over Omega is at least f(A). Say that f is rank-one convex when, for every matrix A0 and every rank-one matrix B, the one-variable function s -> f(A0 + sB) is convex. In the remaining vectorial dimensions m = 2 and n >= 2, is every rank-one convex function quasiconvex?
self_contained_problem:
Let $m,n$ be positive integers and let $\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ denote the space of real $m\times n$ matrices. A function $f:\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called:

(a) quasiconvex if for every bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, every matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, and every smooth, compactly supported vector field $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^m)$, one has
$$\frac{1}{|\Omega|}\int_\Omega f\bigl(A+D\varphi(x)\bigr)\,dx \;\geq\; f(A);$$

(b) rank-one convex if for every $A_0\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and every rank-one matrix $B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, the function $s\mapsto f(A_0+sB)$ is convex on $\mathbb{R}$.

It is known that every quasiconvex function is rank-one convex, and that for $m\geq 3$ and $n\geq 2$ there exist rank-one convex functions that are not quasiconvex.

Question: For $m=2$ and every $n\geq 2$, is every rank-one convex function $f:\mathbb{R}^{2\times n}\to\mathbb{R}$ necessarily quasiconvex?
status_search_result: The question is the planar case of Morrey's conjecture. Šverák (1992) settled the question negatively for m≥3, n≥2, but the case m=2 (n≥2) remains open and is regarded as a major open problem in the calculus of variations, with active recent work (e.g. analytical and numerical investigations published 2019–2022).

paper_title: Quasiwypukłość i otwarte problemy analizy funkcjonalnej
original_question: Let S be the Ahlfors-Beurling transform, characterized here by the property that for a smooth compactly supported complex-valued function f, S applied to the anti-holomorphic derivative of f equals the holomorphic derivative of f. What is the best constant A_p in the L^p inequality ||S omega||_p <= A_p ||omega||_p?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ denote the Ahlfors–Beurling transform on the complex plane, that is, the singular integral operator on $L^p(\mathbb{C})$ ($1 < p < \infty$) defined (for sufficiently nice functions $\omega$) by the principal-value integral
$$ (S\omega)(z) \;=\; -\frac{1}{\pi}\,\mathrm{p.v.}\!\int_{\mathbb{C}} \frac{\omega(\zeta)}{(z-\zeta)^2}\, dA(\zeta), $$
where $dA$ is two-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Equivalently, for every smooth, compactly supported complex-valued function $f:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ one has $S(\bar{\partial} f) = \partial f$, where $\partial = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x - i\partial_y)$ and $\bar{\partial} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x + i\partial_y)$.

For $1 < p < \infty$, define
$$ A_p \;=\; \|S\|_{L^p(\mathbb{C}) \to L^p(\mathbb{C})} \;=\; \sup\bigl\{\|S\omega\|_p : \omega \in L^p(\mathbb{C}),\ \|\omega\|_p \le 1\bigr\}. $$

Determine the exact value of $A_p$ for every $p \in (1,\infty)$. In particular, prove or disprove the conjectured identity
$$ A_p \;=\; p^{*} - 1, \qquad \text{where } p^{*} = \max\{p,\, p/(p-1)\}. $$
status_search_result: The exact $L^p$ operator norm of the Beurling–Ahlfors transform (Iwaniec's conjecture $A_p = p^*-1$) remains a well-known open problem. Substantial partial results provide upper bounds, e.g. Bañuelos–Wang $\le 4(p^*-1)$, Nazarov–Volberg $\le 2(p^*-1)$, with subsequent refinements (e.g. $\le 1.575(p^*-1)$), but the sharp constant has not been established for general $p \ne 2$.

paper_title: Homogeneous manifolds whose geodesics are orbits. Recent results and some open problems
original_question: Classify Riemannian geodesic-orbit manifolds in the dimensions where no complete classification is known. A Riemannian homogeneous manifold M=G/K with metric g is a geodesic-orbit, or g.o., manifold when every geodesic is homogeneous with respect to the largest connected isometry group, meaning that each geodesic through the origin o can be written as gamma(t)=exp(tX).o for some nonzero X in the Lie algebra of G. What is a complete classification of such g.o. manifolds, especially in dimension 7 and in dimensions greater than 7?
self_contained_problem:
A Riemannian homogeneous manifold $M=G/K$ with $G$-invariant metric $g$, where $G$ is the largest connected group of isometries of $(M,g)$, is called a geodesic-orbit (g.o.) manifold if every geodesic of $(M,g)$ is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of $G$. Equivalently, for every geodesic $\gamma(t)$ starting at the origin $o=eK$, there exists a nonzero element $X$ in the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of $G$ such that $\gamma(t)=\exp(tX)\cdot o$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$.

Complete classifications of Riemannian g.o. manifolds are known only in low dimensions (e.g., up to dimension 6). 

Problem: Provide a complete classification of Riemannian g.o. manifolds $M=G/K$ in dimension $7$, and more generally in every dimension $n>7$.
status_search_result: Recent literature (2020–2025) continues to produce new examples and partial classifications of g.o. manifolds—including 7-dimensional constructions, naturally reductive 7- and 8-dimensional spaces (Storm, 2020), and g.o. nilmanifolds (Nikonorov and others, 2024)—but no complete classification of Riemannian geodesic-orbit manifolds in dimension 7 or in higher dimensions is available. The general classification problem remains open.

paper_title: Homogeneous manifolds whose geodesics are orbits. Recent results and some open problems
original_question: For a homogeneous Riemannian space (M=G/K,g) that is not a g.o. space, explicitly describe the homogeneous geodesics it does have. Equivalently, determine which nonzero vectors X in the Lie algebra of G make gamma(t)=exp(tX).o a geodesic, and give an effective method for computing these geodesic vectors even when not every geodesic of M is homogeneous.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M = G/K, g)$ be a homogeneous Riemannian manifold, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively by isometries on $M$ and $K$ is the isotropy subgroup at a base point $o \in M$. Let $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$ be a reductive decomposition of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of $G$, where $\mathfrak{k}$ is the Lie algebra of $K$ and $\mathfrak{m}$ is an $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant complement identified with the tangent space $T_o M$. A nonzero vector $X \in \mathfrak{g}$ is called a geodesic vector if the curve $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX)\cdot o$ is a geodesic of $(M,g)$. The space $(M,g)$ is called a g.o. (geodesic orbit) space if every geodesic through $o$ is of the form $\exp(tX)\cdot o$ for some $X \in \mathfrak{g}$.

Assume that $(M=G/K, g)$ is not a g.o. space. The problem is the following:

(a) Explicitly describe the homogeneous geodesics that $(M,g)$ does possess, i.e., determine the set
$$ \mathcal{V}(G/K, g) = \{ X \in \mathfrak{g} \setminus \{0\} : t \mapsto \exp(tX)\cdot o \text{ is a geodesic of } (M,g)\}. $$

(b) Provide an effective algorithmic method (in terms of the Lie bracket structure of $\mathfrak{g}$, the decomposition $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$, and the inner product on $\mathfrak{m}$ induced by $g$) for computing $\mathcal{V}(G/K, g)$ in the case when $(M,g)$ is not a g.o. space, i.e., when not every geodesic of $M$ arises in this way.
status_search_result: The literature contains the standard geodesic-vector criterion (Kowalski–Vanhecke) and explicit determinations of homogeneous geodesics in many specific classes (flag manifolds, certain Finsler and Randers spaces, sub-Riemannian settings), but no general effective classification of the set of geodesic vectors for arbitrary non-g.o. homogeneous Riemannian spaces appears to have been established. The problem is posed as an open program of describing such geodesics case by case, and current sources show only partial progress in special families.

paper_title: Homogeneous manifolds whose geodesics are orbits. Recent results and some open problems
original_question: Give criteria or proofs determining when the g.o. property of a homogeneous Riemannian metric is independent of the chosen coset representation M=G/K and of the chosen Ad(K)-invariant reductive decomposition g=k+m. Equivalently, clarify when the assertion that (M=G/K,g) is G-g.o. remains valid, changes, or must be reformulated after representing the same Riemannian manifold by another transitive isometry group or another reductive complement.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold. A presentation of $(M,g)$ as a coset space is a pair $(G,K)$, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively on $M$ by isometries of $g$ and $K$ is the isotropy subgroup at a chosen base point, so that $M = G/K$. The pair $(G,K)$ is called reductive if there exists an $\operatorname{Ad}(K)$-invariant complement $\mathfrak{m}$ to the isotropy Lie algebra $\mathfrak{k}$ inside the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of $G$, giving a decomposition $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$ with $\operatorname{Ad}(K)\mathfrak{m}\subset \mathfrak{m}$. Such a complement $\mathfrak{m}$ is identified with the tangent space $T_oM$ at the origin.

The Riemannian manifold $(M=G/K, g)$ is called a $G$-geodesic orbit space ($G$-g.o.) if every geodesic of $g$ is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of $G$; equivalently, for every $X \in \mathfrak{m}$ there exists $Z \in \mathfrak{k}$ such that $[X+Z,\, X]_{\mathfrak{m}} = 0$ with respect to some (hence any) $\operatorname{Ad}(K)$-invariant reductive complement $\mathfrak{m}$.

Problem. Establish criteria, with proofs, that determine when the $G$-g.o. property of a homogeneous Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ is independent of:

(a) the choice of $\operatorname{Ad}(K)$-invariant reductive complement $\mathfrak{m}$ in $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$ for a fixed presentation $M = G/K$; and

(b) the choice of transitive group of isometries, i.e., when passing from one presentation $(G,K)$ of $(M,g)$ to another presentation $(G',K')$ by a different transitive Lie group $G'$ of isometries of $(M,g)$.

In particular, clarify precisely under what hypotheses the assertion "$(M=G/K,g)$ is $G$-g.o." is invariant under change of reductive complement, when it transfers between distinct transitive isometry groups, and when (and how) it must be reformulated when the presentation changes.
status_search_result: The literature on geodesic orbit (g.o.) manifolds notes that, for a fixed reductive presentation, the g.o. property is intrinsic to the presentation, but a general criterion describing how the $G$-g.o. property behaves under change of transitive isometry group or change of reductive complement is not stated as a settled theorem. Recent surveys and papers (2017–2025) on g.o. manifolds continue to discuss this issue and emphasize the dependence on the presentation, indicating the problem remains open in its general form.

paper_title: Homogeneous manifolds whose geodesics are orbits. Recent results and some open problems
original_question: Decide whether every search for homogeneous geodesics represented by three or more exponential factors can be reduced to a search for two-step homogeneous geodesics. A two-step homogeneous geodesic is a geodesic through o of the form gamma(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY).o with X and Y in the Lie algebra of G, and a two-step g.o. space is a homogeneous space in which every geodesic through the origin has such a representation.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M = G/H, g)$ be a homogeneous Riemannian manifold, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively by isometries on $M$ and $H$ is the isotropy subgroup at a chosen origin $o \in M$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ denote the Lie algebra of $G$. A geodesic $\gamma$ of $M$ through $o$ is called a homogeneous geodesic if it is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of $G$, i.e. $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX) \cdot o$ for some $X \in \mathfrak{g}$. The manifold $(M,g)$ is called a g.o. space if every geodesic through $o$ is homogeneous in this sense.

More generally, a geodesic through $o$ is called a $k$-step homogeneous geodesic if it admits a representation of the form
$$\gamma(t) = \exp(tX_1)\exp(tX_2)\cdots\exp(tX_k) \cdot o$$
for some $X_1, \ldots, X_k \in \mathfrak{g}$. In particular, a two-step homogeneous geodesic is one of the form $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX)\exp(tY)\cdot o$ with $X,Y \in \mathfrak{g}$, and $(M,g)$ is called a two-step g.o. space if every geodesic through $o$ admits such a two-step representation.

Determine whether the following holds: for every homogeneous Riemannian manifold $(G/H, g)$ and every geodesic through $o$ that admits a $k$-step homogeneous representation with $k \geq 3$, there exist $X, Y \in \mathfrak{g}$ such that the same geodesic admits the two-step representation $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX)\exp(tY)\cdot o$. Equivalently, decide whether the study of $k$-step homogeneous geodesics (for $k \geq 3$) can always be reduced to the study of two-step homogeneous geodesics.
status_search_result: The notion of two-step homogeneous geodesic was introduced and developed in works on homogeneous Riemannian and Finsler manifolds, with examples and sufficient conditions established, but no result reducing the general $k$-step ($k\geq 3$) case to the two-step case appears in the literature; the question is listed among open problems in surveys on geodesic orbit spaces and remains unresolved as of available sources.
