paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
original_question: Let S-Topd be the full category of strong d-spaces with continuous mappings. Is S-Topd reflective in Top0, the category of T0 spaces and continuous mappings?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions:

(a) A topological space is called T_0 if for any two distinct points there is an open set containing exactly one of them. On any T_0 space X, the specialization order is defined by x ≤ y iff x ∈ cl({y}). Throughout, every space considered is T_0 and is regarded as a poset via this order.

(b) A nonempty subset D of a poset is directed if every two elements of D have an upper bound in D. A T_0 space X is called a d-space (or monotone convergence space) if its specialization order is a directed-complete partial order (dcpo) and every directed subset D ⊆ X has its supremum ⋁D as a limit point of D in X (equivalently, the closure of D contains ⋁D and the principal filter generated by ⋁D is the set of limits of D).

(c) A T_0 space X is called a strong d-space if for every directed subset D ⊆ X, every point x ∈ X with x ≤ ⋁D in the specialization order, and every open neighborhood U of x, there exists d ∈ D such that the principal up-set ↑d intersects U; equivalently, the strong d-space condition strengthens the d-space condition by requiring that suprema of directed sets be reached "uniformly" by open neighborhoods of points below them.

(d) Let Top_0 denote the category whose objects are T_0 topological spaces and whose morphisms are continuous maps. Let S-Top_d denote the full subcategory of Top_0 whose objects are exactly the strong d-spaces.

(e) A full subcategory A of a category B is called reflective if the inclusion functor A ↪ B has a left adjoint; equivalently, for every object X of B there exists an object r(X) of A and a morphism η_X : X → r(X) such that every morphism from X into an object of A factors uniquely through η_X.

Problem: Determine whether S-Top_d is a reflective subcategory of Top_0. That is, decide whether for every T_0 space X there exists a strong d-space r(X) together with a continuous map η_X : X → r(X) such that for every continuous map f : X → Y with Y a strong d-space, there is a unique continuous map f̄ : r(X) → Y with f̄ ∘ η_X = f.
status_search_result: A web search did not locate a published resolution to the question of whether the full subcategory of strong d-spaces is reflective in the category of T_0 spaces. Related work on strong well-filtered spaces, R-spaces, and open well-filtered spaces by Shen, Xi, Xu, Zhao and others continues to appear (including a 2025 preprint on strong well-filteredness of upper topology on sup-complete posets), but none of the located sources explicitly settle the reflectivity of S-Top_d in Top_0.

paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
original_question: Let (X,tau) be a co-sober T0 space, and let k:(X,tau)->(X,tau) be continuous. Suppose k is a kernel operator for the specialization order, meaning k(x) lies in cl{x} and k(k(x))=k(x) for every x in X. Is the image subspace (k(X), tau restricted to k(X)) co-sober?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\tau)$ be a $T_0$ topological space. The specialization order $\le$ on $X$ is defined by $x \le y$ iff $x \in \overline{\{y\}}$. An irreducible closed subset of $X$ is a nonempty closed set $A$ that cannot be written as the union of two proper closed subsets of itself. The space $(X,\tau)$ is called sober if every irreducible closed subset is the closure of a unique point. Dually, a nonempty subset $F \subseteq X$ is called irreducible compact saturated (with appropriate definitions) and $(X,\tau)$ is called co-sober if every irreducible compact saturated subset of $X$ is the saturation $\mathord{\uparrow} x = \{y : x \le y\}$ of a unique point $x \in X$ (equivalently, every "irreducible" element of the relevant lattice of compact saturated sets is the principal filter of a point).

Let $(X,\tau)$ be a co-sober $T_0$ space and let $k : (X,\tau) \to (X,\tau)$ be a continuous self-map which is a kernel operator with respect to the specialization order, meaning that for every $x \in X$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $k(x) \in \overline{\{x\}}$ (equivalently $k(x) \le x$), and
\item $k(k(x)) = k(x)$.
\end{itemize}
Equip the image $k(X) \subseteq X$ with the subspace topology $\tau|_{k(X)}$. Is the subspace $(k(X), \tau|_{k(X)})$ necessarily co-sober?
status_search_result: A direct web search did not turn up any published resolution of this question. It is posed as an explicit open question on co-sober spaces and kernel operators with respect to specialization order, and no follow-up work resolving it was located.

paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
original_question: Is the product space of an arbitrary family of co-sober T0 spaces again co-sober?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a $T_0$ topological space. A nonempty subset $K \subseteq X$ is called irreducible if whenever $K \subseteq A \cup B$ with $A, B$ closed in $X$, one has $K \subseteq A$ or $K \subseteq B$. Denote by $\mathrm{K}(X)$ the set of all nonempty compact saturated subsets of $X$ (a set is saturated if it equals the intersection of its open neighborhoods, equivalently if it is an upper set in the specialization order). A nonempty compact saturated subset $Q \subseteq X$ is called irreducible (in the sense of compact saturated sets) if whenever $Q \subseteq A \cup B$ with $A, B$ compact saturated, one has $Q \subseteq A$ or $Q \subseteq B$. Equivalently, $Q$ is irreducible in $\mathrm{K}(X)$ (ordered by reverse inclusion) when viewed via the upper Vietoris / Smyth structure.

The space $X$ is called co-sober if every irreducible compact saturated subset $Q$ of $X$ is of the form $\uparrow x = \{y \in X : x \leq_X y\}$ for a unique point $x \in X$, where $\leq_X$ is the specialization preorder of $X$.

Question: Is it true that for every family $\{X_i\}_{i \in I}$ of co-sober $T_0$ topological spaces, the product space $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ (with the product topology) is co-sober?
status_search_result: Web searches did not return a definitive resolution of whether arbitrary products of co-sober $T_0$ spaces are co-sober. Related results on sobriety of products (e.g., the 2024 construction of two sober dcpo's whose product is not sober in the Scott topology) exist, but no clear answer to the co-sober product question was located. Status is therefore not verified.

paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
original_question: In knowledge-base mapping generation, how can mapping rules be generated for metadata-data correspondences, where a source data value must become target metadata such as a property name, or target data must become metadata, rather than simply mapping source concepts, properties, or paths to target concepts, properties, or paths?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of automatically generating mapping rules between two knowledge bases (KBs), each modeled as a set of concepts, properties, and instance data, together with a schema (metadata) layer naming the concepts and properties. A standard schema-level correspondence between a source KB S and a target KB T relates a source schema element (concept, property, or path) to a target schema element, and induces data-to-data mapping rules.

A metadata-data (MAD) correspondence, by contrast, asserts one of the following relationships:
(i) a source data value v occurring as an instance value in S must appear as a target metadata symbol in T (for example, as the name of a property or a class in T), or
(ii) a target data value must be produced from a source metadata symbol (for example, the name of a property in S must appear as data in T).

Develop a formal framework and algorithm for knowledge-base mapping generation that, given a set of correspondences between S and T including MAD correspondences, produces executable mapping rules whose execution on instances of S yields instances of T consistent with all correspondences. In particular:

1. Provide a precise semantics for MAD correspondences within a chosen KB data model (e.g., RDF/RDFS or OWL).
2. Define when a set of generated mapping rules is sound and complete with respect to a set of correspondences that may mix schema-level and MAD correspondences.
3. Give a generation procedure that handles MAD correspondences in both directions (data→metadata and metadata→data) and analyze its correctness and complexity.
status_search_result: The question concerns generating mapping rules for metadata-data (MAD) correspondences in knowledge-base mapping generation tools (KMGTs). This is identified as an open problem not addressed by existing KMGTs, and no subsequent work resolving it in full generality was located.

paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
original_question: How can data-driven or example-based mapping generation approaches be adapted to knowledge-base mapping generation tools, especially when many knowledge bases are web-scale and therefore natural candidates for using data examples rather than only schema-level correspondences?
self_contained_problem:
Let a knowledge base (KB) be a pair $K = (S, I)$ where $S$ is a schema (a finite set of classes, properties, and constraints, e.g.\ an RDF/OWL vocabulary) and $I$ is an instance: a (possibly very large, "web-scale") set of assertions over $S$ (e.g.\ RDF triples). Given two knowledge bases $K_1 = (S_1, I_1)$ and $K_2 = (S_2, I_2)$, a KB mapping is a finite set $M$ of logical rules (e.g.\ source-to-target tuple-generating dependencies, or executable transformation rules such as R2RML/SPARQL CONSTRUCT) that, when applied to $I_1$, produce data conforming to $S_2$.

Traditional schema-level mapping generation tools produce $M$ using only the schema-level correspondences $C \subseteq S_1 \times S_2$ (e.g.\ element-to-element alignments). In contrast, data-driven (example-based) mapping generation methods construct $M$ from a finite set of input/output data examples $E = \{(d_i, d_i')\}_{i=1}^n$ with $d_i$ a fragment of $I_1$ and $d_i'$ the intended fragment of $I_2$.

Problem. Design and formally characterize a mapping generation procedure $\mathcal{A}$ which, given $(S_1, S_2, C, E)$ where $E$ is drawn from web-scale instances $I_1, I_2$, outputs a KB mapping $M$ satisfying:
(i) Soundness with respect to examples: for every $(d_i, d_i') \in E$, applying $M$ to $d_i$ yields $d_i'$ (up to a specified semantic equivalence).
(ii) Generalization: $M$ correctly transforms instance fragments outside $E$ that follow the same regularities, in a precisely defined sense (e.g.\ minimality, certain-answer preservation, or PAC-style generalization over a distribution on $I_1$).
(iii) Scalability: $\mathcal{A}$ runs in time and memory sublinear (or otherwise tractable) in $|I_1| + |I_2|$, exploiting the web-scale availability of data examples rather than enumerating instances.

Provide an algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ together with formal guarantees of soundness, generalization, and tractability under explicit assumptions on $S_1, S_2, C$ and on the example sampling process, or prove impossibility results delimiting the trade-offs between (i)–(iii).
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in the surveyed area of knowledge-base mapping generation tools. No published work has been identified that provides a formal data-driven (example-based) mapping generation framework with provable guarantees for web-scale KBs; related example-based schema mapping work (e.g., MWeaver, EIRENE, Gottlob-Senellart) addresses relational schemas rather than web-scale knowledge bases. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
original_question: Can a knowledge-base mapping generation tool collectively learn correspondences, data examples, and mapping rules by combining logical and statistical reasoning, while still handling deep structural and semantic heterogeneity between two knowledge bases that cannot be resolved by simple same-as, isa, or equivalent-class axioms?
self_contained_problem:
Let K_1 and K_2 be two knowledge bases, each consisting of a schema (a set of classes, properties, and logical axioms expressed in some description-logic or first-order fragment) together with an instance set (a collection of ground assertions over that schema). A correspondence is a logical relationship (e.g., subclass, equivalence, sameAs, or more general first-order implication) between symbols or compound expressions of K_1 and K_2. A mapping rule is a (possibly existential, possibly probabilistic) implication of the form φ(x) → ψ(x), where φ is a formula over the vocabulary of K_1 and ψ is a formula over the vocabulary of K_2 (or vice versa). A data example is a pair (a, b) of instances such that a ∈ K_1 and b ∈ K_2 are intended to correspond under some mapping rule.

Design and prove the existence of a Knowledge-Graph Mapping Tool (KGMT), specified as an algorithm M taking (K_1, K_2) as input and outputting a triple (C, E, R) where C is a set of correspondences, E is a set of data examples, and R is a set of mapping rules, satisfying all of the following requirements:

1. (Joint learning) The components C, E, and R are learned collectively: each is used as evidence in inferring the others, and the algorithm performs a single optimization (rather than a strict pipeline) over a joint objective combining logical entailment constraints and a statistical likelihood (e.g., via a Markov logic network, probabilistic soft logic, or analogous formalism).

2. (Logical + statistical reasoning) The objective combines hard logical constraints derived from the axioms of K_1 and K_2 with soft statistical scores derived from instance-level co-occurrence and embedding-based similarities, and admits a precise semantics (e.g., maximum a posteriori inference in a probabilistic logic).

3. (Beyond simple axioms) The output R must be expressive enough to capture deep structural and semantic heterogeneity that cannot be expressed solely by sameAs, isA (subclass), or equivalentClass axioms — for instance, n-ary relational restructurings, attribute-to-relation conversions, conditional mappings, and existential value-creating rules.

4. (Correctness guarantee) Provide a soundness and (approximate) completeness theorem with respect to a declared semantics of correct mappings between K_1 and K_2, together with complexity bounds.

The problem asks whether such an algorithm M exists, and if so, to exhibit one and prove the corresponding correctness and complexity results.
category_tag: knowledge base mapping and ontology alignment
status_search_result: The question is a forward-looking research challenge in knowledge-graph integration. Existing systems such as ILIADS, PARIS, and CODI address ontology merging using simple axioms (sameAs, isA, equivalentClass), and more recent neuro-symbolic and probabilistic-logic systems (e.g., based on Markov logic, PSL, or embedding-based ontology matching) address parts of the task, but no published system is known to jointly learn correspondences, data examples, and expressive mapping rules while handling deep structural and semantic heterogeneity with formal guarantees. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
original_question: Can knowledge-base profiling and mining improve mapping quality by using available or automatically inferred constraints, such as cardinality constraints, functional-property constraints, inverse-functional-property constraints, disjointness constraints, join paths, or other mined dependencies, to resolve ambiguous property-path choices in source-to-target mappings?
self_contained_problem:
Let a source knowledge base S and a target knowledge base T each be specified as a set of typed entities together with a finite set of binary properties; a property path in T is a finite composition p_1 ∘ p_2 ∘ ... ∘ p_k of such properties. A source-to-target mapping is a function that assigns, to each source attribute or relation, a property path in T whose evaluation produces values of the intended type. A mapping is called ambiguous when several distinct property paths in T are type-compatible candidates for the same source attribute.

Consider the following classes of integrity constraints that may either be declared in T or be inferred automatically from instance data in T by profiling/mining procedures:
  (i) cardinality constraints on properties,
  (ii) functional-property constraints (a property is single-valued on its domain),
  (iii) inverse-functional-property constraints (the inverse is single-valued),
  (iv) disjointness constraints between classes or properties,
  (v) join-path constraints (e.g., approximate or exact inclusion dependencies between compositions of properties),
  (vi) more general mined dependencies (such as conditional functional dependencies or denial constraints).

Develop a formal framework in which such constraints are used to filter or rank candidate property paths in T for each source attribute, and prove that there exists a constraint-driven disambiguation procedure that, given any source-to-target mapping instance with at least one ambiguous property-path choice, produces a unique or strictly smaller set of candidate property paths whose induced mapping has provably higher quality (under a precisely defined quality measure, e.g., preservation of source dependencies, consistency with target constraints, and faithfulness to instance data) than mappings produced without using the constraints.

Equivalently: determine whether automatically inferred constraints of types (i)–(vi) are sufficient, in general, to resolve ambiguous property-path choices in source-to-target mappings and thereby improve mapping quality, and characterize the conditions on S, T, and the constraint set under which such improvement can be guaranteed.
status_search_result: The question is posed as a forward-looking research direction concerning whether knowledge-base profiling and constraint mining can disambiguate property-path choices in schema/ontology mappings. No general formal solution or guarantee theorem appears in the literature; existing works on profiling, dependency mining, and ontology mapping (e.g., approaches using functional/inverse-functional properties, disjointness axioms, and inclusion/join-path dependencies) address restricted cases but do not provide a general answer. The status is best regarded as open.

paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
original_question: How can knowledge-base mapping generation tools scale to large source and target knowledge bases by using methods more sophisticated than simple slicing, such as modularization or partitioning, while still generating mapping rules efficiently?
self_contained_problem:
Let a knowledge base (KB) be a pair $K = (S, A)$ where $S$ is a schema (a finite set of classes and properties with subclass/subproperty relations and domain/range constraints) and $A$ is a finite set of assertions over $S$. A mapping between two knowledge bases $K_1 = (S_1, A_1)$ and $K_2 = (S_2, A_2)$ is a finite set $M$ of mapping rules, each of the form $\varphi(\bar x) \rightsquigarrow \psi(\bar x)$, where $\varphi$ is a conjunctive query over $S_1$ and $\psi$ is a conjunctive query over $S_2$. A knowledge-base mapping generation tool (KMGT) is an algorithm that, given $K_1$ and $K_2$, outputs such a set $M$.

Consider the following scalability problem. Suppose $|S_1|, |S_2|, |A_1|, |A_2|$ are too large to be processed in memory by a direct KMGT. A simple slicing approach partitions each KB into disjoint chunks of bounded size and applies the KMGT independently to each pair of chunks; this can miss mapping rules that span chunks and can produce redundant or inconsistent rules.

Problem. Design a KMGT framework that scales to arbitrarily large source and target knowledge bases by using either
(i) modularization, in which each KB is decomposed into a family of modules $\{M_i\}$ such that for every signature $\Sigma$ of interest there exists a module $M_i$ that is a conservative extension of the relevant fragment of the KB with respect to $\Sigma$; or
(ii) partitioning, in which each KB is split into possibly overlapping parts according to a structural or semantic criterion (e.g., graph cuts on the schema graph, clustering of assertions, or locality-based partitions).

Specifically, give an algorithm together with a formal correctness and efficiency analysis establishing:
(a) Soundness: every rule produced is logically entailed by the full KBs.
(b) Completeness (relative to a specified mapping language): every rule that a non-scalable reference KMGT would produce on the entire KBs is recovered, up to logical equivalence.
(c) Scalability: the total running time and memory are sub-linear in a meaningful parameter (e.g., polynomial in the largest module/partition size and near-linear in the total KB size), strictly improving upon simple slicing.

Either exhibit such an algorithm with proofs of (a)–(c), or prove an impossibility result identifying intrinsic obstacles (e.g., that no modularization/partitioning scheme of bounded module size can preserve completeness for a given mapping language).
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research challenge regarding scalability of knowledge-base mapping generation tools. No definitive scalable solution with formal soundness/completeness/efficiency guarantees based on modularization or partitioning appears to be established in the literature; ontology modularization and partitioning techniques exist but have not been shown to fully resolve the scalable mapping-generation problem.

paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
original_question: How can execution of transformation queries produced by knowledge-base mapping generation tools be optimized when the generated SPARQL queries contain many nested OPTIONAL clauses, which are required for open-world knowledge-base integration tasks but are expensive because query engines often process them as left outer joins?
self_contained_problem:
Consider SPARQL, the standard query language for RDF graphs. A basic graph pattern (BGP) is a finite set of triple patterns of the form (s, p, o) in which each component is either an IRI/literal or a variable. The OPTIONAL operator combines two patterns P1 and P2 into a pattern (P1 OPT P2) whose evaluation over an RDF graph G is the left outer join of the evaluations of P1 and P2: every solution of P1 is preserved, extended by a compatible solution of P2 when one exists. SPARQL queries with arbitrarily nested OPTIONAL patterns are known to have PSPACE-complete evaluation in general, and queries built from BGPs and OPT only (well-designed or not) are typically executed by query engines using a left-outer-join physical plan.

In knowledge-base integration and ontology-based data-access scenarios, automatically generated transformation queries that materialize mappings from heterogeneous sources into a target schema routinely produce SPARQL queries that contain many deeply nested OPTIONAL clauses, since attributes in the source may or may not exist for each entity (open-world assumption). The cost of evaluating such queries via left outer joins grows rapidly with the depth and number of OPT operators, because left outer joins admit only restricted reordering and force the engine to retain unmatched tuples padded with nulls.

Problem. Develop a query-evaluation algorithm (with proofs of correctness with respect to the standard SPARQL set/bag semantics) for SPARQL queries of the form

   Q ::= BGP | (Q OPT Q) | (Q AND Q) | (Q FILTER F)

such that, for queries with n triple patterns and k nested OPTIONAL operators, the worst-case evaluation cost on an RDF graph with m triples is asymptotically strictly better than the cost obtained by treating every OPT as a generic left outer join in a relational engine. Specifically: identify a syntactic or semantic subclass of SPARQL OPTIONAL queries that captures the patterns arising from automatic knowledge-base mapping generation, give a sound and complete evaluation procedure for this subclass whose complexity is polynomial in m and n (and ideally independent of k beyond a low-degree polynomial), and prove matching lower bounds showing that no further asymptotic improvement is possible within the subclass.
status_search_result: Optimization of nested SPARQL OPTIONAL queries remains an active research topic. Several partial approaches exist (OptBitMat, Left Bit Right, the Nested Optional Join operator, and various SQL-translation techniques), each improving on naive left-outer-join evaluation for specific subclasses, but no general optimal algorithm for arbitrary nested OPTIONAL patterns is known and the evaluation problem is PSPACE-complete in general, so the problem is considered open in its full generality.

paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
original_question: Can the knowledge-base exchange community build an iBench-like metadata or exchange-scenario generator for evaluating knowledge-base mapping generation tools, with parameters that control factors such as value invention, incomplete source and target knowledge bases, incomplete correspondences, cycles, and multiple alternative interpretations of a correspondence?
self_contained_problem:
Design and construct a parameterized metadata/scenario generator for the evaluation of knowledge-base (KB) mapping generation tools, analogous in spirit to the iBench integration metadata generator used for relational schema mapping benchmarks. Specifically, produce a system that, given a user-supplied configuration, synthesizes complete KB exchange scenarios consisting of: (i) a source KB schema (e.g., a TBox in a description logic or ontology language) together with optional source data (ABox), (ii) a target KB schema together with optional target data, (iii) a set of correspondences/mappings between source and target, and (iv) any auxiliary constraints needed to define the exchange problem. The generator must expose tunable parameters that control at least the following factors:

1. Value invention — the extent to which the target schema requires the introduction of fresh existentially quantified individuals (labeled nulls / Skolem terms) not present in the source.
2. Incompleteness of the source KB — controlled gaps or missing assertions in the source ABox/TBox.
3. Incompleteness of the target KB — controlled gaps or missing assertions in the target ABox/TBox.
4. Incompleteness of correspondences — partial or missing mappings between source and target vocabulary.
5. Presence of cycles in the KBs and/or in the mapping dependency structure.
6. Multiplicity of alternative interpretations of a single correspondence (e.g., the number of semantically distinct logical formalizations a correspondence may admit).

The generator should be capable of producing scenarios of arbitrary size and complexity by composing primitive scenario patterns, and should support repeatable, configurable benchmarking of KB mapping generation tools across all of the above dimensions. The task is to determine whether such a generator can be built and to provide its design and implementation.
status_search_result: While iBench exists as a mature metadata/scenario generator for relational schema-mapping benchmarks, public searches do not reveal an analogous generator for knowledge-base exchange scenarios that exposes parameters for value invention, incompleteness in source/target KBs and correspondences, cycles, and multiple alternative interpretations of correspondences. Existing KB-exchange scenario collections are more limited in parameter coverage. The challenge therefore appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems on structure of positively curved projective varieties
original_question: Let (X,g) be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. For p in X, let V_flat,p be the subspace of T_X,p consisting of tangent vectors v such that R_g(v,x,y,z̄)=0 for every x,y,z in T_X,p, and define ntf(X,g)=dim X−inf_p dim V_flat,p. If ntf(X,g)=dim X, must H^0(X, Ω_X^q)=0 for every q>0, and must X be projective?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,g)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $R_g$ denote its Riemannian (Chern) curvature tensor extended $\mathbb{C}$-linearly to the holomorphic tangent bundle. For a point $p \in X$, call a tangent vector $v \in T_{X,p}$ truly flat at $p$ if
$$R_g(v, x, y, \bar z) = 0 \quad \text{for all } x, y, z \in T_{X,p},$$
and let $V_{\mathrm{flat},p} \subset T_{X,p}$ denote the subspace of all truly flat vectors at $p$. Define
$$\mathrm{ntf}(X,g) := \dim_{\mathbb{C}} X \;-\; \inf_{p \in X} \dim_{\mathbb{C}} V_{\mathrm{flat},p}.$$

Assume that $g$ has semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature, that is, $R_g(v,\bar v, v, \bar v) \ge 0$ for every $v \in T_X$, and assume furthermore that $\mathrm{ntf}(X,g) = \dim_{\mathbb{C}} X$ (equivalently, there exists a point $p \in X$ at which no nonzero truly flat tangent vector exists).

Prove or disprove:
(a) $H^0(X, \Omega_X^q) = 0$ for every $q > 0$;
(b) $X$ is projective.
category_tag: Kähler manifolds with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in recent surveys on positively curved projective varieties, and recent works (e.g., on positivity of tangent sheaves and pseudo-effective holonomy principles for Kähler manifolds with nonnegative holomorphic sectional curvature) discuss partial progress under stronger hypotheses (such as no truly flat tangent vector at some point yielding rational connectedness/projectivity), but the full statement under only the maximality condition $\mathrm{ntf}(X,g)=\dim X$ does not appear to be settled. No source verifying a complete resolution was found.

original_question: Let (X,g) be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. Is the fundamental group of X an extension of a finite group by ℤ^{2m}? context_brief: Classification under positive holomorphic sectional curvature
original_question: Does the blow-up of a Hirzebruch surface admit positive holomorphic sectional curvature? More broadly, can all varieties of a fixed dimension, for example surfaces or threefolds, with semi-positive or positive holomorphic sectional curvature be classified, and can one identify an algebraic-geometric analogue of semi-positive or positive holomorphic sectional curvature?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g)$ be a Kähler manifold with associated Kähler form $\omega$. The holomorphic sectional curvature of $g$ at a point $p \in M$ in the direction of a nonzero holomorphic tangent vector $v \in T_p^{1,0} M$ is defined by
$$H(v) = \frac{R(v, \bar v, v, \bar v)}{|v|^4},$$
where $R$ is the curvature tensor of $g$. The metric $g$ is said to have positive (resp. semi-positive) holomorphic sectional curvature if $H(v) > 0$ (resp. $H(v) \ge 0$) for every nonzero $v$.

For integers $n \ge 0$, the Hirzebruch surface $\Sigma_n$ is the projective bundle $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1} \oplus \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(n))$ over $\mathbb{P}^1$. Let $\widetilde{\Sigma}_n \to \Sigma_n$ be the blow-up of $\Sigma_n$ at one or more points.

(a) Does $\widetilde{\Sigma}_n$ admit a Kähler metric of positive holomorphic sectional curvature?

(b) Classify all smooth projective surfaces, and more generally smooth projective threefolds, that admit a Kähler metric of semi-positive (respectively positive) holomorphic sectional curvature.

(c) Identify an intrinsic algebraic-geometric property of a smooth projective variety that serves as an analogue of the existence of a Kähler metric of semi-positive (respectively positive) holomorphic sectional curvature.
status_search_result: Hitchin and later Yang–Zheng showed that every Hirzebruch surface/manifold admits Kähler metrics of positive holomorphic sectional curvature, but the question of whether arbitrary blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces admit such metrics, and the full classification of surfaces/threefolds with (semi-)positive holomorphic sectional curvature, are not resolved in the literature found. The problem is still posed as open in recent surveys.

Recall that an R-Cartier divisor D on X is called pseudo-effective if its numerical class lies in the closure of the cone generated by classes of effective R-divisors. paper_title: Open problems on structure of positively curved projective varieties
original_question: Let (X,Δ) be a klt pair such that X is smooth and −(K_X+Δ) is nef. Does there exist an orbifold morphism ρ:(X,Δ)→(R,Δ_R) such that (R,Δ_R) is klt, R is smooth, c1(K_R+Δ_R)=0, the general orbifold fibers are slope rationally connected, and the fibration is locally trivial with respect to pairs, meaning that for every small open set U in R the pair (ρ^{-1}(U),Δ) is isomorphic over U to (U,Δ_R|_U)×(X_r,Δ_{X_r}) for a general fiber X_r?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let X be a smooth complex projective variety and Δ an effective Q-divisor on X such that the pair (X,Δ) is klt (Kawamata log terminal) and the anti-log-canonical divisor −(K_X+Δ) is nef.

Recall the following notions:
- An orbifold morphism ρ:(X,Δ)→(R,Δ_R) between klt pairs is a surjective morphism ρ:X→R compatible with the orbifold structures of Δ and Δ_R in the sense of Campana (i.e., the multiplicities of Δ are matched by ramification and by the multiplicities of Δ_R along divisors of R).
- A general orbifold fiber of ρ is the pair (X_r, Δ_{X_r}), where X_r=ρ^{-1}(r) for a general point r∈R and Δ_{X_r}=Δ|_{X_r}.
- The pair (X_r, Δ_{X_r}) is slope rationally connected (sRC) in the sense that any two general points can be joined by a chain of rational curves which are "free" with respect to the pair, generalizing rational connectedness to klt pairs.
- The fibration ρ is locally trivial with respect to pairs if for every sufficiently small open subset U⊂R there is an isomorphism (ρ^{-1}(U),Δ|_{ρ^{-1}(U)}) ≅ (U,Δ_R|_U) × (X_r,Δ_{X_r}) over U, where (X_r,Δ_{X_r}) is a general orbifold fiber.

Question. Does there always exist an orbifold morphism ρ:(X,Δ)→(R,Δ_R) such that:
(i) (R,Δ_R) is a klt pair with R smooth;
(ii) the numerical class c_1(K_R+Δ_R)=0;
(iii) the general orbifold fibers (X_r,Δ_{X_r}) are slope rationally connected;
(iv) ρ is locally trivial with respect to the pairs (X,Δ) and (R,Δ_R) in the sense above?

paper_title: Three open problems in function theoretic operator theory
original_question: Let Theta be a finite Blaschke product, let K_Theta be its associated model space in the Hardy space H^2(D), and let S_Theta be the compression P_Theta M_z restricted to K_Theta of multiplication by z. Let B be another finite Blaschke product with degree(B) < degree(Theta). Must max{|B(z)| : z is in W(S_Theta)} be at least 1/2, where W(S_Theta) is the numerical range of S_Theta?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and let $H^2(\mathbb{D})$ denote the Hardy space on $\mathbb{D}$. For a finite Blaschke product $\Theta$ of degree $n$, define the associated model space
$$K_\Theta = H^2(\mathbb{D})\ominus \Theta H^2(\mathbb{D}),$$
an $n$-dimensional subspace of $H^2(\mathbb{D})$. Let $P_\Theta$ be the orthogonal projection of $H^2(\mathbb{D})$ onto $K_\Theta$, and let $M_z$ be multiplication by the independent variable on $H^2(\mathbb{D})$. Define the compressed shift
$$S_\Theta = P_\Theta M_z\big|_{K_\Theta},$$
a bounded linear operator on $K_\Theta$ with numerical range
$$W(S_\Theta) = \{\langle S_\Theta f, f\rangle : f\in K_\Theta,\ \|f\|=1\}.$$

Question: For every finite Blaschke product $\Theta$ and every finite Blaschke product $B$ with $\deg(B) < \deg(\Theta)$, must
$$\max\{|B(z)| : z\in \overline{W(S_\Theta)}\} \ \geq\ \tfrac{1}{2}\,?$$
status_search_result: The level set Crouzeix conjecture for compressed shifts on model spaces of finite Blaschke products has been verified in several special cases (e.g., unicritical Blaschke products of degree 4, certain 3×3, 4×4, and 5×5 matrix classes) in work by Bickel, Garcia, Gorkin, Liaw and collaborators (Journal d'Analyse Mathématique, 2023; Concrete Operators, 2024), but the general statement remains open.

paper_title: Three open problems in function theoretic operator theory
context_brief: condition number for model-space shift compression
original_question: Let Theta be a finite Blaschke product with distinct zeros, and let S_Theta be the compression of the unilateral shift to the model space K_Theta associated with Theta. For a matrix representing S_Theta that is diagonalized as A = X D X^{-1}, what is the smallest possible condition number ||X|| ||X^{-1}|| among eigenvector matrices X?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Theta$ be a finite Blaschke product with $n$ distinct zeros, namely
$$\Theta(z) \;=\; \prod_{j=1}^{n} \frac{z-\lambda_j}{1-\overline{\lambda_j}z}, \qquad \lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n \in \mathbb{D} \text{ distinct},$$
and let $K_\Theta = H^2 \ominus \Theta H^2$ denote the associated model space inside the Hardy space $H^2$ of the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}$. Let $S \colon H^2 \to H^2$ be the unilateral shift $(Sf)(z)=zf(z)$, and let
$$S_\Theta \;=\; P_{K_\Theta} S\big|_{K_\Theta}$$
be the compression of $S$ to $K_\Theta$, where $P_{K_\Theta}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $K_\Theta$. The operator $S_\Theta$ acts on the $n$-dimensional space $K_\Theta$ and its spectrum is $\{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\}$; in particular it is diagonalizable, so for any matrix representation $A$ of $S_\Theta$ in an orthonormal basis of $K_\Theta$ there exists an invertible $X \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ and a diagonal $D \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ with $A = X D X^{-1}$.

Determine, as a function of the zeros $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n$, the minimal possible value of the condition number
$$\kappa(X) \;=\; \|X\|\,\|X^{-1}\|$$
(with respect to the spectral / operator $2$-norm) over all such eigenvector matrices $X$ diagonalizing $S_\Theta$.
status_search_result: The question is explicitly listed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems in function-theoretic operator theory. No published solution determining the minimal eigenvector-matrix condition number of the compressed shift $S_\Theta$ on a model space with a finite Blaschke product symbol could be located.

paper_title: Three open problems in function theoretic operator theory
original_question: Let p(z) = product_{k=1}^n (z - z_k) be a complex polynomial of degree n >= 2. Define sigma_infinity(p) = min_{c in C} max_{1 <= k <= n} |z_k - c|, the radius of the smallest closed disk containing all zeros of p. If zeta is any point in the convex hull of the zeros z_1, ..., z_n, must the closed disk centered at zeta with radius sigma_infinity(p) contain a critical point of p?
self_contained_problem:
Let $p(z) = \prod_{k=1}^n (z - z_k)$ be a complex polynomial of degree $n \geq 2$ with zeros $z_1, \dots, z_n \in \mathbb{C}$ (listed with multiplicity). Define
$$\sigma_\infty(p) = \min_{c \in \mathbb{C}} \max_{1 \leq k \leq n} |z_k - c|,$$
the radius of the smallest closed disk in $\mathbb{C}$ that contains all of the zeros of $p$. Let $K = \mathrm{conv}\{z_1, \dots, z_n\}$ denote the convex hull of the zeros of $p$.

Prove or disprove the following: for every $\zeta \in K$, the closed disk
$$\overline{D}(\zeta, \sigma_\infty(p)) = \{ z \in \mathbb{C} : |z - \zeta| \leq \sigma_\infty(p)\}$$
contains at least one critical point of $p$ (i.e., a zero of the derivative $p'$).
status_search_result: Schmeisser's conjecture is a strengthening of the Sendov conjecture, replacing the requirement that $\zeta$ be a zero of $p$ with $\zeta$ being any point in the convex hull of the zeros. While Sendov's conjecture itself has been proven only in special cases and remains open in general for arbitrary degree, the Schmeisser strengthening is correspondingly open. Recent work (e.g., on intersections of convex hulls of polynomial shifts and partial bounds of the form $|z-\zeta|\le\sqrt{1-|\zeta|^2}$ for $\zeta$ in the convex hull of critical points) addresses related and weaker forms but does not settle Schmeisser's conjecture.

paper_title: Three open problems in function theoretic operator theory
original_question: Let X be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space and let T be a bounded linear operator on X. Is it true that T must have a nontrivial invariant subspace, meaning a closed subspace M with M not equal to {0} or X and T(M) contained in M? The source records this broad Banach-space form as resolved negatively by counterexamples, including an operator on l^1 with no nontrivial invariant subspaces.
self_contained_problem: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space, and let $T : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator. A closed subspace $M \subseteq X$ is called a nontrivial invariant subspace for $T$ if $M \neq \{0\}$, $M \neq X$, and $T(M) \subseteq M$. Determine whether the following statement is true: for every infinite-dimensional complex Banach space $X$ and every bounded linear operator $T$ on $X$, the operator $T$ admits a nontrivial invariant subspace. Equivalently, decide whether there exists an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space $X$ and a bounded linear operator $T$ on $X$ such that the only closed subspaces $M \subseteq X$ with $T(M) \subseteq M$ are $M = \{0\}$ and $M = X$.
status_search_result: The Banach-space invariant subspace problem in this general form has been resolved negatively. P. Enflo (1976/1987) constructed a Banach space with a bounded operator having no nontrivial invariant subspace, and C. J. Read later produced a bounded operator on the classical Banach space $\ell^1$ with no nontrivial closed invariant subspaces.

paper_title: Three open problems in function theoretic operator theory
context_brief: universal adjoints of affine composition operators
original_question: Let C_+ be the right half-plane, let H^2(C_+) be the Hardy space on C_+, and let phi : C_+ -> C_+ be an affine self-map. Let C_phi be the composition operator on H^2(C_+) and C_phi^* its adjoint. Is C_phi^* - lambda I universal on H^2(C_+) for some complex scalar lambda if and only if phi is elliptic and not an automorphism? Here universal means that every bounded operator on the ambient separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is similar, up to a nonzero scalar multiple, to the restriction of the universal operator to some invariant subspace.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{C}_+ = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z > 0\}$ denote the right half-plane, and let $H^2(\mathbb{C}_+)$ be the Hardy space on $\mathbb{C}_+$, consisting of analytic functions $f : \mathbb{C}_+ \to \mathbb{C}$ with
$$\|f\|^2 := \sup_{x>0} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |f(x+iy)|^2\, dy < \infty.$$
For an analytic self-map $\varphi : \mathbb{C}_+ \to \mathbb{C}_+$ for which the composition operator $C_\varphi f := f \circ \varphi$ is bounded on $H^2(\mathbb{C}_+)$, write $C_\varphi^*$ for its Hilbert space adjoint.

A bounded operator $U$ on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ is called universal if, for every bounded linear operator $T$ on $\mathcal{H}$, there exist a nonzero scalar $\mu \in \mathbb{C}$ and a closed $U$-invariant subspace $\mathcal{M} \subset \mathcal{H}$ such that $\mu T$ is similar to the restriction $U|_{\mathcal{M}}$.

An affine self-map of $\mathbb{C}_+$ is a map of the form $\varphi(z) = az + b$ with $a > 0$ and $\operatorname{Re} b \ge 0$. Such a $\varphi$ is called elliptic when it has a fixed point in $\mathbb{C}_+$, and it is an automorphism of $\mathbb{C}_+$ precisely when $b \in i\mathbb{R}$ (so $\varphi$ is a translation when $a=1$).

Problem: Prove or disprove that, for every affine self-map $\varphi$ of $\mathbb{C}_+$ such that $C_\varphi$ is bounded on $H^2(\mathbb{C}_+)$, the operator $C_\varphi^* - \lambda I$ is universal on $H^2(\mathbb{C}_+)$ for some $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ if and only if $\varphi$ is elliptic and not an automorphism of $\mathbb{C}_+$.
status_search_result: Recent work (Cowen–Gallardo-Gutiérrez and subsequent papers on universal composition operators, including extensions to weighted Dirichlet spaces) characterizes certain linear fractional symbols whose composition operators or their adjoints have universal translates, but the full affine-symbol characterization on H^2 of the half-plane is posed as an open question and does not appear to be resolved in the literature.

paper_title: On two open problems on the normality of bent functions
original_question: Does there exist a non-normal Boolean bent function belonging to the class denoted PS−∖PS_ap?
self_contained_problem:
Let $m \geq 1$ and let $\mathbb{F}_2^{2m}$ denote the $2m$-dimensional vector space over the binary field. A Boolean function $f \colon \mathbb{F}_2^{2m} \to \mathbb{F}_2$ is called bent if its Walsh transform $\widehat{f}(a) = \sum_{x \in \mathbb{F}_2^{2m}} (-1)^{f(x) + \langle a, x \rangle}$ satisfies $|\widehat{f}(a)| = 2^m$ for every $a \in \mathbb{F}_2^{2m}$. The function $f$ is called normal if there exists an $m$-dimensional affine subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^{2m}$ on which $f$ is constant; otherwise $f$ is non-normal.

The Partial Spread class $\mathcal{PS}^-$ consists of bent functions $f$ that are constant (equal to $0$) on each of $2^{m-1}$ pairwise "trivially intersecting" $m$-dimensional subspaces $E_1,\dots,E_{2^{m-1}}$ of $\mathbb{F}_2^{2m}$ (a partial spread of size $2^{m-1}$), and zero outside the union of these subspaces (apart from possibly the origin), with $f(0)=0$.

Identifying $\mathbb{F}_2^{2m}$ with $\mathbb{F}_{2^m} \times \mathbb{F}_{2^m}$, the subclass $\mathcal{PS}_{ap} \subseteq \mathcal{PS}^-$ consists of bent functions of the form
$$f(x,y) = g(x y^{2^m-2}),$$
where $g \colon \mathbb{F}_{2^m} \to \mathbb{F}_2$ is a balanced function with $g(0)=0$ (here $y^{2^m-2}$ denotes the multiplicative inverse of $y$ in $\mathbb{F}_{2^m}^*$, with $0^{2^m-2}=0$).

Question: Does there exist a non-normal Boolean bent function that belongs to $\mathcal{PS}^- \setminus \mathcal{PS}_{ap}$?
status_search_result: The question is addressed in a 2024/2025 publication in Discrete Applied Mathematics titled "On two open problems on the normality of bent functions" by Polujan, Mariot, and Picek, whose stated goal is to resolve the two listed open problems about normality (including the existence of non-normal bent functions in $\mathcal{PS}^- \setminus \mathcal{PS}_{ap}$). The paper reports affirmative constructions, so the problem appears to be solved, although the full text could not be directly fetched here for verbatim confirmation.

paper_title: Protocols for Observational Studies: Methods and Open Problems
context_brief: Sample splitting for observational study protocols
original_question: In an observational study protocol that uses sample splitting, where a planning sample is used to choose outcomes or subgroups and a separate analysis sample is used for confirmatory testing, how should investigators choose the planning-sample fraction as a function of the total sample size, decide how many and which candidate outcomes should be carried forward from planning to analysis, and design sequential versions that allow more than one possible planning sample before committing to the final analysis sample?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an observational study with a total sample of N units (treated and control), in which causal inference is to be performed via a two-stage sample-splitting protocol. The data are partitioned into a planning sample of size n_P and an analysis sample of size n_A = N − n_P. The planning sample is used (without formal inferential guarantees) to select, from a list of K candidate outcome variables (or subgroups), a subset S ⊆ {1,…,K} of outcomes that will be tested in the analysis sample by a pre-specified confirmatory procedure (e.g., a randomization or sensitivity-analysis test, possibly with multiplicity correction over |S|).

Address the following three design problems for such protocols:

(i) Optimal planning fraction. Determine how the planning fraction π = n_P / N should be chosen as a function of N (and of structural parameters such as the number of candidate outcomes K, anticipated effect sizes, variability, and the targeted level Γ of sensitivity to unmeasured confounding) so as to maximize the design sensitivity, expected power, or another principled criterion of the confirmatory test on the analysis sample.

(ii) Outcome-selection rule. Specify a rule, computed from the planning sample, for deciding how many outcomes |S| and which outcomes should be carried forward to the analysis sample, in a way that maximizes the power of the resulting confirmatory analysis (after any required multiplicity adjustment) under plausible models of effects and bias.

(iii) Sequential planning. Extend the above to a sequential protocol that, instead of using a single planning/analysis split, allows the investigator to examine several candidate planning samples (possibly chosen adaptively) before committing to a final analysis sample, while preserving the validity (Type I error and sensitivity guarantees) of the confirmatory test conducted on the eventual analysis sample. Characterize the optimal sequential rule and the corresponding loss (if any) relative to the one-shot split.

Provide answers, or principled methodologies, for (i), (ii), and (iii).
status_search_result: Recent preprints address parts of these questions: "Planning for Gold" (2024) gives a hypothesis-screening rule for choosing which outcomes to carry forward in matched observational studies, and a 2026 preprint "Optimal Sample Splitting for Observational Studies" proposes an adaptive rule for the planning fraction in low- and high-dimensional outcome settings. The sequential / multi-planning-sample version (iii) does not yet appear to have a published general solution, so the full triple of questions remains only partially solved.

paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
original_question: Let K be a tree embedded in the Euclidean plane R^2 and let epsilon be positive. Say that K is genuinely epsilon-disjoinable if there is a continuous or piecewise-linear map f: K -> R^2 such that K and f(K) are disjoint and every point x of K moves by less than epsilon, |x - f(x)| < epsilon. Say that K is epsilon-spanned if two closed round disks of diameter epsilon, whose centers move continuously on K and are never allowed to intersect, cannot be moved so that their two traces on K become the same. Say that K is symmetrically epsilon-spanned if such disks cannot exchange their positions. Does genuine epsilon-disjoinability imply epsilon-spannedness, and does symmetric epsilon-spannedness imply epsilon-spannedness for plane trees?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a tree (a compact, connected, simply connected $1$-dimensional polyhedron) embedded in the Euclidean plane, and let $\varepsilon > 0$.

(i) Call $K$ genuinely $\varepsilon$-disjoinable if there exists a continuous (equivalently, piecewise-linear) map $f \colon K \to \mathbb{R}^2$ such that $f(K) \cap K = \emptyset$ and $|x - f(x)| < \varepsilon$ for every $x \in K$.

(ii) Consider two closed round disks $D_1, D_2 \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, each of diameter $\varepsilon$, whose centers $c_1(t), c_2(t)$ move continuously along $K$ as functions of $t \in [0,1]$, and which are required to remain disjoint at every time $t$ (that is, $D_1(t) \cap D_2(t) = \emptyset$ for all $t$). The trace of $D_i$ on $K$ at time $t$ is the set $D_i(t) \cap K$. Call $K$ $\varepsilon$-spanned if there is no such admissible motion of the two disks that results in their two traces on $K$ coinciding at the end (i.e.\ one cannot move the disks so that, at some time, $D_1(t) \cap K = D_2(t) \cap K$ as subsets of $K$). Call $K$ symmetrically $\varepsilon$-spanned if no such admissible motion exchanges the disks (i.e.\ achieves $(c_1(1), c_2(1)) = (c_2(0), c_1(0))$).

Answer the following:

(a) Does genuine $\varepsilon$-disjoinability of $K$ imply that $K$ is $\varepsilon$-spanned?

(b) Does symmetric $\varepsilon$-spannedness of $K$ imply that $K$ is $\varepsilon$-spanned?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any results addressing these specific implications for plane trees with the notions of genuine $\varepsilon$-disjoinability, $\varepsilon$-spannedness, or symmetric $\varepsilon$-spannedness. No published resolution could be located, but the absence of search hits is not by itself evidence that the problem remains open.

paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
original_question: Let K be a plane tree in R^2 with diameter 1 and let epsilon be positive. A tree is epsilon-chainable if it is the union of closed sets C_1,...,C_n, each of diameter less than epsilon, such that C_i intersects only its immediate neighbors C_{i-1} and C_{i+1}. A tree is epsilon-spanned if two non-intersecting round disks of diameter epsilon with centers moving on K cannot move so that their traces on K are the same. Is every epsilon-spanned plane tree of diameter 1 necessarily 10 epsilon-chainable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a plane tree (a compact, connected, locally connected, one-dimensional planar continuum without simple closed curves) of diameter $1$, and let $\varepsilon>0$.

Say that $K$ is $\varepsilon$-chainable if there exist closed sets $C_1,\dots,C_n$ with $K=\bigcup_{i=1}^n C_i$, each $C_i$ of diameter strictly less than $\varepsilon$, such that $C_i\cap C_j\neq\emptyset$ if and only if $|i-j|\le 1$.

Say that $K$ is $\varepsilon$-spanned if there do not exist two continuous motions of two disjoint round closed disks of diameter $\varepsilon$, whose centers move along $K$, such that the two centers trace out the same subset of $K$ during the motion.

Decide whether the following is true: every $\varepsilon$-spanned plane tree $K\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of diameter $1$ is necessarily $10\varepsilon$-chainable.

paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
original_question: Given any triple of finite graphs K, X, and Y, is there an algorithm that decides whether K is basically embeddable in the product X x Y? In this setting, basic embeddability means that K embeds into X x Y in such a way that each continuous real-valued function on K can be written as a sum of a continuous function of the X-coordinate and a continuous function of the Y-coordinate.
self_contained_problem:
A finite graph is regarded as a one-dimensional topological space (a finite CW complex). Given finite graphs $K$, $X$, and $Y$, an embedding $f:K\hookrightarrow X\times Y$ is called basic if every continuous function $\varphi:K\to\mathbb{R}$ can be represented in the form
$$\varphi(p) = \alpha(\pi_X(f(p))) + \beta(\pi_Y(f(p))) \quad \text{for all } p\in K,$$
for some continuous functions $\alpha:X\to\mathbb{R}$ and $\beta:Y\to\mathbb{R}$, where $\pi_X$ and $\pi_Y$ denote the projections from $X\times Y$ onto its factors. The graph $K$ is said to be basically embeddable in $X\times Y$ if such an embedding exists.

Question: Is there an algorithm that, given any triple $(K,X,Y)$ of finite graphs as input, decides whether $K$ is basically embeddable in $X\times Y$?

paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
original_question: Construct a simple algorithm that takes an oriented link in the oriented 3-sphere S^3 together with surgery coefficients and outputs a colored graph representing the closed 3-manifold obtained by performing that surgery.
self_contained_problem:
Background. A closed PL 3-manifold M can be represented by a 4-colored graph (also called a crystallization, in the irreducible case), i.e. a finite multigraph G whose edges are properly colored by the set {0,1,2,3} such that every vertex has exactly one edge of each color, with the property that the regular 4-dimensional pseudo-complex K(G) associated to G has |K(G)| ≅ M. By a classical theorem of Lickorish and Wallace, every closed orientable 3-manifold can be obtained from the oriented 3-sphere S^3 by Dehn surgery along an oriented framed link L ⊂ S^3, that is, by an oriented link together with a choice of surgery coefficient (a rational number, or ∞) on each component.

Problem. Construct an explicit, simple algorithm with the following specification:
- Input: an oriented link L in S^3 (given, for instance, by a planar diagram) together with a surgery coefficient assigned to each component of L.
- Output: a 4-colored graph G that represents the closed 3-manifold M obtained from S^3 by performing the prescribed Dehn surgery on L.

The algorithm should be combinatorial and effective, taking only the link diagram and the surgery coefficients as data and producing the edge-colored graph directly, without first passing through an arbitrary triangulation or handle decomposition of M.
status_search_result: Algorithms producing edge-colored graphs from framed links exist: there are constructions yielding 4-colored graphs representing the 3-manifold obtained by integer Dehn surgery on a framed link in S^3, as well as 5-colored graphs representing the associated bounded 4-manifolds from Kirby diagrams. These results address the integer-surgery (and dotted-component) case, but a simple unified algorithm handling arbitrary rational surgery coefficients does not appear in fully explicit form in the standard literature, so the problem can be regarded as partially solved.

paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
original_question: Find combinatorial conditions on a colored graph representing a PL manifold M that imply specified homotopy groups of M vanish, especially conditions forcing pi_1(M) or pi_2(M) to be trivial.
self_contained_problem:
An (n+1)-colored graph is a pair (G, γ) where G is a finite multigraph (loops not allowed but multiple edges permitted) which is regular of degree n+1, and γ : E(G) → {0, 1, …, n} is an edge-coloring such that edges incident to the same vertex receive pairwise distinct colors. For each subset B ⊆ {0,…,n}, let G_B denote the subgraph of G obtained by keeping only the edges whose color lies in B; its connected components are called B-residues.

To each (n+1)-colored graph one associates an n-dimensional simplicial cell complex K(G) as follows: take an n-simplex σ_v for each vertex v of G, label the (n−1)-faces of σ_v by the colors {0,…,n}, and for each edge of G with color c joining v and w glue the c-labeled (n−1)-faces of σ_v and σ_w via the simplicial map preserving the color labels of their (n−2)-faces. The colored graph (G, γ) is said to represent a closed connected PL n-manifold M if |K(G)| is PL-homeomorphic to M; this happens iff for every color c ∈ {0,…,n}, every ({0,…,n}∖{c})-residue of G represents the standard PL (n−1)-sphere. Such (G, γ) (with K(G) having exactly n+1 vertices in the contracted case) is called a crystallization of M.

Problem. Determine purely combinatorial conditions on a colored graph (G, γ) representing a closed PL n-manifold M that imply the vanishing of specified homotopy groups π_k(M). In particular, find such combinatorial criteria on (G, γ) that force π_1(M) = 0, and, separately, criteria that force π_2(M) = 0.
status_search_result: The literature on crystallization theory provides presentations of π_1(M) from a colored graph and combinatorial invariants linked to the fundamental group, but no general combinatorial criterion forcing π_1(M) = 0 or π_2(M) = 0 from the colored graph alone appears to be known. Standard surveys present this as an active research direction without a resolution.

paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
original_question: Let M and M' be closed orientable PL 4-manifolds. For a closed PL n-manifold, define its k-complexity c_k(M) by minimizing, over all colored graphs representing M, the rank of the chain module C_{n-k}(G), and define the reduced complexity by subtracting the corresponding baseline complexity of the n-sphere. Is the reduced 4-complexity additive under connected sum, namely does c_tilde_4(M # M') = c_tilde_4(M) + c_tilde_4(M') hold?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A colored graph of dimension n+1 is a pair (G, γ) where G = (V(G), E(G)) is a finite multigraph (loops forbidden) which is regular of degree n+1, and γ : E(G) → {0,1,…,n} is an edge-coloring such that distinct edges sharing a vertex have distinct colors. Such a graph has an associated n-dimensional pseudocomplex K(G): take an n-simplex σ_v for each vertex v ∈ V(G), labeled at its vertices by {0,1,…,n}, and glue σ_v to σ_w along the (n−1)-face opposite to the vertex labeled c whenever v and w are joined by an edge colored c. The colored graph (G, γ) is said to represent the closed PL n-manifold M if |K(G)| is PL-homeomorphic to M; every closed PL n-manifold admits such a representing colored graph.

For each integer k with 0 ≤ k ≤ n, let C_{n−k}(G) be the free abelian group generated by the (n−k)-dimensional simplices of K(G) (equivalently, the (k+1)-residues of (G, γ) of an appropriate type), and let rk C_{n−k}(G) denote its rank. Define the k-complexity of a closed PL n-manifold M by
    c_k(M) = min { rk C_{n−k}(G) : (G, γ) is a colored graph representing M }.
Let S^n denote the n-sphere, and define the reduced k-complexity by
    c̃_k(M) = c_k(M) − c_k(S^n).

Connected sum of two closed orientable PL n-manifolds M and M' is denoted M # M'.

Problem. Let M and M' be closed orientable PL 4-manifolds. Determine whether the reduced 4-complexity is additive under connected sum, that is, whether
    c̃_4(M # M') = c̃_4(M) + c̃_4(M')
holds for every such pair (M, M').
status_search_result: Web searches surface related results on additivity of regular genus and on gem-complexity / k-complexity invariants of 4-manifolds via crystallizations (notably work of Casali–Cristofori), where additivity is established only under restrictive hypotheses such as the existence of (weak) semi-simple crystallizations. No source verifies the conjectured additivity of the reduced 4-complexity under connected sum in full generality, and it continues to be stated as a conjecture; we therefore record it as open.

paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
original_question: Closed 3-manifolds of Heegaard genus two can be represented by 4-colored graphs constructed from six positive integers arranged as (n_1, h_1; n_2, h_2; n_3, h_3). Determine the relations between two such 6-tuples that make their colored graphs represent the same 3-manifold, and classify the homeomorphism types of Heegaard genus two 3-manifolds in terms of these representing 6-tuples.
self_contained_problem:
Background. A 4-colored graph is a finite multigraph $\Gamma=(V(\Gamma),E(\Gamma))$ together with an edge-coloring $\gamma:E(\Gamma)\to\{0,1,2,3\}$ such that any two edges meeting at a common vertex have distinct colors (in particular, $\Gamma$ is 4-regular). Such a graph determines a 3-dimensional pseudocomplex $K(\Gamma)$ by associating to each vertex a tetrahedron, identifying $i$-faces of two tetrahedra whenever the corresponding vertices are joined by an edge of color $i$, and the topological space $|K(\Gamma)|$ is called the geometric realization. A 4-colored graph $\Gamma$ is said to represent a closed 3-manifold $M^3$ if $|K(\Gamma)|\cong M^3$.

It is known that every closed orientable 3-manifold of Heegaard genus at most two can be represented by a 4-colored graph constructed from a 6-tuple of positive integers
$$(n_1,h_1;\,n_2,h_2;\,n_3,h_3),$$
according to the following standard construction: for each $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ one builds an elementary "block" depending on the parameters $(n_i,h_i)$, and the three blocks are assembled using the colors $\{0,1,2,3\}$ to obtain a 4-colored graph $\Gamma(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3)$ whose associated pseudocomplex is a closed 3-manifold of Heegaard genus $\le 2$.

Problem. 
(a) Determine an explicit set of moves/relations on 6-tuples $(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3)$ of positive integers such that two such 6-tuples give rise to 4-colored graphs representing the same closed 3-manifold (up to homeomorphism) if and only if they are related by a finite sequence of these moves.

(b) Using (a), give a complete classification of the homeomorphism types of closed orientable 3-manifolds of Heegaard genus at most two in terms of equivalence classes of 6-tuples under these relations.
status_search_result: Partial progress exists: a G-equivalence relation on 6-tuples is known to preserve the represented genus-two 3-manifold, and catalogues of prime genus-two 3-manifolds of small complexity (e.g. 78 prime 3-manifolds of complexity ≤ 21) have been compiled. However, a complete set of moves giving a sufficient and necessary equivalence, together with a full homeomorphism classification in terms of 6-tuples, does not appear to have been established. The problem appears to remain open in its full generality.

paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
original_question: For a Heegaard genus two 3-manifold represented by a colored graph arising from a 6-tuple of integers (n_1, h_1; n_2, h_2; n_3, h_3), write a finite presentation of its fundamental group directly in terms of that 6-tuple.
self_contained_problem:
Background. A crystallisation of a closed connected 3-manifold $M$ is a 4-edge-coloured graph $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ with $\gamma:E(\Gamma)\to\{0,1,2,3\}$ such that edges of each colour form a perfect matching, $\Gamma$ is regular of degree 4, and the dual ball complex of $(\Gamma,\gamma)$ is a pseudo-triangulation of $M$ with exactly one vertex of each colour. Casali and Grasselli showed that every closed orientable 3-manifold of Heegaard genus at most two can be encoded by a 6-tuple of nonnegative integers
$$(n_1,h_1;\,n_2,h_2;\,n_3,h_3)$$
that determines a crystallisation $\Gamma(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3)$ of the manifold together with a genus-two Heegaard splitting; the integers $n_i$ control the lengths of the three "arc systems" of the crystallisation and the integers $h_i$ are shift parameters.

Problem. Produce an explicit finite presentation
$$\pi_1\bigl(M(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3)\bigr)=\langle\,x,y\mid R_1(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3),\,R_2(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3)\,\rangle$$
of the fundamental group of the closed 3-manifold $M(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3)$ associated to such an admissible 6-tuple, in which the generators and the relators are written as explicit words determined directly by the six integers $n_1,h_1,n_2,h_2,n_3,h_3$ (without invoking an algorithm applied to the crystallisation in each individual case).
status_search_result: Searches reveal that genus-two 3-manifolds encoded by admissible 6-tuples have been catalogued and their fundamental group presentations computed case-by-case via Gagliardi's algorithm applied to the crystallisation, but no closed-form 2-generator 2-relator presentation expressed uniformly in terms of the six parameters appears to be available. The problem's status as of the latest accessible literature is not clearly resolved.

paper_title: On some open problems of Radu
original_question: In the same generalized probabilistic contraction setting, let alpha, beta, and gamma be the control functions used in the condition F_{f(x),f(y)}(alpha(t)) >= beta(F_{x,y}(t)), with gamma(s)=max(alpha(s),1-beta(1-s)). When the triangular norm T governing the Menger-space structure is replaced by an arbitrary Archimedean triangular norm, what conditions on alpha, beta, and gamma are appropriate to obtain a fixed point result?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(S,\mathcal{F},T)$ be a Menger probabilistic metric space, where $S$ is a nonempty set, $\mathcal{F}:S\times S\to\Delta^+$ assigns to each pair $(x,y)$ a distribution function $F_{x,y}\in\Delta^+$ (with $\Delta^+$ the set of left-continuous nondecreasing functions $F:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]$ satisfying $F(0)=0$ and $\sup_{t\ge 0}F(t)=1$), and $T:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to[0,1]$ is a triangular norm, in such a way that the usual Menger axioms hold:
(i) $F_{x,y}=H_0$ if and only if $x=y$, where $H_0(t)=0$ for $t\le 0$ and $H_0(t)=1$ for $t>0$;
(ii) $F_{x,y}=F_{y,x}$;
(iii) $F_{x,z}(s+t)\ge T(F_{x,y}(s),F_{y,z}(t))$ for all $x,y,z\in S$ and $s,t\ge 0$.

Recall that a triangular norm $T$ is called Archimedean if it is continuous and satisfies $T(a,a)<a$ for every $a\in(0,1)$.

Let $\alpha,\beta:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be control functions, and define
$$\gamma(s)=\max\bigl(\alpha(s),\,1-\beta(1-s)\bigr).$$
A mapping $f:S\to S$ is called a generalized probabilistic $(\alpha,\beta)$-contraction if for all $x,y\in S$ and all $t>0$,
$$F_{f(x),f(y)}(\alpha(t))\ge \beta\bigl(F_{x,y}(t)\bigr).$$

Problem. Assume $T$ is an arbitrary Archimedean triangular norm. Determine appropriate conditions on the control functions $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$ that guarantee that every generalized probabilistic $(\alpha,\beta)$-contraction $f:S\to S$ on a complete Menger space $(S,\mathcal{F},T)$ admits a (unique) fixed point.
category_tag: probabilistic metric spaces and fixed points
status_search_result: Web search reveals a substantial literature extending probabilistic contraction principles in Menger spaces under various t-norm classes (Archimedean, H-type, Dombi, Aczél–Alsina, Sugeno–Weber families) with control functions, including works by Hadžić, Pap, Mihet, and Radu. However, no source was found that explicitly settles the precise question of identifying optimal conditions on the triple $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ ensuring a fixed point for an arbitrary Archimedean t-norm; the question appears to remain a topic of ongoing research, so its status is unclear.

paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
context_brief: Finite-element convergence for quasi-isometric variational maps
original_question: For the quasi-isometric variational principle whose feasible condition is det grad y > t Phi(det grad y, grad y) almost everywhere with t>0, for which broad classes of boundary data and solutions can one prove global uniqueness of the minimizer and convergence of finite-element approximations, beyond the smooth near-identity regime where an implicit-function-theorem argument is expected to apply?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega, \Omega^* \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ ($d=2$ or $3$) be bounded Lipschitz domains, and let $y:\Omega \to \Omega^*$ be a mapping in a suitable Sobolev space $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d)$ subject to prescribed boundary data $y|_{\partial\Omega} = y_0$. Consider a quasi-isometric variational principle in which one minimizes a polyconvex stored-energy functional
$$ I[y] = \int_\Omega F(\nabla y, \det \nabla y)\, dx $$
over the admissible class
$$ \mathcal{A}_t = \{\, y \in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d) : y|_{\partial\Omega} = y_0,\ \det \nabla y(x) > t\,\Phi(\det \nabla y(x), \nabla y(x)) \text{ a.e. in } \Omega \,\}, $$
where $t > 0$ is a fixed parameter and $\Phi:\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}^{d\times d} \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is a continuous function chosen so that the constraint guarantees a uniform bilipschitz (quasi-isometry) bound on $y$ with a constant depending only on $t$.

For this constrained variational problem, identify broad classes of admissible boundary data $y_0$ and corresponding minimizers $y^*$ for which one can rigorously establish:
(a) global uniqueness of the minimizer of $I$ over $\mathcal{A}_t$, and
(b) convergence (in an appropriate norm, with explicit rates if possible) of conforming finite-element approximations $y_h^*$ minimizing the discretized functional over a piecewise-polynomial subspace of $\mathcal{A}_t$, as the mesh size $h \to 0$,

beyond the regime of smooth boundary data with near-identity solutions, where uniqueness and convergence follow from a standard implicit-function-theorem perturbation argument.
status_search_result: Searches indicate that convergence of iterations to stationary points has been proven for polyconvex and quasi-isometric functionals, and existence/uniqueness has been studied for restricted problems (volume and smoothness), but a general global-uniqueness and finite-element-convergence theory beyond the near-identity / smooth regime does not appear to have been established. The question is posed explicitly as an open problem and no subsequent work clearly resolving it was found.

Call $y$ quasi-isometric if its local metric distortion is uniformly controlled — for example, if $y$ is differentiable a.e. and the singular values of $

$$\det 
abla y(x) \;>\; t\,\Phi igl(\det 
abla y(x),\,
abla y(x) igr) \qquad 	ext{for a.e. } x\in\Omega.$$
Question: does there exist a sequence $\{y_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ of locally invertible piecewise-affine mappings $y_k:\Omega	o\mathbb{R}^n$ (each affine on the cells of some simplicial subdivision of $\Omega$) such that $y_k 	o y$ in an appropriate function-space topology (e.g.\ uniform convergence together with convergence of gradients in $L^p$)? paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
original_question: For surface grid generation, how can a discrete variational principle be made invariant under the choice of surface parameterization, including non-smooth parameterizations, and what discrete analogue of the finite-element patch test should replace the usual finite-element patch-test condition for spatial mappings?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a (possibly non-smooth) surface admitting parameterizations $\mathbf{r}: \Omega 	o S$, where $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is a parameter domain. A surface-grid generation method assigns to such a parameterization a discrete grid on $S$ obtained as the minimizer of some discrete functional $F_h(\mathbf{x}_1,\dots,\mathbf{x}_N; \mathbf{r})$ defined on the nodal positions of a triangulation (or quadrangulation) of $\Omega$ pulled back to $S$.

Formulate a discrete variational principle for surface grid generation with the following two properties:

(a) Parameterization invariance. For any two parameterizations $\mathbf{r}_1: \Omega_1 	o S$ and $\mathbf{r}_2: \Omega_2 	o S$ of the same surface $S$, related by a (possibly non-smooth, e.g. only Lipschitz or piecewise smooth) change of coordinates $\varphi: \Omega_1 	o \Omega_2$ with $\mathbf{r}_1 = \mathbf{r}_2 \circ \varphi$, the set of optimal grids on $S$ produced by minimizing $F_h$ is the same; equivalently, $F_h$ depends only on the intrinsic geometric data on $S$ and not on the choice of $\mathbf{r}$.

(b) Discrete patch test. State and justify a discrete analogue of the finite-element patch test, suitable for grids viewed as discrete spatial mappings $\mathbf{x}_h: \Omega 	o S$, which replaces the standard finite-element patch-test condition (exact reproduction of affine functions on a patch of elements) by an appropriate condition for the discrete grid mapping. The condition should guarantee consistency of the discrete variational principle with its continuous counterpart in the limit of mesh refinement, in a manner compatible with property (a).

Provide an explicit construction of such a functional $F_h$, prove that it satisfies (a) under the stated class of parameterization changes, and formulate and verify the corresponding discrete patch-test condition in (b).
category_tag: discrete variational principles for surface grids
status_search_result: No specific resolution of this problem could be located. It is posed as an open problem in a survey on variational grid generation, and there is no clear evidence in the literature of a discrete variational principle for surface grids that is provably invariant under non-smooth parameterizations together with a fully formulated discrete-mapping analogue of the finite-element patch test.

paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
context_brief: Need for realizing polyhedral metrics as polyhedra
original_question: When a suitable polyhedral metric is available for the variational grid problem, is it mathematically or computationally necessary to realize that metric by an actual polyhedron, or is it enough to run numerical simulation and minimization directly on manifolds with polyhedral metrics?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. In variational grid generation one seeks a mapping (a grid) from a parameter domain into a target region by minimizing a functional whose integrand depends on the Jacobian of the mapping and on a prescribed Riemannian or polyhedral "control" metric g that encodes the desired local size, shape, and orientation of grid cells. Suppose that the control metric g produced (or required) by such a variational principle is a polyhedral metric on a manifold M, i.e. a metric obtained by gluing finitely many Euclidean simplices along isometries of their faces, so that (M, g) is a flat manifold with conical singularities concentrated on a codimension-2 set.

By a classical theorem of Alexandrov, every polyhedral metric of nonnegative curvature on the 2-sphere can be realized as the induced intrinsic metric on the boundary of a convex polytope in Euclidean 3-space; analogous realization questions exist in higher dimensions and for metrics of mixed curvature signs.

Problem. Decide whether, for the purposes of carrying out numerical simulation and minimization of variational grid-generation functionals with a polyhedral control metric g, it is mathematically or computationally necessary to first construct an isometric realization of (M, g) as an actual polyhedron (e.g. embedded or immersed in some Euclidean space) before performing the optimization, or whether one can equivalently and rigorously formulate and solve the variational problem intrinsically on the abstract manifold-with-polyhedral-metric (M, g) without ever producing such a realization. Provide either:
(a) a proof that an intrinsic formulation on (M, g) is sufficient — including a precise definition of the discrete variational functional on (M, g), an existence/convergence theory for its minimizers, and algorithms that operate solely on the combinatorial-metric data of (M, g); or
(b) a proof that some essential analytic or computational obstruction forces one to realize (M, g) as a polyhedron, identifying the obstruction explicitly.
category_tag: Variational grid generation with polyhedral metrics
status_search_result: A literature search reveals continuing work on variational grid generation with control metrics and on variational realization of polyhedral metrics (e.g., Bobenko–Izmestiev for Alexandrov's theorem, and discrete uniformization for ideal hyperbolic polyhedra), but no source was found that conclusively settles whether realizing the polyhedral control metric as an actual polyhedron is necessary, or whether intrinsic minimization on the manifold-with-polyhedral-metric suffices for variational grid generation. The question therefore appears to remain unresolved in the published literature.
