paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: For orthogonal term-rewriting systems, is the decision problem for strong sequentiality NP-complete?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A term-rewriting system (TRS) consists of a signature of function symbols (each with a fixed arity), a countable set of variables, and a finite set of rewrite rules l → r, where l and r are terms built from the signature and variables, l is not a variable, and every variable occurring in r also occurs in l. A TRS is left-linear if no variable occurs more than once in any left-hand side l. Two rules l₁ → r₁ and l₂ → r₂ (renamed apart) are said to overlap if there is a non-variable position p in l₁ such that l₁|_p and l₂ unify, except for the trivial overlap of a rule with itself at the root position. A TRS is orthogonal if it is left-linear and has no overlaps.

Let Ω be a fresh constant symbol denoting "unknown". Define a partial order ⊑ on terms over the extended signature by Ω ⊑ t for every term t, and f(s₁,…,s_n) ⊑ f(t₁,…,t_n) whenever s_i ⊑ t_i for all i. A position p in a term t (with t|_p = Ω) is called an index of t (with respect to a TRS R) if every term t' with t ⊑ t' that is a redex of R (i.e., matches some left-hand side at the root) has t'|_p ≠ Ω. A redex scheme is a left-hand side with all variables replaced by Ω. An orthogonal TRS R is called strongly sequential if every term t containing Ω that has a redex above it in some reduct admits an index, where indices are computed using the redex schemes only (a syntactic, decidable approximation due to Huet and Lévy).

The decision problem STRONG-SEQUENTIALITY takes as input a finite orthogonal TRS R and asks whether R is strongly sequential. This problem is known to be decidable.

Question. Determine whether STRONG-SEQUENTIALITY for orthogonal term-rewriting systems is NP-complete.
status_search_result: The exact complexity classification of deciding strong sequentiality for orthogonal term rewriting systems is listed among the RTA List of Open Problems. While decidability is known (Huet-Lévy) and certain related variants admit EXPTIME algorithms, no published result establishes NP-completeness (or rules it out). The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: For ground, variable-free term-rewriting systems, what is the complexity of deciding confluence?
self_contained_problem:
A ground term-rewriting system over a finite signature Σ is a finite set R of rewrite rules ℓ → r where ℓ and r are variable-free (ground) terms in T(Σ). The one-step rewrite relation →_R on T(Σ) is defined by s →_R t iff t is obtained from s by replacing some subterm occurrence equal to ℓ by r for some rule ℓ → r ∈ R. Let →*_R denote its reflexive-transitive closure. The system R is confluent if for all terms s, t₁, t₂ ∈ T(Σ) with s →*_R t₁ and s →*_R t₂, there exists u ∈ T(Σ) such that t₁ →*_R u and t₂ →*_R u.

Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem: given as input a finite signature Σ and a finite ground term-rewriting system R over Σ, decide whether R is confluent. In particular, provide tight upper and lower complexity bounds.
status_search_result: Confluence of ground term-rewriting systems was shown decidable in polynomial time by Comon, Godoy, and Nieuwenhuis (2001), and subsequent work by Felgenhauer (2012) gave a cubic-time algorithm. Thus the question of polynomial-time decidability is resolved, with current best upper bound O(n³).

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: For conditional rewrite systems, under what syntactic restrictions does parallel rewriting enjoy subcommutativity, a strong form of confluence analogous to the subcommutativity of parallel rewriting in orthogonal term-rewriting systems?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A term rewriting system (TRS) is a set R of rewrite rules ℓ → r over terms built from a signature and a set of variables. The one-step rewrite relation →_R is defined by ℓσ →_R rσ at any position of a term. The parallel rewrite relation ⇒_R reduces a finite set of pairwise-disjoint (parallel) redex positions simultaneously. A binary relation → is called subcommutative (or has the diamond property) if whenever a → b and a → c there exists d with b → d and c → d. For an orthogonal TRS (left-linear, no critical pairs) the parallel rewrite relation ⇒_R is known to be subcommutative, which gives a strong form of confluence.

A conditional term rewriting system (CTRS) is a set of conditional rules of the form ℓ → r ⇐ s₁ ≈ t₁, …, s_n ≈ t_n, where the conditions s_i ≈ t_i are interpreted (depending on the type of CTRS, e.g., join, oriented, semi-equational, or normal) as requirements that have to hold for a rewrite step using the rule to be valid. The corresponding rewrite relation is defined inductively in levels: →_0 = ∅, and a step at level k+1 uses rules whose conditions are satisfied with respect to →_k. The parallel rewrite relation ⇒_R for a CTRS is defined analogously by contracting pairwise-disjoint parallel redexes (each licensed by the appropriate conditional inference).

Problem. Determine syntactic conditions on a conditional term rewriting system R (such as restrictions on left-linearity, on the variables occurring in the conditions and right-hand sides, on critical pairs of the underlying unconditional system, on the form of the conditions, or on the type of CTRS) under which the parallel rewrite relation ⇒_R is subcommutative, i.e. satisfies: whenever t ⇒_R u and t ⇒_R v, there exists w with u ⇒_R w and v ⇒_R w. Equivalently, characterize the classes of CTRSs for which subcommutativity of parallel rewriting holds, in analogy with the orthogonal (unconditional) case.
status_search_result: Existing literature establishes various confluence criteria for conditional term rewriting systems (level-confluence, shallow confluence, confluence modulo, etc.), but no general syntactic characterization of subcommutativity of parallel rewriting for CTRSs analogous to the orthogonal-TRS case appears to have been published. The question remains listed as an open problem and no resolution was found in the search.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
context_brief: Confluence transfer for normal conditional systems
original_question: Let R be a normal conditional term-rewriting system with conditions s ->! t, where t is a ground normal form of s, and let Rse be the corresponding semi-equational conditional rewrite system with conditions s convertible to t. Under what conditions does confluence of Rse imply confluence of R?
self_contained_problem:
A conditional term-rewriting system (CTRS) is a set R of rewrite rules of the form l → r ⇐ c, where c is a conjunction of conditions on terms s, t. Depending on how conditions are interpreted, one distinguishes:

• A semi-equational CTRS R_se, in which a condition s = t in a rule is satisfied when s and t are convertible (s ↔* t) with respect to R_se itself.

• A normal (oriented) CTRS R, in which every condition has the form s →! t with t a ground normal form, and the condition is satisfied when s rewrites in zero or more steps to t using R itself.

Given a normal CTRS R with conditions of the form s →! t (t a ground R-normal form of s), let R_se be the associated semi-equational CTRS obtained by replacing each condition s →! t by the convertibility condition s ↔* t.

A rewrite relation is confluent if whenever u →* v and u →* w, there exists a term q such that v →* q and w →* q.

Problem. Determine general syntactic or semantic conditions on R (e.g., on its rules, conditions, left-linearity, decreasingness, or termination of the underlying rewrite relation) under which confluence of R_se implies confluence of R.
status_search_result: The question of transferring confluence between semi-equational and oriented/normal conditional term rewriting systems remains an active research topic. Recent work (e.g., Lucas 2024 on confluence of conditional rewriting modulo, and modular confluence studies) provides partial results for restricted classes (orthogonal, decreasing, 2-CTRSs), but no general characterization of when confluence of R_se implies confluence of R is established. The problem appears still open in general.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: In infinitary rewriting for orthogonal term-rewriting systems, does the almost-confluence result known for strongly convergent infinite reduction sequences remain valid when infinite reduction sequences are interpreted using the more liberal Cauchy-convergence notion?
self_contained_problem:
Let R be an orthogonal term rewriting system (a first-order TRS whose rewrite rules are left-linear and have no critical pairs). Equip the set of finite and infinite terms over the signature of R with the standard metric d, where d(s,t) = 2^{-n} with n the minimal depth at which s and t differ (and d(s,t)=0 if s=t); under this metric the set of (possibly infinite) terms is a complete metric space.

A transfinite reduction sequence is a sequence of rewrite steps (t_α →_R t_{α+1})_{α<λ} indexed by an ordinal λ. Such a sequence is:
 • Cauchy-convergent (weakly convergent) of length λ to a limit t_λ if, for every limit ordinal μ ≤ λ, the sequence (t_α)_{α<μ} converges to t_μ in the metric d;
 • strongly convergent of length λ to t_λ if it is Cauchy-convergent and, in addition, for every limit ordinal μ ≤ λ the depths of the redexes contracted at steps t_α →_R t_{α+1} tend to infinity as α → μ.

Write s ↠_R^{str} t (resp. s ↠_R^{Cau} t) to mean that there is a strongly convergent (resp. Cauchy-convergent) transfinite reduction sequence from s to t.

It is known that orthogonal TRSs satisfy the following "almost-confluence" property for strongly convergent reductions: whenever s ↠_R^{str} t_1 and s ↠_R^{str} t_2, there exist terms u_1, u_2 and a "hypercollapsing" equivalence ≈ (the equivalence on terms generated by identifying any pair of terms that can be reduced to a common term whose only redex activity sits inside hypercollapsing subterms) such that t_1 ↠_R^{str} u_1, t_2 ↠_R^{str} u_2, and u_1 ≈ u_2.

Question: Does the same almost-confluence property hold for every orthogonal TRS when ↠_R^{str} is replaced everywhere by ↠_R^{Cau}? Equivalently: for every orthogonal TRS R and all terms s, t_1, t_2 with s ↠_R^{Cau} t_1 and s ↠_R^{Cau} t_2, do there exist u_1, u_2 with t_i ↠_R^{Cau} u_i (i=1,2) and u_1 ≈ u_2?
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Endrullis, Grabmayer, Hendriks, Klop, and van Oostrom on infinitary rewriting for weakly orthogonal systems and on weak (Cauchy) convergence has clarified large parts of the question: infinitary confluence holds for weakly orthogonal TRSs without collapsing rules, but counterexamples to unique normal forms exist when collapsing rules are present, and structural results relate weakly convergent reductions in orthogonal systems to strongly convergent ones. Thus the question has been substantially resolved in the orthogonal/weakly orthogonal setting, but a single uniform "almost-confluence" statement for arbitrary orthogonal TRSs under Cauchy convergence is not stated as fully settled in a single result.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
context_brief: Derivation length for one-rule string rewriting
original_question: For a one-rule length-preserving string-rewriting, or semi-Thue, system, what is the best upper bound on the length of a derivation as a function of the length n of the initial string and the size k of the rule?
self_contained_problem:
A string-rewriting (semi-Thue) system over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ consists of a set of rewriting rules of the form $\ell 	o r$ with $\ell, r \in \Sigma^*$. A single rewriting step $u \Rightarrow v$ holds if there exist $x, y \in \Sigma^*$ and a rule $\ell 	o r$ such that $u = x\ell y$ and $v = x r y$. A derivation from a word $w_0$ is a sequence $w_0 \Rightarrow w_1 \Rightarrow \dots \Rightarrow w_m$, and its length is $m$.

Call the system length-preserving if $|\ell| = |r|$ for every rule, and one-rule if it consists of exactly one rule $\ell 	o r$. Define the size of the (unique) rule as $k = |\ell| = |r|$.

Let $D(n, k)$ denote the supremum, over all length-preserving one-rule systems whose rule has size $k$ and all starting words $w_0$ of length $n$, of the length of any terminating derivation from $w_0$.

Determine the best possible upper bound on $D(n,k)$ as a function of $n$ and $k$.
status_search_result: No closed-form best upper bound on the derivation length for arbitrary one-rule length-preserving string rewriting systems as a function of (n, k) was located in the literature. Related work (canonical automata, match-bounded systems, rational transductions for such one-rule length-preserving systems) studies structural and complexity properties but does not appear to settle a tight general bound. The problem appears to still be open.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: Can practical methods be devised for proving termination of standard conditional rewriting systems, despite the interdependence between normalization and termination in such systems?
self_contained_problem:
A conditional term rewriting system (CTRS) is a finite set of conditional rewrite rules of the form l → r ⇐ s₁ = t₁, …, sₙ = tₙ, where l, r, s_i, t_i are terms over a signature, l is not a variable, and the rewrite relation is defined by: t →_R t' iff there is a rule l → r ⇐ s₁ = t₁, …, sₙ = tₙ, a substitution σ, and a position p in t such that t|_p = lσ, t' = t[rσ]_p, and for each i, s_iσ and t_iσ rewrite to a common term using →_R (so-called "standard" or "join" CTRSs of type 3). 

Such a system is called terminating if →_R is well-founded. The intrinsic difficulty is that the definition of →_R itself depends on normalization (joinability of the conditions), which in turn depends on termination, making direct termination arguments delicate.

Problem: Develop practical, automatable methods for proving termination of standard conditional term rewriting systems, taking into account this circular interdependence between normalization and termination.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: the notion of operational termination of CTRSs has been introduced and shown equivalent to quasi-decreasingness, and characterizations via context-sensitive quasi-reductivity and unraveling transformations exist for deterministic CTRSs. A 2D Dependency Pair Framework has been developed to automate termination proofs for CTRSs. However, fully practical and complete methods for arbitrary standard (join) CTRSs remain an active research area rather than fully closed.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: For recursive path ordering with multiset and lexicographic status, is the existential fragment of the first-order theory of ordering constraints decidable when the precedence on function symbols is partial rather than total?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite signature of function symbols, each with a fixed arity, and let $\mathcal{X}$ be a countably infinite set of variables. Let $T(\Sigma,\mathcal{X})$ denote the set of first-order terms built from $\Sigma$ and $\mathcal{X}$. A precedence is a strict partial order $>_\Sigma$ on $\Sigma$ (not required to be total). To each $f\in\Sigma$ assign a status $\tau(f)\in\{\mathrm{mul},\mathrm{lex}\}$. The recursive path ordering with status $>_{\mathrm{rpo}}$ induced by $(>_\Sigma,\tau)$ is the relation on $T(\Sigma,\mathcal{X})$ defined recursively by: $s=f(s_1,\dots,s_m) >_{\mathrm{rpo}} t$ iff
1. $t=g(t_1,\dots,t_n)$ with $f >_\Sigma g$ and $s >_{\mathrm{rpo}} t_j$ for every $j$; or
2. $s_i \ge_{\mathrm{rpo}} t$ for some $i$ (where $\ge_{\mathrm{rpo}}$ is $>_{\mathrm{rpo}}$ together with syntactic equality); or
3. $t=f(t_1,\dots,t_m)$, $s >_{\mathrm{rpo}} t_j$ for every $j$, and $(s_1,\dots,s_m)$ is greater than $(t_1,\dots,t_m)$ in the multiset (resp. lexicographic) extension of $>_{\mathrm{rpo}}$ when $\tau(f)=\mathrm{mul}$ (resp. $\mathrm{lex}$).

An RPO ordering constraint is a finite conjunction of atomic constraints of the forms $u>_{\mathrm{rpo}} v$ and $u=v$, with $u,v\in T(\Sigma,\mathcal{X})$. The existential fragment of the first-order theory of $>_{\mathrm{rpo}}$ consists of formulas $\exists \bar{x}\,\varphi(\bar{x})$ where $\varphi$ is a Boolean combination of such atoms; satisfiability asks whether there exists an assignment of the variables to ground terms in $T(\Sigma)$ making the formula true.

Question: Is the existential fragment of the first-order theory of the recursive path ordering with multiset and lexicographic status decidable when the precedence $>_\Sigma$ is allowed to be an arbitrary strict partial order rather than required to be total? Equivalently, is satisfiability of RPO ordering constraints decidable for non-total precedences? (The same question is posed for the lexicographic path ordering LPO, the special case where every symbol has lexicographic status.)
status_search_result: Existing decidability/NP-completeness results for satisfiability of RPO/LPO ordering constraints (e.g., Nieuwenhuis's "RPO constraint solving is in NP" and related work) address the case of total precedences. Available sources indicate that the corresponding question for partial (non-total) precedences has not been resolved in the literature, and indeed the full first-order theory of LPO with partial precedence on a unary signature is known to be undecidable, while the existential fragment with partial precedence appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: For a non-orthogonal term-rewriting or combinatory reduction system R, suppose redexes can be mapped to a well-founded linear order so that residual redex degrees never increase and newly created redexes have strictly smaller degree than their creator. Does this decreasing-redexes property imply termination? If not, which useful subclasses still satisfy the implication?
self_contained_problem:
Let R be a (possibly non-orthogonal) term-rewriting system or combinatory reduction system. A redex in a term is an occurrence of a subterm matching the left-hand side of some rule. Given a one-step reduction t →_u t' contracting a redex u, the standard residual theory associates to every other redex v in t a (possibly empty) set of residual redexes v/u in t', and identifies certain redexes in t' as new (created) redexes that are not residuals of any redex in t.

Suppose there exists a well-founded linear order (D, <) and an assignment of a "degree" d(v) ∈ D to every redex occurrence (in every reachable term), satisfying:
(i) for every redex v and every redex u, every residual v' ∈ v/u satisfies d(v') ≤ d(v); and
(ii) every redex w in t' that is created by the contraction of u in t satisfies d(w) < d(u).

Call such an assignment a decreasing-redexes labelling, and say R has the decreasing-redexes property if such a labelling exists.

Question: Does the existence of a decreasing-redexes labelling imply that R is terminating (strongly normalizing) for arbitrary, not necessarily orthogonal, term-rewriting systems and combinatory reduction systems? If not, identify natural subclasses of non-orthogonal systems for which the decreasing-redexes property does imply termination.
status_search_result: The question of whether the decreasing-redexes condition implies termination for non-orthogonal term-rewriting and combinatory reduction systems appears in standard collections of open problems in rewriting (e.g. the RTA list of open problems) and no published resolution was found. Related work by van Oostrom on decreasing diagrams addresses confluence rather than termination, and recent literature continues to treat the non-orthogonal termination implication as unresolved. Status best classified as open.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: Can effective and implementable methods be developed to decide whether a rewrite system decreases with respect to some exponential interpretation, analogous to existing methods for polynomial interpretations?
self_contained_problem:
Let R be a finite term rewriting system over a signature Σ, where each function symbol f ∈ Σ of arity n is interpreted by a function [f] : ℕ^n → ℕ. An interpretation is called exponential if the interpretations [f] are built from constants, projections, addition, multiplication, and exponentiation x ↦ a^x (with base a ≥ 2). Each term t with variables x_1,...,x_k is then assigned a function [t] : ℕ^k → ℕ obtained by composition. The system R is said to decrease with respect to the interpretation if [ℓ](x_1,...,x_k) > [r](x_1,...,x_k) holds for all (x_1,...,x_k) ∈ ℕ^k, for every rewrite rule ℓ → r in R; this implies termination of R.

Problem: Develop an effective and implementable algorithm that, given a finite rewrite system R, decides whether there exists an exponential interpretation (in the above sense) with respect to which R decreases, analogous to the established procedures for deciding the existence of suitable polynomial interpretations. In particular, devise a mechanizable method for comparing expressions built using addition, multiplication, and exponentiation over ℕ that can serve as the core of such a decision procedure.
status_search_result: Foundational work by Lescanne and others established termination proofs via elementary (polynomial/exponential) interpretations and partial mechanization of comparison procedures, but no general effective decision method for exponential interpretations comparable to the polynomial case appears in the literature. Recent automated termination tools rely chiefly on polynomial, matrix, and related interpretations; the problem of effectively deciding decrease under exponential interpretations does not appear to have been resolved.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: What are the computational complexities of term-ordering decision problems, including comparability under recursive path ordering with a suitable precedence and lexicographic path ordering with non-total precedences or variables?
self_contained_problem:
Let Σ be a finite signature of function symbols, each with a fixed arity, and let V be a countable set of variables. Denote by T(Σ,V) the set of (first-order) terms over Σ and V. A precedence on Σ is a (strict) partial order >_Σ on Σ; it is total if it is a linear order.

Given a precedence >_Σ, the recursive path ordering (RPO) >_rpo on T(Σ,V) is defined as the smallest relation such that s = f(s_1,…,s_m) >_rpo t iff one of the following holds:
 (1) t is a variable occurring strictly in s; or
 (2) t = g(t_1,…,t_n) and either
   (a) s_i ≥_rpo t for some i, or
   (b) f >_Σ g and s >_rpo t_j for all j, or
   (c) f = g and {s_1,…,s_m} is greater than {t_1,…,t_n} in the multiset extension of >_rpo.

The lexicographic path ordering (LPO) >_lpo is defined identically except that case (c) is replaced by the lexicographic extension of >_lpo on the tuples (s_1,…,s_m) and (t_1,…,t_n) (together with s >_lpo t_j for all j).

Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problems:

(i) Given Σ, a precedence >_Σ on Σ (not necessarily total), and two terms s, t ∈ T(Σ,V), decide whether s >_rpo t.

(ii) Given Σ, a (possibly non-total) precedence >_Σ on Σ, and two terms s, t ∈ T(Σ,V) (which may contain variables), decide whether s >_lpo t.

In particular, classify each of these problems with respect to standard complexity classes (P, NP, coNP, PSPACE, etc.), determining tight upper and lower bounds.
status_search_result: Partial results are known: the constraint satisfaction / orientation problem for RPO is known to be NP-complete, and SAT-based encodings are used in practice; certain first-order theories of RPO (e.g., unary signature, total precedence) are decidable while related LPO theories have undecidability results. However, a complete and tight complexity classification for the comparability problems with non-total precedences and variables was raised as an open question in surveys of rewriting problems, and no comprehensive resolution covering all listed cases is documented in the search results.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: Is there any finite term-rewriting system, of an appropriate kind, for free lattices?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{FL}(X)$ denote the free lattice generated by a set $X$, regarded as an algebra in the signature $\{\vee, \wedge\}$ subject to the lattice axioms (idempotency, commutativity, associativity of both operations, and the two absorption laws). A term rewriting system over this signature (possibly modulo associativity and commutativity, or in some other suitable framework such as ordered, conditional, or graph rewriting) is called convergent if it is terminating and confluent, so that every term has a unique normal form. 

Question: Does there exist a finite term rewriting system, of some appropriate kind, that is convergent for the equational theory of lattices, so that the normal forms of terms over $X$ are in bijection with the elements of $\mathrm{FL}(X)$?
status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. Freese's expository writings on free lattices and on term rewrite systems for lattice theory note that, despite Whitman's canonical-form algorithm for the word problem in free lattices, no finite convergent (e.g. associative-commutative) term rewriting system for the equational theory of lattices is known, and the existence of one is still posed as an open problem.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: For an equational theory E and an ordering greater-than, is there a set of inference rules that always succeeds in computing a convergent set of rewrite rules R whenever such an R exists for the ordering, even when the ordering cannot be made total on ground terms?
self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be a set of equations over a set of terms built from a signature $\mathcal{F}$ and variables, and let $>$ be a reduction ordering on terms (i.e., a well-founded strict ordering that is closed under contexts and substitutions). A rewrite system $R$ is said to be convergent (with respect to $>$) if every rule $\ell \to r \in R$ satisfies $\ell > r$, if $R$ is confluent, and if its equational theory coincides with that of $E$ (so that every $E$-equivalence class has a unique $R$-normal form). 

Question: Does there exist a set of inference rules for completion that, given any equational theory $E$ and any reduction ordering $>$ for which some convergent rewrite system $R$ contained in $>$ presenting $E$ exists, is guaranteed to compute such an $R$? In particular, must the procedure succeed even when $>$ cannot be extended to a reduction ordering that is total on ground terms?

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: For Boolean-ring based methods for resolution-like first-order theorem proving, can more restrictive strategies be found, such as strategies using only single overlaps or only unifications of maximal atoms, while preserving completeness?
self_contained_problem:
Background. In Boolean-ring based theorem proving, first-order clauses are translated into polynomials over the Boolean ring GF(2)[X]/(x^2 − x : x ∈ X), where conjunction is multiplication, exclusive-or is addition, and atoms become indeterminates. Refutational theorem proving is then carried out by superposition-style inferences on these polynomials: given two polynomials P and Q sharing a (unifiable) atom A, one forms new polynomials by overlapping P and Q on A (after applying a most general unifier), and the goal is to derive the polynomial 1 (representing falsity). Standard completeness proofs allow "multiple overlaps" (superposing on several atoms simultaneously or considering many atom pairs) and impose only mild restrictions on which atoms may be selected.

Problem. Determine whether the following more restrictive inference strategies for Boolean-ring based resolution-like first-order theorem proving are refutationally complete:

(a) A "single-overlap" strategy, in which each inference between two polynomials P and Q is required to superpose on exactly one chosen atom (no simultaneous multi-atom overlap is permitted).

(b) A "maximal-atom unification" strategy, in which, with respect to a fixed admissible ordering on atoms, inferences are restricted to unifications of maximal atoms of the participating polynomials only.

In each case, prove completeness (every unsatisfiable set of clauses admits a derivation of 1 under the restricted strategy) or exhibit a counterexample showing incompleteness. More generally, identify and prove complete the most restrictive natural strategies of these types for Boolean-ring based first-order theorem proving.
status_search_result: Partial progress exists: a method restricting superposition to maximal atoms (extending Hsiang's N-strategy) with a completeness proof via semantic trees has been published, and a linear strategy plus O-linear/pseudo-O-linear strategies based on a partial ordering of atoms have been shown complete. Results on the unnecessity of multiple overlaps in completion theorem proving also exist. However, a definitive resolution of the general question of identifying the most restrictive complete strategies (single-overlap and maximal-atom unification combined) in the Boolean-ring setting does not appear to be fully settled in the literature found.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: Is unification modulo the theory of distributivity, with one right-distributivity axiom and one left-distributivity axiom, decidable?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the equational theory D over a signature with two binary function symbols + and *, axiomatized by the two distributivity laws
  (L)  x * (y + z) = (x * y) + (x * z),
  (R)  (x + y) * z = (x * z) + (y * z).
A unification problem modulo D is a finite system of equations s_i =? t_i (1 ≤ i ≤ n) between terms built from function symbols +, * and variables; the system is D-unifiable iff there exists a substitution σ such that σ(s_i) =_D σ(t_i) for every i, where =_D denotes equality in the equational theory generated by (L) and (R).

Question: Is the D-unifiability problem (for finite systems of such equations) decidable?

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: For associative-commutative unification, do the same or similar transformation rules known to terminate with variable replacement after every step or at the end also terminate under more flexible control strategies?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of associative–commutative (AC) unification: given two first-order terms s and t built from a signature containing one or more binary function symbols declared associative and commutative, find a complete set of substitutions σ such that sσ =_AC tσ, where =_AC denotes equality modulo the associativity and commutativity axioms of those symbols.

Standard AC-unification procedures are presented as nondeterministic transformation systems on systems of equations (e.g., variants of Stickel's algorithm and its refinements). For such transformation systems, termination has been established under restrictive control regimes, namely:
  (a) the strategy that performs a variable-replacement (instantiation) step after every transformation step, and
  (b) the strategy that defers variable replacement until the very end of the derivation.

The problem is to determine whether the same (or analogously formulated) transformation rules for AC-unification still terminate when these rigid control disciplines are loosened, i.e., when variable replacement steps may be interleaved arbitrarily with other transformation steps rather than being constrained to occur after every step or only at the end. Concretely: identify a flexible control strategy strictly more permissive than (a) and (b), and prove that every derivation of the AC-unification transformation system under this strategy is finite; or else exhibit a counterexample showing nontermination.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: For first-order formulas over trees with equality as the only predicate, can negation be effectively eliminated from any formula that is equivalent to a positive formula; equivalently, when such a formula has a finite complete set of unifiers, can that set be computed?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the free term algebra (Herbrand universe) of finite trees over a fixed signature of function symbols, with syntactic equality as the only predicate. Consider first-order formulas built from equations s = t between terms using the connectives ∧, ∨, ¬, → and the quantifiers ∀, ∃, interpreted in this algebra. Call a formula positive if it is built without the negation connective ¬.

A substitution σ is a unifier of a formula φ(x₁, …, xₙ) if σ makes φ true in the algebra of finite trees. A finite set Σ of substitutions is a complete set of unifiers of φ if every unifier of φ is an instance of some σ ∈ Σ.

Question: Is there an algorithm that, given a first-order formula φ over finite trees with equality as the only predicate such that φ is semantically equivalent to some positive formula, produces a negation-free formula equivalent to φ? Equivalently, when such a φ admits a finite complete set of unifiers, can that set be effectively computed?
status_search_result: The problem of negation elimination from first-order (syntactic) equational formulae over the algebra of finite trees has been shown to be decidable, with subsequent works refining the complexity (coNP-complete for DNF, D²p-hard for CNF). Hence the equivalent question of computing the finite complete set of unifiers when one exists has been resolved positively.

paper_title: Open problems in rewriting
original_question: For every finitary unification problem in a syntactic equational theory, can pruning or freezing rules be designed so that the derivation tree generated by syntactic unification rules becomes finite and yields a finite complete set of unifiers?
self_contained_problem:
Let E be a syntactic equational theory over a first-order term signature; that is, an equational theory for which every E-equality s =_E t admits a proof by an equational replacement at the root using an axiom of E followed by paramodulations strictly below the root. Assume further that E is finitary, meaning that for every E-unification problem Γ (a finite set of equations to be solved modulo E) there exists a finite complete set of E-unifiers, i.e. a finite set S of substitutions such that:
  (i) every σ ∈ S is an E-unifier of Γ (σ(s) =_E σ(t) for each equation s = t in Γ), and
  (ii) for every E-unifier τ of Γ there exists σ ∈ S and a substitution ρ with τ =_E ρ ∘ σ on the variables of Γ.

The standard syntactic mutation-based unification calculus for E (the system of transformation rules: Decomposition, Mutate-with-axiom, Variable elimination, etc.) produces, from Γ, a derivation tree whose leaves labelled by solved forms correspond to E-unifiers. In general this derivation tree may be infinite even when E is finitary.

Question: Can one design uniform additional control rules — of "pruning" type (discarding redundant branches that produce only unifiers subsumed elsewhere in the tree) and/or "freezing" type (temporarily blocking the application of mutation steps on certain subterms to prevent non-terminating expansions) — that, when added to the syntactic mutation calculus, guarantee for every finitary syntactic equational theory E and every E-unification problem Γ that the resulting derivation tree is finite and that its solved-form leaves form a finite complete set of E-unifiers for Γ?
status_search_result: Available literature on syntactic equational theories and mutation-based unification (Kirchner, Jouannaud, and successors) treats the computation of finite complete sets of unifiers for finitary syntactic theories as an outstanding methodological problem; no general pruning/freezing strategy guaranteeing finite derivation trees for all finitary syntactic theories was located in web search. Status appears open.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: What additional non-perturbative information about boundary and defect conformal field theories can supersymmetry provide, including through techniques such as supersymmetric localization?
self_contained_problem:
Let a boundary conformal field theory (bCFT) be a conformal field theory defined on a half-space $\mathbb{R}^{d-1}\times\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ whose stress tensor satisfies the boundary condition $T_{n\parallel}|_{\partial}=0$ preserving the conformal subgroup $SO(d-1,2)\subset SO(d,2)$; more generally, a defect conformal field theory (dCFT) is a CFT on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ together with a $p$-dimensional extended operator (defect) preserving the subgroup $SO(p,2)\times SO(d-p)$ of the conformal group. Suppose, in addition, that the bulk theory together with the boundary/defect preserves some amount of supersymmetry, in the sense that a subalgebra of a bulk superconformal algebra is preserved by the defect insertion.

Identify and quantify the non-perturbative information about such supersymmetric bCFTs and dCFTs that can be extracted by supersymmetric techniques. Concretely:

(a) Using supersymmetric localization of the path integral of the ambient theory in the presence of the boundary or defect (for example, on $S^{d}$, on a hemisphere $HS^{d}$, or on squashed/ellipsoid backgrounds), derive exact expressions for defect partition functions, defect/boundary $g$-functions, one-point functions of bulk operators, and correlation functions of defect-local operators.

(b) Determine the CFT data of the defect (defect operator spectrum, OPE coefficients of bulk-to-defect and defect-defect OPE) that can be computed exactly from these localization results, and how these may be combined with superconformal bootstrap constraints.

(c) Establish whether quantities such as the boundary/defect Weyl anomaly coefficients (e.g.\ $b$, the $a$- and $c$-type defect central charges) and the defect free energy can be obtained exactly from localization, and prove or disprove conjectured monotonicity theorems (defect $b$-theorem, defect $F$-theorem) in supersymmetric settings.

State and prove the most general such non-perturbative results, or otherwise characterize the precise limits of what supersymmetric localization can determine about bCFTs and dCFTs.
category_tag: Boundary and defect conformal field theory
status_search_result: The question is a broad research-program-level open problem about what supersymmetric techniques (in particular localization) can determine non-perturbatively about boundary and defect CFTs. Numerous partial results exist (localization computations of defect partition functions, exact one-point functions, defect central charges, and proofs of defect monotonicity theorems in specific supersymmetric setups), but no complete classification is known and the problem remains an active area of research as of 2026.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: How do double-trace interfaces in boundary or defect conformal field theory fuse with one another?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{CFT}_+$ and $\mathrm{CFT}_-$ be two large-$N$ conformal field theories in $d$ dimensions that are related by a relevant double-trace deformation: starting from a CFT containing a single-trace scalar primary $\mathcal{O}$ of scaling dimension $\Delta_-$, the deformation $\int d^d x\, \mathcal{O}^2$ triggers an RG flow whose IR endpoint is a CFT in which the corresponding operator has dimension $\Delta_+ = d - \Delta_-$. A double-trace interface is the planar codimension-one conformal interface $\mathcal{I}$ separating these two theories that is obtained by turning on the double-trace deformation only on a half-space; equivalently, it is described holographically by a bulk scalar in AdS$_{d+1}$ satisfying alternate boundary conditions on the two halves of the conformal boundary.

Given two such double-trace interfaces $\mathcal{I}_1$ and $\mathcal{I}_2$, placed on parallel planes at separation $\varepsilon \to 0$, describe the fusion product
$$\mathcal{I}_1 \star \mathcal{I}_2 := \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \mathcal{I}_1(x_d = \varepsilon)\, \mathcal{I}_2(x_d = 0),$$
including the renormalization of local interface operators and counterterms, the resulting conformal interface (or composite defect) between the appropriate pair of CFTs, the leading-$1/N$ fusion algebra they generate, the spectrum of operators on the fused interface, and the change in the interface contribution to the sphere partition function (the $g$-factor in $d=2$).
status_search_result: General frameworks for the fusion of conformal interfaces/defects exist (e.g. fusion of conformal interfaces in 2d, effective theory for fusion of conformal defects, and fusion of conformal defects in interacting theories). Recent work on RG interfaces from double-trace deformations (2024) addresses aspects of fusion in the holographic large-$N$ setting, but a complete computation of the fusion of two double-trace interfaces (with full renormalized operator spectrum and $g$-factor change) does not appear to have been carried out in full generality, so the question is partially solved.

original_question: Can one develop a more effective collective-coordinate description of sine-Gordon scattering off a non-integrable boundary, despite the fact that the boundary interaction excites many additional modes?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the sine-Gordon model on the half-line $x \le 0$ for a real scalar field $\phi(x,t)$ with bulk Lagrangian density
$$\mathcal{L} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_t\phi)^2 - \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x\phi)^2 - \frac{m^2}{\beta^2}\bigl(1-\cos(\beta\phi)\bigr),$$
supplemented at $x=0$ by a boundary potential
$$V_B(\phi(0,t)) = -M\cos\!\bigl(\tfrac{\beta}{2}(\phi(0,t)-\phi_0)\bigr),$$
giving the Robin-type boundary condition $\partial_x\phi(0,t) = -\tfrac{M\beta}{2}\sin\!\bigl(\tfrac{\beta}{2}(\phi(0,t)-\phi_0)\bigr)$. For generic values of the boundary parameters $(M,\phi_0)$ the boundary breaks the bulk integrability, and reflection of an incoming (anti)kink generically excites infinitely many radiative and breather modes in addition to producing reflected kinks/antikinks.

Develop an effective finite-dimensional collective-coordinate description of kink–boundary scattering in this non-integrable boundary sine-Gordon system: that is, construct a moduli space of field configurations parametrized by a finite set of coordinates (capturing kink position, possibly boundary-localized degrees of freedom, and the dominant excited modes), together with an induced metric and effective potential, such that the resulting reduced dynamics accurately reproduces the qualitative and quantitative features (reflection coefficients, kink/antikink/breather production thresholds as functions of incoming velocity and boundary parameters) of the full PDE dynamics, despite the proliferation of modes excited at the boundary.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., on sine-Gordon with Robin boundary conditions) has established the rich phenomenology of antikink reflection into kinks, antikinks, and multiple breathers in the non-integrable boundary case, and collective-coordinate methods have been applied successfully to related bulk problems (double sine-Gordon, modified sine-Gordon, kink-impurity interactions). However, no fully effective collective-coordinate reduction tailored to the boundary sine-Gordon problem that captures the many excited modes has been published; the problem appears still open.

original_question: What is the correct quantum-field-theoretic description of the sine-Gordon model with a non-integrable boundary, and can techniques from quantum integrability still be adapted to study how integrability breaks down in that setting?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the sine-Gordon model on the half-line $x \le 0$ with Lagrangian density
$$\mathcal{L} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_t\phi)^2 - \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x\phi)^2 - \frac{m^2}{\beta^2}\big(1-\cos(\beta\phi)\big),$$
subject at $x=0$ to a non-integrable boundary condition, for instance a Robin-type condition
$$\partial_x\phi(0,t) + k\,\phi(0,t) = 0$$
with generic real parameter $k$, or more generally a boundary potential $V_B(\phi(0,t))$ that does not fall into the integrable Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov family $V_B(\phi)=M\cos\!\big(\tfrac{\beta}{2}(\phi-\phi_0)\big)$.

Determine to what extent techniques developed for quantum boundary integrability—such as the boundary Yang–Baxter (reflection) equation, the boundary bootstrap, form-factor expansions, and the truncated conformal space approach—can be adapted to compute observables (reflection amplitudes, boundary energies, boundary form factors) in this non-integrable setting, and characterize quantitatively how integrability is broken (e.g., production probabilities for inelastic processes, deviations from factorized reflection, decay of boundary bound states).
status_search_result: Classical and semi-classical analyses of the sine-Gordon model with non-integrable Robin boundary conditions have appeared (e.g., studies of soliton reflection with intricate resonance structure), and the corresponding quantum field theory has been highlighted as an open direction. No complete QFT description of the non-integrable boundary sine-Gordon model, nor a systematic adaptation of integrability techniques to quantify its breaking, appears to be established in the literature.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: Can the relevant boundary conditions for the free fermion and for the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3 be derived directly from first principles, or alternatively by adapting the methods of Novak and Runkel?
self_contained_problem:
Consider two two-dimensional conformal field theories: (i) the free fermion theory of central charge c = 1/2, and (ii) the super-Virasoro minimal model commonly denoted SVIR3, i.e. the third unitary N=1 superconformal minimal model with central charge c = 7/10 (the superconformal description of the tri-critical Ising model). Each of these is a local fermionic CFT, and each admits a finite collection of conformal boundary conditions that preserve the relevant chiral symmetry (Virasoro/super-Virasoro plus fermion parity), as well as conformal defects which, via the folding trick, correspond to boundary conditions in the tensor square of the theory.

Problem. Derive, from first principles of (boundary) conformal field theory — for example by solving the sewing/Cardy-Lewellen consistency constraints, classifying module categories over the relevant chiral vertex superalgebra, or applying a defect-construction procedure analogous to the one realizing conformal defects in a fermionic CFT as boundary conditions in the folded theory (i.e. an extension to the super/fermionic setting of the method that constructs new conformal, non-topological and non-factorised defects of a rational CFT as boundary states of its tensor-square) — the complete set of conformal boundary conditions (boundary states) for:

(a) the free fermion CFT (c = 1/2), and
(b) the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3 (c = 7/10),

including in each case the explicit boundary state expansions in terms of Ishibashi states and the verification that the resulting open-string spectra (annulus partition functions / NIM-rep coefficients) are non-negative integers compatible with modular covariance and with fermion-number selection rules.
status_search_result: The problem of deriving the full set of conformal boundary conditions for the free fermion and for the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3 from first principles (or by adapting Novak–Runkel's folding-trick construction of defects-as-boundaries in fermionic CFTs) does not appear to have been carried out in the literature. Novak–Runkel's framework treats defects in the tri-critical Ising / SVIR3 model and the related "Fermionic CFTs and classifying algebras" program gives partial classifications, but a first-principles derivation of these specific boundary conditions has not been reported. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: For the SO(5)-symmetric D3-D7-brane defect conformal field theory, can one find a closed tree-level formula for one-point functions when the full scalar SO(6) sector is considered, beyond the already understood chiral-primary case?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the defect conformal field theory obtained as the holographic dual of the SO(5)-symmetric D3–D7 probe-brane system with non-vanishing instanton number, in which a codimension-one defect breaks the bulk N=4 super Yang–Mills R-symmetry SO(6) to SO(5). On the gauge-theory side, single-trace scalar operators in the full SO(6) scalar sector are built from the six real scalars of N=4 SYM and, at one loop, are eigenstates of an integrable SO(6) spin chain. Their tree-level one-point functions in the presence of the defect are computed as overlaps of Bethe eigenstates of the SO(6) spin chain with a definite matrix-product state encoding the classical solution sourced by the D7 brane.

Problem: Determine whether there exists a closed-form tree-level expression (for instance, a determinant-type or factorized formula in terms of Bethe roots, magnon momenta, and the instanton number k) giving the one-point function of an arbitrary Bethe eigenstate of the full SO(6) scalar sector in this SO(5)-symmetric D3–D7 defect CFT, valid for any number of excitations and for general k, thereby extending the known closed-form result for chiral-primary (BPS) operators to all non-protected scalar operators.
status_search_result: Tree-level one-point functions in the SO(5)-symmetric D3–D7 dCFT have been computed for chiral primaries and, in the non-protected SO(6) scalar sector, only for operators with a small number of excitations, where closed expressions in terms of Bethe roots are available. The matrix product state has been shown to satisfy an integrability criterion, but a general closed-form expression for the overlap with arbitrary SO(6) Bethe eigenstates (unlike the D3–D5 case, where a determinant formula was obtained) has not been found. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: How should one incorporate finite-string-tension corrections, i.e. 1/λ corrections, into the large-N, large-'t Hooft-coupling analysis of four-point correlators in AdS5 × S5 supergravity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider type IIB superstring theory on the background AdS_5 × S^5 with N units of five-form flux, in the planar/large-N limit at large 't Hooft coupling λ. The leading two-derivative supergravity approximation governs the holographic four-point correlation functions of single-trace half-BPS superconformal primary operators (e.g. the stress-tensor multiplet superprimaries) in the dual N=4 super Yang-Mills theory; these correlators have been computed in supergravity at leading order in 1/N^2 and in the strict λ → ∞ limit.

Finite-string-tension effects correspond to a systematic expansion in inverse powers of λ (equivalently, in α'/L^2 where L is the AdS radius), generated by higher-derivative corrections to the type IIB effective action (such as the α'^3 R^4 term and its supersymmetric completions).

Problem. Develop a systematic procedure to incorporate the 1/λ (finite-string-tension) corrections to the large-N, large-λ supergravity computation of four-point correlation functions of half-BPS single-trace operators in AdS_5 × S^5. Specifically:
(a) Determine, to a given order in 1/λ, the form of the corresponding tree-level Mellin amplitude (or position-space correlator) that is consistent with superconformal Ward identities, crossing symmetry, and the analytic/polynomial-degree growth expected from higher-derivative bulk vertices.
(b) Fix any remaining undetermined coefficients in this expansion using independent input (e.g. localization on S^4, integrated correlator constraints, or the flat-space limit reproducing the Virasoro–Shapiro amplitude).
(c) Extract the resulting predictions for the anomalous dimensions and OPE coefficients of double-trace operators at each order in 1/λ.
category_tag: Holographic correlators and stringy corrections in AdS/CFT
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on incorporating 1/λ (stringy α') corrections into half-BPS four-point correlators in AdS_5 × S^5. Tree-level corrections have been determined up to high orders (e.g. through O(α'^7)) by combining superconformal symmetry, crossing, the flat-space Virasoro–Shapiro limit, and constraints from supersymmetric localization (integrated correlators), with results extended to genus expansion in 1/N^2. The general problem of resumming all 1/λ corrections—i.e. constructing the full Virasoro–Shapiro amplitude in AdS_5 × S^5—remains open, though concrete systematic frameworks have been developed.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: Can the bootstrap analysis of conformal field theories on real projective space be extended to holographic or otherwise strongly coupled theories such as N = 4 super Yang-Mills theory or Liouville theory, and if so does it agree with the corresponding holographic predictions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a conformal field theory on the real projective space $\mathbb{RP}^d$, viewed as the quotient of $S^d$ (or equivalently $\mathbb{R}^d \cup \{\infty\}$) by the antipodal involution. On such a non-orientable background, one-point functions of bulk primary operators are generically nonzero and two-point functions admit a crossing equation derived by comparing the bulk OPE channel with the image (mirror) channel through the parity-identification. This setup defines the "$\mathbb{RP}^d$ bootstrap" for CFT data $\{a_\mathcal{O}\}$ (one-point coefficients) and operator dimensions.

Problem: Extend the $\mathbb{RP}^d$ crossing/bootstrap analysis to strongly coupled or holographic conformal field theories — in particular to four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory on $\mathbb{RP}^4$ (with an appropriate $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauging including charge conjugation) and to two-dimensional Liouville theory on $\mathbb{RP}^2$. Determine the one-point functions and the two-point functions of half-BPS (respectively primary) operators on $\mathbb{RP}^d$ in these theories, and compare the results with the predictions obtained from the dual gravitational/holographic description (for $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, type IIB supergravity on the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ quotient of $AdS_5 \times S^5$). Decide whether the bootstrap results agree with the holographic predictions.
category_tag: conformal bootstrap on real projective space
status_search_result: Subsequent work has carried out exactly this program for $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM on $\mathbb{RP}^4$: a holographic dual via a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ quotient of $AdS_5\times S^5$ (with charge-conjugation gauging) has been constructed, and bootstrap techniques have been used to determine two-point functions of 1/2-BPS operators at leading order in the large central charge expansion, with agreement to holographic predictions. The Liouville theory side appears less developed in the literature. Thus the question is partially resolved for $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM but remains open for Liouville.

original_question: Is every quasi Riemann surface Q isomorphic to the space D_int_0(Σ) of integral 0-currents on some ordinary two-dimensional conformal space Σ with the same Jacobian, and if so how can that isomorphism be constructed concretely?
self_contained_problem:
Define a quasi Riemann surface Q to be a metric abelian topological group equipped with the additional structure (intersection form, complex structure on its middle-dimensional homology, and graded spaces of integral j-currents for j = 0, 1, 2, 3 with their weak metrics) abstracting the properties of the spaces of integral 0-currents on a 2-dimensional conformal manifold. To any 2-dimensional conformal space Σ, associate the abelian topological group D_int^0(Σ) of integral 0-currents of finite total mass on Σ, equipped with its natural weak metric, and define the Jacobian J(Q) (respectively J(Σ)) to be the complex torus built from the middle-dimensional homology together with its complex structure.

Question: Is it true that every quasi Riemann surface Q is isomorphic, as a quasi Riemann surface, to D_int^0(Σ) for some 2-dimensional conformal space Σ whose ordinary Jacobian J(Σ) is isomorphic to J(Q)? If so, give a concrete construction of Σ from Q and of the isomorphism Q ≅ D_int^0(Σ).
status_search_result: The conjecture is stated in Daniel Friedan's papers on quasi Riemann surfaces (2017) as an open conjecture, and no proof or counterexample appears in the literature. It remains an unresolved conjecture used as motivation in subsequent discussions.

paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
original_question: When fields Φ(ξ) on quasi Riemann surfaces are restricted to very small defects ξ that look pointlike inside the ambient 2n-dimensional manifold, do the resulting ordinary local quantum fields define genuinely new local quantum field theories in 2n dimensions?
self_contained_problem:
Let M be a smooth oriented conformal manifold of even dimension 2n, and let Q = Q(M) denote its associated quasi Riemann surface, i.e. the space of integral (n-1)-currents (or, more generally, a suitable completion thereof) in M, equipped with the structure that generalizes the classical Riemann-surface picture for n = 1. Suppose one has a quantum field theory on Q whose fundamental fields Φ(ξ) are indexed by points ξ ∈ Q, generalizing the assignment of fields to points on a Riemann surface.

Consider the restriction of Φ(ξ) to "tiny" defects ξ ∈ Q—configurations that are, from the point of view of M, supported in arbitrarily small neighborhoods of single points of M, so that in the limit they behave as ordinary point insertions in M. The restricted operators then define local fields on the 2n-dimensional manifold M, and via their correlation functions produce a candidate local quantum field theory on M.

Question: Do such restricted fields define genuinely new local quantum field theories on a 2n-dimensional manifold M (for n ≥ 2)—that is, theories not equivalent to any previously known local QFT in 2n dimensions—and, more strongly, can one exhibit constructive examples and characterize the class of 2n-dimensional local QFTs that arise in this way?
category_tag: quasi Riemann surfaces and defect QFT
status_search_result: The construction of quasi Riemann surfaces and the conjecture that fields restricted to pointlike defects produce new 2n-dimensional local QFTs are explicitly posed as speculative open questions in the program on quasi Riemann surfaces. No published construction or proof addressing whether genuinely new 2n-dimensional local QFTs arise this way has been located; the topic remains an open research direction.

paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
context_brief: Adam conjecture for Euler oriented graphs
original_question: For an Euler oriented graph, meaning a connected oriented graph in which every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree, that contains at least one directed cycle, is there always an arc whose reversal decreases the total number of directed cycles?
self_contained_problem:
Call a directed multigraph $D=(V,A)$ an Euler oriented graph if (i) $D$ is connected, (ii) $D$ contains no pair of opposite arcs (i.e., no directed cycle of length 2), and (iii) every vertex $x\in V$ satisfies $d^{+}(x)=d^{-}(x)$, where $d^{+}(x)$ and $d^{-}(x)$ denote the out-degree and in-degree of $x$. A directed cycle in $D$ is a cyclic sequence $v_0,v_1,\dots,v_{k-1},v_0$ of distinct vertices with $(v_i,v_{i+1\bmod k})\in A$ for all $i$. For an arc $a=(u,v)\in A$, the reversal of $a$ replaces $a$ by $(v,u)$, yielding a new directed graph $D^{a}$. Let $c(D)$ denote the total number of directed cycles in $D$.

Prove or disprove: for every Euler oriented graph $D$ with $c(D)\ge 1$, there exists an arc $a\in A$ such that $c(D^{a})<c(D)$.
status_search_result: Ádám's original conjecture (for arbitrary oriented graphs with a directed cycle) has known counterexamples among general digraphs, but it remains open for several restricted classes, including tournaments and simple digraphs, with only partial results (e.g., Jirásek's result for digraphs becoming acyclic after at most three arc reversals, and the case of quasi-acyclic digraphs). The specific variant restricted to Euler oriented graphs does not appear to have been resolved in the literature, and no counterexample or proof was located.

paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
original_question: Let D be a finite digraph with minimum out-degree k. Must D contain k directed cycles C1, C2, ..., Ck that can be ordered so that, for every j at most k, the union of the earlier cycles C1, ..., Cj-1 and the cycle Cj have at most one vertex in common?
self_contained_problem:
Let $D=(V,E)$ be a finite directed graph (loops and multiple arcs disallowed) such that every vertex has out-degree at least $k$, where $k\ge 1$ is an integer. A directed cycle in $D$ is a sequence $v_0\to v_1\to\cdots\to v_{\ell-1}\to v_0$ of distinct vertices with each consecutive arc in $E$.

Prove or disprove: there exist $k$ directed cycles $C_1,C_2,\ldots,C_k$ in $D$ (not necessarily distinct as cycles, but ordered) such that for every $j$ with $2\le j\le k$,
$$\Bigl|V(C_j)\cap\bigcup_{i=1}^{j-1}V(C_i)\Bigr|\le 1,$$
i.e., the cycle $C_j$ shares at most one vertex with the union of the vertex sets of the previously chosen cycles.
status_search_result: The conjecture (Hoàng–Reed) is known to hold for tournaments (Havet–Thomassé–Yeo) and for digraphs with minimum out-degree at most 3 (the δ+=2 case follows from Thomassen, and the δ+=3 case was established by Bang-Jensen, Bessy and Thomassé). The general case for arbitrary k remains open.

paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
original_question: Does the Caccetta-Haggkvist conjecture hold for multipartite tournaments, meaning orientations of complete multipartite graphs: does every such digraph with n vertices and minimum out-degree k contain a directed cycle of length at most ceil(n/k)?
self_contained_problem:
A multipartite tournament is an orientation of a complete multipartite graph; equivalently, it is a digraph whose vertex set can be partitioned into independent sets ("parts") such that between any two vertices in different parts there is exactly one arc, and there are no arcs within a part. For a digraph D and a vertex v, the out-degree of v is the number of arcs leaving v, and the minimum out-degree of D is the minimum of these values over all vertices. The girth of D is the length of a shortest directed cycle in D (or infinity if D is acyclic).

Question: Does every multipartite tournament D on n vertices with minimum out-degree at least k contain a directed cycle of length at most ⌈n/k⌉? Equivalently, prove or disprove that the Caccetta–Häggkvist bound holds in this class: every orientation of a complete multipartite graph on n vertices with minimum out-degree k has girth at most ⌈n/k⌉.
status_search_result: The general Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture is well known to be open, with even the k = n/3 (triangle) case unresolved. Partial results exist for special classes (bipartite tournaments, digraphs with small independence number, forbidden subgraph variants), but no proof or disproof of the conjecture restricted to multipartite tournaments appears in the literature; the restricted statement is posed as an open problem.

paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
original_question: Given a finite digraph D and a positive integer k, if the minimum out-degree of D is at least 2k - 1, must D contain k pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles?
self_contained_problem:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a finite directed graph (loops and multiple arcs forbidden) and let $k$ be a positive integer. The minimum out-degree of $D$ is $\delta^{+}(D) := \min_{v \in V} |\{u \in V : (v,u) \in A\}|$. A directed cycle is a sequence $v_1 v_2 \cdots v_\ell v_1$ of distinct vertices ($\ell \geq 2$) such that $(v_i,v_{i+1}) \in A$ for each $i$ (indices mod $\ell$). Two directed cycles are vertex-disjoint if they share no vertex. 

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $k$ and every finite digraph $D$ with $\delta^{+}(D) \geq 2k-1$, $D$ contains $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles.
status_search_result: The conjecture is confirmed for $k=1$ (trivial), $k=2$ (Thomassen, 1983), and $k=3$ (Lichiardopol, Pór, Sereni). It has also been verified for tournaments (Bang-Jensen, Bessy, Thomassé) and for digraphs with minimum semi-degree $\geq 2k-1$ in special classes, but the full conjecture remains open for general digraphs when $k \geq 4$.

paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
original_question: Let G be a finite directed or undirected graph, and let lambda(G) be the number of vertices in a longest path of G. For every natural number q with 0 < q < lambda(G), must the vertices of G be partitionable into two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs A and B such that lambda(A) is at most q and lambda(B) is at most lambda(G) - q?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite graph, either undirected or directed. A partition of $G$ is an ordered pair $(A,B)$ of vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs of $G$ with $V(A)\cup V(B)=V(G)$. For a graph (or digraph) $H$, let $\lambda(H)$ denote the number of vertices in a longest path of $H$ (in the directed case, a longest directed path). 

Prove or disprove: For every finite (directed or undirected) graph $G$ and every natural number $q$ with $0<q<\lambda(G)$, there exists a partition $(A,B)$ of $G$ such that
$$\lambda(A)\le q \quad\text{and}\quad \lambda(B)\le \lambda(G)-q.$$
status_search_result: The undirected Path Partition Conjecture, first formulated in 1981, remains open. The directed analogue (Directed Path Partition Conjecture) is also still open in general, with only partial results established for special classes of digraphs (e.g., claw-free graphs, locally in-semicomplete digraphs, quasi-transitive digraphs).

paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
context_brief: maximum directed cuts in acyclic digraphs
original_question: For acyclic digraphs with m arcs, let h(m) be the minimum, over all such digraphs, of the maximum size of a directed cut, where a directed cut (X, Y) consists of all arcs from X to Y. What is the infimum alpha_0 of alpha > 0 such that h(m) = m/4 + O(m^alpha) for all m >= 1?
self_contained_problem:
An acyclic digraph is a finite directed graph with no directed cycles. For a digraph $D=(V,A)$ and a partition $V=X\sqcup Y$, the directed cut $(X,Y)$ is the set of arcs of $D$ with tail in $X$ and head in $Y$; its size is $|(X,Y)|$. For an acyclic digraph $D$, let $\mathrm{mc}(D)$ denote the maximum of $|(X,Y)|$ over all partitions $V=X\sqcup Y$. Define
$$h(m)=\min\{\mathrm{mc}(D): D\text{ is an acyclic digraph with exactly }m\text{ arcs}\}.$$
It is known that $h(m)=m/4+o(m)$. Determine
$$\alpha_0=\inf\{\alpha>0 : h(m)=\tfrac{m}{4}+O(m^{\alpha})\text{ as }m\to\infty\}.$$
status_search_result: The exact value of α₀ remains open. Work of Alon, Bollobás, Gyárfás, Lehel and Scott (J. Graph Theory, 2007) establishes the bounds α₀ ∈ [3/5, 4/5] for acyclic digraphs, but no improvement determining the precise infimum is known.

paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
original_question: Does every sink-free finite digraph D have a quasi-kernel Q with size at most |V(D)|/2? Here a quasi-kernel is an independent vertex set Q such that every vertex outside Q can reach some vertex of Q by a directed path of length one or two.
self_contained_problem:
Let D = (V(D), A(D)) be a finite directed graph (no loops or multiple arcs) that is sink-free, meaning every vertex has out-degree at least 1. A quasi-kernel of D is a subset Q ⊆ V(D) such that:
(i) Q is independent in D, i.e. for all distinct u, v ∈ Q, neither (u,v) nor (v,u) is an arc of D; and
(ii) for every vertex y ∈ V(D) \ Q, either there exists x ∈ Q with (y,x) ∈ A(D), or there exist z ∈ V(D) \ Q and x ∈ Q with (y,z), (z,x) ∈ A(D) (equivalently, every vertex outside Q can reach some vertex of Q by a directed path of length 1 or 2).

Prove or disprove: every sink-free finite digraph D admits a quasi-kernel Q with |Q| ≤ |V(D)|/2.
status_search_result: The small quasi-kernel conjecture, due to Erdős and Székely (1976), remains open in general. It has been verified for restricted classes of digraphs, including semicomplete multipartite, quasi-transitive, locally semicomplete digraphs, split graphs, and digraphs with chromatic number at most 4 (Kostochka–Luo–Shan and subsequent works), but the full conjecture is unresolved as of recent surveys.

paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
original_question: Is there a universal positive real constant c < 1 such that every sink-free digraph of order n has a quasi-kernel Q with |Q| <= c n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a finite digraph (no loops, no multiple arcs). A vertex $v\in V$ is called a sink if it has no out-neighbors; $D$ is sink-free if it contains no sinks. A subset $Q\subseteq V$ is independent if no arc of $D$ has both endpoints in $Q$. A quasi-kernel of $D$ is an independent set $Q\subseteq V$ such that for every vertex $v\in V\setminus Q$ there is a directed path of length 1 or 2 from $v$ to some vertex of $Q$. It is known (Chvátal–Lovász) that every digraph has a quasi-kernel.

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant $c\in(0,1)$ such that every sink-free digraph $D$ of order $n$ admits a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|Q|\le cn$?
status_search_result: A 2024 survey on the small quasi-kernel conjecture explicitly states that it has not been proved that there exists some constant c < 1 such that every sink-free digraph G contains a quasi-kernel of size at most c|V(G)|. Various partial results are known for special classes (split digraphs, one-way split digraphs, orientations of certain graphs), but the general constant-factor question remains open.

paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
original_question: Does every oriented graph D have a vertex v whose second out-neighborhood has cardinality at least its out-neighborhood, that is, |N++(v)| >= |N+(v)|?
self_contained_problem:
An oriented graph is a directed graph D=(V,E) with no loops and no pair of opposite arcs (i.e., for any two distinct vertices u,v at most one of (u,v),(v,u) is an arc). For a vertex v∈V, let N^+(v)={u∈V : (v,u)∈E} denote the first out-neighborhood of v, and let N^{++}(v) denote the second out-neighborhood of v, namely the set of vertices w∈V∖({v}∪N^+(v)) such that there exists u∈N^+(v) with (u,w)∈E.

Prove or disprove: every oriented graph D contains a vertex v such that
|N^{++}(v)| ≥ |N^+(v)|.
status_search_result: Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture remains open in its full generality as of 2025–2026. It has been verified for special classes (e.g., tournaments by Fisher, oriented graphs with minimum out-degree ≤ 6, and small orders). Recent work in 2024–2025 has improved the best constant c such that some vertex satisfies |N^{++}(v)| ≥ c·|N^+(v)| (now c ≈ 0.7155), and has established the conjecture for random orientations of G(n,p) for fixed p∈[0,1/2), but no general proof or counterexample is known.

paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
original_question: What is the largest constant c such that every oriented graph has a vertex v satisfying |N++(v)| >= c |N+(v)|, where N++(v) is the second out-neighborhood and N+(v) is the out-neighborhood of v?
self_contained_problem:
An oriented graph is a directed graph with no loops and at most one directed edge between any two vertices (i.e., for any two distinct vertices u, v, at most one of the arcs (u,v) and (v,u) is present). For a vertex v in an oriented graph D, let N^+(v) denote the out-neighborhood of v, namely the set of vertices u such that (v,u) is an arc of D, and let N^{++}(v) denote the second out-neighborhood of v, namely the set of vertices w not in N^+(v) ∪ {v} such that there exists some u ∈ N^+(v) with (u,w) an arc of D.

Determine the largest real constant c with the following property: for every finite oriented graph D, there exists a vertex v of D such that
   |N^{++}(v)| ≥ c · |N^+(v)|.

(Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture asserts that c = 1 is attainable.)
status_search_result: The problem is a weakening of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture (1990), which corresponds to c = 1. The conjecture remains open in general; it is verified for tournaments (Fisher) and various subclasses (quasi-transitive, random/pseudorandom orientations, small orders, m-free digraphs), and partial bounds on c (such as the Chen–Shen–Yuster constant ≈ 0.6573 for tournaments and λ_m-type bounds for m-free oriented graphs) are known, but the exact largest constant for all oriented graphs has not been determined.

paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
original_question: Does every planar oriented graph admit a 2-coloring of its vertices such that each color class induces an acyclic subdigraph?
self_contained_problem:
An oriented graph is a directed graph obtained from a simple undirected graph by replacing each edge by exactly one of the two possible arcs between its endpoints (equivalently, a digraph with no loops, no parallel arcs, and no 2-cycles). A digraph is called planar if its underlying undirected graph admits an embedding in the plane without crossings. Given a digraph D = (V, A) and a positive integer k, an acyclic k-coloring of D is a map c : V → {1, 2, …, k} such that for every i ∈ {1, …, k} the subdigraph of D induced by c⁻¹(i) contains no directed cycle.

Determine whether the following statement holds: every planar oriented graph admits an acyclic 2-coloring; that is, the vertex set of any planar oriented graph can be partitioned into two parts each of which induces an acyclic subdigraph.
status_search_result: The statement is the well-known Neumann-Lara / Škrekovski conjecture (planar oriented graphs have dichromatic number at most 2). It remains open: the best general bound is that planar oriented graphs are 3-dicolourable, and the conjecture has been verified for planar oriented graphs on at most 26 vertices and for planar digraphs of digirth ≥ 4, but no full proof or counterexample is known as of 2026.
